When the grid overflows: a novel probabilistic framework to assess the success of storing excess electricity as heat in high-temperature ATES (HT-ATES) systems
abstract: Abstract Increasing shares of variable renewable electricity (VRE) are creating more frequent periods of surplus electricity, increasing the need for flexible options that can absorb and use this excess generation. One option is to convert surplus electricity into heat, but its effective use requires storage when heat production and demand do not coincide. Because heat demand remains concentrated in the colder months, long-duration seasonal thermal storage is needed to bridge this temporal gap. High-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage (HT-ATES) is one technology capable of providing this seasonal storage function. This study develops a demand-oriented operational probability of success (PoS) framework for evaluating whether HT-ATES can convert historically observed surplus electricity into useful seasonal heat. The Neubrandenburg system in Germany was used as a physically grounded reference case. Historical German electricity data from 2015 to 2022 were represented through empirical four-week surplus distributions and coupled to a chronological Monte Carlo inventory model accounting for charging availability, well thermal throughput, adopted storage limit, and thermal recovery. title: Assessing DASHAT through the New Public Service Lens: A Qualitative Documentary Analysis
abstract: Public service innovation does not by itself demonstrate democratic citizen influence. Dapur Sehat Atasi Stunting (DASHAT), an Indonesian community-oriented nutrition initiative, provides an opportunity to distinguish between program intentions, reported implementation, citizen participation, and documented influence over service decisions. This study examines how documentary evidence portrays DASHAT’s alignment with the seven New Public Service (NPS) principles, with particular attention to citizen participation across four stages of co-production: commissioning, design, delivery, and assessment. The study employed qualitative documentary analysis using directed qualitative content analysis. Thirteen evidence units were extracted from eight selected DASHAT-related documents and mapped deductively to the seven NPS principles. The four stages of co-production served as complementary analytical categories. The analysis distinguished program intentions, reported implementation, empirical findings, and recommendations to establish appropriate boundaries of interpretation. The documents provide evidence of service provision, attention to vulnerable groups, community empowerment, and capacity-building activities. A specific menu-planning activity indicates citizen participation in service design. However, the reviewed sources provide less conclusive evidence of citizen influence over…

title: The lesson planning knowledge of pre-service science teachers
abstract: This study assessed lesson planning knowledge and final teaching demonstration performance among pre-service science teachers at Central Bicol State University of Agriculture–Pasacao Campus during the second semester of academic year 2025–2026. Using a quantitative descriptive-correlational design, the study covered all 82 fourth-year Bachelor of Secondary Education major in Science interns. Data were obtained through a 24-item five-point Likert-scale lesson planning knowledge questionnaire and the Pre-Service Student Teaching Demonstration Evaluation Form. Weighted means, one-way analysis of variance, and Pearson product–moment correlation with t-tests were employed. Respondents were classified as having Very High Knowledge in writing lesson plans (4.52), competencies required to write a lesson plan (4.50), and assessment and assignment (4.59), and Very Knowledgeable in creating lesson objectives (4.46). Knowledge did not significantly differ across the four dimensions (p = .233). All seven final teaching demonstration parameters were rated Outstanding Performance, with means from 4.55 to 4.67; differences among performance parameters were not significant (p = .705). Positive statistically significant correlations were reported between all four knowledge dimensions and seven performance parameters (r = .317–.772). title: Governance of Professional Allowance Payments to Certified Non-Civil-Service Teachers with Inpassing Equivalence at Private Madrasahs: An Analysis of Legal Certainty and Fairness Following the Removal of Length of Service as A Criterion
abstract: This article examines the legal and governance framework for determining Teacher Professional Allowance (TPG) amounts for certified non-civil-service teachers with inpassing equivalence at private madrasahs in Indonesia, focusing on the treatment of length of service. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual and case approaches, it analyses relevant legislation, ministerial regulations, technical guidelines and Supreme Court Decision No. 55 P/HUM/2024. The analysis identifies a lack of alignment across three regulatory levels: higher-level legislation recognises length of service as an element of salary equivalence; Minister of Religious Affairs Regulation No. 4 of 2025 does not expressly mention it; and Director General Decision No. 665 of 2026 excludes it from the calculation. This inconsistency creates risks to legal certainty, proportional distributive justice, transparency, accountability and administrative effectiveness. The article argues that technical guidelines should not negate elements recognised by higher-level norms and proposes a six-stage governance model comprising integrated data collection, hierarchical verification, an operational definition of length of service, transparent calculation, an objection mechanism, and audit and evaluation. The study is normative and does not assess actual implementation in individual regions.

title: The Role of Customer Satisfaction In Mediating The Effect of Service Performance and Perceived Value On Customer Loyalty: Evidence From A B2B Outsourced Cleaning Service In A Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Setting
abstract: Outsourced facility services have become a strategic component of operations in Indonesia's highly regulated pharmaceutical industry, where cleanliness is not a cosmetic concern but a compliance requirement embedded in CPOB, WHO Prequalification, ISO 9001:2015, and ISO 14001:2015 standards. This study examined why an outsourced cleaning-service provider operating exclusively for a single pharmaceutical client since 2013 recorded 38 client complaints between November 2025 and January 2026, of which 66% concerned Service Performance and Perceived Value, and asked whether Customer Satisfaction mediates the effects of these two constructs on Customer Loyalty. Prior research has largely tested this chain in consumer-facing settings, leaving the business-to-business, compliance-driven pharmaceutical outsourcing context empirically unexamined. A quantitative, explanatory cross-sectional survey collected primary data from 355 employees of PT Bio Farma (Persero) Pasteur, Bandung, drawn by simple random sampling from a population of 3,096 and analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS. All eight hypotheses were supported at the 5% significance level. The model explained 74.0% of the variance in Customer Satisfaction and 68.3% of the variance in Customer Loyalty. Service Performance showed the strongest association with Customer Satisfaction (β = 0.543; f² = 0.901), while Customer Satisfaction sh…

title: Innovative Self-Efficacy and Social Identification as Drivers of Service Innovation Engagement and Innovation Performance in Digital SMEs
abstract: Digitalization provides opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to improve their services and strengthen innovation performance. However, realizing these opportunities depends not only on technology adoption but also on individual confidence and social relationships that encourage innovation. This study examines the effects of innovative self-efficacy and social identification on service innovation engagement, as well as the effect of service innovation engagement on innovation performance among digitally enabled SMEs in Surabaya, Indonesia. Using a quantitative explanatory survey approach, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the proposed relationships. The findings indicate that innovative self-efficacy and social identification positively influence service innovation engagement, with social identification demonstrating a stronger relationship. Furthermore, service innovation engagement positively influences innovation performance. These findings highlight the importance of individual confidence, a sense of belonging to business communities, and active involvement in service innovation. This study extends service innovation research to digitally enabled SMEs and offers practical implications for strengthening innovation practices and competitiveness.

Enhanced CO 2 Capture in Type III Porous Liquids via Steric Solvent Structure Regulation
abstract: Abstract Porous liquids (PLs), an emerging class of materials, combine the abundant porous structure of solid adsorbents with the rapid mass-transfer and fluidity properties of liquid adsorbents, showing great potential for CO2 capture. In this study, a targeted solvent structure regulation strategy was proposed to fabricate three sterically hindered solvents for PLs, including the conventional imidazolium ionic liquid [EMIM][NTF2], amino-functionalized ionic liquid [AEMIM][NTF2], and amino-hydrogen-bond bifunctional deep eutectic solvent [EMTA], which were blended with MOF-801 to construct three types of MOF-801-based PLs containing permanent micropores. A set of characterizations and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to confirm the successful synthesis of MOF-801-PLs. Meanwhile, the adsorption performance of MOF-801-PLs for CO2 in mimetic flue gas was evaluated, and the MOF-801-EMTA-PLs exhibited great adsorption capability of up to 1.378 mmol/g, higher than that of MOF-801-AEMIM-PLs (0.541 mmol/g) and MOF-801-EMIM-PLs (0.498 mmol/g). Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations and grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations were used to observe the CO2 adsorption mechanism. This study verifies that tuning solvent molecular structures is a feasible strategy for the design of advanced PLs.

One-Year Participation in A School-Based Yoga Program and Changes in Children’s Self- Regulation and Laceration-Related School Infirmary Visits
abstract: School-based interventions that support children’s psychological and physical functioning are needed to promote healthy development. This study examined changes associated with a year-long yoga program implemented as part of routine elementary school education in Japan. The Asa (morning) Yoga program was implemented during Monday morning homeroom sessions from April 2024 to March 2025 at one public elementary school. Data from 201 children for whom informed consent was obtained were analyzed. Psychological functioning was assessed before and after the intervention, and monthly visits to the school infirmary due to lacerations and bruises were examined across four study periods. Post-intervention scores were significantly higher for difficulty with self-control and difficulty with goal-oriented motivation. Visits to the school infirmary due to lacerations differed significantly across study periods, with fewer visits during January–February than during April–June. No significant pre–post changes were observed in quality of school life, and no significant differences were observed in visits due to bruises. Participation in a year-long, school-based yoga program was associated with changes in selected aspects of children’s psychological functioning and laceration-related infirmary visits. COVID Diaries, U.S. Media Response to COVID Vaccination Program, December 2020 to September 2021
abstract: Abstract We present a curated dataset of U.S. news coverage of the COVID-19 vaccination rollout to support research on media communication during a public health emergency. The dataset contains 5,317 unique URLs from 20 nationwide, open-access media outlets, spanning December 2020 (Phase 1a allocation) through September 2021 (broad availability and emerging mandates). Outlets were selected based on a survey of 489 U.S. adults identifying their primary sources of information about the vaccination program. For each publication, we provide outlet, date, headline, original URL, and a permanent link. These records capture the contemporaneous media environment in which individuals sought information and made decisions about COVID-19 vaccination. The dataset enables analyses of topical emphasis, framing, and agenda-setting across outlets and over time, and provides a resource for reproducible research on audience segmentation, economic drivers of content, and editorial retention strategies during the COVID-19 vaccination campaign.

title: Thermal response during erbium laser-assisted removal of ceramic crowns and laminate veneers: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract This review aimed to systematically map and synthesize the available evidence regarding the thermal effects of laser-assisted debonding of ceramic crowns and laminate veneers on the dental pulp and to identify current knowledge gaps. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the scoping review was conducted after preliminary screening identified limited and heterogeneous evidence for a systematic review. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through June 2026. Two independent reviewers screened eligible studies and extracted data on laser parameters, irradiation protocols, restorative characteristics, debonding performance, and thermal outcomes. A total of 63 records were identified, and 10 studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in this scoping review. Er, Cr: YSGG was the most investigated laser, followed by Er: YAG. The included studies evaluated the debonding of lithium disilicate and zirconia laminate veneers and full-coverage crowns. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in laser parameters, ceramic materials, restoration thicknesses, and outcome assessment methods. Intrapulpal temperature change and debonding time were the most frequently reported outcomes, with most studies reporting temperature increases below the commonly cited historical thermal threshold for irreversible pulp damage. Evolution and Mechanism of Asphalt–Aggregate Interfacial Behavior Induced by Asphalt Ultraviolet Aging: From Microscale Adhesion to Macroscale Mechanical Response
abstract: Abstract The deterioration of asphalt physicochemical properties under ultraviolet (UV) aging affects the microscale and macroscale characteristics of the asphalt–aggregate interface. To reveal the evolution and underlying mechanisms of these characteristics, this study investigated the microscale adhesion and macroscale mechanical response of the asphalt–aggregate interface induced by UV aging of asphalt. First, the variations in the chemical composition, surface morphology, and surface mechanical properties of base asphalt (BA) and high-viscosity asphalt (HVA) under UV aging were elucidated using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), asphalt four-component analysis, and atomic force microscopy (AFM). Subsequently, the microscale interfacial work of adhesion was quantified by AFM measurements and surface free energy theory, whereas the macroscale viscoelastic and tensile responses under dynamic shear and uniaxial tensile loading were assessed using an improved frequency sweep test with aggregate substrates and pull-off tests, respectively. Finally, the intrinsic linkages among the microscale properties of asphalt, the microscale interfacial adhesion, and the macroscale mechanical response were examined using Pearson correlation analysis. title: Colocalization between bone loading and metabolic activity in the human tibia in response to acute exercise
abstract: Abstract Bone strain and remodeling are important factors affecting bone strength. Better characterizing the relationship between these factors in response to acute loading will improve our understanding of bone metabolism in relation to daily physical activities. The purpose of this study was to evaluate colocalization between finite element-estimated bone strain and [18F]sodium fluoride ([18F]NaF) positron emission tomography (PET) imaging-estimated bone remodeling in the tibial diaphysis in response to acute exercise. We hypothesized that the exercise-induced change in standardized uptake values would be greatest in regions of higher strain. 26 participants underwent bilateral PET-magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MRI) scans before and after a bout of stair ascent and descent exercise. Finite element analysis was performed to calculate principal strain distributions in the tibial diaphysis. [18F]NaF standardized uptake values (SUV) were calculated from pre- and post-exercise PET data and mapped to the tibial surface. Mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in SUV were calculated and compared between regions defined by strain percentile. Both normalized mean pre-exercise and exercise-induced change in [18F]NaF SUV increased with maximum principal strain in a pattern suggesting an exponential relationship. title: Recurrent features of stress response in the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium: intracellular inclusions and vacuoles forming upon UV
abstract: Abstract The Zygnematophyceae, the closest algal relatives of land plants, many of which are unicellular, must manage environmental stress responses largely cell-autonomously, making them powerful models for dissecting the ancestral cellular toolkit underlying plant terrestrialisation. In this brief report, we revisit UV-B time-course experiment data on the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium endlicherianum , in which UV-B irradiation triggered a significant accumulation of terminal vacuoles. We re-analysed the corresponding RNA-seq data with a new focus on genes associated with vacuolar biology and lipid metabolism. Within 2 h of UV-B onset, homologs of genes linked to vacuolar functions in land plants were differentially expressed: transcripts of putatively lytic enzymes (a papain-like cysteine protease and two GH38 alpha-mannosidases), of a metal tolerance protein and of two AHK1-like histidine kinases increased, whereas those of the tonoplast H⁺-pyrophosphatase AVP1, the Ca²⁺/H⁺ antiporter CAX5 and the phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate 5-kinase FAB1A decreased. Lipid-related transcripts indicated a shift from membrane lipid biosynthesis towards lipid turnover, including the induction of a SUGAR-DEPENDENT 1-like triacylglycerol lipase. abstract: Aim: This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in four core management accounting functions: cost analysis, budgeting, management control, and decision-making. Method: A structured literature review synthesizes findings from systematic reviews, case studies, experiments, a dissertation, and professional reports to distinguish demonstrated predictive benefits from broader claims about organizational performance. The review is limited by the absence of a complete database export and a study-specific PRISMA flow; it should therefore be read as a structured synthesis of accessible literature rather than a fully reproducible systematic review. Results: Machine-learning models can match or exceed human estimates in selected cost-estimation tasks when adequate historical data are available. In budgeting, machine learning can improve prediction accuracy, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish causal effects or guarantee appropriate resource allocation. In management control, digital tools support more timely and anticipatory monitoring, although the available evidence does not always isolate the effect of AI itself. For decision-making, the usefulness of AI depends on data quality, model explainability, user trust, professional competence, and the preservation of human accountability. title: Analysis of Causes and Risk Mitigation for Delivery Delays Based on On-Time In-Full (OTIF) Data in Non-Cement Distribution Using RCA and FMEA Methods at PT XYZ
abstract: Delivery punctuality is an important indicator of logistics service performance, yet non-cement distribution at PT XYZ still experiences delays. On Time In Full (OTIF) data from May to July 2026 recorded that only 54.64% of 14,986 shipments were delivered on time. This study aims to determine the on-time delivery rate, identify the dominant causes and root causes of delay, and determine mitigation priorities. The methods used were Pareto diagram, Root Cause Analysis (RCA) with fishbone and 5 Why, and Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), with Severity, Occurrence, and Detection rated by two respondents. The Pareto results show that long parking time (49.9%) and unloading schedule (41.1%) caused 91.0% of the delays. RCA identified the root causes as the absence of a standard maximum stopping time, a joint arrival scheduling mechanism with receivers, a procedure for communicating estimated arrival, and a cargo readiness confirmation procedure. Based on FMEA, the highest Risk Priority Number (RPN) belongs to the absence of a joint arrival scheduling mechanism with receivers (336), followed by the absence of an estimated arrival notification procedure (168) and a standard maximum stopping time (120). Joint arrival scheduling with receivers should be the priority for improvement.

title: AI-DRIVEN INNOVATION AND ORGANISATIONAL TRUST IN AI: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF KNOWLEDGE TRANSPARENCY IN FAMILY-OWNED SMES
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly viewed as a driver of organisational innovation through its capacity to generate and recombine knowledge. However, the relationship between AI-driven innovation and organisational trust in AI remains insufficiently understood. Drawing on organisational trust theory and the knowledge-based view of the firm, this study examines the mediating role of transparency of AI-generated knowledge in linking AI-driven innovation to organisational trust in AI. Using cross-sectional survey data collected from managers and executives of family-owned SMEs and analysed through structural equation modelling, the study identifies positive associations among AI-driven innovation, knowledge transparency, and organisational trust in AI. The estimated indirect effect is consistent with the proposed mediating role of knowledge transparency, although the research design does not establish causality. The study contributes to innovation and knowledge research by examining perceived knowledge transparency as a link between AI-driven innovation and trust. It also offers managerial insights into the potential relevance of making AI-generated knowledge understandable and open to discussion.

title: Transformation of Business Communication Model in Crisis: Rebranding of Warung New Bahari into Ekspresss Bahari
abstract: This study examines the transformation of the business communication model in the franchise crisis experienced by Warung New Bahari (WNB), which underwent rebranding into Ekspresss Bahari (WEB) and succeeded in maintaining only 30 of 125 outlets in the Jabodetabek region. Using a qualitative approach with a case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participatory observation of 8 outlets, business document analysis, and two focus group discussions. Findings reveal that there is a structural disjunction between the implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) technology and the Cultural Intelligence (CQ) of organizational actors, manifested in seven forms of communication gaps. The transformation of the communication model was designed through three phases—restart-up, reconcept, and rebranding—by integrating CQ into every layer of business communication. The recommended communication model integrates ERP as a strategic communication platform, CQ as the core competence of organizational actors, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an operational enabler. The novelty of this research lies in bridging the studies of ERP, business communication, and cultural intelligence in the context of crisis, downsizing, and rebranding of franchise-based MSMEs.

title: Implementasi PLTS–PLN dengan Automatic Transfer Switch pada Penerangan Gedung Parkir (Implementation of a Solar PV–Grid System with an Automatic Transfer Switch for Parking Garage Lighting)
abstract: Parking garage lighting needs an uninterrupted power supply, but solar PV output varies with irradiance and weather. This study implements a solar PV–PLN system with an Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) for lighting on the seventh floor of the Universitas Pamulang Viktor parking building, and examines how far the field test records support conclusions about battery backup and energy contribution. The system consists of three 550 Wp PV panels, a 60 A MPPT controller, a 48 V 50 Ah battery, an inverter with a 1,500 W continuous rating, and a 63 A two-pole ATS, serving 75 LED lamps of 18 W each (1,350 W). Observations ran for seven days, 09:00–21:00 WIB, with readings every 30 minutes on the PV, battery, and PLN sides. The load was activated in three scenarios (12, 40, and 75 lamps) without controlled repetition. The system was assembled and supplied the lighting load. The design requirement of four hours at full load is 5.4 kWh, while the battery’s usable AC energy is only about 1.82 kWh (80% DoD, 95% inverter efficiency), equivalent to roughly 81 minutes. Transfer to PLN was observed at around 18:30, when battery voltage approached 45 V. Daily PV output was recorded at 275–446 W. On the first day, battery current differed substantially between instruments (11.86 A and 22.12 A), and ATS transfer time and actual irradiance were not recorded. title: PERFIL CITOPATOLÓGICO DO COLO DO ÚTERO EM MULHERES ATENDIDAS NA ATENÇÃO PRIMÁRIA DO CENTRO-NORTE DE RONDÔNIA
abstract: O câncer do colo do útero permanece relevante problema de saúde pública, especialmente na região Norte do Brasil. Este estudo analisou o perfil epidemiológico, assistencial e citopatológico dos exames realizados em mulheres residentes em Jaru-RO, entre 2020 e 2025, bem como a associação entre faixa etária e desfechos. Trata-se de estudo observacional, retrospectivo, descritivo, analítico e transversal, com dados do SISCAN/DATASUS (n=10.537). Utilizaram-se estatísticas descritivas e inferenciais (qui-quadrado de Pearson e Exato de Fisher; p<0,05). Houve maior frequência de exames entre 40–44 anos (15,76%), predominância de mulheres autodeclaradas amarelas (41,32%) e realização majoritária para rastreamento (99,51%), com 80,90% de citologia prévia normal. As amostras foram predominantemente satisfatórias (99,27%), com representatividade da zona de transformação em 77,60%. As lesões intraepiteliais foram pouco frequentes (LSIL: 0,47%; HSIL: 0,23%), com predomínio de exames sem alterações (99,29%). Na análise bivariada, não houve associação entre faixa etária e adequabilidade da amostra (p=0,351). Observou-se associação significativa com representatividade da zona de transformação (p<0,001), ASC-US/ASC-H (p=0,042), lesões intraepiteliais (p=0,018), células endometriais (p=0,027), citologia anterior (p<0,001) e resultado dentro da normalidade (p<0,001). title: The Economic Impact of Hosting International Sports Mega Events (2015- 2025): A Systematic Narrative Review
abstract: The hosting of the Olympic Games, FIFA World Cup and other sport mega-events is always touted as an economic imperative, with the expectation of an economic boost from the event, job creation, investment in the City's infrastructure, and the creation of a legacy that will last for years to come. The effects on these topics are scattered in the fields of economics, urban studies, tourism management and sociology, however. Research studies were searched from 2015 to 2025 in the two literature databases we used, Semantic Scholar and PubMed Central (PMC), to determine the impact of sport mega-events on the economy. After screening, 31 studies met the inclusion criteria and were quality assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) of 1052 records identified. The three main findings were found using thematic synthesis. First, the hosts might have positive non-market benefits (reputational or “psychic” benefits), which may be unevenly experienced across low-income and minoritized groups. Second, structural negative or negligible aggregate financial impacts are typical in most major events like the Olympics, the FIFA World Cup and Formula 1. Thirdly, small and medium events tend to create small and medium economic impact locally but with uncertain benefits. Issues of debate include tourism, the development of the host country, image impacts and the concept of “legacy.” There …

title: Invisible Wounds: Structural Violence and Institutional Power in 4.48 Psychosis and Cleansed
abstract: This paper examines Sarah Kane's plays Cleansed (1998) and 4.48 Psychosis (2000) through the lens of structural violence and institutional power. Drawing on Johan Galtung's concept of structural violence as indirect harm embedded in social systems, it argues that Kane depicts "invisible wounds", psychological, emotional, and existential traumas inflicted by oppressive institutions such as psychiatric facilities and authoritarian regimes. In Cleansed, the institution manifests as a site of physical torture and identity erasure, reflecting broader societal mechanisms of control over non-normative bodies and desires. In 4.48 Psychosis, violence is internalized, critiquing the medical-industrial complex's failure to address mental suffering. Through fragmented dramaturgy and graphic imagery, Kane exposes how institutional power perpetuates harm, urging audiences to confront complicity in these systems. This analysis synthesizes trauma theory, Postdramatic theatre, and feminist critiques to illuminate Kane's contribution to experiential.

title: A Dynamic MILP Framework for Multi-Stage Food-Grain Supply Chain Optimization: A Case Study of Jharkhand’s Public Distribution System
abstract: Food-grain supply chains involve several activities such as procurement, processing, transportation, storage, and distribution. In the Public Distribution System (PDS) of India, these activities are closely connected because procured paddy has to be processed in rice mills before the milled rice can be stored and distributed to different demand locations. This study develops a dynamic Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for a four-stage food-grain supply chain consisting of procurement centres, rice mills, warehouses, and PDS distribution points. The model considers milling recovery, period-wise milling capacity, procurement availability, route activation, warehouse capacity, inventory balance, demand fulfilment, opportunity cost, and shortage penalty. Transportation costs are calculated from inter-node distances using the applicable Jharkhand Government transportation-rate structure. The model is tested through computational experiments using the East Singhbhum network and is further examined using observed procurement-stage data and a calibrated downstream representation of the Seraikela-Kharsawan district network. For the East Singhbhum simulation, the total system cost decreases from INR 76,102,850.08 under the baseline allocation to INR 75,105,464.62 with the proposed MILP, giving a reduction of 1.31%. title: Kinerja Energi PLTS 1.650 Wp untuk Penerangan Parkir dengan ATS (Energy Performance of a 1,650 Wp Solar PV System for Parking Lighting with an Automatic Transfer Switch)
abstract: This study evaluates the energy performance of a nominal 1,650 Wp solar photovoltaic (PV) system installed to support lighting on the seventh floor of the Universitas Pamulang parking building and connected to the PLN grid through an Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS). Measurements were recorded every 30 minutes from 09:00 to 20:00 Western Indonesian Time over seven days, covering voltage, current, power, energy, and battery state of charge. The summary data report an average PV output power of 351.714 W, while average PLN power on days with an active lighting load was approximately 1,508.990 W. The daily PV energy values listed in the tables range from 0.237 to 0.460 kWh, averaging 0.342 kWh. However, these energy summaries cannot be consistently reconstructed from the full interval data and are therefore not used to quantify PLN energy reduction. A single comparison between the KWS-302 monitor and an AVO meter gives relative differences of approximately 0.88% for voltage and 17.89% for current; current-measurement accuracy is consequently not considered validated. Design calculations indicate a 1,350 W lighting load requiring 5.4 kWh for four hours of operation, whereas the 48 V, 50 Ah battery at an 80% depth of discharge provides a theoretical 1.92 kWh DC, or about 1.82 kWh AC assuming 95% inverter efficiency. title: Exact optical soliton solutions on continuous-wave backgrounds for a coupled fourth-order nonlinear Schrödinger system in weakly birefringent optical fibers
abstract: We investigate exact optical soliton solutions for a coupled fourth-order nonlinear Schrödinger system governing pulse propagation in weakly birefringent optical fibers. Three complementary analytical methods — the generalized exponential rational integral function method (GERIFM), the [Formula: see text]-expansion method, and the tanh-coth method — are systematically applied to derive 12 distinct families of exact solutions, including bright, dark, singular, and combined soliton structures on non-vanishing continuous-wave backgrounds. The mathematical validity of all solutions is confirmed by direct substitution into the governing equations and the reduced ordinary differential equation. Graphical analyses in two and three dimensions demonstrate the temporal stability and robust propagation characteristics of representative solutions. The results provide a theoretical foundation for the design of ultrafast optical communication systems, mode-locked fiber lasers, and nonlinear photonic devices in which fourth-order dispersion and birefringence effects are significant.

title: Development of A Real-Time Monitoring and Overcurrent Protection System For Industrial Air Compressors
abstract: Compressors are vital equipment in the manufacturing industry that generate pressurized air to support various production processes. A common issue encountered in compressors is elevated operating temperatures and premature component failure caused by delayed replacement of consumable spare parts, such as oil, filters, and maintenance kits. This study aims to design and implement an Arduino Nano-based monitoring system for operating temperature, electric current, and running hours to support predictive maintenance routines on compressors. The system integrates a temperature sensor, a current sensor, and an hour meter with an Arduino Nano as the central controller, coupled with a buzzer alarm for early warnings whenever operating parameters exceed predefined threshold limits. The current sensor was evaluated by comparing system readings against a clamp meter across five electrical load variations, showing an average deviation of 0.09 A with a maximum error of 8.11%. Meanwhile, the temperature sensor testing against a ThermoGun as a reference instrument yielded measurement discrepancies of 1–3 °C under ambient and heated conditions. Furthermore, the system successfully provided real-time alerts whenever temperature, current, or operating hours exceeded set limits. The results demonstrate that the developed system reliably and effectively monitors compressor health as an economica…

title: Clinical characteristics and endoscopic management of inflammatory fibroid polyp of the gastrointestinal tract
abstract: BACKGROUND Inflammatory fibroid polyps (IFPs) are rare lesions of the gastrointestinal tract. Knowledge regarding the endoscopic and clinical characteristics of IFPs remains limited. AIM To investigate the clinical and endoscopic characteristics of IFPs and evaluate the outcomes of endoscopic resection (ER) for IFP management. METHODS This retrospective analysis enrolled a consecutive cohort of patients who received ER for IFPs at our institution between March 2014 and December 2024. We collected and analyzed their clinicopathological characteristics, endoscopic findings, and long-term follow-up outcomes. RESULTS A total of 108 consecutive patients were included (59 females, 54.6%), with a mean age of 54.6 ± 10.7 years. The median lesion size was 10 mm (range 5-50 mm). Most lesions were located in the stomach (70/108, 64.8%), followed by the large intestine (36/108, 33.3%); one lesion was found in the esophagus and one in the duodenum. All 108 patients successfully underwent ER, with no severe adverse events reported. Both the en bloc resection rate and the endoscopic complete resection rate were 99.1%. Three of 108 patients (2.8%) developed recurrent lesions postoperatively. A comparative analysis of gastric and colorectal IFP patients revealed significant differences in lesion size, endoscopic techniques, and operative time. abstract: Abstract Peri-implant biomaterials are commonly compared as isolated antimicrobial technologies, although their clinical relevance depends on linked requirements spanning prevention and treatment. Preventive approaches must preserve tissue integration and future cleanability; once disease develops, treatment must provide access to and disruption of mature biofilm, preserve or recover implant-surface competence, control destructive inflammation, support defect-specific regeneration, and enable durable maintenance. This structured critical review proposes a six-gate framework that evaluates preventive surfaces, decontamination methods, local delivery systems, host-directed materials, and regenerative adjuncts against those downstream requirements. Human peri-implant evidence was prioritized for treatment claims. Animal studies, clinically representative in vitro models, simplified implant models, and indirect oral-biofilm or general materials evidence were considered separately. The synthesis shows that mechanical and surgical strategies have the most direct clinical evidence, but no decontamination protocol has shown consistent, durable superiority across clinical settings. Reconstructive biomaterials can improve radiographic defect fill in selected defects, but their additional benefit for composite disease resolution remains uncertain. title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
abstract: Abstract Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents. PEO@Dry retains the intrinsic interfacial reactivity of PEO and LiTFSI while eliminating solvent-derived interference. FEC is found to undergo a spontaneous chemical reaction with Li metal before electrochemical reduction, producing a dense LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that is subsequently reinforced by organic species derived from the electrochemical reactions. The resulting SEI exhibits a well-defined composition and robust structure, leading to an enhanced interfacial stability and electrochemical performance. Comparative research with a DME-based liquid electrolyte reveals that FEC (DME@FEC) follows distinct reaction pathways depending on its solvation state. abstract: BACKGROUND Spontaneously ruptured hepatocellular carcinoma (rHCC) carries high early mortality following emergency hemostatic procedures like transarterial embolization (TAE) or transarterial chemoembolization (TACE). Existing prognostic models lack accuracy, particularly by omitting morphological risk factors such as tumor protrusion. AIM To develop and validate a novel scoring system that integrates quantitative tumor protrusion with clinical parameters to improve 30-day mortality prediction. METHODS This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with rHCC treated with emergency TAE/TACE between January 2007 and December 2024. Three quantitative protrusion metrics (percentage, maximum diameter, and area) were compared for predictive performance. Inter-observer reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 30-day mortality. A weighted scoring system was derived from regression coefficients and internally validated using bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations). The model’s discriminative ability was compared to the model for end-stage liver disease and Child-Pugh scores using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and DeLong’s test. Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the impact of Mat Pilates on functional capacity, flexibility, and depressive symptoms in women diagnosed with breast cancer who received adjuvant radiotherapy. Methods In this randomized clinical trial, 164 women with breast cancer (stages 0–III), aged 18 years or older, were randomized, and 156 were included in the analyses (79 in the Mat Pilates group and 77 in the control group). Handgrip strength, functional exercise capacity assessed by the 2-Minute Step Test (2MST), flexibility, and depressive symptoms were evaluated at baseline, at the end of radiotherapy (RT), and at 30 days, 3 months, and 6 months after RT. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to analyze functional capacity and flexibility, while the cumulative incidence of new depressive symptoms was estimated among participants without depressive symptoms at baseline. Results No significant group × time interactions were observed for handgrip strength (Wald χ 2 = 7.834; df = 4; p = 0.098), the 2-Minute Step Test (Wald χ 2 = 6.877; df = 4; p = 0.143), or flexibility (Wald χ 2 = 3.728; df = 4; p = 0.444). During the RT period, the cumulative of new depressive symptoms was 14.8%. Conclusion Functional capacity and flexibility improved over time, but their trajectories did not differ significantly between the Mat Pilates and control groups. title: The Influence of Cholesterol on the Mechanism of Stabilization of Phospholipid Bilayers by Sucrose
abstract: Abstract Sugars are widely utilized to preserve cells during desiccation and freezing because their addition results in a decrease of the main phase transition temperature of phospholipid bilayers. This has been explained by two opposing models: the water replacement hypothesis, involving direct sugar–phospholipid interaction at the bilayer interface, and the hydration forces explanation, involving an entropy-driven phase transition with sugar molecules accumulating away from the bilayer interface. However, biological membranes contain substantial sterol content, and the influence of cholesterol (CHOL) on these mechanisms remains poorly defined. We conducted molecular dynamics simulations of sucrose (SUC) interactions with pure 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DOPC), 2DOPC:1CHOL, and 1DOPC:1CHOL bilayers at full hydration and under dehydration. SUC expanded bilayers, reduced lipid tail order, and formed direct hydrogen bonds with DOPC headgroups, with the strongest protective effect observed under dehydration. CHOL condensed the bilayers and limited SUC-driven expansion, producing a saturation-limited response at high SUC concentration. SUC remains interfacially associated at low concentration but increasingly accumulates in the interbilayer aqueous region at high concentration, particularly under dehydration conditions. Thus, CHOL modulates the magnitude of SUC-mediat…

title: Xiao Chai Hu Decoction ameliorates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity through an Akkermansia muciniphila–associated gut–heart mechanism
abstract: Abstract Background Doxorubicin (DOX) induces cardiotoxicity partly through ferroptosis. Xiao Chai Hu Decoction (XCHD) has anti-inflammatory and organ-protective activities, but its effects on DOX-induced cardiac injury and the gut–heart axis remain unclear. Purpose This study investigated whether XCHD attenuates DOX-induced cardiotoxicity through gut microbiota remodeling, with particular emphasis on the contribution of Akkermansia muciniphila and the downstream involvement of BMP10-associated ferroptosis. Methods Male C57BL/6 mice received DOX (5 mg/kg/week for 4 weeks; cumulative dose, 20 mg/kg) and XCHD (5–20 g/kg/day). Cardiac function, myocardial injury, histopathology, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-related indices were evaluated. Cardiac transcriptomics and fecal 16S rRNA sequencing were combined with antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and A. muciniphila supplementation to assess microbiota involvement. H9c2 cells treated with XCHD-containing serum and subjected to BMP10 knockdown were used to examine the downstream role of BMP10. Results XCHD improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial injury, fibrosis, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-associated alterations. Analysis of Attitude Toward Green Financing in Support Net Zero Emission by 2060 Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB): A Perspective from MSMEs
abstract: Net Zero Emission (NZE) 2060 has become Indonesia’s national aspiration to achieve a carbon-neutral economy by 2060 that the banking sector has reinforced its role as a key catalyst in promoting environmentally sustainable economic activities, particularly through the provision of green credit, financing, and investment. This study examines the behavior of green MSMEs toward Green Financing in supporting NZE 2060 based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). The research focuses on green MSMEs located in four districts/cities in the Special Region of Yogyakarta (DIY), aiming to analyze the determinants of their behavioral intention to access Green Financing. The study applies the 10-times rule sampling technique and collects primary data from 62 respondents using a Likert scale (1–5) questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS 4.0. The findings reveal that Attitude does not significantly influence Behavioral Intention among green MSMEs actors in accessing Green Financing.

title: Beyond Energy Nationalism: Contractual Lock-In, Gas Export Diversion, LNG Trading Hubs, and Asymmetric Energy Security in Indonesia Singapore Natural Gas Relations
abstract: This qualitative literature review examines the economic, contractual, infrastructural, and environmental consequences of diverting Indonesian natural gas exports from Singapore toward domestic users. It distinguishes Indonesian pipeline gas from shipborne liquefied natural gas (LNG), Singapore-based LNG trading and transshipment, and final Singaporean gas consumption. Using recent peer-reviewed literature and contemporaneous official information, the study critically assesses claims that a small temporary supply reduction implies negligible bilateral dependence or that export interruption necessarily triggers financial default and gas flaring. The synthesis identifies asymmetric but conditional vulnerabilities: Singapore may replace a limited pipeline shortfall through diversified procurement, while Indonesian producers can face revenue and financing risks if domestic offtake or contractual settlement is inadequate. Conversely, a connected and creditworthy domestic customer may create significant economic value through greater electricity reliability and industrial activity. A conceptual framework links physical flows, gas sales agreements, project-finance covenants, infrastructure absorption, political credibility, and methane outcomes. Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
abstract: Abstract Lanthanide photocatalysis has emerged as a promising alternative to precious-metal systems due to its earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique photophysical properties. However, reported lanthanide-based photocatalysts have primarily focused on the generation of reactive radical species, with limited ability to control product selectivity in bond-forming processes. Here we report a single europium-cryptate catalyst that enables selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling of benzyl chlorides by combining single-electron transfer-driven radical generation with bimolecular homolytic substitution reactivity. The reaction proceeds through a Eu(II)-benzyl intermediate that initiates single-electron transfer to form a benzyl radical, followed by SH2 with a Eu(III)-benzyl species to forge the cross-coupling product. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for designing selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling reactions using lanthanide metals, paving the way for the broader application of lanthanide-based photocatalysts in organic synthesis.

Advancing Psychrophilic Anaerobic Digestion of Cattle Manure through Microbial Adaptation, Bioaugmentation and Pathways to Reliable Low-Temperature Biogas: A Critical Review
abstract: ow-temperature anaerobic digestion of cattle manure can recover methane, but slow conversion and delayed start-up can limit reliable energy delivery. This critical narrative review examines biochemical constraints, microbial adaptation and bioaugmentation, performance measurement and translation to useful energy. International evidence is synthesized, with the Ngorongoro Conservation Area of northern Tanzania serving as a motivating application context. The synthesis identifies coordination of hydrolysis, syntrophic conversion and methanogenesis as central to methane onset, production rate and stability. Cold-adapted inocula and targeted consortia can improve methane recovery in selected controlled systems, but differences in substrates, inocula, dosing and reactor operation restrict cross-study comparison and field extrapolation. Combined microbial and carbon amendments require controls that distinguish biological effects from additional substrate contributions. Reliable interpretation also requires explicit solids accounting, gas volume reference conditions and separation of measured recovery from modeled asymptotic potential. Higher methane recovery alone does not establish improved pH stability, methane fraction or microbial persistence. Net energy and economic benefits of these interventions remain insufficiently resolved because methane gains must be assessed alongside pr…

title: Uncertainty-aware planning of hybrid renewable and conventional distributed generation using a novel optimization framework
abstract: Abstract With the increasing integration of distributed generation (DG) units based on renewable energy into power distribution networks, advanced planning models are required to guarantee smooth integration and enhanced network performance. In order to reduce investment costs while lowering line losses and improving voltage stability, this study proposes an optimization planning model for the optimal placement and sizing of DG units. A novel hybrid algorithm, the Improved Genetic Moth Swarm Algorithm (IGMSA), combining the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and an improved Moth Swarm Algorithm (MSA), is introduced to address the complex DG placement problem under renewable-generation uncertainty. This method considers systems with variable renewable energy sources (RESs), including photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind turbines (WT), and their combinations with fuel cells (FC), with uncertainties modeled using the Point Estimate Method (PEM). Three hybrid configurations; namely PV/WT/FC, PV/FC, and WT/FC, are simulated and optimized on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 119-bus distribution systems. Comparative analysis demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed IGMSA against the standard GMSA and other optimization algorithms, yielding competitive Pareto-optimal solutions with an improved balance between exploration and exploitation. Results indicate that the proposed approach can effectively …

title: Naïve Bayes integration with Markov chain and cellular automata for modelling urban land use change
abstract: Abstract Away from the conventional Logistic Regression (LR) technique, this study presents a novel Naïve Bayes (NB) integration with Markov Chain (MC) and Cellular Automata (CA) for modelling urban land use change. Although NB is a simple parametric algorithm similar to the Logistic Regression (LR), previous studies have shown that it can outperform the LR when the features are independent, and the dataset is small and highly dimensional, such as land use datasets. In this experiment, NB was used to classify land use into urban and non-urban classes. The training data, test data, and validation data were extracted from the land use data. The training and test datasets were used to train and evaluate the NB; while the validation data was used to validate the CA prediction. The NB probabilities, transition probabilities from the MC model, neighbourhood interaction, and transition rule from the CA model were combined to determine the evolution of each cell in the prediction. Land use drivers were derived from Landsat-5 Thematic Mapper (TM, 1984), Landsat-7 Enhanced Thematic Mapper Plus (ETM+, 2000), and Landsat-8 Operational Land Imager/Thermal Infrared Sensor (OLI/TIRS, 2020) imageries. title: Design of Fibril-Forming and Cell-Adhesive Peptides Conjugated with Non-Natural Functional Groups Based on Molecular Descriptors
abstract: Abstract We developed a molecular descriptor-based strategy for designing fibril-forming and cell-adhesive peptides conjugated with non-natural functional groups for biomaterial applications. Twenty-one peptides were prepared by introducing one of the 20 standard amino acids at the N-terminus of the fibril-forming core sequence NFGAIL. Their fibril-forming properties were evaluated by thioflavin T fluorescence, circular dichroism, and ζ-potential measurements. Principal component analysis (PCA) classified the peptides according to their fibril-forming characteristics, and correlation analysis identified the molecular descriptors PCD and IC1 as parameters associated with fibril formation. Cell adhesion assays revealed regions in the PCA distribution associated with enhanced cell adhesion. Based on these relationships, peptides conjugated with non-natural functional groups that were not included in the original peptide library were designed and experimentally evaluated. Several designed peptides exhibited enhanced cell adhesion while retaining fibril-forming properties. In particular, a peptide conjugated with acridine carboxylic acid showed cell adhesion 9-fold higher than that of IAPP(22–27) and 1.7-fold higher than that of gelatin after purification. These results demonstrate that molecular descriptors extracted from a limited experimental peptide dataset enable the rational d…

title: Computational Design of a Molecular Pulley for Nanoscale Force Transmission
abstract: Abstract Molecular machines are promising tools for precision nanomachining because they can deform structures at the nanoscale without chemical damage. However, a clear engineering design framework has not yet been established. Practical use requires proper material selection, confirmation of physical feasibility based on molecular interactions, and realistic design guidance. Here, we examine cyclodextrins threaded on flexible hydrogel polymers that act as both sliders and rotational joints while attaching to each other and to surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations show that this system can operate as a molecular pulley and allow for the evaluation of different scalable geometries and their performance. We demonstrate that pulley mechanisms, such as force direction change and force amplification, can be used to control the elastic deformation of nanopatterned solids.

Exploring Microbial Biotransformation of Electro-Homoeopathic Plant Constituents and Its Relevance to Diabetes Mellitus
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a complex metabolic condition characterized by insulin resistance, β-cell dysfunction and chronic inflammation and host–microbial interactions. Plant preparations are composed of several phytochemicals that are known to have a wide range of biological effects and bioavailability in the gut, which could significantly be influenced by the gut microbiota. Microorganisms in the intestine have the enzymic capacity to break, hydrogenate, reduce, dehydroxylate, and hydrolyse natural substances, producing metabolites with different characteristics than their parent substances. Electro-Homoeopathy is a system of botanical medicine that uses plant essences in complex medicines, but so far, there is not much information about the microbial biotransformation of the plant matter components of these medicines. A perspective review of potential relationships between microbial degradation of components of Electro-Homeo plants and mechanisms related to diabetes, focusing on the case of Hydrastis canadensis and the component berberine. Conversion of berberine to dihydroberberine by the intestinal bacteria offers a mechanistic rationale. Phenolic compounds, polyphenols, microbial metabolites, short-chain fatty acids, bile acid signalling, intestinal barrier function, inflammation and insulin sensitivity are also taken into account in the review. title: Halotolerant PGPR Enhances Growth and Floral Performance of Rosa chinensis Under Saline Stress
abstract: Roses are susceptible to salinity stress, which has a substantial impact on their growth and the visual quality of their flowers. The growth and visual quality of ornamental plants are closely associated with their ability to tolerate abiotic stressors. In recent years, the use of plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) has emerged as a potential strategy for improving the growth and quality of ornamental plants in stressful environments. Therefore, the present study was conducted to identify commercially available PGPR species that could be used to develop salt stress tolerance in ‘Surkha’ roses for commercial production. We evaluated three salinity levels (3, 5 and 7 dS m⁻¹ NaCl), applied alone or in combination with one of two PGPR genera. Compared with the corresponding non-inoculated treatments at the same salinity, inoculation with Bacillus spp. at 3 dS m⁻¹ produced a significant increase in leaf area and numerical improvements in several other growth and floral traits; effects of Pseudomonas spp. and of both genera at higher salinity levels were generally small and non-significant. The non-saline control generally showed the highest values for most traits. abstract: The development of Generative Artificial Intelligence has facilitated the creation and modification of digital visual works, including Virtual YouTuber character designs. This convenience raises legal issues when character designs resulting from the creativity of creators are used, imitated, modified, or commercially exploited without authorization. This study aims to analyze the forms of legal protection available to Virtual YouTuber character designers against commercial exploitation based on Generative Artificial Intelligence and to examine the application of Intellectual Property Rights regulations to such issues. This research employs normative legal research using a statutory approach and a conceptual approach. The legal materials consist of primary, secondary, and tertiary legal materials, which are analyzed qualitatively through library research. The results indicate that Virtual YouTuber character designs that fulfill the requirements of copyrightable works are protected by copyright, including moral and economic rights, and their commercial utilization requires the authorization of the creator or rights holder. The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence to produce works by taking or reproducing expressive elements from protected character designs may constitute a copyright infringement, particularly when such works are commercially exploited without authorization. …

title: Food Sovereignty in an Age of Geopolitical Fragmentation: Corporate Power, Global Supply-Chain Vulnerabilities, and the Reconfiguration of Indonesia’s National Food Politics
abstract: Global food politics connects agrifood production and consumption to geopolitical conflict, corporate concentration, trade governance, climate instability, and contested claims over food sovereignty. This qualitative literature review examines how those transnational forces influence Indonesia’s national food-policy orientation, especially its renewed emphasis on domestic production, public reserves, postharvest infrastructure, price stabilization, and village cooperatives. Drawing interpretively on peer-reviewed journal literature published during 2020–2026 and triangulating policy claims against official Indonesian regulations, the review identifies seven interconnected arenas of power: knowledge and seed technologies; agricultural inputs; trade and logistics; finance and corporate organization; rule-setting; narratives and information; and land, procurement, and territorial distribution. Findings indicate that external shocks expose real vulnerabilities, but neither autarky nor indiscriminate import liberalization provides a sufficient response. Indonesia’s institutional challenge is to combine domestic productive capacity with diversified external sourcing, accessible nutritious diets, protected smallholder livelihoods, accountable reserves, ecological safeguards, and meaningful local participation. The review develops a conditional-sovereignty framework that treats autonom…

Evaluasi Kinerja dan Keandalan Operasional Rectifier pada Catu Daya Telekomunikasi (Performance Evaluation and Operational Reliability of Rectifiers in Telecommunication Power Supply Systems)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the electrical performance of a rectifier system in a telecommunication power supply and analyse power supply continuity during module failures. Voltage, current, and output power were measured over seven days at four load points, while failure records were reviewed based on six months of operational history. The results show that the output voltage ranged from 54.04 to 55.13 V, with total output power ranging from 28.03 to 29.62 kW and averaging 28.91 kW. The summed current across the four load points ranged from 510.04 to 542.93 A. Compared with the reference rating of 3,600 A, this represents 14.17–15.08%; however, interpretation of the loading level requires verification of the actual system configuration. Operational records show one rectifier module failure with a reported handling time of 72 hours, without interruption of the power supply because the other modules continued supporting the load. These findings indicate relatively stable electrical output and power supply continuity during the recorded module failure. However, quantitative reliability assessment requires additional data on the number of active modules, operating hours, and total system downtime.

title: A Quasi-Experimental Study to Assess the Effectiveness of a Virtual Reality Distraction Technique on Reducing Pain During Painful Procedures Among Children in a Selected Hospital
abstract: Pain during procedures is a common and distressing experience for hospitalised children. Repeated needle procedures, venepuncture, intravenous cannulation, injections, wound care and other brief interventions may produce fear, anticipatory anxiety and behavioural distress, which can make cooperation more difficult. Virtual reality (VR) distraction uses an immersive digital environment to direct attention away from the procedure and may reduce the amount of attention available for pain processing. This review examines the theoretical basis, clinical use and research evidence for VR distraction in children undergoing painful procedures and presents a practical quasi-experimental framework for assessing its effectiveness in a selected hospital. Evidence from randomised and quasi-experimental studies suggests that immersive distraction can reduce self-reported pain and, in many settings, observable distress. The likely benefit is influenced by age, developmental level, previous procedural experiences, type and duration of procedure, headset acceptability, content preference and the quality of usual care. A proposed study can compare pain scores in an experimental group receiving age-appropriate VR distraction plus routine care with a comparison group receiving routine care alone. Pain should be measured using an age-appropriate validated scale, while demographic and procedural char…

title: The Digital Commons and the Infrastructural Power of Generative AI
abstract: Abstract The use and construction of generative AI reshape how information flows in society and who controls it. This paper investigates these changes and assesses their potential repercussions for the future of our shared information infrastructure. The findings elucidate an emergent social dilemma in which the use and construction of generative AI tend to degrade and compete with our existing infrastructure, while also layering atop the commons new infrastructure that is, by its current design, centralised and mediated. Yet, alternative futures that preserve the collective nature of our infrastructure remain possible. As a first step toward such futures, this paper concludes by exploring interventions to promote a decentralised and unmediated generative commons.

title: Far-red light can power biological nitrogen fixation in cyanobacteria
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen fixation is one of the most energetically expensive biological reactions shaping the biosphere. Here, we demonstrate that some heterocyst-forming cyanobacteria can perform this process solely with low-energy far-red light, after undergoing a light acclimation response known as far-red light photoacclimation (FaRLiP). Although FaRLiP has been shown to drive oxygenic photosynthesis beyond the visible spectrum in some cyanobacteria from shaded terrestrial habitats, it was unknown whether it could also support growth in nitrogen-poor environments. In this study, we focused on heterocyst-forming, nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria carrying FaRLiP genes from various habitats. Based on transcription, protein, and enzymatic activity assays, we demonstrate that FaRLiP does support growth in the absence of combined nitrogen sources. This includes a strain lacking far-red Photosystem II, though it was energy-limited and required additional sugar input. Bioinformatic analyses revealed that this reduced FaRLiP gene cluster variant is transcribed in nitrogen-fixing symbiotic cyanobacteria in natural environments. Together, these results indicate that nitrogen fixation can be powered by low-energy photons, likely facilitating cyanobacterial growth in resource-limited microbial mats as well as shaded symbiotic environments. The Effect of Balance Funds and Regional Original Revenue on Regional Financial Performance through Capital Expenditure in Medan City
abstract: Regional autonomy demands local fiscal independence, where Local Own-Source Revenue (PAD) and Balancing Funds are expected to drive Regional Financial Performance, with Capital Expenditure as a mediator. This study aims to analyze the direct and indirect effects of Balancing Funds and PAD on Regional Financial Performance through Capital Expenditure in Medan City. This explanatory quantitative research uses Medan City Government time series data from 2007-2024. The path analysis method was applied using EViews software. The results reveal that PAD positively and significantly affects Capital Expenditure and Financial Performance. Conversely, Balancing Funds have a negative and significant effect on Financial Performance and an insignificant effect on Capital Expenditure. Capital Expenditure positively affects Financial Performance but fails to mediate the relationship between the two independent variables and Financial Performance. In conclusion, fiscal independence through PAD is the primary lever for financial performance, while reliance on central transfers potentially weakens it.

title: The Effectiveness of Problem-Based Learning in Enhancing ‎Science Literacy ‎Skills and Conceptual Understanding in Science and ‎Social Studies among ‎Sixth-Grade Elementary School Students ‎
abstract: Problem-based learning (PBL) is frequently proposed to strengthen scientific literacy and conceptual understanding, but small school-based comparisons require careful interpretation. This study describes a non-equivalent-group, pretest–posttest comparison involving 38 sixth-grade students from two public elementary schools in Bogorejo, Blora, Indonesia. Nineteen students in one school received PBL-oriented instruction and 19 students in another school received conventional instruction. The revised analysis uses aggregate figures available in the original report; individual-level records and the original statistical output were unavailable for verification. Reported posttest means were higher in the PBL-school group than in the comparison-school group for scientific literacy (78.16 vs. 62.37) and conceptual understanding (80.00 vs. 64.21), with a descriptive difference of 15.79 points for each outcome. The source report also listed normalized gains of 0.709 vs. 0.490 and 0.727 vs. 0.516, respectively; these gains could not be reproduced without individual data and a documented calculation procedure. Because the original inferential tables do not validly establish an independent between-school effect, statistical significance is not asserted in this revision. The observed pattern is compatible with the pedagogical rationale for PBL but cannot isolate an intervention effect from s…

title: Predicting awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed among women in Ethiopia using explainable machine learning
abstract: Abstract Access to safe abortion care remains a significant public health concern in low- and middle-income countries, where unsafe abortion contributes substantially to maternal morbidity and mortality. In Ethiopia, although abortion is legally permitted under specific circumstances and facility-based abortion services are available, awareness of where these services can be accessed remains limited. Evidence on predictors of such awareness remains scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to predict women’s awareness of where facility-based abortion services can be accessed in the community and identify its key predictors using nationally representative data. Data from 8,894 women participating in the 2019 Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Ethiopia survey were analyzed. The data were stratified into development (80%) and independent test (20%) sets. Within each training fold, imputation, categorical encoding, Boruta feature selection, and SMOTENC were performed before model fitting to minimize information leakage. Eight supervised machine learning algorithms were developed and compared using repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation with five repeats. Grid-search hyperparameter tuning was performed for the selected model using the development data. The final model was refitted on the full development set and evaluated on the independent test set using ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, balan…

With continuous observations and actions the continuation alphabet is infinite and the G-test is undefined. We extend quotient learning to 𝒪 × 𝒜 ⊆ ℝ^(d). Histories are keyed by coarse quantile bins; for every pair of bins the continuation laws are compared with a kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) permutation test on raw continuation vectors under Benjamini–Hochberg control, and bins whose test does not reject are merged by union–find. We (i) identify the estimator’s target—the bin-level continuation quotient—and give conditions under which it coincides with the latent quotient of index n; (ii) prove an alphabet-free trajectory bound N = O (Blog (B/δ)/ε_(MMD)² + B²log (1/δ)) for an analysed variant (T) with one window per trajectory, in which the alphabet size |𝒞| of the finite bound is replaced by the MMD separation ε_(MMD); and (iii) characterise finite-sample behaviour as a resolution effect: distinctions below the test’s detection scale are merged, so the returned size depends on the bin count B and the sample budget. title: Enhancing AI Feedback Systems: Lessons Learned from a RAG Implementation Study
abstract: This study investigates the impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on graduate students' perceptions of AI-generated feedback in a cyber-social learning environment. Using a non-equivalent cohort comparison quasi-experimental design, the research compared survey responses from Fall 2023 (n=96) and Spring 2024 (n=86) before and after implementing RAG. Participants engaged in iterative project cycles involving AI feedback, peer reviews, and instructor evaluations. Results revealed significant improvements in perceived feedback quality (p < .001, d = 0.41) and usefulness (p < .001, d = 0.51) following RAG implementation, while perceptions of actionability remained unchanged (p = .68, d = -0.05). Hierarchical regression analyses identified educational level as a positive predictor of quality and usefulness perceptions, whereas age and location negatively predicted actionability, and educational level positively predicted it. These findings suggest that RAG enhances the contextual relevance and perceived value of AI-generated feedback, particularly for advanced students. However, the lack of improvement in actionability highlights a persistent challenge in AI feedback systems. The study recommends integrating RAG with human support and developing targeted interventions to improve feedback literacy and implementation, especially for less advanced students and older learners.

title: Real-time cognitive load estimation from language in interactive learning environments
abstract: Abstract Cognitive load is a foundational construct in learning. Yet, most adaptive educational systems continue to depend on behavioral traces or physiological instrumentation to infer learners’ mental effort, limiting their scalability and ecological validity in open-ended learning contexts. This paper introduces a language-based framework for turn-level, real-time, and non-invasive cognitive load regulation in interactive learning environments. We present the Cognitive Load Estimate from Language (CLEL). This metric synthesizes eight linguistically grounded indicators into a unified estimate of cognitive load derived directly from learners’ written explanations. Building on this metric, we develop the Cognitive Load-Adaptive Multi-Agent Tutor (CLAMAT), a multi-agent instructional architecture in which specialized LLM-based agents coordinate adaptively through a cognitive-load-aware orchestration mechanism. Empirical evaluation with undergraduate learners performing explanatory tasks shows a strong association between CLEL and self-reported mental effort. Teacher evaluations favour CLAMAT feedback in clarity, helpfulness, and perceived adaptivity. Students also show an overall pre–post score improvement after receiving feedback from both systems, although the design does not isolate their respective contributions to learning. These findings demonstrate the promise of language…

PENERAPAN MODEL PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN NUMERASI MURID PADA PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA MATERI SATUAN PANJANG DAN BERAT KELAS III SD
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid melalui penggunaan Problem Based Learning (PBL) dalam materi satuan panjang dan berat pada pelajaran Matematika kelas III sekolah dasar. Penelitian ini dilakukan dengan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilakukan selama dua siklus dengan murid berjumlah 30. Setiap siklus memiliki alur pembelajaran yang sama yaitu perencanaan, aksi, pengamatan, dan refleksi. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes, observasi, dan dokumentasi selama pembelajaran. Hasil penelitian yang didapat memperlihatkan terdapat perkembangan hasil penilaian murid siklus I senilai 2.331 dari maksimal skor 3.240 atau 71,94% berkategori cukup, yang berkembang pada siklus II yaitu senilai 2.694 atau 83,15% berkategori baik. Nilai rata-rata pada aspek kognitif berkembang dari 72,67 menjadi 83,33. Perkembangan aspek-aspek yang dinilai dalam penelitian ini mengungkapkan bahwa penggunaan model pembelajaran PBL dapat memberikan hasil yang baik dalam pembelajaran Matematika materi satuan panjang dan berat. Model PBL dinilai mampu menjadi solusi bagi murid dalam mencerna konsep matematika, menyelesaikan masalah sehari-hari, diskusi, dan masalah kontekstual lainnya. Maka dari itu, PBL dinilai memiliki potensi dalam meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid sekolah dasar.
