Islands in the Machine: A Systematic Geographic Assessment of Insular Territories in Video Games
abstract: Islands occupy a privileged position in human imagination and in the geography of the real world. As circumscribed, ecologically distinct, and often isolated territories, they concentrate geographic diversity into bounded spaces that invite exploration, narrative, and control. These same qualities make islands recurrent settings in video games, where the island serves simultaneously as a spatial container, a design convenience, and a cultural signifier. Yet despite the ubiquity of island environments in interactive media, no systematic attempt has been made to assess how faithfully video games represent the specific geographic properties that define insular territories. This paper presents the first comprehensive geographic analysis of island representation in video games. Drawing on a catalogue of 125 titles spanning multiple genres, platforms and release decades, a seven-block variable framework is developed, covering insularity, geomorphology, climate, hydrography, biogeography, human elements, and spatial scale, and computing an Island Geographic Fidelity Index (IGFI) for each title. Restricting the main analysis to 96 genuinely insular games and using 28 continental titles as a comparative reference, a mean IGFI of 42.2 (SD = 10.8) is found on a 0–100 scale, with Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 serving as a benchmark reference at 98.8. Results show that insularity recognit…

title: Discrimination of ranges of closely related RNA targets using CRISPR-based detection assay developed using machine learning-based optimization
abstract: Abstract Early detection and identification of pathogen strains are crucial for mitigating infectious disease threats, including those posed by closely related zoonotic variants. A key limitation of current molecular detection approaches is their narrow focus on individual targets, which can delay recognition of outbreaks caused by closely related but non-identical pathogens. Here we report a two-channel CRISPR/Cas13a detection assay capable of discriminating between SARS-CoV-2 and a panel of twelve closely related zoonotic sarbecoviruses using a compact duplex assay format. Guide RNA sets with tunable specificity were designed using a two-stage machine learning pipeline: initial candidate filtering with a pre-existing RuleFit model, followed by retraining on 382 sarbecovirus-specific in vitro data points to refine the mismatch threshold from 4 to 6 mismatches for target exclusion. The optimized assay achieved proof-of-concept three-way classification of synthetic RNA targets into: (1) SARS-CoV-2, (2) the closest known near-neighbor BANAL-236, and (3) remaining zoonotic near-neighbors, with a limit of detection of 15–150 fM for synthetic RNA targets. This approach provides a practical framework for surveillance-oriented detection that identifies not only a specific pathogen but also its closest relatives, provided that system-specific validation and model retraining are include…

title: Improvement in phase-C students’ writing skills of pantun following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a deep learning approach
abstract: This study examined changes in Phase-C elementary school students’ pantun writing skills following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a Deep Learning approach. The study employed a quantitative approach using a one-group pretest–posttest design involving 30 fifth-grade students at Al Kautsar Islamic Elementary School in Krian, Sidoarjo. Data were collected through pantun writing assessments, classroom observations, and documentation. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk test, a paired-sample t-test, and N-Gain analysis. The findings showed an increase in the mean pantun writing score from 68.40 on the pretest to 84.70 on the posttest, representing a mean improvement of 16.30 points. The paired-sample t-test indicated a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (p < .001), while the N-Gain score of 0.52 indicated moderate improvement. These findings suggest that students’ pantun writing skills improved following the implementation of differentiated instruction within a Deep Learning approach. However, because the study did not involve a comparison group, the observed improvement cannot be attributed exclusively to the instructional intervention. The findings provide preliminary empirical evidence regarding the implementation of differentiated instruction in pantun writing instruction.

Data were collected through in-depth interviews with four beneficiaries and institutional documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing based on five effectiveness indicators: program understanding, target accuracy, timeliness, goal achievement, and monitoring. Results: BPW Ar Risalah is effective as a benefit distributor (distributive effectiveness): targeting is perceived as accurate, distribution is generally on time with one compensated delay, and monitoring is conducted periodically according to the type of beneficiary. Social assistance of IDR 500,000 per month, scholarships of IDR 1,500,000 per semester, and income of IDR 1,500,000 per month contribute to meeting living needs, education, and income stability, with job creation as the most transformative benefit. However, transformative effectiveness cannot yet be fully concluded: beneficiaries' understanding of the concept and mechanism of productive waqf remains limited, the benefit amounts are supplementary, and monitoring does not yet measure impact. abstract: Abstract Investment decision-making is a challenging problem in financial engineering, particularly when investors are presented with multiple investment options. The decision paths become more complex in the space of digital assets, where investors are faced with a huge number of assets to select from, before even deriving optimal allocations. Within virtual space, the market for cryptocurrencies is gaining traction among investors, especially due to its potential for substantial returns and diversification. However, the market for cryptocurrencies presents unique challenges due to its inherent volatility and uncertainty, underscoring the need for a robust and structured investment framework to guide decision-making. Noting this gap in the literature on cryptocurrency investment, we introduce an innovative two-phase framework for cryptocurrency portfolio construction, designed to address the complexities and uncertainties inherent in cryptocurrency markets. In a two-phased analysis, we start with a Robust Ratio Data Envelopment Analysis (RR-DEA) to screen and preselect the most efficient cryptocurrencies from a pool of available assets, followed by the application of a Robust Goal Programming (RGP) optimization procedure to allocate weights based on the investor’s risk preferences, return targets, and other relevant financial goals. title: OPTIMIZATION OF BATH TEMPERATURE FOR ELECTRODEPOSITED NiFeWMoMn HIGH-ENTROPY ALLOY THIN FILMS
abstract: In this study, NiFeWMoMn high-entropy alloy thin films were successfully synthesized using the electrodeposition method by varying the bath temperature. The structural, morphological, corrosion, magnetic, and compositional properties were systematically investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), electrochemical tests, and Vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM). XRD analysis confirmed the formation of a solid solution with a refined crystalline structure, showing the smallest crystallite size and lower dislocation density at 75 ∘ C. FESEM images revealed uniform and dense surface morphology at this temperature, while EDS confirmed the presence of all intended elements with a more balanced atomic distribution. Electrochemical corrosion studies showed that the sample coated at 75 ∘ C exhibited the lowest corrosion rate and the highest polarization resistance, indicating superior corrosion resistance. Magnetic measurements showed that coercivity increased with temperature 75 ∘ C was identified as the most favorable temperature for achieving a uniform coating, improved corrosion resistance, controlled magnetic behavior, and enhanced structural properties.

Integrated population genomics and phenotypic analyses reveal geographic structure and signatures of recent positive-selection underlying insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis from The Gambia, West Africa
abstract: Abstract Insecticide resistance in malaria vectors is spreading, with newly identified resistance markers raising operational challenges and threatening malaria reduction. Anopheles arabiensis is an important vector in The Gambia; however, the molecular basis of its insecticide resistance remains poorly understood. We observed signals of population structure between coastal and inland An. arabiensis populations in The Gambia, indicating restricted gene flow likely influenced by environmental variation. Pyrethroid and DDT resistance were widespread. However, the prevalence of both phenotypic and genetic insecticide resistance differed between coastal and inland populations. For instance, the Vgsc-L995S and Vgsc-L995F substitutions conferring pyrethroid and DDT resistance were more frequent in coastal populations and were associated with markedly higher phenotypic resistance to these insecticides. We also identified increased frequencies of copy number variation at Cytochrome P450 (Cyp6aa/p, Cyp9k1) and carboxylesterase (Coeae2-7 g) metabolic resistance markers in coastal An. arabiensis. Some observed gene amplifications were unique to Gambian coastal populations, suggesting their independent evolution. title: HierWoodNet: HierStyle multi-scale semantic style transfer method for Chinese woodblock painting
abstract: Abstract Woodblock painting, a traditional Chinese intangible cultural heritage, is known for its vivid colors and distinctive textures. However, modern lifestyles and declining cultural inheritance have led to risks of style loss and discontinuity. AI-based image style transfer offers a promising avenue for preserving and creating woodblock art. However, existing methods struggle with semantic feature extraction, style consistency, and color modeling in this domain. To address these challenges, we propose a hierarchical woodblock style transfer network. Our approach introduces a Content-Aware Positional Encoder based on the Transformer architecture, which enhances multi-scale feature representation and global structural perception. This helps preserve content during style transfer. We further present a HierStyle Encoder that learns rich, hierarchical style features from data, enabling fine-grained control over the transfer process and improving semantic and textural coherence. A progressive decoder integrates multi-stage upsampling with cross-layer connections to preserve semantic structure while injecting detailed style features. Finally, the ChromaNova Color Decoder dynamically optimizes color representation through a multi-dimensional color loss function that considers both color contrast and distribution differences. Quantitative experiments show that our method achieves t…

title: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole
abstract: Abstract Background The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged ‘lake’ at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). To determine how the microbiome within the submerged acid lake adapted to these unique conditions, we collected 59 coupled samples of size-filtered (0.22 µm) planktonic microbes for shotgun metagenomics and solid-phase extracted dissolved organic matter for untargeted metabolomics from 21 stations at depths ranging from 2 to 600 m during a 10-day research cruise in December 2019. Results We identified a distinct microbial community within the submerged acid lake different from the non-acidic sinkholes, with increased abundances of Nitrospinota , Thermoproteota , Planctomycetota , and Actinobacteriota . We also found three enriched classes of dissolved compounds within the submerged acid lake: (1) large, (2) low-polarity, and (3) halogenated metabolites, including iodides and halobenzoic acids. abstract: Pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat melalui pelayanan gereja membutuhkan pengelolaan yang terarah dan berkelanjutan, bukan hanya penyediaan bantuan dan fasilitas usaha. Penelitian terdahulu telah membahas pemberdayaan ekonomi melalui pengembangan potensi lokal, bantuan modal, pelatihan, dan pemanfaatan aset gereja. Namun, kajian yang mengintegrasikan fungsi pengelolaan program ekonomi berbasis pasar dengan faktor pendukung, penghambat, dan dampaknya terhadap pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengelolaan Pasar Obor, mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat, serta menganalisis dampaknya terhadap pemberdayaan ekonomi jemaat di GKI Ekklesia Klasaman, Kota Sorong, Papua Barat Daya. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan pemilihan informan secara purposif. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengelolaan telah mencakup fungsi perencanaan, pengorganisasian, penggerakan, dan pengawasan, tetapi belum terintegrasi secara optimal karena keterbatasan pedoman operasional, pendampingan usaha, dan evaluasi perkembangan peserta. Crop Load Management of Plums Using 1-Aminocyclopropane Carboxylic Acid (1-ACC)
abstract: Excessive fruit set in European (Prunus domestica L.) and Japanese (Prunus salicina L.) plum trees necessitates thinning to optimize crop load, enhance fruit quality, and reduce manual hand thinning. This study evaluated the efficacy of the ethylene precursor 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (1-ACC) as a chemical thinning agent for the European plum cultivar ‘Vibrant’ and the Japanese plum cultivar ‘Early Golden’. Treatments were applied at full bloom (FB) and at the fruitlet stage (8-10 mm diameter) using 1-ACC concentrations of 150, 300, and 450 mg·L⁻¹. Horticultural measurements included crop load, yield, fruit size distribution, fruit quality, phytotoxic effects, and crop value. Applications of 1-ACC effectively reduced crop load, with FB applications producing greater thinning responses than fruitlet-stage applications. Increasing application rates resulted in decreased yield and crop value, while average fruit weight increased. No hand thinning was required in both years of the study due to poor pollination in the ‘Early Golden’ orchard and atypical fruit drop unrelated to 1-ACC treatments following early fruit development in the ‘Vibrant’ orchard; therefore, commercial thinning was not required. Thinning responses varied by cultivar and application timing, underscoring the importance of cultivar-specific thinning strategies. Ethylene evolution following 1-ACC applic…

title: Relationship Between Perceived Stress and Student Incivility Among College Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Student incivility has become an increasing concern in higher education because of its adverse effects on classroom climate, teaching effectiveness, and students' academic experiences. Psychological stress has been recognised as a potential factor influencing uncivil behaviour. This study evaluated the relationship between perceived stress and student incivility among college students and investigated whether perceived stress significantly predicts student incivility. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was followed, and data were collected from 219 college students using structured questionnaires measuring perceived stress and student incivility. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson's correlation, and simple linear regression were performed using Jamovi. A statistically significant positive relationship was identified between perceived stress and student incivility. Regression analysis showed that perceived stress significantly predicted student incivility, although it explained only 4% of the variance in uncivil behaviour. Significant gender differences were observed in both perceived stress and student incivility. Rather than presuming an automatic, uniform progression from student stress to behavioural misconduct, this study provides a nuanced, methodologically transparent evaluation that underscores the sensitivity of stress–incivility dynamics…

title: The Monitoring Paradox: Why Oversight Mechanisms Fail to Predict PPP Infrastructure Projects Performance in Kenya
abstract: Purpose: The study explored role of project monitoring mechanisms in enhancing performance of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects in Kenya. Policy puts a lot of emphasis on the need for monitoring along the project lifecycle; however, many PPP projects continue to display inefficiencies pointing towards weak monitoring systems. Materials and Methods: Data were collected from 252 respondents representing government agencies, private consortia, and project management units across 103 PPP projects. Regression analysis was used to test relationship between project monitoring mechanisms and project performance. Findings: Project monitoring had a statistically significant but weak positive influence on project performance (β = .014, p < .005). The positive but not so profound effect suggests that the monitoring frameworks that exists are largely compliance-oriented rather than the one that drives performance in the project environment. Implications to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study recommends institutionalizing real-time monitoring, feedback systems, and adoption of digital data tools to strengthen accountability within PPP infrastructure projects in Kenya. To anchor these measures, the Public Private Partnerships Act, 2021 and the regulations around privately funded public infrastructure should be amended to create a performance-based monitoring making i…

Hemodynamic effects of cycle ergometry versus dynamic unilateral arm exercise during right heart catheterization: a prospective observational study
abstract: Abstract Background The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC). Methods 50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient’s physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise. title: The Effect of Financial Literacy and Financial Planning on the Financial Control Ability of MSMEs
abstract: Financial control is a critical managerial function for MSME sustainability because it enables owners to compare actual outcomes with plans, identify deviations, and take corrective action. This study examines the associations of financial literacy and financial planning ability with financial control ability among MSMEs. A cross-sectional quantitative survey was conducted using purposive sampling of 91 MSME owners or managers who completed 24 five-point Likert items. Variable scores were calculated as item means and analyzed using multiple linear regression, supported by reliability assessment, residual diagnostics, and HC3 robust standard errors. Mean scores for financial literacy, financial planning, and financial control were 4.615, 3.892, and 4.369, respectively. Financial literacy (B=0.332; β=0.331; p<0.001) and financial planning (B=0.317; β=0.655; p<0.001) were positively associated with financial control. The model was significant, F(2,88)=136.829; p<0.001, with R²=75.67%. However, financial control reliability was low (α=0.424), and residuals were non-normal. The findings suggest that financial planning has a stronger standardized association with financial control than financial literacy, although interpretation should remain exploratory because of measurement-quality limitations and the observational design.

title: Addressing mental health among incarcerated individuals through financial education: evidence from prison-based programs
Financial Technology dan Inklusi Keuangan Masyarakat Pedesaan: Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis atas Manfaat, Hambatan, dan Kebijakan
abstract: Differences in financial service use between urban and rural areas suggest that the expansion of financial technology (fintech) does not necessarily lead to meaningful inclusion. This study synthesizes the roles, benefits, barriers, and policy priorities of fintech for rural communities through a systematic literature review and narrative thematic synthesis of ten core publications from 2021–2025. A reconciled selection flow reports 309 records, 102 duplicates, 95 records excluded during screening, 56 reports not retrieved, 46 reports excluded after eligibility assessment, and ten included studies. The literature suggests that digital payments and financial services may reduce geographical and transaction-cost barriers, while their effects on poverty, productivity, and welfare are highly context- and design-dependent. Most available evidence is national-level or conceptual; direct rural household-level evidence remains limited. Recurring barriers include connectivity, financial and digital literacy, trust, data security, and product suitability. The synthesis proposes a sequenced policy agenda encompassing digital infrastructure and local agents, practice-oriented literacy, context-sensitive services, consumer protection, and outcome-based evaluation. The evidence does not justify a universal numerical claim about poverty reduction.

title: Institutional Perspectives on Youth Digital Vulnerability in Lampung, Indonesia: Problematic Information, Cyber Financial Fraud, and a Community-Based Resilience Model
abstract: This study examines institutional perspectives on youth digital vulnerability in Lampung Province, Indonesia, focusing on problematic information, cyber financial fraud, and community-based prevention. Using a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected through face-to-face, semi-structured interviews with purposively selected representatives from 13 organizational units across provincial and municipal government, police, territorial defense, social resilience, and digital-governance institutions. Documented interview records were analyzed thematically and contextualized using policy and connectivity documents, alongside provincial cyber-governance evaluations covering 2022–2025. The analysis generated four themes: youth vulnerability within an unequal digital environment; problematic information and cyber financial fraud as converging risks; a layered institutional response and its implementation constraints; and a proposed community-based youth digital resilience model. Institutional informants linked youth digital vulnerability to unequal connectivity, uneven information-verification capacity, and limited digital-safety awareness. Problematic information and cyber financial fraud were described as distinct but related risks that may exploit trust, emotion, urgency, and limited verification. Institutional accounts identified complementary functions in public communi…

Tight quantum speed limit for ergotropy charging in the N -qubit Dicke battery
abstract: Abstract We derive a quantum speed limit for ergotropy charging in the N -qubit Dicke battery. With the qubits initially in their ground state and the charger in a coherent state of mean photon number n ¯ , the charging time to a target fraction ε of the maximum extractable work obeys, in the classical-field limit, Γ N τ ∗ ( ε ) ⩾ arcsin ⁡ ε , where Γ N = 2 λ n ¯ / N is a single rate combining the light–matter coupling, the charger amplitude and the system size. The bound is geometric: although the ergotropy is defined by an optimisation over unitaries, it reduces to a fixed function of the angle swept by the collective spin on the Bloch sphere, and the drive bounds the rate at which that angle can grow, so the charging time is at least the required arc divided by the maximum angular velocity. The reduction rests on an exact statement about work extraction: only the coherent component of the drive delivers extractable work, while its vacuum fluctuations deposit energy that remains locked in the passive state. This makes the short-time coefficient independent of the charger occupation, and it is what separates a bound on extractable work from a bound on stored energy, which no instantaneous-power argument can supply. title: Identifying dynamical network markers of financial market instability
abstract: Abstract Market instability has been extensively studied using mathematical approaches to characterize complex trading dynamics and detect structural change points. This study explores the potential for early detection of market instability by applying the Dynamical Network Markers (DNM) theory to order placement and execution data from the Tokyo Stock Exchange. DNM theory identifies indicators associated with critical transitions as their precursors in high-dimensional financial market systems of many interacting elements. In this study, market participants are identified using virtual server IDs from the trading system, and multivariate time series representing their trading activities are constructed. This framework treats each participant as an interacting element, thereby enabling the application of DNM theory to the obtained time series. The results indicate the presence of DNM-related patterns associated with large price movements on a daily time scale. These findings demonstrate the applicability of the DNM framework to market participant behavioral data and provide a basis for understanding mechanisms of instabilizing dynamics in financial market systems. The study could inform potential future developments of DNM-based early warning indicators through the identification of appropriate forecasting horizons and time scales as well as the incorporation of multiple aspect…

title: Detection of TeV emission during early afterglow from poorly localized gamma-ray bursts with ground-based IACTs
abstract: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most luminous and rapidly evolving transients in the Universe. While space-based instruments have extended GRB observations up to energies of ∼100 GeV, the detection of very high-energy (VHE; E>100 GeV) emission from ground-based telescopes, especially during prompt and/or the early afterglow phases, remains challenging. These difficulties arise from the rapid temporal decay of GRB afterglows, strong attenuation by the extragalactic background light, observational latency, and the typical poor sky localization provided by MeV detectors such as Fermi/GBM. In this work, we investigated the prospects for detecting TeV (∼100 GeV--1 TeV) emission from poorly localized GRBs by adopting optimized follow-up strategies based on rapid tiling of large localization regions. We simulated a realistic population of GRBs informed by more than 15 years of Fermi/GBM and Swift/XRT detections and recent progress in the afterglow emission modeling. Using these simulations, we evaluated the detectability of GRB early afterglows by the next-generation imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, which are equipped with larger fields of view, as a function of latency, exposure time, and observational strategy. Our strategy can significantly enhance the detection rate; for instruments such as ASTRI and LACT, it increases by up to a factor of two compared to strategies…

title: Deep learning models for ADITYA-U MHD equilibrium
abstract: Abstract This work presents an integrated deep learning framework for rapid magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equilibrium estimation in the ADITYA-U tokamak. A free-boundary equilibrium database containing 100,760 cases was generated using the pyIPREQ Grad–Shafranov solver from experimentally derived operating conditions spanning 766 ADITYA-U plasma discharges, with constraints representative of circular limiter plasmas near the flat-top phase. The database was used to develop a cascaded framework for predicting scalar equilibrium quantities, 1d safety factor profiles, and 2d poloidal flux profiles. Dense neural networks, principal component analysis (PCA), convolutional neural networks (CNN) and physics-informed neural networks (PINN) were investigated within this framework. The error propagation, cross-models consistency and ablation study of Grad–Shafranov residual were performed for the proposed framework. Across the test dataset, the models achieve median mean absolute errors of 1 × 10 − 2 for the safety factor profile and 2 × 10 − 3 for the normalized poloidal flux profile. The largest model requires approximately 1ms per equilibrium inference on a multi-core CPU. The results demonstrate the potential of the framework as a fast surrogate for equilibrium analysis, experiment planning and real-time plasma control applications for ADITYA-U experiments.

title: Özbekston Respublikasi misolida parranda grippi epidemiyalarining oziq-ovqat xavfsizligi va iste’mol bozoriga iqtisodiy ta’siri
abstract: This thesis provides a comprehensive analysis of the origins of Avian Influenza and the biological characteristics of the virus, as well as the adverse impacts of such an epizootic—within the context of the Republic of Uzbekistan—on the national economy, the poultry sector, and price stability in the consumer market. The study examines the economic ripple effects resulting from the spread of the disease, including the contraction of supply, inflationary pressure on market prices, and the subsequent decline in the population’s purchasing power.

title: From academic excellence to market attractiveness: explaining the transformation gap in higher education institutions
abstract: Purpose This study examines why academic performance does not necessarily translate directly into market attractiveness in higher education institutions. Drawing on capability, institutional and signaling perspectives, it frames this disconnect as a transformation gap: an explanatory condition in which internally generated academic value requires strategic and relational mechanisms to become externally recognized market value. The transformation gap is not treated as a separate latent construct. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative explanatory design was used with 300 strategic-level academic and administrative respondents in Indonesian higher education. Four reflective constructs – academic performance (AP), strategic positioning (SP), relational signaling (RS) and market attractiveness (MA) – were assessed using Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The reported evaluation includes reliability and convergent validity, heterotrait–monotrait ratio (HTMT), collinearity, R2, Q2, f2 and bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. Findings Academic performance was not significantly related to market attractiveness directly (β = 0.07, t = 1.12, p > 0.05), so H1 was not supported. Academic performance was positively related to strategic positioning (β = 0.41, t = 6.85, p < 0.001) and relational signaling (β = 0.38, t = 6.10, p < 0.001). Strategic positi…

title: HEATING CHARACTERISTICS OF A SOLAR-CO₂ AIR SOURCE HEAT PUMP COUPLED SYSTEM WITH VALLEY-ELECTRICITY HEAT STORAGE
abstract: Taking the heating system of a rural household in Yinchuan as the research object, a simulation model of a solar-CO₂ air source heat pump heating system was developed based on TRNSYS, and its operation from November to March of the following year was simulated and analyzed. The results show that the system can reliably satisfy the indoor winter heating demand of rural households, with heating temperature fluctuating little and remaining stable at approximately 18.0 ℃. Regarding the electricity consumption of the coupled system, the energy use of the space-heating pump and the heating circulation pump rises in step with the extreme-cold heat load in winter, showing a pronounced negative correlation with outdoor temperature; in contrast, the energy consumption of the solar collector pump is governed solely by solar irradiation and remains stable throughout the entire heating season. Over the whole heating season, the collector harvested 6,276.26 kWh of heat and the air source heat pump delivered 6,359.19 kWh, the two contributions being nearly equal, with the total heat output of the heat pump slightly exceeding that of the solar collector. The carbon emissions of the solar-coupled heat pump heating system are only 1,433.94 kgCO₂, equivalent to 24.5% of those of a coal-fired boiler (the highest-emitting option), demonstrating remarkable energy-saving and emission-reduction effect…

Assessment of the alignment between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification before and after the Nutri-Score algorithm update: analysis of 450 food products from the Polish retail market
abstract: Abstract Background Nutri-Score is one of the most widely used front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FOPNL) systems in Europe. Whereas Nutri-Score assesses nutritional quality, the NOVA classification categorises foods according to the extent and purpose of processing. An updated version of the algorithm was introduced to improve alignment with current dietary recommendations and reduce favourable ratings assigned to highly and ultra-processed foods. This study aimed to assess the alignment between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification before and after the algorithm update, and to analyse changes in the classification of food products available on the Polish retail market. Methods A total of 450 food products available in Polish supermarkets and representing various food categories were analysed. Products were classified according to the Nutri-Score algorithm (before and after the 2023 update) and the NOVA classification system. A healthfulness classification based on Part B of the KomPAN questionnaire and supplementary author-defined criteria was used to assess changes in Nutri-Score ratings before and after the algorithm update across products with different healthfulness profiles. Results Agreement between Nutri-Score and the NOVA classification increased following the algorithm update (ρ = 0.571 after the update vs. ρ = 0.518 before the update). title: Nonconviction Arrests and Labor Market Trajectories
abstract: Abstract In this Article, I examine whether nonconviction arrests—one of the least severe forms of formal criminal justice contact—destabilize labor market trajectories. Using longitudinal data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997 (NLSY97) and individual fixed-effects models, I isolate the relationship between nonconviction arrests and labor market outcomes among adult men. I find that a nonconviction arrest is associated with a 7.5% point increase in the likelihood of employment disruption in the following survey period. In the longer term, nonconviction arrests are associated with hourly wages that are approximately 10.5% lower and significant reductions in access to employer-provided health insurance (5.1% points) and retirement benefits (8.7% points). Reduced access to benefits appears to be related to lower rates of full-time employment. Given Black men’s disproportionate exposure to nonconviction arrest, these findings suggest that arrest practices may contribute to racial disparities in labor market outcomes.

title: Under the “Light Wellness” Consumer Trend—A Study on Consumer Purchase Intentions and Market Expansion Strategies for Functional Snacks
abstract: This study examines consumer purchase intentions and market expansion strategies for functional snacks within the “light wellness” trend. It reviews relevant theories and the market landscape, combining questionnaire surveys with empirical analysis. Using SPSS and Stata, the study conducts reliability and validity tests, exploratory factor analysis, correlation analysis, regression analysis, and robustness tests. Findings show that perceived value—comprising functional, hedonic, symbolic, social, and conditional dimensions—positively influences purchase intention, with functional value exerting the strongest effect; health concern positively moderates this relationship, and sub-sample regressions confirm robustness. Firms should advance market expansion through product innovation, value communication, scenario building, and channel synergy.

title: FROM GENERATED INFORMATION TO INTERNATIONALIZATION KNOWLEDGE: GENERATIVE AI, ABSORPTIVE CAPACITY AND SMES’ MARKET ENTRY DECISIONS
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can reduce the cost of acquiring information about foreign markets and generating alternative strategies for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Greater information availability does not necessarily improve decision quality, however. This conceptual paper uses a narrative literature review and adopts absorptive capacity as its main theoretical perspective, alongside the Uppsala internationalization process model, to examine the role of experiential knowledge and business networks. The unit of analysis is a specific market entry decision involving a defined product, target market, and entry mode. The paper distinguishes information-processing efficiency, decision quality, and business performance. It proposes that generated content requires value recognition, evidence verification, and contextual integration to support a decision. Proportionate resource commitments and feedback from action may then support the development of reusable knowledge. These processes are connected through feedback rather than a fixed linear sequence. The strategic value of GenAI depends on the fit between the speed of information generation and organizational verification capacity, knowledge embedded in transaction relationships that is difficult to codify, and the incorporation of feedback into organizational routines. Three propositions address the re…

title: Governança de mercado nas plataformas digitais: uma análise do Código de Ética dos aplicativos de delivery
abstract: O presente trabalho objetivou analisar como o Código de Ética e Conduta do aplicativo iFood atua como mecanismo de governança no mercado de delivery por plataforma. A metodologia empregada foi a análise de conteúdo, que possibilitou construir dimensões de análise e articular a ligação entre o arcabouço teórico e o objeto empírico. Os resultados mostram a existência de estruturas de governança nas plataformas, o que questiona se elas são ferramentas para os estabelecimentos comerciais ou estruturas regulatórias. A conclusão é que os mecanismos observados impõem formas de governança, o que abre uma lacuna relevante para o aprofundamento do tema.

title: Entre o velho e o novo: sociabilidades, poder e mudanças no processo de realocação do Mercado Público de Oitizeiro, João Pessoa-PB
abstract: O presente artigo tem como objetivo analisar as transformações nas sociabilidades, nas relações de poder e nas dinâmicas sociais decorrentes do processo de realocação do Mercado Público de Oitizeiro, em João Pessoa–PB. Mais do que avaliar a eficácia administrativa da mudança, busca-se compreender os significados atribuídos por feirantes, consumidores e demais usuários ao deslocamento do mercado, entendendo-o como um evento social e histórico que impacta redes de relações, práticas cotidianas e estruturas simbólicas consolidadas ao longo de décadas. Sua metodologia é de caráter etnográfico e interpretativo, fundamentada na perspectiva da “descrição densa” de Clifford Geertz, realizada a partir de observações de campo nos dias de feira, através de conversas informais com feirantes e frequentadores, além de registrar conflitos, gestos, narrativas e mudanças nas interações sociais. O estudo dialoga com referenciais teóricos de Georg Simmel, Marshall Sahlins, Victor Turner, Max Gluckman, Eric Wolf e Fredrik Barth, articulando conceitos como sociabilidade, evento histórico, drama social, fronteiras sociais e relações de poder. E com isso, os resultados indicam que a realocação do mercado desencadeia tensões, conflitos e reconfigurações nas redes de sociabilidade, caracterizando-se como um “drama social”, nos termos de Turner. A decisão da gestão municipal, percebida como verticalizad…

title: Stock market prediction and trading strategy optimization with S4-integrated deep learning architectures: a comparative study of hybrid fusion mechanisms
abstract: Purpose The accurate prediction of stock market movements remains a challenging task due to the non-stationary, noisy and highly volatile nature of financial time series. While deep learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Transformer have demonstrated promising results, they often struggle to capture both long-term dependencies and short-term fluctuations efficiently. To address these limitations, this paper introduces al hybrid framework that integrates the Structured State Space Sequence (S4) model with three fundamental deep learning architectures via tailored fusion mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Specifically, we propose (1) LSTM-S4, a parallel architecture with attention-based fusion and skip connections; (2) MLP-S4, a serial embedding model that enables temporal modeling for MLP; and (3) Transformer-S4, a tandem structure that combines global attention with local temporal pattern extraction. Extensive experiments are conducted based on real-world data from six Chinese stocks covering diverse sectors and market conditions. Findings The results demonstrate that the S4-integrated hybrid models outperform their base counterparts and existing baseline models in terms of predictive accuracy measured by RMSE, MSE, MAE and $Rˆ2$, as well as simulated investment returns. Statistical Modeling of the Drop Strength of Cotton Fiber-Reinforced Paper Composites Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: . In the present work, a statistical model for the height to failure of cotton fiber-reinforced paper composites subjected to MIL-STD-810G 516.6 drop tests was developed using response surface methodology. The independent variables considered were the density ( ρ ) and alkali treatment time ( t ). The Minitab 22.1.0. statistical software was used for modeling and both linear and non-linear effects were considered. The effect of treatment time was mostly insignificant at the lower densities. However, the effect of variables on the response was in the order of ρ 2 > ρ > t 2 > t . The lowest response (height to failure) was observed in the low-density region (< 0.10 g/cm³), likely due to insufficient material available to accommodate the stress. However, the maximum response was observed at the extended alkali treatment time (4.5 hr. < t < 6.3 hr.) and higher fiber density (0.25 g/cm 3 < ρ < 0.27 g/cm 3 ). The density dominated over the treatment time for the response output. Furthermore, increasing treatment time enhances the response up to a certain point. Once the optimum response was achieved, the response began to decrease slightly with further increases in either density or treatment time. The misalignment and failure of the reinforcement, followed by matrix fracture, were the primary failure mechanisms for composites under the drop test.

Bridging the gap between teacher supply and demand in Indonesia: insights from the government contract-based teacher recruitment policy
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the root causes of Indonesia's teacher distribution crisis, examining the upstream-downstream paradox where a surplus of education graduates coexists with critical teacher shortages in public schools. Design/methodology/approach Employing a Multi-Level Governance (MLG) framework, this qualitative case study analyzes data from 21 key stakeholders, including central and local government officials, university lecturers and teachers. The primary interview data are reinforced by secondary data triangulation from 2021–2024 national recruitment records. Findings The analysis reveals that the shortage is not a supply issue but the result of specific “governance gaps.” These include Fiscal Gaps (local reluctance to hire due to regional allowance costs), Objective Gaps (political patronage), Accountability Gaps (phantom vacancies) and Policy Gaps (fragmented silos). Stakeholders perceive current collaborative efforts as “merely ceremonial” rather than substantive. Research limitations/implications The primary policy focus is 2021–2024, while supply-demand trend analysis draws on national data from 2012 onwards. Long-term policy dynamics may still evolve. Non-state actors in teacher governance were beyond the scope and remain an opportunity for further research. Practical implications The study proposes a “Hybrid Recruitment Governance” model with a split-c…

title: HLA-DQB1 REFLECTS AN ANTIGEN-PRESENTATION-ASSOCIATED IMMUNE MICROENVIRONMENT IN BLADDER CANCER AND SHOWS RESPONSE-RELATED SIGNALS IN AN ATEZOLIZUMAB-TREATED COHORT
abstract: Bladder cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy with variable immune infiltration and limited response rates to immune checkpoint blockade. HLA-DQB1, a major histocompatibility complex class II gene involved in antigen presentation, may participate in tumor immune regulation. However, its expression pattern, prognostic relevance, immune microenvironmental associations, and immunotherapy-related significance in bladder cancer remain incompletely characterized. Transcriptomic and clinical data of bladder cancer were obtained from TCGA-BLCA. HLA-DQB1 expression was compared between tumor and normal tissues, and its association with overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier and Cox regression analyses. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis was used to estimate immune-cell infiltration. Correlations between HLA-DQB1 and immune checkpoints, antigen-presentation genes, and immune-related modules were assessed using Spearman correlation analysis. Differential expression analysis between HLA-DQB1-high and HLA-DQB1-low tumors was performed using limma, followed by GO and Hallmark GSEA. External validation was conducted using GSE13507. Immunotherapy-related analyses were further performed in the IMvigor210 atezolizumab-treated urothelial carcinoma cohort. Mesenchymal Stromal Cell Therapy for Acute Graft-Versus-Host Disease: Timing, Disease Context, and Biomarkers as Determinants of Clinical Response
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is a therapy for hematological malignancies and inherited disorders. However, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have emerged as a cellular therapy because of their immunomodulatory and tissue-repair properties, although clinical responses have been inconsistent. This review examines evidence supporting MSC use for GVHD, focusing on treatment timing, disease stage and severity, patient characteristics, MSC product properties, and biomarkers predicting response. Recent Findings MSCs modulate innate and adaptive immunity, including T cells, B cells, natural killer cells, dendritic cells, and macrophages, through paracrine mediators, extracellular vesicles, and cell-cell interactions. Clinical studies have reported activity in GVHD prophylaxis and treatment, particularly in selected patients with steroid-refractory acute GVHD (SR-aGVHD), whereas randomized studies have not consistently demonstrated benefit across unselected populations. The clinical development of remestemcel-L provided important translational evidence, culminating in FDA approval of remestemcel-L-rknd (Ryoncil) in December 2024 for pediatric patients aged 2 months and older with SR-aGVHD, the first FDA-approved MSC-based therapy for GVHD. Wastewater-based epidemiology during New Zealand's COVID-19 elimination response: real-world public health impact and economic evaluation
abstract: ABSTRACT After more than a year without community transmission, a localised outbreak of COVID-19 occurred in Auckland, New Zealand, in August 2021. The response to this outbreak was supported by wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) with over 5,000 wastewater tests from 217 locations across New Zealand. This study provides specific real-world examples of the use of WBE to detect pathogen circulation and to provide supporting evidence that transmission was absent or limited in a community, and how this can directly influence public health actions. Evidence of community transmission via positive wastewater tests informed the escalation of public health responses, while early identification of infection in communities with no known cases enabled targeted interventions that contributed to effective control and pathogen elimination from a community. The economic benefits of these responses, quantified in millions of NZ dollars per day, highlight the value of WBE at low disease incidence and emphasise the importance of detection patterns in interpreting results and supporting communication to the public regarding infection risk. WBE can be a highly impactful and cost-effective public health tool in the response to disease incursions. Pandemic preparedness must include plans for selecting appropriate WBE sampling locations and ensuring the capacity to analyse sufficient samples rapidly.

title: Case Report: High-grade diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumor-MC2 in a 6-year-old child with diagnostic delay and short-term complete radiological response after CEV-based chemotherapy
abstract: Diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumor (DLGNT) represents a rare central nervous system neoplasm predominantly observed in pediatric patients. Most cases pursue an indolent clinical course; nevertheless, a small subset demonstrates high-grade histology together with craniospinal dissemination and carries a dismal prognosis. We describe a 6-year-old girl presenting with recurrent vomiting and obstructive hydrocephalus. Initial neuroimaging revealed cerebellar cystic lesions and diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement, which was initially misinterpreted as infectious meningoencephalitis. Tumor biopsy was declined by the patient’s family at initial consultation, and ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement was performed for hydrocephalus relief. One year after shunt surgery, craniospinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) documented substantial tumor progression, with corpus callosum infiltration and vertebral body signal abnormalities. Subsequent biopsy established the diagnosis of DLGNT with high-grade histological features, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 80%. DNA-methylation profiling assigned the tumor to the DLGNT-MC2 molecular subclass. Additional molecular findings included KIAA1549::BRAF gene fusion, 1p deletion, 1q gain, and 17q gain, with an intact 19q and no 1p/19q codeletion. The child received eight cycles of carboplatin, etoposide, and vincristine (CEV) ch…

Comparative Effectiveness of Hormonal Replacement Therapy Versus Integrative Non-Pharmacological Interventions in the Management of Menopausal Syndrome: A 24-Month Longitudinal Analysis
abstract: Background: Menopausal syndrome substantially diminishes health-related quality of life in midlife women globally. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) has long been the standard of care for symptom management; however, long-term safety concerns—including elevated risks of breast malignancy, cardiovascular events, and venous thromboembolism—have prompted growing interest in holistic, non-pharmacological alternatives. Direct longitudinal comparative data across Southeast Asian populations remain scarce.Objective: To evaluate and contrast the efficacy of HRT versus a structured integrative intervention programme on symptom severity and quality of life over a 24-month follow-up period.Methods: This prospective, comparative longitudinal study enrolled 500 women aged 45–60 years presenting with moderate-to-severe menopausal syndrome across six Type B hospitals in Indonesia between January 2023 and December 2025. Participants were allocated to either HRT (conjugated equine oestrogen plus progestin; n = 250) or integrative care (individualised lifestyle modification, cognitive behavioural therapy, mindfulness-based stress reduction, and standardised phytoestrogen supplementation; n = 250). Primary outcomes were change in Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) total score and WHO Quality of Life–BREF (WHOQOL-BREF) domain scores at baseline, 6, 12, and 24 months. title: Organising under uncertainty: how startup investors construct value through sensemaking
abstract: Purpose This study examines how early-stage investors construct startup value under conditions of uncertainty. Drawing on a sensemaking perspective, it explores how investors interpret and integrate resource, leadership and contextual cues into coherent valuation judgements of venture potential. Design/methodology/approach Utilising a semi-structured interview approach, qualitative data were generated from seven startup investors in Malaysia, capturing experiential reflections and evaluative reasoning. An iterative interpretive analysis was conducted, with computational text analysis used for supplementary pattern-checking and visualisation. The themes are presented as interconnected dimensions of investors' valuation narratives. Findings The findings illustrate that valuation is constructed through a dynamic sensemaking process in which investors integrate five interrelated dimensions: operational discipline, customer and market focus, technological capability, product–market viability and team and leadership. Investors complement available financial information with interpretive narratives that connect internal capabilities, leadership and external conditions into coherent assessments of venture potential. Leadership emerges as the central integrative mechanism, while early customer validation anchors credibility. Valuation therefore emerges as an ongoing negotiation between …

title: Comparison of Financing Risk Indicators (NPF, CAR, FDR, and CKPN) as Outcome Signals of Risk Management Between Bank Syariah Indonesia and Bank Muamalat Indonesia in 2021-2024
abstract: Backgrounds: The growth of Islamic banking in Indonesia requires effective financing risk management to maintain financing quality and stability. Objectives: This study compares financing risk outcomes, used as signals of risk management performance, between Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) and Bank Muamalat Indonesia (BMI) in 2021–2024, based on the Non-Performing Financing (NPF), Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Financing to Deposit Ratio (FDR) and Allowance for Impairment Losses (CKPN) ratios. Methodology: A quantitative descriptive-comparative approach was applied to secondary data from the banks’ annual reports and financial statements. Findings: BSI’s NPF fell from 2.93% to 1.90%, while BMI’s moved from 0.67% to 3.35%; both stayed below the 5% OJK limit. BSI’s FDR rose from 73.39% to 84.97%, whereas BMI’s remained between 38.33% and 47.14%. BMI had a higher CAR (23.76% to 32.70%) than BSI (20.29% to 22.09%). BSI’s CKPN ratio (2.72% to 3.29%) exceeded BMI’s (0.94% to 1.60%), and its provision coverage relative to NPF stayed between 103% and 144%, while BMI’s fell from 219% to 28%. BSI’s financing risk outcomes were therefore more consistent. Conclusions: BSI’s financing risk outcomes were more consistent, but the ratios cannot confirm how risk management was implemented, and the findings are descriptive, covering two banks over four years without significance tests. title: Lessons From the Development and Assessment of a Community Participative Mental Health and Substance Policy Agenda in the Bronx, NY
abstract: ABSTRACT Context: In 2025, the Bronx, one of New York City (NYC)'s Boroughs, experienced the largest mental health and substance use disparity in NYC. Program: The goal of this practice report is to describe and evaluate the 2025 community-centered policy agenda proposed by a community collaborative named the # not62 campaign. The campaign has fostered constructive partnerships over 2 decades to improve the Bronx's residents' well-being. Implementation: Experts in health services, social work, and behavioral health used measures of legitimacy, feasibility, and government support to assess each policy agenda item, with the purpose of assisting in prioritizing the agenda items and supporting long-term community engagement. Policy Agenda items ranged from supporting more educational and training initiatives for Bronx Youth in the health care field to health education campaigns to reduce stigma and monetary incentives to ensure patient compliance with treatment. Evaluation: Results from the evaluation indicate that the initiatives with the greatest potential for success at the present time are those related to improving and expanding access to mental health services through existing NYC-funded programs and investing in higher education in academic programs related to the health service workforce. Discussion: Although the Bronx is faced with health disparities in multiple mental hea…

title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
abstract: Abstract Purpose Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. Methods An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. Results Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1…

title: Feeling the gap: cognitive-affective divergence in SME managers' Industry 4.0 and sustainability narratives
abstract: Purpose The study investigates how small- and medium-sized enterprise (SME) managers perceive and emotionally engage with environmental and social sustainability in the context of Industry 4.0 adoption. Using semi-structured interviews combined with multimodal sentiment analysis (speech prosody and emotional language), we aim to uncover implicit hesitancy, dissonance, and conceptual fragmentation that traditional methods fail to detect, thereby offering new insights for policy design and corporate social responsibility research in structurally disadvantaged regions. Design/methodology/approach The manuscript employs a mixed-methods design integrating semi-structured interviews with multimodal sentiment analysis. Twenty SMEs in Southern Italy, selected through structured sampling, participated in interviews exploring Industry 4.0 investments, environmental practices, and social sustainability. Recorded interviews underwent (1) thematic and content analysis for explicit responses, and (2) Hume AI-based prosody and emotional language analysis to detect implicit emotional engagement. This dual approach captures both declared positions and underlying affective reactions, enabling the identification of dissonance between cognitive awareness and emotional investment across environmental and social sustainability dimensions. Findings Environmental sustainability is widely recognized (9…

title: The application of Fourier series in forecasting construction project completion: a case study
abstract: Purpose Predicting project completion time is a crucial aspect of construction management for mitigating delays and supporting effective project control. However, existing forecasting methods still rely on extensive historical data and lack optimality in capturing the cyclical and non-linear patterns of project progress. Therefore, an accurate and adaptive prediction model is required to support decision-making under conditions of limited data. Accurate prediction of construction completion remains challenging due to the cyclicality and nonlinearity of progress data, especially when historical datasets are frequently scarce or unavailable. This study develops and validates Optimum Fourier Series–Polynomial Regression (Optimum.FSPR), a hybrid prediction model designed to provide reliable completion forecasts under conditions of data scarcity or high volatility. Design/methodology/approach The Optimum.FSPR technique integrates Fourier Series (FS) to model cyclic patterns with Polynomial Regression (PR) to capture nonlinear long-term trends. Model performance is evaluated using weekly project progress data, with Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) serving as benchmark models and Mean Absolute Error, Mean Absolute Percentage Error and Root Mean Squared Error as evaluation metrics. title: Creating a palliative care skills training for health care professionals in allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation recipients: symptom management to end-of-life care
abstract: Abstract Background Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) presents a complex procedure with curative intent in haematological disorders, but is associated with high toxicity. Acute graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) and infections are early complications with high mortality, while fatigue and chronic GvHD contribute to significant late morbidity. Our preceding study revealed substantial palliative care needs, including patients’ uncertainty and existential fears, alongside Health Care Professionals (HCP) reported uncertainty and call for further training in addressing these challenges. Methods To address these needs, we developed and piloted a one-day training for HCPs, based on Brown’s Design Thinking principles, covering symptom management, end-of-life care, patients’ and family caregivers’ perceived life threat, and goals-of-care discussions. The training, led by a palliative care specialist, was held in three 6-8 h sessions with a total of 28 participants. It was delivered through various learning modules, interactive components, and group discussions. The programme was evaluated at three time points (pre-training, post-training, one-month follow-up) using self-confidence and practice transfer surveys, complemented by open feedback, and analysed descriptively. Results At one month post-training, participants reported increased self-confidence across …

title: Nonlinear Complexity Features Add Nothing beyond the Power Spectrum in Motor-Imagery BCI: A Surrogate-Controlled Reassessment
abstract: A significant amount of research in the field of Motor-Imagery (MI) brain–computer interfaces have shown that nonlinear and higher-order features-such as fractal dimensions, entropies, detrended fluctuation analysis, variational-mode complexity, Phase–Amplitude Coupling (PAC), and bispectrum/bicoherence-enhance the decoding of sensorimotor rhythms. However, the past studies have drawn their conclusions based on within-session cross-validation, per-subject tuning, fusion over a spatial–spectral baseline, and the absence of a surrogate control. The present study poses a more focused and testable question: do these features contain information that goes beyond that provided by the power spectrum when assessed fairly? Using the BCI Competition IV datasets 2a and 2b (18 subjects) under the official independent-session protocol, a single matched shrinkage-LDA classifier is applied to decode fifteen families of features, each family is subjected to an Iterative Amplitude-Adjusted Fourier Transform (IAAFT) surrogate test, and all the families of tests are corrected for multiple comparisons. The results are clear. title: Impact of maternal positioning on maternal comfort and fetal magnetic resonance imaging quality in a 75-cm bore system
abstract: Abstract Objectives To compare maternal comfort between the supine and left lateral positions during fetal MRI and to assess fetal brain image quality with a conventional body array coil vs. a super-flexible coil on a 75-cm bore system. Methods In this prospective study, 50 women with singleton pregnancies (gestational age 25–36 weeks) referred for suspected fetal brain abnormalities underwent MRI on a 75-cm bore 3.0-T system. Each was scanned in both the supine and left lateral positions (order randomized) and rated comfort for each on a five-point Likert scale. Fetal brain images were analysed as three within-subject conditions: supine with conventional coil, supine with super-flexible coil, and left lateral with super-flexible coil. Image quality was assessed subjectively and objectively using repeated-measures analyses. Results Comfort scores were higher in the left lateral position than supine (4.2±0.8 vs. 3.8±0.9; p=0.031), particularly in late pregnancy. Subjective image quality did not differ significantly among conditions. In the primary positional contrast (super-flexible coil held constant), the left lateral position yielded significantly higher SNR in 17 of the 20 brain regions and higher CNR in six of the eight regions (all q <0.05 after false-discovery-rate correction), with differences most pronounced in late pregnancy (15 of 28 metrics remained significant after…

title: Perceived benefits of sustainable fashion: the role of warm glow for other- and self-benefit framing on online consumption intentions
abstract: Purpose Despite the relevance of perceived self-benefits in fashion brand advertising, combining other- and self-benefits still frequently backfires. The current paper explores how sustainable online fashion branding influences consumption intentions when emphasizing other-benefits (sustainability) combined with different affective self-benefits, i.e. intrinsic benefit (good feeling of helping others) and image-benefit (social esteem) through intrinsic and extrinsic dimensions of warm glow feelings. The moderating role of consumers’ value orientations is additionally examined. Design/methodology/approach Findings of two multi-factorial experiments among a total of 482 participants reveal that by advertising different affective self-benefits alongside the other-benefit of sustainability, fashion brands may elicit both intrinsic and extrinsic warm glow. Findings Specifically, added image-benefits may help to elicit extrinsic warm glow, while added intrinsic benefits induce intrinsic and extrinsic warm glow. However, the positive effect of benefit framing is contingent on personal values, with enhancement and transcendence orientation explaining differences in consumer reactions. Originality/value This research offers novel insights into the interplay of other- and self-benefits in sustainable fashion marketing by addressing consumers' affective reactions. title: The power of perception: the impact of inclusivity policies and diversity climate on employee well-being
abstract: Purpose The purpose of the current study is to assess the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being (i.e. life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance). Moreover, we also examine diversity climate as a potential mediator of this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the model of inclusive organizations and the signaling theory, we hypothesized that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies would relate to better employee well-being through a more favorable perception of diversity climate. The sample consisted of 361 faculty and staff from a large Southeastern university. A single-level path-analytic mediation model was used to test hypothesized relationships due to the negligible between-college variance. Findings The results revealed that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies were associated with a more positive diversity climate which, in turn, enhanced certain well-being outcomes – life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance. Further, diversity climate mediated the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being. Our results highlight the importance of not only implementing inclusive policies but, also ensuring that employees perceive them as fair and effective. Originality/value The curren…

Land acquisition reform and schedule performance of highway projects: evidence from India's RFCTLARR Act
abstract: Purpose Land acquisition is widely recognised as one of the most delay-prone activities in infrastructure project delivery. This study empirically evaluates whether transparent and fair land acquisition reforms improve schedule performance of publicly procured infrastructure projects, focusing on India's Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on a dataset of 481 completed highway projects implemented between 2000 and 2019, covering both pre- and post-reform periods. Mean comparison analysis, ordinary least squares (OLS) and seemingly unrelated regression (SUR) models were employed to examine the association between the reform and the three indicators of schedule performance: estimated unit time, actual unit time and time overruns, while controlling for project-specific, governance and state-level factors. Findings The results consistently show that projects implemented after the RFCTLARR Act had lower estimated and actual unit times and significantly lower time overruns. These findings suggest that enhanced procedural fairness, through improved compensation mechanisms, mandatory social impact assessments and structured rehabilitation and resettlement measures, is associated with reduced uncertainty, disputes and execution risk, thereby improving project sc…

title: Pengaruh Beban Perkuliahan dan Fleksibilitas Jam Kerja terhadap Produktivitas Kerja Mahasiswa Pekerja di Universitas Pamulang
abstract: This research investigates how academic workload and working-hour flexibility relate to the work productivity of employed students at Pamulang University. A quantitative associative method was applied, involving 35 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Primary data were obtained through questionnaires using a five-point Likert scale and processed through multiple linear regression analysis, classical assumption testing, partial and simultaneous hypothesis testing, and the coefficient of determination. The findings reveal that academic workload has a negative relationship with work productivity, although the effect is statistically insignificant, as indicated by a significance level of 0.446. Meanwhile, working-hour flexibility demonstrates a positive relationship but does not have a significant effect, with a significance value of 0.097. The simultaneous test also indicates an insignificant effect of both independent variables, with a significance value of 0.236. Furthermore, the R² value of 0.086 indicates that the research variables account for 8.6% of the variation in work productivity, while the remaining proportion is associated with other factors beyond the research model.

Food insecurity as a source of supply chain risk? An alternate perspective on a vicious cycle
abstract: Purpose The objective of this paper is to provide a perspective on food insecurity as an antecedent and enabling condition of supply chain risk. The goal is to scope a research landscape for evaluating this relationship and to encourage future research in this underexplored direction. Design/methodology/approach Building on extant literature on food security and supply chain risk management, we conceptualize food insecurity as a social condition that generates or intensifies existing supply chain risks. Findings We provide a framework and propositions to explore the mechanisms through which food insecurity may become operationally consequential across the micro-meso-macro levels. We also discuss different interventions for mitigation. Practical implications Using real-world examples, we illustrate how the impact of food insecurity-related disturbances may affect supply chain performance. We discuss reactive, active, and proactive interventions involving business decision-making and policymaking. Originality/value We explore an underexplored pathway of how food insecurity affects supply chain performance. We position food insecurity not only as an outcome but as an antecedent of supply chain risk.

title: Sustainability disclosure: transparency or smoke and mirrors?
abstract: Purpose This study aims at advancing the theory of managerial intent and strategic choice with regards to disclosure transparency that companies adopt in sustainability reporting under mandatory disclosure regulations. It investigates whether, and how, corporate performance and governance mechanisms influence the transparency of sustainability reports. Design/methodology/approach The study provides an analysis of sustainability reports published by Italian listed companies, following the implementation of the European Union (EU) Directive 2014/95/EU on sustainability disclosure. Both textual and quantitative analysis are conducted to classify disclosure strategies and to investigate the relationship between transparency levels, corporate performance indicators, and governance structures. Findings The results of this study indicate that firms operating within mandatory disclosure settings do not consistently align the tone of their reporting with their underlying performance and, thus, tone may be used strategically, potentially to obscure unfavourable performance or to manage stakeholder perceptions. Furthermore, the analysis highlights substantial deficiencies in the readability of corporate disclosures. Originality/value This study advances knowledge on the categorization of transparency disclosure strategies. It enhances understanding of the importance of linguistic choices …

title: Social fashion identity: definition, scale development and empirical validation
abstract: Purpose This study contributes to the conceptualization and measurement of how consumers use fashion to express multiple social identities. It aims to conceptualize social fashion identity, develop and validate its measurement scale and establish its dimensionality, reliability, convergent, discriminant and nomological validity. Design/methodology/approach Across two studies, social fashion identity is conceptualized, and a scale was developed and validated in a step-by-step process following Churchill (1979) and DeVellis (1991) procedures. Study 1 focused on construct conceptualization, item generation and scale validation, whereas Study 2 examined the nomological validity. Findings This paper validated the social fashion identity scale as a reliable two-dimensional construct consisting of fashion identity expression and fashion-based group belongingness. Social fashion identity was distinct from fashion consciousness and product involvement, positively associated with fashion consciousness, and positively related to consumers' willingness to pay more for fashion items. Practical implications The social fashion identity scale offers fashion companies a tool to segment their clients, enabling more personalized customer experiences within the fashion market. Furthermore, the findings can contribute to the effectiveness of fashion brands' product development, marketing and pricin…

title: Internal audit quality and earnings management: the roles of competence, independence, and work performance
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether internal audit quality (IAQ) is associated with lower income-increasing discretionary accruals and improved financial reporting quality (FRQ) in an emerging market with uneven regulatory enforcement. Design/methodology/approach Survey-based measures of internal audit (IA) competence, independence and work performance are combined with archival data from non-financial firms listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange. FRQ is proxied by signed discretionary accruals from the performance-adjusted modified Jones model (Kothari et al., 2005), and interaction models examine variation across reporting-pressure and governance conditions. Given the cross-sectional design, the findings are associational rather than causal. Findings Higher IAQ is associated with lower income-increasing discretionary accruals. Competence is the attribute primarily associated with this relationship, whereas independence and work performance show no separate association once modelled jointly. The association is stronger among loss-making firms but weaker where audit committee independence is high, a pattern consistent with substitution between IA and audit-committee monitoring, though the interaction is only marginally significant. Evidence on audit committee financial expertise is weaker and is treated as suggestive. Practical implications In emerging markets, the findings highlig…
