title: Three-dimensional computational evaluation of water-to-air mass stopping power ratio for therapeutic helium-, carbon-, oxygen-, and neon-ion beams and its application to patient-specific quality assurance
abstract: Abstract Objective. Current dosimetry protocols recommend a constant water-to-air mass stopping power ratio, s w,air , of 1.126 with an uncertainty of ±1.5% for light ions, irrespective of ion species and energy. This study aims to develop a computational framework to calculate three-dimensional s w,air distributions of helium-, carbon-, oxygen-, and neon-ion beams for patient specific quality assurance (PSQA), and to systematically investigate spatial variations in s w,air under clinically relevant conditions. Approach. A computational framework was developed to calculate three-dimensional s w,air distributions based on the Bragg-Gray approximation, together with three-dimensional dose distributions for treatment planning. The framework was validated against published datasets for a mono-energetic carbon-ion beam. Treatment plans were generated using helium-, carbon-, oxygen-, and neon-ion beams for rectangular targets with varying spread-out Bragg peak (SOBP) widths and depths, as well as for bone and soft tissue, head and neck, and ocular cases. The corresponding s w,air distributions were calculated in a water phantom and compared with the recommended value of 1.126. Main Results. The mean s w,air within the target increased for shallower targets with narrower SOBP widths. For all ion species, s w,air increased toward the distal end of the SOBP, with larger variations obser…

title: Bridging marine ESG practices and smart technologies: toward sustainable and accessible travel experiences
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how marine environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices and smart tourism technologies (STTs) jointly shape tourists’ perceptions, attitudes, and behavioral intentions in accessible tourism. Design/methodology/approach A two-study structural equation modeling approach was adopted. Study 1 analyzed 689 valid responses from an ocean leisure sample to examine the effects of ESG practices on travel attitudes through perceptions of a friendly environment and destination image. Study 2 analyzed 690 valid responses from a tourism sample to investigate the mediating role of STTs in the relationship between travel attitudes and travel intentions, as well as the moderating role of perceived risk. Findings ESG practices positively influence travel attitudes through perceptions of a friendly environment and destination image. Travel intention strengthens the relationships between ESG practices and perceptions of a friendly environment and between perceptions of a friendly environment and travel attitudes. STTs positively mediate the relationship between travel attitudes and travel intentions. Furthermore, perceived risk strengthens the positive relationship between travel attitudes and STTs but weakens the relationship between STTs and travel intentions. Originality/value By integrating the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework with the Theory of Pla…

title: Uncertainty-aware possibilistic load forecasting for smart grid energy conservation
abstract: Overview efficient electricity usage management in the presence of deep uncertainty is critical for modern power systems with a high renewable share. We present a fuzzy interval regression framework that represents load observations as triangular fuzzy numbers and estimates α-cut interval forecasts without requiring a full probability distribution. The original eight-hour example is retained only as a transparent calculation: at α = 0.5, the corrected two-weight fit gives an in-sample empirical coverage of 83.3% and a mean interval width of 2.164 MW; these values are descriptive and are neither confidence levels nor predictive validation. To provide out-of-sample evidence, the method was additionally evaluated on the public Taylor half-hourly electricity-demand series for England and Wales (4,032 observations), using the first 3,360 points for estimation and the final 672 points for testing. For the one-step model, the mean absolute error (MAE) was 429.1 MW, the root mean square error (RMSE) was 574.5 MW, and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 1.45%. The residual-calibrated, time-of-day triangular spreads had an empirical coverage of 91.7% at α = 0.5 and a mean interval width of 1,804.4 MW. An example of demand-response data is given in the form of a 1 MW effort to reduce base load at four defined hours. Assuming a marginal rate of 0.7 tCO₂/MWh, this gross avoided em…

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Driven Forecasting of Value Added Tax: A Case Study of the Tanzania Revenue Authority
abstract: This study set out to assess the applicability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models in forecasting Value Added Tax revenue, with a focus on the Tanzania Revenue Authority. In assessing the applicability, the historical trends and performance of VAT collection were used to develop AI models to forecast monthly VAT revenue, thereafter providing recommendations for improving VAT forecasting through the adoption of AI technologies. The study utilised time series for the period of January 2021 to December 2024, constructing a dataset covering 48 months. The variables under the data set are: VAT revenue statistics, which provide detailed transactional records of VAT collections across three main categories: imports, purchases, and sales. The granular daily entries are aggregated to obtain monthly totals, creating a coherent time series that is suitable for statistical modelling and forecasting purposes. Other variables include the Consumer Price Index (CPI), GDP and inflation rate. Five forecasting models, SARIMAX, Elastic-Net, XGBoost, CNN-LSTM, and SNaive, were basically applied in predicting VAT revenue. All models under testing performed at different levels, with XGBoost performing better with the lowest MAE TZS 150 billion, RMSE TZS 205 billion and MAPE 275%, demonstrating its effectiveness in capturing non-linear patterns and handling outliers in VAT revenue data. The Elastic…

title: An Integrated Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Cell-to-Pack Imbalance Prediction in Electric Vehicle Battery Systems
abstract: This study presents a machine learning framework for predicting cell-to-pack imbalance in electric vehicle batteries. A set of battery attributes that affect battery performance, including State of Charge (SOC), State of Health (SOH), temperature (including ambient temperature and humidity), and cabin temperature, were used to make this prediction. The collected battery data were pre-processed to improve prediction performance. Three preprocessing methods were used: (i) Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD); (ii) deep denoising autoencoders, and (iii) feature selection using minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) mutual information. This preprocessing step removes noise from the dataset and identifies useful information for prediction. Cell-to-pack imbalance prediction was performed using three interpretable machine learning models: (i) an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM); (ii) fuzzy regression; and (iii) RuleFit. These models provide transparent predictions and help in understanding the factors responsible for battery imbalance. Models were evaluated on an independent 20-sample test set held out from the 100-record dataset. Among the three interpretable models, Fuzzy Regression achieved the strongest predictive performance (R² = 0.998), followed by RuleFit (R² = 0.976), while EBM achieved a lower R² of 0.201 on this independent test set despite providing detailed feature…

title: Theoretical Prediction of Tensile Strength Property of Fiber Metal Laminates
abstract: This study estimates the theoretical tensile strength properties of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Aluminium Laminates (CARALL) fiber-metal laminates (FMLs) for two stacking configurations like Type 1 (aluminum outermost: A|C|A|C|A) and Type 2 (carbon-fiber outermost: C|A|C|A|C) that are taken from the experimental data in literature. For achieving this purpose, two complementary approaches Metal Volume Fraction (MVF) and Classical Laminate Theory (CLT) are adopted. Tsai-Hill / von Mises Criteria are applied for first ply failure and progressive failure. The results indicated that for Type 2, CLT method predicts 728 MPa tensile strength, which is in good agreement with experimental value — an under-prediction of only 6%. The MVF Rule of Mixtures provides a reliable upper bound: +7% for Type 2 and +22% for Type 1 composite samples, respectively. In addition, for CLT progressive failure analysis, 90° CF ply transverse cracking (matrix failure) — FPF at ~463-472 MPa for both types while Aluminum layer yielding/failure — occurs after FPF due to load redistribution, but 0° CF fibre fracture — ultimate failure event, dominant load-bearing mechanism.

The effects of incomplete vibrational accommodation and finite-rate surface catalysis on peak heat flux prediction of hypersonic compression corner
abstract: Abstract In high-enthalpy shock tunnels, gas molecules are excited to higher vibrational and chemical energy states. However, rapid expansion and acceleration through the nozzle leave insufficient time for vibrational deexcitation and recombination, leading to significant gas–surface interaction effects on wall heat transfer. This research utilizes computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to study the influence of vibrational accommodation and finite-rate catalysis on flow field structure and peak heat flux in hypersonic compression corner flows under thermochemical nonequilibrium free-stream conditions, characterized by low-to-medium Reynolds numbers and high Mach numbers. The results indicate that vibrational accommodation and finite-rate catalysis have a negligible influence on the structure of the flow separation bubble. However, both significantly affect the peak heat fluxes, which can be decomposed into three components: translational-rotational heat flux, vibrational heat flux, and catalytic heat flux. More importantly, a validated theoretical method is proposed to predict the peak heat flux by accounting for the effects of incomplete vibrational accommodation and finite-rate catalysis. Furthermore, the proposed theoretical framework suggests an equivalence relation between the vibrational accommodation coefficient and the catalytic coefficient, indicating a quantitative inter…

title: A cascade deep learning network for simultaneous prediction of dose and linear energy transfer in proton therapy of prostate cancer
abstract: Abstract Objective. Prediction of dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LETd) may facilitate LET-aware evaluation of proton therapy plans. This study developed a cascade deep learning framework for simultaneous three-dimensional prediction of dose and LETd distributions for conventional dose-based optimization (DoseOpt) and LETd-incorporated optimization (LETOpt) in prostate intensity-modulated proton therapy. Approach. A total of 150 patients with prostate cancer were included, each with DoseOpt and LETOpt plans. Planning CT images and anatomical structure masks were used as inputs. The cascade network transferred an intermediate latent representation from the dose prediction pathway to the LETd prediction pathway. Stepwise, multitask, and anatomy-only LETd (only-LET) networks served as comparators. Model performance was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Main results. All dose-predicting models showed high spatial agreement, with cascade Dice similarity coefficients of approximately 0.93, 0.96, and 0.95 for the 50%, 75%, and 95% prescription isodose volumes. No significant differences in structure-specific dose errors remained after false discovery rate correction. The cascade model achieved the lowest global LETd mean absolute error (MAE) for DoseOpt and LETOpt, 0.108 ± 0.025 and 0.111 ± 0.025 keV μ m −1 , respectively, significantly lower than those of the multitas…

Diagnostic prediction models for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease and related fatty-liver phenotypes among patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review
abstract: Objective To systematically summarise and critically appraise multivariable diagnostic prediction models for MAFLD and related fatty-liver phenotypes in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Methods Eight databases (four international and four Chinese) were searched from inception to May 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data using the CHARMS framework. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with PROBAST. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, results were synthesised descriptively rather than pooled. Results Eighteen diagnostic studies (study-level: 7 MAFLD, 8 NAFLD, and 3 MASLD) reporting 52 distinct diagnostic model specifications were included. No eligible prognostic studies or prognostic models were identified. Studies on NAFLD and MASLD are regarded as indirect supporting evidence; their performance evaluations neither were combined nor directly compared with the MAFLD model. Feng Leyi et al. (2024) used samples recruited from the same hospital at different times, but the validation period came before the development period, thus the independence of the participants could not be confirmed. It was not classified as an independent external validation. The remaining studies reported significant development-set performance or internal validation; No study provided clear independent external validation. BMI…

title: Melting temperature prediction method for mold flux based on transfer learning algorithm
abstract: Abstract To establish an accurate predictive model for the single hot thermocouple technique (SHTT)-measured melting temperature, a transfer learning strategy was introduced. The proposed model learns general relationships between mold flux composition and melting behavior on the large hemisphere-method dataset in the pre-training process and retains them in the feature-extraction layers. Fine-tuning the output layer with limited SHTT data then adapts the model to SHTT measurements, alleviating the accuracy bottleneck associated with direct training on a small SHTT dataset. The results show that the coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) and mean squared error (MSE) of the pre-trained model (Hemi_MLP) on the test set are 0.87 and 1,268.65, respectively. It provides effective general knowledge of mold flux melting behavior for the subsequent fine-tuning task. The fine-tuned model (SHTT_MLP) achieves 0.99 R 2 and 187.6 MSE on the SHTT test set, which has the best performance among the comparison models. The Shapley Additive Explanations analysis shows that the determination of the SHTT_MLP for the influence of each component on the melting temperature of mold flux is consistent with prior knowledge. Additionally, the SHTT_MLP primarily completes the fine-tuning process by strengthening its sensitivity to CaO/SiO 2 and CaO/Al 2 O 3 .

title: Development and external validation of a pre-drainage prediction model for moderate-to-severe gallstone-related acute cholangitis
abstract: Abstract Background Acute cholangitis may rapidly progress to sepsis and organ dysfunction, making early severity assessment essential. However, few practical tools are currently available based on routine pre-drainage data. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a pre-drainage model for identifying moderate-to-severe gallstone-related acute cholangitis. Methods This two-center retrospective study included 159 patients in the training cohort and 119 in the external validation cohort. Tokyo Guidelines 2018 Grades II–III defined moderate-to-severe disease. Candidate variables measured within 24 h of admission and before drainage were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and refitted using multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed by bootstrap resampling and external validation. Results The four-predictor model included the direct-to-total bilirubin ratio, ln-transformed systemic inflammatory response index, red cell distribution width, and serum calcium. Apparent and optimism-corrected areas under the curve were 0.823 and 0.777, respectively. The external area under the curve was 0.871 (95% confidence interval, 0.804–0.937), but the model overestimated absolute risk (calibration intercept, − 0.828). Exploratory intercept-only recalibration reduced the Brier score from 0.158 to 0.137. Decision curve analysis sugge…

title: Coupled Abrasive and Fatigue Wear Modeling of Blanking Punches for Prediction of Wear Using Linear and Nonlinear Wear Models
abstract: Repeated blanking operations cause progressive degradation of punch edges, leading to dimensional inaccuracies, burr formation, and premature tool failure. This study proposes a coupled abrasive–fatigue wear modeling framework for estimating the lifetime of punches under long-term repeated blanking process. Abrasive wear was modeled using a modified Archard wear formulation, whereas fatigue-induced wear was represented using an extended Lemaitre damage model capable of capturing cyclic damage accumulation within the elastic regime. An adaptive finite element framework incorporating wear-driven geometry updating and element deletion techniques was developed to simulate progressive punch edge degradation during repeated blanking operations. The proposed methodology was applied to an AISI D2 punch and AISI 430 sheet metal under long-term cyclic blanking conditions. The results of finite element analysis demonstrated that the conventional linear wear model predicted gradual wear evolution, whereas the coupled nonlinear wear model effectively captured accelerated wear propagation after approximately 300,000 blanking cycles due to fatigue-induced material detachment. The predicted wear depth evolution showed good agreement with the experimental results, with a maximum relative error below 7%. In addition, the proposed wear update method using accumulated cycles enabled faster wear pr…

title: An edge-conditioned convolution model for carbon flow rate prediction under source-load uncertainty
abstract: Introduction The realization of China’s dual-carbon goals relies on accurate and fine-grained carbon emission modeling of the new-type power systems. Conventional carbon calculation methods are designed for traditional power systems and rely on deterministic power flow calculations. This makes it difficult to capture the impacts of source–load uncertainty on the carbon flow rate under high renewable penetration. Methods This paper proposes a carbon flow rate prediction model based on Edge Conditioned Convolution (ECC) to account for source–load uncertainty. First, a carbon flow rate calculation framework is established by incorporating the full lifecycle carbon emissions of renewable generators and a network loss allocation mechanism. This mechanism combines upstream and downstream power flow tracing to allocate network losses between the generation and consumption sides using an allocation coefficient. Second, an ECC-based carbon flow rate prediction model is developed to incorporate branch attributes into information aggregation through edge-conditioned convolution weights. A physics-informed loss function is adopted to encourage the conservation of the carbon flow rate. Furthermore, by using Sobol sequences and Inverse Transform Sampling (ITS) algorithms to generate multi-scenario data sets, the application scenarios of the prediction model are extended to power systems with…

Nexus among service quality dimensions and halal purchase intention: exploring moderating role of word of mouth
abstract: Purpose The prime objective of this study is to examine the impact of different service quality dimensions, namely, reliability, tangibility and physical environment, on halal purchase intention among the customers of fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG). This study also examines the mediating effect of customer satisfaction along with the moderating impact of word of mouth on the path of customer satisfaction and purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach The data were obtained through FMCG-purposive sampling by distributing questionnaires to FMCG customers. A total of 647 questionnaires were surveyed, and the questionnaires were self-administered. Of these, 347 were valid and considered for analysis using variance-based structural equation modeling (PLS) to test the hypothesis. Findings The study’s results reflected that service quality is important in creating customer satisfaction. In the same way, the physical environment where customers are provided with services and service quality reliability are also key to generating customer satisfaction. In terms of the indirect results, Service quality reliability, physical environment and service quality tangibility are positively associated with halal purchase intention through the mediation of customer satisfaction. In addition, word of mouth strengthens the relationship between customer satisfaction and halal purchase intenti…

abstract: Мета статті – комплексно дослідити нормативно-правові засади організації та проходження військової служби у Другій Речі Посполитій у 1939 р., визначити особливості правового регулювання військового обов’язку, призову, комплектування та мобілізації Війська Польського, з’ясувати роль законодавчих і підзаконних актів у забезпеченні військової готовності держави напередодні Другої світової війни. Особливу увагу приділено нормативним положенням, що визначали правовий статус військовозобов’язаних і військовослужбовців, порядок виконання військового обов’язку та механізми мобілізаційної підготовки. Методологія дослідження. Дослідження здійснено на основі принципів історизму, об’єктивності та системності. Використано загальнонаукові методи аналізу, синтезу, узагальнення та систематизації, а також спеціально-історичні методи: історико-генетичний, історико-порівняльний і проблемно-хронологічний. Застосування історико-правового підходу дало змогу розглянути нормативно-правове регулювання військової служби у взаємозв’язку з політичними, військовими та суспільними процесами в Другій Речі Посполитій. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає у комплексному аналізі нормативно-правових засад військової служби у Другій Речі Посполитій станом на 1939 р. Уточнено основні напрями розвитку польського законодавства у сфері військового обов’язку та військової служби, систематизовано ключові нормативні поло…

title: AI-A-thon Learning Ecosystem to Promote AI Pre-service Teacher Competency
abstract: This study aimed to (1) synthesize the components of the AI-A-thon Learning Ecosystem, (2) synthesize the components of AI Pre-service Teacher Competency, and (3) develop an AI-A-thon Learning Ecosystem to promote AI Pre-service Teacher Competency. A Research and Development (R&D) design was employed, comprising four steps: (1) synthesis of the AI-A-thon Learning Ecosystem components, (2) synthesis of AI Pre-service Teacher Competency components, (3) development of the AI-A-thon Learning Ecosystem, and (4) expert evaluation of the developed system. The AI-A-thon Learning Ecosystem consists of five components: Learners and Learning Community; Content, Resources and AI Tools; Learning Activities and Interaction; Mentorship and Support System; and Assessment and Feedback. AI Pre-service Teacher Competency comprises four dimensions: AI Knowledge, AI Skills, AI Ethics, and AI Character (K–S–E–C). The AI-A-thon learning process consists of five steps: Problem and Objective Identification; Idea Generation and AI Exploration; Prototype Development and Testing; Evaluation and Reflection; and Implementation and Presentation. The developed system was evaluated by 15 experts, with an overall suitability rating of 4.55 (SD = 0.68), corresponding to the highest suitability level under the study’s evaluation criteria. Focus group discussions provided recommendation…

title: Innovation by different means: exploring perceived firm-innovativeness archetypes
abstract: Purpose By integrating four innovation signals (changes in the offering, social innovation, digital innovation, and marketing communications) into a unified framework, this study explores how different combinations of these signals shape customers' innovativeness perceptions in the service sector. Design/methodology/approach This exploratory study uses a large-scale dataset (N = 18,000) from the 2025 Spanish Innovation Index and employs a multi-stage design. First, we use regression analyses to examine the proposed relationships and identify each driver's relative importance. Second, we conduct a k-means cluster analysis to identify strategic archetypes. Finally, we utilize an interpretive analysis of “deviant cases” to illustrate cluster-specific managerial implications. Findings At the aggregate level, social innovation emerges as the most relevant driver of customers perceived firm innovativeness (PFI). Digital innovation is the second most important driver, followed by changes in offerings and marketing communication. Our analysis identifies four PFI archetypes: digital and technology-led innovators, social and close-touch innovators, core-offering-led innovators with a social-digital balance, and social-led innovators. Finally, it provides insights into the success factors of PFI and the barriers faced by deviant cases (the highest and lowest performers) within the same ar…

title: Christian Friedrich Schwartz and the Public Impact of His Missionary Service in South India and England (1750–1813)
abstract: Abstract: Christian Friedrich Schwartz was a German Lutheran Pietist missionary who worked among the Tamil people in southern India from 1750 to 1798. He witnessed the English East India Company’s unstoppable rise and transformation from a mercantile enterprise to a colonial governing power. He came to Tranquebar in 1750l twelve years later, at the invitation of the English military officers and soldiers, he joined the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, which had Anglican roots. His lifestyle radiating values and honesty persuaded the Hindu and Muslim rulers to seek his diplomatic services. The Company sent him as its emissary to Hyder Ali and other stakeholders. Amid his tireless public service, he remained a Lutheran missionary, establishing churches and schools, training catechists, ordaining Tamil pastors, and directing their work. After his death, the Company erected a marble monument in St. Mary’s Church in Fort St. George (now in Chennai). King Serfoji, Schwartz's adopted son, likewise built two monuments, one in marble and the other in granite, and placed them in two churches in Thanjavur. This essay examines, for the first time, the content of these three monuments and places them within the larger context of Schwartz’s public ministry. It draws on archival documents held in the famous Mission Archives of the Francke Foundations (AFSt/M) in Halle (Saale), Germa…

title: Hospital-at-home with point-of-care ultrasound for infections in nursing home residents: feasibility, safety, and care-setting shift in a Taiwanese service evaluation
abstract: Abstract Background Nursing-home residents with acute infection are commonly transferred to hospital, where they are exposed to delirium, functional decline and iatrogenic harm. In October 2024 our nursing home implemented Hospital-at-Home (HaH) under Taiwan’s Acute Care At Home program, using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) to treat pneumonia, urinary tract infection (UTI) and soft-tissue infection (SSTI) on site. We asked whether hospital-level infection care could be delivered safely within the nursing home. Methods Retrospective service evaluation at one central-Taiwan nursing home (HaH period October 2024–December 2025), with a before-and-after description of infection-related hospital use (pre-implementation January–September 2024). Residents entered HaH directly from the nursing home (Model B) or after emergency-department assessment (Model C). Outcomes were completion without escalation to inpatient care, rehospitalization and mortality; the route comparison is descriptive. Results There were 130 HaH episodes (81 UTI, 42 pneumonia, 7 SSTI) in 87 residents (episode-level median age 79.6 years; Barthel Index < 20 in 100 episodes, 76.9%). HaH was completed without escalation in 116 of 130 episodes (89.2%, 95% CI 82.6–94.0). No death occurred during a HaH episode; 30-day mortality was 5 of 130 (3.8%, 1.3–8.7), a lower bound because ascertainment used study-hospital records…

title: Veterinariya xizmatlari xarajatlarini hisobga oliş va boşqarişda sun’iy intellekt texnologiyalarining imkoniyatlari
abstract: The article analyzes the possibilities of using artificial intelligence technologies in the processes of accounting for and managing the costs of veterinary services. Ways of digitally recording and analyzing the consumption of medicines and vaccines and the costs of diagnostics, prevention, treatment, laboratory tests, and transport are considered. Recommendations are given on forecasting costs, optimizing the use of resources, and providing information support for management decisions. Limitations related to data quality, confidentiality, algorithmic errors, and human oversight are also highlighted.

title: Patterns of doctor-patient communication and their associations with health service quality: implications for medical education and practice
abstract: Abstract Background Doctor-patient communication plays an important role in clinical diagnosis and treatment and constitutes a key component of medical education and training. The patient-centered health philosophy drives shift in the priorities of medical education. By identifying patterns of doctor-patient communication and examining their associations with health service quality, this study provides empirical evidence for optimizing medical education. Methods This study collects on-site doctor-patient interaction data using the standardized patient (SP) method and measures doctor-patient communication with the Patient Perspective Patient-Centered Care Scale. Latent profile analysis is adopted to categorize distinct doctor-patient communication profiles, and regression analysis is applied to quantify associations between communication profiles and health service quality. Results This survey yielded 118 sets of doctor-patient interaction data generated by 59 doctors from 26 community health service centers and 12 SPs. Doctor-patient communication is classified into high-level, moderate-level, and low-level profiles. Compared with low-level communication, moderate-level communication (Coef = 0.07, P < 0.01) and high-level communication (Coef = 0.05, P < 0.05) are positively association with consultation standardization; moderate-level communication (Coef = 1.40, P < 0.05) and h…

abstract: The article presents the results of a study of the species composition and distribution patterns of ectoparasites in service dogs kept at a specialized cynological center in the city of Tashkent. The studies were carried out in 2025–2026 at the National Cynological Center of the Customs Committee of the Republic of Uzbekistan on 82 service dogs belonging to 14 breeds. According to the results, ectoparasites were detected in 9 dogs, and the overall prevalence of infestation was 11.0% (95% CI: 5.1–19.8). Morphological identification revealed the ticks Ixodes persulcatus, Dermacentor marginatus, Haemaphysalis punctata and Hyalomma scupense, the fleas Ctenocephalides canis, C. felis and Pulex irritans, and, among lice, Trichodectes canis.

title: Customer Service Training Content and Quality Service Delivery at Julius Nyerere International Airport, Tanzania
abstract: Purpose: This study examined the effects of customer service training content on the provision of quality service delivery at Julius Nyerere International Airport (JNIA), where passenger complaints have risen despite a regulatory requirement for structured customer service training. Design/methodology/approach: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design guided by Public Strategic Implementation Theory, New Public Governance Theory and Public Value Theory was adopted. Questionnaires were completed by 82 of 86 frontline staff selected through stratified random sampling (95.3%), and 12 purposively selected supervisors and managers were interviewed. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression and thematic analysis. Findings: Training content was rated highly (overall M = 4.09). Improvement of staff professionalism (M = 4.32) and relevance to passenger service tasks (M = 4.20) were the strongest aspects, while reflection of real operational challenges at JNIA was the weakest (M = 3.83). Training content was positively correlated with quality service delivery (r = 0.58, p < 0.01) and remained a significant predictor when training frequency and delivery methods were controlled (β = 0.261, p = 0.006). Interviewees stressed the value of realistic, scenario-based content. Research limitations/implications: The study relied on staff percep…

title: Public Service Innovation in Transforming Waste Management into Green Economy-Based Assets through a Quadruple Helix Approach: A Collaborative Study of Waste Bank–Pegadaian
abstract: This study examines public service innovation in transforming household waste management into green economy-based assets through The Gade Clean & Gold program, a collaborative initiative involving Bank Sampah Rukmi, PT Pegadaian, local government actors, community participants, and academics within a Quadruple Helix framework in Gunung Anyar, Surabaya. The background problem centers on the limitations of conventional final-disposal-oriented waste governance, the fragile sustainability of community waste banks when economic incentives are weak, and the absence of an integrated coordination platform among public, business, community, and academic actors. This research aims to analyze multi-stakeholder collaboration dynamics, evaluate the quality of waste-to-gold service innovation, and clarify the differentiated contributions of each Quadruple Helix pillar. A qualitative case-study design was applied through in-depth interviews with seven purposively selected informants, field observation, and document analysis. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldana, while validity was strengthened through source triangulation, technique triangulation, member checking, and saturation-based verification. The findings show that the collaboration has produced measurable outcomes, including 847 active customers and 12.4 tons of managed waste per year, exceedin…

title: Mechanistic Insights into Carbon Source Competition Regulation for Enhanced Ethyl Ester Accumulation in Cheese Flavoring by Inoculation Timing
abstract: Abstract To address flavor imbalance induced by ethyl ester deficiency in enzymatic hydrolysis-fermentation coupled cheese flavor (EMCF), yeast was introduced to promote ethyl ester formation via the ethanol-esterification pathway. Yeast addition generated divergent ethyl ester yields; yeast preinoculation resulted in the highest relative ethyl ester concentration (274.76 ng/g), whereas ethyl ester synthesis was markedly inhibited in LAB preinoculation. These variations stemmed from distinct carbon source competition patterns: carbon source competition between yeasts and LAB was alleviated under yeast preinoculation, favoring yeast ethanol metabolism and esterification, while intensified competition caused excessive acid accumulation. Sensory analysis indicated that yeast preinoculation exhibited milky and buttery notes, while LAB preinoculation featured saltiness, umami, and sourness. Experiments with a yeast strain exhibiting higher ADH and PDC activities further supported the role of inoculation sequence in promoting ethanol accumulation and ethyl ester formation. Carbon source competition acted as the core regulator of flavor formation, supporting targeted ethyl ester enhancement.

title: Beyond one-size-fits-all regulation: Do banking resilience patterns vary across countries?
abstract: Purpose International banking regulation has long assumed resilience patterns work identically across contexts. This study tests whether resilience patterns of association are context-dependent using data from 142 countries classified under the IMF World Economic Outlook (April 2026) taxonomy of Advanced Economies and Emerging Market and Developing Economies (EMDEs). Design/methodology/approach A multidimensional Banking Resilience Index is constructed from CAMELS components for 142 countries over 2000–2023. Fixed effects models examine associations between resilience and future capital adequacy, asset quality and profitability. Dynamic fixed-effects models account for persistence and macroeconomic conditions. Temporal falsification tests assess forward-looking information. Interaction models evaluate economic-group heterogeneity. Crisis-period change analysis examines three major crises. Findings Fixed effects show associations between resilience and future asset quality (β = −0.095, p = 0.007), profitability (β = 0.034, p < 0.001) and capital adequacy (β = 0.051, p = 0.007). Dynamic models render these insignificant. Temporal falsification confirms persistence. Interaction models show no Advanced–EMDE difference (p = 0.283–0.961). Advanced Economies recorded larger resilience improvements during COVID-19 (4.50, p < 0.001) and the Eurozone Crisis (1.33, p = 0.030). Resea…

title: Total glycosides of Yangyin Tongnao formula alleviate myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury through regulation of PI3K/Akt signaling and ferroptosis: network pharmacology and experimental validation
abstract: Background Myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MI/RI) is a major pathological process that limits the benefits of timely reperfusion therapy. Yangyin Tongnao formula (YYTN) is a traditional Chinese medicine for cerebrovascular diseases. Based on the Chinese traditional concept of brain-heart simultaneous treatment, we hypothesized that YYTN may exert protective effects against MI/RI. This study aimed to investigate the potential mechanisms underlying the protective effects of YYTN against MI/RI and to evaluate the cardioprotective effects of its glycoside-enriched fraction, the total glycosides of YYTN (YYTG). Methods Network pharmacology was employed to identify the potential active components, targets, and signaling pathways underlying the protective effects of YYTN against MI/RI. YYTG was prepared as a glycoside-enriched fraction of YYTN. An oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) model was established in H9c2 cardiomyocytes to investigate the cardioprotective effects of YYTG. HUVECs subjected to OGD/R were subsequently used as a complementary model to evaluate the protective effects on vascular endothelial injury. Results Network pharmacology analysis identified 29 active compounds and 231 YYTN-related targets associated with MI/RI, with nine core targets identified by PPI analysis. The PI3K/Akt signaling pathway emerged as a potential key pathway. In OGD/R-chall…

title: Closed-Loop Fabrication of Regenerated Cellulose Battery Separator via Solvent-Guided Structural Regulation
abstract: Abstract The development of battery separators derived from renewable feedstocks that can simultaneously achieve high porosity, robust mechanical strength, excellent thermal stability, reliable electrochemical performance, and satisfactory environmental sustainability remains a core challenge in the field of sustainable energy storage material. Herein, we report a regenerated cellulose membrane prepared through a dissolution/regeneration process using lithium bromide Molecular dynamics simulation results show that water is the effective antisolvent for driving the formation of cellulose–cellulose H-bonds, yielding cellulose with a better crystalline structure. Subsequently, tert-butanol was utilized to replace water in the cellulose membrane precursor prior to drying, preventing capillary-induced pore collapse. This membrane exhibits high porosity of 70.1%, excellent electrolyte uptake capacity of 243.7%, ionic conductivity of 0.77 mS/cm, excellent thermal stability (no shrinkage at 150 °C), and roust mechanical strength. The Na/HC half-cells assembled with this membrane displays high cycle capacity retention rate of 87.1% at 0.1 C after 500 cycles, which is comparable to commercial separators. This membrane fabrication process enables closed-loop solvent recycling, and the membrane fully degraded after 4 months of soil burial, and life cycle assessment indicated lower impacts …

title: Topology-Aware Federated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Dual-Level Voltage Regulation in PV-Rich Distribution Grids
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) generation with high penetration in the distribution networks causes voltage rise, voltage deviation and three-phase imbalance between connected Medium-Voltage (MV) and Low-Voltage (LV) feeders. In this paper, a topology-conscious federated multi-agent reinforcement learning is introduced to subordinated dual-level voltage regulation in PV-rich distribution grids. The given approach represents the network as a graph and implements the state encoding with the help of a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to ensure that every agent is able to represent local electrical state and local topology. Both LV control nodes are considered independent reinforcement learning agents, and the federated aggregation provides the means of updating shared parameters of the model without sharing the raw local measurements. The structure is aimed at minimizing MV voltage violations and LV phase unbalance collaboratively when there are different conditions of PV penetration and communication. The technique is tested on a stochastic load and PV test system on the IEEE 33-bus distribution test system. The findings show that voltage regulation and phase-balancing performance are enhanced when using the centralized RL strategy instead of baseline centralized RL and traditional MARL strategies. The research identifies the promise of topology-conscious learning and federated coordination in the …

title: The relationship of simulation frequency with preparedness and early community action in emergencies of earthquake and tsunami disasters in Gampong Alue Naga Subdistrict Syiah Kuala
abstract: Gampong Alue Naga is a coastal area in Banda Aceh City that is vulnerable to earthquakes and tsunamis. This study aimed to determine the relationship between simulation frequency, community preparedness, and initial response actions during earthquake and tsunami emergencies. This study employed an analytical correlational design with a cross-sectional approach. A total of 140 respondents were selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed using the Chi-Square test and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov 2 Independent Samples test as an alternative analysis because some expected cell counts were less than 5. The results showed that most respondents had a moderate frequency of participation in disaster simulations, comprising 66 respondents (47.1%), a moderate level of preparedness, comprising 100 respondents (71.4%), and a high level of initial response actions, comprising 70 respondents (50.0%). The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test revealed a significant relationship between simulation frequency and community preparedness (Z = 2.729; p < 0.001), as well as between simulation frequency and community initial response actions (Z = 2.893; p < 0.001). These findings indicate that simulation frequency is associated with the level of community preparedness and the ability to perform initial response actions during earthquake and tsunami emergencies. title: Engineering Surface Reconstruction of Perovskite Oxides through Vanadium Doping and Alkalinity Regulation for Enhanced Oxygen Evolution
abstract: Abstract Lattice oxygen participation in perovskite electrocatalysts can significantly enhance oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity, yet it often compromises long-term durability due to severe surface reconstruction and bulk degradation. Here, we deliberately engineer surface reconstruction to reconcile activity and stability by preconstructing a highly active and robust (oxy)hydroxide layer on a perovskite oxide. A vanadium-doped perovskite, SrFe0.25Co0.25Ni0.18V0.02Mo0.3O3 (SFCNM-V0.02), is rationally designed, in which V-doping facilitates rapid OH–-induced reconstruction. Preimmersion in concentrated KOH accelerates the formation of a dense and stable amorphous (oxy)hydroxide layer that suppresses bulk dissolution while serving as the dominant catalytic active phase. Consequently, SFCNM-V0.02 delivers a low overpotential of 265 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and exceptional operational stability exceeding 1100 h in 1 M KOH. Furthermore, by correlating the degree of surface reconstruction with catalytic activity, we analyzed the origin of the pH-dependent variation observed in this work, which provides useful implications for appropriately evaluating pH-dependent behaviors in electrocatalysis. This work demonstrates that controlled surface reconstruction fundamentally governs OER performance in perovskite oxides and provides practical design principles for durable, high-efficiency OER…

title: Frequency of Antibody-Mediated Positive Interference in a Healthy Danish Cohort Using Combined Immunodepletion and Ultracentrifugation with a High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Assay
abstract: Abstract Background Diagnosis of myocardial infarction relies in part on cardiac troponin (cTn) concentrations exceeding the 99th percentile upper reference limit. Positive antibody-mediated interference (PAI) occurs when anti-cTn antibodies form macrotroponin complexes with slow clearance or when heterophilic antibodies generate cTn-independent signals. PAI may inflate the upper reference limit and may increase the risk of missed myocardial infarction. We determined the frequency of PAI using the Abbott Alinity High-Sensitivity cTnI Assay and assessed its impact on the 99th percentile in a healthy Danish reference population. Methods In a cross-sectional cohort of 1053 healthy individuals used to establish Danish 99th percentiles, PAI was assessed in samples within the sex-specific highest 10% of cTn concentrations. Ultracentrifugation and immunodepletion were used to evaluate molecular weight and the effect of IgG removal on measured cTnI. Concordant results from both methods were considered confirmatory for PAI. Sex-specific 99th percentiles were recalculated after excluding individuals with confirmed PAI. Results A low-dilution combined ultracentrifugation and immunodepletion protocol enabled detection of PAI at cTnI concentrations as low as 3.5 ng/L. Among the 86 highest samples, 48 (56%) were classified as PAI, corresponding to an overall frequency of 4.6%. Exclusion of P…

title: Piezoelectrically actuated magnetic dipole twisting resonators enable miniaturized low-frequency antennas
abstract: Miniaturized low-frequency antennas are essential for underwater, underground, and biomedical communications, yet their performance is constrained by the fundamental size-efficiency trade-off, a long-standing physical bottleneck. Here, we introduce a radiation mechanism that circumvents this constraint by replacing the time-varying currents in conventional antennas with the mechanical twisting oscillation of a magnetic dipole. Using piezoelectrically actuated, biomimetic twisting resonators with ultrahigh mechanical quality factors, we demonstrate that low-frequency antennas operating at 15.4 and 668 hertz can be miniaturized to centimeter- and millimeter-scale, respectively, with radiation efficiencies exceeding those of size-matched loop antennas by factors of 49,000 and 5000, respectively. This electromechanical-magnetic transduction enables underwater cross-medium communication over 115 meters with only milliwatt-level power consumption, using 99.9% less power than loop antennas. It also supports implantable wireless devices that achieve a fourfold increase in communication range at identical power consumption, opening a route to long-range, low-power wireless systems capable of operating in some of the most demanding environments.

title: Entre regulação e cultura institucional: a racionalidade técnico-burocrática como matriz da docência universitária técnico-profissional na América Latina
abstract: O artigo analisa criticamente a produção científica latino-americana sobre a Educação Superior, com foco na articulação entre regulação institucional, cultura acadêmica e formação docente técnico-profissional no período de 2005 a 2025. Parte-se do pressuposto de que a literatura tem abordado de forma consistente os efeitos da avaliação institucional e do produtivismo acadêmico, mas tende a tratar de maneira fragmentada as relações entre políticas públicas, cultura institucional e docência universitária. Nesse sentido, o artigo assume as Epistemologias do Sul como lente teórica. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, de natureza teórico-analítica, desenvolvida por meio de revisão narrativa da literatura, com seleção intencional de estudos indexados na base SciELO e orientação interpretativa. A análise foi organizada a partir de três eixos temáticos — regulação e produtivismo, cultura institucional, e formação e identidade docente —, articulados segundo os níveis macro, meso e micro. Os resultados indicam que a racionalidade técnico-burocrática, consolidada por dispositivos avaliativos, opera como matriz organizadora da docência universitária técnico-profissional e como manifestação da Colonialidade do Saber. Essa lógica impõe métricas de consagração do Norte Global, reconfigurando critérios de reconhecimento e hierarquias acadêmicas, além de esvaziar os sentidos atribuídos …

title: Case Report: Running through transplant: preserved aerobic capacity in an elite endurance athlete after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation
abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) imposes profound hematologic, inflammatory, and immunologic stress, and survivors typically show reduced cardiorespiratory fitness that may be further compromised by chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGvHD) and corticosteroid therapy. Competitive, performance-oriented endurance training through these phases has not been described. We report the longitudinal clinical and training course of a 54-year-old elite endurance runner with previously treated Hodgkin lymphoma who resumed structured treadmill exercise on Day +1 after matched-sibling allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma transformed from follicular lymphoma. Daily physiologic training data were aligned with transplant milestones, donor chimerism, donor lymphocyte infusions (DLI), and immunosuppression, and serial cardiopulmonary exercise testing was performed before and after HCT. The patient exercised through marrow aplasia and progressed to timed running within 100 days; he recorded a 5K of 17:55 (Day +314) and a 10K of 41:00 (Day +340), both during active cGvHD on prednisone plus cyclosporine. Directly measured peak oxygen uptake (VO 2 peak) was 75.8 mL/kg/min before HCT and 71.5 mL/kg/min at 7 months post-HCT. Country-level alignment between youth mental health burden and reported workforce capacity
abstract: Objective To assess country-level alignment between youth mental health burden, measured using disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) rates for mental and substance use disorders among individuals aged 10 -24 years, and reported national mental health workforce capacity, and to examine regional differences in this alignment. Methods This ecological analysis linked World Health Organization (WHO) 2021 mental and substance use disorder disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) rates with psychiatrist, psychologist, and mental health nurse densities from 2013 to 2017. Of the 196 countries with complete burden estimates, 193 had World Bank fiscal year (FY) 2022 income classifications and 139 had at least two core workforce indicators. The burden measure assigned equal weight to each of the three 5-year age groups. Percentile gaps were calculated by subtracting workforce percentiles from burden percentiles across the 139-country sample. Additional analyses compared staffing densities, described burden at five time points from 2001 to 2021, and tested sensitivity to economic, index, workforce-year, and spatial specifications. Results The Eastern Mediterranean had the highest median gap (30.9 points), with 10 of 15 countries meeting the high-burden–low-capacity screen. title: Репродуктивное способности и продольжительное использования коров таджикской черно-пестрой породы в условиях Республики Таджикистан
abstract: The article examines the reproductive capacity and length of productive use of Tajik Black-and-White cows. The study was carried out in 2022–2025 on farms of the Isfara, Konibodom and Bobojon Gafurov districts of the Sughd region (northern part) and the Hisor district (central part) of the Republic of Tajikistan. In the central and northern farms, respectively, the age at first insemination was 18.2–19.6 and 21.4–23.2 months, the age at first calving 27.2–28.6 and 30.4–32.2 months, the service period 76.5–79.7 and 89.5–100.5 days, and the conception rate at first insemination 54.8–56.1 and 48.6–52.3%. The reproductive capacity coefficient ranged from 0.82 to 1.00. Cows were used for 6.54–7.12 lactations in the central farms and 5.65–6.64 lactations in the northern farms. As the proportion of Holstein blood increased, the number of calvings with a fatal outcome decreased, and 3/4 Holstein crossbreds calved more easily than Tajik-type Black-and-White cows. Cows born in autumn and winter stayed in the herd 1.1–1.5 lactations longer than those born in spring and summer and, as the most productive animals with a strong constitution, are recommended for herd replacement.

title: Influence of Pressure-Cooking Parameters on the Color, Texture, Nutrient Composition, Antioxidant Capacity, Flavor and Sensory Profile of Drumstick (Moringa oleifera)
abstract: Our country’s rich culinary culture has allowed us to enjoy a variety of vegetables and fruits, resulting in several health benefits. Drumstick, also known as Moringa oleifera, is a remarkable vegetable that is highly regarded and piques our curiosity. Therefore, the aim of the present study focused mainly on the effects of pressure cooking on the physicochemical, nutritional, antioxidant, flavor, and sensory profiles of drumsticks. The drumstick-water ratio and the amount of salt used during pressure cooking varied. The total phenol content and DPPH activity of pressure-cooked drumsticks ranged from 0.29–0.48 mg GAE/g and 31.76–56.70%, respectively. The flavor profiles consisted of 9 aldehydes, 2 alcohols, 5 organic compounds, 2 sulfur compounds, and ketones. Additionally, the phytonutrients identified by /MS were n-hexadecanoic acid, d-glucitol, 1-S-heptyl-1-thio-, benzeneacetonitrile, 4-hydroxy-, benzeneacetonitrile, 3-hydroxy-, and d-glucitol and 1-S-heptyl-1-thio-. Treatment T3 resulted in a high sensory score, whereas T9 resulted in a poor sensory score. Hierarchical cluster analysis supported the sensory results with nutrient components and grouped the treatments into four groups: Raw, A (T1-T4), B (T5 & T8), C (T9), and D (T6 & T7). The principal component analysis categorized all 19 data sets of treatments into four principal components. The results of this study revea…

title: Causes of Occupational Stress among Traffic Police Officers in Urban Tanzania: Evidence from Msimbazi, Dar es Salaam
abstract: Purpose: This study identified the causes of occupational stress among traffic police officers at Msimbazi Police Station in Ilala District, Dar es Salaam, one of the busiest traffic-policing environments in Tanzania. Design/methodology/approach: A convergent parallel mixed-methods design guided by the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) Theory and the Transactional Theory of Stress and Coping was used. Questionnaires were completed by 200 of 218 sampled respondents (91.7%), and 14 key informants, including senior traffic officers and guidance and counselling officials, were interviewed. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative data thematically. Findings: Occupational stress was high (overall mean = 3.95). Long working hours (M = 4.03; 81.0% agreement), poor working conditions (M = 4.01; 80.0%) and heavy workload (M = 4.00; 79.0%) were the strongest stressors, followed by exposure to public aggression (M = 3.89; 75.0%) and lack of support from superiors (M = 3.80; 71.0%). Interviews showed that extended shifts without adequate rest and confrontations with aggressive road users reduced officers’ concentration, energy and composure. Research limitations/implications: The study was confined to one urban station and relied on self-reported perceptions, which limits generalisation. title: Faster Transactions, Persistent Queues: Efficiency of Immigration Service Delivery under the E-Border Management System at Julius Nyerere International Airport
abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated the efficiency of immigration service delivery after the implementation of the E-Border Management System (EBMS) at Julius Nyerere International Airport (JNIA), Tanzania. Design/methodology/approach: A mixed-methods design guided by the Technology Acceptance Model and Diffusion of Innovation Theory was used. Structured questionnaires were completed by 399 respondents (international and Tanzanian passengers, immigration officers, airport staff, IT personnel and ground handlers), 18 key informants were interviewed, and system and annual performance reports were reviewed alongside five days of non-participant observation. Findings: Perceived efficiency was satisfactory (overall M = 4.08, SD = 0.74). Transaction-level indicators were rated highest, processing time (M = 4.16), clearance speed (M = 4.14) and document verification (M = 4.13), while system-level indicators such as waiting time (M = 3.99) and throughput (M = 3.90) were lower. Administrative records showed average processing time falling from 45 to 22 minutes between 2017 and 2022 and throughput rising from 12 to 22 passengers per officer per hour, while downtime incidents rose from 127 to 171 between 2020 and 2022. title: РЕЦЕНЗУВАННЯ КНИГ НА СТОРІНКАХ ЖУРНАЛУ “COSTUME” (2017–2020) В ОРГАНІЗАЦІЇ ДОСЛІДЖЕНЬ З ІСТОРІЇ КОСТЮМА
abstract: Мета роботи – охарактеризувати роль книжкових рецензій у журналі «Costume» в організації досліджень з історії костюма, визначити масштаб і динаміку рецензійного корпусу, його авторську структуру, тематичні пріоритети та основні функції рецензій. Методологія дослідження ґрунтується на поєднанні принципів історизму та об’єктивності, корпусного, контент- і функціонального аналізу, порівняльно-історичного методу, бібліографічного й системного підходів. Наукова новизна визначається тим, що рецензійний розділ «Book Reviews» уперше розглянуто як цілісний сегмент наукової комунікації та механізм організації дисциплінарного поля історії костюма: установлено кількісний масштаб і часову оперативність рецензування, охарактеризовано авторську структуру, простежено участь представників редакційної колегії, визначено основні функції рецензій та їх поєднання. Досліджений корпус дає підстави розглядати його як достатньо репрезентативний для аналізу редакційної та комунікативної практики журналу. Mechanism of Tongfeng Qingxiao Prescription in treating gouty arthritis: a correlation study of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway and macrophage polarization
abstract: Objective The global incidence of gouty arthritis (GA) is continuously rising, and conventional Western medical treatments have certain limitations. The Chinese herbal compound Tongfeng Qingxiao Prescription (TFQXP) has achieved definite clinical efficacy. This study aimed to explore potential molecular correlates underlying the therapeutic effect of TFQXP for GA. Methods An MSU-induced GA rat model was established. DIA proteomics was applied to screen core differentially expressed proteins and enriched signaling pathways. Subsequent in vivo experiments adopted ELISA, Western blot, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry to detect inflammatory mediators including IFN-γ, iNOS, IL-12, IL-23, NO and IL-10, as well as indicators related to macrophage polarization and the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway. Results A total of 1852 common proteins were identified across four groups. Totally 112 differentially expressed proteins were screened between the model group and blank group, and 170 between the TFQXP high-dose group and model group. title: An alternate mechanism for the production of garnet zoning: a case study from the contact aureole of the Western Adamello Tonalite, northern Italy
abstract: Abstract Correct geological interpretation of garnet compositional zoning relies on recognising the mechanisms responsible for producing the zonation. Two generations of garnet are observed in the Western Adamello Tonalite contact aureole. A Variscan generation of garnet predates the intrusion while a second generation is associated with contact metamorphism. We show how the second generation of garnet forms via replacement of the first generation of garnet through interface-coupled dissolution-reprecipitation. While compositional zoning profiles in garnet could be mistaken for diffusional relaxation of an initially sharp epitaxial overgrowth, misfit between the compositional zoning and the unreasonable timescales produced by multicomponent diffusion modelling illustrates that this is not the case. Further, we demonstrate through reaction-transport modelling that the reaction from old to new garnet composition must be dissolution rather than transport-limited. The compositional zoning across the old/new garnet interface is produced by a density gradient in micro-fractures at the replacement interface rather than diffusional transport through a pore-fluid. Through the modelling of dissolution rates, we estimate that the replacement of the precursor garnet by the new garnet generation would have occurred on a timescale of hundreds to thousands of years. title: AttentioScope: a multi-indicator quantification framework with attention mechanism based on thyroid fine-needle aspiration smear images
abstract: The interpretability of deep learning models is crucial for their clinical application in computational pathology. Although attention-based methods can provide intuitive heatmap explanations, their reliability on challenging samples still requires systematic, fine-grained evaluation tools to assess model performance more comprehensively. To this end, this paper proposes a multi-metric quantitative framework based on thyroid fine-needle aspiration smear images to evaluate the comprehensive performance of different models through visual analysis. First, the framework assesses the reliability and focus capability of attention distributions by computing multi-dimensional quantitative metrics such as entropy, concentration, stability, and compactness of the attention heatmaps. Second, by correlating the heatmaps with underlying image features, it identifies whether models rely on pathology-irrelevant low-level features. To validate the effectiveness of the framework, we systematically evaluated four mainstream attention-based multiple instance learning (MIL) models (CLAM, TransMIL, PEGTB-MIL, ADMIL) on athyroid fine-needle aspiration smear image dataset. Experimental results show that in challenging samples of high-performance models, attention mechanisms may exhibit patterns such as feature hijacking or spatial bias, which traditional performance metrics fail to effectively reveal.…

abstract: Метою статті є комплексне історико-правове дослідження правового статусу органів державної безпеки Української РСР у механізмі радянської державної влади впродовж 1946–1991 рр. title: Minga as a meta-mechanism for inclusive entrepreneurship: the case of Salinas’ community-based enterprises
abstract: Purpose This study explores how the minga, an Andean indigenous communal work system, functions as a meta-mechanism for inclusive entrepreneurship. By analyzing community-based enterprises (CBEs) in Salinas, Ecuador, it examines how the minga mobilizes resources, navigates institutional complexity and fosters inclusive socioeconomic processes and outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Employing a qualitative case study, the research focuses on Salinas as a paradigmatic CBEs ecosystem grounded in the minga. Data were collected through 23 semi-structured interviews with community members and enterprise leaders, participant observation of minga events and analysis of organizational archives. Guided by the resource-based view and Bourdieu’s theory of capital conversion as complementary lenses, the study abductively uncovers the underlying mechanisms that render inclusion a constitutive feature of entrepreneurship. Findings The study reveals that minga operates across three layers: (1) a normative layer that institutionalizes reciprocity and collective welfare, countering individualistic entrepreneurial models, (2) a relational layer that fosters a heterarchical structure that integrates diverse community members and (3) an operational layer that embeds inclusion through task allocation, conflict resolution and benefit-sharing. Together, these layers form a recursive architecture in …

title: Research on the Implementation Deviation and Correction Mechanism of Local Government Green Energy Promotion Policies
abstract: Green energy promotion policies designed by China's central government are carried out mainly by local governments, whose choices determine whether national targets for renewable energy deployment are converted into approved projects, installed capacity, and actual consumption. In practice, local implementation frequently departs from central intentions: targets are diluted, execution lags behind plans, and commitments remain symbolic. Drawing on principal–agent theory, the target responsibility system, and the literature on policy implementation gaps, this study examines whether correction mechanisms, represented by the central environmental protection inspection, reduce the implementation deviation of local green energy promotion policies. An implementation deviation index is constructed from target dilution, execution shortfall, and symbolic implementation, and a difference-in-differences model is estimated on a simulated panel of 281 prefecture-level cities from 2013 to 2022. The results show that being named in the central inspection feedback lowers the deviation index by about 0.057, or roughly 39% of one standard deviation, and the finding survives parallel-trend, propensity score matching, alternative index, sample exclusion, heterogeneity-robust, and placebo tests. Mechanism tests indicate that the correction operates through stronger political accountability, larger f…
venue: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies

title: Triarm Polycaprolactone Interface for Spatially Controlled Functionalization of Carbon Nanotube Fibers
abstract: Abstract Carbon nanotube fibers (CNTF) with exceptional strength, electrical, and thermal conductivities possess the potential for deployment in electrochemical and analytical applications. For such applications, CNTF are typically encapsulated using polymeric interface membranes such as polyvinyl chloride (PVC) for accommodating functional elements or recognition molecules. These membranes typically assemble stochastically on CNTF surfaces owing to the nonuniform interfacial interaction energies between the characteristic groups of the polymers and the CNTF surface. This stochastic assembly of encapsulating membranes subsequently inhibits the homogeneous distribution of recognition molecules on the CNTF surface, which influences the analytical performances. Herein, a triarm polycaprolactone (3-PCL) block copolymer is designed to homogenize the interfacial energies between the polymeric membranes and the CNTF surface. The 3-PCL interface is hypothesized to enable spatially controlled assembly of polymeric membranes on the CNTF surface and subsequently a homogeneous distribution of recognition molecules. As an illustration, the CNTF with a 3-PCL interface is demonstrated as an ion-selective microelectrode (ISE) for selective and sensitive detection of ammonium ions (NH4+) via homogeneous incorporation of a NH4+-specific ionophores within an encapsulating PVC membrane on the CNTF…

title: DDA-BNN v1.0: a morphology-aware surrogate model for the optical properties of black carbon-containing particles
abstract: Black carbon (BC) is the most strongly absorbing component of atmospheric aerosol and significantly impacts Earth's energy balance. The optical properties of BC-containing particles depend on particle-level variability in size, chemical composition, and internal morphology. Such particle-level details are not easily represented in large-scale atmospheric models. Existing parameterizations typically assume idealized particle geometries (e.g., homogeneous spheres or concentric core–shell spheres) and homogeneous mixing, which can yield biased predictions and provide no quantitative estimate of model-form uncertainty at the single-particle level. In this work, we present a probabilistic framework for predicting the optical properties of individual BC-containing particles using a hybrid Bayesian neural network (BNN) model trained on discrete dipole approximation (DDA) simulations. The hybrid BNN is a flexible combination of deterministic and Bayesian layers allowing for more realistic treatment of particle optical properties and quantification of uncertainty. The hybrid BNN model predicts extinction efficiency, single-scattering albedo, and asymmetry parameter and returns predictive uncertainty that can be decomposed into aleatoric (data-driven variability) and epistemic (uncertainty due to limited training coverage) components. We show that the hybrid BNN outperforms homogeneous-s…
