Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS2 thin films
abstract: Abstract Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are promising laser-gain media for their direct bandgap and strong excitonic effects. However, existing TMD lasers typically rely on mechanically exfoliated or high-temperature chemical-vapor-deposition-grown materials, with their atomic-scale thickness inherently limiting the available optical gain volume. Here, we report room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS 2 (BM-MoS 2 ) thin films in whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) cavities. Using solution exfoliation and spray coating under ambient conditions, we produce area- and thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films composed of electronically decoupled MoS 2 monolayers separated by organic spacers. This layered architecture preserves the intrinsic monolayer excitonic properties while providing a tunable gain volume beyond that of an isolated monolayer. Integrated with WGM cavities, the thickness-scalable BM-MoS 2 films enable a balance between the quality ( Q ) and optical confinement ( $$\varGamma$$ Γ ) factors. Power-dependent measurements reveal key lasing signatures, including a threshold-like input-output crossover accompanied by linewidth narrowing at a pump power of approximately 1.4 nW, and pump-induced polarization selection. Solution-processable BM-MoS 2 thus offers a scalable gain medium for thin-film laser photonics…

title: Thermodynamic and kinetic control of precursor chemistry for stable Fe–Mo/activated carbon catalysts in hydrodesulfurization of heavy naphtha
Additionality of climate benefits from emission reduction and carbon dioxide removal
abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide removal (CDR) has been identified as a necessary complement to industrial decarbonization for climate change mitigation. Marine CDR (mCDR) approaches, such as ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean capture (DOC), have received considerable attention for their potential to counteract ocean acidification while simultaneously reducing atmospheric CO 2 . However, most model-based assessments of mCDR efficacy either assume a fixed background atmospheric CO 2 value or adopt an idealized future CO 2 trajectory, thereby excluding impacts of important carbon cycle feedbacks that repartition carbon between the ocean, atmosphere, and biosphere. Here, we use an Earth system model to address three core questions: whether the net CO 2 effect of CDR depends on background emissions; whether CDR technologies deployed simultaneously yield additive CO 2 reductions; and whether there is synergy between the radiative forcing (climate) benefits of CDR and emission reductions. We evaluate permutations of direct air capture, OAE, and DOC, quantifying their individual and combined CO 2 effects under various emissions scenarios. We find that the radiative forcing effects of emissions reductions and CDR are largely additive through time, regardless of background emission scenario or CDR type or scale. Furthermore, any given quantity and type of short-term CDR deployme…

title: Sustainable valorization of pineapple leaf waste into biocompatible activated carbon for biomedical and food applications
Spatial modelling of available aluminum in glacial till: informing a boreal forest soil carbon predictor
abstract: Boreal forest soils store 30 % of global forest soil carbon, making them a crucial component of the carbon cycle. However, climate change at high latitudes is increasing temperatures and producing unpredictable precipitation patterns. Soil organic carbon (SOC) formation and stabilization is tied to precipitation patterns, thus climate change will inevitably influence the stability and longevity of boreal forest SOC. The current size and distribution of this reservoir is poorly understood, creating uncertainty under current and future climate scenarios. Previous research demonstrates mineral soil properties may be used to model boreal forest SOC accurately. The surface slope, depth of carbon enriched horizon, and climate characteristics are important parameters for modelling SOC and can generally be obtained or estimated via remote sensing. However, information about the availability of reactive aluminum – non-crystalline forms capable of interacting with organic matter to form stable carbon rich organometal complexes in mineral soils – is not widely available but is controlled by the weatherable aluminum in soil parent material. To bridge this gap, the Newfoundland and Labrador till geochemistry dataset was used here to map and model weatherable aluminum availability in glacial till across the island of Newfoundland as a function of geology and climate. The Random Forest Algori…

title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production
abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO x (NO and NO 2 ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.
venue_publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science

title: When the Carbon Registry Is Wrong: Finality, Correctability and Loss Allocation in Asian Carbon Markets
abstract: Abstract A registry error can leave two parties claiming the same carbon allowance. This article asks when an error should still be reversed and who bears the loss once it cannot be. Comparing China, Korea and Vietnam with European Union law, it ranks remedies by their social cost. An error found before a good-faith acquisition should normally be reversed. After a good-faith acquisition or an accepted surrender, the recorded transfer should normally stand, leaving the original holder a money claim. The registry operator should bear its processing errors and users their input mistakes; a pooled fund should cover only registry-error losses that ordinary claims cannot recover. Any replacement allowance must be offset. China makes the registry decide who holds an allowance, Korea authorises correction and Vietnam requires reconciliation, but none settles how correction affects a good-faith acquirer, a completed surrender or the original holder.
venue: Asian Journal of Law and Economics

title: Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Efficiency and Responses of Recalcitrant Dissolved Organic Carbon Under Future Emissions Scenarios
abstract: Abstract Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is increasingly regarded as a promising ocean-based carbon dioxide removal strategy because it can enhance oceanic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) uptake while alleviating ocean acidification. However, regional differences in OAE efficiency and the associated responses of recalcitrant dissolved organic carbon (RDOC) remain poorly constrained. Here, we incorporate a microbial carbon pump (MCP) module into the carbon-centric Grid-Enabled Integrated Earth System Model (cGENIE) to assess the carbon sequestration potential of OAE and the RDOC response under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios SSP2-45 and SSP5-85 across different regional deployment configurations. By explicitly linking OAE with MCP-mediated RDOC dynamics, our study extends previous carbonate-chemistry-focused assessments to include long-term inorganic–organic carbon feedbacks. In idealized simulations with sustained OAE deployment beginning in 2030 CE, atmospheric CO 2 concentrations are (62–75)×10 −6 lower and global mean surface temperatures are 0.15–0.21 °C lower by 2100 CE than in the corresponding simulations without OAE. Alkalinity deployment in the Northwest Pacific yields the highest long-term efficiency and strongest local surface alkalinity enhancement among the configurations tested. OAE also induces distinct long-term responses among dissolved organic carbo…
venue: Journal of Ocean University of China

title: Effect of additives on physical characteristics, combustion behavior, and pollutant emission of co-pellets produced from torrefied-biomass and semi-dried sewage sludge
abstract: Abstract Co-pelletizing torrefied Camellia oleifera shell (TCOS) with semi-dried sewage sludge (SS) can improve pellet quality but may create new challenges in pollutant emissions and ash slagging. To address these challenges, single and blended CaO/kaolin additives were evaluated for their effects on the physical properties, combustion behavior, emissions, and ash fusion characteristics of the co-pellets. Additives increased compaction energy by 4.09% – 17.43% but had little effect on extrusion energy or pellet density. The single addition of kaolin reduced cumulative SO 2 from 1.17 to 0.97 mg and PM0.1 by 29.72%, while raising ash fusion temperatures (AFT) and lowering the slagging index. The single addition of CaO advanced the NO 2 emission peak, but reduced AFT by up to 118℃, increasing the slagging tendency. For blended additions, TCS-Ca3K1 gave the lowest cumulative NO 2 (3.31 mg), while TCS-Ca1K3 achieved the greatest PM 0.1 reduction (28.75%). XRD confirmed CaSO4 in CaO-added pellets and KAlSiO 4 in kaolin-containing pellets. These results indicate that CaO and kaolin target different pollutants and ash risks, and their ratio can be tailored to balance emission control and slagging mitigation.
venue: International Journal of Coal Science & Technology

title: Sea ice variability and links to East Siberian permafrost carbon remobilization during the last glacial-interglacial transition
abstract: Sea ice plays a central role in the polar climate system, and its rapid decline in the Arctic over recent decades has altered surface albedo and the exchange of heat and gases between the ocean and atmosphere. Investigations of earlier warming events, such as the Preboreal/Early Holocene (PB/EH, 11–8 kyr B.P.), Bølling-Allerød (B/A, 14.7–12.9 kyr B.P.), and Dansgaard Oeschger event 3 (DO-3, 28–27.5 kyr B.P.), likely hold clues on climate system responses to changes in Arctic sea ice. This study explores the history of sea ice over the Southern Lomonosov Ridge and its potential relation to permafrost carbon remobilization. Sea ice conditions over the last 27 kyrs were reconstructed through a combination of the sea ice biomarker IP 25 (Ice Proxy 25) and marine phytoplankton biomarkers (brassicasterol and dinosterol) from the chronologically well-constrained core 31-PC, sampled at the Southern Lomonosov Ridge during the SWERUS-C3 expedition in 2014. The reconstruction allowed for a direct comparison with previously published terrestrial organic carbon (terrOC) remobilization history from the same core. Our findings revealed a seasonal sea ice cover between 27–26 kyr B.P. after the DO-3 warm event, which likely caused more heat and moisture transport from ocean to land and strengthened permafrost thawing along the nearby coastline. A perennial sea ice cover then developed and persi…

title: Regulating the Spin-State and Frontier Orbital of a Molecular FePc Catalyst by Interlayer Electronic Coupling for Enhanced ORR Activity
abstract: Abstract Development of efficient and durable catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction is essential for the advancement of metal–air batteries and fuel cells, yet it remains a significant challenge. Here, we present an interlayer-coupling strategy to modulate iron phthalocyanine by adjacent carbon-supported cobalt species. The resulting FePc@CoNC demonstrates superior ORR activity, with a half-wave potential of 0.927 V and achieving a peak power density of 336 mW cm–2 alongside cycling stability exceeding 1527 cycles. Density functional theory analysis reveals that the adjacent Co single atoms and Co nanoparticles synergistically enhance the localization of Fe dz2 electrons while suppressing spin polarization of Fe 3d orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes adsorption energetics of key intermediates involved in the rate-determining step, thereby accelerating ORR kinetics. These results elucidate the significance of interlayer electronic coupling in axially tuning spin states and frontier orbitals of molecular Fe–N4 centers, offering a general strategy for enhancing oxygen electrocatalysis through electronic structure engineering.

title: Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
Balancing competitiveness and inclusion: a systematic review of smallholder integration models within Sub-Saharan African cashew value chains
abstract: Purpose This study aims to synthesise rigorous evidence on smallholder integration models in Sub-Saharan African cashew value chains and assess whether they simultaneously deliver commercial competitiveness and inclusive development for approximately three million smallholder farmers. Design/methodology/approach A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review searched Scopus and Google Scholar. After eligibility screening and quality appraisal (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool), we retained 39 empirical studies from eight Sub-Saharan African countries for narrative synthesis. Findings We identified seven integration model types across 23 studies; the remaining 16 examined production, land use or welfare without documenting a discrete arrangement. Contract farming alone showed consistently positive competitiveness findings but also the most consistently adverse gender findings. Of 11 studies reporting productivity, four were positive, three negative and three null. Participation barriers (15 studies) and governance inclusion (6) were uniformly adverse. Research limitations/implications The evidence base is concentrated in Ghana (53.8% of studies); Côte d'Ivoire, the world's largest raw cashew producer, is represented by only one study. Designs are predominantly cross-sectional and outcome-associational rather than causal. Future research should prioritise longitudinal designs, governance-…

title: Energy-efficient building heating through simultaneous heat transfer enhancement and pressure reduction in nanofluid-based panel radiators
Structural health monitoring via a knowledge-integration framework: prospective spatial early-warning analysis of the NPL footbridge
abstract: Introduction Condition monitoring of ageing bridges still relies mostly on periodic inspection, which identifies damage only after it has developed. This study seeks to develop prospective monitoring, in which routine sensor data give warning that the structural condition of bridges is changing while there is still time to act. The physical idea we draw on is critical slowing, where a structure approaching a change of state recovers more slowly from small disturbances and becomes more variable. The challenge is to turn this idea into a practical detector that can work on ordinary bridge instrumentation, separate real structural change from seasonal effects, and be evaluated without any information flowing backwards from the evaluation period into the method’s training. Methods We study the National Physical Laboratory (NPL) Footbridge, an instrumented reinforced-concrete cantilever, using its tilt and temperature records for May to October 2012. The entire pipeline is prospective: the environmental correction is a deliberately simple regression fitted on the stable baseline only, chosen after a fuller 17-term model proved too ill-conditioned for reliable extrapolation; the detectors are fitted, calibrated, and evaluated on strictly separated time windows. Results The spatial pattern is clear under this pipeline: all three sensors in the damage zone show a significant rise in va…

title: Environmental Performance and Renewable Resources: The Impact on Economic Growth in the Emerging and Developing Economies
abstract: This study investigates the impacts of environmental performance measured by CO2 emission from industrial processes and renewable capacity measured by electricity production from renewable sources excluding hydroelectric on economic growth in emerging and developing economies. The analysis uses time-series data over the period 2000–2025 and three World Bank aggregates based on historical series of income levels (low, lower-middle, and upper-middle). Foreign direct investment inflows, trade openness, urbanization, and in an original way, the country policy and institutional assessment (CPIA) index—as a proxy for the quality of the institutional and business environment—were included as control variables. The results show that the growth effects of environmental performance, renewable capacity, and institutional quality differ markedly across income levels. Growth persistence emerges only in upper-middle-income economies, whereas in low- and lower-middle-income aggregates growth does not depend significantly on its previous levels. Carbon intensity from industrial processes is positively and significantly associated with growth only in the lower-middle-income group, indicating that carbon-based industrial production still fuels expansion at intermediate development stages. Renewable capacity does not exert significant growth effects in any group. Trade openness promotes growth in…

Prolonged Warm Acclimation Alters Tissue Morphology, Energy Metabolism, and Cellular Responses to Acute Heat Stress in Atlantic Salmon (Salmo salar
abstract: Abstract Thermal acclimation can enhance heat tolerance in cold-water fish, but the associated multi-tissue histological changes, energy-metabolism indices, and cellular stress-response gene expression patterns in Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ) remain unclear. Juvenile Atlantic salmon initially maintained at 16 °C were acclimated at 23 °C for 45 d, returned to 16 °C for 48 h, and then exposed acutely to 23 or 26 °C. Thermal acclimation significantly increased the critical thermal maximum ( CT max ) by about 2 °C, and the elevated CT max persisted after 48 h at 16 °C. Histological analysis revealed gill lamellar thickening, lamellar bending and shortening, epithelial lifting, epithelial vacuolization, and mucous cell hypertrophy. In skeletal muscle, acclimation enhanced the proportion of smaller fibers but reduced that of large fibers. Glycogen and triglyceride contents declined significantly in both liver and skeletal muscle, while lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and malate dehydrogenase (MDH) activities were markedly elevated only in the liver. After acclimated fish were returned to 16 °C for 48 h, the expression of selected stress-response genes, including hsp10, hsp70, gpx , and gr , was remarkably higher in the intestine and skeletal muscle than in non-acclimated fish. During acute heat exposure, acclimated fish showed tissue- and temperature-specific transcriptional responses…

title: Twin transition in construction industry: a systematic review of digital and green integration and a firm-level research agenda
abstract: Purpose Construction firms must digitalise and decarbonise simultaneously, but whether they combine the two programmes is not known. This review maps how the twin transition, the joint pursuit of digitalisation and sustainability, is conceptualised and implemented in the construction sector, and sets out an agenda for firm-level research. Design/methodology/approach Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searches were run in Web of Science and Scopus, combining “twin transition” with digitalisation and sustainability terms. After two-stage screening, 78 peer-reviewed papers were coded against a structured protocol, complemented by a VOSviewer keyword co-occurrence analysis. Findings The literature is expanding rapidly but remains conceptually fragmented. Only a small minority of studies use the term “twin transition” explicitly, none uses the firm-level term twin transformation and most frame digitalisation as the driver of sustainability rather than the reverse. A clear gap separates recommendation from observation: few papers examine the direction of the relationship or whether digital and green programmes are run jointly or in parallel, and firm-level empirical evidence is limited and concentrated in Chinese companies. Technical and data barriers, missing standards and capability gaps dominate the obstacles, while digital tools, organisational capabilities and policy mechanisms d…

An IoT System for Real-Time Energy Supervision of Public Lighting Circuits in Electrical Distribution Networks
abstract: Public lighting circuits require continuous supervision to relate their electrical consumption to the operating status of the luminaires and to detect deviations before a field inspection. An Internet of Things system is developed for real-time electrical supervision using a PZEM-004T v3.0, an ESP32, cellular communication through A9G, and a web-based supervisory platform. The node acquires voltage, current, active power, accumulated energy, frequency, and power factor; active power is used together with a configurable average power to estimate the number of luminaires in operation. Under a representative condition, 218.5 V, 5.844 A, 892.3 W, and 82658 Wh were recorded, with 13 estimated luminaires. In an alert test, a configuration of 14 luminaires produced an estimate of 11.9 units and activated the load-reduction record. The system also recorded a shutdown event with 12103.0 Wh and a deviation of -0.1 %. Historical profiles distinguish operation with relatively stable power from another with repetitive variations during the service period. The architecture converts aggregated electrical measurements into operational indicators for remote supervision and inspection prioritization. The evaluation corresponds to functional validation; metrological accuracy requires subsequent comparison with certified instrumentation.
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering

title: From Skills Gaps to Energy Resilience: Building a Territorialized Solar Workforce Ecosystem in Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia’s electricity plan for 2025–2034 projects 69.5 GW of additional generation capacity, including 17.1 GW of solar power, while government estimates associate the plan with 348,057 solar-related job opportunities. These projections make workforce capability a material implementation issue: renewable infrastructure requires technicians, engineers, safety specialists, project managers and locally available operations-and-maintenance personnel. Yet headline job estimates do not reveal whether workers are available in the required occupations, locations or project phases. This article examines how workforce development can be linked to the resilience of solar infrastructure in an archipelagic state. It uses a focused qualitative documentary analysis, official Indonesian planning and employment documents, and international institutional evidence, interpreted through energy security, capacity development and energy justice perspectives. The analysis identifies four interlocking governance gaps: incomplete skills intelligence; weak alignment between training, certification and project demand; uneven territorial distribution of operational capability; and limited feedback from infrastructure performance into workforce planning. The article proposes a territorialized solar workforce resilience framework in which workforce data, competency standards, work-based learning, local mai…

title: Network pharmacology, gut microbiota, and metabolomics integration reveal that Shenshuai 'an enema prescription (SSAEP) improves CRF mechanisms by reshaping the gut microbiota and correcting host–microbe cometabolism
abstract: Abstract Background Chronic renal failure (CRF) is a global health issue, and the “gut–kidney axis” plays a key role in its pathogenesis. Shenshuai 'an enema prescription (SSAEP) is a Chinese medicine compound based on the TCM theory of “regulation of bowel movement and removal of turbid qi”, which has shown good adjunctive therapeutic effects in delaying the progression of CRF in clinical practice. However, its specific mechanisms remain unclear. Purpose Herein, from the perspective of indirect pharmacology, the therapeutic effects of SSAEP on CRF rats were explored. We hypothesize that its mechanism of action may be largely indirect and occurs primarily through the gut–kidney axis. This study aimed to systematically elucidate the potential mechanism through which SSAEP improves CRF through the regulation of gut microecology using multidisciplinary approaches such as network pharmacology, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and metabonomics. Methods A CRF rat model was established by induction with 2.5% adenine. Low and high doses of SSAEP were administered via enema, and antibiotic intervention and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments were performed to verify the key mediating role of the gut microbiota. The chemical composition of the SSAEP and the metabolic profiles of the serum and colonic contents of the rats were analyzed using UHPLC‒MS/MS; the composition of the gut…

title: Integration of Lean and Six Sigma approaches to software development in improving quality processes of dry transformers
abstract: Purpose This article aimed to use Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma approaches in the development of software to improve the quality process of the dry-type transformer industry by developing an automated validation system implemented through an object-oriented software architecture. Design/methodology/approach This study was based on an action research case conducted at a transformer and electric motor manufacturing company in Santa Catarina, Brazil. Software was developed to reduce failures related to coil dimensions, optimizing the data review process, previously performed manually. The solution was integrated with the company's enterprise resource planning (ERP) and engineering project management. Some development standards adopted were Model-View-ViewModel and Composite for data structuring and validation, in addition to Lean and Six Sigma approaches. Findings During the first six months of application, a potential cost reduction of around US$2000 was identified, eliminating approximately 2.33% of the total nonconformities recorded in the period and 2.26% of the costs related to these failures. Problems such as incorrect turns, diameters outside the specified limits and incompatible materials were avoided, promoting greater process reliability. The application of Lean and Six Sigma ensured a structured approach to identify and eliminate process failures, promoting gains in …
venue: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management

title: Soberania digital em disputa: governança dos territórios, colonialismos e design tecnológico no Sul Global
abstract: Este artigo discute a tecnopolítica em torno do conceito de soberania digital a partir de perspectivas críticas ao colonialismo, problematizando seus significados e valores segundo dois eixos: a relação entre Norte e Sul Global, e a tensão entre os âmbitos nacional e popular. Identifica a origem da noção de soberania no pensamento europeu moderno com os processos históricos de colonização e a persistência da colonialidade do poder nas tecnologias de informação e comunicação (TIC) e em seu design. A partir de autores como Álvaro Vieira Pinto, Frantz Fanon e Aníbal Quijano, sustenta-se que a soberania dos países periféricos não pode ser compreendida nos mesmos termos do Norte Global, exigindo uma rearticulação entre soberania nacional e soberania popular como condição para processos efetivos de descolonização. O artigo propõe a discussão sobre uma soberania digital que tensione os âmbitos nacional e popular, fundamentada na mobilização social e na construção de uma consciência crítica coletiva. Analisa-se como as TICs reconfiguram as dinâmicas de poder global, dando origem a novas estratégias de colonização, como o colonialismo digital e a colonialidade do fazer. Discute-se como a concentração tecnológica nas grandes corporações do Norte Global reforça a dependência do Sul Global, mas também revela brechas para práticas situadas e contra-hegemônicas. Por fim, são apresentadas ini…

title: Revealing the dusty shell of the semi-regular variable V CVn
abstract: The semi-regular variable star V CVn exhibits a highly variable optical linear polarization, yet its position angle (PA) has remained remarkably stable at approximately 100^̧irc ± 20^̧irc over several decades. We present a comprehensive multi-technique study of the system covering six pulsation cycles from 2020 to 2025. This campaign includes high-cadence photopolarimetry, spectropolarimetry, and the first interferometric observations of V CVn using the Center for High Angular Resolution Astronomy (CHARA) array in 2024 and 2025. Our photopolarimetric data reveal a significant increase in polarization, reaching peaks of up to 6% during the 2023--2025 cycles, during which time the characteristic anticorrelation with brightness and the stability of the PA persisted. The interferometric observations resolve the stellar photosphere but show no evidence of large-scale asymmetric structures, such as a bow shock or isolated scattering arcs, at the scales and sensitivities probed. Based on these results, we rule out previous models that invoke interstellar medium (ISM) interactions or static reflection clouds as the primary drivers of the observed polarization. Instead, we propose a circumstellar disk or flattened envelope—analogous to the L_2 Puppis system—as the most plausible explanation. We hypothesize that this stable geometry is shaped or maintained by the star's high proper motio…

title: Design, moda e interculturalidade: metodologia que emerge do território e universidade indígena Aldeia Marakanã
abstract: O artigo analisa a construção de metodologias de design em diálogo com povos indígenas a partir de experiências desenvolvidas na Aldeia Marakanã (RJ). Busca compreender como processos colaborativos, fundamentados nas cosmovisões e nos modos de vida originários, podem contribuir para práticas projetuais interculturais. Ancorado na teoria da ação dialógica de Paulo Freire e em perspectivas decoloniais, o estudo concebe o design como prática relacional, crítica e emancipatória. A pesquisa, de abordagem qualitativa, baseia-se na sistematização das experiências de elaboração coletiva realizadas no Seminário Moda, Arte e Culturas Indígenas, que resultaram na publicação de diretrizes metodológicas na obra Cosmovisões X Moda: qual é a sua tendência? Contribuições e proposições para uma moda étnica e ética. Os resultados evidenciam que a construção compartilhada de metodologias fortalece o protagonismo indígena, amplia processos de escuta e reciprocidade e tensiona modelos hegemônicos de criação em design. Conclui-se que práticas fundamentadas no diálogo, na confluência de saberes e na coautoria contribuem para abordagens éticas e interculturais na moda e no design, além de ampliar a formação crítica de profissionais comprometidos com conhecimentos que emergem dos territórios culturais.
venue: RELACult - Revista Latino-Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade

title: Classical Cepheids in the 4MOST era. I. Method for 4MOST variable stars and NLTE abundance gradients in the Milky Way
abstract: Classical Cepheids (CCs) are key distance indicators and tracers of young stellar populations in the Milky Way. Their period-luminosity-metallicity (PLZ) relation also makes them calibrators of the Hubble constant H_0. Despite their importance, chemical composition, especially effects due to nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE), remains a significant source of systematics in PLZ applications. In preparation for the large sample of CCs expected from the 4MOST Consortium Survey 4: Milky Way Disc and Bulge High-Resolution (4MIDABLE-HR) survey, we present a method for deriving Cepheid atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances in NLTE. Using the Payne artificial neural network (ANN) trained on NLTE spectra, we derived atmospheric parameters and abundances for 17 elements: O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Sr, Y, Ba, and Eu in NLTE and C and Cr in LTE. We applied the new method to archival spectra of Cepheids and derived radial chemical gradients in the Milky Way. We derived robust NLTE stellar parameters and abundances for Cepheids spanning a broad metallicity range, from ∼ -0.87 , dex to ∼ +0.35 , dex . For stars with multi-epoch spectra, we found that the NLTE abundances are consistent across the pulsation cycle, whereas the LTE values showed larger dispersions and biases. The resulting abundance distributions and gradients agree well with Galactic disk expectat…

title: Um diálogo entre o Desenho Universal para a Aprendizagem, as dimensões da formação inicial e os saberes docente
abstract: Este artigo tem como objetivo discutir uma articulação conceitual entre os princípios do Desenho Universal para a Aprendizagem, as dimensões da competência profissional e os saberes docentes e suas implicações para a formação inicial de professores. A fundamentação teórica explora os princípios do Desenho Universal para a Aprendizagem, relacionando-os às dimensões da competência profissional estabelecidas pela BNC-Formação e à natureza plural dos saberes da formação inicial, disciplinares, curriculares e experienciais perspectiva de Maurice Tardif. Metodologicamente, o estudo caracteriza-se como uma pesquisa de abordagem qualitativa e de natureza teórico-conceitual, derivada de parte do referencial teórico de uma tese de doutorado no campo da Educação em Ciências. O trabalho baseia-se na articulação e no estabelecimento de relações entre os referenciais do Desenho Universal para a Aprendizagem, às dimensões da competência profissional docente e aos saberes docentes, e por fim, da discussão de suas implicações para a formação inicial de professores. A análise aponta que a implementação de práticas alinhadas ao Desenho Universal para a Aprendizagem exige a mobilização integrada das dimensões da competência profissional e dos saberes docentes. Conclui-se que o diálogo entre essas abordagens fortalece a formação inicial como um processo que integra teoria, prática e compromisso éti…

title: Nanostructured electrocatalysts for borohydride electro-oxidation: Materials design, reaction kinetics, and fuel cell applications
Outcome-Based Redesign of an International Supply Chain and Trade Course: Authentic Tasks, Individual Evidence, and Assessment Rubrics
abstract: Background: International supply chain and trade courses require learners to connect sourcing, transport, contractual delivery, payment, documentation and risk rather than recall isolated definitions. Purpose: This paper develops a course-level outcome-based education (OBE) design that links interdisciplinary business tasks to observable and individually attributable learning evidence. Methods: A design-oriented curriculum analysis synthesized OBE, constructive alignment, authentic assessment, rubric research and feedback theory. The analysis specified course learning outcomes, mapped them to tasks and evidence, and constructed an assessment and improvement protocol. No student performance data were analyzed. Design results: Four outcomes address business-process analysis, fulfilment verification, alternative decision making, and communication with professional responsibility. A staged cross-border order project joins independent process mapping, document checking, solution comparison, team synthesis and individual oral defence. The proposed grade structure assigns 60% to process work and 40% to a final individual assessment, while a separate outcome-attainment model prioritizes individual evidence. A four-level analytic rubric and an evidence-to-action protocol provide practical criteria for scoring, diagnosis and course revision. Implications: The framework offers a transpare…

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ion-Association Design Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
abstract: Abstract Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic devices, but simultaneously achieving highly linear analog weight updates and a wide dynamic range remains fundamentally limited by a severe trade-off in uncontrolled interface doping kinetics. Although multicomponent electrolytes offer a pathway to tune ion behavior, a predictive framework capable of overcoming this strict trade-off remains unexplored due to the highly nonlinear nature of interionic interactions. Here, we introduce an AI-assisted ion-association design strategy utilizing a binary electrolyte architecture to break through the linearity–dynamic range trade-off. GPR-assisted regression analysis maps complex electrolyte formulations to synaptic nonlinearity, identifying an optimized NaCl·Na-TFSI binary configuration. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest distinct intrinsic ion-association tendencies between Na+–Cl– and Na+–TFSI– pairs, consistent with the observed doping and relaxation behaviors: strongly associated Na+–Cl– pairs suppress abrupt doping to optimize linearity, reducing nonlinearity by up to ∼6-fold compared with single-anion controls, while weakly associated Na+–TFSI– pairs facilitate ion retention to expand the dynamic range (Gmax/Gmin ∼ 103). This balanced dual-anion transport enables linear, extensible, and high-dynamic-range multistate conduct…

title: Design and Optimization of a Porous Photonic Crystal-Based Tamm Plasmon Sensor for Breath Biomarker Detection
Naphthobisthiadiazole-based nonfullerene acceptors for organic solar cells: molecular design, structure–property relationships, and synthetic perspectives
abstract: The development of nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs) based on π-conjugated molecules has driven recent advances in organic solar cells (OSCs), with electron-deficient units playing a key role in their molecular design. This review highlights naphthobisthiadiazole (NTz)-based NFAs and their structure–property relationships, focusing on how fluorination, substitution, and π-extension regulate electronic structures, optical properties, blend morphology, and photovoltaic performance. Particular attention is paid to NTz-based NFAs combined with poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT), a practical donor polymer with favorable cost and processability. This combination has enabled green-light wavelength-selective OSCs that selectively convert green light into electricity while transmitting blue and red light for plant photosynthesis, providing a promising approach to greenhouse agrivoltaics. Finally, the synthetic complexity of NTz-based materials and the potential of direct C–H functionalization as a concise and scalable synthetic strategy are discussed.

title: Robots as lab partners: chemists’ perspectives for informing the design of robot-assisted experimentation
abstract: Experimental laboratory work involves repetitive, labour-intensive manual procedures and strict safety protocols, making it an attractive area for Robotics and Artificial Intelligence (RAI). With research currently focused on technical innovation, there has been little work investigating the human factors of chemist-robot collaboration, and how these technologies will change the nature of work in chemistry. Understanding chemists’ requirements and perspectives is vital to the successful deployment and acceptance of RAI in laboratories. We examined the potential for robot-assisted chemistry experimentation through the perspective of future users by conducting contextual inquiries and semi-structured interviews with nine experimental chemists at various career levels with and without laboratory automation experience. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to gain a situated understanding of how their work could benefit from automation, as well as their perspectives and opinions on working alongside robots. We found that our participants are open to robot-assisted experimentation and have clear ideas for human-robot partnerships in the lab. We identified eight themes characterising chemists’ desired applications, the implementation requirements, and the perspectives on the adoption of robot-assisted experimentation. These findings show that successful acceptance of robot-assisted ex…

title: Genome-scale mining and experimental characterization of antimicrobial peptides from Bacillus
Pengaruh Indeks Pembangunan Manusia Islam dan Pertumbuhan Ekonomi terhadap Kemiskinan dengan Pengangguran sebagai Variabel Intervening
abstract: Aim: This study analyzes the direct and indirect effects of the Islamic Human Development Index (IPMI) and economic growth on poverty, with unemployment as an intervening variable, in Indonesia. Method: A quantitative associative design was applied to secondary panel data from 34 Indonesian provinces for 2016–2022, obtained from Statistics Indonesia (BPS) and related publications. Path analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 3.0, with single-indicator formative constructs and bootstrapping at the 5% significance level. Results: IPMI has a significant negative effect on poverty (? = ?0.273; p = 0.001) and unemployment (? = ?0.337; p < 0.001). Economic growth significantly reduces poverty (? = ?0.200; p = 0.001) but significantly increases unemployment (? = 0.236; p < 0.001), indicating jobless growth. Unemployment has no significant effect on poverty (? = ?0.073; p = 0.272) and does not mediate the effects of IPMI or economic growth on poverty. Novelty/implication: The study tests two pathways simultaneously, namely human development grounded in maq??id al-shar?‘ah and economic growth, within one mediation model covering all provinces. The findings support structural poverty theory: poverty reduction requires comprehensive human development, inclusive growth, decent job quality, and fair wealth distribution rather tha…

title: Combined application of Eucalyptus-derived biochar and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi improves growth, nutrient acquisition, antioxidant responses, and drought tolerance in Cicer arietinum
abstract: This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of Eucalyptus-derived biochar and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on the growth, physiology, nutrient acquisition, and drought tolerance of Cicer arietinum. Plants were grown under normal and drought conditions and received biochar, AMF, or their combined application. Drought markedly reduced plant growth, photosynthetic performance, nutrient acquisition, nodulation, leghemoglobin content, and nitrate reductase activity. It also suppressed AMF colonisation, spore abundance, mycelial development, vesicle formation, arbuscule abundance, and root colonisation percentage. However, when applied together, biochar and AMF significantly alleviated these adverse effects. The combined treatment improved plant growth, chlorophyll production, net photosynthetic rate, relative water content, membrane stability, and antioxidant enzyme activity. Biochar also enhanced mycorrhizal establishment under drought, while treated plants maintained higher N and P concentrations than untreated drought-stressed plants. Treated plants showed greater nodule number and fresh weight, higher leghemoglobin content and nitrate reductase activity, and improved plant N status compared with untreated drought-stressed plants. Phosphorus and nitrogen uptake, which declined sharply under drought, were also substantially restored by the treatments. Overall, t…

title: Species-specific leaf trait adaptations of common woody plants to long-term experimental warming within treeline ecotone of eastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
Population Diversity of Tecomella undulata across South Asia: Diversity identification Markers, Possible Causes, and Potential for Conservation
abstract: Tecomella undulata (Sm.) Seem., the sole species of its genus in the family Bignoniaceae, is a keystone tree of the arid and semi-arid tracts of South Asia, valued equally for its ecological role in desert stabilization and its long history of use in traditional medicine. Habitat fragmentation, unsustainable timber and herbal extraction, weak natural regeneration, grazing pressure and a warming/drying climate has together pushed the species toward endangered status in the Thar Desert of Sindh, Pakistan. Since there is a lack of such study which integrate anatomical, phytochemical, and molecular analysis as diversity identification markers, this review explores and summarizes the available information on population diversity identification using molecular (chiefly ISSR and RAPD), anatomical structure and the phytochemical profile as markers to understand variations in T. undulata populations. Published marker-based work shows substantial genetic diversity retained within populations despite geographic isolation, while anatomical and phytochemical surveys, though comparatively sparse, point to xeromorphic adaptations and stress induced shifts in secondary metabolism that likely track local aridity and soil conditions. We argue that combining molecular, anatomical and phytochemical data is not simply additive but necessary though other approaches like common garden experiment may …
venue: Journal of Applied Research in Plant Sciences

title: Planos Municipais de Cultura e Patrimônio: disputas por reconhecimento e poder na política cultural
abstract: O artigo analisa os Planos Municipais de Cultura (PMCs) como arenas institucionais de disputa por reconhecimento e poder no campo patrimonial, no âmbito do Sistema Nacional de Cultura (SNC). Tomando o patrimônio como eixo analítico, argumenta-se que os PMCs operam como dispositivos institucionais de legitimação cultural, definição de prioridades públicas e regulação da participação social. A metodologia baseia-se em revisão de literatura e análise de marcos legais e institucionais para examinar a arquitetura normativa do SNC e os arranjos participativos dos planos de cultura. Sustenta-se que, ao territorializarem diretrizes nacionais, os PMCs podem reproduzir ou reconfigurar matrizes coloniais de legitimação cultural, a depender da incorporação de sujeitos historicamente marginalizados e da redistribuição de poder no campo do patrimônio.

Extraction of Water from Atmospheric Air Using Solar Power
abstract: Water is one of the most essential natural resources required for human survival. However, the availability of clean drinking water is decreasing in many regions due to population growth, climate change, and water scarcity. The project “Extraction of Water from Atmospheric Air Using Solar Power” aims to develop an eco-friendly and energy-efficient system to obtain water from the moisture present in the atmosphere by utilizing solar energy. The proposed system works by extracting moisture from atmospheric air through a suitable water-condensation process. Solar energy is used as the primary power source to operate the required components, such as a fan, cooling system, and other electrical devices, depending on the design. When the moist air comes into contact with a sufficiently cold surface, the water vapour condenses into liquid water. The collected water can then be filtered and treated to improve its quality for suitable uses. The main objective of this project is to reduce dependence on conventional water sources and provide an alternative water supply, especially in water-scarce and remote areas. The system also aims to reduce dependence on grid electricity by utilizing renewable solar energy, thereby minimizing environmental impact. It may be useful in rural areas, emergency situations, and disaster-affected regions where access to water is limited. In conclusion, this p…

title: Power output, thermal evolution, and bead geometry in wire arc additive manufacturing under power-regulated arc control
“There’s a connection between you and me”: exploring human values through social virtual reality for cultural heritage
abstract: To what extent can virtual reality (VR) for cultural heritage support contemporary audiences in exploring unfamiliar human values and complicated socio-economic contexts? While collaborative VR experiences are increasingly used to inform people about the past, their application to more speculative matters - e.g., alternative social values - to foster more varied outcomes, like historical empathy and care, is uncommon. This paper investigates how archaeological interpretations of egalitarian ways of living can be translated into social interaction design for heritage VR, and what impacts these interaction patterns have on participants. We present ÇVR, a multi-user immersive VR experience that prioritizes values-led engagement through collaboration, with the aim of supporting reflection beyond conventional educational outcomes. Seventeen pairs of collocated participants explore a reconstruction of a Neolithic heritage site and, through guided tasks and conversation, perform social practices suggesting egalitarian values, inspired by archaeological evidence. Our research finds that these interactions promote mutual support, perspective-taking, collaborative meaning-making, and affective engagement with both the people of the past and their present-day partners. We contribute a framework for operationalizing hypothesized human values through social interaction design in heritage VR…

title: VIRTUAL MUSEUMS AS A NEW CULTURAL SPACE
abstract: The purpose of this article is to provide a comprehensive analysis of virtual museums as a new cultural space, to determine their place within the contemporary system of preserving, representing, and interpreting cultural heritage, and to examine the impact of digital technologies on the transformation of museum communication, cultural memory, and interaction between museums and their audiences. The methodological framework is based on an interdisciplinary approach that integrates methods from museum studies, cultural anthropology, digital humanities, and heritage studies, combined with the principles of systemic, historical-comparative, structural-functional, and cultural-anthropological analysis. The application of this comprehensive methodology makes it possible to trace the evolution of virtual museums from electronic catalogues to interactive digital platforms that facilitate new forms of creating, interpreting, and disseminating cultural knowledge. The study demonstrates that the digitalization of the museum sector has fundamentally transformed the traditional functions of museums, shifting them from institutions primarily concerned with the physical preservation of artefacts to open digital cultural spaces where heritage preservation, scholarly communication, education, virtual representation, and cultural interaction converge. Particular attention is devoted to the appl…

title: Colonialidade do poder: planejamento urbano no município de Pato Branco-PR
abstract: O objetivo deste artigo é investigar o papel do arquiteto e urbanista na recomposição de saberes e na descoberta do urbanismo como forma de valorizar diferentes formas de conceber o comunitário. A partir da perspectiva da decolonialidade, o debate expõe a transformação da natureza e dos bens comuns em ativos financeiros, fazendo surgir a segregação territorial, a imposição da tecnocracia como única alternativa possível. A metodologia combina revisão bibliográfica de referências do campo do saber decolonial com estudos sobre algumas características das infraestruturas de drenagem urbanas no município de Pato Branco-PR. Essa abordagem permite o confronto perante o controverso discurso do processo histórico de ocupação do território municipal.

title: Factors Controlling Status of Plant Available Si and Phytolith and PhytOC Production in Intensively Cultivated Rice Ecosystem of India
Multi-Objective Optimization Approach for Power Distribution Network Reconfiguration using Hybrid Particle Swarm and Genetic Algorithm
abstract: Power distribution networks are a critical component of the electric power distribution system. Hence, numerous research has focus on distribution network reconfiguration systems, intending to minimize power losses and interruptions, namely, Customer Average Interruption Index (CAIDI), System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), Energy Not Supplied (ENS), and Voltage Profile (VP) improvement, either by Genetic Algorithm (GA) or Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Nonetheless, existing research has not simultaneously employed a hybrid of GA and PSO optimization methods to ascertain which optimization method is better in terms of improving the reliability indices, such as CAIDI, SAIFI, and ENS, while minimizing power losses and improving the VP, thus leaving a gap in the literature. Hence, the proposed research work seeks to utilize the synergy of GA and PSO optimization techniques on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus systems with the aforementioned reliability targets to unearth which of the optimization techniques is better than the other. Meanwhile, the obtained results indicate that the GA exhibits a higher voltage level enhancement of 2.75% with a corresponding SAIFI reduction of 33%. Nonetheless, the PSO unveils superior or enhanced power loss reduction of 61.75%, ENS reduction of 48%, and CAIDI reduction of 30% with a corresponding computational speed of 0.24 seconds…
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering

title: Moda como Ferramenta de Dominação Colonial: instrumentalização do poder simbólico no contexto do BrasilColônia através das vestes dos escravizados
abstract: O presente artigo aborda como temática principal a instrumentalização da violência simbólica para a imposição e manutenção do sistema escravista no Brasil do período colonial, recorrendo como objeto de análise às vestes utilizadas pelos escravizados africanos neste contexto histórico. Para isso, introduzem-se noções acerca do vestuário e da moda, posicionando-os enquanto sistema simbólico e ferramenta de dominação colonial, respectivamente; apresenta-se o conceito de poder simbólico e as ideias relativas à construção da realidade a partir deste. Para o exercício desta análise, utiliza-se uma pesquisa bibliográfica e interdisciplinar com o objetivo de refletir os conceitos propostos e defender de forma crítica a tese norteadora do trabalho. Conclui-se, por meio de uma análise histórica/social, que a utilização e a valoração das vestes na sociedade escravista do Brasil colonial corresponderam a um mecanismo de dominação dos povos negros africanos escravizados para a determinação do sistema escravista, do ser escravo e a naturalização da diferença colonial enquanto meio para a manutenção deste sistema.
venue: RELACult - Revista Latino-Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade

title: A biografia de um patrimônio cultural, trechos selecionados: entre a rememoração, o apagamento e a potência das ruínas de um sítio arqueológico de Ouro Preto-MG, Brasil
abstract: Este artigo derivado da Tese do autor, defendida no Programa de Doutorado em Sociologia da Universidade de Brasília - UnB, analisa sociologicamente a patrimonialização tardia do Sítio Arqueológico do Morro da Queimada, território em ruínas de um próspero arraial minerador do início do século XVIII, anterior a própria cidade de Ouro Preto (MG). Sua patrimonialização é analisada enquanto um processo que é por natureza dinâmico, descontínuo, inacabado ou não consolidado ainda na atualidade do caso. A patrimonialização é abordada em sua processualidade sócio-histórica tanto linear quanto anacrônica, constituída de políticas de memória, contíguas, coexistentes ou concorrentes no tempo e no espaço de um bem cultural, nos quais diferentes interdependências sociofuncionais tomam em cada tempo uma forma de patrimonialização do lugar, formando uma figuração, que por sua vez, se expressa em mentalidades e imaginários em que o que, como e para quem se preserva o lugar muda ao longo do processo sócio-histórico. É exatamente na mudança dos padrões de interdependência é que ocorre a mudança das concepções de patrimônio cultural ao longo do tempo. O que importa não é o patrimônio em si, mas as relações, interdependências e equilíbrio de tensões estabelecidas, a partir e com o patrimônio do Sítio Arqueológico em diferentes tempos. O que é ou não patrimônio está em movimento e muda na longa dura…
venue: RELACult - Revista Latino-Americana de Estudos em Cultura e Sociedade

title: Pemberian Video Kartun Menggunakan Virtual Reality Untuk Menurunkan Kecemasan Praoperasi Pada Pasien Anak
abstract: Kecemasan praoperasi merupakan masalah yang sering dialami pasien anak karena lingkungan rumah sakit, perpisahan dari orang tua, dan ketakutan terhadap tindakan medis. Kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan mengimplementasikan video kartun menggunakan Virtual Reality (VR) sebagai distraksi nonfarmakologis untuk membantu menurunkan kecemasan praoperasi pada pasien anak. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada Juni–Juli 2026 di RS TK. III Wijayakusuma Purwokerto dengan 23 anak usia 6–15 tahun yang menjalani persiapan operasi elektif. Tingkat kecemasan dinilai sebelum dan sesudah intervensi menggunakan Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale (mYPAS). Video kartun diberikan melalui perangkat VR selama 10–15 menit dengan pendampingan dan observasi respons anak. Sebelum intervensi, 14 anak (60,9%) berada pada kategori cemas berat, 8 anak (34,7%) cemas sedang, dan 1 anak (4,3%) cemas ringan. Setelah intervensi, 13 anak (56,5%) berada pada kategori cemas ringan dan 10 anak (43,5%) tidak cemas; kategori cemas sedang dan berat tidak ditemukan. Hasil ini menunjukkan adanya perubahan distribusi tingkat kecemasan ke kategori yang lebih rendah setelah pemberian video kartun melalui VR. Kegiatan ini mendukung penggunaan VR sebagai alternatif distraksi nonfarmakologis dalam pelayanan praoperasi anak, dengan tetap memperhatikan durasi, kenyamanan, pendampingan, dan keterbatasan desain de…

title: Solar Energy Landscape of Pakistan: Resource Potential, Deployment, Policy Framework, and Future Directions
abstract: Pakistan encounters complex issues in its electric infrastructure, as demand increases with growing reliance on foreign oil and gas, while abundant solar potential remains underutilized across the country, and tariff instability, coupled with subsistence concerns, intensifies systemic stresses. Potential far exceeds practical application, as resources are left underutilized. Starting with an overview, this paper explores solar energy development in Pakistan from various perspectives: resource abundance, technological routes, adoption trends, economics of technology choices, policy frameworks, and barriers to implementation. Out of the 923 works retrieved from the IEEE Xplore and Scopus databases over the period 2015-2026, 105 peer-reviewed papers were identified through systematic screening and snowballing for final analysis. This review makes three contributions. First, it compiles the techno-economic indicators (cost of energy, payback period, and performance ratio) reported by a subset of the reviewed studies across residential, institutional, and utility-scale applications. These values are reported as published in each study, under differing system configurations, currencies, cost years, and assumptions; they are not normalised and should not be interpreted as results of a single standardised comparison. Second, it demonstrates that interdependent feedback loops of import …

title: Substrate physicochemical properties and seedling performance of rubber tree seed-grafted seedlings: relative contributions of physical structure and chemical nutrients
abstract: Introduction The physical structure and chemical nutrients of substrates jointly regulate seedling growth in container nursery production, but their relative contributions and interactions remain unclear, limiting precise substrate formulation. Rubber tree ( Hevea brasiliensis ) seed-grafted seedlings are important planting materials for the natural rubber industry, yet their lightweight substrate technology needs optimization. Methods Seed-grafted seedlings were grown in an inert control (CK, river sand: perlite = 1:1) and five substrate formulations: T1 (pure red soil), T2 (coco coir:peat = 1:1), T3 (red soil: coco coir: sheep manure = 5:3:2), T4 (sugarcane leaf residue: river sand: sheep manure = 4:4:2), and T5 (peat: coco coir: sheep manure: river sand = 3:3:2:2). Growth, physiological, and nutrient parameters were measured, and membership function, principal component, and variance partitioning analyses (VPA) were used to quantify independent and interactive effects of physical and chemical factors. Results Different substrates significantly affected growth, biomass, leaf nutrients, and photosynthetic pigments, while biomass allocation (stem > root > leaf) remained stable. Comprehensive evaluation ranked T2 highest (membership 0.74–0.79) and T3 lowest (0.15–0.20). T2 exhibited greater root development, which was associated with its low bulk density and high porosity;…

title: Decoding decision correctness from EEG under high cognitive workload in virtual reality: implications for collaborative brain-computer interface teams
abstract: Introduction Collaborative Brain-Computer Interfaces (cBCIs) offer a promising mechanism to augment team decision‐making, but existing approaches rely exclusively on evidence available only after a decision has been made and reported, such as reaction time or stated confidence. This limits their use to explaining or discounting a decision after the fact, rather than informing a teams response before it is finalised. We tested whether spatial‐covariance EEG features could instead provide a genuinely pre-emptive signal of an operators decision correctness, available within the response window itself, and whether such a signal depends on cognitive workload. Methods Using a continuous virtual reality target-detection task, participants (N = 23) completed a within-subject visual workload manipulation (High vs. Low), implemented via a Degraded Visual Environment. Results A Riemannian tangent‐space classifier, trained on a strictly motor‐safe EEG window preceding each response, decoded Correct from Incorrect decisions with above‐chance accuracy under High Workload (61.4%, p = .0014, N = 23) but not reliably under Low Workload (N = 17), where near‐ceiling behavioural accuracy left too few error trials for valid classification. Ablation analysis showed the signal was carried predominantly by posterior occipito‐parietal channels, consistent with a perceptual rather than motor origin. At …

title: From green commitment to sustainable harvest: how digital capabilities and institutional pressure power agricultural sustainability
abstract: Purpose The objective of this study is to examine whether, and through which mechanisms, green corporate social responsibility (GCSR) integration improves sustainable farm performance in a climate-vulnerable emerging economy. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and institutional theory, the study analyses the mediating roles of green supply chain dynamic capabilities, sustainable agricultural innovation and digital technology capability, and the first-stage moderating role of coercive institutional pressure. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 420 farmers and agribusiness managers, purposively selected through agricultural extension offices in 30 districts across four Pakistani provinces, was conducted. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 10,000 bootstrap resamples was used to estimate the model, which contains three parallel mediators and three interaction terms. Measurement and structural model quality, predictive relevance, common-method bias, nonresponse bias and endogeneity were assessed through standard procedures. Findings GCSR integration has a significant direct effect on sustainable farm performance, but most of its effect is transmitted through capability building. Digital technology capability carries the largest indirect effect, followed by green supply chain dynamic capabilities and sustainable agricultural inno…

ESG rating disagreement and corporate energy intensity in China: the moderating role of managerial environmental attention
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how ESG rating disagreement affects corporate energy intensity and the role of managerial environmental attention in this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using 18,335 firm-year observations from 4,124 Chinese listed firms between 2019 and 2023, this study uses panel regressions to test the proposed relationships. Findings The results reveal a U-shaped relationship between ESG rating disagreement and corporate energy intensity. Moderate disagreement reduces energy intensity by providing complementary sustainability information, whereas excessive disagreement increases energy intensity by generating signal ambiguity. Managerial environmental attention strengthens this U-shaped relationship. Originality/value These findings deepen our understanding of how information uncertainty shapes corporate sustainability outcomes and how managerial cognitive orientation moderates the consequences of rating inconsistency.

title: Semiconductor optical cooling as heat-to-light energy conversion
abstract: Semiconductor optical cooling can be viewed as a heat-to-light energy-conversion process in which thermal energy is incorporated into electronic excited states and extracted from the material through photoluminescence. This Progress Review describes the development of semiconductor optical cooling and the remaining challenges. We first discuss the fundamental physics of optical cooling from the viewpoints of energy balance and thermodynamics, and then survey experimental studies of semiconductor optical cooling, with particular attention to halide perovskites. We further distinguish between the condition for net cooling and the achievable cooling power, and identify the physical limits arising from the underlying optical and recombination processes. Particular attention is given to photon recycling, Auger recombination, and the factors that determine the attainable temperature. Finally, we discuss material design strategies for controlling heat-to-light energy conversion and perspectives toward thermo-optical materials physics.

title: Evolving energy-water infrastructure strengthens drought resilience in the U.S. Northeast and Midwest
abstract: Abstract Strategies to strengthen regional water security will be essential for navigating a critical 21st-century environmental challenge: securing freshwater supplies against growing demands and increasingly severe climate extremes. This paper assesses the evolution of water security in the historically water-rich U.S. Northeast (NE) and Midwest (MW) to quantify their resilience to severe drought now and in the future. We develop a counterfactual framework that projects sectoral water demands based on socio-economic drivers and deconstructs the benefits of supply- and demand-side adaptations at the regional scale. During the half-century between the historic NE/MW 1960s drought and the 2012–2013 North American drought, rapid socio-economic growth held the potential to push water systems to a breaking point, rendering them unequipped to manage the impact of such severe droughts. However, this study reveals that both regions built resilience through long-term adaptations that averted potential water crises, mitigating otherwise severe summertime water stress (withdrawal-to-available supply) by factors of 2.8 (MW) and 5.6 (NE). While supply-side strategies through reservoir construction and coastal power development played a role, the driving factor has been water demand management, accounting for 83% to 92% of summertime water stress mitigations across the two regions and droug…

title: Government Subsidies and Green Innovation in Renewable Energy Enterprises: The Moderating Role of Financing Constraints
abstract: Renewable energy enterprises are central to the low-carbon transition, yet their green innovation is constrained by high technological uncertainty, long payback periods, and limited access to external finance. Government subsidies are among the most widely used policy instruments for correcting the resulting under-investment, but whether they actually stimulate green innovation, and under what financial conditions they work best, remains unclear. Drawing on market-failure theory, information-asymmetry theory, and signaling theory, this study examines the effect of government subsidies on green innovation in Chinese renewable energy listed companies and tests the moderating role of financing constraints. Using an unbalanced panel of 186 A-share listed renewable energy firms observed from 2012 to 2023 (1,794 firm-year observations), two-way fixed effects estimates show that government subsidies significantly promote green innovation, and the result is robust to alternative measures, instrumental-variable estimation, and Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood estimation. Financing constraints positively moderate this relationship: the marginal effect of subsidies is larger for firms facing tighter constraints, consistent with the view that subsidies compensate for scarce external funds and send positive signals to creditors. The promoting effect is also stronger in non-state-owned ente…
venue: Journal of Economics, Finance And Management Studies

title: Day-to-day peer and family stress as proximal correlates of self-injurious thoughts during adolescence
abstract: Abstract Theory and research both highlight interpersonal stressors as precipitants to self-injurious thoughts and behaviors (SITBs) during adolescence. Yet, little is known about near-term risk or which types of interpersonal stressors (e.g., peer and/or family) are most likely to precipitate adolescent SITBs. This study used an intensive longitudinal design to examine whether peer- and family-related stress were associated with adolescents’ same- and next-day self-injurious thoughts. Participants were 154 female adolescents aged 12–17 years (77.3% White). Youth were oversampled for risk such that 73.4% ( n = 113) were at high risk for future SITBs. Youth completed a 30-day ecological momentary assessment procedure assessing interpersonal experiences and SITBs. Multilevel models showed that peer stress predicted same-day nonsuicidal self-injury urges and suicidal ideation (SI), whereas family stress predicted same-day nonsuicidal self-injury urges only. Neither peer nor family stress predicted next-day self-injurious thoughts. Exploratory models examining bidirectional effects showed that non-suicidal self-injury urges predicted next-day peer and family stress while SI predicted next-day family, but not peer, stress. Findings suggest that daily interpersonal stress is proximally associated with self-injurious thoughts during adolescence and underscore the importance of studyin…

Design and Energy Dissipation Analysis of an Interaction-Region based Single-Polarity Reconfigurable XOR/XNOR Gate for Quantum Dot Cellular Automata
abstract: As Quantum Dot Cellular Automata is emerging as a promising alternative to CMOS technology for nanoscale designs, there is always a necessity for realization of compact and energy-efficient designs that perform reconfigurable logic. This paper shows a single-polarity, reconfigurable interaction-region based XOR/XNOR gate which eliminates the conventional majority-gate based structures by utilization of localized electrostatic interactions within a compact cell layout design. The proposed layout design performs dual functions, XOR or XNOR, using the same layout by varying the polarization of the control cell from -1 to +1, and thus performs dual operations without the requirement of additional hardware or structural modifications. Functional correctness of the proposed XOR/XNOR design is verified by using QCA Designer 2.0.3 under a bistable simulation engine, and energy dissipation analysis was performed using QCA Designer-E using Coherence energy vector simulation engine using both Euler’s method and Runge-Kutta method. The proposed design utilizes an overall area of 0.01μm2 with a latency of 0.5 clock cycles and 9 overall cells with output polarization of 0.965. By comparing the performance parameters of the proposed XOR/XNOR design with existing designs, it shows a reduction in cell count by 71.88% and an improvement in latency by 75%. Additionally, energy dissipation analysi…

title: Evaluating the effect of financial development on energy use in ASEAN economies
abstract: Purpose Energy use plays a pivotal role in sustaining economic growth and improving living standards, particularly in rapidly developing regions such as ASEAN. This study aims to examine the effect of financial development on energy use in ASEAN countries over the period 1996–2020. Design/methodology/approach To ensure robust analysis, cross-sectional dependence is first tested, followed by the application of second-generation unit root tests. Long-run relationships among the variables are assessed using Pedroni, Kao and Westerlund cointegration tests, all of which confirm the existence of cointegration. For the estimation of long-run coefficients, Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS), Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS) and Canonical Cointegrating Regression (CCR) methods are used. Findings The results of this study indicate that financial development exerts a positive influence on energy use in the long run. Furthermore, control variables including economic growth, technological innovation and governance quality are also found to positively affect energy use. Originality/value The findings of this study highlight the critical role of financial development in shaping energy demand across the ASEAN region.
venue: International Journal of Energy Sector Management

title: Exploring surplus resource theory and the role of dietary energy in the expression of play behaviour in pigs
abstract: Abstract Surplus Resource Theory proposes that play behaviour is expressed more abundantly in juveniles that have access to necessary resources. We propose that sufficient dietary energy is likely to be a requirement for play and therefore hypothesise that pigs on an energy-deficient diet will show reduced play. A total of 128 mixed sex pigs of 28 days old, were randomly allocated across two diets: control (CE) or low energy (LE). Pigs were given access to a play arena, for 20 min, 4 times over 10 days and on alternative occasions, before entering the arena, offered a sucrose supplement. We hypothesised the provision of sucrose would increase play, particularly for pigs on the LE diet. Dietary treatment and play session interacted on social object ( P = 0.025), solo locomotor ( P < 0.001) and social locomotor play ( P < 0.001). Dietary treatment and pen mate average sugar intake interacted on social object ( P = 0.019) and social locomotor play ( P < 0.001). The interaction between dietary treatment and pen mate average sugar intake ( P = 0.002) affected total play. Overall, the CE diet appeared to extend the developmental period of heightened engagement in social play. Our findings suggest that diet quality in weaned pigs may impact specific aspects of play behaviour with potential benefits for animal welfare.

title: Aging-Aware Attention-Driven Transformer Reinforcement Learning Framework for Sustainable Hybrid Battery Energy Management in Electric Vehicles
abstract: Battery degradation is another important constraint of the hybrid electric vehicle systems, where the standard approach to energy management focuses on short-term fuel efficiency and does not consider the long-term health of the battery. In this paper, a proposal has been made on an Aging-Aware Attention-Driven Transformer Reinforcement Learning (AAT-DRL) framework of intelligent hybrid battery energy management. Transformer-based temporal feature encoding, along with actor-critic reinforcement learning architecture, is combined in the model to encode patterns that are sensitive to degradation such as temperature, current stress and depth-of-discharge. The multi-objective reward is developed with an aim to optimize the energy efficiency, thermal safety and battery life. The framework is tested at standard driving cycles (UDDS, NEDC and WLTP). In the results, it is shown that the degradation index has reduced by 38%, the SOC has become more stable and thermal fluctuations have been reduced, with a peak efficiency of 95.3%, which is a better performance than the state-of-the-art DRL methods. The solution offers a healthy, scalable and battery management system for the next generation based on the proposed approach.
