More than exercise: health-related quality of life and participation motives in dragon boating among people with breast cancer—a cross-sectional study
abstract: Dragon boat participation may support people with breast cancer during treatment and survivorship. This cross-sectional study examined whether lower health-related quality of life (HRQoL) is associated with stronger participation motives. As motives are linked to coping strategies, the results are interpreted in terms of different coping types that can be beneficial in the context of breast cancer. A total of 156 breast cancer survivors (aged 37–73 years) from the German dragon boat community completed standardized questionnaires assessing HRQoL (SF-36) and participation motives (Bern Motives and Goals Inventory). Regression analyses revealed a significant model for distraction/catharsis, F (8, 135) = 4.93, p < 0.001, R 2 = 0.23. Lower psychological wellbeing (β = −0.31, p = 0.013), physical functioning (β = −0.24, p = 0.035), and social functioning (β = −0.23, p = 0.046) were associated with stronger motives of distraction/catharsis. The model for aesthetics was also significant, F (2, 141) = 5.54, p < 0.005, R 2 = 0.07, indicating that greater pain was related to a stronger aesthetics motive (β = −0.25, p = 0.011). The findings suggest that dragon boating may function as emotion-focused coping strategy and, i.e., in the context of pain, as a meaning-focused coping strategy. Implications for recruitment and trainer education are discussed.

title: Problematik Pemilihan Kepala Daerah dengan Calon Tunggal: Implikasi terhadap Partisipasi Pemilih yang Bermakna dan Electoral Justice
abstract: Pemilihan Kepala Daerah (Pilkada) dengan calon tunggal menimbulkan problematik bagi electoral justice (keadilan elektoral) karena mempersempit ruang kompetisi dan pilihan politik pemilih. Pilkada 2024 diikuti 37 daerah dengan calon Tunggal yang dua di antaranya dimenangkan kolom kosong. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis problematik tersebut terhadap partisipasi pemilih yang bermakna serta merumuskan upaya penguatannya. Penelitian menggunakan metode yuridis normatif dengan pendekatan perundang-undangan, konseptual, dan kasus, melalui analisis kualitatif preskriptif terhadap peraturan perundang-undangan, putusan Mahkamah Konstitusi, dan literatur. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan, pertama, calon tunggal memang tidak otomatis menurunkan angka partisipasi tetapi berpotensi membatasi kualitas partisipasi karena pemilih tidak dihadapkan pada alternatif yang nyata. Kedua, akses terhadap koreksi hukum terbatas, dari delapan perkara PHPU Kada calon tunggal 2024, hanya satu dikabulkan sebagian, Putusan MK No. 24/PHPU.BUP-XXIII/2025, sedangkan lainnya tidak diterima terutama karena kedudukan hukum pemohon dan ambang batas dalam UU Pilkada. Ketiga, kerangka hukum telah berkembang melalui Putusan MK No. 126/PUU-XXII/2024 yang menetapkan pemilihan ulang paling lama satu tahun setelah kolom kosong menang dan mengubah desain surat suara menjadi pilihan “setuju” atau “tidak setuju”. Meski demik…

title: Value-Added Tax and Organizational Neutrality in Coalition Loyalty Reward Programs: Differential Effects on SME Participation and Impact on Social Welfare
abstract: Abstract This paper asks whether Korea’s VAT treatment of cross-firm reward-point redemption is organizationally neutral. Points used with their issuer may reduce the taxable amount, while reimbursements for points issued by another firm are generally included in the redeemer’s taxable amount. Under stated assumptions, total output VAT may be higher when a similar reward crosses a firm boundary, though the inter-firm reimbursement may justify the difference. The paper’s central mechanism is administrative: VAT adds classification, invoicing, period-matching, correction, retention, and penalty-control work to ordinary settlement, and the fixed member- or relationship-specific component of that work can weigh more heavily on low-volume SMEs under four stated conditions. Welfare effects follow two tracks: efficiency costs requiring no market failure, and competition-related harm requiring benefits the coalition cannot capture. The paper suggests administrative simplification within the current base and treats base-level reforms as provisional options requiring legislation and safeguards.
venue: Asian Journal of Law and Economics

Kinetics, mechanics, and structural disorder: non-equilibrium phase transformation in lithium-ion battery materials
abstract: Abstract The equilibrium phase diagram is a poor guide for lithium-ion battery electrodes under load. Operating electrodes are open, driven systems in which transformation pathways are governed as much by kinetics and mechanics as by thermodynamics—departures from equilibrium are large, mechanistically coherent, and exploitable for engineering. This review surveys the field of non-equilibrium phase transformation in lithium-ion battery materials across three interconnected themes: kinetic and mechanical suppression of first-order phase transitions in olivine LiFePO 4 (LFP) and layered transition-metal oxides; chemo-mechanical feedback by which electrode mechanics reshapes surface reaction kinetics; and the pathway-altering mechanisms by which the free energy landscape is restructured under non-equilibrium conditions, producing qualitatively opposite transformation behavior in LFP and LiNi x Mn y Co z O 2 (NMC). Finite-deformation continuum models formally derive diffusion-induced creep and kinetic plasticity as inelastic mechanisms, coupling mechanical state to surface reaction kinetics through a modified Butler–Volmer boundary condition. Crystal-scale analysis establishes that defect stress fields shift the electrochemical landscape in LFP by amounts consequential for electrode design. Multilayered free-energy theories introduce structural disorder as a dynamically evolving st…

title: Central Transfer Dependence, Economic Growth, And Own-Source Revenue Growth in The Regencies and Cities of North Sumatra
abstract: This study examines whether dependence on central transfers and economic growth in the previous year are associated with the growth of own-source revenue (pendapatan asli daerah, PAD) in the regencies and cities of North Sumatra, Indonesia. Using a balanced panel of 33 regions for 2022 to 2025 (132 observations), the study estimates two-way fixed-effects models with standard errors clustered by region and reports a series of sensitivity checks. Transfer dependence is positively associated with revenue growth in every specification, with coefficients between 3.1 and 5.2. The baseline estimate narrowly misses significance at the 5 percent level (p = 0.053) and becomes significant when one extreme observation is excluded or winsorized (p = 0.007 to 0.012). Lagged economic growth shows no robust association once year effects are included. The results do not support the argument that transfer dependence suppresses local revenue growth, which suggests that policy attention should shift from the volume of transfers toward collection capacity and the implementation of tax reform. The study contributes by analyzing the growth, rather than the level, of own-source revenue with lagged regressors and by documenting how sensitive the estimates are to an influential observation. The analysis is exploratory, and the estimates describe conditional associations rather than causal effects

Pre-converted radish and beetroot matrices for curing camel sausage: residual nitrite and quality changes during refrigerated storage
abstract: The performance of vegetable-derived curing ingredients can vary with the meat matrix. Whole pre-converted radish and beetroot were examined in raw camel sausages stuffed into 18 mm cellulose casings and packed in resealable ziplock bags during a 10-day storage period at 4 ± 1 °C. Six formulations were studied. Negative control (NC) received no added sodium nitrite, positive control (PC) contained 156 mg/kg sodium nitrite, R3 and R6 contained 3% and 6% fermented radish, respectively, and B3 and B6 contained 3% and 6% fermented beetroot, respectively. Residual nitrite, phenolic content, DPPH inhibition, thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), proximate composition, instrumental color, total viable count (TVC), pH, texture, and sensory attributes were measured on days 0, 5, and 10. Day 5 was used as the first practical assessment after the recommended 3-day refrigerated period, and day 10 as an extended-storage assessment. At day 5, PC had the lowest TBARS value (0.09 mg malondialdehyde (MDA) equivalents/kg), and the highest sensory color score (8.40). On day 5, R3 did not differ significantly from PC in any sensory attribute except color ( p ≥ 0.05) with overall acceptability scores of 7.40 and 7.75, respectively, whereas TVC in R6, B3, and B6 were below both controls. On day 10, all vegetable treatment had lower TVC than NC (6.57 log10 CFU/g) and PC (6.88 log10 CFU/g).…

title: Decision factors for electric vehicles: moderating effect of prior experience
abstract: Purpose This study examines how product-focused and contextual/supporting EV decision factors influence consumer attitudes and behavioral intentions from an elaboration likelihood model (ELM) perspective. It further investigates whether prior EV experience changes the relative influence of these factors on attitude formation. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 527 consumers with and without prior EV experience. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), and multi-group analysis (MGA) was conducted after assessing measurement invariance. Findings ASS/parts management, design and usability, economic value and environmental friendliness significantly improve EV attitudes, whereas performance advantage, perceived low maintenance cost, subsidies and charging convenience do not. Attitude significantly increases purchase and word-of-mouth (WOM) intentions. MGA reveals two statistically significant between-group differences. Design and usability have a stronger positive effect on attitude among consumers without prior EV experience than among those with prior experience. In contrast, perceived low maintenance cost has a stronger effect among experienced consumers than among inexperienced consumers. No significant between-group differences are found for the remaining relationships. Originality/value This study draw…

title: Finite Element Validation and Meshing Strategy for Pit-Corroded Pipes under Axial Compression
abstract: This study presents a validated finite element (FE) framework and an efficient meshing strategy for analyzing pit-corroded pipes under axial compression. The model is benchmarked against experimental and numerical results reported in a previous study, ensuring reliability by comparing buckling modes and load–displacement responses. A mesh convergence study identifies an optimal global element size of 3 mm, with local refinement of 0.5 mm in defect regions to accurately capture stress concentrations. Both shell and solid elements are evaluated in terms of accuracy and computational cost. While solid elements, particularly Solid187, achieve higher accuracy, with relative errors below 10%, they incur significantly greater computational cost. To improve efficiency, a quarter-symmetry model is introduced, reducing computational time by up to 50% without compromising accuracy. The proposed approach provides a robust and computationally efficient framework suitable for large-scale parametric studies of corroded pipeline structures.

title: Gene therapy strategy to treat Cornelia de Lange syndrome due to Hdac8 Deficiency
abstract: Abstract Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS) is a rare, multi-system genetic disorder characterized by developmental and cognitive impairments with systemic manifestations. Among the genes associated with CdLS, loss-of-function variants in HDAC8 account for approximately 4% of cases (referred to as CdLS5), causing the dysregulation of the cohesin complex, a core pathogenic mechanism of the disorder. Currently, no gene-based therapeutic strategy exists to directly address CdLS resulting from HDAC8 deficiency. Here, we created a new CdLS5 mouse model by introducing a clinically reported HDAC8 p.Ile19Ser variant in the mouse Hdac8 gene using CRISPR-Cas9 technology. Comprehensive molecular, morphological, and behavioral characterization revealed that the new Hdac8I19S mouse strain exhibits a robust phenotype, including marked alterations in deacetylase activity and pronounced developmental and behavioral deficits. This model was subsequently used to evaluate a gene augmentation approach aimed at increasing HDAC8 protein levels and restoring cohesin function through delivery of human HDAC8 transgene. Two AAV vectors driving expression of human HDAC8 were assessed. Although efficient delivery and robust expression were achieved, only modest effects on Smc3 acetylation, a key HDAC8 substrate, were observed, and no significant improvement in cognitive or behavioral phenotypes was detecte…

title: A Gaussian Process Regression based MPPT Strategy for Interharmonic Mitigation in On-Grid PV Systems
abstract: The widespread adoption of Photovoltaic (PV) systems as a renewable solution to rising energy demands has led to growing concerns regarding Power Quality (PQ) issues in grid current. The inherent intermittency of PV systems, along with several control techniques employed, is responsible for the generation of interharmonics that have severe impacts on the power system, including resonance and control instability. The severity of these issues increases with higher levels of PV penetration. Among the various contributing factors, the perturbation employed in the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) strategy for PV systems is reported as a significant source of interharmonics, especially under low power conditions. This paper investigates the influence of perturbation step size on MPPT performance and interharmonic emission in a 100-kW grid-connected PV system. The limitations of fixed and hybrid Perturb and Observe (P&O) methods are analyzed in terms of tracking speed and power quality indices. To overcome the limitations of conventional perturbation-based MPPT methods, a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) based MPPT approach is presented in this paper. Comparative analysis in simulation demonstrates that the proposed GPR-based MPPT significantly reduces Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) as well as Total Interharmonic Distortion (TIHD) in the grid current, while achieving faster track…
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering

title: Eggshell-associated Escherichia coli from United Arab Emirates retail eggs exhibits diverse antimicrobial resistance phenotypes, resistome profiles, and genomic backgrounds
abstract: Background Antimicrobial-resistant bacteria associated with foods of animal origin are an increasing food-safety concern; however, data on the hygienic indicator Escherichia coli from retail eggs in the Middle East remain scarce. This study investigated the occurrence, antimicrobial resistance, virulence determinants, and genomic diversity of E. coli recovered from retail table eggs in the United Arab Emirates. Methods A total of 200 retail egg packs, comprising 2,400 individual eggs, were collected from supermarkets in three major cities between October 2024 and June 2025. Eggshells and egg contents from each pack were analyzed separately. Phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed on 50 isolates, and 20 selected isolates underwent whole-genome sequencing. Results E. coli was recovered from 50 of 200 eggshell pools (25.0%; 95% confidence interval: 19.2–31.6%) but was not detected from any of the 200 egg-content pools under the analytical conditions used. An unadjusted pack-level analysis showed an association between the labeled production system and E. coli detection, with higher recovery in cage-laid packs (Fisher’s exact test, P = 0.011). Non-wild-type phenotypes were frequently observed for ciprofloxacin (76.0%), nalidixic acid (60.0%), tetracycline (48.0%), ampicillin (46.0%), and chloramphenicol (40.0%). Multiclass resistance (i.e., resistance to three…

title: Мониторинг нитратной безопасности овощной продукции в условиях розничной торговли
abstract: The paper presents the results of ecological and analytical monitoring of nitrate content in vegetable products sold through retail chains in Perm Krai. The study included organoleptic assessment, sampling and quantitative analysis of nitrate nitrogen in tuber crops and vegetables using a rapid method. The data obtained were compared with the maximum permissible concentrations (MPC) according to MU 5048-89. No exceedances of hygienic standards were found in any of the samples studied. Recommendations are proposed for reducing the risks of xenobiotics entering the human body.
venue: Partner conferences of the International Scientific Journal Research Focus

title: Emotional attributes of digital assistants driving engagement, purchase intentions and well-being
abstract: Purpose Grounded in the stimulus–organism–response (SOR) model and the spillover concept, the study examines how digital assistants’ (DAs) affective attributes shape customer engagement, which then spills over into emotional values, purchase intentions and well-being. Design/methodology/approach A two-wave longitudinal survey was conducted, yielding 440 responses at Time 1 and 315 at Time 2. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) by SmartPLS 4.0 was used to verify the reliability and validity of the measurement model and test the hypothesised relationships. Findings The findings reveal that DAs’ aesthetics, friendliness and playfulness significantly increase customer engagement, with effect sizes for these emotional stimuli varying from low to high. Customers’ active engagement also subsequently influences their emotional values: perceived happiness and relaxation. Together, these emotional values have a positive and significant effect on purchase intentions. The results also show that customer well-being is significantly spilled through purchase intentions. Moreover, customer engagement, emotional values and purchase intention yield substantial serial mediation effects in the relationships between attributional stimuli and well-being. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in extending the SOR model to a psychological outcome (well-being) an…

title: Can traditional retail physical shops employ wearable mixed reality in-store?
abstract: Purpose The quality of the consumer experience with mixed reality (MR) technology in physical retail environments remains underexplored. The study explores the quality of consumer MR head-mounted display experiences in traditional physical shops and proposes a theoretical framework for understanding space-user behaviours in MR-enabled physical environments. Design/methodology/approach This study uses triangulation and grounded theory to empirically investigate the implementation of an MR Product Configurator app in a UK fashion shop. It derives managerial and design implications for developing MR-enabled shops. Findings The findings suggest that retailers carefully design ergonomic MR environments to improve accessibility of user experience and facilitate adoption. The results address eight factors for interior design (colour, lighting, privacy, safety, sound, merchandise display, spatial dimension, and spatial layout) and four factors for MR system design (interaction design, UI design, system accessibility, and technological stability) for design recommendations to enhance the MR accessibility of physical retail environments. Originality/value An MR customer experience framework is proposed through 68 consumers who adopted an MR headset in-store. The framework depicts the quality of customer experience and current challenges. By addressing these problems, the practical implem…
venue: International Journal of Retail & Distribution Management

title: Adoption of buy-online-return-in-store services in sustainable retailing: consumer minimalism perspective
abstract: Purpose The growing importance of sustainable consumption and omnichannel retailing has positioned the buy-online-return-in-store (BORS) policy as both an operational innovation and an eco-efficient practice. This study investigates how consumer minimalism (CM), as a value-based lifestyle orientation, influences consumers' adoption of BORS services within an extended technology acceptance model (TAM) framework. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 268 consumers via a structured survey using convenience sampling, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS was employed to test the structural model and hypotheses. Findings The results reveal that CM significantly enhances perceived ease of use (PEOU) and attitudes toward BORS, with attitude emerging as the primary mediator linking values to intention to adopt. Minimalism showed no direct effect on perceived usefulness or behavioral intention, and PEOU did not directly influence attitude, suggesting that classical TAM relationships may not fully hold in sustainability-oriented retail contexts. These findings highlight the importance of value-based mechanisms in shaping technology-related adoption beyond traditional utilitarian pathways. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its single-country context, reliance on self-reported data and cross-sectional design. F…

Development and external validation of an interpretable machine learning model for identifying prevalent metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in patients with early-onset type 2 diabetes
abstract: Objective Patients with early-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus (EOT2D) are at high risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet interpretable tools for estimating prevalent MASLD in this population are lacking. We developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model using routinely available clinical variables to prompt consideration of liver ultrasonography at the index visit. Methods We included 1,322 outpatients and inpatients with EOT2D (907 [68.6%] with prevalent MASLD), divided 7:3 into training (n = 925) and internal test (n = 397) sets. After multiple imputation by chained equations (m = 5), 68 candidate variables underwent least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, Boruta selection, and collinearity screening (variance inflation factor < 5). Eight machine learning models were tuned by 10-fold cross-validation. The final model was selected on the basis of internal discrimination and calibration, interpreted with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and externally validated in 515 patients (68.0% with MASLD) from four affiliated community hospitals in the same region. Results Twelve variables were retained. The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model matched the leading algorithms in discrimination and maintained stable calibration. It achieved an AUROC of 0.773 (95% CI 0.721–0.824; AUPRC 0.864) …

title: Validation-aware interpretable machine learning for sustainability-oriented monitoring of monthly NDVI anomalies in an alpine basin of Qinghai, China
abstract: This study evaluates the accuracy and spatiotemporal generalization of machine-learning estimates of baseline-referenced monthly NDVI anomalies in an alpine study area in Qinghai, China. Pixel-wise reference anomalies were calculated from a 2006 to 2015 monthly climatology, and predictors from 2016 to 2025 included contemporaneous and lagged hydrothermal variables, antecedent NDVI anomalies, and terrain and soil attributes on a common 30 m grid. Target-month NDVI was used to define the observed response, not as a direct model predictor. Five algorithms were assessed using random-split and spatial-block validation, together with a 2025 withheld-year assessment that also informed model selection. Under predefined configurations, gradient boosting decision trees achieved the most favorable overall withheld-year validation performance. A reduced configuration combining month, contemporaneous hydrothermal variables, and lagged NDVI anomalies achieved R 2 = 0.263 and RMSE = 1.145 in 2025, compared with R 2 = 0.254 and RMSE = 1.152 for the full configuration. Lagged NDVI supplied the strongest predictive signal, whereas terrain and soil covariates added little skill. The results characterize same-month anomaly estimation under the evaluated conditions; applications to missing-data reconstruction and management decision-making require separate validation.

title: Enhancing the robustness of brain-inspired perception decision machine for fake speech detection
abstract: Introduction The rapid development of speech synthesis, voice conversion, and large-scale generative models has made fake speech more natural and difficult to detect. Existing detectors can respond differently to the same sample, yet fixed fusion does not use the state of each detector to decide how much that detector should contribute. Methods Building on the brain-inspired perception-decision framework of Feng et al., we propose the Dynamic Routing Perception-Decision Machine (DR-PDM). The method retains detector embeddings, class probabilities, one-class Softmax scores, and evidential uncertainty as detector-state information, and uses these states to generate sample-dependent fusion weights. For internally evaluated systems, operating thresholds are selected by a reproducible discrete equal-error-rate rule on development scores and frozen before evaluation. WaveFake uses its own nonoverlapping training, development, and evaluation splits: all four experts and the Router/fusion backend are trained on WaveFake training data, and no ASVspoof-trained expert weights are used. It is therefore a within-dataset experiment. Results At the applied thresholds, DR-PDM obtains precision/missing-rate pairs of 99.995%/2.085%, 99.815%/0.930%, and 100.000%/0.007% on ASVspoof2019 LA, ASVspoof2021 LA, and WaveFake, respectively. The zero-false-positive WaveFake result has a two-sided 95% exac…

title: Normalized RGB imaging and transfer learning predict surface moisture at exposed earthen sites
abstract: Abstract Repeated assessment of moisture content is essential for the preventive conservation of open-air earthen sites, yet conventional contact-based methods cannot readily provide dense spatial coverage. This study proposes a non-destructive method that predicts surface moisture content from chromatic features. A laboratory reference model was first developed using normalized RGB features (R_norm, G_norm, B_norm) that are insensitive to illuminance variation, and the model was then adapted to complex field lighting conditions through transfer learning. The transferred model yielded high prediction accuracy for the silty clay and silt tested in this study under conditions of low surface roughness (PEDI ≤0.3). Within the tested conditions, this workflow enables low-cost, non-contact assessment of surface moisture content and offers a practical tool for the field investigation and preventive conservation of open-air earthen sites.

title: Instance-specific brain image registration: learning deformable fields from a single image pair without external datasets
abstract: Abstract Objective. To eliminate the reliance on large-scale external training datasets and achieve high-precision alignment for complex brain structures by overcoming the prevalent challenges of data scarcity and domain shifts in current deep learning-based registration methods. Approach. We propose a novel Instance-Specific Deep Brain Registration Framework that independently trains a dedicated model for each specific image pair. By reconceptualizing a single image pair as an internal dataset generator, we introduce a Multi-Scale Random Patch Learning strategy to construct a diverse local-to-global sample space. Architecturally, we design a Context-Aware Flow Predictor integrated with a Recurrent Context Transfer mechanism within a coarse-to-fine paradigm. Furthermore, a Topology-Aware Adaptive Optimization strategy is incorporated during the inference phase. By dynamically tracking the local spatial folding status, it adaptively adjusts spatial regularization to effectively suppress topological distortions while maximizing voxel-level accuracy. Main results. Extensive experiments on mono-modal, multi-modal, and pathological brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our method can handle large anatomical deformations without relying on external training datasets. It achieves highly competitive registration performance compared to mainstream population-based and implicit neural repr…

title: Teaching model of practical courses in higher education based on computer-supported learning —taking underground building structures” as an example
abstract: As a core course for civil engineering undergraduates and postgraduates specializing in underground engineering, Underground Building Structures requires solid theoretical knowledge and strong practical competence. Following outcome-based education philosophy, this study explores industry-education integration strategies for application-oriented talent training. A virtual-simulation numerical-experiment platform and exercise bank are constructed. Rock-strength mechanical experiments are introduced into classroom instruction via numerical testing to help students consolidate and internalize fundamental theories. Centered on practical knowledge output supported by engineering-oriented numerical tests, this curriculum achieves the goals of knowledge input internalization, output consolidation, and teaching-research integration. It effectively guides students to apply knowledge and improves their learning initiative and creative capacity. The overall curriculum-objective-attainment value reached above 0.65 after reform.

title: Development and validation of an early warning model for secondary spinal epidural abscess in pyogenic spondylitis based on interpretable machine learning: a single-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Secondary spinal epidural abscess (SEA) in pyogenic spondylitis (PS) can rapidly compress the spinal cord or cauda equina, leading to irreversible neurological deficits such as paraplegia. Once formed, it often requires emergency surgical decompression and is associated with significantly poorer outcomes. Therefore, early identification of high-risk patients before abscess formation is of important clinical value. Objective To develop and internally validate a machine learning model for predicting the risk of secondary SEA in patients with PS, based on clinical indicators routinely available early after admission. Methods A total of 240 patients with PS were retrospectively enrolled at a single center between January 2016 and December 2025, of whom 60 (25.0%) developed secondary SEA. Patients were stratified and randomly divided into a training set ( n = 168) and a test set ( n = 72) at a 7:3 ratio. Fifty-seven candidate variables, including clinical, laboratory, and imaging data first available early after admission, were collected. In the training set, predictors were screened using univariate logistic regression ( p < 0.10) combined with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold cross-validation. Four models were subsequently developed: L2-regularized logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and eXtre…

title: Explainable deep learning localizes age-discriminative candidate regions on hand radiographs of adult women
A multi-method AI framework integrating explainable machine learning, Bayesian multilevel modeling, and latent profile analysis for childhood stunting surveillance in Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Applying AI-driven analytical methods to real-world hierarchical health data presents methodological challenges—including latent constructs, nested structures, and non-linear relationships—that no single algorithm can fully resolve. This study develops and evaluates a multi-method AI triangulation framework integrating causal discovery, explainable machine learning with SHAP, Bayesian Multilevel Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), and Latent Profile Analysis (LPA), applied to district-level stunting prevalence and its determinants across 514 districts nested within 38 provinces in Indonesia. Among the key methodological findings, we document the conditions under which causal discovery algorithms exhibit limited sensitivity in real-world settings: the Bayesian Network Structure Learning and the Peter-Clark (PC) algorithm recovered only 33.3% (2 out of 6) of theoretically specified edges, attributable to weak effect sizes, measurement error attenuation, and level-of-analysis mismatches—providing preliminary considerations for responsible AI deployment. The Bayesian Multilevel SEM achieved full convergence (R-hat = 1.000), identifying provincial poverty as the dominant stunting determinant (standardized γ = 0.630; unstandardized γ = 0.356) and explaining 42.3% of between-province variance. The Random Forest–SHAP pipeline explained 38.95% of district-level variance and det…

title: Detection of candidate acoustic biomarkers for Parkinson's disease using an explainable machine learning composite spectrogram approach
abstract: Introduction Speech abnormalities are common in Parkinson's disease (PD), and machine learning (ML) offers a potential framework for objective and scalable speech-based diagnostics. This study introduces an explainable ML pipeline that leverages a novel vowel articulation-based composite input to detect PD and identify candidate phoneme-level biomarkers. Methods Two publicly available datasets of PD speech recordings were analyzed. Sustained vowel articulations were converted into log-mel spectrograms either individually or as a composite image by vertically concatenating a set of vowels per subject. Processed spectrograms were used to train ML models, with performance assessed using repeated random subsampling with five participant-level 80:20 splits and bootstrapped area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A support vector machine, logistic regression, and random forest trained on conventional acoustic features served as baselines. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to quantify model attention across vowel regions. Results A total of 150 participants (49.3% PD) were included. After adjustment for age, sex, and dataset, cepstral peak prominence and harmonics-to-noise ratio were significantly higher in PD, particularly for the vowel /u/. The ML model achieved an average AUROC of 0.895 using individual vowels and 0.890 using …

Innovative Process for Cellulose Acetate Recovery from Cigarette Butts by Means of Natural Deep Eutectic Solvents
abstract: Abstract This work investigated a waste product of environmental concern, cigarette butts, as a potential source of cellulose acetate. It is estimated that there are 967 million smokers worldwide who produce approximately 6 trillion cigarette butts each year, causing a direct environmental impact. The proposed approach aimed to transform this polluting waste into a high-value material, recovering pure cellulose acetate from cigarette butts for reuse in a variety of applications. Developing an effective and environmentally friendly recovery method was very challenging. This was achieved by using different types of natural deep eutectic solvents (DES), which are a class of innovative solvents that combine the properties of ionic liquids and organic solvents. They are known for their sustainability and versatility. The efficiency of the various DES employed was evaluated using thermogravimetric analysis, nuclear magnetic resonance, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy and Fourier-transform infrared analysis. Based on the results obtained, the most effective DES was identified as that consisting of choline chloride and levulinic acid, which allows clean cellulose acetate to be recovered with a yield of up to 93%.

title: The effect of climate policy uncertainty and geopolitical risks on foreign tourism activities in India
abstract: Purpose While existing literature emphasises economic factors to examine tourism demand, growing uncertainties in recent years have shaped international tourism. Hence, this study examines how climate policy uncertainty (CPU) and geopolitical risks (GPR) affect India's inbound tourism demand. Design/methodology/approach We use foreign exchange earnings from tourism (FEET) and foreign tourist arrivals (FTA) to study India's tourism demand from abroad over the period 2003M1 to 2019M12. We employ a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag model to identify asymmetric short- and long-run effects and a time-varying Granger causality analysis to capture evolving causal dynamics. Findings The empirical results reveal significant nonlinear and state-dependent dynamics. CPU exerts a persistent negative effect on tourism demand, suggesting regulatory risk surrounding climate-related policies and weakening destination attractiveness. However, GPR exhibits short-lived, episodic effects, altering perceived safety during global and regional crises. The findings suggest that India's tourism sector is more sensitive to CPU than to GPR in the long run, because CPU alters the anticipated cost of future travel and tourism investment. Our results can be understood through the combined lenses of real options, expectations and risk perception theory. Research limitations/implications The findings in…

title: Optimization of post‑stroke rehabilitation: data from own clinical study of the possibilities of impact on indicators of the International Classification of Functioning
abstract: Aim: Improving the effectiveness of therapeutic and rehabilitation measures in patients during the late recovery period and with the consequences of a cerebral infarction. Methods: The results of treatment of 250 patients who suffered an ischemic stroke with a prescription period of at least 6 months and no more than 1 year (late recovery period) were analyzed. The average age of 136 women and 114 men was 63.1 years (from 28 to 74 years). The patients were divided into two 1:1 groups: the main group (received, along with basic therapy and rehabilitation, Mexidol 500 mg (10 ml) parenterally for 14 days, followed by Mexidol FORTE 250 250 mg 3 times a day orally for 2 months) and the comparison group (only basic therapy and rehabilitation). The analysis of the dynamics of the state of functions, activity, and participation was determined according to a specific set of domains in the International Classification of Functioning (ICF) system. Results: In the main group of patients, after completing therapy, a statistically significantly larger number of patients exhibited no or mild impairments, and a statistically significantly smaller number of patients had severe and absolute impairments, compared to the comparison group, across most of the analyzed domains of function, task performance, and social engagement. Conclusions: The study has demonstrated the contribution of sequential …

Digital twin driven GAT and PPO for semantic fidelity preserving robotic embroidery path optimization of Mosuo costume patterns
abstract: Abstract In electrical automation systems, when using robots to process complex vector patterns, a short tool path may interrupt critical contours or compromise structural continuity, while unsuitable motion speeds can increase tracking error and process risk. Therefore, the processing sequence and robot speed need to be optimize d without violating the structural requirements of the pattern. DT-GAT-PPO is a digital twin-based framework that integrates a Graph Attention Network (GAT) with Proximal Policy optimization(PPO). Processing points and their contour connections, feasible transitions, and expert-defined structural relationships are presented in a semantic attributed graph. A multi-head GAT encodes the graph along with the current process state, and a hybrid-action PPO policy selects the next processing node and its corresponding motion velocity. Reward balances semantic-structure preservation and non-productive travel with processing time and drive energy, trajectory deviation, jump operations, and failure risk. Training is performed in a calibrated digital twin, and then domain randomization and residual adaptation are employed to reduce the simulation-to-reality gap. A total of 1,260 digitized Mosuo costume vector patterns from 18 pattern families and physical robotic embroidery experiments were conducted. The calibrated twin had a position root-mean-square error of 0…

Deposition stability and process window optimization of polycaprolactone in robotic pellet-based additive manufacturing
abstract: Purpose Polymer pellet-based additive manufacturing (PBAM) enables large-scale, high deposition-rate; however, geometric deposition stability and comprehensive manufacturing process windows for low-viscosity, semi-crystalline polymers remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate and model geometric deposition stability in polycaprolactone (PCL) under high deposition-rate conditions. Design/methodology/approach A structured design of experiments was conducted to evaluate the effects of screw speed, robot travel speed and nominal layer height. Multivariate regression models were developed to quantify parameter interactions and predict key deposition metrics, including layer height deviation (Δzdiff), mean layer height (hzmean) and mean width (wdtmean). Findings The regression models showed high explanatory capability (R2 = 0.959–0.961) and statistically significant overall effects (p < 0.05). Distinct deposition regimes − under-extrusion, geometrically stable deposition and over-extrusion − were identified from the geometric responses and interpreted in terms of material throughput and robotic kinematic. Research limitations/implications This study is limited to the investigated PCL material, robotic PBAM configuration and parameter ranges, without direct rheological characterization, independent dimensional validation, mechanical testing or clinical evaluation. title: Optimization of PEG precipitation for macroprolactinemia screening
abstract: Abstract Objectives To determine whether 20 % or 25 % polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG) is more suitable for macroprolactinemia screening and to investigate methodological factors affecting PEG precipitation. Methods Serum samples from five individuals with macroprolactinemia and five hyperprolactinemic controls were analyzed. Gel filtration chromatography quantified the precipitation of individual prolactin (PRL) molecular forms. Nonspecific monomeric PRL precipitation was assessed using an artificial serum matrix. Incubation time, temperature, pH, and PEG solvent were also investigated. Results In the artificial serum matrix, monomeric PRL precipitation was significantly lower with 20 % than with 25 % PEG (29.3 ± 5.0 % vs. 39.2 ± 6.2 %; p=0.0053). In macroprolactinemic sera, both PEG concentrations precipitated more than 90 % of macroPRL and big PRL, with no significant differences between the two concentrations. However, monomeric PRL precipitation was significantly lower with 20 % than with 25 % PEG (28.5 ± 9.4 % vs. 39.8 ± 11.0 %; p=0.0033). Despite this difference, the proportions of monomeric PRL in the PEG precipitates differed by only 3.0 percentage points. Incubation time and temperature had limited effects on the signal-to-noise ratio. Increasing pH reduced precipitation rates without substantially altering this ratio. A 0.1 mol/L phosphate buffer at pH 7.0 maintained h…

title: Management Control Optimization under Managerial Overconfidence: A Principal–Agent Model of Business Development Decisions
abstract: Business development decisions require resource commitments under uncertain opportunity quality, giving managerial judgment a central role in investment evaluation. This study develops an agency model to examine how managerial overconfidence shapes optimal incentive intensity and monitoring intensity. A behavioral parameter captures the manager's overestimation of opportunity value, while the board anticipates the investment response and selects both control instruments. Equilibrium analysis examines how biased beliefs, environmental uncertainty, effort costs, and monitoring costs influence control choices. Overconfidence raises perceived investment returns and increases managerial effort for given control choices. Comparative statics suggest that stronger bias reduces optimal incentive intensity and increases optimal monitoring intensity. Inflated expectations provide investment motivation and reduce the need for financial rewards. Monitoring reduces evaluation error losses outside the compensation measure. Numerical illustrations show lower optimal incentive shares and higher monitoring intensity as overconfidence increases. These findings connect managerial cognition with endogenous control design and clarify how behavioral and informational conditions shape business development decisions. The model distinguishes the motivational effects of overconfidence from evaluation los…

An inexact LPA for DC composite optimization and application to matrix completion with outliers
abstract: Abstract This paper concerns a class of DC composite optimization problems which, as an extension of convex composite optimization problems and DC programs with nonsmooth components, often arises in robust factorization models of low-rank matrix recovery. For this class of nonconvex and nonsmooth problems, we propose an inexact linearized proximal algorithm (iLPA) by computing at each step an inexact minimizer of a strongly convex majorization constructed with a partial linearization of their objective functions at the current iterate. We establish the full convergence of the generated iterate sequence under the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz (KL) property of a potential function, and employ the composite structure to provide a verifiable condition for the potential function to satisfy the KL property of exponent $1/2$ at the limit point, so for the iterate sequence to have a local R-linear convergence rate. This condition is weaker than the one provided in Li & Pong (2018, Calculus of the exponent of Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz inequality and its applications to linear convergence of first-order methods. Found. Comput. Math., 18, 1199–1232, Theorem 3.2) for identifying the KL property of exponent $p\in [0,1)$ for a general composite function. The proposed iLPA is applied to a robust factorization model for matrix completion with outliers and nonuniform sampling, and numerical comparisons with th…

title: Cervical Spondylosis (Waja ul Unuq): An Integrative Review of Unani and Modern Concepts
abstract: Cervical spondylosis is a chronic degenerative disorder of the cervical spine and an important cause of neck pain, disability, radiculopathy, and myelopathy. It involves progressive changes in intervertebral discs, vertebral bodies, facet and uncovertebral joints, ligaments, and adjacent soft tissues. Modern medicine considers age-related degeneration, biomechanical stress, occupational factors, trauma, posture, smoking, metabolic factors, and genetic predisposition among important contributors. In Unani medicine, the condition is understood within the broader framework of Waja ul Mafasil and, when involving the cervical region, is described as Waja ul Unuq. Classical explanations emphasize Su-e-Mizaj, accumulation of Mawad-e-Fasida, and predominance of Balgham. This review summarizes the historical background, Unani concept and pathogenesis, modern etiopathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and therapeutic approaches. It also compares the two perspectives and identifies areas where preventive, rehabilitative, and regimenal approaches may complement contemporary care. An integrative understanding may support patient-centred management while encouraging scientific evaluation of traditional interventions.

title: Becoming: movimentos da criação de uma proposta rizomática transdisciplinar para o ensino de inglês no Ensino Médio Integrado
abstract: Este trabalho se situa no campo da Linguística Aplicada e traz problematizações de uma pesquisa pós-doutoral em andamento, a qual investiga o processo de criação de uma proposta didática de ensino de inglês com conexões rizomáticas, voltada para o Ensino Médio Integrado. O estudo visa compreender possíveis reconfigurações epistemológicas, curriculares, subjetivas, e o surgimento de agenciamentos durante o percurso do planejamento. Os participantes são duas professoras de inglês e dois professores de informática de diferentes campi do Instituto Federal do Paraná (IFPR). De caráter transdisciplinar, a proposta didática considera o uso de tecnologias digitais de comunicação e informação, e tem como ponto de partida o componente curricular “Inglês Aplicado à Computação”, integrante da grade curricular do terceiro ano do curso Técnico em Informática, no IFPR, Campus Cascavel. A pesquisa baseia-se em pressupostos teóricos de perspectiva crítica que dialogam com o pós-estruturalismo, convergindo para os estudos deleuze-guattarianos sobre rizoma e cartografia. Trata-se de um estudo qualitativo que tem a cartografia como perspectiva teórico-epistemológica, pela qual o pesquisador compreende o mundo e com ele se relaciona, acompanhando os processos que acontecem no campo investigado. title: A Low-Cost Embedded System for Non-Technical Loss Detection in Low-Voltage Distribution Networks
abstract: A low-cost wireless embedded system was developed and evaluated for the local and real-time detection of non-technical losses caused by electrical bypasses in low-voltage service drops. The architecture consists of two ESP32-based measurement nodes equipped with PZEM-004T V3 modules and interconnected through ESP-NOW. Node A measures the electrical variables at the service connection point, whereas Node B acquires the billing-point variables, processes the received telemetry, and displays the operating status through a local web dashboard. The detection model incorporates the estimated resistive loss of the service drop and applies a current-dependent dynamic threshold to distinguish technical losses from unexplained power discrepancies. Measurement pairs are validated through sequence identification, timestamp-based synchronization, and wireless-link quality criteria before classification. The experimental campaign comprised 40 scenarios, including 20 controlled tests and 20 different residential service drops with conductor cross-sectional areas of 6 and 10 mm², lengths from 4 to 25 m, and different load profiles. Thirty-eight acquisitions satisfied the established quality criteria. The system obtained 9 true positives, 28 true negatives, 0 false positives, and 1 false negative, corresponding to an accuracy of 97.37%, sensitivity of 90.00%, specificity of 100.00%, and precisi…

Justification and Integrated Illegality: An Economic Framework for Criminal Law and Competition Law
abstract: Abstract This paper builds a common welfare architecture for legal permission rules in criminal law and competition law, and distinguishes throughout between doctrine it represents, normative premises it adopts, and results that follow from them. In criminal law, the received Japanese account on which an unlawful attacker’s interest forfeits protection is represented as a discount, bounded by the ratio of anticipated harms, on the harm borne by the source of a threat. Conditional on that representation, any incompleteness of the forfeiture reintroduces a balancing term of the same order; the three emergency justifications are distinguished by who bears the harm; and a defender’s prior provocation is separated from the attacker’s wrongfulness. In competition law, the paper models incentives to deliver benefits promised in green cooperation and derives a benchmark-specific threshold for cartel unsustainability. Both fields’ deterrence assessments share an untested assumption about substitution.

title: Full Pore System Characteristics, Fractal Dimensions, and Controlling Factors of Lacustrine Laminated Shale: Implications for Shale Oil Reservoirs in the Liaohe Depression, NE China
abstract: Abstract Clarifying the pore system of unconventional oil and gas reservoirs is essential for understanding hydrocarbon accumulation, improving recovery efficiency, and accurately assessing resource potential. However, research on pore systems in lacustrine shales remains limited, largely because the development of diverse laminas produces strong heterogeneity. In the current research, 20 samples from the fourth member of the Shahejie Formation in the Western Sag, Liaohe Depression of the Bohai Bay Basin were systematically characterized through a combined approach that includes CO2 adsorption, N2 adsorption, and high-pressure mercury intrusion (HPMI) experiments. Fractal dimensions for micropores (D1), mesopores (D2), and macropores (D3) were obtained using the V–S model for CO2 adsorption, the FHH model for N2 adsorption, and the MSP model for HPMI. The results demonstrate that the laminated shale is composed of light-colored layers rich in quartz, feldspar, calcite, and dolomite, which often alternate with darker layers primarily consisting of clay minerals and organic matter. The pore system of the laminated shale consists mainly of intergranular pores, intercrystalline pores, dissolution pores, and microfractures within the matrix, excluding pores associated with organic matter. In terms of pore volume, the pore system is primarily characterized by mesopores and macropores…

title: A 1951–1998 Lutao coral Pb isotope record reveals site-specific, marine-integrated anthropogenic Pb pollution signals in the Northwest Pacific
abstract: Coral lead (Pb) isotope records provide multi-decadal perspectives on marine Pb histories, but how individual records represent regional isotope histories remains an important interpretive question. We present a 1951–1998 Pb isotope record from a Porites coral at Lutao, southeast of Taiwan, and compare it with published records from Dongsha and Ogasawara in the Northwest Pacific. The three coral records exhibited substantial inter-site isotopic differences during 1953–1963, smaller differences in interval-mean 208 Pb/ 207 Pb during 1964–1984, and persistent site-specific characteristics. In 1985–1998, Lutao had a statistically distinguishable lower 208 Pb/ 207 Pb composition than Dongsha, whereas the middle-to-late change within Lutao itself was not statistically resolved. This contrast shows that inter-site isotopic differences need not imply an equivalent temporal shift at an individual site. Published Pb isotope reference fields are compatible with multiple possible source combinations but do not uniquely identify historical sources or marine transport mechanisms. Together, these results reveal spatial heterogeneity in coral Pb isotope histories, with smaller inter-site differences during 1964–1984, and highlight the need to evaluate the spatial representativeness of individual coral Pb isotope records before extrapolating site-specific signatures to regional historical inte…

title: Entre a avenida e o cubo branco: Vermelho-Mangue e reconfiguração da visualidade carnavalesca no sistema de arte
abstract: Resumo Este trabalho investiga a inserção da obra Vermelho-Mangue (2025), derivada de um carro alegórico concebido pelos carnavalescos Leonardo Bora e Gabriel Haddad para o desfile da Acadêmicos do Grande Rio (2025), no espaço expositivo do Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, no Rio de Janeiro. A análise se concentra na transposição dessa visualidade carnavalesca – construída a partir de metodologias de criação coletiva e fortemente territorializadas — para o contexto museológico, buscando compreender de que maneira esse deslocamento produz efeitos institucionais e políticos, especialmente, ao tensionar hierarquias historicamente estabelecidas entre arte erudita e cultura popular. Em contraste com uma possível “visão tecnocrática”, centrada exclusivamente em resultados, o estudo propõe pensar a gestão dessa obra no museu como uma forma de ação política, entendendo seu processo de inserção como um campo de disputa no qual práticas, valores e modos de legitimação são continuamente reconfigurados. A partir das contribuições de Muniz Sodré, Françoise Vergès e Rita Segato, discute-se a carnavalização não apenas como um recurso estético, mas como um regime estético-político capaz de operar processos de descolonização das instituições artísticas e, ao mesmo tempo, de tensionar a lógica de mera “administração do existente”. Argumenta-se, ainda, que a presença do carnaval no CCBB-RJ não se…

title: Dos papéis às práticas: reflexões iniciais sobre as potencialidades e os desafios de consolidar o Sistema Nacional de Cultura em Pernambuco
abstract: Este ensaio tem como objetivo refletir sobre as potencialidades e os desafios de implementação do Sistema Nacional de Cultura em Pernambuco. Trata-se do trabalho de conclusão das disciplinas Políticas Culturais: trajetória e desafios contemporâneos; e Gestão Cultural: do tecnicismo ao engajamento, cursadas no âmbito da Especialização em Política e Gestão Cultural, realizada pela Universidade Federal do Recôncavo Baiano, em parceria com o Ministério da Cultura, por meio da Escola Solano Trindade de Formação e Qualificação Artística, Técnica e Cultural. A partir de revisão bibliográfica e análise documental, percorre-se a trajetória do SNC desde sua concepção até o atual marco regulatório (Lei nº 14.835/2024), destacando o papel catalisador das leis emergenciais da pandemia (Lei Aldir Blanc e Lei Paulo Gustavo) e da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc (PNAB). Como estratégia metodológica, as autorias partem das suas experiências laborais: ela, na Secretaria de Cultura do Estado de Pernambuco, e ele do Escritório Estadual do Ministério da Cultura em Pernambuco, para, em articulação aos conteúdos abordados nas duas matérias, analisar de forma crítica os diversos momentos da implementação do Sistema Nacional de Cultura no Estado, em busca de aprimorar sua consolidação como uma política estruturante. title: Linking the complement system to endometriosis pathogenesis: a systematic review of diagnostic potential
abstract: Endometriosis (EM) is a chronic gynecological disorder affecting roughly 5-10% of women in their reproductive age, with symptom onset often occurring during adolescence but diagnosis frequently delayed for several years. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving immunological, hormonal, genetic, and environmental factors. Increasing evidence suggests that immune dysregulation, particularly involving the complement system, a key effector of innate immunity and mediator of inflammatory responses, contributes to EM pathogenesis by sustaining chronic inflammation, angiogenesis, and lesion development. This review summarizes the available evidence on the involvement of complement components in EM pathogenesis and evaluates their potential use as biomarkers. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Embase following PRISMA guidelines, including all eligible studies published up to July 2026. After full-text screening, 64 of 652 studies were selected and included in the final analysis. Overall, evidence supported a predominant involvement of the alternative complement pathway in EM, with complement component C3 emerging as the most extensively investigated molecule (35/64 studies). Evidence for the classical and lectin pathways was comparatively limited and heterogeneous. Moreover, several complement regulators emerged as differentially expressed in trans…

title: Early detection of drug-resistant epilepsy via multi-domain EEG fusion with prefrontal candidate biomarkers
abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) is associated with poor clinical outcomes. Interictal scalp EEG-based DRE identification faces a methodological limitation: segment-level models often capture individual-specific EEG patterns rather than group-level pathological differences. In this retrospective study of 42 patients (21 DRE, 21 non-DRE), we constructed an EEG-based DRE recognition framework. Multi-domain features (temporal, spectral, nonlinear) were extracted, and a mutual validation strategy integrating patient-level statistical tests and machine learning was applied to verify the pathological discriminative validity of features. A multi-domain support vector machine was built with ReliefF feature selection, evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation and hold-out validation, and further analyzed for interpretability and clinical correlations. Significant between-group differences were found in clinical and electrophysiological features, with prominent alterations in prefrontal temporal statistics, θ/β band power and entropy features. The multi-domain model consistently outperformed single-domain models; prefrontal β/γ power and entropy features were identified as core candidate biomarkers, significantly correlated with disease duration and seizure frequency. This study identifies prefrontal EEG features as candidate DRE biomarkers, and the combined validation framework supports…

title: Gut microbiota and metabolomic features associated with hemoglobin improvement in patients with aplastic anemia: an exploratory clinical multi-omics study
abstract: Background Hematologic recovery after treatment varies substantially among patients with aplastic anemia (AA). This exploratory clinical multi-omics study aimed to characterize gut microbial and metabolomic features associated with hemoglobin improvement in patients with AA. Methods Nineteen patients with AA who received kidney-nourishing and marrow-benefiting traditional Chinese medicine combined with conventional Western medical treatment were included. According to hematologic response at approximately 6 months, patients were classified as responders ( n = 14) or non-responders ( n = 5). Paired fecal and serum samples collected before and after treatment were analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. Hb_change, defined as post-treatment hemoglobin minus baseline hemoglobin, was used as the primary clinical variable. Associations between omics features and Hb_change were assessed using Spearman correlation with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Leave-one-out analysis, bootstrap confidence intervals, baseline Hb-adjusted models, and paired longitudinal analyses were used to further examine selected associations. Results Hb_change was greater in responders than in non-responders (31.5 vs. 10.0 g/L, p = 0.006). In the pretreatment microbiome, Methyloversatilis was negatively correlated with Hb_change (rho = −0.712, p = 0.000627, q = 0.0881), whereas Shuttlewor…

title: Multi-channel discrimination of crystallographic defects in 4H-SiC epitaxial wafers using optical inspection, photoluminescence and X-ray topography
abstract: Accurate identification of crystallographic defects in 4H-SiC epitaxial wafers is essential for ensuring the yield and reliability of SiC power devices. Although a variety of inspection techniques have been developed, defect visibility varies substantially among characterization methods, making reliable automated defect classification challenging. In this study, a multi-channel defect identification framework that integrates optical inspection, photoluminescence, and X-ray topography using a convolutional neural network was developed. Images acquired by the three techniques were spatially registered and combined into multi-channel datasets for analysis. A Faster R-convolutional neural network was trained using annotated data collected from 18 epitaxial wafers. The trained model was evaluated using an independent test wafer containing reliability-relevant defects, including micropipes, basal plane dislocations, threading screw dislocations, stacking faults, stacking-fault complexes, polytype inclusions, and particle inclusions. Compared with models trained on individual inspection modalities, the multi-channel model exhibited improved classification performance by integrating complementary morphological, luminescence, and crystallographic information.

title: The TNG50-SKIRT Atlas: Multi-wavelength properties of galaxy discs in the TNG50 simulation
abstract: We investigate the wavelength dependence of disc scale lengths in galaxies from the TNG50–SKIRT Atlas (TSA), and assess whether the simulated galaxies reproduce the structural properties and scaling relations observed in real galaxies, as well as the physical origin of the wavelength dependence. We measure disc scale lengths from one-dimensional radial surface-brightness profiles of multi-wavelength synthetic images. The disc-dominated region is defined interactively per galaxy and applied consistently across bands. We restrict the analysis to nearly face-on, star-forming galaxies and retain only systems whose r -band profiles are well described by an exponential model. The resulting scale lengths are compared to observational samples and analysed using both dust-attenuated and dust-free images, as well as intrinsic stellar population maps. We find that the majority of TSA galaxies exhibit exponential discs in realistic mock observations. The TSA galaxies reproduce the observed disc scale length--stellar mass (luminosity) relation, but are systematically larger at fixed mass or luminosity. The dependence of disc scale length on morphology is weak. Disc scale lengths correlate strongly across wavelengths but decrease systematically with increasing wavelength. When normalised by the stellar-mass scale length, the TSA galaxies exhibit a clear and monotonic trend consistent with ob…

title: WavLM-Guided Dual-Gated Multi-Level Acoustic Feature Fusion for Speech-Based Depression Detection
Development of the Health District Evaluation Framework (HDEF): a multi-method study of population health evaluation in Singapore
Multi-toxicant exposure to beauvericin, arsenic trioxide, and glyphosate enhances cytotoxicity and intracellular ROS levels in NIH-3T3 fibroblast cells
abstract: Introduction Human exposure to environmental contaminants typically occurs through complex chemical mixtures rather than individual compounds; however, the toxicological interactions among co-occurring contaminants remain poorly understood. This study investigated the cytotoxic interactions of the mycotoxin beauvericin (BEA), the pesticide glyphosate (GLY), and arsenic trioxide (ATO) in binary and ternary combinations using NIH‐3T3 fibroblasts. Methods Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay. Toxicological interactions were quantitatively characterized using the Chou‐Talalay method based on combination index (CI) and dose reduction index (DRI) analyses. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation was measured to evaluate oxidative stress. Results Among the individual toxicants, ATO exhibited the greatest cytotoxicity, followed by BEA and GLY. Combination analysis revealed distinct interaction profiles depending on mixture composition. BEA + ATO and BEA + GLY consistently exhibited synergistic cytotoxicity, whereas ATO + GLY showed predominantly additive effects. Notably, the ternary mixture displayed a dose‐dependent interaction pattern, transitioning from antagonism at a low effect level (IC 10 ) to synergism at a high effect level (IC 50 ). These interaction profiles were accompanied by increased intracellular ROS generation, with synergistic combinations s…

title: Multi-scale insights into the hierarchical architecture and mechanical anisotropy of bamboo lignocellulosic fibers
Global trends and emerging frontiers in rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms: a multi-database bibliometric analysis
abstract: Background Research on rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms (R-NENs) has grown, but the development of this site-specific literature and the consistency of its main patterns across databases have not been examined together. Methods We mapped English-language articles and reviews from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC), then used separately screened Scopus and PubMed records to compare publication trends, leading countries, and prespecified clinical themes. Author keywords and Keywords Plus were normalized and deduplicated within records. Results The primary WoSCC corpus included 875 publications. Of these, 803 met the direct title-and-abstract rule used for validation; the corresponding Scopus and PubMed sets contained 1,018 and 703 records. Annual output was strongly correlated across databases (Pearson r=0.979–0.992), although record overlap was moderate (Jaccard=0.531–0.545). Country and theme ranks showed partial agreement, while their absolute frequencies varied. Across time, the literature moved from historical ‘carcinoid’ terminology toward endoscopic resection, pathological risk, prognosis, and decisions after local treatment. Conclusion The analysis maps how R-NEN research has developed and where further clinical studies are needed. Cross-database agreement supports the overall growth pattern and some broad rankings, but it does not establish the validity of any tre…

title: Enhanced multi-object detection in brachial plexus ultrasound images using transformer-based semantic and spatial feature fusion
abstract: Abstract Advances in medical imaging have led to the widespread use of ultrasound for diagnosing and treating peripheral nerve blocks. However, challenges such as speckle noise and low spatial resolution hinder the accurate identification of neural structures. To address these issues, a model named transformer-based detection with semantic and spatial feature fusion (TDSS) was introduced, integrating spatial edge adaptive enhancement, multi-scale semantic fusion, and spatial distillation-assisted detection modules. These components improve edge perception, multi-scale semantic reasoning, and localization accuracy. Experiments on the Ultrasound Brachial Plexus Dataset demonstrated the superior performance of the model: TDSS achieved an AP of 0.407 for nerve detection and an overall mAP of 0.583, providing robust support for clinical medical image detection. The source code for the proposed TDSS framework is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18824199 .

title: Integrated Reactive CO2 and NH3 Capture and Conversion to Ammonium Carbamate: Material Design toward Low-Concentration Sources
abstract: Abstract Carbon dioxide (CO2) and ammonia (NH3) emissions are responsible for global warming and eutrophication, among other causes. Ionic liquids (ILs) stand out as versatile designer absorbent/catalyst materials that contribute to the capture and conversion of both gases. This work focuses on the efficient and innovative use of ILs in NH3 and CO2 integrated capture and conversion (ICC) to produce ammonium carbamate (AMC) using an efficient self-regenerating catalytic system operating at room temperature, with spontaneous product separation by precipitation. Experimental ICC tests were carried out using 10 ILs, with remarkable structural differences, and different NH3 and CO2 partial pressure and experimental times. Two different optimization routes were explored by tuning the IL material features through molecular design: (i) an NH3-driven mechanism using IL as the physical absorbent and (ii) a CO2-driven mechanism using IL as the reactive capture agent, selected to promote high CO2 chemical absorption and activation and easy IL regeneration and AMC removal. The use of an IL as a reactive capture agent strongly improves the process performance with fast ICC rates even at low NH3 and CO2 partial pressures, highlighting the CO2-driven approach as a versatile ICC technology capable of efficiently treating diluted NH3 and CO2 streams to produce value-added AMC products.

Principles of textbook development and instructional design for beginner Uzbek: a contrastive linguistic perspective
abstract: Addressing the needs of students majoring in Uyghur or Chinese who take Uzbek as a minor, this paper examines two language textbooks through content analysis and Uzbek–Uyghur comparison. It proposes principles based on communicative needs, explicit explanation of differences, differentiated support, and the recycling of language content. Contrastive analysis is incorporated into contextualized input, task performance, and revision following feedback, providing a basis for developing a textbook for beginning learners of Uzbek.

title: Estudos decoloniais da América Latina: interseções entre o design e o artesanato para novos futuros
abstract: O design decolonial emerge como uma resposta crítica à dominação eurocêntrica que historicamente moldou as práticas e os discursos do design na América Latina, influenciando modos de produzir, interpretar e valorizar objetos e saberes. Nesse contexto, este artigo analisa as interseções entre o design decolonial e o artesanato geracional, compreendendo-os como espaços de resistência, reexistência e produção de alternativas ao modelo hegemônico, com ênfase nas convergências entre o crochê e o bordado. Muito antes do processo de colonização, diversas comunidades latino-americanas já desenvolviam tradições artesanais têxteis, transmitidas intergeracionalmente como parte de sistemas simbólicos, culturais e identitários próprios. Essas práticas configuram-se como formas complexas de expressão e comunicação, articulando memória, pertencimento e modos de vida situados. No que se refere ao crochê, sua prática emerge em diferentes contextos históricos e se expande no período pós-colonial, sendo compreendida como espaço de construção de subjetividades, fortalecimento de vínculos sociais e constituição de redes afetivas. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, de natureza exploratória e interdisciplinar, orientada por uma perspectiva decolonial. Tal abordagem possibilita compreender as dimensões simbólicas, culturais e políticas das práticas artesanais, ao mesmo tempo em que valoriza s…

title: Canine osteoarthritis: occurrence, functional impact, management and associated factors in a cross-sectional survey of French-speaking dog owners
Explainable AI-based framework for 3D structural as-built modeling of aging buildings in Korea using laser scanning
abstract: Purpose This study proposes a framework for automatically generating 3D structural as-built models of aging buildings by predicting the structural dimensions of members concealed behind finishes using laser scanning and machine learning, particularly when original construction drawings are unavailable. Design/methodology/approach Laser scanning captures building geometry but includes both structural components and non-structural finishes (e.g. plaster), making it unsuitable for directly extracting structural dimensions. To address this, the proposed framework extracts geometric features from point clouds and employs machine learning techniques to predict structural dimensions of columns, beams, walls and slabs. Six machine learning models – Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Linear Regression and Support Vector Regression (SVR) – were trained using data collected on 1,560 column elements, 2,875 beam elements, 870 wall elements and 148 slab elements across 50 buildings and validated through two real-world case studies. Findings The best-performing model achieved MAPE of 10.51% for column width (95%CI: 8.47–12.71), 12.98% for column depth (95% CI: 10.86–15.41), 14.91% for beam width (95% CI: 13.63–16.15), 18.91% for beam depth (95% CI: 17.94–19.90), 10.42% for walls (95% CI: 8.89–12.00) and 10.70% for slabs (95% CI: 7.11–14.50). The predicted dimensions enabled reconstru…

title: Health insurance shields families, yet inequalities still shape India's path toward financial protection and equity
O direito ao ócio e à criatividade: a pedagogia da capoeira angola como contraponto a uma educação mercantilizada
abstract: Este artigo analisa criticamente as políticas educacionais contemporâneas que, pautadas por avaliações em larga escala e pela mercantilização do ensino, reduzem a escola pública a um simulacro de adestramento para o mercado flexível e para a ideologia do empreendedorismo de si. Em contraposição a esse sequestro do tempo vital da juventude trabalhadora, propõe-se a pedagogia da Capoeira Angola como um contraponto político-epistêmico e metodológico. Metodologicamente, a pesquisa de natureza qualitativa e exploratória baseia-se em revisão bibliográfica e análise histórico-documental, com ênfase na criminalização histórica da “vadiagem” e da “capoeiragem” pelo Código Penal de 1890. Discute-se a vadiagem não como inércia, mas como categoria revolucionária que reivindica o direito inalienável ao ócio criador e à soberania temporal contra a lógica do “negócio” (nec-otium). Como resultado, caracteriza-se a Capoeira Angola como um sistema artístico-marcial autopoiético que recusa a competição e a esportivização da vida. Conclui-se que a transposição tática dos fundamentos da roda — como a mandinga, a malícia e a cooperação — para o cotidiano da escola formal oferece caminhos para que educadores transformem as salas de aula em trincheiras de resistência, instrumentalizando os estudantes com a agudeza cognitiva necessária para ler as contradições sociais e lutar pela emancipação coletiva.
