title: Correcting stellar contamination in transmission spectroscopy with contemporaneous monitoring: Application to GJ 1214 b
abstract: Transmission spectroscopy has emerged as an essential tool for characterising the atmospheres of transiting exoplanets. However, stellar surface inhomogeneities contaminate transmission spectra, which poses a major challenge, particularly to high-precision observations such as those from the (JWST). James Webb Space Telescope We developed and applied a set of practical methodologies to correct for stellar contamination in transmission spectroscopy data, thereby improving the accuracy of exoplanet atmospheric characterisation. We obtained coordinated multi-band photometry and high-resolution spectroscopy around JWST observations of GJ,1214,b and applied two correction frameworks: (i) an inversion with the StarSim code, in which we infer stellar activity parameters from the monitoring data and propagate them to corrections; and (ii) , a data-driven approach in which neural networks (NNs) are trained on a large suite of simulations to learn the mapping from the monitoring data to the corrections. StarSim Both frameworks agree within the uncertainties and indicate that the JWST observations of GJ,1214 occurred at a favourable rotation phase with low stellar contamination. For , the inferred corrections can be constrained at the ∼10--30 ppm level across the JWST wavelength range, implying post-correction residuals of the same order. If the same system were observed near activity max…

title: Climate shapes mosquito-borne disease transmission in africa: a scoping review of climatic determinants, biological responses and transmission dynamics
abstract: Abstract Background Mosquito-borne diseases remain a major public-health challenge in Africa, and their transmission is strongly influenced by climatic conditions. However, the evidence is geographically uneven and methodologically heterogeneous. Objective To map and synthesise evidence on the influence of temperature, rainfall/precipitation and relative humidity on mosquito-borne disease transmission in Africa, and to compare climatic patterns across major vector–pathogen systems. Methods A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR. Peer-reviewed primary studies conducted in Africa, or providing identifiable Africa-specific evidence, were included if they investigated malaria, dengue, chikungunya or Zika and assessed temperature, rainfall/precipitation and/or relative humidity in relation to biological, entomological, ecological, transmission-related or epidemiological outcomes. Results Eighteen primary studies were included: 10 on malaria, 6 on dengue and 2 on Zika; none specifically addressed chikungunya. Temperature was the most frequently assessed exposure. Malaria studies showed non-linear and context-dependent temperature relationships, including a field peak in malaria positivity near 25 °C. Dengue studies showed heterogeneous temperature signals, including stronger temperature–incidence relationships above approximately 21 °C and increased transmission-related …

title: Shock impedance mismatch and transmission loss in fiber–metal laminates: a computational and experimental study
abstract: Abstract The shielding performance of multi-layered sandwich structures is influenced by the shock impedance mismatch at material interfaces. In this study, an integrated computational, analytical, and experimental framework was developed to evaluate the acoustic transmission loss (TL) of fiber–metal laminates (FMLs) incorporating fabric-reinforced polymer core plies. A dimensionless shock-impedance formulation based on the Buckingham- $$\pi $$ theorem was employed to examine the influence of material properties, including Poisson’s ratio, on three-dimensional elastic wave propagation and aid in material selection. A mesoscale representative volume element (RVE) approach was used to derive the effective orthotropic properties of aramid-, basalt-, and Zylon-reinforced plies, which were subsequently incorporated into a macroscale finite-element (FE) harmonic-acoustics framework to evaluate TL over the 63–1300,Hz frequency range. In parallel, a multi-layer analytical formulation was developed to estimate insertion loss and the corresponding frequency-dependent TL response. The empirical parameters of the analytical model were calibrated using a single baseline configuration and subsequently applied to six additional stacking sequences, for which the mean TL difference from the corresponding FE predictions remained below $$3.06\%$$ . Impedance-tube measurements of the baseline Al–B…

title: Financial Leverage, Profitability, and Firm Value: Evidence From Primary Consumer Goods Companies Listed on The Indonesia Stock Exchange
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dan menjelaskan pengaruh Financial Leverage dan Profitabilitas terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada perusahaan sektor Barang Konsumen Primer yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2019–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif. Populasi penelitian terdiri atas 125 perusahaan, dengan teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditentukan, sehingga diperoleh 10 perusahaan sebagai sampel penelitian. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan metode regresi linier berganda, sedangkan pengolahan data dilakukan dengan bantuan program EViews versi 13. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Financial Leverage dan Profitabilitas secara simultan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan yang diproksikan dengan Price to Book Value (PBV). Secara parsial, Financial Leverage yang diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan. Demikian pula, Profitabilitas yang diproksikan dengan Return on Assets (ROA) berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan.

title: Corporate GHG emissions and financial performances: the moderating role of CEO overconfidence
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether CEO overconfidence shapes the relationship between corporate greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and firm financial performance. It asks whether emissions are uniformly value-destroying or whether their financial consequences depend on executive cognition and the operating scale embedded in emissions-intensive activity. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses panel data on 1,816 US-listed firms over 2002–2020, with up to 33,179 firm-year observations depending on variable availability. GHG emissions are measured using total emissions, Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3, revenue-scaled emissions intensity and environmental cost indicators. Firm performance is captured by return on equity, return on assets and Tobin's Q. CEO overconfidence is measured mainly through the Holder67 option-based proxy. The study applies firm and year fixed-effects models, scale-sensitive robustness tests, an alternative overconfidence proxy based on overinvestment, two-stage least squares and dynamic panel generalized method of moments (GMM) diagnostics. Findings GHG emissions are positively associated with firm performance when firms are led by overconfident CEOs. This result holds across accounting and market-based measures and remains evident when emissions are separated by scope and when revenue-scaled intensity is examined. The positive association is stronger under h…

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Financial Decision-Making Quality among SMEs in Freetown, Sierra Leone: The Moderating Role of Digital Capability
abstract: This study investigates the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on financial decision-making quality (FDMQ) among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Freetown, Sierra Leone. It examines the moderating role of digital capability. The study used a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design with a sample of 250 owner-managers and finance officers from SMEs in formal and semi-formal business clusters in Freetown, based on the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework and Resource-Based View (RBV). The data were analyzed using SPSS with descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and hierarchical moderated multiple regression. Findings showed that AI adoption (β = .573, p .001) and digital capability (β = .283, p .001) were significant, positive predictors of FDMQ. The AI adoption–FDMQ relationship was also significantly moderated by digital capability (β = .195, ΔR² = .035, p .001). Simple slopes analysis showed that the effect of AI adoption was more than doubled when digital capability increased from low to high. AI adoption enhances SME financial decision-making, but its impact relies on supporting digital capabilities. The study builds on the TOE and RBV frameworks in an under-researched West African context. It emphasizes the importance of integrating AI provision with digital capability development. Findings suggest associations, not causal or broa…

title: Physics-grounded sequence-domain graph learning for adaptive fault location in IBR-dominated offshore wind farm transmission networks
abstract: Abstract Fault location in offshore wind-farm networks dominated by inverter-based resources (IBRs) is complicated by converter-limited fault currents, cable charging currents and high fault resistance, which violate the assumptions of classical impedance-based estimators. This paper proposes PG-SDGL, a physics-grounded sequence-domain graph-learning framework that combines a graph-attention sequence-domain graph neural network (SeqGNN), a three-sequence physics-informed neural network (3Seq-PINN) for fault-resistance decoupling, sequence-residual split-conformal prediction intervals, cable charging-current compensation, an analytical IBR fault-current decomposition, a harmonic high-impedance-fault (HIF) gate with Dempster–Shafer fusion of two intelligent electronic devices and a protection-consistency index (PCI). The framework was evaluated in simulation on a 69 kV network with a 60 km overhead interconnection line and three 5–9 km submarine cable feeders, for four fault types and fault resistances of 2–150 Ω. Feeder-identification accuracy was 99.4–99.6%. Over 2–40 Ω, the average main-line mean relative error (MRE) was 0.195%, compared with 0.631% in the published random-forest benchmark on the same line model. The average fault-resistance mean absolute error decreased from 4.67 Ω (random-forest benchmark) to 2.07 Ω (single-sequence PINN) and 1.98 Ω (3Seq-PINN). The sequence…

title: Direito Humano à Água e Desigualdades Territoriais: uma análise crítica das políticas públicas de segurança hídrica no Brasil
abstract: O acesso à água potável constitui um direito humano fundamental reconhecido internacionalmente, porém sua efetivação permanece marcada por profundas desigualdades territoriais e socioambientais. No Brasil, apesar da ampla disponibilidade hídrica e da existência de marcos legais estruturantes, como a Política Nacional de Recursos Hídricos e o Marco Legal do Saneamento Básico, o acesso seguro e contínuo à água ainda não é garantido de forma universal. Este artigo analisa criticamente as políticas públicas nacionais voltadas à segurança hídrica, discutindo os avanços normativos, os instrumentos institucionais de gestão e os limites de sua implementação no território brasileiro. A partir de revisão bibliográfica, análise documental e abordagem geográfica crítica, o estudo examina a construção do direito humano à água no cenário internacional, sua incorporação ao arcabouço jurídico brasileiro e as tensões entre gestão técnica dos recursos hídricos e justiça socioambiental. A análise evidencia que a desigualdade no acesso à água resulta da interação entre fatores ambientais, sociais e institucionais, revelando como políticas públicas frequentemente reproduzem assimetrias históricas que afetam especialmente populações rurais, comunidades tradicionais e territórios periféricos. Nesse contexto, argumenta-se que a segurança hídrica deve ser compreendida não apenas como um problema técnic…

title: Scope 3 Emissions Framing and Corporate Climate Litigation: Encouraging the Right Narratives?
abstract: Abstract The article analyses the framing of scope 3 emissions in corporate climate litigation and the narratives they give rise to. It examines scope 3’s origins and its presence in legislative and other regulatory measures before analysing scope 3 emissions framing in a series of landmark cases globally. The case law on scope 3 is presented across five broad categories involving corporations: business challenges to climate disclosure legislation, and then greenwashing, project, due diligence and liability cases brought by the climate movement. How do we and how should we frame what a company’s emissions are, for which it is legally responsible? The article outlines how the case law reflects a framing contest over what emissions properly belong to a company. It then discusses narratives involved in some of the key scope 3 emissions categories. While finding that there are strategically positive narratives for the climate movement, it argues that some of its corporate climate litigation plays into problematic private governance and market-led narratives. A case is made for a carbon takeback obligation (CTBO) as part of a policy-led narrative to help resolve these tensions.

Out of the Mattresses and Into the Banks: Unpacking Financial Disintermediation and Liquidity Dynamics in South Sudan
abstract: This study investigates the behavioral, structural, and macroeconomic drivers of mattress banking, the widespread practice of hoarding cash outside formal financial institutions in South Sudan. Drawing on mixed-methods field data collected in 2026 (N=800), consisting of 650 structured survey respondents and 150 qualitative interview and focus group participants, the research identifies cultural attachment to traditional saving methods (12.1%) and fear of government scrutiny (11.3%) as the most salient factors, alongside systemic bank liquidity concerns (7.1%) and institutional distrust (6.7%). Macroeconomic impacts include weakened monetary policy, reduced access to private-sector credit, and significant losses to formal bank deposits, with households facing heightened risks of theft (8.3%) and asset destruction from disasters (7.5%). Regression and thematic analyses reveal that women, rural residents, the unbanked, and informal sector workers are particularly vulnerable to mattress banking, which is further exacerbated by chronic salary delays and low financial literacy. The study recommends a multi-pronged approach to reintegrate informal liquidity: expanding digital and mobile banking, strengthening regulatory oversight and deposit insurance, simplifying account opening, and fostering public trust through robust consumer protection and financial education. Theoretically, the…

title: Crystal-axis dependence of nonreciprocal spin-wave transmission in asymmetric Fe/MgO/NiFe trilayers
abstract: We investigated the crystal-axis dependence of nonreciprocal spin-wave transmission in asymmetric Fe/MgO/NiFe trilayer waveguides. Spin-wave transmission was measured in the Damon–Eshbach geometry for two configurations: the easy-axis configuration, with the magnetic field applied along Fe[100], and the hard-axis configuration, with the field along Fe[110]. The transmission spectra exhibited propagation-direction-dependent differences in both amplitude and frequency. In particular, the directional amplitude difference of one experimentally observed branch reversed its polarity upon reversal of the external magnetic field in both configurations. Micromagnetic simulations showed propagation-direction-dependent localization of the dynamic magnetization and revealed that the spectral separation between the Fe-like and NiFe-like branches depended on the orientation relative to the Fe crystal axes. These results demonstrate the important role of the Fe crystal axes in nonreciprocal spin-wave transmission in asymmetric magnetic multilayers.

title: A Design of an Effective Banking Application with Customer Churn Prediction and Enhanced Market Equilibrium Based Security Testing Through Machine Learning
abstract: Banking application and compliance with the EU PSD2 directive and the impact of protection motivation theory oninformation security. It identifies a gap in PMT literature and examines factors influencing consumer adoption of Fintech banking amidst ongoing digitalization. To overcome this issue, a new model has developed Customer Churn Prediction and Enhanced Market Equilibrium based Security Testing (CCMEST). This investigation proposes that integrating analytical modeling, market analysis, security validation, hypothesis testing, and machine learning will enhance banking applications through a model that factors in labor, capital, management, and effort using a Cobb-Douglas production function to assess firm value-added and managerial incentives and Cumulative distribution function (CDF). Companies will be evaluated on capital, management talent, and their effectiveness in achieving market equilibrium while assessing compensation and value-added. Security Testing involved 19 tests on banking API operations, focusing on secure communication, authentication, transaction fetching, and unauthorized request rejection. Hypothesis Testing evaluated statistical correlations using t-statistics, p-values, and PLS-SEM, with significant results determined by pre-set thresholds. title: Modeling the Future of Finance: Digital Transformation, Fintech Innovations, Market Adaptation, and Strategic Growth
abstract: The financial industry is undergoing a profound transformation driven by rapid advancements in digital technologies, fintech innovations, and evolving market dynamics. This paper explores the critical role of digital transformation in reshaping financial services, emphasizing the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, big data analytics, and cloud computing to enhance efficiency, security, and customer experience. Fintech innovations have disrupted traditional banking models, enabling digital payments, decentralized finance (DeFi), roboadvisors, and open banking, fostering financial inclusion and accessibility. Market adaptation remains a crucial aspect of this evolution, as financial institutions must navigate regulatory challenges, cybersecurity threats, and shifting consumer expectations. This study examines the impact of digital disruption on traditional financial frameworks, highlighting the adoption of agile methodologies, risk management strategies, and regulatory compliance to ensure stability and resilience in a rapidly changing landscape. Additionally, the rise of embedded finance and digital currencies is reshaping transactional ecosystems, prompting financial institutions to innovate and collaborate with technology providers to sustain competitive advantage. Strategic growth in the digital finance era requires a data-driven approach, leveraging pre…

title: Forecasting High Electricity Demand Using Explainable Machine Learning
abstract: The objective of this study was to predict the onset of high demand, the highest half-hourly average power, and the total duration of high demand over the next two hours using historical electricity consumption data from residential households. Half-hourly measurements from 2013 for 200 standard-tariff residential households selected from the Low Carbon London dataset were used. High demand was defined as exceeding the 90th percentile of each household’s average power values during the January–February period. The models were developed using data from 160 households; transfer performance was evaluated on the 40 households not included in model training. The process was divided into a training period (March–June), model selection in July, calibration of prediction intervals in August, and a testing period (September–December). The selected models were retrained using March–July data. Separate models were built for the three targets; Random Forest, histogram-based gradient boosting (HistGB), XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost were compared against a weekly seasonal reference. Model selection was initially based on average precision (AP) for the target and mean absolute error (MAE) for power and duration. For the residential units used in the training, the HistGB model selected during the testing period produced an AP of 0.4183; the CatBoost models produced an MAE of 0.2704 kW for po…

title: Economic Policy Uncertainty as a Driver of Risk Premia in Emerging Market Swap Spreads
abstract: We examine the impact of domestic and global economic policy uncertainty (EPU) on interest rate swap spreads in the BRIC economies, representing the leading emerging markets. We mainly find that the impact of EPU is state-dependent and follows a regime-switching model. On applying the Markov regime-switching model, the effect of EPU was found to be statistically significant only in the relatively less volatile regime. During the high-volatility regime, the impact of EPU is surpassed by noise and other extraneous variables of the term structure and volatility index. When the impacts of domestic and global EPU are examined separately, global EPU is found to reduce swap spreads across all major maturities. This pattern suggests the relative resilience of these economies during periods of heightened global uncertainty and reflects investors’ tendency to drift toward safer fixed-income instruments. In contrast, the effects of domestic EPU are maturity-specific. During low-volatility regimes, higher levels of domestic EPU were causing widening of long-term swap spreads. This divergence indicates that domestic policy uncertainty is more potent in transmitting adverse credit and liquidity conditions over longer horizons, thereby increasing long-term risk premia in the swap market. title: First Report of Neopestalotiopsis vacciniicola Causing Leaf Spot on Rhododendron delavayi in China
abstract: In March 2025, leaf spot was observed on nursery-grown Rhododendron delavayi in Dali, Yunnan, China (25°40′52″N, 100°18′01″E); of 300 plants randomly surveyed from the nursery population, 108 were affected. Adaxial lesions began as dark brown to purplish flecks, enlarged into tan-centered necrotic spots, coalesced, and caused premature leaf abscission; abaxial discoloration was less conspicuous. Nine symptomatic leaves were randomly collected from six plants showing typical symptoms. Lesion-margin pieces (ca. 5 × 5 mm) were disinfected in 70% ethanol for 30 s and 1% NaOCl for 1 min, rinsed, dried, and plated on potato dextrose agar (PDA). Twenty-one Neopestalotiopsis-like colonies were recovered from 27 pieces (77.8%); seven isolates were obtained. S1-1, S1-2, and S1-3 from different leaves had similar morphology. On PDA at 25°C, representative S1-1 formed white to creamy, cottony colonies after 7 d. Conidia of S1-1 were fusoid to slightly curved, mostly 4-septate, with three pigmented median cells and hyaline end cells, 13.5–26.0 × 5.9–8.4 μm (mean ± SD = 20.0 ± 3.2 × 7.0 ± 0.6 μm; n = 30), excluding appendages. They bore two to three tubular, unbranched, filiform apical appendages, 5.2–24.8 μm long, and one basal appendage. ITS, tef1-α, and tub2 were amplified from all three isolates using ITS1/ITS4 (White et al. 1990), EF1-728F/EF1-986R (Carbone and Kohn 1999), and Bt2a/Bt2b…

title: Expanding market shaping best practices to new contexts: Diagnosing insulin market health and charting a path forward
abstract: Market shaping tools such as the Healthy Market Framework (HMF) and associated Market Action Plans (MAPs) have supported access to essential health products in low- and middle-income countries by aligning partners around shared goals and driving progress forward. Despite their utility, these tools are rarely applied outside of the centralized, donor-financed markets they were designed for. Insulin is a fragmented market with persistent access gaps that market shaping efforts could address. In this viewpoint, we describe how the Insulin Healthy Markets Task Force (IHM-TF) developed the first HMF and MAP for insulin, adapting a methodology built for a fundamentally different market context. We outline the process for diagnosing market health, the stakeholder engagement needed to translate this into a prioritized MAP, and the lessons learned in applying these tools to markets lacking neutral coordinating bodies, adequate and sustained financing, and shared market data. Extending market shaping to fragmented markets depends on building the coordinating infrastructure these markets lack and sustaining a coalition around a shared purpose. As the global health architecture shifts toward greater country ownership, this approach can help country governments, civil society, and supply chain actors diagnose and act on barriers to insulin access in their own contexts.

Understanding the Evolution of Dairy Goat Farming in Mediterranean Systems: Market Volatility, Climate Stresses, and the Role of CAP Subsidies
abstract: Autochthonous breed dairy goat farming plays a key socio-ecological role in Andalusia (Spain); however, census and farm numbers have declined sharply over five decades (1974–2023). This study analyzes the drivers of this trajectory by combining official census statistics with a participatory workshop to conceptualize qualitative direct causal paths. The sector experienced structural restructuring, where technical efficiency gains were offset by farm-gate price setting asymmetries and supply cost volatility, aggravated by recurring droughts and reduced forage autonomy. Common Agricultural Policy direct payments were perceived merely as short-term liquidity supports. Crucially, a lack of generational renewal—driven by rural decline, quality-of-life concerns, heavy workloads, and low social recognition—constitutes one of the main risks to sector continuity. Participant scores reflect perceived factor importance rather than direct closure metrics. To overcome vulnerability, future resilience would require transformative strategies rather than incremental adjustments, such as farm automation to improve labor conditions, enhanced forage self-sufficiency, knowledge transfer on autochthonous breeds, and local value added through short supply chains and artisanal cheesemaking.

title: First Report of Leaf Spot Caused by Fusarium concentricum on Tea Plant ( Camellia sinensis ) in China
abstract: Tea plant [Camellia sinensis (L.) O. Kuntze] is one of the world’s important beverage crops with significant health benefits (Wei et al. 2018). In May 2024, leaf spot symptoms were observed in 11 representative tea plantations in Xixiang County, Shaanxi Province (107.77° E, 32.98° N). The disease occurred during a period of warm and humid conditions with frequent rainfall events. Among 100 surveyed tea plants, 15 showed typical symptoms, resulting in a disease incidence (DI) of 15%. Lesions covered 10% to 50% of leaf area. Symptoms were primarily observed on mature leaves. Initial symptoms appeared as small, water-soaked lesions along the leaf margins. As the disease progressed, these lesions gradually expanded, turning yellowish-brown and further developing into semicircular to irregular necrotic spots delineated by distinct dark-brown borders. Severe lesions exhibited concentric rings, and infected leaves became deformed and wilted (Fig. S1A). To isolate the pathogen, 30 symptomatic leaves were randomly collected and surface-sterilized in 75% ethanol for 30 s, followed by 1% sodium hypochlorite for 30 s, and rinsed three times with sterile water. Tissue pieces were excised from lesion areas of symptomatic leaves and cultured on potato dextrose agar (PDA) at 28°C in the dark for 72 h. Thirty-three isolates were obtained, and 11 light-yellow isolates were selected for identific…

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reshaping Consumer Behavior and Market Dynamics in the Digital Economy
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a transformative technology in the digital economy, enabling businesses to analyze consumer behavior and enhance marketing strategies. The primary drawbacks of these social media platforms are lower data quality and a lack of advanced analytics to meet end users’ requirements. For that purpose, this article develops a novel computational model to analyze digital marketing trends using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques. The proposed methodology begins with a computational data model for efficient data collection and preprocessing steps, including sentiment labeling, geospatial analysis, ground-truth validation, and data augmentation. A hybrid classification approach is employed, integrating traditional ML models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) with deep learning models, including a CNN-LSTM architecture and the DeepNAO framework. The hybrid design enables effective extraction and improves classification accuracy. The model simulation, Pythsimulation, and the analysis parameters (including loss, accuracy, and precision) for both calculation models. Among the considered models, the DeepNAO model performs best in terms of accuracy and precision, offering optimized strategies for the competitive digital product market.

First report of Cercospora cf. sigesbeckiae causing Cercospora leaf spot of soybean in the Republic of Korea
abstract: During field trials conducted in 2022 and 2023, Cercospora leaf spot was observed on soybean ( Glycine max ) collected from Gimje-si, Jeollabuk-do; Yeoncheon-gun, Gyeonggi-do; and Muan-gun, Jeollanam-do, in the Republic of Korea. Lesions bearing black spore structures were observed on plants. To isolate the pathogen, infected tissues were surface-sterilized with 0.5% sodium hypochlorite for 1 min and cultured on potato dextrose agar (PDA). After seven days of incubation, white to gray fungal colonies with aerial mycelia were transferred to PDA and incubated at 25 °C under a 12-h photoperiod. Three isolates, 24YC2, MA35, and GJ3, were selected for morphological identification and pathogenicity testing. Conidiophores were brown to dark brown, straight to slightly curved, with multiple septa, measuring approximately 35–125 × 3.1–5.5 μm (n = 25). Conidiation was induced on soybean-based medium containing 16% (w/v) soybean tissue extract and 2% (w/v) agar under a 12-h photoperiod at 25 °C for 7 days. Conidia were hyaline to pale brown, cylindrical to filiform, and multicellular, measuring 45–120 × 3.5–5.7 μm (n = 25), consistent with previous descriptions of C. cf. sigesbeckiae . title: Energy-enstrophy balance and the evolving shape of Jupiter’s Great Red Spot
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the statistical mechanics approach to the organization of two-dimensional turbulence into a steady flow, we propose a variational principle to explain the observed tendency of Jupiter’s Great Red Spot (GRS) to become more circular. For this, we first derive, at leading order in the thin-shell parameter, a consistent set of nonlinear governing equations for the leading-order dynamics of flows confined to a thin zonal band in Jupiter’s upper troposphere, near the cloud tops. Jupiter’s internal heat source and interactions with the ambient flow may modify the kinetic energy of the GRS but its enstrophy is conserved at leading order. Within the framework of the leading-order dynamics, we show that the state of maximal kinetic energy at a fixed enstrophy for a prescribed area corresponds to a circular vortex and that this energetically optimal state is nonlinearly stable. This provides an energetic benchmark for interpreting the observed rounding trend of the GRS, with velocity and thermal features of the optimizer consistent with recent data. However, the discrepancy between the optimizer’s center-peaked vorticity profile and the observed hollow core shows that the optimizer is not an inevitable terminal state. Interactions with the ambient flow, radiative losses and three-dimensional stratified dynamics are factors that may prevent the GRS from attaining it.

title: A EFETIVIDADE DA LEI DE COTAS NA INCLUSÃO DA PESSOA COM DEFICIÊNCIA NO MERCADO DE TRABALHO FORMAL BRASILEIRO: OS DESAFIOS DA BAIXA ESCOLARIDADE E DA CONTRATAÇÃO PELAS EMPRESAS DE MENOR PORTE
abstract: O presente estudo analisa a efetividade da reserva legal de empregos para pessoas com deficiência no mercado de trabalho formal brasileiro, com ênfase em dois fatores que limitam o alcance da política: a desigualdade educacional e a participação das empresas de menor porte. A pesquisa é bibliográfica e documental, de abordagem qualitativa, com método dedutivo e análise de normas, dados oficiais e decisões da Justiça do Trabalho. O marco central é o art. 93 da Lei nº 8.213/1991, que obriga empresas com 100 ou mais empregados a reservar de 2% a 5% de seus cargos a pessoas com deficiência ou beneficiários reabilitados. Os dados examinados mostram que a política criou um canal relevante de inserção no emprego formal, pois mais de 93% dos vínculos de pessoas com deficiência identificados pelo eSocial em dezembro de 2025 estavam em empresas sujeitas à cota. Ao mesmo tempo, o cumprimento agregado permanece distante da universalidade, e a baixa escolaridade restringe o acesso a ocupações formais: em 2022, 63,3% das pessoas com deficiência de 25 anos ou mais estavam sem instrução ou com o ensino fundamental incompleto. A análise também evidencia que a exclusão das empresas com menos de 100 empregados da obrigação quantitativa reduz o alcance direto da política, embora não as afaste dos deveres de não discriminação e acessibilidade. Conclui-se que os resultados da Lei de Cotas devem ser …

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Musculoskeletal Conditions among Market Traders in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, Rivers State
abstract: Background: Musculoskeletal conditions (MSCs) are an important cause of pain, disability and reduced productivity among informal-sector workers, particularly market traders exposed to prolonged standing, heavy lifting, repetitive movements, and inadequate rest breaks (da Costa & Vieira, 2010; Pega et al., 2021). This study determined the prevalence of MSCs and identified their sociodemographic and occupational determinants among traders in the Rumuokoro and Choba markets in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional design was employed, and 300 traders were recruited aged 30 years and above with at least six months of trading experience through random sampling across the two markets. Data were collected using structured, interviewer-administered questionnaires that incorporated a modified Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire and sections on sociodemographic characteristics and occupational exposures. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Version 25, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression at a 5% significance level. Results: The prevalence of musculoskeletal conditions was 81.7% (n=245), with the lower back (68.6%), knees (52.2%) and shoulders (44.5%) being the most affected regions. Almost half (45.3%) experienced pain daily, and 82.0% reported that pain interfered with their work. Significa…

Cyber-Resilient Dynamic EV Hosting-Capacity Control Against False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Distribution Systems
abstract: Dynamic hosting-capacity control lets electric vehicle (EV) charging stations use the voltage headroom of distribution feeders. Because charging power is set from voltage measurements, a false data injection attack (FDIA) that inflates the reported voltage makes the controller over-allocate power and drives the real voltage below its limit. This paper models the closed loop of measurement, estimation, control and feeder for a 0.6 MW station on the IEEE 33-bus system and proposes a physics-informed defense: a consistency test between the controller’s voltage and a reconstruction built only from protected substation measurements, the station’s revenue meter and load forecasts. For attacks confined to the field-meter set and chosen independently of the measurement noise, invariance to the attack allocation follows by design because the trusted reconstruction has zero gain from those field meters. Under the nominal 10% load pseudo-measurement uncertainty and the protected-meter noise levels used in the case study, the layered detector identifies 70–95% of stealthy 0.0075 p.u. attacks, against 34–66% for conventional residual-based detectors; over 30 simulated days, it cuts daily under-voltage time from about 180 min to 2–8 min for injections of 0.01 p.u. or more. This detection resolution degrades as forecast or protected-anchor uncertainty increases. A supervised neural classifier…

title: Regulatory measures to facilitate the development and registration of paediatric medicines: when market forces fail
abstract: Introduction. Paediatric drug development and registration are more complex than for adults and are rarely profitable. Finding solutions to improve access to paediatric medicines is a pressing global issue. A common approach is to stimulate the pharmaceutical industry with regulatory incentives, although these vary between countries. The World Health Organization is working to harmonise them. Aim. To compare regulatory measures adopted by the European Union (EU), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and the East African Community (EAC) to facilitate the development and registration of paediatric medicines. Materials and methods. Open-access regulatory databases of the EAEU, the EU and the EAC were searched for documents regulating the medicine registration process. A content analysis was conducted to identify regulatory provisions for paediatric medicines. These were categorised as either regulatory incentives or obligations. Results and discussion. Three documents were selected from the EAC, two from the EU and one from the EAEU. In the EU, 12 measures were identified in the form of incentives and obligations covering the development, registration and market placement stages. In the EAEU, one incentive measure at the registration stage was identified. No paediatric provisions were found in the EAC documents. The EAEU and the EAC may need to assess current mechanisms and expand r…

title: Logistics Service Providers as Compliance Intermediaries: Reallocating Traceability Obligations in Vietnam’s Agro-Forestry Export Supply Chains
abstract: The European Union Deforestation Regulation, applicable from 30 December 2026, shifts the market barrier facing Vietnam’s three leading agro-forestry exports, coffee, rubber and timber and timber products, from product attributes to an obligation of proof grounded in data. Existing scholarship concentrates on smallholders and exporting firms, leaving unanswered the question of who actually creates, holds and transmits traceability data once goods leave the processing plant. Using desk research with a four-tier source-reliability protocol, this study constructs a matrix contrasting statutory responsibility with de facto control over data. The findings reveal a structural misalignment: legal responsibility is concentrated in the EU importer, whereas the data determining compliance resides with collectors and logistics service providers, actors bearing no statutory duty. The study proposes the concept of the compliance intermediary, specifies three conditions for its emergence and four conditions for its effective operation, and cautions that low-risk country status exempts operators only from risk assessment, not from the underlying information requirements.

title: Agent Orange Exposure Does Not Modify the Rate of Developing Certain Service-Connected Cancers in U.S. Veterans with Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance
abstract: Abstract Introduction Agent Orange (AO) exposure has been associated with increased risk of monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS), the precursor of multiple myeloma, as well as certain hematologic and solid malignancies in U.S. military personnel. However, the association between AO exposure and subsequent cancers among Veterans with a prior diagnosis of MGUS has not been examined. Materials and Methods The source of subjects were US Veterans diagnosed with MGUS in the national Veteran Health Administration system between 1988 and 2024. A retrospective cohort analysis using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models was employed to evaluate the association between AO exposure and developing certain service-connected cancers after MGUS diagnosis, adjusting for age at MGUS diagnosis, sex, military branch, and tobacco use. Results were reported as adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results Subsequent cancers occurred in 850 out of 3,246 patients (26%) during the study period with a median follow-up of 5.2 years. AO exposure was not associated with a higher rate of cancers overall (aHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.79-1.15; P = .60), or specific service-connected cancers, such as plasma cell neoplasms (aHR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.78-1.47; P = .69), respiratory cancer (aHR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.55-1.34; P = .50), prostate cancer (aHR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.69-1…

title: Beyond Structural Reforms: Cultivating an Abundance Mentality for Homegrown Administrative Reform in Uganda's Civil Service
abstract: Administrative reforms have traditionally focused on strengthening institutional structures, legal frameworks, accountability mechanisms, and public sector capacities. While these reforms remain important, comparatively little attention has focused on the behavioural and cognitive orientations that shape how public servants implement reforms and respond to increasingly complex governance challenges. This paper proposes that cultivating an Abundance Mentality may constitute an underexplored behavioural dimension of administrative reform in Uganda. Drawing on emerging debates in Behavioural Public Administration, Public Value Governance, and Transformative Learning Theory, the paper develops a conceptual framework that explains how higher education institutions can cultivate abundance-oriented public servants capable of innovation, collaboration, ethical leadership, and citizen-centred service delivery. The paper employs a systematic desk-based review of the literature and develops a conceptual framework from the resulting thematic synthesis of public administration, organisational behaviour, leadership studies, and adult education to explain how an Abundance Mentality can be developed through curriculum design, transformative pedagogies, reflective learning, and institutional culture, and then diffused into the civil service through professional practice. The paper contends that…

Strategic Agency in Service Provision: Promoting Pathways to Resilience and Sustainable Livelihoods for Families and Children in South Africa
abstract: This phenomenological study explored how service providers at Future Families in South Africa understood and exercised strategic agency in supporting pathways to resilience and sustainable livelihoods among families and children facing adversity. Guided principally by the Pathways to Resilience Model and the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, with strategic agency used as an interpretive concept, the study examined provider accounts of organisational practices, staff development and perceived changes among service users. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 22 participants: five care workers, five social auxiliary workers, five team leaders, five programme managers, one training manager and one executive director. Data were analysed using interpretative phenomenological analysis. Participants described Future Families as an enabling organisational ecosystem in which staff wellbeing, reflective practice and professional development supported responsive service delivery. They also reported perceived improvements in parenting, relationships, coping and livelihood activities among families. Because no clients or family members were interviewed, these accounts are presented as service providers’ perceptions rather than independently verified outcomes. The findings suggest that social service organisations should invest in staff wellbeing, reflective supervision and profess…

title: Home office no serviço público
abstract: This article investigates the impacts of remote work on the health of staff at a federal educational institution, in the context of the transition to remote work driven by the covid-19 pandemic. Focusing on administrative-educational staff, the study identifies the impacts of this work modality and investigates the factors affecting workers’ health. A qualitative, exploratory approach was adopted, with data collected through a sociodemographic questionnaire (76 respondents) and semi-structured interviews (18 participants), analyzed through content analysis. Results indicate that most participants experienced greater flexibility and autonomy, contrasting with increased stress and anxiety. The discussion is situated within the regulatory framework of telework in the federal public service and the specificities of administrative work in universities, linking the accounts to the psychodynamics of work and the sociology of work.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Gating Mechanism via Controllable SEI Regulation toward Robust Zinc Anodes
abstract: Abstract Interphase chemistry is conventionally ascribed to electrolyte composition, while electrochemical operating conditions are treated merely as kinetic parameters. Here, we demonstrate applied current programs at the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on Zn via an electrochemical kinetic-gating mechanism. N-Hydroxyethyliminodiacetic acid reorganizes Zn2+ solvation and supplies interfacial precursors, whereas current density selects their reaction pathways. High current establishes a kinetically constrained window that promotes coupled conversion of sulfate and NHA species into a compact organic–inorganic SEI enriched in ZnS and Zn–N; low-current formation produces a loose and nonprotective interphase. High-current activation enables stable Zn deposition even after switching to low current, evidencing that interphase properties are determined by formation history. The programmed anode delivers 5300 h at 5 mA cm–2, and Zn||NH4V4O10 pouch cells sustain 700 cycles. These findings establish current as an active control variable for interfacial reaction selection, offering a route toward programmable interphase chemistry beyond composition-only design.

title: A Frequency‐Decomposed Residual Learning Framework for Volume Data Neural Representation
abstract: Abstract Implicit neural representations (INRs) have been widely adopted for volume data modeling in scientific visualization due to their continuous representation capability and flexibility. However, existing INR‐based methods still struggle to accurately capture high‐frequency details due to spectral bias, which can degrade reconstruction quality and affect downstream analysis. To address this issue, we propose a frequency‐decomposed residual learning framework for neural volume representation. Specifically, we decompose the volume data into low‐frequency components and high‐frequency residuals, and jointly model them with a shared INR by reformulating volume representation as a multi‐task learning (MTL) problem. To alleviate potential learning conflicts between different frequency branches while preserving model compactness, we introduce a lightweight feature gating mechanism on top of the shared backbone to adaptively reweight shared features for the two branches, enabling more effective modeling of low‐ and high‐frequency information. Experimental results on multiple scientific datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing approaches in reconstruction, super‐resolution, and compression tasks, while maintaining comparable model size and computational efficiency. Further ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed frequency‐decomposi…

title: Preparation of Ether-free Polycarbazole-Based Anion Exchange Membranes and Regulation of Cations on Membrane Properties and Fuel Cell Performance
abstract: Abstract Quaternized ether-free aromatic polymers from superacid-catalyzed polycondensation are excellent candidates for high-performance anion exchange membranes (AEMs). Most current studies mainly focus on cation-modified carbon-aromatic AEMs. However, the structure–property relationship of cation-functionalized heteroaromatic polyarylene systems is still insufficiently understood. This work develops a series of carbazole-based ether-free AEMs with different side-chain quaternary ammonium (QA) cations, including conventional trimethylammonium, charge-delocalized imidazolium, and N-cyclic piperidinium and quinuclidinium. All membranes share the same polycarbazole backbone. Thus, the side-chain cation structure primarily determines membrane comprehensive performance. QPC-TMA with trimethylammonium groups exhibits the highest hydroxide conductivity at 80 °C, owing to its high ion exchange capacity and well-developed microphase separation. In comparison, QPC-QUI with bulky quinuclidinium groups shows outstanding alkaline and oxidative stability under harsh aging conditions. It shows least conductivity loss (2.65% loss for 1080 h) and weight loss (0.81% loss for 72 h).In fuel cell tests, the QPC-QUI-based AEM achieves a peak power density of 998 mW cm–2, which is higher than QPC-TMA (928 mW cm–2). This work proves that rational cation structural design of ether-free heteroaromatic…

title: A Photo‐Assisted Calcium−Oxygen Battery Based on Dipole Heterogeneity Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Calcium–oxygen (Ca–O 2 ) batteries represent an attractive energy‐storage technology that offers the potential for high energy density through reversible CaO 2 /O 2 chemistry. However, practical Ca−O 2 batteries are largely limited by the formation of an inert discharge product and intrinsically sluggish reaction kinetics, which lead to large polarization. Here, we report a rechargeable Ca–O 2 battery with an ultralow overpotential of 1.11 V via a photo‐assisted strategy based on dipole heterogeneity regulation. Dynamic light‐driven charge transport within the cell establishes favorable oxygen diffusion pathways and electrochemical reaction routes, significantly improving the transport efficiency of O 2 and charge carriers. Theoretical simulations elucidate the kinetic origin of this light‐enhanced process, revealing that regulating the reaction routes for CaO 2 formation and decomposition is effective in lowering the product‐decomposition energy barrier. The resulting photo‐assisted Ca−O 2 battery system achieves a round‐trip efficiency of 66.12% under illumination, revealing the effectiveness of the dipole‐heterogeneity‐enabled photo‐assisted strategy for Ca−O 2 electrochemistry. This work not only provides a strategy to mitigate the inherent kinetic limitations of traditional Ca–O 2 batteries but also provides insights for the development of new photo‐assisted energ…

title: Immune functions of vascular structural cells are endothelial communication, smooth muscle transdifferentiation and lymphatic immune regulation
abstract: The vascular wall maintains structural integrity, regulates blood flow, and supports tissue functions and homeostasis. Evidence also shows that its structural cells participate in immune sensing, inflammation and tissue remodeling. Vascular endothelial cells (ECs), vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), and lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) encounter different combinations of inflammatory, metabolic, mechanical, microbial, tissue and intracellular immune-derived signals. We propose here that their anatomical locations and cell-intrinsic programs shape distinct, context-dependent immune functions of vascular structural cell types. ECs act as immune communicators at the blood-tissue interface. In response to inflammatory cues, they produce cytokines and chemokines, express adhesion molecules, regulate vascular permeability, and direct leukocyte recruitment. VSMCs respond to persistent vessel wall stress through phenotypic plasticity, secretomes and transdifferentiation, adopting cell states that may support repair and plaque stability or contribute to fibrosis, calcification, and disease progression. LECs combine innate sensing with regulation of immune cell trafficking, antigen handling, peripheral tolerance, adaptive immune responses, and fluid balance. Single-cell transcriptomic studies also identify immune-associated signatures in other vascular structural cell populations, i…

title: Adaptive Smart-City Governance Under European Digital Regulation: A Comparative Systems Analysis of Madrid and Barcelona
abstract: Cities increasingly operate as complex adaptive systems in which institutional capacity, civic participation, environmental pressures, digital infrastructures, and regulation interact across multiple levels. Yet less is known about how these dimensions combine within alternative metropolitan governance configurations and how common European digital regulation becomes embedded in them. This study asks how the five analytical domains combine into distinct metropolitan smart-city governance configurations under a shared regulatory environment and how path-dependent institutional trajectories shape those combinations. A structured qualitative comparative case design was applied to 34 institutional documents from Madrid, Barcelona, Spain, and the European Union. Documents were coded through a theory-informed framework and examined through within-case analysis, pattern matching, documentary triangulation, and cross-case comparison. The findings identify two overlapping configurations: Madrid shows stronger digital-administrative integration, transversal coordination, and outward-facing strategic development, whereas Barcelona displays greater municipal–metropolitan articulation, policy-specific civic participation, and socio-ecological embedding. In both cases, the GDPR and EU AI Act operate as institutional boundary conditions whose local incorporation depends on existing governance…
