cAMP signalling in osteoimmune regulation: mechanistic determinants and translational evidence
abstract: Bone remodelling and repair depend on interactions amongst skeletal, stromal and immune cells, and disruption of these interactions contributes to bone disease. Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signalling transduces endocrine, inflammatory and mechanical cues across osteoblast-lineage cells, osteocytes, osteoclast-lineage cells and immune cells. However, elevated intracellular cAMP does not produce a uniform skeletal response. Receptor identity, the spatial and temporal organisation of cAMP signals, the identity and differentiation state of the responding cell, and downstream effector engagement together influence bone formation, osteoclast differentiation and immune-cell responses. Protein kinase A (PKA) mediates several well-characterised responses, whereas exchange proteins directly activated by cAMP (EPACs) can mediate distinct downstream effects. This review compares the evidence for these mechanisms, distinguishing receptor-associated observations and cAMP elevation from effects experimentally shown to depend on PKA or EPAC. The discussion focuses on osteoporosis, inflammatory bone destruction, including periodontitis-associated alveolar bone loss, and experimental strategies for local bone regeneration. Evidence directly linking cAMP signalling to osteoimmune mechanisms in osteoarthritis and tumour-associated bone disease is less complete. Parathyroid hormone 1 rece…

title: Principals' Suspension Threat as Correlate of Academic Engagement and Adherence to School Regulation in Uyo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria: Gender and Age Assessment
abstract: This study investigated the principals' suspension threat as a correlate of students' academic engagement and adherence to school regulations in Uyo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria using gender and age as predictor variables. Four research questions were raised. Ex-post facto research design was adopted. The population comprised 5200 senior secondary two students in the 14 public secondary schools in Uyo, from which a sample of 725 was derived using a multistage sampling approach. The researcher's developed 'Suspension and Students Engagement and Adherence Scale (S-SEAS), was used for data collection after face-validated by three experts. The content assessment reliability approach was used to test for S-SEAS reliability, and the data generated was calculated using Cohen's Kappa statistics, which resulted in the estimate of 0.87. The collated data was analyzed using percentages, charts, means, and graphs. Results revealed that males were the majority (58.1%) in the study, while in terms of age, those within 16 years of age were the majority (69.1%). The majority of the sample assessed were suspended, especially in the cadre of males and those within 17-20 years of age. The categories of suspension were mostly from the classes, followed by those suspended from the school. Majorly, the reasons for the suspension were lateness to school, insubordination, and violen…

title: A Photo‐Charging Time Regulation Strategy for Enhancing the Solar‐to‐Electrochemical Energy Efficiency of Photo‐Rechargeable Devices
abstract: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable devices (PRDs) that directly integrate photovoltaic and energy storage units have emerged as a promising solution for stable off‐grid power supply. Present efforts to improve PRD efficiency focus on parameter matching between the two units. Although static matching strategies, represented by voltage matching, are effective under ideal conditions, they exhibit significant limitations when applied to energy storage units that lack an obvious voltage plateau. Herein, a photo‐charging time regulation strategy is proposed as a universal optimization framework to enhance PRD efficiency, which is realized by maximizing the energy efficiency product of the photovoltaic and energy storage units via precise time control. Furthermore, this strategy reveals that when photo‐charging time is governed by a cut‐off voltage, the optimal value typically deviates from the maximum power point voltage of the photovoltaic units. To validate this strategy, PRDs were constructed by integrating passivated emitter and rear cell (PERC) solar cells with Co‐doped Ni(OH) 2 ‐based asymmetric supercapacitors. By controlling the photo‐charging time to 5.7 s, the PRDs deliver a maximum overall efficiency of 11.61% (under AM 1.5G photo‐charging and discharging at 2 A g −1 ). This work provides a viable and scalable strategy to maximize the solar‐to‐electrochemical energy efficiency, p…

title: Hydraulic Response and Microstructural Evolution During Erosional Failure of Spoil Slopes Under Extreme Rainfall
abstract: Progressive failure of spoil slopes under extreme rainfall involves multiscale processes, including rainfall infiltration, fine-particle migration, and weakening of the particle skeleton, while their cross-scale evolution remains insufficiently understood. To investigate this mechanism, laboratory model tests were conducted under a rainfall intensity of 108 mm/h with degrees of compaction of 75%, 80%, and 90%. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and PFC2D simulations were further employed to examine failure characteristics at the macroscopic, microstructural, and particle scales. The results show that, at 80% compaction, the slope underwent a progressive sequence of fine-particle migration and toe deposition, erosion-gully development, toe undercutting, and intensified shoulder erosion. Pore-water pressure responses also showed clear spatial differences between the crest, middle slope, and toe. As the degree of compaction increased from 75% to 90%, the maximum deposition length, maximum deposition depth, and dry mass of deposited material decreased by 29.8%, 31.0%, and 38.6%, respectively. SEM observations indicate that increasing compaction generally enhances particle contact and structural integrity, thereby reducing local structural disturbance caused by prolonged rainfall. PFC simulations show that particle displacement is mainly concentrated in the shallow slope, particular…

title: CMTM3 is associated with selected unfolded protein response markers and vascular/stromal features in glioblastoma
abstract: Background Previous studies have implicated CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing 3 (CMTM3) in glioma progression and have demonstrated effects on glioma-cell proliferation and invasion. However, its relationship with cellular composition of the glioblastoma (GBM) microenvironment and adaptive endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-stress responses remains incompletely characterized. We therefore investigated the cellular context of CMTM3 expression and its association with selected unfolded protein response (UPR)-related signals in GBM, together with complementary functional validation in GBM cells. Methods GEO, TCGA, and Human Protein Atlas datasets were integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing, survival analysis, protein-interaction and correlation analyses, functional enrichment, and immune-infiltration profiling. CMTM3 was silenced in U87 and U251 cells, followed by migration, colony-formation, CCK-8, and Western blot assays. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress was induced with tunicamycin (2 μg/mL, 24 h). Results In the legacy TCGA glioma cohorts, CMTM3 expression was associated with higher WHO grade, IDH-wild-type status, and older age, whereas higher CMTM3 expression in TCGA-GBM was associated with shorter overall survival. In the vascular-enriched single-cell dataset, CMTM3 expression was detected across multiple populations and was prominent in endothelial and mural/pe…

title: Genome-wide analysis of the GRAS family and its transcriptional response to strigolactone during post-drought recovery in elephant grass
abstract: Abstract Background Strigolactones (SL) are pivotal in shaping root system architecture to aid drought acclimation; yet, the transcriptional landscapes underpinning this response in elephant grass ( Cenchrus purpureus ) remain elusive. While the GRAS transcription factor family is established as a regulator of plant development, its evolutionary trajectory and transcriptional behaviour in response to SL under water-deficit conditions have not been explored in this species. Results We identified 126 CpGRAS genes classified into 12 subfamilies. Among them, LISCL and PAT1 were the most expanded, whereas DLT, SCL4/7, and unknown1 contained the fewest members. Chromosomal distribution analysis indicated that the expansion of this family was primarily driven by whole-genome duplication events. While most members exhibited strong purifying selection (Ka/Ks < 1), the LISCL and HAM subfamilies displayed relatively higher divergence. Promoter analysis revealed a widespread enrichment of cis-elements responsive to abscisic acid (ABA), jasmonic acid (JA), gibberellin (GA), and drought stress. Through comparative transcriptomic profiling of roots subjected to 14 days of drought stress and sampled 14 h after a single SL application during re-watering, we found that SL treatment was associated with a distinct upregulation of the PAT1 ( CpGRAS30-4 ), HAM ( CpGRAS22-2/22-6 ), SCR ( CpGRAS28-4 )…

title: The Generative Logic and Implementation Pathways of AI-Empowered Precision Enhancement in Disaster Monitoring and Forecasting
abstract: The increasing frequency of extreme weather events and compound disasters has rendered traditional disaster monitoring and forecasting models inadequate for meeting complex operational demands. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a critical tool for enhancing the precision of disaster forecasting. To elucidate the mechanisms through which AI empowers forecasting precision and to propose feasible optimization pathways, this paper integrates existing research with domestic practical cases. It deconstructs the rich connotations of forecasting precision across three dimensions—spatiotemporal, intensity, and impact—and analyzes the generative logic of AI empowerment from value, technological, and institutional perspectives, while also examining its practical boundaries. The study reveals that AI-driven improvements in forecasting effectiveness do not rely solely on technological upgrades, but rather constitute a governance process involving the synergistic coupling of technology, institutions, and grassroots capacity. Accordingly, this paper proposes countermeasures including the establishment of unified data platforms, the construction of human-AI interactive systems, the localization of AI models, and the refinement of a“peacetime-wartime integrated”emergency technology support system, thereby providing theoretical underpinnings for the modernization of emergency managemen…
venue: Transactions on Environment, Energy and Earth Sciences

title: Identifying the effective cost ratio and a model-consistent shadow carbon price in deteriorating item inventory systems: a deterministic inverse optimisation approach
abstract: Firms in perishable goods supply chains leave a detailed trail of replenishment decisions, yet the cost structure behind those decisions, and the value a firm place on its own carbon emissions, stay hidden. This paper develops a deterministic inverse optimisation framework that reads part of that hidden structure back out of observed behaviour. A forward inventory model for a deteriorating item shows that ordering, holding, spoilage and carbon costs collapse into an effective setup term and an effective holding term, so behaviour identifies only a single cost ratio and the deterioration rate; individual accounting costs are not recoverable from decisions alone. A two-stage estimator recovers the deterioration rate from the inventory balance linking orders to sales and the cost ratio from the optimality condition, then backs out a model-consistent shadow carbon price from the ratio and the firm’s known accounting costs. We prove which quantities are identified, characterise a confounding valley in which holding, spoilage and emission costs cannot be separated from decisions alone, and show the shadow price is recoverable only when the emission signature differs from the cost signature. A numerical study separates finite-sample dispersion from asymptotic bias, documents a bias floor that persists as the sample grows at fixed noise, tests recovery under realistic measurement error…

title: Making Price Guarantees Claimable: Turning Retail Price Promises Into Trust
abstract: Retail price guarantees (PGs) reassure customers that they will not overpay, yet their practical value depends on whether customers know the guarantee exists, understand how to claim and regard the process as fair. This Practitioner Corner article examines these issues using survey evidence from 1,219 loyalty programme members of a major automotive and outdoor specialty retailer in New Zealand. The study combines academic rigour from a published field study on PG advertising believability with practitioner analysis of previously unreported indicators of awareness, process knowledge, prior claiming, claim experience and future claim likelihood. The findings reveal a clear claimability gap: although price was the dominant shopping reason, fewer than half of respondents were aware of the Price-Beat Guarantee before the survey, only 15.3% understood the claiming process, and only 5.9% had previously requested a refund. However, 84.7% of actual requesters found the process easy, and 67.5% of all respondents were likely to request the guarantee in future. The article translates the findings through a three-level practitioner resource architecture: Figure 1, PG Claimability Performance Dashboard and Management Priorities; Figure 2, PG Claimability Audit-Action-Evaluation Worksheet: One-Page Practitioner Overview; and the Supplementary Practitioner Tool in the Supplemental Material, PG…

title: Forecasting the Saudi nursing workforce: a detailed quantitative analysis of saudization, gender, and sectoral distribution towards the future
CWIA: A Model-Free, Low-Cost Adversarial Perturbation Method for Wind Power Forecasting
abstract: Adversarial robustness assessments of wind power forecasting should account for attacker resources, cross-architecture stability, and detectability. Existing attacks commonly require surrogate-model preparation or perturbation learning, leaving the threat from minimal-preparation attacks insufficiently characterized. We propose the continuous wind injection attack (CWIA), a deterministic method that directly perturbs wind speed using an available regional input scale. CWIA requires no private wind farm training data, surrogate training, target predictions or gradients, universal-perturbation fitting, or online optimization. A predefined temporal ramp confines injection to wind speed and permits online application through a single vector addition with boundary projection, retaining the additive application of a prepared UAP. Evaluations on PSML use four forecasting architectures, six surrogate-based attack baselines, constant-offset ablations, and nine anomaly detectors to examine effectiveness, preparation requirements, and temporal boundary behavior. On MISO, CWIA produces MAEs of 0.1335–0.1443 p.u. across the four targets at a 15% normalized maximum budget, while its zero-start ramp preserves the tested temporal boundary score, establishing a useful low-preparation baseline with detector-dependent detectability.

title: Three-Dimensional Imaging, Printing, and Augmented Reality in Surgical Oncology: A Descriptive Implementation Framework at a Comprehensive Cancer Center
abstract: Background: Three-dimensional (3D) visualization of radiological imaging has emerged as a valuable tool in surgical oncology, with applications spanning diagnostics, perioperative planning, intraoperative guidance, and patient communication. Despite its growing clinical relevance, integration into routine surgical workflows remains inconsistent and poorly standardized across specialties. Methods: We describe select cases illustrating a multispecialty feasibility and implementation experience evaluating the integration of 3D reconstruction, 3D printing, and augmented reality into surgical oncology workflows across a comprehensive cancer center. Describing cases and series of interest, we demonstrate how a structured implementation workflow was applied covering image acquisition, segmentation, volumetric rendering, and modality selection based on the specific clinical problem. A feasibility framework is proposed in terms of workflow integration, modality-to-problem fit, and clinical utility as described by the operating team. Results: Seven select case groups spanning pediatric, head and neck, urologic, gynecologic, and thoracic surgical oncology were included, with group sizes ranging from 1 to 14 patients. In 3 patients with hepatoblastoma, 3D printed anatomical models were successfully integrated into patient and family education consultations to convey tumor extent and the sc…

title: Managing Rubber Waste Flows in Closed-Loop Production Systems: Forecasting the Mass of Vulcanized Waste Based on Technological Parameters
abstract: Rubber waste recycling is a crucial element of the circular economy. However, high uncertainty of secondary resource flows disrupts recycling stability. This study develops an organizational and methodological framework for closed-loop rubber waste management, linking organizational design with operational forecasting. A comparative analysis of organizational models justifies the cluster (centralized) model as the optimal environment for reliable data collection. Using empirical data from a single manufacturing enterprise producing rubber sealing rings by injection molding (610 shift-level observations), two forecasting models were developed and compared: a linear regression model and a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network. The MLP identified four significant predictors: production volume, vulcanization time, sulfur content deviation, and mold wear. Scenario analysis revealed a non-linear relationship between production and waste generation: higher production increased waste (up to 2.20 kg/shift), while extreme secondary-factor deviations (mold wear 54%; sulfur deviation 1.08%) caused waste to peak at 1.65 kg/shift even at the lowest production volume (1300 units/shift). The approach provides a transparent, interpretable mathematical expression for process engineers, shifting waste management from reactive to proactive control. Given the single-enterprise, single-product …

title: Physics-informed and data-efficient machine learning for storm surge forecasting during typhoons
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of accurately forecasting storm surges during tropical cyclones, which is crucial in reducing coastal damages. We develop a physics-informed and data-efficient model, a storm surge neural network (SSNN), that embeds shallow water equations into a machine learning (ML) framework with a specifically designed piecewise loss function to effectively incorporate physical constraints. The SSNN is iteratively trained to make rolling forecast and can produce more accurate forecasts than a standard data-driven model even with a smaller size of training data. The improvement in the performance by the SSNN model is evident, particularly in coastal areas with varying strong winds. This is especially true for forecasts beyond 16 hours, where the data-driven model struggles to provide accurate predictions. Combining physics with ML could offer a promising way to improve storm surge forecasting and support coastal hazard preparedness.

title: Effective Consensus and Price Reliability in Decentralized Asset Markets
abstract: Cryptoasset prices are often treated as if they reveal a single underlying value, even when trading is thin, market access is fragmented, and the asset provides no enforceable claim on cash flows. This paper develops a conceptual framework for assessing the reliability of quoted prices in decentralized asset markets. Price reliability refers to cross-venue consistency, depth-adjusted stability, shock resilience, and manipulation resistance; it does not require an observed price to equal a unique intrinsic or fundamental value. The framework distinguishes four mechanisms often compressed into the term consensus: protocol consensus validates the ledger, oracle consensus supplies external information, market consensus aggregates orders into executable prices, and governance consensus determines how rules and control rights change. It characterizes effective consensus quality as a multidimensional diagnostic profile assessed through independence, diversity, redundancy, and credible participation across these layers. Five propositions address the roles of market liquidity, source independence, shared infrastructure, governance participation, and feedback between oracle inputs and automated liquidation. By integrating these mechanisms and their cross-layer dependencies, the framework offers a basis for future measurement, governance design, and regulatory assessment.

title: Who sets the price? India's unregulated private hospitals, out-of-pocket spending, and the case for government-stewarded insurance
abstract: India increasingly relies on a large private hospital sector that, despite the Clinical Establishments Act of 2010, operates with little effective price regulation or transparency; charges for the same procedure vary widely, and out-of-pocket payments still cover about two-fifths of health spending. This Perspective argues that the unchecked pricing power of private providers is a central driver of catastrophic health spending, and that the most credible remedy is not blunt price control but stronger governance: enforcing existing regulation while shifting from passive to strategic purchasing through open, competitive, performance-based contracting. It draws on the most visible marker of distortion, the cesarean gap: private facilities perform cesareans in 47% of deliveries against 14% in public facilities, at several times the out-of-pocket cost, a gap that measured clinical risk does not fully explain. Where the state acts as a strategic purchaser, as the Central Government Health Scheme and Ayushman Bharat–PMJAY already do, it can set prices, standardise quality and curb such incentives. The Perspective examines why fragmented, thin insurance leaves a large “missing middle” exposed, how that gap might be closed through a contributory pool, and how extending publicly stewarded, single-price purchasing across the private sector could protect patients. Regulation and purchasing…

title: Configuration over Architecture: Deep Learning Models for Daily Streamflow Forecasting in Snowmelt-Dominated Watersheds of Southwestern Alberta
abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasting in snowmelt-dominated headwaters is critical for flood mitigation, reservoir operations, and water resource management, yet it remains challenging due to non-linear interactions among snowmelt dynamics, meteorological forcing, and watershed hydrology. This study evaluates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models for daily streamflow prediction in three mountainous watersheds of southwestern Alberta and systematically examines the sensitivity of model performance to key configuration decisions, including timestep selection, feature engineering, seasonal period, adjacent gauge inclusion, weather forecasting, and attention mechanisms. Results demonstrate high predictive accuracy of up to 0.98 NSE for typical daily streamflow when the models are optimally configured. However, all models substantially underpredicted a 1995 extreme flood event by 44–78%, reflecting the inherent challenge of predicting rare events with imbalanced training data. The extreme-event underprediction was masked by aggregate evaluation metrics over a typical flow period, which necessitated a separate evaluation for the extreme event in the LSTM performance evaluation. These findings provide guidance for configuring LSTM models for small watersheds and highlight data augmentation and uncertainty quantification as future directions for improving extreme event predictions.

title: Diffusion-Enhanced attention LSTM: A hybrid framework for agricultural price forecasting
BEYOND PRICE: HOW PLATFORM POWER SHAPES DEMAND ALLOCATION IN ONLINE HOTEL CHANNELS
abstract: Rate disparity remains a widely used but poorly understood pricing strategy in the hotel industry. While previous research generally assumes that lower prices shift demand toward less expensive channels, this study investigates whether such effects occur in practice. Using high-frequency booking and pricing data from five full-service hotels across multiple online travel agencies (OTAs), we analyze how rate disparity relates to the distribution of demand across channels. The findings show that the impact of price differences is limited, highly non-linear, and strongly dependent on contextual factors. Channel market power and hotel-specific characteristics seem to play a more significant role than price advantages under the observed conditions. Rate disparity reallocates demand across channels rather than increasing total demand within the sample studied, and its effectiveness varies across demand seasons and competitive environments. These results challenge the prevailing focus on price-based competition and suggest that platform dynamics and hotel attributes may play a more central role in distribution outcomes.

title: Abnormal Passenger Flow Forecasting for Rail Transit Based on Multi-Source Big Data Fusion
abstract: To address the problem of forecasting abnormal passenger flow at urban rail transit stations caused by large-scale events, holidays, and weather changes, this paper proposes a multi-source big data abnormal spatio-temporal prediction framework, MBDASPF. Based on historical entry and exit passenger flow, the model incorporates external disturbance factors such as day of week, holidays, weather, official event website information, and Weibo super topic data, and adopts a “branch-transform-fuse” strategy to extract the historical passenger flow correlation and the abnormal disturbance correlation, respectively. The historical branch employs GRU to capture recent proximity, daily periodicity, and weekly tendency, while the disturbance branch employs LSTM to model the influence of external events. Finally, through two-stage fusion and an attention-based output layer, multi-step forecasting for the next 10, 20, and 30 min are realized. Experiments on data from the Olympic Sports Center Station of Nanjing Rail Transit Line 10 show that MBDASPF outperforms ARIMA, SVR, BPNN, and GRU overall in terms of MAE, RMSE, and MAPE, and can more effectively characterize abnormal passenger flow fluctuations during large-scale events.
venue: Transactions on Environment, Energy and Earth Sciences

title: Long-Term Wind and Solar Resource Variability and Forecasting for Sustainable Energy Planning in the Galapagos Islands
abstract: The increasing use of isolated electrical systems based on renewable energy sources (RES) requires a comprehensive understanding and analysis of the variability of renewable energy resources (RER) and, in turn, appropriate forecasting techniques for sound sustainable energy planning. For this reason, this study presents a quantitative assessment of RER variability in response to wind speed and solar irradiance on Santa Cruz Island, Galapagos, Ecuador. This study analyzes the temporality and variability of renewable energy resources (RERs), i.e., wind speed and irradiance, used in renewable energy systems (RES). To this end, four forecasting methods are examined: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Autoregressive Integrated Seasonal Moving Average (SARIMA), regression trees, and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) trained via backpropagation (BP). These models are evaluated under identical conditions, using standard performance metrics. This research underscores the importance of integrating long-term resource characterization with predictive modeling to support the planning of sustainable power systems in ecologically sensitive islands.

title: A Novel Deep Learning Approach for Tropical Cyclone Path Prediction Based on LSTM-BiLSTM
abstract: Under global climate change, the frequency of typhoons and their strong wind, heavy rain, and storm surge increase, seriously threatening the life and property of human society. However, traditional tropical cyclone track prediction methods have difficulties in processing large amounts of complex data in terms of prediction efficiency and accuracy. Recently, deep learning methods have shown a potential capability to process complex data efficiently and accurately. In this paper, we propose a novel data-driven approach based on combination of Long Short Term Memory + Bidirectional Long short Term Memory (LSTM-BiLSTM) models to forecast tropical cyclone landing locations using the historical tropical cyclone tracks and various meteorological attributes. The features obtained from Finite Volume Method (FVM) is given to LSTM-BiLSTM. It is noted that FVM is integrated with a three-dimensional conservation of energy paradigm showcasing its effectiveness in capturing vital atmospheric and oceanic interactions. The model is trained on a real-world tropical cyclone dataset from the years 2007–2017. Through a comparison with existing forecasting methods, the results verified that our proposed model performed around 97% of accuracy, 93% of precision, 98% of recall, 2.66 e–2 of error with 190.9 seconds of elapsed time for testing.

title: Prediction of lncRNA-protein interacting pairs using LLM embeddings based on evolutionary information
abstract: Interactions of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) with proteins is responsible for numerous cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin remodeling, cell differentiation, and intracellular signaling. Several computational methods have been developed for predicting lncRNA–protein interaction (LPI) pairs; however, many existing approaches were developed using earlier versions of interaction databases, potentially limiting their applicability to more recently characterized interactions. In this study, we developed a sequence-based framework for LPI prediction using a large non-redundant dataset comprising 128,374 interacting and an equal number of non-interacting pairs. Initially, similarity-based approach BLAST was tried which had poor discriminative power, due to low sequence similarity between sequences. Subsequently, we developed convolutional neural network and machine learning models using sequence-derived features and protein language model embeddings. The CatBoost model integrating Dinucleotide Autocorrelation (DACC) features for lncRNAs and ESM-2-t30 embeddings for proteins achieved an AUC of 0.929 on the training dataset and 0.692 on the homology-aware validation dataset. These results demonstrate the potential of combining sequence-derived features and protein language model representations for LPI prediction while highlighting the challenges associa…

title: Multiscale Drug–Cell Interaction Modeling via Hybrid Graph Architectures and Knowledge-Aware Fusion for Drug Synergy Prediction
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of drug combination synergy remains challenging due to the vast combinatorial space and strong cellular context dependency of drug responses. To address these limitations, we present MILSyn, a multimodal interaction learning framework designed to capture multiscale drug–cell interactions through three integrated components: (1) relational modeling of heterogeneous graph structures using a hybrid RGCN-GATv2 architecture, (2) cross-modal fusion of biochemical features spanning SMILES, substructures, 3D conformations, and multiomic profiles, and (3) knowledge-aware reasoning via LLM-derived semantic embeddings. Evaluated on DrugComb and four benchmark data sets, MILSyn consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models, demonstrating robust generalization in cold-start scenarios and notable performance gains under few-shot fine-tuning for rare tumors. Attention-based analyses provide exploratory summaries of gene-, pathway-, and substructure-level features associated with the model’s predictions, generating hypotheses for further investigation. By combining scalability with interpretability, MILSyn provides a practical framework for prioritizing candidate drug combinations in precision oncology.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Radiomics-based risk prediction: survival in sarcopenic gastrointestinal and genitourinary cancer cohorts using a population-specific sarcopenia definition
abstract: Abstract Objective This study demonstrated that the recently proposed Asian (Japanese)-cohort-based skeletal muscle index (SMI) definition (< 36.2 $${{\rm{cm}}}^{2}\rm/{m}^{2}$$ cm 2 / m 2 for males and < 29.6 $${{\rm{cm}}}^{2}\rm/{m}^{2}$$ cm 2 / m 2 for females), along with other factors such as radiomic and clinical variables, could improve risk categorization for survival in sarcopenic, gastrointestinal (GI), and genitourinary (GU) cancer patients. Materials and methods This retrospective study involved 2,015 patients who underwent major surgery at our institution between 2006 and 2018. From the axial CT image of the L3 vertebral region, the skeletal muscle was segmented to calculate the SMI values. 646 radiomic features were extracted from the image, and the Boruta algorithm was used to identify the most pertinent features. The final set of features consisted of these features and clinical variables. The dataset was split into training and testing sets comprising 1,512 patients (75%) and 503 patients (25%), respectively. Four models were evaluated in this study: (1) random survival forest (RSF)-based radiomic model, (2) Cox proportional hazard-based model, (3) Asian (Japanese)-specific SMI definition-based model, and (4) integrated model, which combines experiments (2) and (3). The Kaplan–Meier (KM) curves, log-rank tests, and Harrell’s concordance index (C-index) were com…

title: Rapid prediction of microscale stress fields in fiber-reinforced composites from limited finite element data using a deep learning framework
abstract: Predicting transverse stress response of fiber-reinforced polymer composites at the microstructural level traditionally relies on finite element method (FEM) simulations of representative volume elements, which are computationally expensive and time-consuming. While deep learning offers a faster surrogate, most existing approaches require hundreds to thousands of FEM-generated training samples, creating a significant data bottleneck. The results demonstrate that accurate stress-contour prediction can be achieved using as few as 20 base representative volume element simulations, expanded to 80 training samples through rotation and reflection augmentation. To address this limited dataset and emphasize mechanically critical stress concentration regions, a two-stage U-Net framework with a dual-output head and a custom attention loss based on red–green–blue (RGB) pixel values was developed. The first stage trains the model on exaggerated stress contours to identify regions of peak stress, while the second refines predictions using standard stress contours to recover realistic stress magnitudes. Trained on 80 augmented samples derived from 20 base simulations, the model reproduced FEM-validated stress contours with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.366 ± 0.284 MPa and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.943 ± 0.006 . Expanding the base dataset to 85, yielding 340 augment…

title: Laser-Scattering-Image-Based Intelligent Sensing for Dust Concentration Prediction in Top-Blown Furnace Applications with ICPO-CKGPR
abstract: Top-blown furnaces are important equipment in non-ferrous metal smelting processes, where dust concentration variations provide useful information for process monitoring and environmental management. However, conventional dust measurement methods may suffer from limited measurement efficiency and insufficient adaptability under complex operating conditions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a laser-scattering-image-based intelligent sensing framework with an improved crested porcupine optimizer-based combined-kernel Gaussian process regression model, termed ICPO-CKGPR, for dust concentration prediction under simulated top-blown furnace conditions. First, a laboratory-scale laser scattering image acquisition platform was established to collect scattering images under different dust concentration conditions, and 5000 timestamp-matched image–concentration sample pairs were obtained using a particulate matter sensor as the reference measurement source. Subsequently, a multi-domain feature representation strategy integrating grayscale-domain, frequency-domain, and spatial-domain information was developed to enhance the characterization capability of dust scattering images under multi-scale variations and disturbances. Furthermore, a combined-kernel Gaussian process regression model consisting of radial basis function, Matérn, and rational quadratic kernels was constru…

title: PREECLAMPSIA: MODERN APPROACHES TO EARLY PREDICTION, DIAGNOSIS AND PREVENTION (LITERATURE REVIEW)
abstract: В статье представлен обзор современных подходов к прогнозированию, ранней диагностике и профилактике преэклампсии. Рассмотрены основные механизмы развития заболевания, диагностическая значимость ангиогенных биомаркеров sFlt-1 и PlGF, а также возможности комбинированного скрининга в первом триместре беременности. Особое внимание уделено профилактике преэклампсии и перспективам применения современных диагностических алгоритмов в Республике Узбекистан.
venue: Eurasian Journal of Medical and Natural Sciences

title: Experimental Investigation and Prediction of the Conventional Properties of Sustainable Asphalt Binder Mastic Modified with Calcined Red Mud
abstract: Abstract In the past, studies have reported the production of asphalt binder mastic with red mud as filler, culminating in improved mixture performance. However, this involves repetitive laboratory testing, which can be both time-consuming and resource-intensive. Therefore, this work predicts the performance of calcined red mud-modified asphalt binder mastic using response surface methodology (RSM). The red mud was calcined at 400 ° C, 500 ° C and 600 ° C, used as filler in asphalt binder mastic at filler-to-binder ratios of 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0, and its effects on mastic conventional properties, moisture susceptibility and short-time aging resistance were investigated. In the RSM analysis, the independent variables considered are red mud content and degree of heat treatment, while the dependent variables include the mastic conventional properties (penetration, softening point and penetration index), moisture susceptibility and short-time aging resistance. The experimental results show that penetration decreases and the softening point and penetration index increase with increasing filler/binder ratio and calcination temperature, demonstrating improved performance. The developed model showed R 2 values of 0.9374, 0.9616, 0.9532, 0.8813, and 0.9398 for softening point, penetration, penetration index, stripping rate, and AIC, respectively, indicating good predictability. TREINAMENTOS E CAPACITAÇÕES EM PRIMEIROS SOCORROS NO CONTEXTO DE CRECHES E ESCOLAS: UMA REVISÃO DE ESCOPO
abstract: Este estudo consiste em uma revisão de escopo que teve como objetivo caracterizar os treinamentos e/ou capacitações em primeiros socorros no contexto de creches e escolas. Seguindo as diretrizes PRISMA, a busca selecionou 7 artigos científicos publicados entre 2018 e 2024. Os achados indicam que a maioria dos docentes e funcionários presenciam emergências na rotina escolar sem o devido treinamento prévio, o que resulta em baixa autoconfiança. Em contrapartida, as intervenções teóricas e práticas com uso de simulações e treino em manequins demonstraram elevar significativamente a segurança percebida e o desempenho prático do corpo docente. Constatou-se, contudo, a perda progressiva de habilidades ao longo do tempo. Conclui-se que a capacitação contínua é fundamental para a consolidação de ambientes escolares seguros o que ressalta a importância da inclusão do tema nas matrizes curriculares da graduação.

title: Why risk‐based premiums will not close the catastrophe protection gap: Conventional pricing, reinsurance capacity, and public scheme design
abstract: Abstract Only about one‐fifth to one‐quarter of the economic losses caused by natural catastrophes in the European Union are insured, and the gap is widening as climate‐related losses grow. EIOPA and the ECB have proposed an EU‐level scheme combining a public–private reinsurance pool, funded by risk‐based premiums, with a public disaster fund. This paper asks whether risk‐based pricing at a public layer can close a gap that risk‐based pricing at the private layer has not. The capital‐market‐imperfections account of catastrophe insurance failure presupposes a knowable loss distribution; climate non‐stationarity removes that condition, and catastrophe pricing is better understood as conventional valuation under fundamental uncertainty. A five‐equation model of conventional pricing, with a demand side, makes reinsurance capacity endogenously cyclical and generates a rationing ratchet whose threshold is derived analytically and verified by simulation: prices soften within a few periods of a market break while attachment points and terms do not, and once climate‐driven model revisions recur before risk‐adjusted prices recover, rationing ratchets up and the insured share falls persistently. Simulated coverage is 15 points lower under conventional pricing with drifting losses than under a constant‐load benchmark, and the model reproduces the documented moments of the 2022–2026 cycle. …

abstract: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) can trigger oxidative stress through an imbalance between oxidant production and antioxidant defenses. Total antioxidant capacity (TAC) reflects antioxidant activity, while malondialdehyde (MDA) indicates lipid peroxidation. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) may improve antioxidant capacity by supporting glutathione synthesis. This study evaluated high-dose intravenous NAC administration on TAC and MDA levels in hospitalized CAP patients with comorbidities. A randomized controlled trial involved 44 patients at Patut Patuh Patju Regional General Hospital, Gerung. Participants were allocated to an intervention group receiving standard treatment plus NAC (n = 22) or a control group receiving standard treatment alone (n = 22). Biomarkers were measured before and after treatment and analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann–Whitney U tests. Mean TAC increased from 5.709 to 9.813 in the intervention group (p = 0.005), while decreasing from 26.223 to 25.164 in controls (p = 0.205). Postintervention TAC differed significantly between groups (p < 0.001). Mean MDA increased from 281.0485 to 410.6223 in the intervention group (p = 0.210) and from 535.273 to 791.773 in controls (p = 0.205), without a significant postintervention difference (p = 0.127). NAC administration was associated with increased TAC within the intervention group, but MDA changes were nonsign…

abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate on the metal-centered autocatalytic reduction of metmyoglobin (MbFeIII(H2O)) by sulfide species (H2S/HS–), focusing on the role of hydrodisulfide (HSS–) as the autocatalytic species in the reaction mechanism. The reaction is initiated with the formation of the MbFeIII(SH–) complex, under inert atmosphere. By adding increasing concentrations of HSS– to MbFeIII(SH–) complex, an acceleration of the metal-centered reduction forming myoglobin (MbFeII) is observed. Furthermore, the addition of HSS– to MbFeIII(SH–) modifies the autocatalytic kinetic regime suggesting an interplay between the bound and added sulfur species. Spin-trapping experiments that arrest the autocatalytic regime still yield the MbFeII product in the presence of added HSS–, enabling the isolated kinetic analysis of the disulfides-mediated reduction of MbFeIII(SH–). QM/MM calculations allowed a description of mechanistic details, suggesting that the most plausible mechanism for the autocatalytic step consists in a trans-S-sulfuration reaction where, while the Fe–S bond remains intact, a sulfur atom from the HSS– anion binds the coordinated sulfide in MbFeIII(SH–). Altogether, this study supports a metal-centered reduction mechanism based on a new S–S bond formation for the reaction intermediate, and provides a framework for hemeprotein reduction by the interplay of sulfide and…

title: Rethinking Meningioma Biology: Integrating Molecular and Microenvironmental Insights for Mechanism-Guided Therapy
abstract: Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial tumors, accounting for 42.6% of all central nervous system tumors. Although many meningiomas are indolent, clinical behavior is highly heterogeneous, with recurrence occurring in a minority of low-risk tumors but in more than half of clinically high-risk cases despite standard therapy. During the past decade, significant advancements in molecular profiling have provided insights into meningioma biology and have begun to influence clinical practice. Genomic sequencing, DNA methylation profiling, and gene expression analyses have revealed distinct molecular subgroups with prognostic and therapeutic implications. These advancements, coupled with a growing understanding of the meningioma immune microenvironment, have expanded therapeutic possibilities beyond traditional surgery and radiation approaches. Here, we review how molecular profiling is refining patient stratification and treatment selection, examine the evidence supporting various therapeutic approaches, and explore ongoing clinical trials. Finally, we highlight the critical challenges in advancing personalized medicine for meningioma patients. This comprehensive review provides an integrated overview of current diagnostic and treatment paradigms while offering perspectives on future directions in meningioma therapy.

abstract: Introduction Agrivoltaic (APV) systems can modify soil microclimate, but their short-term Q9 effects on soil organic matter (SOM) and microbial functioning remain incompletely understood. Methods We assessed SOM fractions and microbial activity in permanent grassland and raspberry shrubland under and outside APV over two years (2024–2025), sampling two soil depths. Three replicate plots represented each vegetation × APV combination. Thermogravimetric SOM fractions and oxidizable carbon were evaluated alongside dehydrogenase activity, basal respiration, substrate-induced respiration (SIR), and microbial functional diversity (MFD). Results Responses varied among vegetation types, APV conditions, depths, years, and measured variables. SIR responses showed significant interactions among all four factors, indicating context-dependent patterns rather than a uniform APV effect. Changes in oxidizable carbon and thermogravimetric SOM fractions were selective, while MFD showed lower-order effects but no four-way interaction. Exploratory PCA showed that associations among microbial indicators and SOM fractions varied across vegetation–APV combinations and soil depths. title: Nonreductive Catalytic Cyclizations of Carbon Dioxide into Synthons for Fine-Chemical, Pharmaceutical, and Polymer Applications
abstract: Conspectus Nature enables the transformation of carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen via photosynthesis representing a crucial chemical process for life on earth. This carbon fixation process also helps to balance the global carbon cycle controlling the uptake of carbon from the atmosphere. Ever since the industrial revolution, anthropogenic carbon emissions have increased at such a pace resulting in an imbalance of the carbon cycle and, as a consequence, effects known as global warming and the occurrence of more extreme weather patterns. The “excess” of carbon dioxide is commonly perceived as waste, with little to no value to humanity. Thus, ideally technologies able to transform this waste carbon into value-added compounds and materials would be economically of interest to various communities. The principal technology to complement the chemical diversification that Nature can provide for carbon dioxide conversion is catalysis. Catalysis offers an approach to activate substrates in different ways building on diverse reactivity principles and contemplating on the possibility to activate CO2 directly or the coreactant. This includes the use of Brønsted or Lewis bases, transition metals, photo- and organo-catalysis, offering us a wide variety of activation modes. title: Microplasma glow discharge chip for open-air atomic emission spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract This work presents a miniaturised glow discharge spectral emission chip, a compact wetchemical multi-ion sensor featuring integrated on-chip thick-planar metallic-film electrodes with a perpendicular porous layer, fabricated on a glass substrate. The device can operate at atmospheric pressure in ambient air and utilises a 500 ms DC to create the plasma. It employs a synthesised sol-gel-derived porous silica channel to wick the micropipetted liquid samples into the plasma region and controlled introduction of liquid samples in air plasma. The fabricated chip has a 5 mm × 5 mm footprint and an interelectrode gap of 55 µm. It demonstrates the detection of sodium in NaCl solution, with an estimated instrumental LOD of 0.2116 ppm, using a volume of less than 0.7 µL, showcasing a portable, simplified fabrication approach as an alternative to a conventional large-scale ICP-AES system for on-site monitoring of liquid samples.

title: Estimation of Rice Leaf Area Index Coupling Feature Selection from Multi-Temporal UAV Imagery with Machine Learning
abstract: Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a key biophysical parameter characterizing crop canopy structure and growth status. Large-scale, dynamic, and high-precision estimation of LAI using remote sensing is critical for crop growth assessment and yield forecasting. This study investigates rice LAI estimation across multiple growth stages by integrating optimally selected features from multi-temporal unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery into modeling algorithms. Based on controlled experiments with varying nitrogen fertilizer gradients, rice field LAI data were synchronously collected alongside high-resolution red–green–blue (RGB) and multispectral UAV images. Vegetation spectral indices were then extracted, and principal component analysis (PCA) was performed on these indices to obtain the first principal component (PC1). Subsequently, gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) calculations were conducted on the PC1 image to extract texture features. Feature selection was performed separately using recursive feature elimination (RFE) guided by Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) for random forest (RF), variable importance in projection (VIP) for partial least squares regression (PLSR), and backward elimination for stepwise regression (SR). Each model was developed using its corresponding selected predictors for individual growth stages and the combined dataset. The results demonstrated that the…

Quantifying light coupling to guided modes in semiconductor slabs with arbitrary scattering patterns
abstract: Optimizing broadband optical absorption in thin semiconductor layers using nanopatterned light-trapping structures remains a major challenge, as the applicability of existing models is restricted. When absorbing layers are thinned to the wavelength scale, guided mode bands discretize and statistical limits are no longer applicable. Coupled-mode theory can make accurate predictions for narrow-band excitation of structures with only a few sufficiently separated modes in order to determine a suitable periodicity, but when localized resonances are introduced in the scattering unit and resonant peaks start overlapping, no further design directives are extractable from it. Here, we present what is believed to be a new post-processing framework applied to standard FDTD simulations to obtain quantitative information from full-field simulations on the energy- and momentum-resolved scattering and absorption distributions for both periodic and arbitrary non-periodic nanopatterns. This enables tailoring of the pattern parameters to steer light into specific guided modes and analyze their absorptive properties and trapping capabilities. We demonstrate the applicability of this toolbox using three case studies in which we assess the impact of localized Mie resonances and (quasi-)random structural correlations on the modal absorption, separate Beer-Lambert and Fabry-Perót contributions to abs…

title: A Triboelectric‐Hydrogel System for Mechano‐Metabolic Re‐Coupling in Skin Expansion: Recharging From Energy Crisis
abstract: ABSTRACT Skin expansion is an effective technique for reconstructing large skin defects, yet its clinical utility is constrained by a progressive decline in regenerative capacity of skin, largely due to an underlying cellular energy crisis. Electrical stimulation enhances mitochondrial energy production, while mechanical regulation optimizes energy allocation. We designed a biocompatible composite system (TP‐PAM/G) capable of synergistic electro‐mechanical regulation to re‐energize tissue. The system comprises a triboelectric nanogenerator layer fabricated from thermoplastic polyurethane and poly(vinylidene fluoride) that harnesses the ubiquitous mechanical forces of expansion to generate sustained mild electrical stimulation, and a hydrogel layer synthesized from polyacrylamide and gelatin that redistributes heterogeneous stresses. TP‐PAM/G exhibits excellent mechanical compliance and tissue adhesion, enabling stable, long‐lasting electric stimulation in response to expander stretching. In vitro results demonstrated that this electrical stimulation promotes the proliferation and migration of fibroblasts and endothelial cells and enhances collagen synthesis and angiogenesis. These effects were underpinned by upregulated mitochondrial activity. title: Multi-scale simulations of wind farm impacts on nighttime near-surface temperature in complex terrain
abstract: Various studies have shown that wind turbine wakes can induce temperature variations. Investigating these effects near the ground is particularly important for assessing their potential impact on vegetation and human activities. In this study, the multi-scale Meso-NH/SURFEX/EOL modeling framework, which includes coupled atmosphere, land-surface and actuator models, is used to evaluate the impact of the Ensemble Éolien Catalan wind farm on ground and near-surface temperatures, as well as terrain-specific flow dynamics during a stable nocturnal radiative cooling event associated with frost risk in nearby vineyards. The simulations are performed using nested domains to dynamically downscale the atmospheric conditions from the operational weather forecast AROME-1.3km to a horizontal resolution of 5 m, allowing explicit representation of turbine wakes through rotative actuator disk representation. Turbine-induced meteorological variations are quantified by comparing simulations performed with and without the actuator model. The results reveal that near-surface meteorological responses arise from the combined influence of individual turbine wakes and the large-scale impact of the wind farm, which modifies the flow dynamics and temperature field. In the wind farm, a mean near-surface warming of approximately 0.4 °C is found, with localized temperature increases reaching up to 1.6 °C i…

title: Optimal Power Flow for Sustainable Operation of Transmission Systems with High Renewable Penetration
abstract: The paper presents an integrated approach to Optimal Power Flow (OPF) in transmission systems with a high share of renewable energy sources (RESs) supported by energy storage systems (ESSs). Unlike conventional approaches, the proposed integrated evaluation framework minimizes operating cost subject to technical (network and ESS) constraints, while separately reporting RES utilization/curtailment and CO2 outcomes as post-solve indicators. The model was implemented as a browser-based JavaScript application using a custom Big-M Simplex linear programming solver and tested on a 24 h horizon under multiple scenarios representing conditions informed by Baltic/Latvian load, generation, and price profiles, applied to a modified IEEE 9-bus test network, including standard operation, high price volatility, high RES penetration, and a transmission line outage (N-1 criterion). The results demonstrate that ESS integration together with RES usage maximization reduces total operating costs by up to 10.2% compared to the baseline strategy without ESS and optimization (about 4.7 percentage points of this saving come from the lower minimum output of the conventional unit alone), increases RES share by about 5 percentage points, and decreases RES curtailment to 0%, under a terminal state of charge condition that prevents the ESS from ending the horizon more depleted than it started (imposed in H…

title: Robot-Assisted Mapping of Precursor Formulation, Microstructure, and Electronic Structure in Lead-Free Silver–Bismuth-Iodide Materials for Photovoltaics
abstract: Abstract Silver–bismuth iodides offer a lead-free alternative for photovoltaic energy conversion, but their device performance depends strongly on the precursor formulation and the absorber formation. In this work, the AURORA robotic platform was adapted to investigate this formulation–performance landscape through sequential, population-level screening of 80 device-level records from mesoscopic photovoltaic devices. An initial concentration screen of an equimolar AgI:BiI3 formulation revealed a strongly nonmonotonic response, with the highest photovoltaic performance at a nominal loading of 1.0 mol L–1 for each precursor. Subsequent variation of the precursor ratio showed that the nominal stoichiometry alone is not sufficient to predict device performance. Under nominal 1000-lux white-LED illumination, the Ag-rich 2:1 formulation showed an apparent forward-scan power conversion efficiency of (19.8 ± 7.6)% (mean ± standard deviation, n = 16), calculated using a nominal incident irradiance of 0.25 mW cm–2, more than twice that of the equimolar formulation and more than five times that of the Bi-rich formulation. This improvement can predominantly be linked to the photocurrent rather than to open-circuit voltage and was associated with the formation of a more compact, interconnected absorber morphology. title: Constraints on regular black holes with nonminimally coupled electromagnetic fields
abstract: A bstract Construction of physically realistic theories admitting regular black hole solutions remains an important open problem in gravitational physics. While theories with electromagnetic fields minimally coupled to gravity have been extensively studied over the past two decades, theories with nonminimal couplings remain comparatively unexplored. We investigate theories containing the interaction terms RF ab F ab , R ab F a c F bc and R abcd F ab F cd , which generically arise in low-energy effective Lagrangians. We prove that magnetically charged regular black holes are excluded, except possibly for a special choice of coupling constants, and argue that a similar conclusion applies to electrically charged regular black holes. We further show that similar conclusions hold for Lagrangian terms of the form f ( R , F ab ⋆ F ab ).

title: EXTREPSO: An Energy Estimator Based on Machine Learning with PSO Optimization for UASNs
abstract: Underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs) are severely affected by propagation delay, limited bandwidth, and constrained node energy. This work presents EXTREPSO, a machine learning framework that combines an Extra Trees Regressor with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for offline hyperparameter tuning of a hop-level energy-efficiency predictor. The target is derived from Aqua-Sim NG trace fields using the payload size, the simulator Tx_power field, and observed hop delay. Aqua-Sim NG defines PT as transmitted signal power in watts, so the target has dimensional units of bit/J; however, because the observed hop delay includes propagation and protocol-related waiting, it is treated as an operational trace-derived metric rather than a state-resolved modem-energy measurement. In the original 80:20 benchmark, Extra Trees was the strongest baseline among seven classical ML and three DL models. A leakage-resistant sender-grouped outer five-fold evaluation with inner grouped validation was subsequently used to compare baseline Extra Trees, PSO-tuned Extra Trees, and an interpretable inverse-power baseline on untouched test folds. PSO tuning produced a modest average improvement over baseline Extra Trees (mean RMSE 2107.31 versus 2230.58), but the improvement was not consistent across folds; the inverse-power baseline achieved the lowest mean RMSE (1765.88). title: Optimizing Multilinear Polynomial Representations of Boolean Functions for Neural Network Synthesis
abstract: We consider the problem of obtaining a neural network (NN) representation of a Boolean network (BN), where each Boolean network (BN) vertex is a k -input Boolean function (BF) ( k≤ K ). A neural network (NN) representation can be constructed by mapping each Boolean function (BF) to its multilinear polynomial (MP) representation and then to a two-layer sub-NN; composing sub-NNs completes the representation. In this article, we show that structural properties (number of neurons/connections, neuron in-degree) of such a NN representation can be efficiently optimized while maintaining functional equivalence with the original BN ( lossless optimization). Our approach establishes a correspondence between multilinear polynomials (MPs) and their two-layer-NN representation, enabling sub-NN optimization by minimizing MPs under structural criteria. To accelerate optimization, we utilize criterion invariance under Negation-Permutation-Negation (NPN) transformations. This allows us to classify BFs into equivalence classes, optimize canonical representatives, and then derive optimal representations for remaining class members via Negation-Permutation-Negation (NPN) transformations. Since optimizing sub-NNs may affect the composed NN depth, we propose an algorithm for lossless optimization under depth constraints. title: Design and Experimental Evaluation of a Posture-Adjustable Cable-Based Clamping–Cutting End-Effector for Safflower Filaments
abstract: Safflower filaments grow in random directions, whereas rigid-cutter picking end-effectors have large front ends and a fixed approach posture. To address these problems, a posture-adjustable cable-based clamping–cutting end-effector for safflower filaments was designed. Carried by a Delta parallel robot, it uses a two-axis deflection platform to align its axis with the flower growth direction and replaces rigid jaws and blades with twisted cable clamping and staggered twin-wire cutting. Twisted-string clamping and cutting-stroke models were established to determine the parameters of the guide orifice and the clamping and cutting mechanisms, and an end-effector–flower axis-angle test and a field picking test were conducted. The projected front-end area was 69.1% smaller than that of the previous-generation rigid-blade picking head. In single-attempt picking of 136 safflowers in the field, the complete clamping rate was 95.6%, the cutting success rate after complete clamping was 99.2%, and the clamping–cutting success rate was 94.9%. With the axes aligned (0–10°), the mass picking rate was 90.39%, within the range of values in the literature for rigid-blade end-effectors; at 30–40°, it decreased to 62.07%. The cable-based end-effector reliably clamps and cuts filaments with a small front end, and the end-effector–flower axis angle significantly affects the mass picking rate. These…

title: Optimal design of multiphase interface synergistic lubrication: molecular dynamics insights into DLC films under oil lubrication
abstract: Abstract This study employed molecular dynamics simulations to systematically investigate the microscopic friction mechanisms of a sealing pair consisting of diamond-like carbon (DLC) coated plungers and nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) under oil-lubricated conditions. A friction model comprising base oil and the DLC-NBR interface was first constructed, and four different quantities of oil molecules ( Q oil ) were set to analyze the effects of lubrication status on friction behavior, structural evolution, stress transmission, and temperature evolution of the system. The results indicate that the interfacial friction behavior initially improves and deteriorates with increasing oil content. When the Q oil is just sufficient (15CH), the oil lubrication effect reaches its optimal state. At this point, the oil molecule adsorption layer transforms the friction interface from solid-solid contact to solid-liquid contact, inhibiting the migration of molecular chains on the NBR surface. The oil molecule adsorption layer acts as a stress buffering layer, reducing the shear stress and normal stress of the friction pair by approximately 50% respectively, thereby lowering the friction force to 28.6 nN. title: The Effect of Digital Transformation on Employee Performance with Readiness for Change as a Moderating Variable at The Public Works and Spatial Planning Office of Central Kalimantan Province
abstract: Digital transformation has become an increasingly important requirement for public-sector organizations; however, previous studies have reported inconsistent findings regarding its effects on employee performance. This study aimed to examine the effect of digital transformation on employee performance and investigate the moderating role of employees' readiness for change at the Public Works and Spatial Planning Office (DPUPR) of Central Kalimantan Province, Indonesia. An explanatory quantitative research design was employed. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered to 164 respondents from a target sample of 167 employees, selected through purposive sampling from a population of 288 employees. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model satisfied the established criteria for convergent validity, discriminant validity, and reliability. The results indicated that digital transformation had a positive and statistically significant effect on employee performance (β = 0.251; t = 3.271; p = 0.001). title: THE GREEN ROOM protocol for a mixed-methods study on virtual nature for mental well-being in the acute psychiatry ward
abstract: Abstract Background Acute psychiatric hospitalization often takes place in highly restrictive environments where patients have limited access to restorative natural settings despite growing evidence that nature exposure benefits psychological well-being. Immersive virtual reality (VR) offers a promising, low-risk approach to providing nature-based experiences within acute psychiatric wards. However, evidence regarding its implementation and effectiveness in routine inpatient psychiatric care remains scarce. Methods THE GREEN ROOM is a single-centre mixed-methods study combining an implementation evaluation with a pragmatic randomized controlled trial. The implementation phase will use semi-structured interviews with patients and healthcare professionals, guided by the Non-adoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread and Sustainability (NASSS) framework, to identify barriers and facilitators to implementation and to inform refinement of the intervention protocol. The second phase consists of a pragmatic, parallel-group randomized controlled trial including 120 psychiatric inpatients, stratified according to voluntary versus involuntary admission status. Participants allocated to the intervention group will receive immersive nature-based VR sessions in addition to treatment as usual. title: A aplicação da realidade virtual no alívio da dor e da ansiedade na oncologia pediátrica
abstract: Objective. To investigate the use of Virtual Reality (VR) in managing pain and anxiety in pediatric oncology patients, identifying its effects, forms of application, and contributions to humanized care. Method. A scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) investigated the use of Virtual Reality in managing pain and anxiety in pediatric oncology. The PCC search in the MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases used terms verified in MeSH. Specific inclusion criteria (2015–2025, free access, English/Spanish/Portuguese languages, age group 6–18 years) and exclusion criteria were applied, resulting in 5 articles out of 532. The selection was conducted independently. Results. Of the five included studies, four were randomized clinical trials (80%) and one was an observational study (20%). All reported a significant reduction in pain and anxiety scores compared with standard care. Conclusions. VR proves to be a promising, effective, and safe non-pharmacological strategy for managing pain and anxiety in pediatric oncology, contributing to more humanized care practices. Future studies should expand the number of participants and explore optimized interventions, including resources like biofeedback.

title: Mechanically Actuated Pancharatnam‐Berry Metasurfaces for Non‐Volatile and Zero‐Static‐Power Programmable Wavefront Manipulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Programmable metasurfaces enable dynamic electromagnetic control, but implementations requiring continuous electrical bias incur state‐maintenance power and may require distributed biasing networks. Herein, we propose and validate experimentally a mechanically coded metasurface platform dubbed MetaFlip, which synergizes the transient magnetic actuation with the intrinsic Pancharatnam‐Berry (PB) geometric phase modulation. A 180° out‐of‐plane mechanical flip selects two orthogonally oriented anisotropic facets, producing binary phase states that are retained without continuous coil‐driving power; switching and auxiliary electronics still consume energy. The simulated joint 1 dB and 2 dB operating bandwidths are 72 and 117 MHz, respectively, with a maximum inter‐state phase error of 3.56° relative to 180° within both bands. Customized binary coding matrices are loaded to unlock diverse wavefront engineering capabilities: high‐resolution near‐field focusing and reconfigurable far‐field beam splitting. More importantly, when deployed as a reflective relay in a non‐line‐of‐sight wireless communication testbed, MetaFlip can concentrate the spatial electromagnetic energy toward the receiving antenna, supporting high‐fidelity image transmissions. abstract: ABSTRACT 2,2,6,6‐tetramethylpiperidine‐1‐oxyl (TEMPO) derivatives are widely studied as positive electrolytes in aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) due to their high redox potential. However, TEMPO‐based AORFBs suffer from stability issues with molecule degradation. In this work, a unique stabilization strategy beyond molecular engineering is developed by designing a TEMPO‐based redox‐targeting (RT) flow battery via a proton‐competition mechanism. A RT flow battery is constructed with 4‐acetamido‐TEMPO as redox mediator and polyaniline (PANI) as the solid material, achieving 4.37‐fold enhancement in capacity (35.72 Ah L −1 ), high coulombic efficiency (99.99%) and excellent capacity retention (99.94% per cycle over 500 cycles within 840.82 h). The outstanding stability of the TEMPO‐based flow battery is attributed to the synergistic interaction between proton buffering and RT reactions. This study elucidates a key pathway for suppressing TEMPO radical hydrogenation through a proton competition mechanism, which relies on the reversible doping/de‐doping cycles of the PANI. Operando spectroscopic studies and density functional theory calculations elucidate the mechanism, revealing an intermediate transition state and confirming that proton competition by PANI is pivotal for radical stabilization. title: Molecular Understanding of Ligand-Governed Al0 Electrodeposition from Al3+ Complexes in Protic Solvents and Ionic Liquids
abstract: Abstract Commercial Al(OTf)3 and Al(TFSI)3 salts have attracted significant interest in aluminum-ion batteries (AIBs), with aqueous electrolytes exhibiting typical charge–discharge profiles whose origin remains debated. Meanwhile, these salts have also been explored as alternatives to halide-based ionic liquid (IL) electrolytes, which suffer from low oxidative stability and corrosive character in device applications. Here, we systematically analyze the electrochemical behavior of these salts in both protic and IL electrolytes to elucidate the mechanism governing Al0/3+ electrochemistry. This work reveals that Al0 electrodeposition consistently fails in the examined Al(OTf)3 and Al(TFSI)3-based electrolytes owing to residual water, which cannot be fully removed even after rigorous drying processes and the addition of moisture-scavenging LiAlH4. For Al3+ complexes in these electrolytes, breaking a labile ligand is energetically more favorable than complete Al3+ desolvation during charge-transfer processes at the electrode interface. The calculations further suggest that protic molecules coordinated to a Lewis-acidic cation are more readily deprotonated at the electrode interface than in the bulk electrolyte. The less Lewis-acidic Zn2+ shows the same preference for ligand decomposition over desolvation. Cluster calculations further suggest that [Zn(H2O)6]2+ can release twice as ma…

title: Ion‐Dipole Engineered Hierarchical Ion‐Gradient Piezoionic Elastomers for Enhanced Soft Energy Harvesting and Multimodal Sensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Piezoionic elastomers transduce mechanical deformation into electrical signals through ion migration, yet achieving effective and stable ion gradient remains challenging. Here, we present hierarchical ion‐gradient piezoionic elastomers (HiGPiE), featuring spherulitic ionic microcompartments coupled with nanoscale asymmetric ion organization and ion‐polymer interactions within an [EMIM] + [BF 4 ] − ionic liquid (IL)‐incorporated PVDF matrix. [EMIM] + cations strongly interact with PVDF through ion–dipole interactions, whereas [BF 4 ] − anions exhibit comparatively higher mobility, enabling asymmetric and selective migration under mechanical stress. The hierarchical architecture enhances charge separation through two synergistic mechanisms: (i) localized stress concentration within the spherulitic ionic microcompartments and (ii) asymmetric ion organization and migration, supported by experimental and theoretical analyses. HiGPiE containing 56 wt.% IL (HiGPiE‐56) exhibits a high piezoionic coefficient of 73.5 ± 8 mV kPa −1 , over 13‐fold higher than reported polymeric systems, together with a power density of 54 ± 4.7 mW m −2 . In piezoiontronic operation, pressure‐driven ion redistribution enables a tunable interfacial capacitance of ∼17.2 µF cm −2 and a sensitivity of 44.6 nF kPa −1 . Proof‐of‐concept demonstrations include a soft piezoionic mechanotransducer for wirel…

title: Adaptive Lightweight Security Framework for Energy-Efficient Intrusion Detection and Secure Communication in IoT Environments
Sustainable Procurement Optimization Using Predictive Compliance Dashboards in ESG-Critical Energy Infrastructure Projects
abstract: The growing emphasis on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) criteria has intensified the need for sustainability-oriented procurement strategies within energy infrastructure projects. This review explores the integration of predictive compliance dashboards to enhance procurement optimization in ESG-critical contexts. These dashboards leverage real-time analytics, historical compliance data, and AI-driven insights to forecast risks, enforce regulatory alignment, and support proactive decision-making across procurement lifecycles. By embedding sustainability metrics into procurement processes, energy firms can ensure supplier transparency, reduce environmental footprints, and strengthen social responsibility and governance standards. The study examines existing frameworks, case applications in energy infrastructure projects, and the technological architecture underlying predictive dashboards. It further highlights challenges related to interoperability, data governance, and regulatory fragmentation, proposing a roadmap for the scalable adoption of dashboard-driven procurement systems. This paper contributes to sustainable infrastructure development by underscoring the strategic importance of data-centric tools in managing ESG performance across complex supply networks.
