title: Geomechanics of Refracturing and Infill Well Development in Unconventional Reservoirs: A Review on Stress Evolution and Fracture Propagation
abstract: Secondary stimulation introduces fractures into reservoirs whose pressure, stress and fracture condition have been altered by earlier development. Refracturing and infill-well treatments can consequently reactivate old pathways, create new orientations or produce unequal fracture wings. This review links these responses through an evolved geomechanical state that retains primary-fracturing, closure and production history. Published analytical, numerical, laboratory and field studies are compared using two coupled controls: path selection and pathway activation or propagation resistance. Principal-stress orientation, gradients and interfaces influence direction, while resolved normal traction, contact, toughness and hydraulic access determine whether a candidate pathway opens and continues to grow. The distinction explains why a favorable reorientation zone may still feed an old fracture, and why parent-directed steering can coexist with local resistance near inherited fractures. Refracturing evidence emphasizes the sequence of access modification, new initiation and subsequent competition; parent-child studies emphasize heterogeneous depletion, asymmetric growth and the difference between mechanical accessibility and remaining resource. Modeling methods are assessed by their ability to reconstruct the produced state and transfer it consistently into a propagation calculation. M…

title: Modeling individual nearby radio galaxies as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray accelerators
abstract: Abstract Nearby radio galaxies are among the most promising candidates for the acceleration of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). In this work, we develop a physically motivated, source-resolved framework to quantify the contribution of the three nearest Fanaroff–Riley Class I (FR-I) radio galaxies – Centaurus A, Virgo A, and Fornax A – to the UHECR flux measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory. Acceleration spectra derived from detailed jet-acceleration models are combined with numerical simulations of extragalactic propagation, while the more distant radio-galaxy population is treated as a continuous background. By fitting our simulation exclusively to the measured UHECR energy spectrum, we determine the relative contribution of each source and constrain the fraction of jet power converted into UHECR luminosity. We find that a small number of nearby radio galaxies can account for the highest-energy UHECR flux with acceleration efficiencies of order $$10^{-3}$$ 10 - 3 – $$10^{-2}$$ 10 - 2 , while the background contribution remains subdominant. Some resulting scenarios yield mass-composition trends broadly consistent with observations at the highest energies and predict distinct levels of secondary neutrino fluxes. These results demonstrate that physically grounded, source-specific modeling of nearby radio galaxies provides a physically motivated contribution to the inter…

title: Green Mobile Computing: A Review of Energy-Aware Smartphones, Cellular Radio Access, Edge Intelligence and Smart Grid Analytics
abstract: Mobile devices, cellular networks and the computing services behind them now form a large and growing source of electricity demand in the information and communication sector. A smartphone drains its battery through the screen, the radio and background applications, while the network that serves it spends most of its energy in base stations that stay powered even when traffic is light. Research on these problems is split across mobile software, wireless networking, edge computing and power-system communities, each optimizing its own layer. The objective of this review is to bring these strands into one picture that follows energy from the handset, through the radio access network and the edge or cloud, to the buildings and grids that supply the power. The review organizes 41 studies into a five-layer taxonomy and compares their aims, methods and reported outcomes. Device-level studies point to screen state, radio signalling, application wake-ups and user behaviour as the main drivers of handset energy use, and a mapping study found user behaviour to be the factor most often linked to battery drain. Network studies show that sleep modes and lean carrier designs can cut a large share of radio access energy, and that one set of architectural measures could reduce total mobile network energy by roughly a third. Edge studies report that energy-aware offloading and federated training…

title: Dietary Energy Density Functions as a Transferable Decision Principle in Children: Evidence from Structured Errors, Generalization, and Time-Constrained Decisions
abstract: Background/Objective: Dietary energy density (ED; kcal/g) influences energy intake and is central to obesity prevention. Little is known about how children understand energy density and apply the knowledge in decision-making contexts. This study examines classification accuracy, structured error patterns, and decision-making during a serious game intervention: a cognitive decision-process analysis of how children apply the concept of dietary ED, using serious gameplay data as behavioral readout. Methods: Gameplay data from a cluster-randomized controlled trial were analyzed. Children aged 9–11 years (n = 82) participated in a serious game intervention targeting energy density of foods (tasks with and without time pressure), beverage sugar content, and overall meal composition. Analyses focused on first-attempt responses to assess spontaneous application of the dietary ED concept. In-game decision patterns were used to assess children’s ability to classify foods by ED, estimate sugar content in beverages, and adapt food choices across repeated gameplay sessions. Results: Children understand ED. Misclassifications occurred predominantly between adjacent ED categories, with medium-ED (1.5–2.5 kcal/g) foods posing the greatest challenge. Classification accuracy was highest for fruits, vegetables, and high-energy sweets, while cereals and dairy products showed greater variability. U…

title: GIC-Net: AI-Driven Green IoT-CAN Bus Networks for Sustainable Energy Management with Optimization and Data Compression
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) applications has significantly increased energy consumption and network complexity, so that it becomes very essential for the development of efficient and sustainable communication. This paper proposes GIC-Net, an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven Green IoT-CAN Bus network designed for sustainable energy management through intelligent optimization and data compression techniques. The proposed framework integrates a Green IoT network model with dynamic cluster-based architecture with cluster head selection, cluster member management, and sleep scheduling to enhance energy efficiency. Additionally, an IoT-CAN Bus communication layer is developed to enable reliable, low-latency data transmission, supported by optimized data collection and compression mechanisms to reduce bandwidth and storage overhead.To further improve system performance, AI-driven optimization algorithms are employed for adaptive decision-making, while a comprehensive energy model is formulated to evaluate energy consumption, residual energy, and system lifetime. The proposed approach is validated through extensive simulations, considering key performance metrics such as cluster head selection efficiency, number of alive nodes, energy consumption, delay, packet delivery ratio, and total system energy.

title: Morphology Dependent Charge Storage in Electropolymerised Porphyrin Films on Gold Nanostructures
abstract: ABSTRACT The effect of morphology of the underlying gold nanostructure on the charge storage behavior of electropolymerized 5,10,15,20‐tetrathien‐2‐ylporphyrin is systematically examined in the present study. Electropolymerisation of thien‐2‐yl‐substituted porphyrins occurs through oxidative coupling of the thiophene moieties, leading to the formation of extended π‐conjugated polymeric networks. The fabricated electrodes were characterized using UV visible spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, XPS, SEM, HR TEM and AFM. A comprehensive electrochemical investigation involving cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge–discharge experiments, electrochemical impedance spectral measurements and kinetic analysis reveals that the morphology of the gold substrate plays a decisive role in deciding the charge storage kinetics of the hybrid polymeric materials. The results demonstrate that spherical gold nanostructures predominantly promote surface controlled capacitive charge storage whereas dendritic nanostructures introduce diffusion related limitations. These findings underscore the importance of nanostructure morphology in tailoring charge transport and optimizing the electrochemical performance of polymer based energy storage materials.

title: Modeling and Analysis of an Electrically Heated Molten-Salt Thermal Storage System for Thermal Power Flexibility
abstract: Electrically heated molten-salt storage converts surplus electricity into heat for later use. We combine a fixed-property heater model, a proper orthogonal decomposition–neural network (POD–NN) surrogate, and cyclic plant dispatch. The 210 cases computed with COMSOL Multiphysics 6.4.0.293 (COMSOL AB, Stockholm, Sweden) comprise 168 training, 21 validation, and 21 independent test cases. Two POD modes retain 99.998368% of the training fluctuation energy. Across all independent tests, mean case root mean square error (RMSE) is 0.716 K and pooled RMSE is 2.089 K. The worst case has an RMSE value of 9.424 K and maximum pointwise error of 20.098 K, mainly from coefficient prediction at a withheld grid corner. Five computed fields exceed 873.15 K, a numerical screening reference that is not an enforced temperature limit. These fields are retained to assess the numerical model and do not establish feasible operating conditions. Analytical comparisons verify model components; independent validation of the complete heater remains necessary. At the fixed nominal heater condition, cost minimization selects no charging, whereas emissions minimization avoids 91.930 t CO2/day at an additional cost of 2135 CNY/day. The results quantify the cost–emissions tradeoff for the stated model and daily scenario.

title: Nanoscale Confinement of Cu x S Conversion Products in Na 2 Ti 3 O 7 ‐Derived TiO 2 Matrix for Durable Sodium‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Fast sodium storage in conversion‐type sulfide anodes is often hindered by unstable phase evolution, sluggish interfacial kinetics, and insufficient mechanistic understanding of buried heterointerfaces. In this study, we report a phase‐ and coordination‐engineered Cu sulfide/mixed‐phase TiO 2 nanohybrid, fabricated through precursor‐directed interfacial reconstruction of layered Na 2 Ti 3 O 7 . Sequential Cu incorporation, surface‐confined HKUST‐1 growth, and NaSH‐assisted sulfidation steps simultaneously tuned the TiO 2 polymorphic landscape and Cu local coordination, transforming the parent titanate into an intimately integrated Cu x S–TiO 2 (B)/(A) nanohybrid with residual titanate motifs, abundant grain boundaries, and defect‐rich heterointerfaces. This engineered interface combines the conversion chemistry of high‐capacity Cu sulfide with structurally robust Ti‐based insertion/buffer domains, resulting in shorter Na + transport pathways, improved charge transfer kinetics, and enhanced surface‐dominated pseudocapacitive storage. Importantly, voltage‐selected ex situ Cu K‐edge XANES/EXAFS, XPS, and TEM analyses elucidated the electrochemical reaction pathway: Cu(I)‐rich sulfide domains are progressively converted into metallic Cu/Na 2 S‐like products during sodiation and partially transformed into disordered Cu x S during desodiation, while TiO 2 /titanate domains p…

title: Tax Revenue and Fiscal Sustainability in Ikot Ekpene Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State: An Empirical Analysis
ANALYSIS OF NON-METALLIC MINERAL AND ROCK MINING ENTREPRENEURS' COMPLIANCE IN OPTIMIZING NON-METALLIC MINERAL AND ROCK TAX REVENUE IN BULUNGAN REGENCY
abstract: This study analyzes the compliance of non-metallic mineral and rock (MBLB) mining entrepreneurs in optimizing MBLB tax revenue in Bulungan Regency, North Kalimantan Province, Indonesia. Using a qualitative research design with a narrative-qualitative analytical approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews with three key informants at the Regional Revenue Agency (Badan Pendapatan Daerah) of Bulungan Regency, supplemented by secondary data including regional revenue reports, tax realization records, and mining licensing documents from 2023 to 2025. The findings reveal that compliance among mining operators remains extremely low: out of approximately 24 mining entrepreneurs, only 3–4 entities with valid permits routinely report and pay their MBLB tax obligations. The consistently exceeded revenue targets are attributable primarily to a single dominant enterprise (PT. PJA) and supplementary collections from construction contractors, rather than to widespread voluntary compliance. Four principal obstacles impede compliance: (1) complex and costly mining permit acquisition processes, (2) insufficient understanding and awareness among small-scale miners regarding tax obligations, (3) inadequate government monitoring and surveillance of mining activities across the regency's vast terrain, and (4) limited human resources and budgetary capacity of the regional tax administra…

title: Tourism-Derived Revenue Dependence and Within-Year Variability Along the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor: Merchant and Visitor Evidence
abstract: Tourism-attributed revenue dependence and within-year variability were examined among sampled merchants along the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor, with visitor and product-market observations providing supporting evidence. The analysis used 240 merchant-month records from 20 merchants in 2024, 1000 visitor-survey responses, 70 matched merchant–trade product-category-month records, and a 720-observation monthly price panel covering 2020–2025. Estimated tourism-attributed merchant sales totaled CNY 2.92 million (64.80% of recorded revenue). The mean coefficient of variation (CV) for tourism-attributed monthly sales exceeded that of total monthly sales (0.369 versus 0.330; paired t(19) = 3.765, p = 0.0013). Merchant tourist share and QR-scan activity were not significantly associated with adjusted monthly sales. In the visitor survey, QR-code scanning (β = 0.667), satisfaction (β = 0.319), and product-category exposure (β = 0.229) were positively associated with stated post-visit purchase intent (all p < 0.001); expenditure and trip duration were not. Matched product-category trade associations were generally imprecise, and the nominal product-price ratio showed no significant category-adjusted monthly trend (p = 0.283). title: Optimal Development of Hydropower Storage Potential for Enhancing Flexibility of Cascade Hydro–Wind–Solar Systems
abstract: Developing cascade water energy storage potential is an effective way to enhance hydro–wind–solar flexibility and promote the accommodation of variable renewable energy. This study proposes an optimization method for developing cascade water energy storage potential that considers reservoir dredging, energy storage pump station, and reversible pumped-storage unit. Firstly, the characteristics of various measures for developing water energy storage potential are analyzed, and the operating boundaries and constraints of the cascade water energy storage system are determined. Secondly, considering the volatility of grid-connected large-scale green energy, a short-term multi-objective cascade water energy storage system optimization scheduling model is established with the goal of renewable energy generation and peak-shaving benefits. Finally, a multi-objective fuzzy evaluation method is adopted to quantitatively analyze the impact of different measures on the green energy generation and peak-shaving of the cascade water energy storage system. The cascade hydropower system of Gansu section of the Yellow River basin is selected as a case study, and the results indicate that (1) at matched average daily cascade hydropower output, reservoir 2 dredging reduces the residual-load standard deviation by 27.8% on average, whereas the composite evaluation of generation and peak shaving impro…

title: CoSPACE: Coordinated Construction Scheduling, Material Logistics, Shared Storage, and Crew Deployment for Resource-Efficient Site Planning
abstract: Resource-efficient construction planning requires coordination of schedules, material replenishment, limited storage and crew deployment. This study develops CoSPACE, a four-layer chromosome and seven-stage engineering decoder that jointly evaluates project duration (PD), material logistics cost (MC) and crew idle exposure (CIE). CIE measures unused capacity within each labour type’s deployment window, avoiding the redundancy between whole-project idle labour and PD under fixed workloads. Thirty seeded search archives are reconstructed for a deterministic ten-activity benchmark, with decoded-plan verification, an earliest-start reference and controlled gene-group interventions. Nine empirical pooled non-dominated points attain the verified 33-day duration bound. MC ranges from 1473.48 to 1662.40 monetary units as CIE decreases from 119 to 67 worker-days. For this benchmark, a selected compromise reduces MC by 21.94% and CIE by 9.41% against the deterministic reference. Controlled replays distinguish inventory, ordering-frequency and mobilization mechanisms; fixing priorities leaves the compromise unchanged, whereas removing delays worsens logistics cost and CIE. A separate matched-budget study evaluates four fixed cases, including two constructed instances and an adapted published project network with hypothetical logistics and non-interchangeable labour. Development and Performance of Elastomer Seals for Hydrogen Storage and Distribution Systems: Challenges, Solutions, and Future Perspectives—Part II: Component-Level Performance, Design, Modeling, and Qualification of Elastomer Hydrogen Seals
abstract: The expansion of hydrogen storage and distribution infrastructure demands elastomeric seals that maintain integrity under high pressure, thermal variations, pressure cycling, and rapid decompression. Hydrogen permeation, swelling, mechanical degradation, and gas-induced damage can impair sealing performance and increase leakage risk. This review examines elastomeric hydrogen seals from a component-level perspective, building on material characterization to assess how formulation, operating conditions, and seal design affect reliability. The literature is organized around elastomer formulations, hydrogen transport and property evolution, degradation and durability, and seal performance, numerical modeling, and qualification. Particular emphasis is placed on the interaction between hydrogen uptake and desorption, dimensional recovery, contact-pressure retention, groove geometry, squeeze, extrusion, and rapid gas decompression resistance. Seal failure results from coupled processes, including swelling, cavitation, blistering, crack growth, fatigue, aging, and loss of sealing contact. Existing qualification methods remain fragmented and do not consistently represent realistic hydrogen exposure and service cycles. More reliable seal design and lifetime prediction require standardized testing protocols and integrated experimental–numerical assessments connecting material behavior wit…

Influence of Process Parameters on Surface Modification Using Electric Discharge Machining: A systematic review
abstract: Electric Discharge Machining (EDM) has emerged as a vital non-traditional machining process widely used in shaping hard-to-machine materials while also contribute the capability to modify and enhance surface characteristics. Other than primary function of material removal, EDM has established to be an innovative surface engineering technique that can alter surface morphology, microstructure, mechanical properties, and functional behaviour of work materials. This systematic review explores the influence of EDM process parameters on the surface modification outcomes across various material systems. The study focuses on understanding how process variables, such as discharge voltage (V), discharge current (I), pulse on/off time, pulse interval time, electrode polarity, dielectric medium, and tool material, influence the formation of surface layers, recast zones, micro-cracks, and surface topography. Special attention is given to powder-mixed EDM (PMEDM), a technique that describes with sufficient electric conductive powders into the dielectric to alter discharge characteristics and promote favourable surface alloying. The impact of powder type, concentration, and dielectric flow rate is examined in detail to understand their role in enhancing surface quality, reducing surface defects such as cracking, heat affected zones etc., and introducing desired elemental composition into the …

Optimal Energy Management for Hydrogen and Electric Based Integration Based on Machine Learning and Demand Response Using Multi Objective Optimization Algorithm
abstract: ABSTRACT The coordination between hydrogen and electricity within interconnected multi‐microgrids is challenging due to time‐varying renewable generation, electrical and hydrogen demand, and V2G availability, along with satisfying constraints associated with storage, network, market, and demand response across day‐ahead and intraday operation. This study introduces an integrated hydrogen electric multi‐microgrid energy management system based on RNN–LSTM forecasting, day‐ahead‐to‐intraday scheduling, incentive‐based demand response, and bi‐objective NSGA‐II optimization. The proposed framework is implemented on the IEEE 33‐bus radial distribution network with four interconnected microgrids incorporating PV and wind generation, BESS, EV/V2G, electrolyzers, hydrogen storage, an external hydrogen market, and hydrogen fueled vehicles. Five different scheduling scenarios are investigated to analyze the effect of using updated intraday information, DA‐to‐ID corrective scheduling, demand response, and hydrogen market participation. The proposed RNN–LSTM forecasting technique achieves R 2 values of 0.9765, 0.9623, 0.9590, 0.9830, and 0.9189 for hydrogen demand, V2G, PV generation, electrical demand, and wind generation, respectively. For the proposed Scenario S4, the knee‐point solution leads to an operating cost of 60,892.55 USD/day and 113,099.60 kg/day of grid‐related CO 2 emissions…

Equal-capacitance field-moment analysis of electric-field nonuniformity in high-aspect-ratio metal–insulator–metal capacitors
abstract: Abstract Atomic layer deposition (ALD) provides conformal dielectric coatings for three-dimensional metal–insulator–metal capacitors, yet thickness variations in high-aspect-ratio features can produce localized electric-field enhancement even at the same overall capacitance. Here, we introduce an equal-capacitance field-moment framework that isolates the effect of dielectric-profile shape from the mean inverse thickness. Each nonuniform profile is compared with a uniform dielectric having the same capacitance, and the residual field nonuniformity is quantified by a p -root field-moment factor, R p , which increasingly weights thin regions through a geometric description of the field distribution. The framework is evaluated computationally using 11 archived measured Al 2 O 3 thickness profiles and 101 open ALD transport simulations. Nested leave-one-process-family-out validation shows that normalized penetration depth alone reconstructs R 8 with an RMSE of 1.809, whereas including bottom coverage and transition-front slope reduces the RMSE to 0.279, with improvement in all eight held-out process families. When penetration depth, capacitance factor, and bottom coverage are matched within 5%, the largest R 8 ratio between nonduplicate profiles is 1.015. Relaxing the bottom-coverage tolerance to 10% while retaining the other two matching tolerances at 5% yields a selected maximum r…

title: An Electric‐Eel‐Inspired Hydrogel Power Source with Photothermally Assisted Ion‐Gradient Recovery
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogel‐based power sources represent a promising strategy for powering flexible electronic devices. However, most existing electric‐eel‐inspired hydrogel power sources remain constrained by the intrinsic limitations of hydrogel systems, particularly the difficulty of restoring ionic gradients after discharge. By contrast, electric eels can re‐establish transmembrane ionic gradients after discharge through ion‐pump‐mediated transport. To address this limitation of existing devices, a dual‐ion concentration gradient and a single‐walled carbon nanotube‐graphene hybrid network are integrated into a bilayer hydrogel power source (BHPS). Compared with most previously reported hydrogel power sources, BHPS delivers a higher power output and, after prolonged discharge, enables partial reconstruction of the ion gradient under light irradiation. A single BHPS delivers an open‐circuit voltage of 1.75 V and a short‐circuit current density of 2.34 mA·cm −2 , while maintaining stable operation under short‐term equilibrated temperature and humidity conditions. Notably, upon scalable integration, the BHPS can generate up to 134 V while retaining good mechanical stability. This study reports an electric eel‐inspired hydrogel power source that can reconstruct its ionic gradient after discharge, offering a new strategy for advancing the functional design and optimization of hydrogel‐bas…

title: Multi‐Energy Coupling in Hierarchical Textiles for Photo‐Thermal‐Electric Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Solar interfacial evaporation and thermoelectric generation coupled systems show promising application potential in seawater desalination and energy harvesting. However, a portion of the heat generated by photothermal conversion is used for interfacial evaporation, while the remaining heat continuously dissipates to the thermoelectric generator (TEG) module and the surrounding environment. Without proper regulation, such disordered heat dissipation not only reduces the evaporation heat utilization efficiency but also weakens the temperature difference driving force of TEG, thereby limiting the simultaneous enhancement of water‐power cogeneration. In this study, a sandwich evaporator (SE) system is proposed based on solar absorption pathway optimization and hierarchical heat flow regulation. A polypyrrole photothermal layer is in situ constructed on cotton, and a V‐shaped structure is employed to enhance solar harvesting, achieving efficient photothermal conversion. An independent water supply layer is introduced to suppress ineffective heat conduction. Meanwhile, a water‐cooling layer is integrated at the cold sink of TEG, enabling synergistic cooling and waste heat evaporation. Finally, SE achieves an evaporation rate of 2.18 kg·m −2 ·h −1 and a peak power density of 224.15 mW·m −2 under 1 kW·m −2 solar radiation. This system demonstrates good energy conversion perfor…

title: A gradient multi-isocenter VMAT strategy for efficient craniospinal irradiation on an intelligent couch-shifting accelerator
abstract: Abstract Delivering high-quality craniospinal irradiation (CSI) remains challenging because of the need to achieve adequate target coverage across ultra-extended volumes while minimizing dose to normal tissue and maintaining clinically practical treatment efficiency. Although helical tomotherapy (HT) provides excellent dose conformity for CSI, prolonged delivery time and increased low-dose exposure may limit its clinical applicability. This study aimed to investigate whether increasing the number of isocenters in a gradient multi-isocenter volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) strategy could enhance modulation capability for extended target volumes and provide a clinically feasible alternative to HT. Sixteen patients who received CSI at The Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University between January 2022 and March 2026 were retrospectively selected. For each patient, two VMAT strategies using an intelligent couch-shifting accelerator (TaiChiPro) were generated: a conventional multi-isocenter configuration (Group A) and an increased-isocenter configuration (Group B). HT plans delivered on a Radixact™ system were generated as reference plans (Group C). Dosimetric parameters of the planning target volume (PTV), organs at risk (OARs), low-dose exposure of normal tissue, monitor units (MU), delivery time, and patient-specific quality assurance results were evaluated. title: Board NGO Experience and Corporate ESG Performance: The Moderating Role of Organizational Psychological Capital
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between directors with non‐governmental organization (NGO) experience and firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, as well as the moderating role of organizational psychological capital (OPC). Using 1659 firm‐year observations from UK FTSE 350 companies between 2012 and 2021, we combine manually collected board data with natural language processing to measure OPC from annual‐report narratives. The results show that NGO‐experienced director representation is positively associated with ESG performance, particularly its environmental and social dimensions. We find limited evidence suggesting that OPC may strengthen the positive association between NGO‐experienced director representation and ESG performance. The study extends emerging research on NGO‐experienced directors by examining overall ESG performance and identifying OPC as a complementary organizational resource that may condition this association. The findings contribute to corporate governance, sustainability, and organizational psychology research and offer implications for boards, investors, and policymakers.

title: SAE-MOGWO-PRS: A probability ranking strategy-based grey wolf optimizer for spatio-temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization
abstract: The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogeneity in evaluation times. Instead, they perform high-fidelity evaluations on all objectives for promising population positions identified by their associated surrogate-assisted optimization algorithms in the solution space. While this approach provides complete and error-free solution evaluations, it does not yield the most computationally efficient procedure. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Surrogate-assisted Evolutionary Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer with Probabilistic Ranking Strategy (SAE-MOGWO-PRS). This algorithm is designed to determine which individuals and objective functions within the population should undergo high-fidelity evaluation, thereby enhancing their ability to generate non-dominated solutions with improved convergence and diversity in the Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer. To validate the efficacy of the proposed SAE-MOGWO-PRS algorithm, we compared it against four state-of-the-art surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization algorithms, including those that specifically handle heterogeneous evaluation times. The comparative analysis on four test problems demonstrates the superior performance of t…

title: Combined use of prostate-specific antigen density and PI-RADS score to optimize prostate biopsy strategy
abstract: Introduction: We aimed to compare detection rates of prostate cancer (PCa) and clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) between MRI-targeted and transrectal ultrasound (TRUS)-guided systematic transrectal biopsy, and to evaluate prostate-specific antigen (PSA) density (PSAD) as a tool to refine biopsy strategies and reduce unnecessary systematic biopsies. Materials and methods: We retrospectively reviewed 630 biopsy-naïve men who underwent combined MRI-targeted and systematic prostate biopsy in 2023. The mean age was 67.5 years, mean PSA was 6.69 ng/mL, and mean prostate volume was 48.4 cm 3 . Patients were stratified into four PSAD categories: <0.10, 0.10–<0.15, 0.15–<0.20, and ≥0.20 ng/mL/cm 3 . Cancer detection rates were assessed according to biopsy modality, Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) score, and PSAD. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify predictors of csPCa. Results: Overall, PCa was detected in 78.1% (492/630) of patients, of whom 87.0% (428/492) had csPCa. Increasing PSAD was associated with csPCa and a greater number of positive biopsy cores ( p < 0.001). In the multivariable analysis, PSAD remained an independent predictor of csPCa (odds ratio [OR] 3.87, p < 0.001). PI-RADS score was also independently associated with higher-grade disease. PSAD was significantly correlated with PI-RADS score. Among men wit…

title: Molecularly Programmed Stress Dissipation Strategy for Ultrastretchable Neuromorphic Electronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsically stretchable organic synaptic transistors (ISOSTs) using semiconducting polymers (SPs) hold promise for on‐body signal processing by mimicking biological synaptic functions and processing temporal bio‐signals directly at or near the point of data acquisition. However, conventional SPs designed primarily to increase polymer softness and mechanical compliance often lack molecular‐level mechanisms for effective stress dissipation, thereby limiting device‐level stretchability to below 100% and causing substantial degradation in electrical performance. Here, we demonstrate ISOSTs achieving 150% device‐level stretchability through molecularly programmed stress dissipation (MPSD) of an SP without incorporating soft segments into the backbone. This strategy promotes conformational flexibility and suppresses side‐chain interdigitation, enhancing chain dynamics and amplifying mechanical contrast between crystalline and amorphous domains. This facilitates localized stress accommodation and induces the formation of nano‐to‐micro scale crack clusters, termed artificial stretch marks (ASMs), which emulate the adaptive mechanical behavior of human skin. Leveraging this mechanism, ISOSTs maintain 83.8% of maximum current even under 150% strain while preserving synaptic behaviors. Furthermore, physical reservoir computing using the ISOSTs preserves electromyography classif…

title: OsMED25-OsWRI1 Fine-Tunes Fatty Acid Biosynthesis: A Key Strategy via Intron Retention
abstract: Abstract In rice grains, the mechanisms governing fatty acid biosynthesis remain largely elusive. Although WRINKLED1 (WRI1) is well established as a core transcription factor activating fatty acid biosynthesis under multi-level regulation, its post-transcriptional regulation has been scarcely explored. Here, we demonstrate that OsWRI1 transcripts undergo alternative splicing (AS) via intron retention (IR), producing two functionally distinct splice variants: OsWRI1α and OsWRI1β. OsWRI1α encodes a canonical protein containing two AP2 domains, whereas OsWRI1β produces a truncated protein due to a premature termination codon. Genetic analyses confirm that OsWRI1α functions as a positive regulator of fatty acid biosynthesis, while OsWRI1β exerts an inhibitory effect by directly interacting with OsWRI1α, disrupting its dimerization, and preventing activation of downstream target genes including OsACP1 and OsFAD2. We further identify OsMED25 as a critical regulator of this AS event. OsMED25 is recruited to a 360-bp intronic region of OsWRI1 that corresponds precisely to the retained intron in OsWRI1β, where it recruits the splicing factor OsPTB4 to promote intron retention, thereby repressing fatty acid biosynthesis. The induction of OsWRI1β expression by jasmonic acid (JA) signaling, which we identify as a suppressor of fatty acid biosynthesis, is strictly dependent on OsMED25. Mech…

title: Research on a Dual-Key-Peg Progressive Constraint Strategy Based on Force-Sensing Variable Admittance Control
abstract: Rigid multi-peg-in-hole assembly is prone to contact coupling, uncertain contact sequences, and jamming under small clearances. This study proposes a dual-key-peg progressive constraint strategy integrated with the proposed variable-damping admittance controller. Two key pegs are selected from a convex-hull supporting edge, and two-stage active tilting prescribes a contact sequence under the stated geometric conditions. Spiral search, reverse orientation recovery, and periodic sweeping progressively establish the two key-peg constraints. Throughout assembly, six-axis force/torque feedback drives a contact-risk index based on incremental lateral force and moment, contact growth, and a regularized moment-to-force descriptor. This risk measure continuously regulates lateral translational and tilting rotational damping, enabling low damping for sensitive search under mild contact and increased damping for suppressing excessive compliant motion under high-risk interaction. For constant virtual inertia and positive bounded damping, energy analysis establishes passivity and dissipation of the continuous-time admittance correction channel. Across uniform and non-uniform four-peg and six-peg configurations, assembly success rates were 93.3–96.7%.

title: El aprendizaje cooperativo como estrategia para fortalecer las habilidades sociales en Educación Física
abstract: La investigación analizó el aprendizaje cooperativo como estrategia pedagógica para fortalecer las habilidades sociales en Educación Física, mediante una revisión narrativa de literatura científica con enfoque cualitativo y alcance descriptivo-analítico, correspondiente al período 2020–2026. El corpus documental estuvo constituido por 15 publicaciones científicas relacionadas con el aprendizaje cooperativo, las relaciones interpersonales, el desarrollo socioemocional y las estrategias pedagógicas en Educación Física. Los documentos se contrastaron en tres ejes: fundamentos e implementación del aprendizaje cooperativo; habilidades sociales, desarrollo socioemocional y estrategias pedagógicas; y evidencia científica sobre resultados educativos. Las publicaciones comprendieron investigaciones empíricas, propuestas pedagógicas, revisiones sistemáticas y un metaanálisis, cuyos enfoques metodológicos y contextos educativos se analizaron de manera diferenciada. En general, los hallazgos destacaron las posibilidades del aprendizaje cooperativo para favorecer la comunicación, la empatía, el respeto, la responsabilidad compartida, la participación y las relaciones interpersonales positivas. Sin embargo, los resultados variaron según las características de las intervenciones, las poblaciones estudiadas y los procedimientos de evaluación. An Augmented Lagrangian Lyrebird Optimization for UPQC-based optimal power flow in wind-integrated power systems
abstract: The large-scale integration of wind energy into modern power systems introduces operational uncertainties, voltage instability, and power quality degradation due to the intermittent nature of wind speed variations. This paper proposes a Power Quality-Constrained Optimal Power Flow (PQ-OPF) framework for wind-integrated power systems using the Augmented Lagrangian Lyrebird Optimization Algorithm (AL-LOA). A probabilistic wind generation model based on the Weibull distribution is employed to capture stochastic wind behavior, and the wind turbine output is modeled using a piecewise nonlinear power curve. The formulated PQ-OPF problem incorporates voltage deviation, reactive power limits, line flow constraints, and total harmonic distortion (THD) as power quality constraints. The Augmented Lagrangian method effectively handles equality and inequality constraints, while the Lyrebird Optimization algorithm enhances global search capability and convergence robustness in nonlinear and non-convex solution spaces. To further improve system performance, a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) is optimally installed at a critical bus identified based on voltage and harmonic analysis. The proposed method is validated on the IEEE 57-bus test system under varying wind penetration levels (20%–50%). Simulation results show that the proposed AL-LOA-based PQ-OPF achieves up to 14.6% reduction …

title: Topology-Aware Feasibility Assessment and Coordinated Setting of Transformer Primary and Backup Protection in Islanded Renewable Power Systems
abstract: Islanded microgrid topology and converter current limiting can alter transformer protection currents. We formulate primary and backup coordination as a topology-indexed feasible domain. A bridge test identifies source contributions that cross the protected transformer, and a joint model tests differential sensitivity and stability, overcurrent pickup and timing, load security, and device limits. At the selected inputs, four supported bridge states in an eight-entry reference library retain non-empty domains. The weak-GFL case has a narrow backup–pickup interval (0.984–1.042 pu), and its feasibility classification changes across the tested lower-current factors; the high-load case remains empty (1.860 pu load-security lower bound versus 1.326 pu sensitivity upper bound). A seven-bus reference EMT study includes 112 baseline cases, a 1232-case direction/location/resistance scan, and a 288-case coupled-controller scan. The CT stress screen reduces the all-source reference-domain volume from 0.08391 to 0.07059. All numerical results use the declared reference-network and device inputs.

Retail Fuel Sales in a Regulatory Grey Area: Consumer Protection and Civil Liability Perspectives
abstract: Retail fuel sales have evolved into a form of informal energy distribution, driven by the limited reach of Indonesia’s formal fuel distribution system. Despite its growing role in supporting community mobility and microeconomic activities, the practice simultaneously raises legal concerns regarding consumer protection, public safety, and civil liability. This study aims to examine the characteristics of civil legal relations arising from retail fuel sales practices, the implications of the absence of regional regulations on the liability of business actors, and the urgency of developing a more adaptive risk-based regulatory framework. The research employs a normative juridical method strengthened by contextual empirical analysis through statutory, doctrinal, and conceptual approaches related to consumer protection, tort law, and risk-based regulation. The findings show that retail fuel sales create a high-risk private legal relationship because the transaction involves flammable substances distributed without adequate safety standards, metrological supervision, or operational safeguards. The absence of regional regulations has resulted in unclear standards of care, disproportionate allocation of legal risks, and weakened legal protection for both consumers and micro-scale business actors. title: Performance Comparison of Artificial Neural Networks and Hedonic Pricing model in Predicting Residential Property prices in Lagos Metropolis, Nigeria
abstract: The search for techniques that can achieve better valuation estimates is a global issue, while much research has been done in the advanced countries, only a few researches are known to have been done in the area of adopting the advanced techniques in predicting property prices in Nigeria. The current paper compares the performance of the hedonic pricing model (HPM) and artificial neural networks (ANN) models in predicting the prices of residential properties in Lagos metropolis, Nigeria. Residential property prices and data for the variables affecting property prices were obtained from the databases of 53 firms of practicing Estate Surveyors and Valuers in the study area. A total of 3,079 datasets, encompassing property, neighborhood, and environmental-based features were gathered and employed in the research along with 19 explanatory factors. The entire dataset was split into training and testing at a ratio of 80% and 20% respectively to assess the prediction ability of the ANN and HPM. For both models, the performance evaluation metrics of R-squares, mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and root mean square error (RMSE) were computed and then compared. ANN model outperformed HPM model in predicting residential property prices in the Lagos metropolitan residential property market. The outcome of the research provides decision inputs for policymaker…

title: Beyond Patents: External R&D Conditions, Organisational Capabilities, and Technical Efficiency in Agri‐Food Firms
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether the external R&D environment is associated with the technical efficiency of agri‐food firms and whether this relationship differs between patenting and non‐patenting enterprises. Using 1668 observations for 243 firms over 2004–2021, including 27 patenting and 216 non‐patenting firms, with substantially broader coverage from 2012 onwards, the analysis applies conditional data envelopment analysis (DEA), complemented by firm fixed‐effects regressions and a Simar–Wilson bootstrapped truncated regression. Comparing conditional and unconditional frontiers shows that external R&D conditions alter firms' positions relative to the production frontier. The preferred fixed‐effects specification finds no robust differential association by patenting status after controlling for persistent firm heterogeneity and year shocks. The complementary Simar–Wilson analysis suggests a stronger association among non‐patenting firms and no significant association among patenting firms, consistent with a possible compensatory role of external R&D conditions. These associations are non‐causal and highlight the organisational relevance of external knowledge and innovation ecosystems.

title: Macromolecular Oxidative–Coupling Strategy for Colorimetric Determination of Tadalafil in Pharmaceutical Formulations
abstract: ABSTRACT A simple and sensitive colorimetric method has been developed for the determination of tadalafil based on a macromolecular oxidative–coupling reaction. In the first step, tadalafil was oxidized using potassium permanganate (KMnO 4 ) as an oxidizing reagent; this was followed by a coupling with a crystal violet dye, which resulted in a blue solution with the highest absorption at the wavelength 590 nm in a basic medium. The factors affecting the reaction have been studied; they included: type and volume of oxidation agent, dye type and volume, base's type and volume, oxidation time, addition sequence, temperature, and coupling time. The best conditions were reached for the formation of the colored complex. The method showed a good linearity within a concentration range between 45 and 50 µg/mL with a determination coefficient ( R 2 ) = 0.9995, while Sandell's index reached 0.163934 µg/cm 2 and molar absorptivity was 2375.34 L/mol/cm. The limit of detection was also determined to be 0.3825 µg/mL, and the limit of quantification was 1.1591 µg/mL. As for accuracy, the recovery percentages (Rec%) ranged between 96.72% and 102.87%, while the values of relative standard deviation (RSD%) ranged between 0.2808 and 0.0923, confirming that this method is of high sensitivity and accuracy and was successfully applied for the determination of tadalafil within its pharmaceutical formu…

title: Studies Using the Multiphase Optimization Strategy in Digital Mental Health: Scoping Review
abstract: Abstract Background Improving the cost-effectiveness and scalability of mental health interventions remains challenging. The Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) framework provides a structured approach for developing, optimizing, and evaluating behavioral interventions by balancing effectiveness with efficiency, economy, and scalability. It does so across 3 phases: preparation (theoretical grounding and component selection), optimization (experimental testing), and evaluation (confirmatory trial). Digital mental health interventions are especially suited to this modular approach, as they enable researchers to easily manipulate components and personalize delivery. Objective This study aims to examine how the MOST framework has been applied in the digital mental health field and to provide recommendations for future application. Methods Systematic searches were conducted in Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, PsycInfo, and PubMed. Papers were included if they used the MOST to develop or optimize a digitally delivered mental health intervention. Studies targeting children aged under 12 years, reviews, and theoretical or simulated applications were excluded. Results Thirty-seven papers representing 18 research projects met the inclusion criteria. The preparation phase was often incomplete and inconsistently reported, with optimization criteria largely absent and conceptual models o…

Decoupling Polarization From Loss: A Synergistic Strategy for High‐Efficiency Electrocaloric Cooling
abstract: ABSTRACT The electrocaloric effect is promising for solid‐state cooling, but leakage currents in ferroelectric ceramics cause parasitic Joule heating that obscures intrinsic cooling under high fields. We address this in Pb(Ni 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3– PbTiO 3 near the morphotropic phase boundary via Mn acceptor doping, which suppresses defect‐mediated conduction and the associated Joule heating while retaining large field‐induced polarization. XPS and EPR analyses indicate reduced Ti 3+ and oxygen‐vacancy‐related defect contributions after Mn incorporation. The resulting suppression of leakage current leads to a marked increase in the activation energy for d.c. transport and substantially reduces baseline drift in direct calorimetry, confirming an intrinsic thermal response. Translating this materials‐level improvement to a device‐relevant architecture, we demonstrate that Mn‐doped PNN‐PT multilayer ceramics can sustain exceptionally high operating fields. This yields a Δ T = 3 K at 150 kV cm −1 , critically, a broad operational plateau with Δ T > 2.5 K across a 60°C temperature span (60°C–120°C), while also providing peak cooling capacity and wide thermal robustness. Enhanced performance arises from coexisting rhombohedral and tetragonal nanodomains, flattening the free‐energy landscape and facilitating polarization rotation. title: Reliability-Aware Adaptive Split Federated Learning with Uncertainty-Guided Personalization for Non-IID ECG Classification in IoMT Networks
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) enables distributed electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring, but statistical and resource heterogeneity complicates collaborative learning. This study proposes Reliability-Aware Adaptive Split Federated Learning (RA-ASFL) for non-independent and non-identically distributed (non-IID) ECG classification. The framework integrates three mechanisms: adaptive split selection based on resource constraints, privacy exposure risk, predictive uncertainty, and split-conditioned reliability; reliability-aware aggregation using client-level learning quality and stability to determine separate contribution weights; and uncertainty-guided global–local personalization. These mechanisms distinguish computation placement, client reliability estimation, and aggregation influence. Experiments used five-class MIT-BIH heartbeat classification and five-superclass multilabel PTB-XL classification under simulated heterogeneous IoMT conditions. On MIT-BIH, RA-ASFL achieved 98.03% accuracy, 97.93% F1-score, and 99.43% ROC-AUC, exceeding resource-only AdaptSFL by 0.55 and 0.58 percentage points in accuracy and F1-score, respectively. On PTB-XL, macro AUROC reached 94.3% and macro F1-score reached 74.6%, compared with 92.8% and 72.3% for AdaptSFL. Ablation results identified reliability-aware aggregation and personalization as the principal contributors to predictive perfor…

title: GLOBAL ECONOMIC UNCERTAINTY AND GEORGIA
abstract: Global economic uncertainty is a major challenge facing the contemporary world economy. Geopolitical tensions, shifts in international trade, inflationary pressures, and financial market volatility have particularly significant implications for small and open economies. This study examines the key drivers of global economic uncertainty and analyses their impact on Georgia’s economic development, with particular emphasis on foreign trade, foreign investment, tourism, and macroeconomic sustainability. The research draws on secondary data and academic literature using qualitative, descriptive, and comparative methods. The findings identify risks associated with the Georgian economy’s dependence on external factors, as well as opportunities to strengthen its economic resilience. The study emphasizes economic diversification, developing domestic production and exports, improving the investment climate, and preserving macroeconomic stability.

title: Does Trade Uncertainty Shake Sustainability? Insights From the ESG ‐Based Sustainability Uncertainty Index ( ESGUI ) Using Wavelet Tools
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the scale‐dependent association between trade policy uncertainty (TPU) and ESG‐based sustainability uncertainty (ESGUI) at the global, US, and China levels. Monthly data from November 2002 to June 2025 are analyzed with continuous, multiple, and partial wavelet methods, while the CASS Shipments Index captures freight activity. The results reveal heterogeneous conditional coherence rather than a uniform crisis effect: the global, US, and China panels display different timing and persistence patterns. In lag‐only models that control for global economic policy uncertainty, market volatility, geopolitical risk, freight activity, and crisis episodes, lagged TPU remains jointly associated with global ESGUI but not China ESGUI. Baltic Dry Index substitution and wavelet‐specification checks preserve the broad time–frequency structure. The evidence supports a conditional and temporally ordered association, not causal transmission. The study clarifies the distinct constructs, tests common‐shock explanations, and identifies institutionally heterogeneous sustainability‐risk horizons.

title: Beyond Quit Intention: Implicit–Explicit Attitude Profiles, Uncertainty Stress, and Stage-Based Smoking Cessation Status Among Chinese Young Adult Smokers
abstract: Background: Smoking behaviour change is commonly conceptualized as a stage-based process, yet stage-based cessation status, quit intention, and cessation action may be associated with psychological factors beyond self-reported motivation. Dual-attitude theory suggests that implicit and explicit attitudes may jointly relate to smoking behaviour, while uncertainty stress may further influence these associations. This study examined the associations of implicit–explicit attitude profiles with smoking behaviour change and the moderating role of uncertainty stress among young adult smokers. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of 292 Chinese smokers aged 18–35 years from a source sample of 659 adult smokers. Participants were classified into four implicit–explicit attitude profiles based on SC-IAT and self-reported attitudes. Ordered and binary logistic regression models examined associations of attitude profiles with stage-based cessation status, quit intention, and cessation action, adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics. Uncertainty stress was examined as a moderator. Results: Compared with the consistent positive profile, the consistent negative profile was associated with higher odds of being at a later stage of behaviour change (OR = 6.02, 95% CI 2.78–13.03), having quit intention (OR = 5.27, 95% CI 2.08–13.31), and reporting cessation action (OR …

title: Continuous-Time Hidden Markov Modeling for Remaining Service Life Estimation of Building Elements Under Inspection Uncertainty
abstract: Service life estimates derived from inspections depend on both deterioration dynamics and the accuracy of condition assessments. This study develops a continuous-time hidden Markov framework for estimating the remaining service life of building elements from sparse inspection histories. A sequential deterioration model describes progression towards a poor condition threshold requiring major intervention, rather than structural collapse. The framework is implemented in MATLAB 2026a and applied to records of 25 elements from two inspection campaigns. Transition intensities and initial state probabilities are estimated by maximum likelihood for fixed scenarios of inspection error. Posterior condition probabilities are then used to calculate remaining life distributions and survival measures. Sampling variability is assessed by complete weighted enumeration of a stratified bootstrap, while optimization from multiple starting points checks numerical reproducibility. Inspection histories produce different life estimates for elements with identical latest ratings, although the hidden model does not improve data fit over the observable continuous time benchmark. Broad uncertainty in estimated life measures persists despite reproducible optimization, indicating that limited inspection information remains a major constraint within the adopted model. The framework provides a transparent l…

title: Shield or Bottleneck? Navigating ESG Sustainability Uncertainty in Global Supply Chains: Asymmetric Evidence From Developed and Developing Economies
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the dynamic impact of the ESG‐Based Sustainability Uncertainty Index (ESGUI) on the Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (GSCPI) across five developed (USA, Germany, France, Japan, UK) and five developing economies (China, India, Brazil, Mexico, Vietnam) using monthly data from November 2002 to June 2025. To capture multi‐horizon nonlinearities and tail dependence across distribution quantiles at the individual country level, and to empirically evaluate group‐level structural heterogeneity across economic cohorts, we employ Wavelet Kernel‐Based Regularized Least Squares (WKRLS), complemented by Wavelet Quantile Regression (WQR) and Wavelet Quantile Granger Causality (WQGC), Panel Quantile Regression (PQR) with multiple breaks as complementary dual‐verification procedures. Empirical findings reveal a fundamental macro‐structural asymmetry: in developed nations, heightened sustainability uncertainty acts as a structural “bottleneck”, exhibiting a significant positive long‐term impact on supply chain pressures due to rigid compliance burdens and accumulated regulatory costs. Conversely, developing economies turn this uncertainty into an adaptive “shield”, displaying a dominant negative relationship as agile supplier diversification and nearshoring realignment alleviate logistical friction within sustainable supply chain management (SSCM). title: Pemasaran Terintegrasi Melalui Saluran Multi-Channel untuk Meningkatkan Visibilitas dan Penjualan UMKM Melalui Aplikasi SIPOPU
abstract: This community service program is designed to develop the economic potential of product owners in Desa Mekarsari, Tanjung Lago, Banyuasin. Considering the product potential of SMEs involved in the community service program, these products represent valuable assets that can be further developed and marketed to a wider market. Training on the use of the SIPOPU sales application is expected to increase the visibility of SMEs products in Desa Mekarsari and ultimately improve their sales performance. SIPOPU is a digital system that facilitates SMEs in marketing their products beyond geographical boundaries, as this platform is accessible to SMEs throughout Indonesia and by various stakeholders. Therefore, training on the effective use of the SIPOPU application is crucial to maximize the sales potential of local products in a more organized, efficient, and reliable manner.

title: Campaña de educación financiera para fortalecer la gestión de actividades emprendedoras en el entorno social de estudiantes de Economía en línea
abstract: El estudio analiza la contribución de una campaña de educación financiera al fortalecimiento de la gestión de actividades emprendedoras en el entorno social de estudiantes de la carrera de Economía en línea. El objetivo fue examinar las variaciones en las prácticas de planificación financiera, registro contable, control del flujo de caja y toma de decisiones económicas, mediante un procedimiento de modelación cuantitativa. Se adoptó un enfoque cuantitativo, con estructura longitudinal y diseño preexperimental de un solo grupo, bajo un esquema de medición antes y después. Se estableció un escenario de análisis de 60 personas emprendedoras vinculadas al entorno social de los estudiantes. La intervención formativa comprendió 160 horas distribuidas en seis módulos relacionados con elaboración de presupuestos, separación de finanzas personales y empresariales, registro de operaciones, identificación de costos, fijación de precios, administración del flujo de caja y uso responsable del crédito. La evaluación consideró una escala de cinco puntos y pruebas t de Student para muestras relacionadas. En el escenario de modelación, la puntuación global pasó de 2,54 (DE = 0,43) a 3,53 (DE = 0,62), con una diferencia media de 0,99 puntos, t(59) = 17,13, p < 0,001. title: Privacy-Preserving Intelligent Financial Information Processing in Cloud-Edge Distributed Systems Based on Homomorphic Encryption and MapReduce
abstract: Privacy-preserving financial big-data processing must simultaneously control plaintext exposure and the computational cost of distributed analytics. This paper proposes a cloud-edge MapReduce-ECC framework in which edge terminals perform local validation, sharding, feature fusion, and ciphertext generation, while cloud Reduce nodes aggregate only matched protected shards and HDFS stores encrypted blocks with rack-aware replication. The design clarifies key separation, ciphertext matching, fault recovery, and compliance-oriented data-localization rules. Experiments on a 5.5-TB operational e-commerce financial dataset show that 42 Map nodes provide the best observed parallel-processing trade-off. The HDFS deployment maintains storage-task completion and post-storage availability close to 100%, while the stated trust-boundary design prevents plaintext financial shards from being transmitted to ordinary cloud workers. These results indicate that the framework provides a scalable privacy-oriented processing pipeline for distributed financial information systems.

Algorithmic Advantage: How Artificial Intelligence (AI) Shapes Audit Firms Performance in Ghana
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming auditing process and methodology by shifting the profession from retrospective sampling to continuous, population-wide assurance and predictive risk management. But little is known about how this technology affects audit firms’ overall performance in emerging economies. This research aims to address these issues by exploring the impact of AI adoption in auditing on performance and the extent to which organizational agility mediates this influence, while organizational culture and learning moderate it. The study collected responses from 226 audit professionals at Big Four audit firms in Ghana through surveys and computer-assisted web interviews using a purposive sampling strategy. The data was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) 4.11.8 in SmartPLS. The findings indicate that AI adoption improves organizational performance and agility. Organizational agility had a positive and significant impact on organizational performance and partially mediated the relationship between AI adoption and organizational performance. Organizational culture had a significant positive moderating impact on the relationship between AI adoption and organizational performance and between AI adoption and organizational agility. title: Securing Medical WSN: A Comprehensive Approach to Data Transmission in the Healthcare Landscape
abstract: The term WSN has been in use in the realms of transdisciplinary research. A novel the concept of a method to collect and store heterogeneous and patient-sensitive medical data is a way to go. medical wireless sensor net. The aim of this paper will be to present a secure transmission approach to the data gathering in the Medical WSN (M-WSN). This is done in three steps. technique: symmetric key generation, discontinuous multi-path transmission and user authentication. The first stage of the system is to install a gateway that would give access to the cloud data servers. The second step is to create the secret keys which make the message random. Data fragmentation and uploading to the server constitutes the third step. The evaluation was done on the basis of opinion that the proposed standard is useful in reducing response time and delay in case of medical information is being posted up and downloaded on the server.

title: Financial Planning Behaviour and Loan Dependency among Newly Appointed Government Employees in Uttar Pradesh
abstract: Purpose: Financial planning is very important for ensuring financial stability as well as minimizing the dependence on loans, especially in the initial years of their job. Financial planning becomes imperative when government employees newly join their service as there are many financial obligations that they have to fulfil. The main objective of this research study is to evaluate the financial planning behaviour of newly appointed government employees of Uttar Pradesh and its impact on loan dependency. Methodology: In the analysis of the study, quantitative, descriptive and analytical research approach has been used. The primary data was collected from 178 newly recruited government employees in the state of Uttar Pradesh by making use of a structured questionnaire based on the five-point Likert scale. Convenience sampling technique was used for selecting the respondents for the study. The gathered data were analysed using IBM SPSS. Findings: The study results show that demographic factors like gender, age, education, and monthly income have a major impact on financial planning behaviour. The study further shows that there is a significant inverse relationship between financial planning behaviour and reliance on loans, which means that financially well-planned employees tend to rely less on loans. The Right to Take Rights Away: Brazil’s 1964 & 2016 Coups
abstract: Leigh Payne’s right-against-rights framework describes deliberate tactics employed by the Right Wing to undermine, attack, and destroy democracy in defence of the status quo. Working under the assertion that both Brazil’s 1964 military coup and 2016 presidential impeachment were coups perpetrated by the Right Wing, this investigation serves to connect both events via this singular framework to demonstrate how they were both specifically “right-against-rights coups,” analyse the fragility of Brazilian democracy in the face of the Right Wing, and discern the future of Brazil’s democracy.

Vertex-based Curvilinear OPC via Bezier Curves
abstract: Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) is a critical step in semiconductor manufacturing, as it mitigates lithographic distortions and improves the pattern transfer fidelity from masks to silicon wafers. With the adoption of multi-beam mask writers, mask geometries are evolving from traditional Manhattan shapes to curvilinear patterns, offering improved resolution and process robustness. However, existing curvilinear OPC methods still suffer from limited optimization efficiency and accuracy, largely due to the difficulty of contour parameterization. To address this issue, we propose a gradient-based framework for vertex-based curvilinear OPC, where the mask is represented by connected Bézier curve segments controlled by trainable vertices, and the resulting rasterized mask is optimized to reduce lithographic errors. We evaluate the proposed method on the industry-standard dataset. Experimental results show that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on L 2 , PVBand, and VPE, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed gradient-based curvilinear optimization framework.

title: A pilot classroom intervention using project-based learning for steel framing design in a civil engineering course
abstract: Project-based learning in Civil Engineering can connect structural modelling, standards application, and technical communication through an authentic design task. This descriptive educational case study documents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a semester-long steel-framing redesign project. It examines what its collective output reveals about the traceability of calculations and collective assessment. Twenty-five seventh-semester students worked in five groups for approximately 16 weeks and consolidated their contributions into a single redesign project. The activity combined interpreting reference documents, structural configuration, modelling in SAP2000, verification against regulations, preparing drawings, receiving tutor feedback, and preparing the calculation report. The lecturer assessed the integrated project using a weighted rubric comprising eight criteria. The project achieved a total score of 85 per cent, with 100 per cent for structural configuration, application of standards, and presentation, but 60 per cent for the calculation report. The technical results characterised the collective output and, together with the rubric, enabled a distinction between the project's computational execution and the traceability of the documented calculations. The case study identifies calculation traceability and the limitations of collective assessment as teaching i…

title: Computational Design and In Silico Evaluation of Novel Cannabinoids Targeting the CB2 Receptor: Chemical Reactivity, Binding Mode, and Predicted ADMET Profile
abstract: The CB2 cannabinoid receptor represents an attractive therapeutic target due to its immunomodulatory relevance and its lack of psychoactive effects. Here, we applied an integrated in silico approach to design and prioritize JWH‐015–derived ligands with improved CB2 affinity and pharmacokinetic properties. Density functional theory calculations (PBE/TZVP/GEN‐A2*) provided global and local reactivity descriptors that were correlated with predicted binding interactions obtained from a consensus docking strategy (AutoDock4, Vina, and Smina). Structural stability and interaction persistence were further assessed by nine 500‐ns molecular dynamics simulations. Among the designed structures, analog 9 exhibited the most persistent and favorable interactions with key CB2 residues throughout the simulations, supporting its suitability as a lead candidate. In contrast, analogs 12 and 20 displayed notably safer biosafety profiles, indicating value as alternative scaffolds for further chemical exploration. These results support the rational design of CB2‐targeted ligands and identify structural features that may guide future synthesis and biological evaluation.

title: The Impact of Lean Principles on the Design and Improvement of Emergency Department Performance
abstract: Objectives Emergency departments (EDs) constitute essential components of most healthcare systems; However, in many countries, its efficiency has diminished due to the reliance on outdated guidelines and flawed operational systems. Redesigning the ED through modern approaches, such as Lean, can enhance process flow and service delivery. The purpose of this study is to apply Lean principles to improve ED performance through optimized design. Methodology A comprehensive literature review, combined with a comparative, analytical, and synthetic approach to evaluate ED design guidelines, was conducted to examine new systems related to patient stratification, triage, and process flow. In addition, the field method and direct observation (Gemba), along with a Fishbone diagram, were employed to understand treatment processes and identify bottlenecks. Findings The Lean approach influences access and the layout of ED spaces, resulting in substantial modifications. Key differences include the use of an Intake system (a combination of First Look and Rapid Medical Evaluation), result waiting and results/ECG rooms in the shared zone, internal waiting areas within the emergency and outpatient zones, standardized dimensions of examination rooms and acute and observation cubicles, among others. Conclusion In this study, we established a revised operational process flow and a concise set of ED d…

title: Your Future Is Whatever You… Generate It? GenUI as a New Challenge in Inclusive User Experience Design
abstract: AI-based technologies shape the future of interface and user experience design (UI and UX). Recently, the industry dictionary has added a new term: GenUI (Generative UI – Generative User Interface). Rather than to AI-assisted interface design, it refers to a new way of interaction, in which the interface is not rigid and static (formed by a designer), but dynamically created by AI in real time, in response to the user’s needs and preferences. The new UI paradigm changes the user–system relationship. It shifts from accurate commands to communicating intentions and goals, while the system decides how to execute them. Customised interfaces seem to be a great opportunity for designing more inclusive digital experience. The revolutionary vision of UI future, however, carries serious risks. Personalisation does not equal inclusiveness, and the current discourse around GenUI does not pay sufficient attention to accessibility. If GenUI future is dominated by the logic of profit-driven economy and capitalistic optimisation, existing inequalities may exacerbate. The article studies the notion of generative systems and tries to answer the question whether they can support care and agency, and not only efficiency, and to what extent designers are accountable for the developed generative systems. Keywords: GenUI, artificial intelligence (AI), digital accessibility, UX design

title: Drug Repurposing in Pre‐Eclampsia: Maternal Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Considerations for Clinical Trial Design
abstract: Pre‐eclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy affecting 3–8% of pregnancies worldwide, with no disease‐modifying therapy currently available. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy, yet no candidate has been validated to date. Pregnancy‐associated physiological changes alter drug pharmacokinetics (PK), and pre‐eclampsia itself may further modify drug disposition, complicating dose selection and contributing to inconclusive clinical trial outcomes. A structured literature search identified six prospective or randomized controlled trials of repurposed drugs for established pre‐eclampsia: esomeprazole, omeprazole, sulfasalazine, pravastatin, recombinant antithrombin, and metformin. All drugs were well tolerated, with metformin the one to show promising clinical benefit by prolonging gestation; the remaining five drugs yielded inconclusive or null efficacy outcomes. Critically, PK sampling was conducted in only three trials, and none systematically characterized exposure–response relationships using key pre‐eclampsia biomarkers, including soluble fms‐like tyrosine kinase‐1, soluble endoglin, and placental growth factor. Further common methodological limitations included small sample sizes (12–120 participants), heterogeneous gestational age eligibility criteria, and dosing regimens extrapolated from non‐pregnant populations without pregnancy‐specific optimization. Power System Zoning and Regional Minimum Inertia Requirement Assessment Based on an Improved Spectral Clustering Approach
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable-energy generating units, power-system inertia continues to decline and becomes unevenly distributed in space. Consequently, frequency responses differ markedly among regions following a disturbance, and assessment based on a single center-of-inertia (COI) frequency may conceal local frequency-security risks. This paper proposes a regional inertia assessment and minimum-inertia calculation method based on linearized analysis. First, a generalized relative correlation gain matrix is constructed from a linearized multi-machine model to quantify the dynamic correlation of generator frequency responses. Spectral clustering and the Calinski–Harabasz (CH) index are then used to determine the system partition. Next, synchronous-machine inertia, load-voltage characteristics, virtual inertia, and primary frequency control are considered in stages. The minimum regional inertia requirements are calculated under rate-of-change-of-frequency (RoCoF) and frequency-nadir constraints, and the larger value is taken as the regional inertia threshold. Simulations on the IEEE 10-machine 39-bus system show that the proposed partitions capture regional differences in frequency response and that the estimated values agree closely with the actual aggregated inertia after synchronous machines are replaced.
