title: Novel enzymes for amino acid biosynthesis in diverse bacteria and archaea: GapMind 2026
abstract: We previously described GapMind, an automated web-based tool for annotating amino acid biosynthesis pathways in bacterial and archaeal genomes. We used GapMind to identify gaps in biosynthetic pathways and systematically used comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics to identify candidate genes to fill these gaps. We confirmed the activity of ten of the proposed enzymes by using cross-species complementation assays. Highlights include a route to glycine via glyoxylate, two families that can replace phosphoserine phosphatase, an alternative N-succinyl-L,L-diaminopimelate desuccinylase, an alternative N-acetylornithine deacetylase, and a putative bifunctional MetB/MetC. We updated GapMind to include these additional enzymes. Across 208 prokaryotes that have high-quality genomes and can grow in minimal media, the average number of unexplained missing steps or gaps in amino acid biosynthesis dropped from 1.4 per genome to 0.7 per genome. The majority of remaining gaps involve the gain or loss of phosphate groups.

title: The Moderating Effect of Profitability on the Relationship between Sustainability Reporting and Value of Environmentally Sensitive Firms in Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the moderating effect of profitability on the relationship between sustainability reporting and firm value. The dataset encompasses 60 environmentally sensitive companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), the study employed census sampling technique utilizing panel data over a five-year span from 2018 to 2022, the data were analyzed using multiple regression analyses with help of STATA software version 14. The results revealed that sustainability reporting has a positive and significant effect on firm value. Conversely, profitability shows a positive and significant effect on firm value. Also, the result revealed that profitability has positive and significant moderating effect on the relationship between sustainability reporting and the value of environmentally sensitive firms in Nigeria. The study concludes that high level of profitability tends to strengthen the relationship between sustainability reporting and value of listed environmentally sensitive firms in Nigeria. The study recommends that, listed environmentally sensitive firms in Nigeria should improve their sustainability reporting compliance and prioritize it relevance and quality, aligning it with stakeholder interest, integrating it into core business strategy, and implementing continuous monitoring and feedback mechanisms. title: A role for p16 High immune cells in disease tolerance as a crucial defence strategy
abstract: Abstract In the context of infectious diseases, it is well established that older individuals are more susceptible to pathogens. However, an organism's survival does not rely solely on its ability to eliminate pathogens, a process collectively referred to as resistance. An additional protective strategy, known as disease tolerance, has evolved in multiple species. In response to severe inflammation and tissue damage, disease tolerance allows the host to limit the negative impact of infection without directly reducing pathogen burden. It relies on mechanisms that control tissue damage and stress response to preserve host health and physiological fitness. In recent years, the concept of disease tolerance has gained attention, as it offers a complementary approach to traditional resistance-based strategies in managing inflammation, tissue damage and infection, ultimately improving survival outcomes. However, the full spectrum of disease tolerance mechanisms and the therapeutic opportunities to enhance them remain incompletely understood. In this context, we will discuss recent insights into disease tolerance and propose a role for immune cells exhibiting senescence-like features—specifically, the activation of the p16 gene—in the positive regulation of disease tolerance, with implications for treating various pathological conditions and potentially extending healthspan. title: Transfer Teknologi Platform ISLAND-MARKET Berbasis E-Commerce dan Business Intelligence untuk Penguatan Digitalisasi UMKM Negeri Hatumete
abstract: Digital transformation has become increasingly important for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to expand market access, improve transaction management, and support data-driven decision-making. This community engagement program aims to introduce and transfer the ISLAND-MARKET platform, integrating e-commerce and Business Intelligence (BI), to MSMEs in Negeri Hatumete, Maluku, Indonesia. The program adopts a participatory approach encompassing partner needs assessment, technology preparation, socialization, application demonstrations, user training, and assistance in utilizing the BI dashboard. ISLAND-MARKET integrates product, category, order, customer, payment, shipping, voucher, sales analytics, and reporting features. Its BI dashboard presents key business performance indicators, including total revenue, number of orders, products sold, number of customers, active products, and pending orders, along with period-based sales visualizations. Activity documentation confirms that platform introduction and socialization sessions were conducted through presentations and application demonstrations. These activities represent an initial step toward introducing digital technology for more structured business management. title: Stock Market Reaction to the Announcement of the Change of Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia (An Event Study Analysis)
abstract: The objective of this study is to measure the response of the capital market to the announcement of the change in the Minister of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia by means of event study. Market response is calculated through abnormal return (AR), cumulative abnormal return (CAR), trading volume activity (TVA), and standard deviation (SD) of stocks of companies in the banking sector that are listed on Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The event date for this study is set as September 8, 2025, where the change in the Minister of Finance was announced. The data observation period will employ an event window of 30 days before and 30 days after the event. The research sample will include banking stocks that were actively traded throughout the research period and that had all the required data. The secondary data used for the analysis will be the stock prices and trading volumes that are available from Indonesia Stock Exchange. The analytical procedures involve calculation of actual return, market return, abnormal return, average abnormal return, cumulative abnormal return, and trading volume activity. Testing of hypothesis is done by using One-Sample t-Test for AR and CAR and Paired-Sample t-Test for examining the difference in trading volume activity and standard deviation of stock prices before and after the event. title: Stock market response to battery electric vehicle tax incentives in Indonesia
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractBattery electric vehicle fiscal incentives are increasingly used to accelerate transportation decarbonization, yet their implications for investors in emerging economies remain poorly understood. This study analyzes the short-term response of ten Indonesia Stock Exchange-listed firms associated with the electric-vehicle value chain to the introduction of Indonesian Minister of Finance Regulations No. 8/2024 and No. 9/2024. An event-study design was applied using a Market Model estimated over 120 trading days, cumulative abnormal returns, and standardized abnormal trading activity. Event-induced variance, cross-sectional dependence, multiple testing, nonsynchronous trading, alternative event dates, firm-level contamination, and placebo periods were incorporated into the robustness analysis. For the primary event specification centered on 12 February 2024, the full-sample cumulative average abnormal return over days 0 to +2 was +1.536% but statistically insignificant (p = 0.332). Mean standardized abnormal trading activity was also positive at +0.236 but insignificant (p = 0.399). Accordingly, neither the predicted positive return response nor the increase in abnormal trading activity was supported. Gender Vulnerabilities: Modelling the Relationship Between Labour Market Performance and Energy Consumer Price Inflation in Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the relationship between labour-market performance and energy consumer price inflation (CPI) in Nigeria from a gender-vulnerability perspective using annual data from 1991 – 2024 and analyzed using the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) dynamic estimation and necessary diagnostic tests. Female labour vulnerability, male labour vulnerability and the gender vulnerability gap were constructed from gender-disaggregated labour-market indicators, while energy consumer price inflation, headline inflation, food inflation, global energy-price inflation and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth were used as explanatory and control variables. The findings showed that energy consumer price inflation was highly volatile over the study period and rose sharply in the most recent years. The ARDL estimates revealed that female labour vulnerability was persistent over time and GDP growth had the clearest vulnerability-reducing association. The analysis also showed that global energy-price pressure was positively associated with female labour vulnerability, suggesting that energy shocks were more visible when analyzed through gender gaps rather than through female labour indicators alone. The study concluded that energy consumer price inflation is a relevant gender-vulnerability issue in Nigeria, but its labour-market effect is better understood through transmission channels …

title: Ibrahim, the law and the EU’s internal market of pornography
abstract: Abstract This article examines the case of Ibrahim, a Syrian-born porn actor living in Europe, whose life story was told by Ben Judah in his book This is Europe . While this tale may appear to be the success story of a self-made man, a closer reading of the chapter reveals a certain sense of despair within the gilded cage of the pornography industry. The contribution aims to demonstrate that Ibrahim’s story, as narrated by Judah, offers a unique lens through which to examine broader issues: the internal contradictions of the European project between fostering economic integration and promoting social well-being, and the difficult regulation of human bodies and pornography within the European legal framework. The article begins by examining Ibrahim’s journey from precarious asylum seeker to transnational porn superstar. It then explores the relationship between Ibrahim’s story and European law. First, it examines how his various legal statuses, from migrant to German citizen, shape his daily life, then it examines the relationship between Ibrahim and internal market law, and how this legal framework grants him access to an entire economic system. Finally, it considers how Ibrahim’s story fits into the EU’s approach to the platform economy. The conclusion of the essay highlights the European legal system’s failure to understand and acknowledge the difficulties of Ibrahim’s life a…

title: Improving data quality in German office construction: a template-based framework for an SME-driven market
abstract: Germany’s construction industry lags behind other European countries in terms of digital transformation, particularly in building information modelling (BIM). This is attributed to several factors, including a large proportion of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and limited investment resulting from insufficient data quality (DQ) in 3D deliverables. Against this backdrop, this study investigates barriers to DQ during information production, the affected DQ dimensions, and potential solutions. The aim is to contribute to the ongoing discussion on improving DQ in construction by offering practical solutions tailored to the constraints of SMEs. Specifically, this study focuses on the planning phase of office building projects in Germany. Data were collected through focus groups and individual interviews. Data analysis revealed several critical barriers that compromise DQ in the examined environment: incomplete information requirements, unresolved interfaces, limited participation in Closed BIM environments, inadequate implementation of the Exchange Information Requirements, inconsistent 3D deliverables, insufficient data validation expertise, and non-compliance with schedules and model structures. The most affected DQ dimensions are completeness, reliability, and usability. Among the potential solutions identified, object templates emerged as a practical approach to impro…

title: The legitimacy of engaging in race-related social media messaging: college sport communicators’ perceptions
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to assess American college sport communicators’ (CSCs) perceptions and justifications regarding their decisions to post race-related content on behalf of their athletic department via social media. Design/methodology/approach Interweaving institutional theory, the model of rhetorical legitimation (Harmon et al., 2015) and whiteness, this study explored CSCs’ (N = 163) responses to three open-ended survey questions via abductive analysis. In doing so, the authors discern how CSC rhetoric functions to maintain or disrupt whiteness in college athletics. Findings Findings suggest that CSCs engage in interfield (e.g. desire to disrupt whiteness in college athletics), intrafield (e.g. want to maintain whiteness in college athletics) and between-level rhetoric. The incongruence across coded responses in terms of perceived role suggests instability in the NCAA organizational field, which may be indicative of field-level change. In practice, these sentiments may manifest as some CSCs choosing to address racial inclusion on social media, which in turn can yield a more inclusive institutional field. However, disengagement from creating race-related content functionally operates to privilege and uphold whiteness within college athletics. Originality/value This work examines legitimacy and whiteness in sport organization’s social media advocacy efforts t…

title: Consumer willingness to pay for organic tea in an emerging market: addressing hypothetical bias and attribute non-attendance in a discrete choice experiment from Iran
abstract: Purpose This study evaluates consumer preferences and willingness to pay (WTP) for organic tea attributes – health, food safety, sensory quality, and certification – in the emerging Iranian market, while jointly addressing two methodological challenges that may distort WTP estimates in discrete choice experiments (DCEs): hypothetical bias and attribute non-attendance (ANA). Design/methodology/approach A discrete choice experiment was conducted with 384 tea consumers in Tehran across three survey treatments: baseline, Cheap Talk, and Honesty Priming. Preferences were estimated using conditional logit and Endogenous Attribute Attendance (EAA) models, with WTP confidence intervals derived via Krinsky–Robb bootstrapping. Findings Health-related attributes (residue-free safety and pesticide reduction) command the highest WTP premiums. Cheap Talk and Honesty Priming substantially reduce stated attribute non-attendance (by approximately 40 and 63%, respectively). The EAA model outperforms conditional logit in model fit, and Honesty Priming yields the most conservative WTP estimates; the total premium under the EAA–HP specification equals approximately 15.7% of the base price. Research limitations/implications The sample is restricted to an affluent urban district of Tehran, limiting generalizability to the wider Iranian population. title: Unraveling performance asymmetry: environmental accounting and knowledge management as economic and environmental decision-support tools in an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine the asymmetric effect of environmental management accounting (EMA) and environmental knowledge management practices (EKMP) on the financial (FP) and environmental performance (EP) of firms in an emerging market. Design/methodology/approach It adopted the cross-sectional design with stratified random sampling and PLS-SEM to analyze data from 347 respondents across manufacturing firms in Ghana. Findings The findings reveal an important asymmetry in the performance consequences of EMA. While EMA significantly improves FP, it does not exert a corresponding influence on EP, suggesting that EMA functions primarily as an economic decision-support mechanism rather than a direct environmental improvement tool. Conversely, EKMP contributes to FP, but the magnitude of its effect is relatively small and less direct than its influence on EP. Research limitations/implications The complex effect of EKMP on FP suggests that environmental performance may serve as an intermediate mechanism through which EKMP enhances FP; thus, the nexus should be mediated by factors like EP, ESG and green innovation. Practical implications Managers should not treat EMA and EKMP as interchangeable practices. A one-pot asymmetric ERA-CRISPR/Cas12a assay for visual detection of white spot syndrome virus in shrimp
abstract: Introduction White spot syndrome virus (WSSV) threatens shrimp aquaculture. PCR is sensitive but laboratory dependent. Isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas12a offers an alternative, but one-pot integration is limited by competition between double-stranded amplicons and crRNA for Cas12a. Methods A one-pot assay (OAERA-Cas12a) integrating asymmetric enzymatic recombinase amplification (aERA) with CRISPR/Cas12a was developed. Key parameters were optimized. Analytical specificity was tested against common non-target shrimp pathogens. Sensitivity was determined using plasmid standards. Diagnostic performance was evaluated on 57 samples from farm submissions and a proficiency-testing programme. qPCR was used for comparison. Results Optimal conditions were determined to be 1:120 primer ratio, 1 µM Cas12a, 4:1 Cas12a-to-crRNA, and 46 °C. No cross-reactivity was observed in the tested panel. The approximate plasmid-based LoD was determined to be 10 copies/µL (24/25 technical replicates, 96%, exact 95% CI 79.7–99.9%); 25/25 replicates were positive at 50 copies/µL. Because the lower CI bound was below 95%, a ≥95% detection probability was not established with high precision. The readout was completed within 15 min. Agreement with qPCR was observed for OAERA-Cas12a: 9/9 positive (100%, 95% CI 66.4-100%), 48/48 negative (100%, 95% CI 92.6-100%), and 57/57 overall (100%, 95% CI 93.7-100…

title: Immigrants and the market for taxi drivers
abstract: Abstract Immigrants face many obstacles to labor market integration in developed countries, often clustering in certain lower-skilled occupations. To investigate the role of such occupations, this paper studies how labor market outcomes evolve after gaining access to a canonical immigrant occupation: taxi driving. Comparing individuals who choose to pursue and pass the necessary written examinations for a taxi driver’s license to both those who have not yet done so and those who never take taxi examinations, we find that non-Western immigrants increase their monthly earnings by nearly 50 percent between 1 and 3 years later. Moreover, reliance on social insurance programs drops substantially. Natives experience smaller benefits and appear to use taxi driving to recover from negative labor market shocks. We also find that immigrants remain in taxi driving over time and that recently arrived immigrants reap the largest benefits.

title: Digital labor market pressure and employment anxiety among computer science undergraduates: professional belonging, career adaptability, and employment resilience
abstract: Introduction Digitalized recruitment has introduced new pressures into the school-to-work transition, particularly for computer science undergraduates facing AI substitution concerns, rapidly changing skill requirements, and increasingly visible comparisons of career readiness. This study examined the association between digital labor market pressure (DLMP) and employment anxiety (EA), the mediating roles of professional belonging (PB) and career adaptability (CA), and the moderating role of employment resilience (ER). Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire survey collected 467 valid responses from computer-related majors, including 139 sophomores, 158 juniors, and 170 seniors. The analysis examined direct associations, parallel and chain mediation pathways, the moderating effect of ER, and differences across undergraduate grades. Results DLMP was positively associated with EA and negatively associated with PB and CA. PB was positively associated with CA, while both PB and CA were negatively associated with EA. Bootstrap confidence intervals supported three indirect pathways linking DLMP to EA through PB, CA, and the sequential combination of PB and CA. ER moderated the DLMP-EA association, with a stronger positive association at lower levels of resilience. Seniors reported higher DLMP and EA, while PB was lower among students in higher grades. Cost-effectiveness and price threshold analysis of daraxonrasib versus chemotherapy for previously treated metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in China
abstract: Background Metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (mPDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy with limited treatment options after first-line progression. Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), a RAS(ON) inhibitor, has demonstrated clinical benefit in previously treated mPDAC patients in the RASolute 302 trial. However, its economic value in China remains uncertain. This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of Daraxonrasib versus Chemotherapy in previously treated mPDAC. Methods A three-state partitioned survival model was developed to evaluate costs and health outcomes from the Chinese healthcare system perspective. Clinical inputs were derived from reconstructed individual patient data from the RASolute 302 randomized clinical trial, with long-term survival extrapolated using parametric survival models. Costs were estimated using China-specific healthcare resource utilization and medical service prices. Outcomes included costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs). A 10-year time horizon with an annual discount rate of 4.5% was applied. Deterministic sensitivity analyses, probabilistic sensitivity analyses, and price scenario analyses were performed. Results Compared with chemotherapy, the model estimated that daraxonrasib generated an additional 0.30 QALYs (0.98 vs. 0.68 QALYs) at an increased cost of US$38,125.89 (US$44,844.71 vs. US$6,7…

title: A unified ML LLM decision support framework for SME financial analytics forecasting risk and advisory recommendations
abstract: Abstract In the financial decision-making process of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and individuals, integration of forecasting, risk quantification, and advisory generation is a tripartite requirement that is not addressed by existing systems. We present MoneyMind AI, a modular, system integration pipeline-based Financial Decision Support System (FDSS) with tightly integrated components: (i) Data ingestion & preprocessing, (ii) Structured financial analytics engine computing per financial metric like income, expenses, Net Cash Flow (NCF), and Profit Margin (PM) from the transaction-level CSV data, (iii) Machine Learning (ML) forecasting module using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression (LR) and Random Forest (RF) ensemble methods, which offers 1, 2, and 3-month ahead financial forecasts, and (iv) a composite Financial Health Scoring (FHS) algorithm that integrates the four primary metrics the PM, Cash Flow Stability (CFS), Revenue Growth (RG) rate, and Expense Volatility (EV) into a tri-class risk stratification schema, (v) A Large Language Model (LLM) driven recommendation engine that supports the generation of action-oriented, natural language-based financial advisory based on a prompt-engineered API call, converting the structured financial summary results. Early identification of sepsis in critically ill children using inflammatory and nutritional markers: development and internal validation of a prediction model with a maternal–neonatal subgroup analysis
abstract: Objective To construct and validate an early prediction model for pediatric ICU sepsis based on easily accessible inflammatory and Nutritional markers, to provide an objective quantitative tool for ICU clinicians to rapidly screen sepsis in critically ill children. Methods 456 critically ill children (Including 55 newborns) admitted to the ICU of A certain children's hospital from January 2024 to December 2025 were retrospectively enrolled, and randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a ratio of 7:3. Taking whether the child was diagnosed with sepsis as the primary outcome, inflammatory and related biochemical markers including age, gender ratio, Lactate, WBC, PCT, Plt, N%, L%, RDW, CRP, Tbil, Cre, ALB, ALT and IL-6 and etc. were included for univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis to screen independent predictive factors for sepsis. The “rms” package in R software was used to construct a visual nomogram model. The discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit of the model were verified through ROC curve, calibration curve, and decision curve analysis, respectively. Results The occurrence of neonatal sepsis is related to prenatal chorioamnionitis( n = 9), urogenital tract infections( n = 6), and colonization of Group B streptococcus (GBS) in the mother( n = 5). Physics-guided long short-term memory–Transformer prediction of ship motion and broaching in oblique stern waves
abstract: Accurate ship-motion prediction and early identification of unstable navigation states are essential for autonomous vessels operating in following-oblique waves. This study proposes a physics-guided long short-term memory (LSTM)–Transformer encoder–decoder model for joint motion prediction and surf-riding/broaching identification of an autonomous trimaran. Numerical simulation data are generated under different operating conditions, and physics-based state labels are constructed using the ship–wave speed ratio, heading deviation, yaw-rate response and rudder saturation. The proposed framework combines LSTM-based local temporal feature extraction with Transformer-based global dependency modelling. A state-identification branch is further introduced, and a multi-objective loss function is designed by integrating motion prediction, state classification, physical consistency and ordinal risk constraints. Comparative studies with different models and model variants are conducted to evaluate the prediction accuracy, robustness and generalisation capability of the proposed method. The results show that physically meaningful variables and state-related constraints strongly affect the prediction of navigation-state features. The proposed model improves both motion-response prediction and unstable-state identification, providing a more interpretable and reliable short-term forecasting fr…

title: AdaFusionNet: Adaptive Trajectory Prediction of Group Two-wheelers in Interactive Conflict Scenarios for Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: Abstract The accurate prediction of two-wheeler motion trajectories is essential for ensuring the safety of autonomous vehicles (AVs), particularly at crowded intersections in China. Existing trajectory prediction approaches face limitations in representing the diverse motion patterns, dynamic constraints, and group-level behavioral characteristics of two-wheeler riders. This paper proposes an adaptive trajectory prediction framework for two-wheelers by integrating the revised social force model (RSFM) and a spatiotemporal Transformer (STTransformer) module. The RSFM models group-level interactions among two-wheelers, capturing self-organization, leader-follower dynamics, and herding behaviors. The STTransformer extracts temporal dependencies and spatial interaction patterns using multi-head spatiotemporal attention mechanisms to capture group motion patterns. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) serves as the fusion module, recurrently integrating the trajectory predictions generated by the RSFM and STTransformer together with a local traffic-scene complexity representation constructed from the numbers and mean speeds of nearby pedestrians and vehicles. Experimental results on the Signalized INtersection Dataset (SIND) show that AdaFusionNet achieves an accuracy improvement of over 11% at the 3 s prediction horizon compared with the selected baselines. The error distributions further …

title: Adaptive structural fusion for dielectric constant prediction using physics-guided graph neural networks
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of dielectric response is essential for improving the discovery of materials for electronic, energy-storage, radio-frequency, sensing, and optoelectronic applications. However, dielectric datasets are typically dominated by materials with low to moderate dielectric response, while high-dielectric materials are severely under-represented, making reliable prediction across the full property range challenging. This work proposes a physics-guided extension of the Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN) for total dielectric constant prediction through Adaptive Structural Fusion (ASF). This refines learned atomic representations using five physically motivated local descriptors: coordination number, mean bond length, bond-angle variation, local electronegativity difference, and atomic polarizability. A context-dependent Knowledge-Guided Graph Aggregation (KGGA) module is subsequently evaluated both independently and in combination with ASF to investigate whether adaptive graph aggregation depends on the quality of the underlying node representations. Four controlled architectures -the baseline CGCNN, CGCNN with KGGA, CGCNN with ASF, and the proposed model CGCNN with both ASF and KGGA- were evaluated on an identical frozen split of a curated benchmark containing 5,874 inorganic crystalline materials. Relative to the baseline CGCNN, the proposed …

title: Structural optimization, degradation behavior and mechanical properties of Mg–2Zn–1Mn alloy bone plates based on a stress corrosion prediction model
abstract: Abstract Degradable magnesium alloy bone plates have considerable potential for fracture fixation because of their excellent biocompatibility and mechanical compatibility. However, in physiological environments, they are susceptible to the combined effects of corrosive media and service loads, which may lead to localized corrosion, stress corrosion cracking, and the progressive deterioration of mechanical properties, thereby compromising the stability and safety of the implant. Therefore, rational control of the degradation rate and improvement of service reliability are of great significance. In this study, an Mg–2Zn–1Mn magnesium alloy bone plate was investigated. Based on a previously established and calibrated pitting corrosion–stress corrosion coupling model, the key structural parameters of the bone plate, including geometry, hole spacing, hole diameter, and thickness, were optimized. The results showed that the combination of type (b) geometry, a hole spacing of 9.0 mm, a hole diameter of 3.4 mm, and a thickness of 3.25 mm provided the best overall performance. Compared with the original design, the mass loss of the optimized bone plate after 36 h decreased from 40.09% to 29.41%, while its bending yield strength increased from 276 MPa to 305 MPa. No simulated structural failure occurred during the degradation process. These findings demonstrate that optimizing key struct…

AI-Intelligent Demand-Sensitive Transportation Scheduling with IoT-Crowd Prediction an Reinforcement Learning Optimization
abstract: Efficient scheduling of transportation in smart cities is made difficult by the dynamic nature of passenger demand and crowd movements. Previous methods for scheduling, which use established timetables and explicit guidelines, struggle to adapt to real-time changes in demand, often resulting in long wait times for passengers, inefficient usage of transportation resources, and higher overall operating costs. This research presents a cluster-aware intelligent transportation framework that combines an approach to forecasting transportation demand with an adaptive scheduling process using data from IoT-based mobile signals. The use of DBSCAN to determine areal mobility clusters from the mobile signal data allowed a Cluster-Aware CNN-GRU model to learn complex patterns of spatial-temporal movement, resulting in the accurate prediction of the future demand for transportation. The proposed forecasting methodology achieved high levels of accuracy in its prediction of demand, with a MAE of 0.1033, and an RMSE of 0.1290. The forecasted demand was then utilized as input to a Deep Q-Network (DQN) scheduling module, which allocated transportation resources dynamically based on the forecasted mobility needs of the population. Analysis of the experimental data demonstrates that using the hybrid forecasting/scheduling framework led to a reduction in both passengers wait times and operational c…

Influencing factors of hormone replacement therapy acceptance intention and construction of a nomogram prediction model among women aged 35–60 years with menopausal dry-eye symptoms in China: a cross-sectional study based on the health belief model
abstract: Background Perimenopausal women are at high risk of several eye diseases, particularly dry eye disease (DED), yet their acceptance of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) remains low, and no quantitative screening tool is available for ophthalmic settings. This study aimed to explore factors influencing HRT acceptance intention among Chinese women aged 35–60 years with menopausal dry-eye symptoms based on the Health Belief Model (HBM), and to construct the first nomogram prediction model for opportunistic screening through ophthalmology–gynecology collaboration. Methods This cross-sectional survey recruited 902 women aged 35–60 years with dry-eye symptoms by convenience sampling between May and September 2026 (1,161 questionnaires distributed; 902 included in the analysis, 77.7% of the number distributed). Dry-eye status was defined by self-reported OSDI symptoms (score > 0), not objective ophthalmic testing. The outcome was the continuous HRT behavioral intention score (2–14). After univariate screening, multiple linear stepwise regression was fitted to build a nomogram. title: CONSTITUTIVE OVEREXPRESSION OF THE DELLA-LIKE GENE ZPR31 FROM ZYGOPHYLLUM POTANINII MAXIM SUPPRESSES THE ANTIOXIDANT RESPONSE OF ARABIDOPSIS THALIANA UNDER MANNITOL-INDUCED OSMOTIC STRESS
abstract: ZpR31, a DELLA-like transcript whose deduced protein shares sequence similarity with GAI1, was previously identified by suppression subtractive hybridization (SSH) as downregulated in mannitol-stressed Zygophyllum potaninii. To characterise its function, transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana lines constitutively overexpressing ZpR31 (ZpR31-OE) were generated and, together with wild-type (WT) Col-0 plants, exposed to 200 mM mannitol. After 15 days of treatment, malondialdehyde (MDA) content was markedly higher in two independent ZpR31-OE lines (approximately 23–32 nmol g‑1) than in WT (approximately 16.5 nmol g‑1), indicating more extensive membrane lipid peroxidation. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity increased markedly in stressed WT (from approximately 410 to 515 U g‑1), whereas it declined to approximately 210 U g‑1 in both ZpR31-OE lines. Stem-loop RT-qPCR of six stress-associated microRNAs in ZpR31-OE plants relative to WT revealed transient induction of miR156, miR165, miR398 and miR827 at 24 h, a delayed miR393 peak at 48 h, and sustained miR171 repression. Because miR398 is normally downregulated under oxidative stress to permit induction of Cu/Zn-SOD genes, its induction here suggests a plausible mechanism by which ZpR31 suppresses the SOD response. These results indicate that ZpR31 acts as a negative regulator of osmotic-stress tolerance in Arabidopsis, consistent with it…

Housing environmental enrichment influences mouse behavior and response to experimental metabolic disorders
abstract: Housing environmental is essential for animal welfare but may also influence the metabolic and behavioral outcomes of preclinical studies. This study investigates whether two commonly used enrichment materials, Nestlets and Sizzle, modify the effects of a high-fat diet (HFD) on metabolic and behavioral phenotypes in adult male C57BL/6 J mice. A total of 128 mice were fed either a normal diet (ND) or HFD for six months and housed in enriched cages containing either Nestlets (Nest) or Sizzle nesting material ( n = 32 mice/condition). Metabolic parameters and behavioral performances were assessed at six months. Results show that HFD induced weight gain, hypercholesterolemia, fasting hyperglycemia, and impaired glucose tolerance under both enrichment conditions. However, Nest-enriched mice displayed lower cholesterol levels and differences in glycemic responses compared with Sizzle-enriched mice, suggesting that nesting material can modulate the severity of diet-induced metabolic alterations. Furthermore, environmental housing also affected behavior. Nest-enriched mice showed higher locomotor activity and reduced anxiety compared with Sizzle-enriched mice. Interestingly, HFD-induced impairment of visual recognition memory in the novel object recognition test was detected only in Nest-enriched mice. Overall, these findings demonstrate that different enrichment materials can substant…

title: Macroscopic plastic response and atomic-scale dislocation evolution of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during ultrasonic surface rolling
abstract: To address the insufficient understanding of the surface plastic deformation mechanism of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during ultrasonic surface rolling processing (USRP), this study adopts an approach combining finite element (FE) simulation and molecular dynamics (MD) analysis. The effects of static load, ultrasonic vibration frequency, and ultrasonic amplitude on residual stress and surface plastic deformation are investigated, and the dislocation evolution and local deformation response under ultrasonic vibration are analyzed at the atomic scale. A three-dimensional explicit dynamic FE model based on the Johnson-Cook constitutive law is established to examine the variations of surface residual stress, equivalent plastic strain, and plastic displacement under different static loads, ultrasonic vibration frequencies, and ultrasonic amplitudes, and the validity of the FE model is verified against experimentally measured residual stress results. The results show that static load is the dominant factor governing the degree of macroscopic surface plastic deformation. Within the investigated static-load range of 100–400 N, the magnitude of the peak residual compressive stress increases overall from 685.11 MPa to 722.09 MPa, although the variation is not strictly monotonic, while the maximum PEEQ increases from 0.12481 to 0.38641 and the affected depths increase markedly. title: Nucleotide excision repair deficiency identified by mutational signatures is associated with cisplatin response in triple-negative breast cancer
Case Report: Circulating tumor DNA-confirmed complete response in a marker-negative primary mediastinal seminoma with a rare KIT D820V mutation
abstract: KIT is the most frequently mutated oncogene in seminoma, and the mutational spectrum in mediastinal seminomas differs from testicular cases. AKT1 point mutations, common in breast, gynecological, and colorectal cancers, are unreported in germ cell tumors. We describe a 52-year-old male with a 12.38 cm anterior mediastinal seminoma (OCT3/4+, CD117+) harboring a pathogenic KIT p.D820V activation loop mutation and a co-occurring AKT1 p.W80R pleckstrin homology variant, representing dual-level PI3K/AKT pathway activation not previously described in a germ cell tumor. Complete response after BEP chemotherapy was confirmed by PET-CT and clearance of circulating tumor DNA (1335.6 to undetectable mean tumor molecules/mL), confirming molecular response in a marker-negative (AFP/β-hCG) extragonadal seminoma. Structural modeling predicts p.D820V confers constitutive kinase activation with sensitivity to type I tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The co-occurrence of upstream KIT and downstream AKT1 mutations has implications for targeted therapy at relapse.

title: Modulation of the TGF-β1-related response of human dental pulp stem cells by PRF membranes with and without bone allograft
abstract: Introduction To our knowledge, no previous study has directly compared the TGF-β1-related responses of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) to conditioned media derived from A-PRF+, H-PRF, Gel A-PRF+, and e-PRF, with and without bone allograft. Aim To evaluate the TGF-β1-related cellular response of hDPSCs following exposure to conditioned media derived from different PRF preparations, used alone or combined with bone allograft. Materials and methods Four PRF preparations (A-PRF+, H-PRF, Gel A-PRF+, and e-PRF) were investigated with and without bone allograft. Each experimental group included 10 independent biological samples (n = 10). Conditioned media were collected after 24 h and on day 14. hDPSCs cultured in unconditioned medium served as controls. After 48 h of treatment, TGF-β1-related cellular immunoreactivity was assessed using Cell ELISA and normalized to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH). Statistical analysis included the Kruskal–Wallis test with Dunn’s post hoc test and Bonferroni correction. Direct paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction. Results PRF preparations without allograft showed no significant increases in the normalized TGF-β1/GAPDH signal compared with controls. After 24 h of conditioning, significant increases were observed for H-PRF, Gel A-PRF+, and e-PRF combined with allograft co…

title: Environmentally conditioned paired difference learning with field residual preservation for recovering controlled mooring response parameters from nonstationary buoy observations
abstract: Introduction Long-term motion records from aids-to-navigation buoys combine nonstationary environmental responses, mooring-state variations, and positioning errors. These components are difficult to separate when tension measurements and damage labels are unavailable. Methods We propose field-residual-preserving environment-conditioned paired-difference learning. The method first estimates the predictable horizontal response from forward-aligned wind, wave, current, and attitude variables. It then adds controlled response differences to the same measured record and uses matched random-forest models to infer an equivalent response coefficient, a trajectory reference-center offset, and future statistical reference-radius exceedance probabilities. Results During the retrospective later-period evaluation, the random-forest environmental model reduced vector NRMSE by 41.58 % ± 0.13 % relative to a two-dimensional mean baseline. The complete M2 method achieved a joint NMAE of 0.2659 ± 0.0002 , with a paired improvement of 0.0126 (95% interval: [0.0074, 0.0173]) over M0. The reference-center offset vector MAE decreased by approximately 0.371 m, which represents controlled-parameter recovery accuracy. Estimating spatial response distances of reef-associated communities in the Wuzhizhou Island marine ranch using generalized additive models
abstract: Artificial reefs are widely used to enhance fishery resources and restore degraded marine habitats, yet quantitative information on the spatial responses of biological communities to reef distance remains limited in tropical marine ranching systems. This study investigated the spatial response distances of different catch groups to reef distance in the Wuzhizhou Island marine ranch, Sanya, Hainan Province, China. Based on five surveys conducted at 28 stations from 2019 to 2021, a total of 263 species of catches were collected using five sampling methods angling, gill net, trap, diving sampling, and bottom trawling. The catches were classified into five groups total catches, reef-dependent, reef-approaching, sand-mud bottom-preference, and strong-swimming. Generalized additive models (GAMs) were fitted using the Shannon-Wiener diversity ( H ), Pielou evenness ( J ), Margalef richness ( d ), and the Index of Relative Importance ( IRI ) as response variables. GAMs were used to characterize the relationships between community indices and reef distance, with additional sampling-method-adjusted models conducted to evaluate sensitivity to sampling heterogeneity. The strong-swimming group the reef-distance smooths were nonsignificant for all indices examined; no transition response distance was reported. The estimated response distances spanned 830–1120 m for the total catches group, 1…

title: Optimized hybrid-chemical synthesis with morphology-controlled synthesis of copper-based nanomaterials as a response to emerging fungal drug resistance
abstract: The rapid development of nanoscience and nanotechnology has unlocked new possibilities in biomedicine, particularly in diagnostics, imaging, and targeted therapies. Among various nanomaterials, metallic nanoparticles, especially those based on copper, have attracted growing interest due to their unique physicochemical properties, ease of synthesis, and broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. In this study, we report the synthesis and characterization of copper-based nanoparticles with significant antifungal activity against Candida spp., a genus responsible for a wide range of fungal infections, including life-threatening invasive candidiasis. Two distinct synthetic approaches were employed: a green, plant-mediated method to produce bimetallic Cu@Au nanoparticles with novel morphologies, and conventional synthesis routes for metallic Cu 2 O and Au nanoparticles. All nanoparticles were evaluated under the same experimental conditions to assess their antifungal efficacy against Candida albicans and Candida krusei , the latter being intrinsically resistant to fluconazole. In addition to their antifungal activity and moderate cytocompatibility at the effective concentrations, the Au@Cu nanoparticles exhibited intrinsic peroxidase-like catalytic activity, as demonstrated by colorimetric assays, UV–Vis spectroscopy, and steady-state kinetic analysis. The enzyme-like catalytic behavior…

title: Case Report: Complete metabolic response to alectinib in a TNS1-ALK-rearranged uterine inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor, with stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligoprogression
abstract: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumors of the uterus harboring a TNS1-ALK fusion are rare, and their response to the anaplastic lymphoma kinase ( ALK ) inhibitor alectinib, including the management of oligoprogression with stereotactic body radiotherapy, is poorly documented. Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumors (IMTs) are mesenchymal tumors that, although generally regarded as rare and low-grade neoplasms, have the potential for local recurrence and, rarely, distant metastasis. Anaplastic lymphoma kinase ( ALK ) gene rearrangements are detected in approximately half of IMTs, representing an important biomarker for targeted therapies. Here we present a 53-year-old woman diagnosed with an inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor of uterine origin who developed metastatic recurrence after surgery and, following the detection of ALK fusion positivity ( TNS1-ALK ), achieved a complete metabolic response with alectinib therapy. A CHEK2 mutation was also identified in the patient, who was evaluated for hereditary cancer predisposition. A rapid response was achieved with alectinib in both the pulmonary metastases and the vaginal recurrence site. After approximately 12 months of alectinib therapy, limited (oligoprogressive) disease developed in the lung; stereotactic body radiotherapy was applied to the pulmonary nodules while systemic alectinib therapy was continued. This case highlights the ef…

title: Resolving the Quantum Origin of Anisotropic Raman Response in Quasi-1D Ta2Ni3Te5
abstract: Abstract Probing anisotropic electron–phonon interactions (EPIs) is fundamental to understanding low-dimensional quantum materials, yet isolating their intrinsic signatures remains a challenge due to the confounding influence of extrinsic effects. Here, we resolve this ambiguity in quasi-one-dimensional Ta2Ni3Te5 through a combination of angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT). Anomalous four-lobe angular dependences were observed in Ag phonon modes, which deviate from the real-valued Raman tensor prediction. Further, we explicitly highlight that, despite their distinct physical origins, light absorption and birefringence yield mathematically identical angular dependencies in Ta2Ni3Te5, rendering phenomenological fitting alone insufficient to identify the true physical mechanism. By employing a full quantum treatment incorporating detailed interaction mechanisms, we capture the qualitative characteristics and mode-to-mode diversity of the anomalous angular responses observed experimentally. The DFPT calculations further reveal mode-specific and momentum-resolved EPIs, providing microscopic support for anisotropic EPIs as the mechanism of anomalous Raman responses.

title: Demand aware spectral resource orchestration through fast fourier transform assisted redundancy suppression for energy efficient multi user MIMO OFDM networks
KinaseMD 2.0: an updated database of kinase mutations and drug response
abstract: Abstract Kinase mutations can alter activity, inhibitor response and downstream phosphorylation signaling, particularly within four resistance-associated substructures: gatekeeper, G-loop, αC-helix, and A-loop. KinaseMD 2.0 (http://modinfor.com/KinaseMD/) updates the kinase-centered database in three areas. Integrating source-curated annotations with Dr. Kinase predictions expanded substructure annotations from 1162 to 13 522 and kinase coverage from 388 to 547. Updated pharmacogenomic and signaling layers contain 422 244 drug-response measurements, 1614 candidate drug-resistance evidence records, and 359 600 predicted phosphorylation-network rewiring events. The new Kinase Perturbation Evidence Mapping (KPEM) workflow combines LLM-based literature extraction from an initial collection of over 480 000 publications with standardized processing of 30 public drug-treatment phosphoproteomic datasets. It provides 23 757 kinase-level records of literature-reported evidence and 53 029 phosphoproteomic records across 5124 drug/agent categories and 1598 disease contexts, distinguishing reported phosphorylation evidence from inferred kinase-associated signaling responses. By linking resistance-associated substructures, cancer mutations, drug response, and phosphorylation signaling, KinaseMD 2.0 supports studies of drug-resistance mechanisms and kinase-inhibitor design and development.

title: Protection of Medical Information Confidentiality as a Function of State Power: Legal Mechanisms and Implementation Challenges
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the problems of protecting the confidentiality of medical information as a special function of state power in the context of the digital transformation of healthcare. The urgency of the problem is due to the introduction of EGISZ, the increasing economic value of medical data, the experience of the COVID-19 pandemic, the fragmentation of legal regulation and the challenges of the globalization of medical services. The article analyzes the multilevel system of legal support for the confidentiality of medical information in the Russian Federation, identifies problems of terminological inconsistency, lack of certainty of criteria for the legality of data disclosure, and gaps in regulating the processing of biometric and genetic information. The new risks of the digital age are being examined: the vulnerability of centralized information systems, the problem of re‑identifying anonymized data, and the ethical and legal dilemmas associated with the use of artificial intelligence.

title: A Charge-Consistent Long-Range Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Compatible with Quantum Linear System Algorithms
abstract: Abstract Charge equilibration in machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) requires repeatedly solving linear systems, providing a promising target for quantum linear-system algorithms (QLSAs). However, conventional electronegativity equalization schemes suffer from spurious fractional charges between neutral fragments at large separations. To address this limitation, we incorporate atom-condensed Kohn–Sham density functional theory approximated to second order (ACKS2) into a long-range equivariant neural-network MLIP. Across benchmark systems, the ACKS2-based model improves energy, force, and charge predictions. At a molecule–metal interface, ACKS2 restores molecular fragments to near-neutral charge states upon separation while preserving local charge redistribution near adsorption. Because ACKS2 charge equilibration reduces to solving a linear system, the classical solver can be directly replaced with the Harrow–Hassidim–Lloyd algorithm during inference, demonstrating compatibility with quantum linear-system solvers. These results indicate that ACKS2 provides a promising framework for charge-aware MLIPs and highlight a potential pathway toward atomistic simulations based on QLSAs.

title: Predictive Beam Management with Spatio-Temporal Hyper Networks and Reinforcement Intelligence for Sustainable Massive MIMO Architectures
abstract: Massive MIMO is the basis of current 5G and future 6G wireless networks, with antenna gain significant spectral efficiency and network capacity, but is unable to support dynamic environments due to computational complexity, power consumption and CSI overhead. The research presents a single adaptive and energy-efficient beam management system, including hybrid analogue-digital beamforming and advanced intelligence based on learning. This system extends Deep Reinforcement Learning to optimize beams in real-time, graph-based learning to optimize beams selectively by topology, neuro-symbolic policy optimization to predict and study control, and spatio-temporal forecasting using hypernetworks to CSI, which cuts feedback costs by a major factor. The proposed framework reduces redundant CSI updates by dynamically changing beam patterns based on user movement, interference, as well as the changes in traffic conditions, and provides strong signals quality and low-latency adaptation. The main innovation is the combination design of prediction beam adaptation and energy aware CSI management. The performance of simulations shows that spectral efficiency, power and computing scalability have been significantly improved, making the solution a viable and future-proof architecture of intelligent massive MIMO network.

title: Unraveling the roles of malicious envy and servant leadership in the ties between everyday sadism and knowledge sabotage
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether malicious envy mediates the relationship between everyday sadism and knowledge sabotage. It also examines whether servant leadership can mitigate malicious envy’s harmful influence on knowledge sabotage. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 355 full-time employees in southeastern Nigeria using a three-wave, time-lagged design. Findings The results confirm that malicious envy mediates the link between everyday sadism and knowledge sabotage. However, contrary to the hypothesis, servant leadership did not moderate the relationship between envy and sabotage. Practical implications Rather than using aggressive screening procedures, organizations should strike a balance by evaluating qualifications, skills and interpersonal dynamics, while focusing on building workplaces that discourage toxic behaviors. Since eliminating envy entirely is unrealistic, management should address its structural roots. This can be done by creating objective, fair reward systems and transparent performance-appraisal processes that reduce zero-sum peer comparisons. Originality/value This study complements previous studies linking malevolent personality traits and insidious emotions to knowledge-related deviance and the role of leadership in mitigating knowledge-related harm.

title: Systemic connectedness and shock transmission across FinTech, clean energy, Islamic and traditional assets
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the dynamic connectedness and risk transmission among FinTech, clean energy, Islamic, and traditional financial assets, with particular emphasis on their behavior under varying market conditions and crisis periods. Design/methodology/approach This study uses conditional autoregressive value-at-risk, frequency connectedness, and wavelet local multiple correlation techniques to capture tail risk dynamics and time-frequency spillovers across asset classes. The analysis is conducted across multiple investment horizons, including daily, weekly, and monthly frequencies. Findings The results reveal a high level of interconnectedness across all asset classes, as indicated by a substantial total connectedness index. Short-term spillovers dominate over medium- and long-term dynamics, suggesting rapid transmission of shocks. The findings further indicate that connectedness patterns intensify during periods of economic and geopolitical stress, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine conflict. Islamic FinTech and Sukuk markets exhibit strong intraclass linkages and significant spillover effects with other financial assets. In addition, certain assets emerge as net risk transmitters, offering potential hedging and diversification benefits during crisis periods. Practical implications The findings provide valuable insights for in…

title: Rail-Guided IoT Imaging System for Leaf-Level Monitoring in Small-Scale Citrus Plots
abstract: This paper presents a rail-guided IoT imaging system designed to overcome the difficulty of obtaining consistent, leaf-level citrus images for long-term agricultural monitoring by combining deterministic electromechanical positioning, embedded control, edge computing, and cloud-based data management. It incorporates a cable-suspended linear actuation mechanism together with two inclined cameras, motion control based on ESP32 microcontrollers, a Raspberry Pi 5 for processing, and AWS S3 for cloud services to automate the processes of image acquisition, synchronization, storage, and remote visualization. By limiting image capture to a fixed and repeatable path, the platform reduces the variation in viewpoint that is typically found with aerial and ground-mobile robots, thus allowing the systematic production of consistent image datasets for use in plant phenotyping and pest monitoring. The system was implemented and tested in a citrus orchard under real-world operating conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the system's autonomous and stable operation, reliable image acquisition, continuous synchronization with the cloud and repeatable monitoring over long periods of time with a low-cost hardware design suitable for research-scale setups. The platform provides a reproducible embedded imaging setup, which improves the consistency of agricultural image acquisition and enables…

title: The Dark Side of Mindfulness at Work: How Mindfulness Training Enlivens Machiavellian Incivility
Comparative Effects of E-Tendering, E-Sourcing, E-Invoicing and Procurement Policy on Public Sector Project Delivery in Nigeria
abstract: While the assessment of public sector project delivery in Nigeria rests on cost and completion time, little evidence has been available to compare e-procurement dimensions on both outcomes at once. Prior studies have tended to test single dimensions of e-procurement in isolation or to rely on a single composite performance measure, leaving procurement managers without evidence on how the dimensions compare directly against each other. This study addressed that gap through a descriptive survey with two regression models, using data collected from 361 procurement staff across four federal organisations in Abuja to compare the effect of e-tendering, e-sourcing, e-invoicing and government e-procurement policy on project cost and project completion time. All four predictors significantly predicted project cost, while only government e-procurement policy and e-invoicing significantly predicted completion time. Government e-procurement policy and e-invoicing recorded the largest unstandardised coefficients for both cost (B = 0.348 and B = 0.189, both p < 0.001) and completion time (B = 0.530 and B = 0.258, both p < 0.001). E-tendering (B = 0.128, p < 0.001) and e-sourcing (B = 0.088, p = 0.004) were significant for cost only, and neither was significant for completion time (p = 0.801 and p = 0.097, respectively). The two models accounted for 50.0% and 61.0% of the variation in cost an…

title: Patient perceptions of artificial intelligence in breast disease management: a cross-sectional survey in China
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly integrated into healthcare, yet patient perceptions—particularly in breast disease management—remain underexplored. Understanding these attitudes is critical for optimizing AI implementation and addressing disparities in trust and acceptance. Objective To assess patient attitudes toward AI tools in breast disease management and identify how age and education influence willingness to adopt AI in clinical settings in China. Methods A cross-sectional, online, questionnaire-based survey was conducted among patients who underwent surgery for breast diseases in the Department of Breast Surgery at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH) through the wenjuanxing application (a survey platform) from March to May 2025. Of 530 invited participants, 457 (response rate: 86.2%) completed the questionnaire, which evaluated prior AI use, trust levels, concerns, and willingness to engage with AI tools. Primary outcomes included perceptions of AI utility, trust in AI versus physician recommendations, privacy concerns, and willingness to use AI for pre-diagnosis, triage, and clinical decision support. Results Among participants, 91.7% found AI tools at least “somewhat helpful,” though 66.7% cited lack of emotional support as a key drawback. When AI and physician advice conflicted, 50.8% fully trusted doctors, while 43.3% preferre…

title: Visibility management and profile construction on Tinder
abstract: Purpose This article examines how visibility and recognizability are configured through self-presentation on Tinder. It conceptualizes visibility management as a framework for examining the degree and form of exposure through which users become available for recognition and evaluation within a platform environment. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on digital ethnography and qualitative analysis of 100 Tinder profiles, the study examines recurrent configurations of facial and bodily recognizability, visual concealment and other forms of visual and textual disclosure. The corpus consists of female profiles presented to two research accounts in the Barcelona area in 2023. Findings The findings identify three modes of profile presentation: concealment, negotiation and integration. These modes capture different configurations of exposure and recognizability. Concealment substantially restricts physical recognizability while retaining varying forms of visual or textual disclosure; negotiation combines recognizable and obscured elements within the same profile; and integration combines comparatively high physical recognizability with curated lifestyle representation. Rather than operating through a simple opposition between visibility and concealment, these modes indicate a continuum in which bodily exposure, facial recognizability and other forms of disclosure vary independently a…

title: Deciphering Salinity Tolerance in Mungbean (Vigna radiata L.) through Root System Architecture, Multivariate Divergence Analysis and Multi-trait Ideotype Selection
abstract: Background: Soil salinity is a major abiotic constraint on mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) productivity. Breeding resilient varieties requires an understanding of genetic diversity and the identification of salt-tolerant genotypes, with root system architecture being a key determinant of adaptation to saline conditions. Methods: The experiment was conducted at Lovely Professional University, Punjab, using a factorial randomized block design (FRBD) with three replications. Root architecture was examined via scanning, while genetic divergence was assessed using Mahalanobis D2 cluster analysis and principal component analysis. Genotype screening employed nine stress tolerance indices along with the multi-trait genotype Ideotype distance index (MGIDI). Result: Root structure progressively deteriorated with increasing salinity, with KDMB-5023 and KDMB-5025 showing relatively greater structural resilience. Mahalanobis D2 analysis grouped genotypes into four clusters, with the maximum inter-cluster distance observed between Cluster I and Cluster IV (D2 = 8.498). Principal component analysis retained three components explaining 92.40% of total variation, with plant height, shoot length, vigour index and leaf area collectively contributing 82.47% of genetic divergence. Multi-index stress tolerance analysis identified KDMB-5020, KDMB-5030, KDMB-5014, KDMB-5025 and KDMB-5001 as the most tole…

title: HIV–brucellosis coinfection in a pastoral region of China: clinical features, diagnosis, and management in a seven-patient case series
abstract: Background Brucellosis is an under-recognized opportunistic and endemic infection in people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLWH), particularly in pastoral settings with frequent livestock exposure. Evidence from China remains limited, and practical guidance on diagnosing and co-managing brucellosis with antiretroviral therapy (ART) is scarce. Methods We conducted a single-center, retrospective case series of seven consecutive PLWH with confirmed brucellosis managed at a tertiary infectious diseases referral hospital in northwest China between July 2021 and May 2025. Diagnosis was based on blood culture and/or standard tube agglutination test (SAT) according to accepted diagnostic thresholds. Data on demographics, exposure history, clinical manifestations, diagnostic findings, treatment, co-infections, and follow-up outcomes were abstracted from medical records. Results All seven patients were male, with a median age of 46 years (IQR 36–75), and all had documented livestock-related exposure. Constitutional symptoms were common, while focal manifestations were prominent. Two patients had lumbar spondylitis/spondylodiscitis, including one who required surgical intervention, and two had epididymo-orchitis and/or hydroceles. Brucellosis was confirmed by blood culture in four patients, while six had positive SAT results; one patient was culture-positive but persistently SA…

title: Innovative management practices, regulatory policy, and institutional resilience amid economic turbulence
abstract: The article examines innovative management practices in the context of turbulence in global markets. The current economic environment is characterized by high uncertainty, frequent external shocks and instability, which reduces the effectiveness of traditional management approaches and requires a transition to more flexible decision-making models. The theoretical basis of the study is approaches to management in conditions of high uncertainty, complexity and rapid changes, as well as the concept of dynamic capabilities of enterprises, which explains their ability to adapt, use new opportunities and restructure internal resources. The empirical analysis is carried out on the example of Ukraine as an economy functioning in conditions of increased turbulence. The study used the Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index and the Geopolitical Risk Index as the main indicators of external shocks. The index of industrial production and inflation are used as indicators of the real sector. The methodology includes correlation and regression analysis, including verification of nonlinear dependencies, analysis of time lags, as well as autoregressive integrated moving average modeling of time series. The study period covers 1997–2025. The results showed that geopolitical risks have a statistically significant and non-linear impact on industrial production, while global economic uncertainty d…

title: Developing and Evaluating Digital School Asset Management for Accountability in an Indonesian Island District
abstract: Elementary schools require reliable asset information to account for infrastructure and coordinate district oversight. This study developed and evaluated a digital School Asset Management Information System (SIMA) in Tinangkung, an Indonesian island district. An ADDIE research-and-development process combined baseline interviews and surveys, model design, expert review, pilot testing, and an expanded one-group pretest–posttest evaluation. Four experts judged the model fit for implementation with minor revisions; 30 users completed an 18-item practicality questionnaire; and 14 schools contributed paired accountability measurements. Preliminary responses showed manual records in 10 of 11 schools (90.9%) and no direct district data integration in seven (63.6%). The initial practicality score was 75.51% of the possible total. After implementation, mean data accuracy increased from 74.2% to 98.2%, reporting timeliness from 0.0% to 92.3%, and digital asset traceability from 75.4% to 100.0%. Mean normalized gains were 0.94, 0.92, and 1.00, respectively. Primary paired comparisons were statistically significant at the 5% level. The findings indicate promising short-term administrative improvements associated with a three-axis school–cloud–district system, while the absence of a comparison group prevents exclusive causal attribution. The analysis concerns operational governance indicato…

A host-tumor interaction-based five-dimensional risk stratification system integrating immune surveillance, inflammation, nutrition, coagulation, and tumor burden for prognostic evaluation in stage III colorectal cancer
abstract: Objective Stage III colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits substantial prognostic heterogeneity, underscoring the need for robust risk stratification tools. We aimed to develop and validate a novel five-dimensional (5D) score integrating immune surveillance, inflammation, nutrition, coagulation, and tumor burden to improve prognostic assessment in these patients. Materials and methods We retrospectively enrolled 338 patients with stage III CRC, who were randomly assigned to a discovery cohort (n=228) and a validation cohort (n=110). Preoperative peripheral blood biomarkers were detected before surgery to construct the 5D score. Patients were followed for three years to assess recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS). Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox proportional hazards regression, and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to evaluate the prognostic performance of the score. Results Low levels of the combined lymphocyte-eosinophil-basophil immune- surveillance axis and prealbumin, together with elevated monocyte counts, fibrinogen, and the combined CEA-CA19–9 score, were significantly associated with inferior survival. The 5D score showed a strong stepwise association with both RFS and OS (plog-rank<0.001). Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified the 5D risk stratification system as an independent prognostic factor i…

title: The impact of centralized drug purchasing policy on pediatric medicines and related health system performance outcomes: a systematic review and evidence gap map
abstract: Background Centralized drug purchasing policies have been applied in many countries, but the impact on pediatric medicine supply has been controversial. In this study, we evaluated the impact of centralized drug purchasing policies on pediatric medicines and related health system performance outcomes. Methods Eight databases, including Cochrane, Embase (Ovid), and PubMed and so on, were searched from inception to August 2026. Two researchers independently conducted literature screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. The main outcomes were categorized according to the WHO-HSPA framework. Thematic analysis was used to summarize the evidence of these outcomes and create an evidence gap map. Results Twelve studies were included in this study, all from China. These comprised two ITS, three uncontrolled before–after studies, two controlled before–after studies, and four surveys, with seven at high risk of bias, four at moderate risk, and one at low risk. The studies covered seven pharmaceutical system outcome domains and four health system performance outcome domains. Centralized drug purchasing policies could reduce the price, cost, and increase the affordability of selected medicines, indicating financial protection, without a significant impact on effectiveness, safety, and efficiency. However, they could also lead to issues such as clinicians’ distrust in the quality o…

title: A sustainable natural resource management hierarchical model in Vietnamese mining industry: environmental policy and regulation impacts on technical operation capability
abstract: Purpose This study builds a sustainable natural resource management (SNRM) model, as prior studies on how environmental policy and regulation and stakeholder involvement incorporate technical operation capability are lacking, and comprehensive insights into the specific challenges and strategies for SNRM practices are needed. Design/methodology/approach This study aims to identify a valid set of attributes for SNRM in the Vietnamese mining industry, develop a causal hierarchical model and identify the important attributes for improvement via a hybrid approach. Institutional theory, stakeholder theory and dynamic capability theory under the foundation of the socio-technical perspective theory are applied. Findings The hierarchical structure of SNRM includes 4 perspectives, 8 aspects and 22 criteria, with causal aspects such as environmental policy and regulation, financing mechanisms, stakeholder involvement and digital transformation. The practical focuses are environmental governance, green financing, external suppliers and joint venture partners, renewable energy adoption, and automation and robotics. Technological innovation plays crucial roles in SNRM adoption. Originality/value This study develops a theoretically grounded causal SNRM framework integrating institutional, stakeholder, dynamic capability and socio-technical perspectives, while extending SNRM through technolog…

title: Ectogenesis and Biosafety: Challenges of Artificial Reproduction for the Constitutional Law Status of the Embryo and the Person
abstract: The article examines the transformation of the constitutional and legal status of the embryo and fetus in the context of emerging ectogenesis technologies. It substantiates the necessity of granting the unborn fetus a special protective sui generis status, which serves as a public-law biosecurity safeguard against commercialization, eugenic practices, and property-based utilitarian use.

title: Exercise of Human Rights to Preserve, Modify and Protect Genetic Information
abstract: The rapid development of genetic technologies, the sequencing of the human genome, and the expanding practice of using genetic information in medicine, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology inevitably bring to the forefront the issue of legal protection of a person from the improper use of their genetic data. Genetic information is no longer just a part of personal data; it is a new type of information that does not fall under either personal data or medical confidentiality and is subject to special legal protection due to the fact that such data is inextricably linked to the individual, their dignity, including intangible benefits such as spirituality, integrity, and individuality. The category of personal dignity in relation to genetic data acquires particular significance. It concerns the inadmissibility of reducing a person to their biological characteristics, the protection against genetic discrimination, and the right of a person to independently determine the fate of their genetic information. In this context, it is appropriate to speak of the formation of bioethical personal dignity as a complex legal value that includes the right to informational autonomy, bodily integrity, and protection from any forms of reductionism in which a person is considered solely as a carrier of the genetic code.

Do what you want to do: an analysis of positive mental health literacy among pre-service teachers at a regional university in China
abstract: Positive mental health literacy (PMHL) is an important resource for promoting psychological wellbeing and resilience. Research on teachers’ mental health literacy has, however, concentrated on the recognition of mental illness among in-service teachers; its positive dimension has rarely been examined among pre-service teachers, and never in relation to their motivation for entering the profession. This study investigated the level of PMHL among pre-service teachers, examined differences in PMHL across demographic and background characteristics, and explored their perceptions of factors related to positive mental health. A convergent mixed-methods design was adopted, and data were collected from 455 pre-service teachers at a regional teacher-education university in Hunan Province, China, using a questionnaire comprising demographic items, a PMHL scale, and four open-ended questions. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t -tests, and one-way ANOVA, while qualitative data were analysed through thematic analysis. The findings showed that pre-service teachers demonstrated a generally high level of PMHL ( M = 3.78, SD = 0.67).
