title: Death marks the spot
Trust, Reputation, and the Market for Lemons: A Free-Energy Model of Endogenous Belief Refinement
abstract: This paper examines how internalized honesty and reputation can mitigate adverse selection when buyers lack an exogenous quality index. A privately informed seller probabilistically chooses whether to offer or withhold a product using a free-energy policy rule. Internalized norms enter as a prior policy bias, whereas reputation changes anticipated consequences. A buyer observing an offer updates beliefs about quality through Bayes’ rule and decides whether to purchase at an exogenous posted price. Seller payoffs specify reservation values, offering costs, and expected reputational losses. Seller policy incorporates the anticipated probability of purchase, and a behavioral consistency condition requires this anticipation to agree with the buyer’s optimal response. On the full-purchase branch, stronger honesty and reputation discourage lemon offers and increase the buyer’s posterior probability of high quality. I derive a threshold under which purchase after an offer is strategically consistent and high-quality trade occurs with positive probability. This is a result about posted-price trade rather than a complete Akerlof-type unraveling equilibrium. The framework shows how socially embedded behavior can generate informative seller actions without a physical quality index.

title: Numerical Assessment of Wave Energy Conversion into Electricity in Lebanon: Modeling, Techno-Economic and Environmental Analysis
abstract: Lebanon’s prolonged electricity crisis has renewed interest in renewable energy; yet the wave energy resource of its 220 km Mediterranean coastline has not been reassessed since 2013 and has never been evaluated within an integrated techno-economic framework. Model-derived daily significant wave heights for 2022 and 2023 at three coastal sites (Tripoli, Beirut and Saida), obtained from an operational wave forecast and compared with three other wave datasets, were analyzed with linear wave theory, consistently with the offshore origin of the data. Three wave energy converters (Pelamis, Wave Dragon and AquaBuoy) were evaluated from their power matrices, followed by techno-economic and CO2 emission assessments. The annual mean wave power flux was 2.6–4.3 kW/m (other wave datasets: 1.4–3.2 kW/m), about 41% lower than the preliminary shallow-water estimate, and a 31-year reanalysis shows that 2022 was an average year and 2023 about 10% below average. All converters operated far below their rated power: Wave Dragon had the highest capacity factor (about 4.9%), three to four times lower than for the same device in the Madeira Archipelago, but with interpolated power matrices its output was halved and Pelamis ranks first. With 2026 costs and electricity valued at the weighted avoided cost of the current utility–generator supply (0.419 USD/kWh, an upper-bound revenue case), the 20-year …

title: Civil Society and the Market: Are They Necessary Protagonists or Antagonists?
abstract: One of the most persistent and perplexing ideas in social science is civil society, which makes it a great subject for analytical investigation. Because it provides a flexible framework for analyzing the "geometry of human relations," or the patterns of group behavior and interaction that give societies at least some answers to issues of structure and authority, meaning and belonging, citizenship and self-direction, the idea has endured. Since classical Greece, intellectuals have looked back to civil society as a means of coming up with fresh perspectives on age-old and well known issues as their surroundings have changed. However, because there are so many different definitions and understandings of civil society—many of which are poorly connected to and articulated with one another—and because the claims that are occasionally made about its explanatory power never quite match the complexities and contingencies of actual cultures and societies—particularly when interpretations created at one time or in one part of the world are transported to another—civil society is also a confusing and contentious concept. The history of civil society has at least three centuries of interactions with business and the market, but since the fall of the Berlin Wall and the emergence of corporate social responsibility in the late 1980s and early 1990s, these interactions have become much more fr…

title: Enhancing Strategic Decision Quality through Market and Competitive Intelligence
abstract: The value of competitive intelligence can be assessed by examining how its findings inform strategic choices. Which assumptions did the analysis lead decision-makers to reconsider, and how did it shape their evaluation of strategic alternatives? These questions become increasingly important as digital platforms and artificial intelligence expand organizations’ capacity to process information. Assessing the value of this expanded capacity requires understanding how managers interpret analytical findings and whether their use improves the quality of strategic decisions. Integrating market, competitor, and customer information is an established approach within competitive intelligence. Earlier research links this integration to understanding the external environment and supporting strategic decisions (Aspinall, 2011; Santos & Correia, 2010). The contribution of contemporary research therefore lies in explaining the mechanisms through which organizations identify relevant signals, assess their interpretations, and apply the resulting insights. Recent scholarship examines competitive intelligence in relation to data analytics capabilities and conceptually connects it to sensing external change, taking strategic action, and organizational adaptation (e.g., Černý et al., 2026; Ranjan & Foropon, 2021). The research challenge is therefore to explain the mechanisms through which integrat…

title: Platforms as Enforcement Infrastructure: Copyright in China’s Online Music Market
abstract: Abstract Between 2012 and 2018, China’s online music market transformed from a piracy-dominated environment into one of the world’s largest licensed digital music markets. This Article explains that transformation through the concept of platforms as enforcement infrastructure, emphasizing platforms’ capacity not only to regulate their own users but to project legal enforcement beyond their individual domains and across the broader internet ecosystem, through both formal legal processes and informal enforcement channels. Drawing on legal and regulatory analysis and an original dataset of copyright infringement judgments, the Article argues that three interrelated conditions made large-scale enforcement possible: consolidated state capacity to discipline major platforms; the prospect of market concentration that incentivized platforms to invest in the purchase and enforcement of exclusive licenses; and the technological, financial, and legal capacity of platforms to enforce copyright at scale. Under these conditions, platforms became central to the practical operationalization of copyright beyond their own domains. At the same time, this enforcement model generated structural costs, including heightened market concentration and the expansion of content control.

title: From Green Rewards to Green Customers: A Systematic Review of the Market-Facing Outcomes of Green Human Resource Management
abstract: Green human resource management (GHRM) is expected to support credible sustainability positioning, but its customer and market effects remain unclear. This systematic review examines GHRM and green rewards in relation to these outcomes. Searches of Scopus and Web of Science identified 23 empirical studies. Selection followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020; synthesis used a context–intervention–mechanism–outcome framework, the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, direction-based vote counting and certainty grading. All reported effects were positive. Reputation outcomes showed the largest coefficients and strong certainty under the review’s rules, but 12 of 13 studies did not use customer ratings. Customer outcomes and customer-directed employee behaviour received moderate certainty. Only three studies isolated reward-related effects, whose relative magnitudes were inconsistent; none tested the full employee-to-customer chain. Identified mechanisms included employee commitment, green knowledge sharing, shared green experiences and green branding. Environmental regulation strengthened associations. The review develops a multilevel framework, six design propositions and a research agenda. The findings suggest that market value depends on the visibility and credibility of green practices, while green rewards remain largely untested as a distinc…

title: Co-Movement and Market Integration of Bitcoin and Ethereum: An Empirical Correlation Analysis
abstract: The rising relevance of cryptocurrencies as investments has drawn attention to the analysis of how the values of such investments correlate with each other. In particular, this research paper studies BTC/ETH co-movement and evaluates the strength of the relationship between Bitcoin and Ethereum as well as the consequences for portfolio diversification. To investigate co-movement, daily prices of BTC and ETH are collected from Yahoo Finance for the period from January 2018 to December 2024. This dataset is made up of 2,557 observations for each cryptocurrency. Descriptive statistics, graph analysis and Pearson correlation analysis are used to study BTC and ETH prices. The results have shown that there is a very strong positive co-movement between BTC and ETH (Pearson coefficient = 0.9036 (CI 95%: 0.8962 - 0.9104; *p* < .001)). The positively skewed distributions of Bitcoin and Ethereum were observed. Besides, Bitcoin had larger dispersion and higher kurtosis than Ethereum. Normalised prices showed the general similarity of the two cryptocurrencies' price behavior with the exception that the 2021 rally was more successful for Ethereum and the 2024 growth was more significant for Bitcoin. Nevertheless, because the study uses price levels as the basis for the test, it becomes necessary to conduct further tests using correlation measures based on returns in order to measure their ma…

title: Digital food delivery services in an emerging market: socioeconomic determinants and implications for service adoption in Türkiye
abstract: This study aims to identify the demographic, economic, and technological factors associated with individuals’ likelihood of ordering food online in Türkiye. Understanding these determinants is essential for enhancing digital food service accessibility and consumer satisfaction in emerging economies. Using nationally representative microdata from the 2023 Turkish Statistical Institute’s Household Information Technologies Survey, a binary logistic regression model was employed to estimate the probability of online food ordering. The model incorporated demographic variables (age, gender, education), economic factors (income and occupation), digital access indicators (computer ownership, social media use, and online information search), and regional classifications. Survey weights were applied to ensure representativeness. Results reveal that income level, age, gender, education, occupation, ownership of digital devices, social media use, and region were significantly associated with online food ordering behaviour. Women and younger, higher-income, and better-educated individuals are more likely to order food online. Regional disparities persist, with western Türkiye showing higher adoption rates than central and eastern regions, reflecting a digital divide in food delivery engagement. The findings suggest that improving technological infrastructure, digital literacy, and service q…

title: Direitos, trabalho e migração: percepções de imigrantes sobre o mercado de trabalho em Caçador, Santa Catarina
abstract: O aumento do fluxo migratório para o Brasil, impulsionado por crises econômicas, políticas e humanitárias, tem ampliado a presença de trabalhadores estrangeiros em diversos setores. Nesse contexto, este estudo analisa as percepções de imigrantes sobre desafios e oportunidades no mercado de trabalho em Caçador/SC. Com abordagem mista e natureza aplicada, a pesquisa utilizou um questionário on-line composto por 17 questões, aplicado a 110 imigrantes, majoritariamente haitianos, além de cubanos e venezuelanos. As análises quantitativas foram conduzidas por estatística descritiva e as qualitativas por análise de conteúdo. Os resultados revelam que a barreira linguística constitui o principal obstáculo à integração laboral, seguida pela dificuldade de reconhecimento de diplomas, o que limita o acesso a ocupações compatíveis com a formação dos imigrantes. Preconceito, adaptação cultural e burocracia documental também aparecem, ainda que em menor escala. O estudo contribui ao evidenciar fragilidades estruturais na inclusão socioprofissional de imigrantes e ao propor ações voltadas ao ODS 8, especialmente no que diz respeito ao trabalho decente e à redução das desigualdades.

title: The natural history of interstitial lung disease in common variable immunodeficiency
Parameter-Efficient Temporal Convolutional Networks for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
abstract: Accurate prediction of multivariate datasets increasingly relies on deep learning models, often increasing complexity and computing requirements, particularly for multi-horizon predictions. This work proposes a model designed to significantly reduce computing requirements while retaining predictive accuracy. By replacing standard convolutions with depthwise and grouped pointwise operations, the model preserves temporal processing and captures dependencies without substantially complicating the architecture. Evaluated on five multivariate datasets across four forecasting horizons, the proposed model is compared against conventional and depthwise Temporal Convolutional Networks; lightweight variants, such as TSMixer and FITS; and advanced models like Informer, Autoformer, and iTransformer. It reduces multiply–accumulate operations by 58.9–70.8% and trainable parameters by 14.15–35.8% compared to standard temporal convolution networks. Notably, forecasting accuracy varies across datasets and horizons, with small differences between TCN variants corresponding to run-to-run variability. The findings reveal that the model excels in accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, offering an alternative for multivariate time-series forecasting when computational cost is a critical consideration.

title: Multi-Sensor Wharf Yard Settlement Forecasting via SSA-PCA Sensor Fusion and Heterogeneous Gradient Boosting
abstract: Accurate prediction of wharf yard settlement is difficult because monitoring records combine long-term drift, nonlinear load responses, sensor noise, and redundant exogenous variables. This study presents a three-stage framework that integrates multi-sensor data, separates trend and residual components, and combines heterogeneous learners. An ARIMA model first extracts the linear settlement trend. Singular spectrum analysis then denoises temperature and stress signals, principal component analysis reduces their dimension, and explicit temporal encodings represent daily, weekly, and long-term patterns. A sliding window joins the historical residuals with the exogenous and temporal features. XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost predict the residual correction on complementary feature subsets, with hyperparameters tuned independently for each library, and their out-of-fold predictions are combined by non-negative least squares (NNLS) weights estimated separately for each monitoring station. The trend and residual predictions are finally combined. Tests on 60 days of hourly data from 15 monitoring stations yield an MSE of 1.0098, and an R2 of 0.9492. The method outperforms the LSTM, Prophet-XGBoost, and other evaluated baselines.

title: A Solar-Powered Multiparameter IoT Buoy for Dissolved-Oxygen Monitoring and Short-Term Water-Quality Forecasting in a High-Altitude Trout Raceway
abstract: In high-altitude trout raceways, dissolved oxygen (DO) declines are brief and start from a narrow margin below saturation. We built a solar-powered floating node with five water-quality channels, a serviceable probe cartridge, switched sensor rails and store-before-transmit telemetry and operated it for 89 days in a raceway at 2100 m a.s.l. (Amazonas, Peru). It recorded 25,522 five-minute observations (99.57% coverage) with 99.95% packet delivery. Under calibration transfer, DO error was 0.100 mg L−1 and the field variability of temperature, DO and turbidity exceeded it 3.5–4.2-fold. On a chronologically separated test period, three-hour DO RMSE was 0.180 mg L−1 with five-channel inputs and 0.260 mg L−1 with DO-history inputs alone, against 0.362 mg L−1 for an hour-of-day control. Six-hour gains were not resolved: departures from the diel course had decorrelated, the test period shifted toward low DO and turbidity events, and out-of-range conductivity produced spurious troughs. A three-hour DO < 6.5 mg L−1 classifier reached ROC-AUC 0.946 and, with two-sample confirmation, detected all 24 complete low-DO episodes, against 15 with DO history alone. Battery-terminal measurements showed the awake controller as the largest identified load; calculated balances indicated that the installed 15 W module sustains the five-minute cycle and that deep-sleep standby would cut daily charge b…

title: Meteorology-Guided Randomness-Operator PSO Optimization of RBF Neural Networks for Real-World Photovoltaic Power Forecasting: A Case Study of a 20 MW PV Plant in Jining, China
abstract: This paper presents a novel photovoltaic (PV) power prediction method based on a radial basis function neural network (RBF-NN) and randomness-operator particle swarm optimization (ROPSO). The ROPSO method uses the range of meteorological variables to construct a search space to optimize the RBF-NN. First, ROPSO analyzes the possible range of unknown parameters defined by the meteorological conditions of the plant site. Then, based on the range of unknown parameters, ROPSO constructs a squeezed search space for the RBF-NN, thus speeding up the parameter identification process and making the identification process more efficient. A real case study of a 20 MW grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system in Jining City, China, is used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed forecasting technique. Various evaluation metrics, including the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (R2), are employed to assess the effectiveness of the prediction scheme. The simulation and numerical results indicate that the radial basis function neural network model optimized by ROPSO can achieve higher efficiency compared to other alternatives.

title: A Short-Term Load and Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Method Based on Robust Data Preprocessing and QPSO-BiLSTM
abstract: Accurate short-term load and photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for power-system dispatch and renewable-energy accommodation under high PV penetration. However, measured source-load data often contain outliers and missing values, while the forecasting performance of bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks is sensitive to hyperparameter selection. This paper develops an integrated short-term load and PV power forecasting framework that combines characteristic-aware robust data preprocessing with BiLSTM modeling tuned by quantum particle swarm optimization (QPSO). An iterative 3σ criterion is first used to detect spike, drop, negative, and flat anomalies according to the different characteristics of load and PV data, and piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation is then applied to repair abnormal and missing points. A BiLSTM network is used to capture bidirectional temporal dependencies, and QPSO is introduced to optimize the number of hidden units, maximum training epochs, and learning rate. Experiments were conducted on measured load and PV datasets with a 15 min resolution, and the proposed model was compared with long short-term memory (LSTM), BiLSTM, and a BiLSTM tuned by particle swarm optimization (PSO), denoted PSO-BiLSTM. In the primary forecasting evaluation on measured grid data, QPSO-BiLSTM achieved mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) values…

title: Expert Strategies: Controversies in Management of Sinonasal Malignancies—Global Perspectives Through a Mixed Methods Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Sinonasal malignancies (SNMs) are a rare group of diseases with limited high‐level evidence to guide management. Where data are currently lacking, contemporary management principles may be guided by clinical expertise and experience. Methods Structured qualitative thematic interviews with multidisciplinary international experts in the management of SNMs. A mixed‐methods design involving qualitative and quantitative analysis of the collected data was completed. Results A total of 40 experts comprising 22 academic institutions across nine countries were included. Surgical factors, including anatomic limitations of resectability and criteria for consideration of orbital exenteration, are discussed. There are mixed opinions on the role of induction systemic therapy and when to employ its use. Nuances in the management of specific histopathologies, including olfactory neuroblastoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, sinonasal mucosal melanoma, adenocarcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma, are explored. Commonalities and discrepancies between experts are summarized. The importance of histopathology‐specific management and multidisciplinary management is highlighted. Conclusions Management of SNMs is complex, with a wide variety of practice patterns among experts. This work serves as a modern …

title: Parameter-Level Attribution of Uncertainty in Electricity Carbon Footprint Factors: A Case Study of Coal-Fired and Hydropower Plants in a Chinese Province
abstract: Provincial carbon footprint factors of electricity underpin product carbon footprints, green certificate trading, and carbon border adjustment, yet their uncertainty is usually reported as one aggregate interval that does not show which part better measurement could reduce and which part an accounting convention fixes. This case study examines eight plants in one Chinese province with original 2025 accounting workbooks (four coal-fired, four hydropower). Each is rebuilt into a normalized parametric model reproducing the original total. Measurable quantities are propagated by Monte Carlo sampling and apportioned with variance-based sensitivity indices; database choices and accounting conventions are enumerated as discrete scenarios and compared with, rather than added to, the probabilistic interval. For the coal-fired plants, the measurement-driven 95% interval is about −11% to +12%, dominated by coal input; the background database shifts the factor by a comparable amount, whereas every accounting convention shifts it by less than 30% of the interval half-width. For the hydropower plants, the interval is wider, yet harmonizing the amortization horizon of civil works alone moves the factor by 1.5 to 2.8 times that half-width. The findings are specific to the sample and suggest differentiating data collection and factor publication by generation type.

title: Fairness-Constrained Coordination of Distributed PV and Battery Storage in Grid-Connected Energy Communities: A Seasonal Assessment
abstract: Coordinating distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation and battery storage can improve local renewable utilization. However, the schedule that produces the lowest total operating cost may not benefit all participants equally. Aggregate indicators can also conceal seasonal grid dependence. This paper develops a season-aware co-optimization framework for battery dispatch and local energy sharing in grid-connected energy communities, combining economic efficiency and distributive fairness with a seasonal assessment of energy autonomy. Evaluation covers 6576 hourly intervals from January to September 2024 for a 100-user subset of a Norwegian Energy-Community Dataset, including 87 residential and 13 commercial users. Five counterfactual scenarios distinguish standalone operation, sharing, private batteries, coordinated sharing and storage, and fairness-constrained coordination. A monthly two-stage ε-constraint formulation first minimizes community operating cost, then maximizes the minimum normalized user saving relative to private-battery operation, subject to individual no-harm constraints. Unconstrained coordination reduces cost, grid imports, and exports by 4.7%, 7.5%, and 82.7%, respectively, relative to standalone operation. With an allowable fractional increase above the minimum community-cost value of 0.5%, the fairness-constrained solution retains a 4.6% saving against stand…

title: Estimation of Precipitable Water Vapor over the Caucasus Region Using the Mesoscale WRF Model
abstract: Ground-based millimeter and submillimeter astronomy requires detailed astroweather and astroclimatic studies of potential sites in mountain regions. Using the mesoscale WRF model, validated against data from three upper-air stations, we examined the spatiotemporal distribution of precipitable water vapor (PWV), effective height of water vapor, wind field and cloudiness over the Caucasus region for the period from 26 March to 4 April 2025. Three operating observatories—SAO RAS, GAS GAO and Peak Terskol as well as three mountain summits in Dagestan, namely Dzhufudag, Kurapdag and Shunudag, promising for millimeter and submillimeter observations—were considered. The sites fall into two groups differing in the variability in PWV: a western group with values of 9.3 ± 1.9 mm at SAO RAS and GAS GAO (coefficient of variation 20–21%) and an eastern group (Dagestan) with a drier atmosphere ranging from 2.8 ± 1.2 to 4.3 ± 1.6 mm (36–42%). Given the similar values of effective height, the key factors driving the contrast in moisture content are the heights of sites, synoptic advection, and the specific pattern of airflows around local topographic features. The averaged PWV field is strongly shaped by orography: ranging from 4–8 mm along the high-mountain part of the Caucasus Range to 16–20 mm over the lowlands. On the night of 1–2 April 2025, when the regional minimum was observed, PWV fel…

title: Multi-Objective Planning of Distributed Energy Storage Considering Distribution-Level Electricity Market Simulation
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-objective distributed energy storage planning method that couples distribution-level electricity market simulation to improve the coordination between storage investment, market participation, and distribution network operation. The method incorporates technical–market-based candidate-bus screening, joint energy and frequency regulation market clearing with endogenous price formation, and life-cycle economic assessment. An improved NSGA-II algorithm is employed to obtain the Pareto-optimal solutions, while the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) is used to select a compromise solution among annualized life-cycle net cost, nodal voltage deviations, and network losses. The proposed method is evaluated on an extended IEEE 33-bus distribution system using 24-h typical-day load and renewable generation profiles. Compared with the baseline scenario, the selected storage configuration reduces average network losses from 0.20135 MW to 0.08235 MW and average nodal voltage deviations from 0.028 p.u. to 0.019 p.u., while increasing the renewable energy accommodation rate from 81.73% to 95.63%. The resulting storage investment achieves a life-cycle net present value of CNY 0.8745 million with a simple payback period of 7.33 years. In addition, compared with the PSO-based energy storage planning method, the method proposed in t…

title: Climate variability and electricity demand in Sub-Saharan African economies
abstract: This study examines the role of climate conditions in shaping per-capita electricity demand across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). The analysis uses a balanced panel dataset covering 45 countries over 2000–2021, representing 990 country-year observations. To capture potential non-linear effects, a Panel Threshold Regression (PTR) model is employed, with intra-annual temperature variability serving as the threshold variable. The results reveal a statistically significant threshold at 27.04 °C 2 of intra-annual temperature variance, equivalent to a monthly temperature standard deviation of 5.20 °C, indicating that the impact of temperature on electricity demand differs across climate regimes. Below this threshold, greater temperature variability is associated with higher electricity consumption, by approximately 21.9 kWh per capita in Model 1 (not statistically significant) and 27.8 kWh per capita in Model 2 (significant at the 10% level), for each additional one-unit (1 °C 2 ) increase in intra-annual temperature variance. Seasonal estimates show that temperature fluctuations during June–August (JJA) have the strongest influence below the threshold, whereas September–November (SON) exerts the largest effect above it. Oil rents are associated with lower electricity demand, a pattern consistent with, though not conclusive proof of, substitution toward fuel-based energy alternatives. Pop…

title: The Sky’s the Limit: Asset Price Spirals When Margin Traders Are All In
abstract: Abstract We analyze a setting in which some investors are all in and buy as much of a risky asset as their margins allow. A higher price of the asset increases all-in investors’ wealth, against which they borrow to buy more shares. If all-in investors have enough wealth and access to at least 2:1 leverage, then prices can spiral upward indefinitely. This is true even if there exist deep-pocketed investors with no explicit limits to arbitrage. Increasing access for retail investors to leverage through leveraged ETFs, derivatives, and margin suggests increasing opportunities for price spirals and collapses. (JEL G12, G30)

An Analysis of Market Types and Price Behaviour of Gram (Cicer arietinum L.) in Hanumangarh District of Rajasthan, India
abstract: Background: Gram (chickpea) production and marketing are important to farm households in Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan. Evidence jointly addressing crop growth, seasonal prices, growers’ perceptions of price factors and marketing channels at district level remains limited. Aims: To estimate growth in the area, production and productivity of gram, to study and forecast its price behaviour, to rank the factors affecting its price, and to examine the relationship between market types and price in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan, India. Study Design: A descriptive-cum-analytical design combining a primary cross-sectional farm survey with secondary time-series data. Place and Duration of Study: Nohar and Bhadra blocks of Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan; the primary survey was conducted during the 2024–25 rabi marketing season, with secondary data for 2004–05 to 2023–24 (area, production, productivity) and 2013–2025 (monthly modal prices). Methodology: A total of 120-gram growers were selected by multistage sampling and interviewed using a structured, pre-tested schedule. The Compound Growth Rate (CGR) and seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) models were used for growth analysis and price forecasting, the Weighted Mean Score (WMS) for ranking price-determining factors, and Pearson’s correlation for the market-type–price relationship. Ignition Theoretical Prediction Model for Aircraft Fuel Tanks Impacted by Polymer-Based Reactive Materials
abstract: Abstract Reactive fragment Al/W/PTFE is a novel polymer-based composite material, which is mainly applied to impact aircraft fuel tanks. The coupled kinetic-chemical energy damage of Al/W/PTFE makes the damage process of the aircraft fuel tank ignition extremely complex. Currently, there is no comprehensive model to predict the outcome of ignition damage. In this study, an ignition theoretical prediction model was first established. First, based on the comprehensive temperature rise of reactive fragments and an improved Avrami-Erofeev equation incorporating the proposed nonlinear reaction rate, a new computational model was developed. Second, considering the fuel characteristics of RP-3 kerosene and calculating the state parameters and the temperature rise of the ullage layer in the tank, an ignition theoretical prediction model accounting for the coupled kinetic-chemical energy damage of reactive fragments was established. Finally, impact ignition damage tests were conducted in which reactive fragments impacted an aircraft’s equivalent fuel tank, and the model’s accuracy was verified against experimental results. The research results show that the theoretical ignition critical velocity of a reactive fragment impacting the ullage layer of a nonfull fuel tank ranges from 520.00 to 535.59 m/s, with an error of 2.67% to 5.74% compared to experimental data (506.49 m/s). The model c…

Clinical Interchangeability of Total Corneal Astigmatism Prediction Methods: An Agreement Analysis
abstract: Purpose: To compare agreement between total corneal astigmatism (TCA) predictions from a deep learning (DL) model and those from the Barrett Toric Calculator (Barrett) and Abulafia–Koch (AK) formulas. Methods: In 100 eyes with corneal astigmatism, Pentacam HR imaging (Oculus Optikgeräte GmbH) was used to generate TCA predictions with the AK formula, Barrett formula, and a previously validated DL model. Agreement was assessed using Pearson and Spearman correlation, mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and Bland-Altman analysis. Clinical interchangeability was predefined as 95% limits of agreement within ±0.25 diopters (D) for magnitude and ±5 degrees for axis. Predictions were also decomposed into Cartesian X and Y vector components. Results: The AK and Barrett formulas demonstrated near-perfect agreement for both magnitude ( r = 0.99; MAE: 0.070 D, RMSE: 0.11 D) and axis ( r = 1.00; MAE: 1.11°, RMSE: 1.68°), with 95% limits of agreement both within the interchangeability thresholds. Compared with both conventional methods, the DL model showed larger systematic differences. Compared with the Barrett formula, magnitude agreement was r = 0.92 (MAE: 0.24 D; RMSE: 0.27 D), and axis agreement was r = 1.00 (MAE: 4.71 degrees). Similar findings were observed versus the AK formula (magnitude r = 0.94, MAE: 0.20 D; axis MAE: 4.92°). The DL model consistently underest…

Capacity of geostationary satellite optical feeder links with optical, coding, and network-level turbulence mitigation
abstract: We demonstrate that jointly optimizing physical, link, and network layers can significantly enhance the capacity and/or availability of bidirectional optical links between ground and geostationary satellites through atmospheric optical turbulence. We model link capacity under realistic optical turbulence conditions from 25 different locations over the span of one year and evaluate trade-offs between adaptive optics correction (optical level), data interleaving (coding level), and location diversity (network level) of ground stations. Accounting for only turbulence outages, at individual sites interleaving of 20–50 ms can be effective; however, networking of 2–4 ground stations with adaptive optics, taking advantage of the spatial decorrelation of turbulence conditions, is sufficient to almost completely mitigate turbulence without any interleaving.

Bridging the Intention–Behaviour Gap in Household Energy Saving: A Systematic Review Based on the Theory of Planned Behaviour
abstract: Household energy use is a major source of carbon emissions, yet residents’ intentions to save energy often fail to translate into action. This systematic review examined how the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) explains household energy saving and what may condition this intention–behaviour gap. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched Web of Science, Scopus and APA PsycInfo and synthesised 89 studies (2009–2025) by vote counting. Attitude was the most consistent predictor of intention (positive in 92.2% of the studies testing this path), followed by perceived behavioural control (80.7%) and subjective norm (70.3%). Personal norm predicted intention in seven of eight studies, supporting integration with the Norm Activation Model. Intention predicted behaviour in 29 of 30 studies, but only moderately (mean β = 0.46 among significant results), and only half of the studies measured behaviour, mostly by self-report. Building on these findings, we propose a conceptual framework in which habit strength is hypothesised to weaken the intention–behaviour link for curtailment behaviours, and facilitating conditions, such as income and infrastructure, to moderate it for investment behaviours. Interventions may therefore need to disrupt energy-intensive habits for everyday saving and remove practical barriers to investment; longitudinal and experimental studies should test these propositions.

title: Evaluation of PSO-Tuned DBSCAN and Local Hash-Linked Recording of Synthetic Power Quality Disturbances in Electric Vehicle Charging and Electromobility Systems
abstract: Electric vehicle charging motivates the joint consideration of disturbance analysis and traceable event records. This study evaluates particle-swarm-tuned density clustering coupled to a local hash-linked recording procedure. The primary search maximizes silhouette without event labels, using duration and magnitude from synthetic grid-side and electromobility populations of 325 and 132 events. Thirty independent populations and matched-budget random and grid searches quantify agreement, rejection and variability. The primary method attains mean adjusted Rand indices of 0.477 and 0.267, with retained fractions of 0.591 and 0.313, respectively. Complete synthetic waveform-feature ablations reduce agreement under the same search settings. A separate experiment on 47 eligible measured grid events also finds no mean improvement from adding a band-limited harmonic descriptor. Held-out comparisons favor the tested support-vector, random-forest and graph neural classifiers over the specified nearest-core extension of density clustering. Canonical event payloads connect fitted clusters to stored records. Alterations without rehashing are detected locally, whereas consistent rewriting and tail deletion require an independently trusted terminal digest and record count. These results identify the limits of silhouette-only optimization and distinguish local record consistency from sensor au…

Avaliação térmica plantar como estratégia preventiva para úlceras em indivíduos com neuropatia periférica diabética
abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is associated with loss of foot sensation and an increased risk of diabetic foot ulcers (DFU), making the early identification of changes related to their development important. This study aims to analyze plantar thermal assessment, through thermometry and infrared thermography, as a complementary resource for the early identification and prevention of DFU in individuals with diabetic peripheral neuropathy. This is an integrative literature review with a descriptive and qualitative approach, conducted in the PubMed, BVS, SciELO, and PEDro databases between July and August 2026. Studies published between 2021 and 2026 in Portuguese and English were considered, and seven studies were selected after applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The studies analyzed showed favorable results for plantar temperature monitoring, with a reduction in the risk or recurrence of DFU across different protocols, although differences in methods, equipment, and interpretation criteria were identified. The findings indicate that thermal assessment may contribute to the early identification of changes associated with DFU risk, particularly when the results guide the adoption of preventive measures. Plantar thermal assessment shows potential as a complementary resource for the prevention and monitoring of individuals at risk of DFU; however, more standardized proto…

title: A Chemical Timer Strategy Programs the Onset of Peroxidase Chemiluminescence
abstract: Abstract Peroxidase chemiluminescence (CL), particularly horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-mediated CL, is widely used in biochemical analysis and immunoassays. However, the onset of CL is typically instantaneous and difficult to control, imposing strict timing requirements for measurements and compromising reproducibility and imaging quality. Herein, we report a general chemical timer strategy that programs CL onset using catechol-type phenolics as signal delayers. Protocatechuic aldehyde (PCAL) and protocatechuic acid (PCA) enable concentration-dependent delays from seconds to minutes while largely preserving emission intensity and extending signal duration. The strategy is compatible with multiple luminol derivatives, a non-luminol acridan substrate, and other peroxidases. Applying the chemical timer, peroxidase-mediated CL encoding and dynamic patterning are demonstrated, and a class of time-resolved enhanced chemiluminescence (ECL) reagents is developed to provide defined imaging windows for immunoblots, enabling kinetic suppression of background and noise. Notably, this strategy is compatible with commercial ECL kits via simple additive introduction, providing a practical route to achieve time-resolved CL readout in routine bioassays.

title: Hierarchical Early-Warning Strategy for Overheating-Induced Thermal Runaway in High-Nickel Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) can undergo thermal runaway (TR) under thermal abuse, and high-nickel LIBs face more severe safety challenges. Therefore, early warning of TR is crucial for the safe operation of LIBs. Overheating-induced TR experiments were conducted on 15 Ah NCM811 LIBs at different states of charge (SOCs, 10–100%), with synchronous monitoring of expansion force, temperature, voltage, and characteristic gases (CO, CO2, HF, and H2). Based on signals variations, five characteristic moments were defined, dividing TR into five stages: abnormal expansion-force increase (tabn), cell venting (tV), first gas detection (tG), internal short circuit (tISC), and TR (tTR). As SOC increased, deeper cathode delithiation and anode lithiation accelerated internal reactions, shifting all moments earlier. The expansion-force signal enabled the earliest anomaly identification, up to 1275 s before TR onset, while CO detection within 30 s after venting provided chemical confirmation. Voltage signals accurately indicated ISC, and temperature signals directly reflected the essence of TR. Consequently, a three-level early-warning strategy was proposed: Level 1 (dF/dt > 1 N/s), Level 2 (sequential force–gas confirmation), and Level 3 (“voltage + temperature” with duration constraints). The thresholds are SOC-independent, offering a reference for engineering deployment in high-nickel pouch …

title: Perioperative Therapy Versus Surgery-First Strategy for Resectable Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: Current Evidence, High-Risk Stratification, and Future Directions
abstract: Background/Objectives: Long-term survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains poor. Although neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) has been increasingly investigated in resectable disease, its benefit compared with upfront surgery remains uncertain. This review evaluates evidence from randomized and prospective trials and explores clinical and molecular factors that may refine patient selection. Methods: We reviewed key randomized and prospective clinical trials evaluating NAT in resectable PDAC, including NORPACT-1, PANACHE01/PRODIGE-48, PREP-02/JSAP05, NEONAX, PREOPANC-1, PREOPANC-2, and CASSANDRA (PACT-21), the last two of which directly compared different NAT regimens head-to-head in the neoadjuvant setting, whereas PREOPANC-1 compared neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy with upfront surgery. Outcomes of interest included overall survival (OS), resection rates, and treatment-related differences across resectable and borderline resectable populations. We also examined emerging clinical and biomarker-driven stratification strategies. Results: Trials in strictly resectable PDAC have demonstrated mixed results. NORPACT-1 reported inferior OS with neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX compared to upfront surgery (median OS 25.1 vs. 38.5 months; HR 1.52). PANACHE01/PRODIGE-48 showed comparable OS despite higher R0 resection rates with NAT. In contrast, PREP-02/JSAP05 demonstrated improved OS with …

title: Robson’s Ten-group Classification System- An Emerging Strategy to Audit Caesarean Section Rate
abstract: Background: For reducing birth related complications for both mother and baby caesarean section (CS) is a major procedure which is in rising trends for the past few decades. However, CS is not without its own adverse consequences to rethink about its real indication to do as a lifesaving procedure. Objective: To audit the worrisome increasing CS rates to guide actions accordingly with Robson’s Ten-group classification system. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study was done from January 2022 to December 2023 at BNS Upasham, Khulna, Bangladesh. All patients delivered during this period were included and classified according to RtGCS to audit the CS rates in each group. Results: Within total 865 deliveries during the study period, number of CS was 547(63.23%). Highest contributor to total CS rate found by RtGCS group 5(56.30%) & by group 2(15.72%) respectively with RtGCS group 10(4.57%) was third in position. RtGCS group 6(0.69%) and group 7(0.46%) were least in contribution to total CS rates. Conclusion: Policy is to be made to regular audit, to identify reason for increasing caesarean section and execute accordingly to reduce the CS specially the primary primary caesarean section to have control on overall CS rates. title: Assessing the Feasibility and Acceptability of Implementing an Enhanced Social Network Strategy to Reduce HIV Within Recent Transmission Networks in the US South
abstract: Abstract Black sexual and gender minorities (BSGM) in the U.S. South experience high HIV incidence and low engagement in prevention and treatment services. We conducted a mixed-methods implementation science study to assess perceived drivers of aspects of the feasibility and acceptability of implementing an enhanced Social Network Strategy (eSNS). We did this to further inform its adaptation for BSGM in Charlotte, NC from CDC’s evidence-based program. The adaptation incorporated PrEP referrals and HIV care re-engagement. We conducted Personal Network Surveys (PNS) (n=59) and in-depth interviews (IDIs) (n=17 initial, n=8 follow-up). In the eSNS, community members ( Ambassadors) are coached by disease intervention specialists to refer people from their social networks to HIV testing, prevention, or treatment. The 59 survey participants (median age 28) were 79% cisgender men, 7% transgender women; 66% living with HIV. Most PNS participants reported comfort discussing HIV. Most of the IDI participants were interested in serving as Ambassadors . The eSNS demonstrated strong feasibility and acceptability among BSGM. Implementation recommendations included augmenting both confidentiality protections and Ambassador training.

Impact of Target Costing on New Product Development Strategy for SMES in Nigeria's Manufacturing Sector
abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) constitute over 96% of businesses and 84% of employment in Nigeria’s manufacturing sector and are critical to economic diversification and industrial growth (National Bureau of Statistics [NBS], 2024). Central to the survival and competitiveness of manufacturing SMEs is their ability to continuously develop new products that meet customer needs at profitable prices. However, Nigerian manufacturing SMEs operate in a challenging environment characterized by high production costs, unstable exchange rates, poor infrastructure, limited access to finance, and intense competition from imports (Ariyo, 2022). These conditions often lead to cost overruns, product failures, and low profitability during New Product Development (NPD). Traditional cost management approaches such as cost-plus pricing is ineffective in this context because they determine price after costs have been incurred (Horngren, Datar, & Rajan, 2022). Target Costing, a proactive, market-driven cost management technique that determines allowable cost as `Market Price to Desired Profit` and works backward during the design phase, offers a viable alternative (Cooper & Slagmulder, 1997). Despite its documented benefits in developed economies, there is limited empirical evidence on the adoption and impact of target costing on NPD strategy among manufacturing SMEs in Nigeria. title: The Impact of Multiple Social Media Platform Use on Relationship Satisfaction and Uncertainty Among Romantic Partners at a Midwestern University
abstract: Guided by the Media Multiplexity Theory to examine the relationship of multiple social media use with relationship satisfaction and uncertainty among romantic partners. A cross-sectional study was conducted between October 2024 and March 2025 at a medium-sized Midwestern University with 190 students using online Qualtrics. Multivariate regression analyses were conducted to identify the predictors of satisfaction and uncertainty. p -value less than .05 was considered significant. The study found that neither platform quantity nor communication frequency significantly predicted satisfaction or reduced uncertainty. Instead, uncertainty emerged as a negative predictor of satisfaction (β = –.55, p < .001), and a marginal positive association between platform diversity and uncertainty (B = 0.07, p = .08). Education and college years were also associated with variations in satisfaction and uncertainty. These findings highlight the central role of relational certainty in maintaining satisfying romantic relationships.

title: Effects of Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge‐to‐Edge Repair on Right Heart Dimension and Function
abstract: Background Transcatheter tricuspid edge‐to‐edge repair (T‐TEER) has developed as a treatment option for patients experiencing severe tricuspid regurgitation. T‐TEER consistently reduces tricuspid regurgitation, but data on subsequent right heart remodeling remain limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate changes in right heart dimension and function after T‐TEER using extended echocardiographic follow‐up. Methods The study was based on the international EuroTR (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation), including patients undergoing T‐TEER between 2016 and 2024 at 18 European centers. Eligible were patients with available baseline and follow‐up (≥90 days postprocedure) echocardiographic assessment. Results A total of 699 patients (mean age, 78±8 years; 56% women) were included in the analysis. Echocardiographic follow‐up was performed at a median of 407 days (interquartile range, 205–801 days). Right heart dimensions significantly decreased: right ventricular (RV) midventricular diameter from 40.2±8.9 to 37.1±8.4 mm ( P <0.001) and end‐diastolic area from 28.7±9.0 to 26.2±9.6 cm 2 ( P <0.001). Procedural success was significantly associated with positive RV remodeling (odds ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.07–3.09]). For RV function, a decline of fractional area change from 37.8%±10.2% to 33.3%±10.1% ( P <0.001), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excu…

title: REFORMA TRIBUTÁRIA DO CONSUMO: NEUTRALIDADE, NÃO CUMULATIVIDADE PLENA E OS LIMITES DO DIREITO AO CRÉDITO NA LEI COMPLEMENTAR Nº 214/2025
abstract: O artigo examina se a Lei Complementar nº 214/2025, ao regulamentar o Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS) e a Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), realiza a não cumulatividade ampla e a neutralidade prometidas pela Emenda Constitucional nº 132/2023 ou se reproduz, no direito ao crédito, restrições que marcaram o ICMS. A pesquisa é qualitativa, exploratória e de base bibliográfica e documental. Analisam-se o texto constitucional, os dispositivos da lei complementar sobre o momento de apropriação do crédito, a idoneidade documental, o uso e consumo pessoal, o estorno e o tratamento dos optantes do Simples Nacional, a partir do texto consolidado das normas e de obras doutrinárias publicadas em 2025 e 2026. Discute-se também o argumento em favor do split payment, apresentado como proteção contra créditos inidôneos. Conclui-se, em caráter hipotético, que a promessa de plenitude convive com condicionantes relevantes, sobretudo a vinculação do crédito à extinção do débito, e que a compatibilidade dessas condicionantes com a neutralidade depende de interpretação que preserve o crédito de quem não controla o pagamento da etapa anterior. O tema segue em regulamentação, e as conclusões devem ser lidas com essa cautela.
authors: Aluisio Augusto Lunardi Barbosa de Moraes

title: Green Finance, Innovation, and Financial Stability: Assessing the Role of Sustainable Investment in South Africa’s Transition Economy
abstract: This study empirically examines the dynamic relationship between green finance, financial innovation, exchange rate volatility, and macro-financial stability in South Africa’s transition economy. Using quarterly time-series data spanning 2000Q1-2025Q4, we construct a multivariate framework incorporating green bond issuance and ESG-linked capital flows (green finance proxy), a composite financial stress index and banking sector Z-score (financial stability proxies), digital financial innovation indicators, the real effective exchange rate, GDP growth, and the policy repo rate. After confirming non-stationarity at levels using Augmented Dickey-Fuller and Phillips-Perron tests, Johansen cointegration tests reveal a long-run equilibrium relationship among the variables, justifying estimation through a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). Impulse Response Functions indicate that a one-standard-deviation shock to green finance reduces financial stress by approximately 0.28 standard deviations within four quarters (p < 0.05), while improving banking sector resilience as measured by the Z-score. However, exchange rate depreciation offsets nearly 20% of the stabilising effect, highlighting the role of currency risk in transition financing. Variance decomposition analysis shows that green finance innovations explain 17-22% of forecast error variance in financial stability over a 10-quar…

title: European growth models after the global financial crisis: feedback channels, interdependence and change in Germany, Poland, and Spain, 2009–2025
Multi-Objective Planning of Distributed Energy Storage Considering Distribution-Level Electricity Market Simulation
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-objective distributed energy storage planning method that couples distribution-level electricity market simulation to improve the coordination between storage investment, market participation, and distribution network operation. The method incorporates technical–market-based candidate-bus screening, joint energy and frequency regulation market clearing with endogenous price formation, and life-cycle economic assessment. An improved NSGA-II algorithm is employed to obtain the Pareto-optimal solutions, while the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) is used to select a compromise solution among annualized life-cycle net cost, nodal voltage deviations, and network losses. The proposed method is evaluated on an extended IEEE 33-bus distribution system using 24-h typical-day load and renewable generation profiles. Compared with the baseline scenario, the selected storage configuration reduces average network losses from 0.20135 MW to 0.08235 MW and average nodal voltage deviations from 0.028 p.u. to 0.019 p.u., while increasing the renewable energy accommodation rate from 81.73% to 95.63%. The resulting storage investment achieves a life-cycle net present value of CNY 0.8745 million with a simple payback period of 7.33 years. In addition, compared with the PSO-based energy storage planning method, the method proposed in t…

title: Enhancing Smart Grid Flexibility Through Demand- Side Virtual Power Plant Coordination of Water Distribution Networks in MATLAB/Simulink
Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

title: Comparative constitutive modelling of anisotropy, pore-pressure response and strain localization in Opalinus clay
abstract: Abstract Several countries are considering argillaceous rocks as host formations for the geological disposal of radioactive waste. These rock types possess favourable properties for the retardation of radionuclide migration from the deep geological repository (DGR), including very low permeability, low molecular diffusivity, high sorption capacity and self-healing characteristics. However, several internal and external events and processes, such as excavation of the DGR, thermal loading from the waste, and gas generation, can mechanically disturb the host rock and might adversely affect its favourable properties. The assessment of the host rock performance as a barrier to radionuclide migration necessitates the development of robust constitutive models. In the present paper, constitutive models developed by six research teams of the international DECOVALEX project are presented and compared. The models were developed using a comprehensive experimental database from laboratory tests performed on Opalinus Clay, an argillaceous host rock formation in the Swiss DGR concept. The laboratory tests consist of uniaxial compression tests, Brazilian tensile tests, and consolidated-undrained (CU) triaxial tests with pore pressure measurements, followed by microscopic observations of the deformation and failure modes. The models reproduced the main features of the experimental observations,…

title: Benchmarking hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for power grid optimization problems
Real-time machine learning control of a Hall thruster discharge plasma
Molecular Differentiation of Bipolaris oryzae and Nigrospora oryzae Associated with Brown Spot Symptoms in Rice
Energy security in the Age of Electricity
abstract: Abstract The global energy system is being reshaped by a second major supply shock in five years, surging electricity demand and intensifying competition over the technologies needed to meet it. In today’s more uncertain geopolitical landscape, energy security and electrification should not be seen as competing priorities – instead, they are deeply intertwined. Electrification can allow countries to make greater use of their domestic resources, reduce dependence on imported fuels and lower emissions. But these benefits will not be realised automatically. Grids, flexibility, resilient supply chains, access to finance and modern energy services must advance alongside innovation in electric technologies. The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, in November 2026 offers an opportunity to translate these priorities into tangible progress, with a proposed global ambition to raise electricity’s share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, while recognising different national circumstances and starting points.

title: Species composition, purity and safety concerns of edible insects in a Cambodian market
abstract: Abstract Insects are increasingly recognised as sustainable protein sources amid rising global food demand and the environmental impacts of conventional livestock production. However, although entomophagy is widespread in Southeast Asia, empirical information regarding Cambodia is limited. In this study, we investigated the composition and handling of insect-based food items sold at Skun Market in Kampong Cham Province, Cambodia, through surveys conducted in September and December 2022 and March 2023. Mixed fried assortments were purchased, sorted and taxonomically identified and the proportions of each group were quantified. Crickets, mainly Brachytrupes portentosus and Gryllus bimaculatus , were sold in high purity (mean 87.9%), whereas water beetles showed low purity (mean 79.0%) and frequently contained non-target taxa, including Diplonychus rusticus . A variety of additional insects, including mole crickets, ground beetles, cicadas, grasshoppers and dung beetles, were also detected in the cricket samples. Harmful or potentially toxic insects are occasionally mixed into assortments, raising concerns similar to those raised by contamination issues reported in other processed animal products. In the water beetle samples, vendors appeared to distinguish between Dytiscidae and Hydrophilidae and higher proportions of Dytiscidae were associated with higher prices, suggesting poss…
venue: Journal of Insects as Food and Feed

title: Regulatory compliance and quality of veterinary oxytetracycline injections in Zambia: findings from post-market surveillance
abstract: Objective Substandard antimicrobials affect the One Health ecosystem comprising both human and animal health, food production and food security, driving up Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) rates. This study assessed compliance with regulatory and quality specifications of oxytetracycline injection marketed for veterinary use in Zambia. Methods Between August 2023 and December 2023, a total of 48 samples of assorted marketed brands of oxytetracycline injection for veterinary use on the Zambian market were collected and analyzed for conformity to marketing authorisation terms on labeling and quality parameters, including identification, assay, and pH tests at the National Drug Quality Control Laboratory, Lusaka, Zambia. Results Conformity to labeling for information such as product name, active pharmaceutical ingredient, dosage form, batch number, expiry date, manufacturer, and container description were assessed at 100%. However, compliance with storage conditions and product registration numbers was assessed at 95.8% and 43.8%, respectively. All samples met requirements for specific quality tests such as identification, assay, and pH. Conclusion Although the sampled oxytetracycline injections met some labeling requirements and specific quality parameters, essential factors for effective disease treatment and combating AMR, the low rate of product registration compliance indicated…

title: The innovation and development of capital theory under the conditions of socialist market economy
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to deepen the comprehensive and accurate understanding of the essence, types, characteristics, laws of motion and functions of capital in the socialist market economy, explore policies for rationally regulating and guiding the sound development of various forms of capital and thereby to uphold the basic socialist economic system, advance high-quality development and common prosperity and modernise and sinicise Marxist political economy. It systematically addresses why China has innovated and developed capital theory, what the new capital theory contains and in what respects it innovates upon and develops Marx's theory of capital and the capital theory of mainstream Western economics. Design/methodology/approach Adopting materialist dialectics and a problem-driven comparative approach, the paper first reviews and synthesises the main content of Marx's theory of capital and of mainstream Western capital theory, identifying the historical and practical limitations of the former and the fundamental defects of the latter. It then examines the new perspectives on capital theory advanced in China since the reform and opening-up and, grounded in the reality of China's primary stage of socialism, constructs and expounds the new capital theory of socialist political economy with Chinese characteristics and demonstrates its scientific validity through theoretical r…

title: Credibility displacement in algorithmic financial reporting: a critical review of AI, disclosure credibility and capital-market consequences
abstract: Purpose This review examines how financial-reporting credibility is shaped when algorithmic systems enter the reporting chain. It asks where credibility is produced, tested and understood when artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, large language models, eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) analytics and related tools affect reporting information. Design/methodology/approach The paper combines a search and screening procedure informed by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) with a concept-centric synthesis. The evidence base comprises a 226-paper curated core and a 144-paper close-synthesis subset. Sensitivity analyses re-examine the 39-record outlet boundary and the close-synthesis threshold. Findings The evidence remains dispersed across research on textual disclosure and natural language processing (NLP), audit analytics and assurance, structured reporting using XBRL, market interpretation, accounting information systems (AIS) implementation and AI governance. Across these streams, algorithms can improve reporting processes but may also alter the grounds on which reporting assertions are accepted. We describe the latter possibility as credibility displacement: model-related output, provenance or validation partly substitutes for scrutiny of the underlying assertion or for identifiable professional and institutional…

title: The Impact of 2022 Electricity Tariff Increases on Household Electricity Consumption: An Econometric Analysis of Kalmunai Municipal Council
abstract: Electricity tariffs aim to promote efficiency, equity, and financial stability. Ceylon Electricity Board increased the tariffs after making losses in 2022. The research is meant to establish whether there is any correlation between electricity tariffs and consumption. Data were collected over three years, from 2022 to 2024, using 101 households in each year. The same number of households were observed in each year, totaling 303 samples (101 households × 3 years). This research examines any changes in households' electricity consumption using the data collected over these three years. Random Effects regression analysis model has been used to analyze the data collected using Stata software. According to the results of the analysis, electricity consumption is associated with electricity tariffs and electricity expenditure. From the data collected, it is clear that there is a correlation between household electricity consumption and electricity tariff, income, and number of appliances. There is a positive correlation between electricity tariff and consumption. This is contrary to expectations but can be attributed to economic performance in the post-COVID era, increases in income levels, and use of appliances during the sample period. However, the application of modern technology, like solar panels, shows an inverse relationship with the use of electricity. This research recommends…
venue: International Journal of Accounting and Business Finance

title: Optimalisasi Monitoring Service Level Prosedur Melalui Penyusunan Instrumen Monitoring dan Prioritisasi Prosedur Berbasis Risiko di PT. Pelindo Multi Terminal
abstract: PT Pelindo Multi Terminal mengelola 182 prosedur aktif, namun monitoring service level masih terbatas, manual, berbasis audit, dan belum mempertimbangkan prioritas risiko sehingga belum optimal sebagai instrumen pengendalian proses bisnis. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengoptimalkan monitoring service level melalui prioritisasi prosedur berbasis risiko dan pengembangan instrumen monitoring yang terstruktur. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan applied research dengan metode kualitatif deskriptif-evaluatif. Data dikumpulkan melalui studi dokumentasi, wawancara terstruktur, diskusi teknis, dan expert judgment dari Divisi Sistem Manajemen, Business Process Owner, dan Divisi Manajemen Risiko, sedangkan tahap pengujian instrumen melibatkan 9 partisipan pada level Officer dan Vice President. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan content analysis, Criticality Analysis berbasis ISO 31010, serta Framework Maturity Assessment Model melalui tahap scope, design, populate, dan test. Dari 182 prosedur, 169 memiliki service level; 92 tergolong moderate to high dan high, kemudian 33 prosedur ditetapkan sebagai prioritas setelah proses scoping. Instrumen yang dikembangkan dinilai layak, mudah digunakan, dan mampu mendukung evaluasi secara konsisten. Penelitian ini menghasilkan model monitoring berbasis risiko yang memperkuat pengendalian proses bisnis dan efektivitas manajemen operasional.

title: EDITORIAL VOL. 11 2026 – Evolución tecnológica al servicio de la comunicación científica. MOJP 4.0 y una nueva etapa de desarrollo editorial
abstract: This editorial presents MOJP 4.0, a technological evolution of the editorial infrastructure of the Peer-Reviewed Scientific Journal of the MenteClara Foundation, developed by Oscar R. Gómez and his engineering team on the basis of OJS 3.5.0.5. It describes its main innovations: optimization of the metadata architecture, implementation of interoperable semantic schemas, improved identification of authors and institutions through persistent identifiers, expansion of OAI-PMH services, and integration of XMP metadata into PDF documents. It also presents Custom Head Injector, a native MOJP 4.0 module compatible with OJS 3.5.0.5 and later versions, which expands the possibilities for customizing and integrating metadata, semantic schemas, and external services into the HTML header of editorial platforms. The editorial also introduces the XMP-PDF Module, a technology designed to enrich scientific documents with structured information about their bibliographic identity, editorial provenance, rights, and other relevant data. These developments are part of an institutional trajectory of innovation, technological autonomy, and commitment to the principles of openness, interoperability, and the circulation of scientific information.
venue: Revista Científica Arbitrada de la Fundación MenteClara

title: The Role of Pre-Service Teachers’ Reflective Journals in Authentic Assessment
abstract: This study explored how pre-service teachers used reflective journals during an Authentic Assessment Intervention Program in Educational Test and Measurement. The study formed part of an explanatory sequential mixed-methods project involving 42 BEd Fourth Year (Second Semester) pre-service teachers at Yangon University of Education. This study focuses on qualitative evidence from journals completed throughout the intervention. Seven journal questions, organised around pre-topic and post-topic reflection, invited participants to record prior knowledge, feelings, participation, learning difficulties, beliefs about authentic tasks, and suggestions for instruction. The entries indicated that journal writing helped participants review and evaluate their learning, recognise strengths and weaknesses, monitor participation and collaboration, express affective responses, and connect course concepts with real-life situations and future teaching. The journals also gave the teacher timely formative evidence about misconceptions, readiness, learning needs, and requests for clearer explanations, realistic examples, additional feedback, and more time for discussion. Reflective journaling therefore served a dual purpose within authentic assessment: it supported learner self-monitoring and reflective thinking while also informing responsive instructional adjustment. These findings suggest that …

title: Code-sharing and Service Quality in African Aviation Markets
Evolutionary drivers of China’s interprovincial healthcare service network: a temporal exponential random graph analysis of provincial panel data
abstract: Background High-quality healthcare resources remain unevenly distributed across China, while cross-provincial care seeking, teleconsultation, and regional medical collaboration are increasingly common. Existing studies have mainly explained regional disparities in terms of resource endowments, geographic proximity, and spatial accessibility, with less attention to network structure, tie formation and persistence, and changes during public health crises. Methods Using panel data for 31 provincial-level administrative units in mainland China from 2009 to 2023, we constructed a directed interprovincial healthcare service association network with a modified gravity model. Social network analysis, temporal exponential random graph models (TERGMs), and separable temporal exponential random graph models (STERGMs) were used to examine network structure, endogenous mechanisms, sender and receiver effects, and differences before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Results The network shifted from expansion and integration toward contraction and differentiation. The number and density of ties increased from 2009 to 2013, declined after 2014, and fell markedly in 2019, while rising hierarchy indicated stronger core-periphery differentiation. Beijing, Shanghai, and Jiangsu formed the core of tie reception and path control; Zhejiang, Fujian, Henan, and Guangdong served as regional bridges; and…

title: Imagining the child’s perspective: pre-service social studies teachers’ visual representations of childhood vulnerability, empathy, and moral meaning
abstract: This study examined how social studies teacher trainees construct meanings of childhood vulnerability through visual and written representations, with particular attention to empathic perspective-taking and moral meaning-making. Rather than conceptualising vulnerability as individual fragility, the study examined how children were positioned in relation to voice, agency, rights, and structural conditions. An interpretative qualitative design integrating art-based inquiry, multimodal visual analysis, and reflexive thematic analysis was employed with 51 fourth-year social studies teacher trainees at a state university in Türkiye. During a 14-week Art and Museum Education module, participants produced visual works addressing childhood vulnerability and accompanying reflective texts, generating 51 paired visual–textual units. Analysis identified three interrelated patterns: the paradox of visibility, in which children were made visually salient yet remained discursively silent ( n = 20); the construction of vulnerability through enclosure, fragmentation, and control ( n = 17); and a shift from emotional response towards an ethical encounter grounded in empathy, rights, and professional responsibility ( n = 14). Frequencies indicate the dominant theme of each unit; many units also carried features of the other themes. Because the production guidelines explicitly invited participants…
