title: Análisis sistemático de la participación ciudadana electrónica universitaria
abstract: Contexto: La participación ciudadana electrónica (e-Participación) se considera como un elemento relevante dentro de las instituciones de educación superior, ya que favorece procesos de gestión más abiertos y colaborativos. A pesar de avances, la investigación disponible muestra enfoques dispersos y una limitada integración de todas las etapas que conforman el ciclo de participación. Método: Con el propósito de conocer la situación actual de este campo, se desarrolló una revisión sistemática de literatura basada en la metodología Kitchenham. El estudio tuvo un enfoque bibliográfico y descriptivo, tomando en consideración publicaciones científicas difundidas entre 2021 y 2026. Luego del proceso de selección se analizaron siete investigaciones relacionadas con la participación electrónica en entornos universitarios. Resultados: Los hallazgos colocan en evidencia una amplia presencia de aplicaciones móviles como medio principal para realizar la interacción entre la comunidad estudiantil y las autoridades. Entre las funciones más frecuentes que se encontraron fueron: la geolocalización, el registro fotográfico de incidencias y el seguimiento del estado de los reportes. Sin embargo, también se identificaron desafíos, entre ellos las limitaciones de acceso a las tecnologías de información y comunicación, la baja participación estudiantil y las dificultades derivadas de reportes dupli…

title: Mechanistic Insights into the Combined Effects of Substituent Modification, Electronegativity Modulation, Solvent Polarity, and External Electric Fields on ESIPT and Antioxidant Potential in 4′,5-Dihydroxy-7-methoxyflavone
abstract: Abstract Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations were employed to systematically investigate the effects of substituent electronic characteristics, para-position heteroatom substitution, solvent polarity, and external electric fields (EEFs) on excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), emission photophysics, and antioxidant-related reactivity of 4′,5-dihydroxy-7-methoxyflavone (GKO) and its derivatives. Geometric, infrared vibrational, reduced density gradient (RDG), frontier molecular orbital (FMO), natural bond orbital (NBO), and potential energy curve (PEC) analyses reveal pronounced photoinduced reorganization of the intramolecular hydrogen-bonding environment. For GKO in dichloromethane (DCM), the H···O distance decreases from 1.670 Å in S0 to 0.987 Å in S1, accompanied by substantial elongation of the donor O–H bond, indicating pronounced proton displacement toward the acceptor upon excitation. The ground state proton transfer barrier of GKO is 6.41 kcal mol–1, decreasing to 4.57 kcal mol–1 with −CN substitution and increasing to 7.32 kcal mol–1 with −NH2 substitution. O → S substitution at the para position of the proton acceptor lowers the S0 barrier to 5.26 kcal mol–1, whereas increasing solvent polarity from DCM to DMSO produces only a minor decrease to 6.31 kcal mol–1. In the excited state, no appa…
venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A

title: Opening the Commons: Community Land Trusts as a Strategy for Geoist Land Reform
abstract: Abstract Geoists hold that we have strong moral and economic reasons to equalize the rents of land, for example, by taxing its economic value and allocating the proceeds as a universal basic income. It is widely recognized among economists that such land value taxes are uniquely efficient and equitable. But despite its moral and economic virtues, the policy has proven politically intractable, as it would diminish the capitalized value of land as an asset. In this article, I explore an alternative strategy for socializing these land rents, using Community Land Trusts (CLTs). These could generate a bottom-up mechanism for rent redistribution that circumvents some political challenges to land value taxation. However, I argue that they may still remain vulnerable to problems of regulatory capture and rent-seeking. The paper integrates normative theory, public choice economics, and institutional design, and draws upon historical case studies to illustrate and evaluate the strategy’s viability.

title: Vestibular implant as a novel peripheral neuromodulation strategy for complex movement disorders. A pilot study in patients with Parkinson’s disease associated with bilateral vestibular dysfunction
abstract: Background Parkinson’s disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder of distributed sensorimotor networks, in which axial symptoms such as gait impairment and postural instability frequently become refractory to conventional therapies. The vestibular system provides continuous input to basal ganglia, cerebellar, thalamic, and cortical pathways involved in motor control, representing a potential target for peripheral neuromodulation. This study investigates the effects of chronic vestibular implant (VI) stimulation in patients with PD and concomitant bilateral vestibular hypofunction (BVP). Methods Six patients received a VI, including three patients with PD-associated BVP. All participants were prospectively evaluated before implantation and 12 months after device activation. Outcomes were compared with a matched cohort of three patients with isolated BVP receiving the same implant. Motor results were assessed using the Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale part III (MDS-UPDRS III), together with dynamic balance, quality-of-life measures, comprehensive vestibular testing, and dopaminergic neuroimaging using 123I -Ioflupane SPECT (DaTSCAN). Results All patients with PD-associated BVP demonstrated clinically relevant motor improvement following VI activation, with MDS-UPDRS III reductions of 45, 20, and 27 points, respectively. The most consis…

title: When war reshapes uncertainty: the Ukraine conflict, oil markets and great-power geopolitics
abstract: Purpose The present study aims to investigate the effect of Russia–Ukraine conflict on the geopolitical risk of major economies like the United States, Russia, China and India. The study also provides empirical evidence regarding Russia–Ukraine conflict's effect on oil price uncertainty and US–China tension. Design/methodology/approach The study applied wavelet power spectrum (WPS) and plot wavelet coherence plot to study the dynamic effect of Russia–Ukraine conflict on geopolitical risk of major nations, oil price uncertainty and US–China tension. Findings The WPS executed on the geopolitical risk index of Ukraine reveals that the Russia–Ukraine conflict generated intense and persistent geopolitical risk in Ukraine. Wavelet coherence analysis reveals strong coherence between Ukraine and the United States, China and Russia. The linkage between Ukraine and India remains weak and episodic. It is also observed that during the conflict geopolitical shocks propagate through global energy markets, thereby increasing uncertainty beyond national borders. It is also evident that regional conflicts can intensify great-power rivalries. Originality/value Unlike prior research that mainly relies on event-based frameworks, the present study employs wavelet coherence analysis to capture the dynamic transmission of geopolitical risk arising from the Russia–Ukraine conflict to geopolitical risk…
venue: Journal of Economic and Administrative Sciences

title: Measuring Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use and GenAI Reliance in EFL Learning: Initial Scale Development and Validation
abstract: This study developed and examined initial validity evidence for a scale assessing autonomous and reliant use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in English as a foreign language (EFL) learning. Participants were 416 students enrolled in required English courses at one Japanese university. The sample was randomly divided into an exploratory sample (n = 205) and an independent confirmatory sample (n = 211). Exploratory factor analysis of 10 initial items supported two factors: Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use (six items) and GenAI Reliance (three items). One of the ten items (REL4), which concerned worry about reliance, did not load meaningfully on either factor and was treated as an exploratory single item. The initial confirmatory factor analysis showed mixed fit. A post hoc model allowing a residual covariance between two autonomy items (AU1 and AU2) showed improved fit (robust CFI = .959, robust TLI = .940, robust RMSEA = .073, and SRMR = .060). Internal-consistency coefficients were .86 for Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use and .70 for GenAI Reliance, and the latent factor correlation was small and nonsignificant (r = .11, 95% CI [−.07, .30]). The heterotrait-monotrait ratio was .175, 95% CI [.132, .343]. These findings provide preliminary evidence that Autonomous and Efficacious GenAI Use and GenAI Reliance may represent distinct dimensions. Further validat…

title: Viza rejimini liberallashtirishning kiruvchi turizmga ta'sirini baholash: gravitatsiya modeli va mashinali o'qitish uyg'unligi
abstract: В статье оценены факторы туристских потоков в Узбекистан и влияние реформы либерализации визового режима 2018–2019 годов. Для этого предложена «Модель факторов туристской привлекательности», объединяющая гравитационную модель, анализ событий и алгоритмы машинного обучения. Гравитационная модель оценена методом псевдомаксимального правдоподобия Пуассона по официальным данным в разрезе стран за 2014–2025 годы. Согласно результатам, туристский поток определяется численностью населения страны (эластичность 0,83), доходом (0,89) и расстоянием (−1,59); поток из сопредельных стран выше в 7,5 раза, из стран СНГ – в 11,4 раза. Эффект визового режима формировался в течение нескольких лет и в 2022–2024 годах соответствовал росту потока на 102–178 %. Модель XGBoost обеспечила наибольшую точность вне выборки (R² = 0,850). Выявлен низкий уровень использования потенциала на рынках Индии, Пакистана и Бангладеш.

title: Peningkatan Kemampuan Berbicara melalui Model Problem Based Learning Berbantuan Permainan Ular Tangga Edukatif berbasis Kartu pada Materi di Iklan Kelas VIII A Smp N 7 Purwokerto
abstract: This study aimed to improve students’ speaking skills through the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by a card-based educational snakes-and-ladders game on advertising material in Grade VIII A at SMP Negeri 7 Purwokerto. The study employed Classroom Action Research using the Kemmis and McTaggart model, comprising planning, action, observation, and reflection. It was conducted in two cycles involving 31 students. Data were collected using a speaking skills observation sheet consisting of 20 indicators, interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed descriptively. The mean speaking assessment score increased from 75.32 in Cycle I to 90.65 in Cycle II. The number of students scoring above 75 increased from 16 (51.61%) to 31 (100%). In Cycle II, the separate game boards used by individual groups were replaced with one large shared banner and a turn-taking system. This revision aimed to organize the game flow and provide more structured opportunities for speaking. The findings showed an improvement in speaking assessment results across the two action cycles. The research success criterion, defined as at least 70% of students scoring above 75, was achieved in Cycle II.

title: German medical students’ learning environment during the fading COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Background The Medical School’s learning environment (MSLE) is important for medical students’ academic performance and mental well-being. COVID-19 disrupted medical education worldwide through restrictions on practical and in-person teaching. Although several studies have showcased the immediate effects on medical students’ perceptions of MSLE and mental well-being, less is known about the changes during the transition to post-pandemic medical education. Methods Four cross-sectional online surveys were conducted at a German medical school between winter 2021/2022 and summer 2023. MSLE was assessed using three items from the Johns Hopkins Learning Environment Scale (JHLES) and three self-developed items. Various validated items assessed distress (DT), perceived stress (PSS-4), depression (PHQ-2), anxiety (GAD-2), and loneliness (R-UCLA-3). Analyses included group comparisons and binary logistic regression. Results Across four survey waves, 687 individual medical and dental students participated. Positive MSLE perceptions were more frequent in later waves, although differences were not significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Social connectedness and access to mentoring were reported significantly more frequently in later waves. Higher age, more advanced study years, greater perceived stress, and perceived lack of practical experience were associated with …

title: Frugal machine learning for pharmaceutical SME supply chain resilience: a real empirical case study
abstract: Purpose This study addresses a critical gap in pharmaceutical supply chain management for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing economies: the absence of validated, context-appropriate and practically deployable demand forecasting tools. Investigate which machine learning approach provides the most accurate, interpretable and economically impactful forecasts and how it can be transformed into an operational decision support tool. Design/methodology/approach A two-phase case study was conducted with a Tunisian pharmaceutical SME using 484,245 transactional records (2017–2022), aggregated to 72 monthly observations per product. Six forecasting models were evaluated under strict temporal validation: autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) (classical baseline), linear regression, recurrent neural network, long short-term memory (LSTM), Random Forest and XGBoost. All models accessed the same information set; neural networks used a six-month look-back window selected on the 2021 validation set. The best model was deployed in an open-source Streamlit web application integrated with Power BI dashboards. Three novel analytical layers were added: segmented performance analysis, feature importance extraction and economic impact quantification. Findings XGBoost achieved the best performance (R2 = 0.64, root mean squared error (RMSE) = 36,147), substantially outpe…

title: Role-Based Training Optimization A/B Testing Micro-Learning Vs. Traditional BIM-VDC Onboarding for Field Adoption - A Conceptual Framework
abstract: Over the last decade, many construction management organizations and the subcontractors have spent time buying different kinds of software that will streamline the process and communication using technology. A few of these common platforms include Autodesk Forma (previously Autodesk Construction Cloud), Revizto, Dronedeploy, and a bunch of adjacent platforms. While this software offers a great set of solutions, they do come with a requirement of having a human capability to use it, understand it, and then train it further. Every time a researcher has delivered a training to the project team there has been one lesson understanding that the same set of trainings and tools for the same software cannot be delivered to a large domain of audience that has personnel from different scope within the business, like the architects or the designers, field superintendents, project managers, QAQC personnel etc., across active job sites. This way of delivery may give initial boost to the usage of software but the observation shows that there has been decline in the use of right tool after two weeks of training where people go back to the physical drawings standard phone pictures (that are dated) and the text communication to resolve the issue. The technology was never the issue but the way it was implemented made the difference in the efficiency of trainings. Building on lessons from on-field…

title: Study on predicting double cracks coalescence behavior based on hyperparameter optimization of the kernel extreme learning machine classification model
abstract: Purpose The study aims to develop an intelligent prediction framework for dual-crack coalescence behavior and enhance the prediction accuracy and generalization performance of crack state judgment under multiple crack morphologies. Design/methodology/approach Four typical machine learning classifiers including LR, KNN, SVM and KELM are comprehensively compared on datasets of linear, elliptical and circular dual cracks. The Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (KELM) with the best overall performance is selected as the base model. A Reinforced Multi-strategy Parrot Optimization (RMPO) algorithm is employed to globally optimize KELM's hyperparameters, taking regularization coefficient C and RBF kernel parameter as optimization variables. The negative average validation-set accuracy from inner-fold cross-validation is adopted as the fitness function for adaptive searching within a nested stratified cross-validation workflow. Findings KELM outperforms other machine learning models in predicting three types of dual-crack coalescence. After hyperparameter tuning by RMPO, the hybrid RMPO-KELM model achieves prediction accuracies of 0.973, 0.911 and 0.824 for linear, elliptical and circular dual cracks respectively. Compared to grid search (GS) and the Parrot Optimization Algorithm (PO), the optimized model achieves a more accurate nonlinear fit between crack geometric inputs and coalescenc…

title: Identification of hub genes involved in the pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis: a multi-omics study integrating machine learning, Mendelian randomization, and mediation analysis
abstract: Background Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a steadily increasing global prevalence, yet its precise molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers for UC and explore potential metabolite-mediated pathways linking gene expression to UC. Methods Gene expression datasets were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database and analyzed using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, and multiple machine learning (ML) algorithms to identify key UC-associated genes. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis based on cis-expression quantitative trait loci was performed to assess potential causal associations between candidate gene expression and UC, with the random-effects inverse-variance-weighted method used as the primary analytical approach. Exploratory two-step MR mediation analysis was subsequently conducted to investigate potential metabolite-mediated pathways. In addition, core-gene expression was assessed in a dextran sulfate sodium-induced mouse model of colitis. Results By integrating transcriptomic analysis, WGCNA, PPI network analysis, and 127 ML model combinations, we identified six potential diagnostic biomarkers for UC: CXCL1, CXCL2, CXCR2, ENPP3, MMP1, and PPBP. The pri…

Implementation of Interactive and Collaborative Methods in Social Studies Learning and Their Empirical Effect on Student Learning Interest
abstract: Social Studies Education (IPS) plays a crucial role in developing middle school students' understanding of social phenomena, community dynamics, and surrounding environmental issues. However, conventional teacher-centered learning practices often limit student participation, leading to sub-optimal learning interest. This empirical research aims to analyze the implementation of interactive and collaborative methods in Social Studies instruction and to measure their significant influence on students' learning interest. Using a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group design, data were gathered from 64 eighth-grade students divided into an experimental class (utilizing interactive-collaborative techniques, n = 32) and a control class (utilizing traditional lectures, n = 32). Data collection techniques included a validated 5-point Likert scale interest questionnaire and direct classroom observation rubrics. The empirical findings demonstrated a statistically significant increase in the experimental group's learning interest post-test score (mean = 84.50) compared to the control group (mean = 71.20). Independent sample t-test analysis yielded t_count = 5.412 with p < 0.001, confirming that the integration of interactive dialogue and collaborative group investigation significantly boosts student enthusiasm, attention, active participation, and lear…

title: The Effectiveness of Game-Based Simulation and Rapid Prototyping in Project-Based Learning on Students’ Understanding and Kinematics Problem-Solving Skills
abstract: Physics learning requires students to interpret physical meaning and apply kinematics concepts in contextual situations. This study examined initial changes in students’ cognitive achievement following the integration of Game-Based Simulation and Rapid Prototyping into Project-Based Learning (PjBL). A quantitative pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design involved 92 Grade X students from three senior high schools in Kerinci Regency, Indonesia. Data comprised a five-item multiple-choice cognitive test administered before and after instruction and three four-point Likert questionnaires on perceived conceptual understanding, perceived problem-solving experience, and student response. The mean cognitive score increased from 40.22 to 89.35 (gain = 49.13; N-Gain = 0.841). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated a statistically significant pretest–posttest difference (p < 0.001; r = 0.868). At the indicator level, the largest increase was in motion representation/velocity–time relationships (+82.61 percentage points), followed by distance calculation (+72.83 points) and travel-time/fastest-route analysis (+59.78 points). Questionnaire averages were 90.99% for perceived conceptual understanding, 88.62% for perceived problem-solving experience, and 94.34% for student response. The questionnaire results represent students’ self-reported perceptions, not direct evidence of probl…

title: The Effect of ChatGPT Use on Students’ Reflection on Pancasila and Citizenship Education Learning Materials
abstract: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) into education has created new opportunities to support reflective learning; however, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between ChatGPT use and learning reflection in Pancasila and Citizenship Education remains limited. This study examined the relationship between ChatGPT use and students' learning reflection among Grade XI students. A quantitative correlational design was employed involving 56 Grade XI students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using validated questionnaires comprising 15 items measuring ChatGPT Use and 12 items measuring Learning Reflection. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression. The results demonstrated a positive and statistically significant relationship between ChatGPT use and learning reflection (R² = 0.813, p < 0.001). Descriptive analysis indicated that ChatGPT Use (M = 54.21, SD = 3.57) and learning reflection (M = 42.77, SD = 4.38) were classified as being in the "Good" category. These findings suggest that ChatGPT can support reflective learning when integrated into well-designed pedagogical activities under teacher guidance. This study contributes empirical evidence regarding the educational use of Generative AI in Pancasila and Citizenship Education and provides practical implications for promoti…
venue: Journal of General Education and Humanities

title: Growth-mindset leadership and engineers' learning agility: psychological safety as mediator and algorithmic HRM intensity as moderator
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether leader growth mindset is associated with engineers' learning agility and idea implementation through team psychological safety, and whether that climate pathway is weakened when human resource processes are more intensely mediated by algorithmic and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled systems. Design/methodology/approach A multi-source, multi-wave field study was conducted across 60 research and development teams over four months. Leaders reported growth mindset and algorithmic Human Resource Management (HRM)intensity at Time 1, engineers reported team psychological safety at Time 2 and learning agility at Time 3, and idea-implementation counts were obtained from leaders and available organizational records. Hypotheses were tested with multilevel models and bootstrapped indirect-effect estimates. Findings Leader growth mindset was positively associated with team psychological safety, which in turn was positively related to engineers' learning agility and idea implementation. Higher algorithmic HRM intensity was negatively associated with psychological safety and attenuated the positive relationship between leader growth mindset and team psychological safety. Conditional indirect effects were stronger when algorithmic HRM intensity was lower. Originality/value This study extends leader goal-orientation and psychological-safety research by con…

title: Recursive Pixel Partitioning and Multi-Stream Deep Learning for Annotation-Efficient Lung Disease Classification
abstract: Accurate lung disease classification from chest X-ray (CXR) images remains challenging in annotation-scarce clinical settings where pixel-level lung masks are unavailable. We propose a two-stage framework combining recursive pixel partitioning (RPP) with multi-stream deep learning for lung disease classification. Unlike anatomical segmentation, RPP hierarchically decomposes images into structured spatial sub-regions without manual masks, enabling multi-resolution feature extraction while preserving spatial organization. Dedicated streams process individual partitions, and their features are aggregated through collaborative learning to reduce information loss associated with single-stream convolutional neural networks. The framework is evaluated on two frontal CXR datasets: a balanced three-class dataset of 1,088 images (361 COVID-19, 365 Normal, and 362 Pneumonia) from the COVID-19 Radiography Database and Chest X-ray dataset, and the Shenzhen tuberculosis dataset (326 normal and 326 tuberculosis images). ImageNet-pretrained InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, Xception, ResNet101, and NASNetMobile are used for feature extraction. On the three-class task, the multi-stream model achieves 97.71% test accuracy, exceeding the best single-stream baseline (MobileNetV2, 94.50%) by 3.21 percentage points while converging approximately four times faster. On the Shenzhen dataset, it achieves 89.3% …

title: Estimating groundwater levels and their associated uncertainty through spatiotemporal kriging of groundwater-level data
abstract: Abstract Sustainable groundwater management requires, among other factors, reliable monitoring of groundwater levels (GWLs) and their spatiotemporal evolution in an aquifer with meaningfully quantified uncertainty. Geostatistical methods can estimate GWL surfaces directly from available groundwater monitoring data. This contrasts with groundwater flow modeling, which requires much more detailed data. This study estimates spatiotemporal GWL maps and quantifies associated uncertainties by spatiotemporal kriging, which combines spatial interpolation with temporal gap filling and noise filtering. The central hypothesis is that including hydrogeological information in kriging improves GWL predictions. To test this hypothesis, spatiotemporal trends and soft information inspired by hydrological understanding are included. These include digital elevation models, river exchange components, and the confinement status of aquifers. To test the necessity of full statistical involvement through Bayesian hyperparameter inference, universal kriging is operated in a fully Bayesian framework and then compared to simpler approaches like non-Bayesian and residual space–time kriging. The approach is demonstrated for the Wairau Plain aquifer, New Zealand, where the spatiotemporal GWL estimates can be compared with transient simulation results from a numerical groundwater flow model. The results indi…

title: Uncertainty Based New Class of Neutrosophic Estimators of Population Variance Using Simple Random Sampling
abstract: In sampling surveys, estimating the population variance accurately is important for data analysis and decision-making. The conventional estimators often fail to account for uncertainty, leading to biased or inefficient results. This article proposes an uncertainty-based new class of neutrosophic estimators for the population variance using simple random sampling (SRS). The proposed neutrosophic estimators use the auxiliary information to enhance the efficiency of the estimates. The bias and mean square error (MSE) expressions for the proposed neutrosophic estimators are derived and compared their performance with the adapted neutrosophic estimators. Simulation studies and real data applications show that the proposed neutrosophic estimators obtain lower MSE and higher percent relative efficiency (PRE) under different conditions. The findings suggest that the proposed estimators significantly improve the precision of the estimates under uncertain environments.
venue: International Journal of Uncertainty, Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems

title: Equity-aware multi-objective optimization of nature-based solutions for flood susceptibility reduction
abstract: Abstract Nature-based solutions (NBS) are increasingly promoted for flood mitigation, yet how to allocate limited resources while balancing aggregate effectiveness and social equity remains poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether directing greater mitigation benefits toward socially vulnerable communities necessarily requires substantial losses in overall flood-susceptibility reduction. We develop an equity-aware multi-objective optimization framework for allocating tree planting and wetland restoration across census block groups under fixed budget, suitability, and intervention-capacity constraints. The framework explicitly represents the trade-off between aggregate flood-susceptibility reduction and vulnerability-weighted mitigation benefit, while high-priority locations are identified using a composite flood risk metric integrating flood susceptibility, population exposure, and social vulnerability. We apply the framework to Dorchester and Somerset Counties, Maryland, and evaluate exact optimization alongside greedy, random, and reinforcement-learning benchmarks. Under a USD 20 million budget, moderate vulnerability weighting produced substantial gains in vulnerability-weighted mitigation benefit with little loss in aggregate performance. In Dorchester, aggregate susceptibility reduction changed from 33.47% under the pure-efficiency solution to 33.21% under m…

title: Optimization of Turning Parameters for Aluminum 7075 Using the Taguchi Method: A Statistical Approach
abstract: This study focuses on optimizing turning parameters for machining Aluminum 7075 using the Taguchi method. The effects of cutting speed, feed rate, and depth of cut on machining performance were investigated to improve surface finish and material removal rate (MRR). Experiments were conducted with cutting speeds of 200–240 mm/min, feed rates of 0.08–0.14 mm/rev, and depths of cut of 0.1–0.8 mm, while maintaining a constant machining time of 120 seconds. An L9 orthogonal array and ANOVA were used to analyze the influence of process parameters. The optimal conditions were a cutting speed of 240 mm/min, feed rate of 0.08 mm/rev, and depth of cut of 0.8 mm, resulting in a minimum surface roughness of 0.945 µm and improved machining efficiency.

title: Configuration-Aware Aircraft Maintenance Program Bridging: Data Model, Decision Rules and Scheduling Optimization Illustrated with FAA Airworthiness Directives
abstract: This design-science paper specifies the IMPB-TDO framework: a relational data model with explicit limit anchors and evidence links; seven ordered decision rules that assign each requirement–aircraft pair to one of seven disposition classes, including an engineering exception that is never defaulted to “not applicable”; flight-hour, flight-cycle and calendar forecasting with “whichever occurs first/later” logic; and a network-flow mixed-integer program that schedules only approved tasks. Four Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Airworthiness Directives (ADs) from 2024–2025 serve as illustrative cases, and the framework is demonstrated on a synthetic 14-aircraft fleet and on randomly generated capacity-constrained fleets. The ADs differ in what determines applicability (all serials, in-service embodiment, repair method, certificate date) and in costing unit; two published fleet cost totals are ceilings, not expected costs. In the worked example on AD 2025-16-06, production embodiment, a planned modification and an undocumented configuration each changed the disposition. On a fleet built to contain these situations, an SB-aware tracking comparator still differed on 3 of 14 configuration-sensitive pairs, all traceable to provenance or coupled actions; a model-level filter differed on 10. On 18 generated instances with fleet-wide inspector capacity, the optimization lowered the co…

title: Constraint-Native Globalization: Extending the Value-Yield Optimization (VYO) Framework to the Internationalization of Resource-Constrained SMEs
abstract: International business scholarship has long documented that the benefits of globalization accrue unevenly: large multinational enterprises (MNEs) capture most cross-border value, while small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which constitute the overwhelming majority of firms worldwide, remain largely excluded from global value chains. This exclusion is primarily a matter of constraint rather than ambition or product quality. The prevailing internationalization models-stage theories, the Uppsala model, and born-global paradigms-assume access to market intelligence, foreign-market capital, multilingual talent, and regulatory-compliance capacity that resource-constrained SMEs often cannot supply. The Value-Yield Optimization (VYO) Framework (Yevsiukova, 2026) addressed this problem domestically by ranking AI-driven optimization opportunities according to the return achievable within a firm's real capital, labor, and technical limits. This paper introduces the Global Value-Yield Optimization (G-VYO) Framework, which extends VYO to the cross-border domain. G-VYO differs from VYO in three respects: it adds three cross-border factors (market distance, currency and macroeconomic volatility, and regulatory friction) to the constraint-weighting function; it adds a sixth stage, a systemic resilience audit of the international portfolio; and it introduces a three-axis readiness-hea…

A MODAL EXCITATION SPECTRUM-BASED FRAMEWORK FOR VIBRATION-ORIENTED OPTIMIZATION OF CYCLICALLY SYMMETRIC BLADED STRUCTURES
abstract: The vibration-oriented optimization of cyclically symmetric bladed structures subjected to aerodynamic excitation remains computationally demanding because conventional strategies typically require repeated harmonic response analyses throughout the optimization process. Controlled modifications of blade geometry, mass or stiffness can reduce critical resonant responses; however, the most favourable modification depends on the operating excitation, the structural dynamic characteristics and practical design constraints. This paper presents a computationally efficient optimization framework based on the proposed Modal Excitation Spectrum (MES). Unsteady aerodynamic pressure fields obtained from computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are transformed into equivalent harmonic nodal forces acting on the structural finite element model. These forces are projected onto mass-normalized structural mode shapes to obtain generalized modal forces representing the aerodynamic excitation in the modal domain. The MES describes the distribution of modal excitation over the selected structural modal branches, whose natural frequencies are tracked relative to the prescribed operating-frequency range. The maximum mass-normalized generalized modal force among the selected structural modal branches is employed as the objective function. Consequently, repeated harmonic response analyses are excluded from…

title: System Dynamics Modeling for Performance Optimization in a Pipe Manufacturing System: An Ethiopian Case Analysis
abstract: This study presents a system dynamics-based case study aimed at evaluating and enhancing the performance of a manufacturing system, with specific application to the Amhara Pipe Factory in Ethiopia. Manufacturing systems in developing economies often face challenges related to capacity utilization, operational inefficiencies, and human performance, which collectively limit their ability to meet customer demand and maintain competitiveness. To address these issues, a system dynamics model integrating human factors, process factors, and product and service factors was developed using empirical data collected through questionnaires, interviews, direct observations, and company records. Statistical analysis using IBM SPSS was applied to identify and prioritize key performanceinfluencing factors, which were subsequently incorporated into the simulation model developed in Vensim software. Three policy scenarios were evaluated to assess potential performance improvements: variation in customer demand, reduction of cycle time and downtime, and enhancement of employee training and experience. Simulation results indicate that increasing customer demand by 50% improves production performance by 0.457%, while reducing cycle time and downtime by 50% increases performance by 2.257%. The most significant improvement was observed under the human-factor-focused scenario, where enhancing employee…

Triple burden at the HIV–hepatitis B–malaria interface: viral–parasite interactions, epidemiological complexity and the case for integrated surveillance and community-based prevention in sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and malaria overlap across sub-Saharan Africa, yet they differ in how they spread, how long they last and how programmes measure success. This critical narrative review examines the evidence for biological interaction at each interface, the diagnostic and epidemiological traps that their overlap creates, and the case for integrated surveillance and community prevention. HIV-associated immunosuppression consistently increases the frequency and severity of malaria, and acute malaria transiently raises plasma HIV RNA. HIV accelerates the natural history of chronic HBV. Because HIV treatment and prevention are shifting towards regimens and long-acting products with no activity against HBV, a documented hepatitis B surface antigen result has become essential before any regimen change. Antiretroviral and antimalarial drugs also interact in clinically relevant ways. A direct interaction between HBV and Plasmodium is plausible, through interferon-mediated suppression of HBV during malaria, but it rests mainly on animal models and small, inconsistent human studies, and no reliable estimate of triple infection exists. Fever, anaemia and abnormal liver tests during malaria can mask a concurrent chronic viral infection, and routine facility data can produce apparent coinfection patterns that reflect testing intensity rather than b…

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis supports a causal association of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with benign prostatic hyperplasia and interactions between VCAN-high fibroblasts and macrophages in hyperplastic prostate tissue
abstract: Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) are common among middle-aged and older men and can coexist clinically. However, the direction of causality and the underlying biological links between them remain unclear. Methods The population-level association between COPD and BPH was evaluated using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), and Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal directions and immune-related genetic features. We integrated transcriptomic analyses of both diseases and used differential expression, functional enrichment, co-expression network analysis, and machine learning to characterize disease-associated transcriptional profiles and identify shared candidate genes. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses were further used to determine the cellular localization of the key candidate, characterize associated functional states, and assess potential cell-cell interactions. Finally, core mechanisms were validated through co-culture, immunofluorescence, and other experiments. Results NHANES analysis showed that COPD was significantly associated with prevalent BPH. MR supported a causal effect of COPD on BPH risk; this finding remained stable in multivariable analyses, whereas reverse MR showed no clear effect. Immunogenetic analyses suggested partially…

An integrated computational and experimental framework identifies apigenin as a potential therapeutic agent targeting EGFR/STAT3/MMP9 signaling in glioma
abstract: Background Glioma is the most common primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system and is characterized by aggressive progression, high recurrence rates, and limited therapeutic options. Apigenin, a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits promising anti-tumor properties; however, its molecular mechanisms in glioma remain insufficiently understood. To systematically identify the therapeutic targets and molecular mechanisms underlying apigenin-mediated anti-glioma activity through an integrated computational and experimental approach. Methods An integrated bioinformatics framework combining network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, and machine learning algorithms was applied to identify potential therapeutic targets of apigenin in glioma. Differentially expressed genes were screened using TCGA and GTEx datasets, and prognostic genes were identified through LASSO Cox regression, ElasticNet, and stepwise Cox regression analyses, followed by construction and validation of a multigene prognostic model. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), over-representation analysis (ORA), and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed to explore functional mechanisms. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET prediction were conducted to evaluate the interaction stability and drug-like properties of apigenin with candidate targets. Furthermor…

title: Dual pillar career paths or intertwined career patterns? (Unexpected) Insights into the German science system
abstract: Abstract Academic career paths are shaped not only by individual aspirations but also by social-institutional arrangements and organizational opportunity structures. In Germany, the science system is traditionally portrayed as a “dual pillar” structure, comprising universities and non-university research institutions (NURs). Although collaboration between these pillars has increased, particularly through science policy initiatives such as the Excellence Strategy and the Pact for Research and Innovation, it remains unclear whether career paths continue to follow separate tracks or increasingly span both pillars. This study investigates the career paths of doctoral graduates in six STEM disciplines using sequence analysis of CV data. We identify typical career patterns and interorganizational mobility between institutional contexts. Our findings reveal that some researchers pursue careers exclusively within universities or NURs, while others transition from one to the other. However, truly intertwined patterns crossing both types of institutions are rare and tend to be linked to specific academic goals, such as attaining a professorship. Drawing on Hermanowicz’ sociology of academic careers and Laudel and Gläser’s concept of organizational career, we conceptualize universities and NURs not simply as pillars, but as distinct organizational contexts with partially overlapping logic…

title: Multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to extended Shared Socioeconomic Pathways
abstract: Despite their profound consequences for the global carbon cycle, multi-centennial ocean biogeochemical responses to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate long-term oceanic responses to atmospheric CO 2 forcing using the Model for Interdisciplinary Research on Climate, Earth System version 2 for Long-term simulations (MIROC-ES2L) Earth system model driven by extended Shared Socio-economic Pathway (SSP) scenarios through to the year 2500. Ocean–atmosphere p CO 2 disequilibrium exhibits strong scenario dependence. Under the low-emission scenario SSP1–2.6, oceanic CO 2 undersaturation gradually weakens and approaches near equilibrium by 2100. By contrast, under the high-emission scenario SSP5–8.5, rapid increase in atmospheric p CO 2 results in increasing undersaturation of CO 2 in the ocean over the 21st century. Thereafter, surface-ocean CO 2 supersaturation progressively expand into the equatorial and subtropical oceans between the mid–23rd and late 25th century. The Southern Ocean remains persistently undersaturated throughout the simulations, consistent with sustained influence from deep waters that are weakly affected by anthropogenic perturbations. Under SSP5–8.5, oceanic CO 2 uptake continues to increase until the late 21st century. Thereafter, it gradually weakens as surface-ocean p CO 2 approaches atmospheric levels, whereas t…

title: Multi-Hazard Resilience of Desert Roads in Southern Libya: A Geo-Engineering Decision Framework
abstract: Background: Desert roads in southern Libya connect dispersed settlements but face interacting sand encroachment, episodic flash floods, extreme heat, and geotechnical deterioration. Objective: This article develops a transparent geo-engineering decision framework for multi-hazard resilience screening and selection of feasible interventions without claiming new field measurements. Methods: A critical, thematic synthesis of recent peer-reviewed research and publicly accessible Libyan hazard reports was organized around exposure, asset fragility, network criticality, intervention performance, and evidence confidence. A staged appraisal procedure integrates multi-hazard screening, engineering suitability checks, multicriteria comparison, and uncertainty testing. Results: The synthesis identifies distinct failure pathways: sand impedes carriageway operation, floods threaten drainage crossings and embankments, while heat and weak subgrades accelerate pavement distress. The proposed framework produces a hazard–asset matrix, a tiered portfolio of avoidance, protection, maintenance, and monitoring responses, and explicit gates for local verification. It distinguishes transferable international methods from location-specific evidence that remains incomplete. Discussion: Network redundancy and access to emergency services can change priorities even where physical damage is modest. Uncerta…

title: The effects of work overload on emotional exhaustion among nurses: serial mediation of job stress and depression
abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion among nurses. Specifically, the study investigates the serial mediating effect of job stress and depression on the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion. Design/methodology/approach Data were gathered between October 2025 and January 2026 through an online and face-to-face cross-sectional survey of 613 nurses working in two state hospitals in Türkiye. Sequential mediating effects were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences PROCESS macro (Model 6). Findings The findings showed that work overload is positively related to emotional exhaustion. Furthermore, the results revealed that job stress and depression sequentially mediate the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion. Originality/value This research offers a clearer understanding of the potential psychological mechanisms underlying the relationship between work overload and emotional exhaustion among nurses. It also extends the literature by informing the development of interventions aimed at alleviating job stress and reducing depression levels among nurses in the healthcare sector. In particular, primary caregivers and hospital administrations responsible for nurses should develop work overload-conscious, stress-reducing, and mental health-supporting methods to improve …

title: Computational Modeling and Performance Evaluation of Optical Imaging Systems with Different Aperture Geometries under Atmospheric Turbulence Filtering
abstract: Analyzing the functionality of optical systems following their production holds considerable scientific and practical relevance. It provides a wide range of possibilities for research and the advancement of novel methodologies to furnish thorough data regarding the optical system; the point spread function (PSF) is a vital component for measuring the effectiveness of such systems. Core pictorial information is usually interwoven throughout an image's arrangement characteristics and ambient context. These factors demand tailored processing strategies to maintain appropriate image resolution. This study presents a formulation aimed at substantially increasing image sharpness and clarity by employing the PSF equation for optical systems having circular, rectangular, square, and triangular apertures. Utilizing Mathcad software, we executed an atmospheric turbulence filter characterized by parameters δ=0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1 on all optical systems as a way of enhancing images. Situated at the system's entrance, this filter replicates or reduces the influence of atmospheric turbulence on light and the resulting image, particularly in extended-range systems. The filter's function is not explicitly for enhancing images; rather, it replicates the influence of air turbulence on the system, enabling the assessment of the system's (or filters') proficiency in sustaining resolution under …

title: Agricultural Information Networks, Information Needs and Risk Management Strategies among Smallholder Farmers in Southeast Nigeria
abstract: This study examined agricultural information networks, information needs, and risk management strategies among smallholder farmers in Southeast Nigeria using the Diffusion of Innovation Theory. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS Version 21 with descriptive statistics including means, frequencies, rankings, and standard deviations, while qualitative data from focus group discussions were examined thematically using Braun and Clarke’s six-step framework. Findings show dominance of farmer-to-farmer networks, traditional knowledge systems, and kinship ties as the most trusted sources of agricultural information, while institutional and digital platforms were least utilized. Major information needs centred on disease and pest management, climate-related risks, fertilizer use, and improved seed varieties, reflecting farmers’ vulnerability to environmental and production uncertainties. Within Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovation Theory, interpersonal communication channels such as peer networks significantly influenced awareness and adoption of agricultural practices. The study concludes that strengthening farmer-led networks and improving access to credible institutional information sources can enhance risk management and innovation adoption among smallholders in the region. Implications suggest that extension agencies and development actors should leverage existing social structu…

title: Evaluation of the Quran literacy program at Muhammadiyah Simpang Empat Junior High School using the CIPP Model
abstract: Low Qur’an reading proficiency among junior high school students from general education backgrounds poses a unique challenge for Islamic-based schools. This study aims to evaluate the Qur’an Literacy Program at Muhammadiyah Simpang Empat Junior High School using the CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product) evaluation model. This study used a qualitative approach, with data collection methods including in-depth interviews, structured observations, and document analysis. The evaluation results at the context stage showed that this program arose from a real need and is highly relevant to the school’s vision and mission. The evaluation at the input stage indicated that, despite limitations in the number of teachers and financial support, the program was designed and implemented efficiently, realistically, and collaboratively. The process stage revealed that program implementation was consistent with the plan, student participation was high, and regular monitoring and improvements were conducted. In the product stage, the program proved successful in improving students’ ability to read the Qur’an, fostering religious attitudes, and having a positive impact on students’ self-confidence. This program also has strong potential for replication in other schools.
venue: International research journal of management, IT and social sciences

title: Decoupled vegetation structure and composition in a mangrove–apicum ecotone in Northeastern Brazil
abstract: Abstract Mangrove–apicum ecotones are heterogeneous transition zones in which woody colonization need not follow a single age-ordered trajectory. We reanalysed an author-validated area-level matrix from ten successional mangrove patches in the Barra de Gramame estuary, northeastern Brazil. Five patches belonged to a 6–10-year and five to an 11–15-year site-history category inherited from the original survey. Individuals of Avicennia schaueriana , Laguncularia racemosa and Rhizophora mangle were classified into two height-defined structural strata (< 1 m and >1 m) and counted over 225 m2 per patch; a single 900 m2 reference stand was used descriptively. Hierarchical Bayesian modelling, fully enumerated exact permutations, Bray–Curtis and Aitchison analyses, beta-diversity partitioning and leave-one-area-out diagnostics were applied. The <1 m stratum contained 7,439 individuals, compared with 1,898 individuals in the >1 m stratum. Posterior density ratios (< 1 m/>1 m) were 2.73 (95% credible interval: 1.46–5.12) in 6–10-year areas and 3.64 (1.94–6.73) in 11–15-year areas, whereas site-history effects remained uncertain. Abundance-sensitive assemblage structure differed significantly between height strata (Bray–Curtis R2 = 0.213, exact P = 0.00195), whereas relative species composition did not clearly differ under Aitchison geometry (R2 = 0.029, P = 0.105). Long-haul L + S-band WDM transmission over a 1052-km dispersion-shifted fiber link with inter-band nonlinearity management
abstract: We demonstrated long-haul inline-amplified wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) transmissions with 10.8-THz signal bandwidth in the L and S bands over a 75.2-km-span dispersion-shifted fiber (DSF) link. In L + S-band DSF transmission, where the signal is allocated on both sides of the zero-dispersion wavelength, some S-band channels and L-band channels can become group-velocity matched, leading to strong inter-band Kerr nonlinear interactions. In addition, the edge-to-edge bandwidth of the L + S-band WDM signal exceeds the peak Raman-shift frequency in the silica-core fibers, resulting in significant power transfer due to inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS). We investigated the feasibility of L + S-band long-haul coherent transmissions over DSF links by optimizing the launch power for each band. We also evaluated a band-wise bidirectional transmission configuration in which the S-band and L-band signals propagate in opposite directions to avoid inter-band phase matching. Highly efficient parametric waveband converters based on periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides were employed for the generation, reception, and amplification of the S-band signals. title: Blockchain Technology and Financial Services Transformation: Evidence from Institutional Cryptocurrency Adoption
abstract: Introduction/Main Objectives: The advent of blockchain technology has introduced a new paradigm in the financial landscape through decentralization, immutability, transparency and enhanced efficiency in financial services. This study focuses on institutional cryptocurrency adoption and its implications for financial services transformation in the blockchain era. Background Problems: Most studies have focused on the institutional adoption of one cryptocurrency or one institutional investment channel. This study focuses on institutional cryptocurrency adoption via three distinct institutional investment channels for Bitcoin and four other key cryptocurrencies. Novelty: There have been some limited studies that have attempted to quantify the various institutional channels for investing alongside the key cryptocurrencies. This study set out to fill this gap through a thorough empirical assessment of institutional cryptocurrency adoption. Research Methods: The study adopted a quantitative method and secondary data was obtained from credible databases and market reports on cryptocurrencies. Descriptive analysis and comparative concentration of ownership analyses were used on the basis of participation of institutions, geographical coverage, institutional holdings, CR5, CR10, Herfindahl Hirschman Index (HHI) and Gini coefficient. title: Financial Leverage and Financial Performance in Emerging Tourism Economies: Empirical Evidence from Sri Lanka’s Listed Hotel Sector
abstract: Financial leverage plays a critical role in shaping a company’s performance, particularly as businesses strive to reduce their overall cost of capital. Thus, this study investigates the relationship between financial leverage and financial performance among high market-capitalized hotels listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) over the period of 2015–2024. Drawing on trade-off, pecking order, and agency theories, this study investigates the effect of two key financial leverage indicators, debt ratio and debt-to-equity ratio, on financial performance using measures such as return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE) while using firm size as the control variable. Using panel data, the study covers 18 listed hotels and 180 firm-year observations and employs regression analysis. The findings reveal that the debt ratio has a significant positive effect on ROA, supporting the trade-off theory's notion that moderate debt enhances asset utilization and operational efficiency. Conversely, debt-to-equity ratio shows no significant impact on ROA. Regarding ROE, the debt-to-equity ratio and debt ratio demonstrate a significant positive effect, suggesting that higher leverage can improve shareholder returns under prudent management. The study enriches the limited empirical literature on capital structure within Sri Lanka’s tourism sector and offers practical insights for hotel mana…

title: Digital Financial Literacy, Technology Trust, and Financial Attitudes: MSME Financial Well-Being in Pangkalpinang
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the influence of digital financial literacy, trust in technology, and financial attitudes on the financial well-being of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) owners in Pangkalpinang City.Methodology: This study employs a quantitative approach using multiple linear regression analysis, along with t-tests and F-tests, to examine the impact of digital financial literacy and trust in technology on the financial well-being of MSME owners in Pangkalpinang City. The sample consists of 107 respondents selected via purposive sampling. Following data transformation, data from 100 respondents were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS version 32.Results: Digital financial literacy has a significant negative effect on financial well-being, whereas trust in technology and financial attitudes have significant positive effects. These three variables explain 86% of the variation in financial well-being.Conclusions: Digital financial literacy, trust in technology, and financial attitudes collectively influence the financial well-being of MSME owners in Pangkalpinang City.Limitations: The study is geographically limited and utilizes non-probability sampling, which restricts the generalizability of the findings.Contribution: This study provides empirical evidence regarding the application of Consumer Financial Well-Being Theory and the Theory…

title: Financial Performance Implications of Capital Structure Choices: Evidence from Listed Non-Financial Companies in Sri Lanka
abstract: Capital structure decisions are considered as critical in the present highly competitive financial world, as firms strategically adopt them to accomplish their goals. The composition of a firm’s capital influences its overall cost of financing and value. Particularly, firms need to cautiously evaluate the advantages of debt financing in contrast to the potential costs of insolvency and financial distress. The primary objective of the study is to examine the extent to which capital structure choices influence the financial performance of non-financial companies in Sri Lanka. This study includes the independent variables of the Debt-to-Equity Ratio and Debt to-Total Assets Ratio, reflecting the proportion of debt and equity used to finance operations and growth and the dependent variables are Return on Equity (ROE) and Return on Assets (ROA), which measure financial performance. Under the stratified random sampling method 70 non-financial companies were selected and the relevant data of the sample companies were collected for the period from 2020 to 2024 from the audited annual financial statements of the companies. The statistical techniques of Pearson’s correlation and panel data regression were used to analyse the association between the capital structure decisions and the financial performance. title: The Right to Disconnect in Modern Employment: Protecting the Boundary Between Work and Personal Life in the Digital Era
abstract: Digital transformation has changed the way humans work, especially regarding time and space. Smartphones, emails, instant messaging applications, and collaborative work platforms allow employers to contact employees almost anywhere and at any time. The boundary traditionally established by labor law between "working hours" and "rest periods" is therefore increasingly eroded. This article examines the right to disconnect as a new legal institution designed to protect that boundary. The study uses qualitative methods: textual analysis, comparative jurisprudence, historical analysis, synthesis, logic, and descriptive statistics based on secondary data. The article systematizes international scientific literature, compares representative legal models (France, Spain, Belgium, Portugal, Ireland, Ontario, Chile, Australia, and the European Union), and then juxtaposes them with current Vietnamese law. The results show that the right to disconnect has evolved from a bargainable declaration into an enforceable legal obligation backed by sanctions. Meanwhile, Vietnam's Labour Code of 2019 is still designed according to the logic of physical time and lacks legal instruments to regulate out-of-hours digital communications. Guided by the directives of the Documents of the 14th National Congress of the Party on human development, digital transformation, and the building of harmonious, stable,…

title: Qashqadaryo viloyatida moliyaviy xizmatlardan foydalanish imkoniyatlarini baholash va hududiy tafovutlarni qisqartirish yo'llari
abstract: В статье рассматриваются подходы к оценке доступности финансовых услуг в районах и городах Кашкадарьинской области и меры по сокращению территориальных различий. В качестве основных показателей используются обеспеченность точками банковского обслуживания, объёмы кредитов и вкладов в расчёте на душу населения, а также уровень использования цифровых платежей. Сопоставление районов и городов по этим показателям позволяет выявить территории с ограниченным доступом к финансовым услугам. Для сокращения территориальных различий предлагаются меры по расширению охвата банковскими услугами, развитию инфраструктуры цифровых платежей и повышению финансовой грамотности населения.

title: Financial Performance and Firm Value: The Moderating Role of ESG Disclosure in Indonesian Mining Firms
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether Return on Assets (ROA) affects firm value (Tobin’s Q) and whether Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure moderates this effect in Indonesian mining firms.Methodology: An explanatory quantitative design with secondary data was applied to nine mining firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange that issued complete annual and sustainability reports in 2021–2025 (45 firm-year observations). ESG disclosure was scored by content analysis of the 30 indicators of the National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations (NASDAQ) ESG Reporting Guide 2.0. Moderated panel regression was estimated in EViews, and the Chow and Hausman tests selected the fixed effect model.Results: ROA has a positive but insignificant effect on Tobin’s Q (coefficient 0.433, p = 0.176). The ROA × ESG interaction is positive (3.722) but not significant at the 5% level (p = 0.070). The model is jointly significant (adjusted R² = 0.809), largely because of firm fixed effects.Conclusions: The evidence is insufficient to conclude that ROA influences firm value or that ESG disclosure alters that influence at the 5% level.Limitations: The sample is small, the period is short, no control variables are included, and the binary disclosure index varies little across firms.Contribution: The study tests ESG disclosure as a moderator, not a direct predictor, wi…

title: The Mediating Role of Digital Literacy Between Financial Literacy and Investment Scam Awareness
abstract: This study analyses whether digital literacy mediates the relationship between financial literacy and investment scam awareness. Despite the rapid expansion of digital financial services, there remains limited knowledge of whether financial and digital literacy interact to shape resistance to online investment scams. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among undergraduates who were selected through stratified random sampling in Sri Lanka. Financial literacy is measured through budgeting skills, financial attitude, financial product literacy and risk awareness. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied to estimate the direct effects and mediating effects. Budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness enhance digital literacy, while financial attitude shows no meaningful effect. Digital literacy exhibits the strongest direct influence on investment scam awareness. Mediation analysis confirms that digital literacy transmits the effects of budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness to scam awareness, whereas financial attitude remains non-significant. The study conceptualizes digital literacy as a coping appraisal mechanism that enables individuals to operationalize financial knowledge in digital financial environments. Guided by Protection Motivation Theory, the study interprets financial literacy as supporting threat appraisal…

Inverse design of terahertz metasurface polarization converters based on generative adversarial networks
abstract: A reflection-type broadband terahertz metasurface polarization converter with a three-layer structure—comprising a patterned metal layer, a dielectric layer, and a metallic ground plane—is inversely designed based on a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP). By incorporating the Wasserstein distance and a gradient penalty term, the WGAN-GP effectively overcomes the training instability inherent in conventional generative adversarial networks, thereby enabling the construction of an end-to-end mapping model from target spectra to metasurface structural parameters. The results demonstrate that the WGAN-GP achieves efficient and high-accuracy inverse design, with a single inference time of only 30 ms and a mean absolute error of structural parameter prediction as low as 0.1263. The optimized metasurface polarization converter exhibits a consistently high polarization conversion ratio exceeding 0.8 over the 3–7.5 THz frequency range, corresponding to a relative bandwidth of up to 86%, and maintains excellent angular stability within an incidence angle range of 0° to 50°. This work not only verifies the efficiency and reliability of WGAN-GP in the inverse design of complex electromagnetic devices, but also provides an effective solution for the development of high-performance terahertz metasurfaces, with the potential to accelerate device innovati…

title: RECONSTRUÇÃO ESTÉTICA DE SOBRANCELHAS EM PACIENTES COM ALOPECIA NÃO CICATRICIAL: UMA ABORDAGEM COMBINADA ENTRE DESIGN E ESTÍMULO COSMÉTICO
abstract: A alopecia não cicatricial caracteriza-se pela perda parcial ou total dos pelos sem destruição definitiva do folículo piloso, podendo acometer diferentes regiões do corpo, incluindo as sobrancelhas. Essa condição pode causar impactos estéticos, emocionais e psicossociais significativos, comprometendo a autoestima, a autoimagem e a qualidade de vida dos indivíduos. Nesse contexto, a tricologia e a estética associada desenvolveram abordagens não invasivas voltadas à recuperação funcional e estética dos pacientes acometidos por essas alterações capilares. O presente trabalho teve como objetivo analisar a reconstrução estética de sobrancelhas em paciente com alopecia não cicatricial por meio de uma abordagem combinada entre design de sobrancelhas e estímulos cosméticos, considerando seus possíveis benefícios estéticos. Tratou-se de um estudo descritivo, de caráter qualitativo, realizado por meio de relato de caso clínico, com avaliação estética, registros fotográficos e análise da evolução do tratamento. A associação entre estímulos cosméticos e técnicas de design de sobrancelhas foi utilizada com o propósito de contribuir para o estímulo ao crescimento dos fios e a melhora da harmonia facial. O trabalho também permitiu discutir a atuação da estética e da tricologia no manejo das alopecias não cicatriciais, destacando a importância de abordagens humanizadas e integrativas na reabil…

title: Design, Implementation, and Empirical Evaluation of a Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model in Higher Education
abstract: AI-supported assessment increasingly enables adaptive tasks, automated analysis, and personalized feedback, yet their integration into coherent, human-supervised formative assessment remains insufficiently established. This study developed and evaluated the Human–AI Collaborative Adaptive Assessment Model (HA-CAAM) using Design and Development Research structured through the ADDIE framework. Implemented in a higher-education Media Education course, the model employed performance-responsive task adaptation using predefined thresholds, rubric-guided AI-assisted scoring, formative feedback, and instructor verification. Five experts validated the model, 148 students provided quantitative and qualitative implementation feedback, and 50 student responses were independently assessed by two human raters and AI. Expert validation provided initial evidence of content validity (mean Aiken's V = 0.818). Students reported generally favorable experiences, particularly regarding clarity and feedback usefulness, although Learning Support and Overall User Experience received comparatively lower ratings. AI-generated scores demonstrated strong agreement with human-reference scores (ICC = 0.898), despite individual discrepancies. These findings provide initial evidence of content validity, positive implementation experiences, and scoring agreement, rather than demonstrated improvements in learnin…

Intergenerational Effects of Türkiye’s Education Reform on Children’s Academic and Health Outcomes
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the intergenerational effects of Türkiye’s 1997 compulsory schooling reform, which increased mandatory schooling from five to eight years. Drawing on a novel dataset from the nationally representative 2022 Turkish Child Survey, we use a regression discontinuity design (RDD) to identify the effect of mothers’ exposure to the education reform. We find that the reform significantly increased maternal educational attainment and, in turn, improved children’s performance in Turkish, while having no statistically significant effect on mathematics achievement. Maternal exposure to the reform also had positive effects on children’s mental health, increasing happiness and reducing anxiety, but did not affect their general health status. These effects are heterogeneous by child gender, with boys benefiting more than girls. Analysis of potential channels shows that increased parental investment may be one relevant channel explaining the observed effects, while reduced child work appears to play a limited role.
