Analysis of the Effectiveness of Upskilling Programs in Improving Agent Performance to Face Market Dynamics
abstract: The rapidly evolving sales environment requires sales agents to continuously enhance their competencies to respond effectively to changing market demands. However, the effectiveness of upskilling programs in improving job performance remains insufficiently understood, particularly from the perspectives of sales agents themselves. This study aimed to examine the implementation of upskilling programs for sales agents, explore their experiences in applying newly acquired skills during customer interactions, and identify the facilitating factors and barriers influencing the transfer of training to workplace practices amid changing market conditions. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through semi-structured interviews, observations of sales activities, and document analysis involving sales agents and supervisors. The findings revealed that formal training enhanced agents' conceptual understanding of products and sales procedures, while informal knowledge sharing among colleagues reinforced their practical competencies. Nevertheless, the transfer of acquired knowledge and skills into consistent workplace behaviors was not automatic but depended on opportunities for practical application, the quality of supervisory feedback, peer support, and the alignment of training content with actual customer needs and sales situations. Operational constraints, i…

title: Supply chain networks in horticulture: an assessment of farmers' perceptions and market linkages
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the determinants of horticulture supply chain efficiency (SCE) and the mediating effects of market linkage strength (MLS). Design/methodology/approach The study conceptualises and tests a partial least squares structural equation modelling model based on the resource-based view and relational exchange theory, with the data collected from 500 horticultural farmers from Shimla, Kullu and Kinnaur districts of Himachal Pradesh. Findings The findings show that logistics capability (LC) has the strongest effects on MLS (β = 0.395) and SCE (β = 0.388), followed by information and coordination (IC). Transaction fairness (TF) and digital adoption (DA) significantly strengthen MLS, while MLS positively influences SCE (β = 0.233). MLS provides complementary mediation for LC and IC and indirect-only mediation for TF and DA. Originality/value The study integrates operational capabilities and relational mechanisms to explain how market linkages contribute to horticultural supply-chain efficiency, offering context-specific evidence from an underexplored horticultural setting.

title: Intelligent Detection of Securities Market Manipulation Using Multimodal Financial Data
abstract: Market manipulation through securities involves increasingly sophisticated mechanisms such as irregular trading, selective information disclosures, and joint activities in different securities, posing threats to surveillance relying solely on a particular information source due to both false positives and late identification of manipulations. We propose a multimodal framework for the detection of market manipulation on China's A-share market by fusing one-minute market microstructure time series, corporate announcements, financial news, and evolving relationships among securities. Enforced cases by China Securities Regulatory Commission from 2018–2025 were combined with unenforced stock-period observations and temporal, textual, and relational features are extracted using Temporal Convolutional Network, MacBERT encoder, and Graph Attention Network, respectively, followed by cross-modal attention to generate a risk score. Our framework achieved macro-F1 of 0.872 ± 0.009, AUROC of 0.946 ± 0.006, and AUPRC of 0.821 ± 0.012 on the unseen data, outperforming the TCN-only model in market only by a wide margin of 0.036 ± 0.007 and 0.028 ± 0.006 for removing text and graph information, respectively. In the 2025 market surveillance simulation, reviewing the top 10% of ranked observations led to detecting 0.643 ± 0.031 of manipulations with 0.074 ± 0.009 false-positive rate.

title: Field of Study, Skill Specificity and Early-Career Labor-Market Returns among Chinese University Graduates
abstract: Against the backdrop of the massification of higher education, the supply of college graduates in the labor market has been steadily increasing. Wage disparities among graduates in different fields during the early stages of their careers have gradually become more pronounced, and the relationship between academic discipline and income has emerged as a key focus of research on human capital. This study examines how fields of study are associated with early-career wages among Chinese university graduates. It also examines skill specificity, major–job matching, and labor demand. This paper employs a structured literature review and a relatively comprehensive analytical approach based on published empirical studies to compare research findings on wage differentials, job-specific skills, and major job-skill mismatches. The existing evidence suggests that graduates from occupationally specific majors can receive higher starting wages if their jobs are related to their studies. Major–job mismatch is often associated with lower wages, although the size and direction of this relationship vary across studies and groups. It further discusses how the supply of graduates and demand for particular skills may shape these wage differences. The study concludes that early-career wage returns reflect the interaction of field-specific human capital, job matching and market conditions, with implic…

title: Conservation in place: perceived pay inequity as a chronic occupational stressor in a high-unemployment labor market
abstract: Perceived pay inequity is well established as a predictor of turnover intention, but less is known about how employees respond to it when they stay. Using the exit–voice–loyalty–neglect (EVLN) framework to interpret employees' responses, and conservation of resources and effort–reward imbalance theories to explain what those responses cost, this study examined how employees in a South African fast-moving consumer goods organization, situated in a labor market with high unemployment, experience and respond to perceived pay inequity. The study is a secondary analysis of semi-structured interviews conducted for a master's dissertation with ten permanent employees and managers at the head office of a large organization in Gauteng province. Transcripts were re-analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The study makes three contributions. First, it shows that perceived pay inequity is relational in two directions: participants judged their pay against others, but also against their own past, registering unfairness when their workload grew faster than their pay. Second, it shows that the most prominent response, a deliberate withdrawal of discretionary effort while remaining in post, is better understood as defensive than as affective loyalty: participants described staying not as attachment or patient optimism but as a position from which they recalculated what they owed and protec…

title: Pet insurance services adoption: how values, reasoning, and insurance literacy shape consumer intentions in an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine pet-insurance adoption in India through behavioral reasoning theory (BRT), focusing on how openness to change and social value shape reasons for and against adoption, how these reasons influence attitude and purchase intention and whether insurance literacy strengthens the attitude–intention relationship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was used. Interviews with 17 pet owners identified the facilitators and inhibitors. Survey data from 352 respondents were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test the mediation and moderation effects. Demographic moderation was treated as an exploratory analysis. Findings Openness to change strengthened both reasons for and reasons against adoption, whereas social value strengthened supportive reasoning and reduced opposing reasoning. Reasons for adoption positively influenced attitude and intention, whereas reasons against adoption had negative effects. Attitude was the strongest predictor of purchase intention, and insurance literacy strengthened the attitude–intention relationship. The unexpected positive association between openness to change and reasons against adoption suggests that receptiveness to novelty may intensify scrutiny of benefits and barriers instead of uniformly increasing adoption readiness. Research limitations/implications The …

title: Priced at disclosure, revealed at horizon: cybersecurity incidents and deferred market risk
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether cybersecurity incident disclosures are associated with short-window market valuation and subsequent risk measures of large listed Indian firms. Design/methodology/approach A market-model event study evaluates 29 retained incidents involving NIFTY 50 constituents. A quarterly panel of 47 firms and 3,002 firm-quarter observations is then used to estimate post-incident changes in cost of equity and realised volatility through two-way fixed-effects, cohort-time, event-time, resampling and leave-one-out analyses. Findings Mean firm-level cumulative abnormal returns are statistically indistinguishable from zero across all reported windows, and attack-category differences are insignificant. Aggregate cost-of-equity estimates are also null. Positive realised-volatility coefficients emerge in later event-time quarters and are jointly significant from t+5 through the late-post bin, although the static effect does not survive family-wise multiple-testing correction. The late-window joint result does not remain significant at the 5% level under a four-outcome Bonferroni sensitivity and is not adjusted across the wider event-time search. Research limitations/implications The incident sample and treated sector groups are small, notification timing and proposed transmission mechanisms are not observed and individual event-time coefficients remain pointwise …

title: Capital Market Liberalization and Inter‑City Corporate Investment
abstract: As a core component of institutional reform in China's financial system, capital market liberalization raises an urgent and critical question: Can it overcome financing barriers and information frictions that hinder cross-regional capital flows, thereby advancing the development of a unified national market? Using the official launch of the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect as a quasi-natural experiment, this study constructs a difference-in-differences model based on data from A-share listed companies between 2000 and 2024 to systematically examine the impact of capital market opening on corporate cross-regional investment. The findings show that the implementation of the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect significantly promotes firms' investments across regions, a result that remains robust after a series of sensitivity tests. Mechanism analysis reveals that capital market liberalization operates through three channels: improving corporate information disclosure quality to reduce information identification costs in distant markets, alleviating financing constraints to broaden funding sources for cross-regional expansion, and increasing institutional investors' shareholdings to strengthen external oversight over management's cross-regional investment decisions. This research offers a new perspective on the microeconomic consequences of capital market liberalization and provides e…

title: How Do Loot Box Probabilities Affect Secondary Market Prices and Player Choices in Video Games
abstract: This study aims to investigate how the probability of winning in video game gacha systems influences players' choices regarding the acquisition of virtual skins, as well as the relationship between this probability mechanism and secondary market prices. Taking Identity V as the research object, this paper focuses on its Gold‑level skins; the official base drop probability for this kind of skin is 0.7%, each single draw is priced at 9.6 yuan, and for players who have not received any gold skin, the game will give out a guaranteed gold skin on the 200th draw. Under this setting, the study calculated the cumulative probability of obtaining a gold skin with different draw numbers, and it also worked out the corresponding spending; these computed results were then compared with the real‑world prices of various gold skins available on the secondary market. Several basic economic concepts, such as scarcity, supply and demand, as well as opportunity cost, were applied in this paper to illustrate the price gap that exists between these two markets. According to the calculation results, players will have a higher probability of receiving a gold skin when they carry out more draws; meanwhile, the 200‑draw cap prevents players from making an unlimited number of attempts. Data collected from the secondary market also presents huge price differences among gold skins; some permanent gold skin…

title: Smart psychological service platform usage frequency and depressive symptoms among university students: a chain mediation model involving psychological capital and self-compassion
abstract: Introduction Drawing on Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examined the associations between the usage frequency of Smart Psychological Service Platforms (SPSPs) and depressive symptoms among university students, as well as the chain mediation of psychological capital and self-compassion in this association. Methods A cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from 1,082 university students. The mediating roles of psychological capital and self-compassion, including their sequential indirect association, were examined. Results SPSP usage frequency was significantly and negatively associated with depressive symptoms among university students. Both psychological capital and self-compassion served as independent mediators in this association. A significant sequential indirect effect was also observed, linking SPSP usage frequency to depressive symptoms through psychological capital and subsequently self-compassion. The pathway “usage frequency → psychological capital → depressive symptoms” showed the largest indirect effect, followed by the chain pathway “usage frequency → psychological capital → self-compassion → depressive symptoms,” whereas the pathway “usage frequency → self-compassion → depressive symptoms” was comparatively weaker. Discussion The findings suggest that external digital mental health resources may be associated with interna…

title: Circular economy 10R strategies in aviation waste management: a systematic review of implementation logic and service implications
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, categorizes and explains how circular economy (CE) 10R strategies are implemented in aviation waste management and why adoption differs across airline-airport service systems. It distinguishes aviation waste management from broader carbon-oriented aviation sustainability debates and examines how circular waste practices may affect service reliability, stakeholder coordination and service quality. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review was used as the methodological approach. Scopus and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed English-language journal studies published between 2000 and December 2025. After deduplication and screening, 39 studies were retained for bibliometric mapping and 34 studies for qualitative content analysis. VOSviewer keyword co-occurrence analysis, descriptive bibliometric profiling and theory-informed coding were combined to synthesize CE 10R strategies, enablers, barriers, success factors and service-system implications. Findings The synthesis shows that aviation waste research remains concentrated in environmental and operational outlets, with limited engagement with service quality scholarship. Adoption is uneven across the 10R hierarchy: Recycle and Recover dominate, whereas Refuse, Rethink and Reduce remain less developed because of biosecurity rules, safety standards, fragmented airlin…

title: PENGARUH SERVICE QUALITY, CUSTOMER VALUE DAN EXPERIENCE TERHADAP WILLINGNESS TO PAY MELALUI KEPUASAN PESERTA
abstract: Keberlanjutan Program Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN) yang dikelola BPJS Kesehatan menghadapi tantangan serius akibat rendahnya kemauan peserta membayar iuran, terutama pada segmen Pekerja Bukan Penerima Upah (PBPU)/mandiri. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh service quality, customer value, dan customer experience terhadap kemauan membayar iuran (willingness to pay) BPJS Kesehatan dengan kepuasan peserta sebagai variabel intervening pada peserta JKN di wilayah kerja BPJS Kesehatan Kantor Cabang Atambua, yang meliputi Kabupaten Belu, Malaka, Timor Tengah Utara, dan Timor Tengah Selatan, Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Timur. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan kuesioner berskala Likert 1–5 yang disebarkan kepada peserta JKN yang memenuhi kriteria inklusi, termasuk peserta yang pernah mengalami gagal bayar. Ukuran sampel ditentukan berdasarkan pedoman Structural Equation Modeling dan dialokasikan secara proporsional pada keempat kabupaten. Data dianalisis menggunakan Analysis of Moment Structures–Structural Equation Modeling (AMOS-SEM) untuk menguji sepuluh hipotesis, mencakup pengaruh langsung, pengaruh mediasi, dan pengaruh kepuasan terhadap kemauan membayar. Hasil penelitian diharapkan memberikan kontribusi teoretis pada model perilaku membayar dalam layanan kesehatan serta rekomendasi praktis bagi BPJS Kesehatan dalam meningkatkan kepatuhan pembayaran iu…

title: TransitSim-LLM: a closed-loop framework for GTFS-driven transit service evaluation using open-source LLMs and SUMO microsimulation
abstract: Introduction Resource-constrained transit agencies face challenges in translating service data into actionable interventions and evaluating their operational consequences. Methods This study develops TransitSim-LLM, an integrated framework combining General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) diagnostics, large language model (LLM) reasoning, and Simulation of Urban Mobility (SUMO) microsimulation. The framework integrates seven service diagnostics, issue prioritization, validated intervention generation, comparative simulation, and planning interpretation. It was evaluated using the MyBas network in Johor Bahru, Malaysia. Results The analysis covered 21 routes and 271 stops, identifying four principal service concerns. Two intervention scenarios satisfied five predefined technical validation criteria. The frequency-enhancement scenario increased completed vehicle trips by 5.2%, reduced the reported waiting-time indicator by 6.2%, and increased vehicle kilometers by 5.8%. Benchmarking four openly available LLMs yielded diagnostic quality scores of 85/100 for three Llama models. LLM-generated scenarios achieved higher rubric-based quality scores (80-86) than rule-based (43) and random (25) alternatives. Discussion TransitSim-LLM demonstrates the potential of integrating structured transit diagnostics, LLM-assisted intervention generation, and microsimulation for evidence-informed …

title: Digital and media literacy of pre-service early childhood teachers in the context of digital education: a bibliometric analysis of research trends
abstract: The digital transformation of education is increasing the demands placed on the professional preparation of pre-service early childhood teachers, including the development of digital competence, media literacy, and emerging competencies related to the use of artificial intelligence. Despite the growing body of research in this area, the conceptual structure of the field and the relationships among these strands remain insufficiently systematized. This study aims to analyze the structure and development of international research on the digital and media literacy of pre-service early childhood teachers, identify the main thematic directions, examine the nature of their interrelationships, and determine existing research gaps. The bibliometric corpus was constructed using data from Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection through a refined search strategy, comparison of the results of two searches, and manual screening of non-relevant records. To avoid distortions associated with an incomplete calendar year, the analysis was limited to the period 2012–2025, resulting in a final corpus of 86 publications. The analysis was conducted using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and included descriptive bibliometric indicators, analysis of scientific collaboration and citation impact, structured content analysis of the most highly cited publications, frequency and network analysis of author ke…

title: Service participation depth in experiential services: media touchpoints and supportive practices
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how media touchpoints, involvement and supportive practices are associated with any live attendance and attendance intensity in spectator sport services. Design/methodology/approach Individual-level data from the Sports Life Survey 2024 (Adults) were analyzed using a two-part Bayesian sparse model: a Bernoulli-logit model for any attendance and a zero-truncated negative binomial model for conditional attendance intensity. Prior predictive checks and sensitivity analyses assessed key modeling decisions. Findings Any attendance showed positive posterior associations with online J.League viewing, televised Nippon Professional Baseball viewing, transportation support, televised J.League viewing and sport-club involvement. Online Nippon Professional Baseball viewing remained positive across specifications, but its main-model 95% credible interval narrowly included zero. Conditional attendance intensity was positively associated with online J.League viewing and preparation support. Sample-averaged predictions indicated a 22.9-percentage-point difference in any-attendance probability and a 2.71-attendance difference in the conditional expected count for online J.League viewing; preparation support showed a 2.79-attendance difference in the conditional expected count. Practical implications Managers should distinguish initiatives aimed at generating p…

title: A Service–Debt–Fiscal Compatibility Framework for Availability-Payment PPPs
abstract: Background: Availability payments can support infrastructure investment where user revenues are uncertain, but a contractual payment commitment does not, by itself, reconcile service incentives, debt repayment, and fiscal affordability. Objective: This study develops a conceptual framework through a structured comparison of publicly documented arrangements in Indonesia’s Palapa Ring Western and Eastern packages, Florida’s I-595 corridor, and New Zealand’s Transmission Gully restructuring. Methods: A purposive documentary comparison, source appraisal, and mechanism coding inform the development of the conceptual model. A contrasting restructuring case examines the limitations of interpreting payment continuity as evidence of unchanged risk transfer. Results: The comparison distinguishes payment entitlement, operational exposure, and financing continuity. The Service–Debt–Fiscal Compatibility Framework (SDFCF) integrates service deductions, debt-service coverage, liquidity, and fiscal limits. An illustrative scenario involving a payment of 100 units, operating outflows of 35 units, and debt service of 50 units permits a deduction of 5 units while maintaining a minimum debt-service coverage ratio (DSCR) of 1.20. A bounded application to the I-595 corridor demonstrates how disclosed payment and reserve terms constrain appraisal, while unreported costs, covenants, and fiscal ceiling…

title: Implementation of a Sharia-Based Waste Bank as a Community Empowerment Model for Managing Economically Valuable Waste
abstract: Waste management requires a community-based approach that addresses environmental cleanliness while increasing the economic value of recyclable materials. This community service activity aimed to implement a Sharia Waste Bank as a community empowerment model for managing economically valuable waste. The program applied a participatory approach through socialization, customer registration, waste sorting and collection, weighing, transaction recording, and community assistance, with students involved as facilitators. The results showed the establishment of a more structured waste management mechanism involving paper, plastic bottles, and glass bottles, supported by weighing and value-recording procedures. Community participation in depositing recyclable materials indicated that the waste bank could function as both an environmental education platform and an economic empowerment instrument. The implementation of the Sharia Waste Bank strengthened community involvement by transforming waste from discarded material into a resource with measurable economic and value.
venue: MOVE: Journal of Community Service and Engagement

title: Transforming Kitchen Waste into Biogas through Community Empowerment in Petamburan
abstract: Dense urban settlements face limited organic-waste treatment capacity, inconsistent household waste sorting, and insufficient skills in operating biogas technology. This community engagement program aimed to strengthen the capacity of residents of Neighborhood Unit 009, Petamburan, Central Jakarta, to convert kitchen waste into energy and organic fertilizer. The program involved community outreach, hands-on training, technology deployment, mentoring and evaluation, and sustainability strengthening. Twenty-three residents participated, and five were appointed as local operators. A 1,400-L digester was installed and initially charged with 200 kg of fresh cow manure as the microbial inoculum, followed by the gradual addition of sorted kitchen waste. The mean waste-sorting knowledge score increased from 72.61 to 100.00, while the biogas-technology score increased from 71.88 to 93.62. Slurry was first collected during the second week, and methane-containing biogas was detected during the fourth week. Integrating appropriate technology, practical training, standard operating procedures, an operational logbook, and resident-led management improved community knowledge and operational readiness.

title: Characteristics of decision-making by a pre-service teacher during teaching placements: insights from structured written reflections
abstract: The study objective was to characterize the decision-making of a pre-service primary teacher as articulated in post-teaching structured written reflections following instruction with students aged 11–12 years. The study adopted the “Teaching in Context” theoretical framework, which allowed for the joint consideration of the pre-service teacher's teaching goals, resources, and orientations across teaching decisions—both those reported as enacted in the classroom and those future-oriented. The data collection instrument was a reflective prompt with questions and suggestions to guide and structure writing reflection on mathematical teaching episodes in authentic classroom settings. Data consisted of three structured written reflections by the pre-service teacher upon completing each self-selected teaching episode. A qualitative and deductive analysis of the three written reflective accounts was conducted. Initially, excerpts related to the dimensions of the theoretical framework were identified. Subsequently, decisions were characterized by distinguishing between reported enacted decisions and future-oriented decisions. Finally, the characteristics of both types of teaching decision-making were compared. The results reveal a common pattern across both types of decision-making: addressing students’ errors and difficulties by utilising everyday situations as a learning resource. Thi…

Discursive Manipulation of National Security and Industrial Competitiveness in U.S. AI Regulation: Domestic Contestation and the Fragmentation of Global AI Governance
abstract: Against the backdrop of generative AI emerging as a core strategic asset for major powers, the rhetorical tropes of national security and industrial competitiveness are subject to strategic manipulation by divergent domestic actors. The deregulatory camp within the White House invokes industrial competitiveness to roll back security-focused executive orders; the security faction in Congress expands chip export controls in the name of national defense; state-level authorities counter federal overreach through consumer protection mandates; and Silicon Valley deploys a two-pronged lobbying strategy. Taking the 2023-2026 policy pendulum and BIS chip regulations as its analytical case, this paper demonstrates that domestic contestation spills over globally through transmission channels. This has produced a global AI governance landscape defined by fragmentation, hollowed-out soft law processes, and a three-bloc divide across the U.S., the EU, and China, while the shortening commitment half-life of U.S. policy positions has inflated the costs of multilateral cooperation. The study also identifies limited positive spillover effects. In response, the paper puts forward targeted strategies. The conclusion argues that U.S. internal regulatory divisions constitute a mechanism that externalizes domestic political costs as global governance uncertainty. Understanding this mechanism is a pre…

Mechanisms and Structural Regulation of Metal–Organic Framework Materials for Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
abstract: Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction can convert CO 2 into high-value chemicals and fuels such as CO, HCOOH, CH 3 OH, and CH 4 by utilizing solar energy, representing an important pathway for carbon resource utilization. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with their tunable metal nodes, organic linkers, and regular pore structures, exhibit unique advantages in CO 2 enrichment, light absorption, charge transport, and stabilization of key intermediates. This review focuses on the mechanisms and structural regulation of MOFs for photocatalytic CO 2 reduction. It first introduces the fundamental processes of photogenerated carrier generation and migration, CO 2 adsorption and activation, proton-coupled electron transfer, and product formation. It then summarizes representative MOF systems based on Zr, Fe, and Ti, as well as the performance characteristics of composites with metal nanoparticles, molecular catalysts, and semiconductors. On this basis, it further analyzes the influence mechanisms of metal-node regulation, linker functionalization, defect engineering, pore-microenvironment modulation, and heterointerface construction on light absorption, charge separation, intermediate adsorption, and product selectivity. Existing studies indicate that the photocatalytic performance of MOFs depends on the synergistic matching of their electronic structure, active sites, and local reaction micro…

title: Ginseng-Douchi ameliorates high-fat diet-induced obesity and metabolic disorders via gut microbiota regulation
abstract: Objective This study evaluated the anti-obesity effects of Ginseng-Douchi (SC), a novel functional food fermented from ginseng and soybean (both medicinal and edible resources) using Bacillus subtilis , and explored its gut microbiota regulatory mechanisms in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice. Methods C57BL/6 mice were fed an HFD to induce obesity and then randomly assigned to normal-control, HFD model, orlistat positive-control, and SC low-, medium-, and high-dose groups. All treatments were administered by gavage for 8 weeks. Body weight, Lee index, serum biochemical indices, and inflammatory cytokines were assessed. Liver, adipose, and colon tissues were harvested for H&E, Oil Red O, and AB-PAS histological staining. For liver and brown adipose tissue, target-gene qPCR, IHC, and protein ELISA were performed. Gut microbiota was profiled by metagenomic sequencing, including taxonomic annotation as well as KEGG and CAZy functional analyses. Results High-dose SC significantly inhibited HFD-induced weight gain (35.74 ± 1.17 g vs. 44.14 ± 1.82 g in HFD), lowered Lee index (345.00 ± 1.19 vs. 375.00 ± 1.86), and reduced visceral fat. Serum TC, TG, and LDL-C were decreased; hepatic steatosis and colonic mucosal barrier damage were alleviated. SC restored UCP1 protein abundance in brown adipose tissue despite reduced Ucp1 transcript levels after intervention, lowered serum TN…

The Neural Basis of Emotion Regulation: A Review of Prefrontal-Limbic Mechanisms and Their Implications for Psychotherapy
abstract: Emotion regulation involves the strategies by which people adjust the strength, time course, or display of emotional responses. This review integrates psychological theory, functional neuroimaging, meta-analytic evidence, and intervention studies to characterize the neurocognitive basis for emotion regulation,which emerges from dynamic interactions among distributed brain networks. Regulation depends on context-sensitive activity in the amygdala, insula, and cingulate cortex during emotion generation, whereas intentional control engages lateral and medial prefrontal regions that maintain goals, interpret events, and shift attention or meaning. Effective regulation therefore relies on information integration rather than the inhibition of one brain region by another. Depression and anxiety involve maladaptive regulation patterns and ineffective prefrontal-limbic interaction, although these alterations are heterogeneous and non-specific to particular diagnoses. Cognitive behavioral therapy, exposure therapy, and mindfulness-based interventions may alter appraisals, salience, self-referential processing, and neural connectivity. However, small samples, heterogeneous tasks, and the correlational nature of functional imaging constrain causal and clinical inference. Future work should adopt integrated, longitudinal, multimodal, and ecologically valid designs to identify individual-lev…

title: Heat stress suppresses keratinocyte inflammation in psoriasis via HSF1-METTL14-mediated m6A regulation of CRYAB
abstract: Abstract Keratinocyte-driven inflammation plays a central role in the pathogenesis of psoriasis. Although hyperthermia therapy has demonstrated clinical benefits, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that local hyperthermia at 41 °C significantly alleviates imiquimod-induced psoriasiform inflammation and suppresses NF-κB signaling. The small heat shock protein CRYAB, which is downregulated in psoriatic lesions and inversely associated with disease severity, is markedly upregulated in response to heat stress. Elevated CRYAB expression inhibits IKKβ-dependent NF-κB activation and mitigates inflammatory responses in psoriatic skin. Heat exposure also enhances the expression of the m 6 A methyltransferase METTL14 in keratinocytes. Mechanistically, heat-activated HSF1 contributes to METTL14 upregulation and exhibits increased enrichment at a predicted HSF1-binding region within the METTL14 promoter. Consistent with previous observations, METTL14 is reduced in psoriatic lesions, and its overexpression suppresses NF-κB–mediated inflammation. Bioinformatic analysis predicts multiple m 6 A sites in CRYAB mRNA, and mechanistic studies confirm that METTL14 facilitates CRYAB m 6 A methylation under heat stress, thereby promoting its expression and anti-inflammatory function. IGF2BP2 further facilitates CRYAB expression as an m6A reader. Together…

title: Stakeholder information pressure and environmental action: the roles of environmental regulation and public monitoring in China
abstract: Introduction A central question in environmental governance is when information transparency is associated with environmental action rather than only symbolic response. This study examines how environmental regulation and public monitoring condition the associations between stakeholder information pressure and two environmental outcomes: green patent applications and observed environmental penalties. Methods Using Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2011 to 2023, we measure stakeholder information pressure (SIP) from media sentiment, stakeholder‐facing disclosure, and employee‐related information, and treat green patent applications and environmental penalties as the primary environmental outcomes, alongside ESG strategic orientation and ESG ratings as intermediate, visibility-oriented responses. Results SIP is positively associated with ESG strategic orientation and ESG ratings. Its associations with green patenting and observed environmental penalties vary across regulatory, media, and ownership conditions. Additional joint-interaction models excluding media sentiment show positive two- and 3‐year patenting associations for the joint reference group and retain positive regulatory and media interactions and negative ownership interactions. Discussion The findings indicate that transparency is more closely associated with environmental action under supportive governance condition…

title: Documented frequency of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome among patients with small cell lung cancer in a large United States health system
abstract: Background Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) is the paraneoplastic syndrome most often associated with small cell lung cancer (SCLC). Four published series in which unselected patients with SCLC were examined neurologically report LEMS in 1.3–3.8%; analyses of claims data report under 0.2%. We measured how often LEMS is documented among patients with SCLC in a large United States health system. Methods In this retrospective cross-sectional study at MedStar Health, a 10-hospital academic health system, patients with SCLC were identified between May 24, 2019 and May 2025 by structured ICD-10 and chemotherapy-based queries (Arm 1A) and, because ICD-10 has no code specific to SCLC, by classifying oncology notes containing “small cell” with a large language model, every positive classification then confirmed against the note text (Arm 1B). Patients with LEMS were identified without date restriction using diagnosis codes, amifampridine orders, and text search, then adjudicated by chart review. Results We identified 436 patients with SCLC (425 by text classification, 11 by structured query only) and 9 meeting a LEMS case definition (2 definite, 2 probable, 5 possible). No patient with SCLC diagnosed during the study period had a documented LEMS diagnosis (0/436; 95% CI 0–0.84%). One further patient with SCLC and possible LEMS was found only by the unrestricted search and died b…

title: Reducing the number of component failures in open pit dump trucks based on adjustments to the frequency of scheduled maintenance
abstract: Currently, dump trucks are the most widely used type of transport vehicle in open-pit mining operations. To maintain to reflect the specific operating conditions of each particular company. However, the use of these regulations often leads to insufficient readiness of the company's maintenance services for potential failures. To address this issue, the authors collected and analyzed statistics on failures of components and assemblies of dump trucks from two open-pit iron ore mining operations for the period of 2020–2023. The analysis revealed that the power unit, suspension, wheels, and frame were the least reliable components. Based on analyzing the strategies employed by the companies to maintain the established level of machine technical availability, we determined the target function for the optimal maintenance interval for the components considered. Upon transforming the target function according to the established laws of failure rate distribution based on the number of failures, we obtained two expressions that allow us to find the optimal maintenance frequency for the components under consideration. When testing these expressions, we compared the expected number of failures per year with the actual number of failures, which showed a significant reduction. The use of the calculated maintenance intervals resulted in a reduction in the number of emergency failures per year…

title: Effects of Extremely Low-Frequency (50/60 Hz) Electromagnetic Field Exposure on Oxidative Stress Biomarkers in Rodent Models: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: Extremely low-frequency electromagnetic fields at the 50/60 Hz mains frequency are ubiquitous and classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer as possibly carcinogenic to humans. Altered redox balance is the most frequently proposed mechanism, yet rodent findings are inconsistent and have not been quantitatively synthesised. Following PRISMA 2020, PubMed and Scopus were searched for controlled studies in rats or mice exposed to 50/60 Hz fields and reporting oxidative stress biomarkers. Risk of bias (SYRCLE) and certainty of evidence (GRADE, adapted for animal studies) were assessed, and Hedges’ g was pooled using random-effects models. Eight rat studies (1–7000 μT) yielded 48 non-independent effect estimates across seven biomarkers. Exposure increased malondialdehyde (SMD 2.84; 95% CI 1.70–3.98), total oxidant status (1.33; 0.50–2.17), total thiol molecules (1.27; 0.25–2.29), and total antioxidant status (1.25; 0.72–1.78), whereas superoxide dismutase and catalase were unchanged. Heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 52–82%), four biomarkers derived from a single laboratory, and certainty was very low throughout. Findings suggest a shift toward oxidative stress, with greater lipid peroxidation and oxidant burden alongside higher non-enzymatic antioxidant capacity; direction is better supported than magnitude. Most exposures exceeded ICNIRP public reference levels,…

title: A cost-aware intermittent demand forecasting method combining temporally attenuated discrete gray model with reward-guided adjustment
abstract: Purpose Intermittent demand in distribution-center operations is difficult to forecast because long zero-demand periods are often interrupted by irregular demand bursts. This study develops TADGM–RGPL, a cost-aware gray forecasting framework that combines a temporally attenuated discrete gray model (TADGM) with reward-guided parameter learning (RGPL), to account for both statistical calibration deviation and the asymmetric inventory consequences of underforecasting and overforecasting. Design/methodology/approach TADGM introduces a bounded recency-sensitive driver directly into the DGM state-transition equation, while RGPL learns a scalar decision-calibration factor from pre-origin inventory-cost feedback. The framework is evaluated on 701 intermittent and lumpy DC-SKU series using 4,206 rolling-origin windows. Conventional intermittent-demand methods, gray models, XGBoost and LightGBM are included as benchmarks. Findings TADGM does not dominate the benchmark methods in point-forecast accuracy. Standard TADGM–RGPL significantly reduces inventory cost relative to the conventional intermittent-demand and gray benchmarks under the stockout-sensitive p/h = 10 setting, whereas XGBoost and LightGBM achieve lower overall cost when all series are pooled. ADI-stratified analysis shows that TADGM–RGPL attains the lowest average cost in the highest-intermittency quartile, although its adv…

title: Evaluating the Transition of System Efficiency between Special Moment Frames and Eccentrically Braced Frames across Building Height and Seismic Demand
abstract: The design efficiency of Special Moment Frames (SMF) and Eccentrically Braced Frames (EBF) was evaluated for various building heights and seismic demand levels in accordance with Indonesian seismic regulations for steel structures. A controlled parametric matrix was established with controlled variables, comprising three-, seven-, and eleven-story office building models. Analyses were conducted for Pontianak and Lampung, representing low and high seismic demand regions, respectively. The seismic force-resisting systems were alternated between SMF and EBF, while the architectural geometry and gravity framing were kept constant. The comparison used the governing maximum inter-story drift and the normalized mass of the seismic resisting steel frames. In all six matched cases, EBF produced lower design-level inter-story drift than SMF, with reductions ranging from 32.36% to 92.58%. However, EBF did not consistently require less steel. Under higher seismic demand, EBF was lighter at all three heights, with mass savings of 25.52%, 40.41%, and 33.03% for the 3-, 7-, and 11-story prototypes, respectively. The results indicate that the principal low-rise benefit of EBF is improved deformation control, whereas the frame-mass advantage is conditional on building height and seismic demand. Because the study is limited to six linear-elastic design cases, it does not establish a universal tr…

title: Response to Letter to the Editor: Higher noise reduction improves diagnostic accuracy of computer-aided detection of pulmonary embolism on CTPA
Children’s environmental self-reports: dimensionality, response-style sensitivity, and cross-national comparability in TIMSS 2023
abstract: Introduction The 2023 cycle of the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) is the first international assessment to ask Grade-4 children (around age 10) directly about their environmental values and self-reported pro-environmental action. We examined the association between values and reported action, and how far that association and cross-national comparisons of means were sensitive to measured proxies for response style. Methods We analyzed data from 58 education systems and 359,098 students, after excluding benchmarking files that duplicate national samples. Measurement models assessed dimensionality and comparability. Within-system associations were pooled across systems, and sensitivity analyses adjusted for acquiescence and extreme responding indexed by unrelated mathematics and science items. Results Stronger environmental values were associated with more self-reported action across all systems ( β = 0.45). Adjustment for response style attenuated the value–action and knowledge–action associations by 9% and 17%, respectively, but left both intact. At the system level, the two proxies accounted for 25% of the between-system variance in mean values (95% bootstrap CI [0.09, 0.47]; leave-one-system-out range 0.22–0.30). Girls reported stronger environmental values than boys (d = 0.20; d = 0.18 in systems with scalar gender invariance). Cross-system metr…

title: ЄВХАРИСТІЙНА АНТРОПОЛОГІЯ ЯК ВІДПОВІДЬ НА ПОСТТОТАЛІТАРНІ ПРАКТИКИ РОЗЛЮДНЕННЯ
abstract: Людина, як соціальна істота, значно залежить від соціально-політичних та культурних течій та практик в суспільстві її існування. ХХ століття сповнене антилюдськими практиками, такими як війни (Перша та Друга світова, криваві колоніальні завоювання, локальні конфлікти), анексії територій, репресії, штучно створений голод, тощо. Зважаючи на це, можна відмітити значний вплив соціально-політичних подій ХХ століття на формування культурно-особистісного профілю громадянина, що змушений був формуватись в системі координат радянського союзу в умовах зламу усталеної економічної моделі розвитку суспільства, практик колективізації, войовничого атеїзм, широко застосовуваних репресії, а також штучно спровокованого голоду (голодомор в Україні, ашаршилик в Казахстані). Метою нашого дослідження став аналіз персонально-орієнтованих релігійно-культурних практик набуття ідентичності в пост-тоталітарному світі кінця ХХ – початку ХХІ століття. Методологія. Нами проведено аналіз трансформації релігійної ідентичності громадян пострадянських суспільств після падіння тоталітарних режимів завдяки використання євхаристійних практик – практик вдячності. Наукова новизна. Нами проведено аналіз змін в суспільстві від заперечення та атеїзму до осмисленого прийняття Бога через пошук істини. В представленій роботі наведено дані, що показують значення соціальної антропології, зокрема євхаристійної антропології, …

title: Belimumab added to multi-target therapy in lupus nephritis: a retrospective cohort study of efficacy, divergent temporal response patterns, and safety
abstract: Background Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe complication of systemic lupus erythematosus. Belimumab, a B-cell-activating factor (BAFF) inhibitor, improves renal outcomes when added to standard therapy, but its efficacy and temporal effects when combined with multi-target therapy regimens containing tacrolimus remain poorly characterized. We compared multi-target therapy plus belimumab with multi-target therapy alone in active LN. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, 28 patients with active LN (14 per group) received multi-target therapy (glucocorticoid, mycophenolate mofetil, and tacrolimus, a calcineurin inhibitor) with (case group) or without (control group) belimumab. The patients were assessed at baseline and 3, 6, and 12 months after treatment initiation. Primary endpoints were 24-hour urinary protein (24hUP), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). C3, C4, anti-dsDNA, SLEDAI-2K, and IgG/IgA/IgM were the secondary endpoints. Comparisons were conducted using Welch’s t or Mann-Whitney U tests (between-group), paired t or Wilcoxon tests (within-group), and Cohen’s d effect sizes. Results Compared to baseline, both groups exhibited significant improvement in proteinuria, SLEDAI-2K, anti-dsDNA, and complement. eGFR remained stable, with no significant between-group differences at any timepoint. Temporal patterns diverged…

Dose-formulation risk gradients of gastrointestinal adverse events with subcutaneous and oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and dose-response network meta-analysis
abstract: Objective To quantify formulation- and dose-dependent risk gradients of gastrointestinal adverse events (GI AEs) with subcutaneous and oral semaglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and assess follow-up duration as a potential moderator, to inform hypothesis-generating clinical considerations. Methods PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Descriptive single-arm random-effects pooling summarized within-dose GI AE proportions without comparative inference; all between-treatment comparisons relied on a frequentist network meta-analysis (NMA) generating odds ratios (ORs), with treatments ranked by the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Meta-regression on follow-up duration was post-hoc and exploratory. The review was not prospectively registered. Results Twenty RCTs enrolling 18–014 participants were included. Pooled single-arm proportions were similar for subcutaneous semaglutide 0.5 mg (0.40, 95% CI 0.33–0.46) and 1.0 mg (0.42, 95% CI 0.37–0.46); follow-up duration was positively associated with logit-transformed 0.5 mg incidence (β = 0.0082 per week, 95% CI 0.0020–0.0143; 58.1% of heterogeneity explained). Pooled single-arm proportions for oral semaglutide were 0.25 (95% CI 0.11–0.46) at 3 mg, 0.42 (95% CI 0.2…

title: HIV-1 clade C-derived SHIV-C109 viral infection and response to antiretroviral drug therapy in humanized mice
abstract: Simian-human immunodeficiency viruses (SHIVs) are commonly used as surrogates in NHP models for HIV-related studies. Most SHIV studies focused on HIV-1 clade B, although clade C is more prevalent, especially in low-resource regions outside of North America. Here we evaluated SHIV-C109 infection dynamics and antiretroviral therapy (ART) in a dual-purpose hu-HSC humanized mouse model permissive for both HIVs and SIVs. SHIV-C109 comprises a SHIVHXBc2 P3.2 backbone with an R5-tropic HIV-1 clade C envelope. Hu-HSC mice from multiple immune cohorts were inoculated with SHIV-C109 and monitored for a prolonged period to determine the persistence of viremia and CD4 + T-cell decline. Our results showed successful infection and sustained viremia for >45 weeks. RNAscope analysis showed disseminated viral infection in lymphoid organs such as the spleen and lymph nodes. CD4 + T-cell depletion was observed during the chronic infection phase. As a prelude to translation to the NHP model, we also assessed the efficacy of antiretroviral therapy on this virus using the hu-HSC mouse model. Antiretroviral drugs bictegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide were administered via diet. Viral suppression was achieved in all treated mice for several weeks. These results support the potential value of the hu-HSC mouse model in preclinical studies on HIV-1 clade C viruses. Importantly, compara…

title: Targeting CD44v3 rescues Entrectinib response in brain metastasis of triple negative breast cancer overexpressing TrkA
Intervention against autodigestion enhances cardiovascular stability and trauma response in the elder
abstract: Abstract An important step to improve the quality of life in older adults is to reduce their heightened sensitivity to trauma challenges, such as elective surgery. Our recent evidence indicates that a mechanism behind aging and reduced quality of life involves the leakage of pancreatic digestive enzymes from the gastrointestinal tract into the bloodstream and peripheral organs. The leaked enzymes degrade plasma proteins, extracellular matrix proteins, and membrane receptors, leading to cell and organ dysfunctions typical for aging. Here, we hypothesize that blockade of leaked digestive enzymes improves the quality of life in the elderly and their response to trauma. A one-week oral treatment of old rats with a pancreatic digestive serine protease (trypsin) inhibitor, without significantly impairing normal digestion, decreases protease activity in the central circulation and benefits older individuals facing trauma. We find that this pretreatment stabilizes the cardiovascular system of aged rats, improves metabolic disturbances caused by hemorrhagic shock, and significantly enhances their response to shock. Systolic and mean arterial blood pressures are normalized, and the baroreflex, which is severely impaired in aged rats, is substantially improved by the pretreatment. The survival rate during central blood pressure reduction is significantly higher in old rats pretreated agai…

title: Evaluation of drought response of two Romanian cultivars of Camelina sativa
abstract: Camelina sativa is being re-evaluated as an oilseed crop for low-input agricultural systems. To assess its adaptation to Romanian conditions, we characterized the water-deficit response of two Romanian cultivars, Mădălina and Camelia, from germination to seed production. Germination under osmotic stress was assessed in the laboratory at 10, 15 and 20% polyethylene glycol (PEG 6000). In the greenhouse, water deficit was imposed from full flowering by lowering soil moisture to 30% and then to 20% of pot water-holding capacity, compared with 80–90% in the controls. Leaf relative water content (RWC), chlorophyll index (SPAD), seed yield per plant, seed oil content and fatty acid composition were measured, and all greenhouse data were analyzed with the pot as the experimental unit. Both cultivars tolerated moderate osmotic stress, with 94–100% germination up to 15% PEG, but showed a clear threshold at 20% PEG, where final germination fell to 22% (Mădălina) and 36% (Camelia), hypocotyl growth was completely inhibited and radicle growth was strongly reduced. From flowering onward, water deficit reduced RWC by 37–43% and SPAD by 28–47% in both cultivars, with no significant genotype × water-regime interaction, and by the third week of stress leaf senescence was visibly more advanced in Camelia. Seed yield per plant decreased by 10–16%, but not significantly, whereas oil content decline…

title: Follicular development dynamics, ovarian response, and reproductive outcomes among three recombinant FSH preparations: a single-center retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background Recombinant follicle-stimulating hormone (rFSH) preparations differ in their glycosylation profiles and pharmacological properties. However, whether these molecular differences influence follicular growth dynamics during controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) remains unclear. We compared follicular development, ovarian response, and reproductive outcomes among follitropin alfa, beta, and delta. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 329 women undergoing their first controlled ovarian stimulation cycle with follitropin alfa ( n = 151), beta ( n = 111), or delta ( n = 67). Primary outcomes were oocyte yield, mature oocyte yield, follicle-to-oocyte index (FOI) and follicle-to-mature oocyte index (FmOI). Secondary outcomes included follicular development, endocrine profiles, embryological outcomes, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, cumulative pregnancy rate, and cumulative live birth rate. Outcomes were compared using multivariable regression analyses or logistic regression analysis adjusted for age, anti-Müllerian hormone, and body weight. Results Follitropin alfa and beta showed broadly comparable ovarian responses and stimulation durations, whereas differences were observed in comparisons involving follitropin delta. Exploratory analyses revealed modest numerical trends toward higher oocyte yield and FOI and shorter stimulation duration with follitro…

title: Gut microbial characteristics associated with pegylated interferon treatment response in chronic hepatitis B: insights into the gut–liver axis
abstract: Background Pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) treatment response varies considerably among patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The role of the gut microbiota in this heterogeneity remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize gut microbial features associated with Peg-IFN response and explore their potential relevance to the gut–liver axis. Methods A total of 64 patients with CHB who completed 24 weeks of Peg-IFN-based therapy were enrolled in this study. Fecal samples collected at week 24 were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Microbial characteristics and clinical factors associated with treatment response were evaluated, followed by development of an integrated classification model. Results Among the 64 patients, 38 were classified as responders and 26 as non-responders. Responders exhibited distinct gut microbial profiles, characterized by increased microbial richness ( p = 0.014), altered community composition ( p = 0.045), and different microbial interaction patterns. Dorea abundance was enriched in responders and independently associated with treatment response. Multivariable logistic regression identified lower baseline HBsAg levels (OR = 0.562, p = 0.048), higher platelet counts (OR = 1.020, p = 0.007), and increased Dorea abundance (OR = 3.876, p = 0.008) as independent factors associated with response. Restricted cubic spline analysis supported a signific…

title: Distinct plasma proteomic trajectories during PD-1 blockade and PEG-IFNα therapy are associated with HBsAg response in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Background PD-1 blockade and pegylated interferon-α (PEG-IFNα) are promising immunomodulatory strategies for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but their systemic immune effects and response-associated proteomic patterns remain poorly defined. Methods We performed longitudinal plasma proteomic profiling using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel in 25 nucleos(t)ide analogue-suppressed patients with CHB receiving PD-1 blockade (n=10) or PEG-IFNα (n=15). Plasma samples were collected at baseline, week 12, and week 24. Longitudinal protein changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and associations with week-24 HBsAg decline were evaluated using responder–non-responder comparisons and Spearman’s rank correlation. Responders were defined by an HBsAg decline of ≥1 log 10 IU/mL at week 24. Results Seventy-seven proteins passed quality-control criteria. PEG-IFNα induced substantially broader longitudinal proteomic remodeling than PD-1 blockade, with most changes occurring within the first 12 weeks. Treatment-by-time analyses identified distinct trajectories between therapies, including differential changes in IL-18R1, TNF, CX3CL1, CXCL9, and CXCL10. Response-associated analyses suggested treatment-specific patterns: IL-10 was the leading exploratory signal in the PD-1 cohort, whereas IL-12B, CDCP1, and FGF-21 were more prominent in the PEG-IFNα cohort. These response-related a…

title: Advancing quality education through academic libraries: an empirical assessment of information literacy and learning outcomes in the higher education system
abstract: Purpose This study examines the relationships among Academic Library Services (ALS), Information Literacy Competence (ILC) and Learning Outcomes and Academic Impact (LOA) among Ph.D. scholars at a selected Indian university. Guided by the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and Sustainable Development Goal 4, the study evaluates the contribution of ALS and information literacy to doctoral learning and research development. Design/methodology/approach A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among 452 Ph.D. scholars from diverse academic disciplines. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, an independent-samples t-test and one-way ANOVA. Findings The findings revealed significant positive relationships between ALS and ILC (r = 0.60, p < 0.001) and between ILC and LOA (r = 0.63, p < 0.001). Multiple regression analysis showed that ALS (ß = 0.26, p < 0.001) and ILC (ß = 0.28, p < 0.001) were significant positive predictors of LOA. The measurement instrument demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α = 0.90). No statistically significant gender difference was identified, whereas perceptions differed significantly across academic disciplines (F = 3.84, p = 0.005). Overall, the findings indicate that ALS and ILC are positively associated with perceived …

title: Theoretical and methodological foundations of proactive operational efficiency management in mining companies
abstract: The study justifies theoretical and methodological foundations of proactive operational efficiency management in mining companies within the Industry 4.0 paradigm. Its relevance is explained by a divergence between the following two processes. The physical volume of the gross value added in the Russian mining industry declined by 1.7% in 2025 with the mining and geological conditions deteriorating measurably, e.g. the stripping ratio at the Polyus Group rose from 1.5 to 2.4 m³/t in a single year, while the coal production cost grew from 2,234 to 3,400 Rubles per tonne. At the same time, the utilization capacity factor of the open-pit excavators remains at 0.45–0.49 against 0.80–0.90 in the record-high months. A hypothesis is made that in the cyber-physical production the measurement costs cease to be an exogenous parameter and become a design variable, which shifts the whole configuration of the in-company control. The objective is to justify a conceptual model combining noninvasive real-time monitoring, dynamic labour rate setting and minimisation of the in-house transaction costs. The methods used include comparative analysis, content analysis of corporate reporting, decomposition of the equipment time fund and theoretical modelling. A four-level closed cybernetic control loop is proposed; control costs are decomposed into measurement, monitoring and enforcement; an observabi…

title: How fashion livestreamers co-create visual culture with Gen-Z audiences on livestream platform
abstract: Purpose As livestreaming becomes an increasingly important mode of digital interaction, fashion shopping streams are reshaping how style is performed and negotiated in real time. This study examines how fashion livestreamers communicate style to Gen Z audiences in Vietnam and how Gen Z viewers influence fashion performances through real-time interaction. Together, these perspectives illuminate how authenticity, identity and stylistic meaning are collaboratively produced during fashion livestreaming. Design/methodology/approach Guided by social performance theory and participatory culture, the study draws on 31 semi-structured interviews with fashion livestreamers and Gen Z viewers in Vietnam. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to examine how streamer performance and audience participation shape fashion livestream interactions. Findings Livestreamers combine curated presentation, improvisational styling and persona-building while continuously adapting to audience comments, emotional reactions and styling suggestions. Gen Z viewers actively influence outfit choices, aesthetic presentation and the direction of the performance. Through this real-time reciprocal negotiation, authenticity, identity and stylistic meaning are jointly constructed. Originality/value The study contributes a qualitative perspective to livestream commerce research by applying social performance theory to …

title: Accidental supply chains: an exploratory study of social enterprise coordination in Australian organics recovery
abstract: Purpose To explain how social enterprises coordinate circular organics recovery in regional settings where formal infrastructure is incomplete and institutional support remains thin. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, abductive multiple-case study of two Australian organics recovery arrangements, drawing on 26 semi-structured interviews, site observations, documentary sources and iterative tracing of material flows and coordination over time. Findings Circular coordination developed through four overlapping phases: initiation, stabilisation, legitimation and institutionalisation. Repeated routines and micro-infrastructure, supported by relationship-based brokerage, made recovery workable amid structural, socio-political and emergent complexity. Supply-chain championing was centralised in SoilCo and decentralised in CoffeeCos, but remained active across the full process. Greater visibility strengthened legitimacy and formalisation while also creating new scrutiny and operating burdens, including competition for previously unwanted material. Research limitations/implications The study prioritises analytical depth in two Australian organics recovery cases. Research across other materials and institutional settings could test the scope and boundary conditions of accidental supply chains. Practical implications Regional circularity requires investment in coordination and rel…

title: Integrated assessment technology for heritage building restoration: a structural equation modelling approach
abstract: Purpose This research develops and validates a comprehensive technology-based assessment system for heritage building restoration that integrates project management triangle factors with adaptive reuse sustainability factors, addressing the critical gap in standardized evaluation frameworks for developing countries. Design/methodology/approach The research design used structural equation modelling-partial least squares, data were collected from 100 construction professionals across seven heritage buildings in Java Island, Indonesia. The model integrates capital investment, asset condition and regulatory factors with scope, time and cost management dimensions through advanced psychometric validation. Findings The data collected from 100 construction professional in Indonesia, and the results reveal capital investment as the dominant factor influencing project management outcomes (β = 0.481–0.567), while regulatory factors show moderate relationships particularly with scope management (β = 0.328). Asset condition exhibits weaker associations, reflecting funding prioritization over technical considerations in developing country contexts. The system explains 29.8–44.5% variance in project management constructs with strong psychometric properties (Construct Realibility (CR) > 0.7, average variance extracted >0.5) and acceptable fit (SRMR = 0.076, Normed Fit Index (NFI) = 0.912…

title: The Factory That was Never Built: Evidence from a Survey Experiment on Compensation in China
abstract: Conventional welfare accounting assigns the same present value to cash flows that occur at the same times, yet third-party compensation assessments may depend on whether the affected activity has already started. This paper randomizes a survey to 600 adults from mainland China. The author asks participants to assess one of two things that are the same in all other respects: a) a factory that stops running after running for one year, and b) a factory that got the approval, fund and site allocation, but was cancelled before the start of construction. In both cases, the facility is expected to generate an annual local net income of CNY 48 million for ten years beginning the following year, and the government considers the same ten-year compensation plan in each case. The result is that people give higher compensation after the start of operations: the average is CNY 74.4 million for the after start of the operations, compared to CNY 58.4 million for the before start of the construction, that is a difference of CNY 16.0 million (which is 33% of the designated income). This difference is small for the low compensation amounts but becomes larger in the upper half of the distribution, where the responses are also more variable. It is slightly smaller at the very top. These results show that the operational status matters for the third-party determinations about the compensation, not o…

title: Surgery during regorafenib therapy in children, adolescents, and young adults with bone sarcomas: perioperative management and feasibility
abstract: Background Regorafenib is an oral multikinase inhibitor with documented activity in relapsed and metastatic bone sarcomas, but data on its perioperative management in children, adolescents, and young adults are scarce. Given its antiangiogenic mechanism and potential impact on wound healing and bleeding risk, defining safe perioperative strategies is essential when surgery is required during ongoing treatment. Methods This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the REGBONE clinical trial at the Institute of Mother and Child included children, adolescents, and young adults with relapsed or metastatic osteosarcoma or Ewing sarcoma who received regorafenib and underwent at least one surgical procedure between April 2022 and December 2025. The parent trial enrolled patients aged 9–21 years. Perioperative management involved temporary regorafenib interruption and individualized postoperative resumption guided by predefined wound‐healing criteria. The data cutoff was January 30, 2026. Results Fourteen patients underwent 18 surgical procedures across 14 regorafenib interruption episodes. The median age at surgery was 16.2 years [IQR 12.8-18.0]; most had osteosarcoma (93%). Thoracic procedures accounted for 67% of surgeries. The median from the last regorafenib dose to the first procedure was 17 days [IQR 11-22]. Regorafenib was resumed after 12 of 14 interruption …

title: Who Needs Blockhouses? The Final Stage in the Construction of the CER System of Permanent Fortifications amid the Collapse of the Russian Empire, 1916–1917
abstract: Despite a number of recent publications, the history of defensive construction on the Chinese Eastern Railway (CER) continues to be one of the least studied aspects of the railway’s history. The article is devoted to the final stage in the construction of blockhouses designed to protect the most technically complex engineering structures along the railway. Its purpose is to examine the difficulties in coordinating the transfer of responsibility for an almost completed system of permanent defensive structures on the CER to the Transamur District of the Separate Border Guard Corps (TD SBGC) and the Inspector of the Engineering Department of the Irkutsk Military District. This process began in 1916 and ended in the first half of 1917, amid the collapse of the Russian Empire. The article presents the dynamics of the blockhouse construction process during the final stage of the work, based on documents from the RSMHA that are used in scholarly research for the first time. Based on an analysis of documents from the Main Military Technical Directorate, the Main Directorate of the General Staff, the Headquarters, and the Engineering Department of the Irkutsk Military District, the article reconstructs the decision-making process concerning the transfer of these structures. The difficulties in coordinating these issues are examined in the context of the confusion and administrative burd…

title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

title: Does Economic Momentum Exist in VALORANT? A Discrete-Time Markov Chain Analysis with Logistic Regression and Random Forest Validation
abstract: Does winning beget more winning in VALORANT? This paper examines whether teams that pull ahead financially keep pulling ahead, or whether the game's economy naturally evens things out. A four-state Markov chain is fitted to transitions between economic regimes across 214 professional matches (5,136 rounds) from the 2023–2024 VCT season. Logistic regression and a random forest model are also used to test whether the patterns hold up across different modeling approaches. The results are hard to ignore: winners stay in full-buy 78% of the time, while losers remain there only 31%. Each extra 1,000 credits of advantage raises the odds of winning by about one-third (OR = 1.34, p < 0.001). Adding regime labels increases AUC from 0.68 to 0.72, representing a 5.9% gain. Overall, the findings suggest that money begets money in VALORANT and that the in-game economy has memory. Economic regimes provide useful information beyond static credit numbers alone and help explain how financial momentum develops across rounds.

title: The Impact of Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones on Urban Carbon Emission Intensity: Evidence from a Difference-in-Differences Approach
abstract: Cities must cut carbon emissions per unit of output to meet the dual carbon goals, and green finance is expected to help. We study China's Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones, launched in 2017, using a panel of 287 prefecture-level cities over 2013-2022. A difference-in-differences design with two-way fixed effects shows that treated cities lowered carbon emission intensity by about 12% relative to untreated ones, with larger reductions in later years. Two mechanisms drive this outcome: credit expands and becomes more available to low-carbon projects, and industry upgrades toward greener production instead of contracting. The effect appears almost exclusively where local financial systems are relatively developed. These results offer city-level causal evidence on green finance and argue for tailoring future reform to local financial conditions.
