title: Express diagnostics of power transmission systems of mine excavators
abstract: In conditions of intensified mining operations, the EKG-20K open-pit excavators in Uzbekistan and Russia demonstrate high levels of unscheduled downtime for their pressure and lift drives, accounting for 36–44% of the total equipment downtime. Traditional preventive and predictive maintenance methods fail to provide the required level of availability. This paper proposes a Conscientious Maintenance and Repair concept that integrates an adapted Fine-Kinney method with express field diagnostics of oil and an algorithm for a comprehensive assessment of the technical condition. The integrated algorithm automates the Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC) and the Equipment Health Index (EHI). A key indicator of the technical condition is the content of iron, zinc, and phosphorus in the oil, which enables prediction of failures with a high degree of probability. The system includes a five-stage analysis procedure, a unified DTС system, and a risk assessment matrix in accordance with GOST. Implementation of the Conscientious Maintenance and Repair System ensures an increase in the fleet availability up to 0.9 and a reduction in unscheduled downtime by 20–30% without increasing costs, as well as a 19.7% increase in the service life of the lift and thrust gearboxes

title: When AI takes control, who takes responsibility? Structural analysis of agentic AI risks in supply chains
abstract: Purpose Agentic AI systems execute procurement decisions, reroute shipments and renegotiate supplier contracts at speeds that preclude real-time human review. The existing literature offers limited analytical attention to the risks that arise when decision authority is delegated to agents. This paper develops a risk taxonomy for agentic AI in supply chains and traces the hierarchical dependencies and influence magnitudes among the identified risks. Design/methodology/approach A systematic review of literature, analyzed through theories–characteristics–contexts–methods framework, produces the risk taxonomy. A hybrid modified total interpretive structural modeling and fuzzy decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory methodology is then applied to structured expert judgments to establish the causal hierarchy and quantify inter-risk influence. Findings Three risks, namely workforce skill gap, data quality and reliability and ethical misalignment occupy the deepest level of the causal hierarchy. Lack of accountability and governance and data privacy emerge as terminal outcomes. All three analytical methods converge on a conclusion: agentic AI risks originate at the institutional layer, with technical risks acting as transmission mechanisms. Practical implications The findings indicate that effective governance requires that workforce capability, data integrity and objective-fun…

title: Retraction notice: Mapping user query behavior patterns for learning and investigation exploratory tasks: a cognitive complexity perspective
Visual Filters and Digital Subjectivity on Chinese Social Media: Platform Power, Beauty Labour, and Identity Negotiation
abstract: In the digital presentation of the self, visual filters can have a huge impact in Chinese social media on identity construction and expression, emotional expression, and social expectation negotiation. In this research, we will look at the double effect of the visual filters on Douyin and Xiaohongshu (Rednote) and how they (re)produce aesthetic standards and offer possibilities for individual agency. Taking on the qualitative case study approach, the three types of filtering - beautification filters connected to the "bai-you-shou" aesthetic, crying filters for an expression of emotions, and cartoon distortion filters for concealment of identity - are examined based on the theory of disciplinary power and technologies of the self and the theory of emotional capitalism and the theory of everyday tactics. The analysis shows that beautification filters are suitable for the function of self-surveillance and beautification work in the online space, and the emotional filters have an influence on the presentation and perception of emotion in an online space. Filters for concealment, on the other hand, offer other ways to work on issues of visibility and negotiate privacy. These practices show visual filters to not only be about platform control, but also not solely about personal empowerment. Rather, they must be comprehended within the dynamic between platform architecture and cultura…

title: User dynamic capabilities and entrepreneurial mode preference: a mixed-methods study from an effectuation perspective
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how users' dynamic capabilities are associated with their preference between independent and collaborative entrepreneurship in online innovation communities, drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and effectuation theory. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a mixed-methods approach combining structural equation modeling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to analyze questionnaire data from 215 users of open-source and brand-oriented innovation communities. Findings Resource-integration capabilities are the key factor distinguishing preferences for different entrepreneurial modes: they exhibit a significantly positive association with independent entrepreneurship preference while exhibiting a significantly negative association with collaborative entrepreneurship preference. Opportunity-sensing, network-building and agile-learning capabilities, as general foundational and higher-order meta-capabilities, are jointly positively associated with both types of entrepreneurial modes. fsQCA further identifies multiple equivalent configurations: the combination of low resource-integration capabilities and high social capital is associated with a preference for collaborative entrepreneurship, whereas the combination of internal capability completeness and strong entrepreneurial intention is associated with a preference f…

VLA-SSM: a visual learning analytics system for monitoring soft skills development through academic performance, STEM project participation, and stakeholder assessment
abstract: A comprehensive assessment of students’ soft skills alongside their academic achievement is an important task in higher education. The purpose of this study was to develop the Visual Learning Analytics System for Soft Skills Monitoring (VLA-SSM), which integrates academic performance, STEM project outcomes, and self-/peer-assessment data, and to examine the statistical relationships among these indicators in monitoring students’ soft skills. The study employed a quantitative research design and involved 122 first-year students enrolled in a Physics program. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and simple linear regression analysis were used to analyze the data. The results showed that Project Grade was a statistically significant predictor of the Soft Skills Indicator ( β = 0.759, p < 0.001), with the regression model explaining 57.6% of the variance in the Soft Skills Indicator (R² = 0.576). VLA-SSM provides an integrated digital environment for collecting, processing, monitoring, and visualizing students’ academic performance, STEM project outcomes, and soft-skills-related assessment indicators. The system may support data-informed pedagogical decision-making and the planning of individual learning trajectories; however, the statistical findings should be interpreted as evidence of relationships among the integrated learning indicators rather than as direc…

title: Child Neurology: Neonatal Management of Tyrosine Hydroxylase Deficiency
Weighted technical and scale efficiency of Greek public general hospitals grouped by bed capacity: a DEA analysis (2019–2023)
abstract: Purpose This study examines the weighted technical efficiency and scale efficiency of Greek public general hospitals within the National Health System during the period 2019–2023, grouping hospitals by capacity size (small ≤ 200 beds, medium 201–400 beds, large ≥ 401 beds). The analysis investigates efficiency differentials across hospital size categories and the evolution of operational performance before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in a context of sustained fiscal pressure on public health systems. Design/methodology/approach Efficiency is assessed using Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA), applying Constant Returns to Scale (CRS) and Variable Returns to Scale (VRS) models. Indicators of technical efficiency, pure technical efficiency and scale efficiency (SE = CRS/VRS) are estimated using the MaxDEA Lite software. Weighted annual efficiency scores are calculated by hospital size group, enabling consistent intertemporal comparisons and a clearer interpretation of structural performance differences across hospital categories. Findings The results reveal variations in technical and scale efficiency across hospital size groups and differences in operational performance during the study period. Overall, efficiency shows a gradual post-pandemic improvement, indicating enhanced managerial adaptability and more effective resource utilisation, although structural differences between …

title: Sustainable off-grid cage culture: assessing the performance of a functional, energy-autonomous, solar-powered farming model for Etroplus suratensis (Bloch, 1790) in remote mangrove habitats
Power and the Cost of Faith: A Case Study of Religion Communication and Commercialisation in the Digital Age
abstract: Religious activities in China today are being changed by the digital era. Electronic wooden fish apps, Buddhist amulets and symbolic accessories are now popular among young people, but they often reduce the profound religious traditions to mere consumer goods and performative symbols. How modern society is changing people's conception of, application for and dissemination of religious ideas. Based on the two contrasting case studies, this paper will examine the mechanisms of religious distortion and countermeasures. Firstly, the religious merit and morality have been reduced to commodities and have lost their original ethical connotations. The second case is that temples, museums and other knowledge-based media can promote religious literacy through ethical content. According to the study, the cost of faith in modern society is not due to religion itself but rather to how it is expressed and consumed. Call for institutional accountability, platform regulation and educational innovation to promote critical religious literacy and preserve the deep cultural and ethical values of religion.

title: A hybrid framework with quantum-inspired feature selection and hyperparameter optimization for rice price forecasting
abstract: Introduction Rice price volatility in India is driven by temporal dependence, climatic variability and supply-side uncertainties, creating continuous challenges for farmers, traders and policymakers. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework for rice price prediction that combines quantum-inspired feature selection and hyperparameter optimization with time-series decomposition. Methods A unified dataset was constructed by integrating daily rice market prices (2001-2023) with climatic variables, agricultural supply metrics and spatial information from 23 Indian states and 602 districts. Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) split the price series into trend, seasonal and residual components to capture the structure of price variations. An eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model forecast the trend, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network modeled the seasonal-residual components. A Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA) performed feature selection, and Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO) tuned hyperparameters (Hybrid QGA-QPSO). Forecast accuracy was assessed with the Diebold-Mariano (DM) test, residual diagnostics and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results QGA reduced the original 47 variables to 11 optimal predictors, and QPSO ensured stable hyperparameter convergence. The Hybrid QGA-QPSO model achieved RMSEs of 164.57, 242.59 and 294.07 Rs./qtl, wi…

title: The Impact of Hainan Free Trade Port Tax Policies on the Finances and Stock Price of Strait Holdings
abstract: Since the Chinese government constructively released the "Overall Plan for the Construction of Hainan Free Trade Port" in 2020, Hainan's tax policies have officially taken effect for registered and substantially operating incentivized enterprises. According to the implementation and promotion of relevant policies, this article aims to explore the short-term and long-term effects of the pre-closure trial tax policies and the series of post-closure policies of the Hainan Free Trade Port on the financial performance and stock prices of incentivized enterprises. This paper takes Strait Holdings as an example, using the event study method, combined with the company's financial statements, to analyze the multiple impacts of this tax policy on the financial and stock prices of Strait Holdings. The research results indicate that the tax policy of the Hainan Free Trade Port has an overall positive impact on the long-term financial performance of companies. Further research has found that under the continuous promotion of long-term policies and the ongoing development of the company, tax policies will continue to have a favorable impact on the company's finances, whereas in the short term, this financial indicator, particularly the stock price, does not show a significant increase.

title: Price Elasticity and Strategic Pricing in Music-Streaming Platforms
abstract: In the digital age, digital platforms have gradually replaced traditional consumption patterns and become an essential part of daily consumption. The emergence of new consumption has reshaped the way consumers access services and altered the factors influencing consumption decisions. This change is particularly apparent in streaming or cultural consumption, with strong personalized features. This study investigates consumer demand for Spotify, Apple Music, Tencent Music, and NetEase Cloud Music, focusing on the impact of subscription price, differences among various consumer groups, and strategic competition between platforms. Using quarterly panel data from 2021 to 2025, this paper employs a log-log regression model to estimate price elasticity. The result show the estimated values, -0.062 (Apple Music), +0.051 (Spotify), -0.125 (Tencent Music), and +2.002 (NetEase Cloud Music). Only Tencent Music's result is statistically significant at the 5% level. Interactions effects within user groups further show that the 2020-21 user groups of Apple Music (-0.145) and Tencent Music (-0.190) are the most price-sensitive. When cohort price elasticities are incorporated into a constrained constant-elasticity revenue model, all four platforms price reach the upper testing price limit. A Bertrand-style competition model then produces constrained equilibrium prices of $13.19 (Spotify and App…

title: Climate-adaptive aquaponics in Tunisia: a multi-regional performance combining assessment solar-thermal experiments and predictive forecasting
SSLR-AE Net: Tasmanian Devil Optimized Deep Learning Architecture for Ultra-Short-Term Solar Irradiance Forecasting
abstract: Stable grid operation and the effective integration of renewable energy supplies depend heavily on accurate short-term solar irradiance predictions. However, accurate prediction is difficult due to the extremely nonlinear behavior of solar irradiance and the inherent unpredictability of climatic variables. This research proposes a more efficient regression-based forecasting approach by employing the integration of Tasmanian Devil Optimization (TDO) for adaptive hyperparameter tuning as well as a State-Space Latent Retention Autoencoder (SSLR-AE) network to address the aforementioned issues. The enhanced framework has been developed to perform better than the baseline SSLR-AE model as well as conventional Deep Neural Networks (DNN) in terms of a range of performance metrics, including R2, MSE, RMSE, MAE, and MAPE, respectively. The results demonstrate a substantial reduction in error rates as well as improved convergence stability. Overall, it can be observed that the proposed approach provides a reliable and accurate solution for short-term solar irradiance forecasting, and it can be used in sophisticated smart energy management.

title: Analysis of Price Dynamics, Production, and Foreign Trade of Avocado in Türkiye
ESG Rating Disagreement and Stock Price Crash Risk: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
abstract: Environmental, social and governance (ESG) ratings issued by different agencies frequently point in opposite directions, yet it remains unsettled whether such disagreement helps market participants or confuses them. Drawing on a panel of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2018 to 2024, we measure rating disagreement as the dispersion among three domestic raters—Huazheng, Wind, and SynTao Green Finance—and relate it to subsequent crash risk. Pooled two-way fixed effects estimates yield no significant average relation, indicating that the noise channel and the information channel embedded in disagreement counterbalance each other. Tests based on stock price synchronicity do not detect an information channel at the aggregate level. Splitting the sample by analyst forecast dispersion, however, uncovers a sharp boundary condition: disagreement is followed by significantly lower crash risk only among firms whose information environment is relatively transparent, and the contrast between groups is significant at the 5% level. Disagreement therefore behaves as information where investors are able to verify it and as noise where they are not. Implications for rating-market regulation, disclosure policy, and rating users are discussed.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Price Dynamics and Volatility of Virtual Items in Online Games: Evidence from CS:GO Weapon Balance Updates and Case Releases
abstract: Virtual-item prices can react to game updates, but these responses are difficult to separate from trends already under way. Based on Buff.163 daily minimum listing price data from July 2021 to January 2024, this paper examines five CS:GO events—two weapon balance adjustments (M4A1-S magazine capacity reduction, combined AWP and M4A1-S nerf) and three weapon case releases (Dreams & Nightmares, Recoil, Revolution)—using event study methodology, a two-way fixed-effects DID model, and volatility analysis. The results show that treatment-group skins exhibit a significant pre-trend reversal before and after the updates; their outperformance relative to the AK-47 control group disappears immediately and turns sharply negative post-update. M4A4 skin prices exhibit a positive abnormal performance as a substitute weapon. All three cases show negative price dynamics relative to the benchmark over their observable periods. The study demonstrates that virtual asset pricing is highly sensitive to game balance decisions, while also revealing that pre-trends and data gaps impose serious constraints on causal inference.

Tracking a solar energetic eruption and associated energetic particles from the Sun to spacecraft
abstract: Solar energetic particles (SEPs) in the heliosphere are produced by flaring processes on the Sun or shocks driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs). Electrons in particular are regularly detected remotely as electromagnetic radiation (X-rays or radio emission) --- which they generate through various processes --- as well as in situ by spacecraft monitoring the Sun and the heliosphere. We aim to combine remote-sensing and in situ observations of an energetic solar eruption to link energetic processes in the solar corona to energetic particles observed in situ in the heliosphere. This will be done using the tools developed in the Horizon Europe SOLER project. We investigated a solar energetic eruption at the Sun together with its associated signatures of accelerated electrons observed at radio and X-ray wavelengths and combined these remote observations to in situ particles observed by spacecraft on 10 March 2024. These observations were combined with a magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) model of the solar corona in order to make the remote to in situ connections. We observe a high-energy SEP event at multiple spacecraft (>25 MeV protons and 1 MeV electrons), despite the event being associated with a slow white-light CME. Remote observations of the Sun show that the event was associated with a fast, large-scale coronal wave (1400 km/s) and multiple regions where electrons are accelerated …

title: The use of high-resolution ct (HRCT) of the temporal bone for accurate preoperative prediction of stapes prosthesis length in patients with otosclerosis
abstract: Abstract Introduction Otosclerosis is managed surgically by stapedotomy or stapedectomy with the insertion of a stapes prosthesis. An ideal prosthesis length and accurate placement are crucial for good surgical and hearing outcomes. Methods This retrospective review was conducted on 179 ears diagnosed with otosclerosis that underwent stapes surgery at our institution between January 2014 and March 2023. Preoperative high–resolution computed tomography (HRCT) imaging of the temporal bone was used to measure the distance between the long process of the incus and the stapes footplate. The measurements were independently obtained by two otolaryngologists (observers 1 and 2) and a radiologist (observer 3). The actual measured and rounded values were analyzed and compared along with the inter-observer agreement for prosthesis length and accuracy predictability. Results The mean radiological distance measured from preoperative HRCT imaging was 4.25 mm (range = 4.1 to 4.4 mm). The interobserver agreement was moderately reliable between observer 1 and 2 (ICC 0.57; 95% CI: 0.43, 0.68); between observer 2 and 3 (ICC 0.58; 95% CI: 0.43, 0.68); between observer 3 and the actual length of prosthesis used (ICC 0.50; 95% CI: 0.32, 0.62). title: CardioTwin-AI: development and internal validation of a digital twin-based adaptive risk-aware learning framework for heart disease prediction
abstract: Heart disease is one of the most common causes of death in the world and early identification of individuals at elevated cardiovascular risk requires reliable risk-assessment methods that can support clinical decision-making. Many conventional machine-learning models focus primarily on disease classification or risk prediction and do not explicitly provide patient-specific virtual representations. This study introduces CardioTwin-AI, a Digital Twin-based Adaptive Risk-Aware Learning Framework (ARLF) to predict the presence or absence of heart disease. We propose a data-driven, patient-specific Digital Twin representation based on clinical attributes, in which the patient state is mapped to a corresponding virtual state and evaluated using state-level synchronization measures, including Twin Simulation Error (TSE) and Twin Fidelity Score (TFS) to quantify representation consistency. The deep feature representations are generated by feature engineering process based on autoencoder, and then analysed by the ARLF prediction model to estimate the probability of the presence of heart disease. It achieved high patient-state representation consistency between the source clinical state and its virtual representation, with a Twin Fidelity Score of 99.76% and a Twin Simulation Error of 0.002402. The proposed ARLF model achieved accuracy of 90.21%, precision of 90.32%, recall of 94.11%, F1…

title: Surrogate Machine Learning Models for ADME Prediction: From Synthetic Labels to Experimental Data
abstract: Abstract Optimization of absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties is central to small-molecule drug discovery, yet is often constrained by limited access to large and consistent experimental data sets. The performance and generalizability of machine learning (ML) models for ADME property prediction rely on the composition of the training data. Surrogate data sets comprise compounds annotated with synthetic ADME labels (predictions) generated by ML models trained on experimental data. This can offer a consistent data augmentation or sharing strategy without requiring access to proprietary data sets; ML models trained on these data can be referred to as surrogate models. However, systematic strategies for developing, evaluating, and applying surrogate models remain underexplored, particularly in the context of transfer learning and validation on new experimental data. In this work, surrogate modeling strategies were investigated for ADME prediction using a data set of over 270,000 compounds with synthetic labels across 25 endpoints. ML models were built on such surrogate data set and evaluated on prospective in-house and public experimental ADME data. Surrogate models based on multitask graph neural networks were predictive under prospective in-house validation and across multiple properties on external data. Uncertainty estimates were informative and…

title: Hybrid Metaheuristic–AI Modeling for Accurate Prediction of CO₂ Solubility in Amine–Ionic Liquid Hybrid Solvents
abstract: Reducing CO₂ emissions from fossil-fuel-based processes requires accurate and reliable predictive tools for designing advanced solvent systems for post-combustion carbon capture. In this study, an extensive experimental database of CO₂ solubility in hybrid amine–ionic liquid (IL) solvents was compiled and modeled using four hybrid metaheuristic–machine-learning frameworks: Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting combined with the Multi-Verse Optimization Algorithm (HistGBoost-MVOA), Tabular Neural Network combined with the Moth-Flame Optimization Algorithm (TabNet-MFOA), Support Vector Regression combined with the Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (SVR-IWOA), and Extreme Learning Machine combined with the Jellyfish Optimization Algorithm (ELM-JFOA). The input variables included temperature, amine concentration, IL concentration, molecular weights of the amine and IL, and CO₂ partial pressure, while the CO₂ mole fraction in the liquid phase (xCO₂) was considered the target variable. To ensure robust model development, outlier detection was performed using the Isolation Forest algorithm, followed by Robust Scaling for data normalization. Model performance was evaluated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation and independent testing based on R², RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and PBIAS, together with Taylor diagrams, centered RMSE (cRMSE), SHAP-based interpretability analysis, and bootstrap uncer…

title: Development and Validation of a LASSO-Based Prediction Model for Postoperative Bleeding Following Pediatric Tonsillectomy and Adenoidectomy
abstract: AIM: Despite technological advancements, children undergoing adenotonsillectomy using low-temperature plasma radiofrequency ablation remain at risk for postoperative bleeding. This study aimed to construct a precise machine learning-based model to predict the risk of postoperative bleeding in this population. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study involving 306 pediatric patients who underwent the procedure between January 2023 and January 2025 was conducted. Clinical data, including demographic characteristics, preoperative laboratory findings, and surgical details, were collected and cleaned. The dataset was randomly divided into a training set (n = 244) and a validation set (n = 62) at an 8:2 ratio. A predictive model was developed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) cross-validation algorithm, and its performance was assessed in the validation cohort. RESULTS: Among 306 children, 24 (7.8%) experienced postoperative bleeding. Univariate comparisons identified significant differences in 11 variables: age, height, weight, body mass index (BMI), disease duration, postoperative infection, dietary compliance, postoperative pain, lymphocyte count, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR) (all p < 0.05). title: Prediction of the self-association of the nuclear inhibitor of DNA-binding and differentiation proteins
abstract: Abstract The inhibitor of DNA binding and differentiation (ID) proteins (ID1–ID4) are members of the helix-loop-helix (HLH) family of transcriptional regulators that play a critical role in regulating cell cycle progression and cell differentiation. Their overexpression in various cancer types makes them promising therapeutic targets. It has been reported that ID4 acts as a tumor suppressor, as ID4 heterodimerizes with ID-1, -2, and -3 and promotes bHLH DNA binding, essentially acting as an inhibitor of inhibitors of differentiation proteins. In this work, we utilize advanced computational biophysics and bioinformatics tools to map the structural foundations of ID protein self-association. High-resolution models were generated and subjected to 100 ns Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations to capture their conformational dynamics in physiological environments. Through protein–protein docking (HADDOCK) and interface analysis, aiming to characterize the binding hotspots of both homodimers and heterodimers, facilitating the development of inhibitors that can disrupt its pathological interactions. Results revealed that ID1 can self-dimerize and form a stable dimer with ID4. The dimerization is exerted by the HLH domain, and the dimers are stable compared to the monomeric isoforms. Cross-Game Generalization and Context Dependence of Cybersickness Prediction Using Consumer-Grade HMD Motion Data
abstract: Cybersickness remains a persistent barrier to sustained virtual reality (VR) use. Consumer-grade head-mounted displays (HMDs) provide motion data that can support symptom prediction, but most prior models have been evaluated within a single game or data environment, leaving cross-game generalization uncertain. This study reanalyzes HMD motion trajectories and Simulator Sickness Questionnaire (SSQ) responses from 60 complete participants across four commercial VR games in the publicly available Questset dataset. Fifteen session-level motion features were extracted, symptom change was represented as ΔSSQ, and Ridge Regression and Random Forest were evaluated under within-game and cross-game conditions. Cross-game error increased most clearly when Beat Saber was the target game under both models, whereas other transfer directions showed smaller penalties. Several feature–symptom correlation directions also changed across games, although none of the 60 exploratory correlations remained significant after False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction. These results suggest that HMD-based cybersickness prediction may be context-dependent and should not be assumed to transfer automatically to unseen VR content; larger within-subject, multi-game studies are needed to confirm this pattern.

Serum guanylate-binding protein 5 as a novel biomarker for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model in a multicenter retrospective case-control study
abstract: Background Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) affects 8–70% of critically ill sepsis patients and is associated with higher mortality, prolonged ICU stay and long-term cognitive decline. Its early diagnosis is difficult because no specific biomarker is available and bedside assessment is often confounded by sedation. Guanylate-binding protein 5 (GBP5) is an interferon- γ –inducible GTPase that promotes NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and has been implicated in sepsis-associated organ injury, but its clinical value in SAE is unknown. Methods In this multicenter, retrospective case-control study, adults (18–80 years) meeting Sepsis-3.0 criteria were enrolled at three tertiary hospitals between October 2024 and October 2025 and classified as SAE ( n = 145; GCS <15 not attributable to other causes) or non-SAE ( n = 186; GCS=15). Admission serum GBP5 and other laboratory biomarkers, including NSE, S100 β , IL-6, TNF-α, IL-10, CRP, and PCT, were measured. The cohort was randomly split into a training dataset ( n = 232) and internal validation dataset ( n = 99). Univariate comparison, multivariable logistic regression, ROC analysis and a nomogram were performed; performance was assessed by C-index, bootstrap-calibrated curves (1000 iterations) and decision curve analysis (DCA). title: Deriving a Multi-Objective Function for Load Balancing in Cloud Environment Via Adaptive Bayesian Belief Network with Ridge Regression-based Load Prediction
abstract: Cloud infrastructures require intelligent workload distribution mechanisms to maintain optimal throughput, control power consumption, and ensure efficient resource utilization. Traditional load balancing approaches fail to address several persistent issues - including workload unpredictability, delayed response cycles, server overutilization, and suboptimal task scheduling. This study proposes an Adaptive Bayesian Belief Network-Ridge Regression framework, termed MRA-SAO-ABBNRR, which employs a Modified Random Attribute Snow Ablation Optimizer. The proposed model integrates Bayesian Belief Networks with Ridge Regression to forecast future workload patterns from historical cloud telemetry. Overfitting is mitigated through correlation analysis across input attributes. Additionally, a modified random attribute snow ablation optimization scheme is used to fine-tune workload prediction and to support a multi-objective task allocation strategy spanning resource utilization, response time, makespan, scalability, and energy efficiency. All experiments were conducted in MATLAB 2020a, and benchmark comparisons were drawn against four existing models, namely Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory, Variable Model Matching Intelligent Self-Distillation, Ensemble Prediction and Risk Uncertainty Assessment, and Bayesian Belief Networks-Ridge Regression. The proposed framework del…

title: Machine Learning Improves Prediction of Emerging Inorganic Contaminant Adsorption Removal Compared With Simple and Multiple Linear Regression
abstract: Accurate prediction of emerging inorganic contaminant adsorption is important for accelerating the screening of adsorbent materials for water and wastewater treatment. This study directly compared simple linear regression (SLR), multiple linear regression (MLR), random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) using the same adsorption dataset and common evaluation metrics. The final dataset comprised (n=302) observations, partitioned into training (75%), validation (15%), and test (15%) subsets after data cleaning and normalization. SLR and MLR showed poor predictive performance (R² = −0.08 and −0.30, respectively), whereas the nonlinear ensemble models substantially reduced prediction error. On the test subset, random forest achieved R² = 0.51, MAE = 2.44, and RMSE = 3.10, while XGBoost achieved R² = 0.78, MAE = 2.07, and RMSE = 3.90. Thus, XGBoost provided the highest explained variance and the lowest mean absolute error, whereas random forest produced the lowest test RMSE. Feature-importance analysis identified nitrogen content and pore volume as the most influential predictors, followed by oxygen content, hydrogen content, ash content, carbon content, specific surface area, and pH. The results demonstrate that nonlinear tree-based models provide a more informative predictive framework than conventional linear regression for this dataset, although external validation …

title: Risk prediction models for the risk of portal vein thrombosis in patients with liver cirrhosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Portal vein thrombosis (PVT) is a common complications of liver cirrhosis. Its occurrence increases the difficulty of clinical management for patients with liver cirrhosis, accelerates disease progression, and raises mortality. Therefore, early prevention, diagnosis and identification of patients with PVT are of vital importance. This study used a meta-analysis to evaluate risk prediction models for PVT in liver cirrhosis, aiming to provide a scientific basis for future model development and clinical application. Methods We searched databases including PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for relevant literature published from database inception to July 2026. Two researchers conducted the literature screening and data extraction, and used the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) to evaluate the risk of bias in the prediction models. Meta-analysis was performed using Stata 14.0. Results A total of 11 studies were included, involving 8670 participants and 15 prediction models were involved. Two of these prediction models underwent external validation. The PROBAST assessment indicated that all studies were at a relatively high risk of bias, although the prediction models showed good applicability. The area under the curve (AUC) values of these prediction models ranged from 0.608 to 0.919.The pooled AUC of the 15 prediction models was 0.81 (95% confidenc…

title: Indoor Air Quality Prediction Using Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: To investigate variations in indoor NO₂ concentrations under a subtropical climate, their relationships with indoor and outdoor environment parameters, and ways to improve prediction accuracy, this study monitored indoor and outdoor air quality in a teaching building from May 18 to May 31, 2025. Measurements included NO₂, PM2.5, PM10, O₃, temperature, and relative humidity. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated, and variables with |r| ≥ 0.3 were selected as model inputs. Multiple linear regression (MLR) and artificial neural network (ANN) models were developed and evaluated using R² and RMSE. Based on validation results, the preferred ANN used two hidden layers, with 150 and 75 neurons, and ReLU activation. On the test set, MLR achieved an R² of 0.5975 and an RMSE of 4.8597, whereas ANN achieved an R² of 0.8528 and an RMSE of 2.9389. Compared with MLR, ANN increased R² by approximately 25.53 percentage points and reduced RMSE by approximately 39.52%. ANN also reduced the underestimation observed at high concentrations and improved accuracy across concentration ranges. These findings show that indoor NO₂ depends on multiple indoor and outdoor factors and that ANN captures their complex relationships more effectively than MLR. The results support ANN-based indoor NO₂ prediction under subtropical conditions and may inform air-quality monitoring and forecasting in simila…

title: Artificial Intelligence for Tennis Performance Analysis and Match Prediction
abstract: Tennis players' technical movements, movements, spatial behavior, and other aspects during matches can already be well analyzed by artificial intelligence, but the data and game predictions obtained from these analyses still need to be integrate. This is the research direction of this narrative review. This review summarizes the relevant data sources, calculation methods, technical features, performance indicators, and prediction methods. Based on technical action information, a comprehensive discussion was conducted around the main line of "from analyzing performance indicators to final prediction", and the relationship between research at different levels was elaborated. At the same time, this review also indicates that videos, Hawk-Eye technology, and wearable devices during matches can provide sufficient information on players' movement and spatial use; These data captured through external devices and analyzed by artificial intelligence need to be combined with the competition context in order to be used as supplementary data for in-game prediction. On this basis, this review proposes research directions for connecting action analysis with whole game prediction, including unified indicators and label definitions, prediction based on standard time series, and comparison using time series validation, probability calibration, and traditional benchmark models. This comprehensiv…

title: Explainable Machine Learning for One-Year Stock Return Prediction Using Financial Indicators
abstract: This study examines whether annual financial indicators can rank U.S. stocks by their subsequent one-year price changes. The dataset contains 22,077 firm-year observations and 221 numeric indicators from 2014–2018. Ridge, Lasso, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM are fitted using the 2014–2016 observations and evaluated on the 2018 financial-data cohort, whose target covers 2019. The 2017 cohort is excluded from model fitting. LightGBM records the highest test Spearman rank information coefficient, 0.0805, and a top-minus-bottom decile difference of 26.69 percentage points. Lasso has the lowest root mean squared error and mean absolute error, so the preferred model depends on the evaluation criterion. SHAP analysis of LightGBM identifies earnings yield, weighted-average shares outstanding, price-to-book ratio, the Energy sector indicator, and share issuance or buybacks as its five leading inputs. These attributions describe the fitted model rather than causal return determinants. The reported experiment uses full-sample winsorization and lacks filing timestamps; consequently, its chronological split does not eliminate information leakage. The findings are descriptive comparisons within one annual test cohort, and the decile difference should not be interpreted as an implementable investment return.

title: Neural network prediction of the mass distribution of behind-armor debris generated by tantalum alloy explosively formed projectile penetration into steel targets
Subgroup-Aware Evaluation and Interpretability in Myopia Prediction using Deep ROC and XAI
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) models are familiar for their great success in classification challenges within different domains. For medical diagnostics, those models have numerous applications as well. Basically, these ML models generate good predictions. However, sometimes, for clinicians, they are unable to depend on and use those models in a timely manner while making clinical decisions. Moreover, this factor arises because of the "black box" nature of these models. In medicine, it is a matter of concern. Because it is crucial to understand the base for predictions of patients’ safety and treatment assurance. Besides, recording key performance differences between risk groups is significant for informed clinical decision-making. In that case, traditional measures like the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve and the Area Under the Curve (AUC) show some limitations. Hence, to defeat such matters, this study proposes a unified framework for experimenting with Myopia prediction (known as nearsightedness) and evaluating the results using some advanced techniques. This approach integrates Deep ROC analysis with Explainable AI (XAI) methods, where for XAI, Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) are applied. Here, the Deep ROC analysis is more refined and has clinical relevance, as the model performance is generated within s…

title: Machine-learning models for preoperative prediction of new-onset hypocalcemia within 48 h after intertrochanteric fracture surgery in older adults
abstract: Background Older adults undergoing surgery for intertrochanteric fractures are vulnerable to early perioperative metabolic disturbances. We evaluated preoperative machine-learning models and compared them with single-predictor and conventional regression benchmarks for new-onset hypocalcemia within 48 h after surgery. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 332 patients aged ≥65 years with preoperative corrected calcium concentrations ≥2.15 mmol/L. Hypocalcemia was defined as an albumin-corrected calcium concentration <2.15 mmol/L. The primary analysis used Boruta feature selection and stratified five-fold outer cross-validation repeated five times, with four-fold inner cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning by AUROC. Imputation, preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning were repeated within each outer training fold. Models were compared using patient-level repeated out-of-fold predictions. Results New-onset hypocalcemia occurred in 92 patients (27.7%). The out-of-fold AUROCs were 0.639 for corrected calcium alone, 0.615 for albumin alone, and 0.442 for measured total calcium alone, compared with 0.670 for conventional logistic regression, 0.671 for a generalized additive model, and 0.6829 (95% CI: 0.6177–0.7407) for Stable Kernel Naive Bayes. The AUROC difference between Stable Kernel Naive Bayes and corrected calcium alone was 0.044 (95% CI: −0.022 t…

title: When Similar Models Disagree: Model Multiplicity and Geographic Robustness in School Meal Utilization Prediction
abstract: Competing predictive models can achieve similar aggregate performance while producing different classifications and downstream conclusions for the same individuals. This model disagreement raises an important question about whether conventional performance metrics adequately capture the reliability of model-based analyses. This study investigates model-choice disagreement across multiple analytical layers using voluntary-response survey data from 8,802 respondents who reported receiving meals through Indonesia’s Free Nutritious Meals program. Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using a nested school-disjoint validation framework. All three models were compared in terms of discrimination and probability calibration, while the competitive models were further examined through high-risk classification, predictive attribution, model-based scenario analysis, and province-holdout robustness. LR and XGBoost achieved nearly identical PR-AUC values (0.7270 and 0.7277, respectively), with similarly close pooled PR-AUC under province holdout (0.7288 and 0.7285). Despite this aggregate similarity, the models assigned different high-risk classifications to 5.41% of respondents. Their scenario analyses also produced different threshold-crossing rates: 8.87% of eligible respondents under LR (382 of 4,307) and 6.66% under XGBoost. Random Forest exhibited weaker p…

title: J-PAS: Exploring the connection between local environment and the triggering of bursty star formation in extreme emission line galaxies
abstract: Extreme emission line galaxies (EELGs) are typically compact low-mass systems undergoing intense bursts of star formation whose spectra are dominated by very strong nebular emission lines. Their physical conditions resemble those of galaxies in the early Universe, making them ideal analogues for investigating the processes that regulate star formation, feedback, and chemical enrichment at low redshift. Our objective was to characterise the local environment of a sample of EELGs identified in the J-PAS survey in order to determine whether their extreme properties are associated with the presence of nearby companions, as expected if galaxy–galaxy interactions were the main trigger of the burst. Using the J-PAS internal data release, we analysed a sample of 917 EELGs in the redshift range of 0.03łesssim złesssim0.9, previously selected using photometric and machine-learning methods over an area of ∼30 deg2$. We employed the pair probability function formalism, which combines the full photometric redshift probability distributions of galaxy pairs, to statistically identify companions within projected separations up to 200, and velocity differences up to $500, . Stellar masses, star formation rates, dust attenuation, and metallicity estimates were derived for the EELGs and their companions through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting using , and Monte Carlo simulations were pe…

title: Supply Chain Design and Optimization Strategies under Carbon Tariffs
abstract: As the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) moves into force, green and low-carbon transformation has become a question Chinese supply chains can no longer postpone. This transformation is shifting trade competition from "cost competition" into "green competition." This paper builds a supply chain analytical framework covering Scope 1/2/3 emissions and, through case and comparative analysis of Apple and BYD, proposes strategies along four dimensions. The study finds that CBAM brings heavy compliance cost pressure but also strategic opportunity: Apple pushed 320 suppliers to commit to 100% clean electricity and made selected products carbon neutral, while BYD cut supply chain emission intensity by 25-30% through vertical integration. Even so, Chinese enterprises still struggle with data acquisition, Scope 3 accounting, cost balancing, collaborative reduction mechanisms, and the fragmentation of green trade rules.

title: One stone, two birds? The impact of China's low-carbon city pilot policy on firms' investment efficiency
abstract: Purpose Reducing carbon emissions while sustaining economic growth is a central policy challenge for most countries. Capitalizing on the low-carbon city pilot (LCCP) policy in China, we investigate how environmental regulation affects the investment efficiency of carbon-intensive firms. Design/methodology/approach Exploiting the staggered LCCP rollout as a quasi-natural experiment, we use a triple-difference (DDD) design comparing polluting versus non-polluting firms around pilot designation. The sample covers Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2019 (24,463 firm-year observations). Investment efficiency is the absolute residual from Richardson (2006); we employ firm and high-dimensional fixed effects with robust errors, plus parallel-trend, placebo, and robustness checks. Findings The LCCP significantly improves investment efficiency of heavily polluting firms. The effect is stronger for firms with weaker external monitoring and higher agency costs, and works mainly by curbing under-investment. Parallel-trend and placebo tests support causality. Mechanism analysis points to strengthened monitoring, lower agency costs, and better corporate social responsibility performance. Originality/value This study links China's LCCP to corporate investment efficiency, reframing climate policy as a capital-allocation intervention. Our findings speak to the “double dividend” debate in …

title: Integrating metabolomics and proteomics uncovers core carbon metabolic dysregulation in Wilms’ tumor in children
Aperture-dependent [O iii] profile variability: Clues to the nature of double-peaked narrow emission lines
abstract: In this work we propose a simple and practical aperture-dependent method for investigating the physical origin of double-peaked narrow emission lines (DPNELs). Spectroscopic observations obtained from different apertures probe different spatial regions and therefore different gas kinematics within the narrow line region (NLR). Consequently, changes in the profiles of DPNELs observed with different apertures can provide important constraints on their physical origins. We applied this method to SDSS J094144.83+575123.6 (SDSS J0941) by comparing spectra obtained from the SDSS, DESI, and LAMOST surveys. Significant differences are found in the double-peaked profiles of the different spectra, demonstrating that aperture effects can strongly influence the integrated DPNEL profiles. The dual active galactic nucleus (AGN) model, where the two nuclei lie in a plane perpendicular to the line of sight, can qualitatively explain the asymmetric sampling of the two NLRs, but it cannot explain the different peak separations of different spectra. The observed asymmetric evolution of the two components disfavors a simple AGN-driven outflow and a rotating disk-like NLR scenario. Of the models considered, only a more complex non-axisymmetric rotating NLR provides a self-consistent explanation for the observed aperture-dependent variations. In this scenario, the blueshifted emitting region is more…

title: Symbolic and substantive carbon accountability in e-commerce logistics: a longitudinal comparison of Amazon, UPS and Trendyol
abstract: Purpose E-commerce logistics firms disclose more emissions data than ever. This article asks whether more disclosure has meant more accountability, measuring emission decoupling, disclosure quality, target attainment and cross-vintage comparability for three firms on a common window. Design/methodology/approach A pre-registered longitudinal comparison of Amazon, UPS and Trendyol over 2022–2024, from 14 primary reporting documents and 7 cross-check sources. Four indices are computed: Tapio emission-decoupling elasticity under 3 activity denominators, a 15-item Disclosure Quality Index scored against a published codebook, a target-gap ratio and a restatement-to-change ratio measuring cross-vintage revisions against the annual change those vintages are used to interpret. The coding was performed twice and agreement reported. Findings The firms diverge on disclosure quality and converge on target failure. UPS scores 90.0 of 100 in every year; Amazon rises from 60.0 to 66.7 and plateaus; Trendyol falls from 73.3 to 43.3, entirely through accounting transparency and verifiability, while inventory coverage is unchanged. Disclosure volume is maintained while the infrastructure that makes it checkable is withdrawn. All five announced targets sit off their required trajectories, and the revision to Amazon, 2023 total across 2 report vintages is roughly 49 times the annual change that fig…

Trading Partners' Logistics Performance and China's Exports
abstract: In the background of the advancing development of the global supply chain, the connection between logistics and international trade has become increasingly close. This paper is intended to investigate the relationship between trading partners' logistics performance and China's exports from the dual dimensions of theory and empirical, and provide a new perspective for understanding the operation mechanism of international trade. In this study, China's export volume is taken as the dependent variable, and World Bank's Logistics Performance Index is adopted as the core explanatory variable. A two-way fixed-effects model is constructed for empirical analysis, and panel data of 31 major trading partners of China from 2010 to 2022 are employed. Furthermore, robustness check and heterogeneity analysis are conducted. The results show that there is a positive correlation between trading partners' logistics performance and China's exports. This conclusion is supported by the robustness check. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that this relationship is significant in developed countries but not in developing countries. On the basis of the above conclusions, it is suggested that enterprises and the government can strengthen the formulation of logistics system, thereby promoting the common prosperity of the international economy in the win-win cooperation.

Associations of plasma biomarkers and amyloid positron emission tomography with regional tau burden in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Abstract Purpose Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) and plasma biomarkers are clinically established; however, their topographical relationship with regional tau burden remains unclear. We investigated whether amyloid PET and plasma biomarkers are associated with regional tau pathology, measured using second-generation tracer florzolotau ( 18 F) PET, across the Alzheimer’s disease (AD) continuum. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study enrolled participants who underwent biomarker assessment between September 2018 and May 2022. The primary outcome was the voxel-wise spatial correlation of florzolotau ( 18 F) standardised uptake value ratio with amyloid PET centiloid and plasma biomarkers, assessed using age- and sex-adjusted whole-brain and region-of-interest (ROI) linear regression analyses, including multivariate models adjusted for amyloid PET centiloid. Results The study included 92 individuals (mean age, 71 [standard deviation, 8.8] years; 46 men), comprising 40 amyloid-negative healthy controls, 10 patients with preclinical AD, 21 with mild cognitive impairment due to AD, and 21 with AD dementia. In initial analyses, regional tau uptake correlated widely with plasma amyloid-beta 42/40 (Aβ42/40) ratio, p-tau, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). However, following multivariate adjustment for global amyloid burden, correlations for Aβ42/40 and GFAP w…

title: Control of emission interval and timing in triggered periodic superradiance
abstract: Abstract To achieve more controllable development of coherence in solids, we investigated the effect of a trigger laser tuned to the superradiance (SR) transition wavelength on periodic SR observed in an Er:YSO crystal. For period control, applying the trigger laser reduced both the SR period and its variance, demonstrating enhanced controllability of coherence development dynamics. As the trigger laser power increased, both the period and the number of emitted SR photons decreased while maintaining a proportional relationship. This behavior is explained by a reduced SR threshold under a constant excitation rate and is reproduced by numerical simulations based on the Maxwell–Bloch equations. For timing control, we found that SR could be triggered even when the excitation laser alone was insufficient. This enabled us to control the emission timing of SR using short trigger pulses and provided a device capable of generating SR at desired timing.

Carbon risk, accounting conservatism and the moderating role of financial materiality adoption: international evidence
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to investigate the direct effect of carbon risk on conditional accounting conservatism and examine the moderating role of the adoption of the financial materiality (FM) principle. Design/methodology/approach This study conducts multivariate regression analysis on a panel of 315 firms from high-emission sectors across 17 countries (2020–2024), drawing on the Refinitiv Eikon and Bloomberg databases. Findings The results indicate that carbon risk has a negative effect on conditional conservatism. FM further amplifies this negative relationship. As this reporting principle is intended to enhance transparency and promote the timely recognition of carbon risk, the finding may be consistent with its symbolic implementation. Robustness checks show that external assurance of environmental disclosures neither mitigates this delayed recognition nor attenuates the amplifying effect of FM. The findings remain robust under alternative measures and after addressing potential endogeneity concerns. Originality/value This study offers post-2020 evidence on the relationship between carbon risk and conditional conservatism, addressing a literature that remains limited, mixed and largely rooted in earlier regulatory contexts. Moreover, whereas prior research has primarily examined FM’s implications for non-financial disclosure, this study shifts attention to its unintended c…

title: An Overview of Perovskite Quantum Dots for Carbon Dioxide Photoreduction
abstract: The rising level of atmospheric CO₂ necessitates more efficient artificial photosynthesis methods. Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) are promising photocatalysts because their bandgaps are easily tunable, and they feature high light absorption and efficient charge carrier mobility. This review surveys recent progress in PQD-based CO₂ photoreduction, covering synthesis methods, characterization techniques, and thermodynamic requirements. Among synthesis methods, the hot-injection technique is widely used as the benchmark for high-quality PQDs due to its excellent size control, whereas the ligand-assisted reprecipitation (LARP) method offers a simpler and more scalable alternative at room temperature. Characterization approaches—XRD, TEM, and XPS—are discussed for structural analysis, along with in situ FTIR for detecting surface ligands and reaction intermediates. Thermodynamic feasibility is evaluated by comparing the conduction band position of PQDs with the redox potentials of CO₂ reduction. Furthermore, we discuss key challenges, including moisture degradation, fast charge recombination, and Pb toxicity. Finally, future directions such as machine learning-assisted design, operando studies, and heterostructure engineering are outlined.

title: Integration of acoustic resonance testing for accelerated and cost-effective quality control of pins in screw coupling manufacturing
abstract: Abstract Modern railway manufacturing is under increasing pressure to reduce quality-control (QC) costs without compromising safety. This study investigates Acoustic Resonance Testing (ART) as a fast, non-destructive pre-screening method for detecting structural and material non-conformities in screw coupling pins, which are safety–critical components of 850 kN railway couplers. Eighteen heat-treated steel pins were evaluated using standard QC results and frequency response functions (FRFs), with rule-based and Random Forest classification. The rule-based classifier achieved 88.9% accuracy and detected six of eight NOK pins (NOK recall = 0.75). In a single six-pin test split, the Random Forest correctly classified five pins (83.3% accuracy), detecting both NOK pins and generating one false-positive NOK decision. These results provide preliminary pilot-scale evidence; 90 features and only 12 training pins pose a substantial overfitting risk and preclude reliable assessment of model stability. Economic modelling of Standard, ART, Hybrid and Full Skip strategies showed operational cost reductions of approximately 96.7% and processing-time reductions of 49.5% for Full Skip. Including initial investment, expenditure fell by 81.5% and 87.1% over 3 and 5 years. The scenarios assume that validated ART screening permits omission of routine hardness and laboratory testing; batch-level se…

Effect of electromagnetic coupling treatment on the tribological properties of YG6X hard metal
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the effect of electromagnetic coupling treatment on YG6X cemented carbide by comparing the phase composition, mechanical properties (especially hardness) and tribological properties of untreated samples, single-pulse magnetic field-treated samples and magnetic-electric field coupling-treated samples, so as to provide technical support for the high-performance development and application expansion of cemented carbides. Design/methodology/approach This study uses YG6X cemented carbide as the sample, designing three groups: Untreated (0 V, 0 T), Craft1 (single-pulse magnetic field, 0 V, 1.5 T) and Craft2 (electromagnetic coupling, 1.5 V, 1.5 T). Samples are polished and ultrasonically cleaned. XRD analyzes phase composition, a microhardness tester measures hardness and a friction tester conducts dry reciprocating sliding tests. 3D profilometer, SEM and EDS are used to observe wear morphology and element distribution. Findings This study finds that electromagnetic coupling treatment (Craft2) outperforms untreated and single-pulse magnetic field treatment (Craft1) on YG6X cemented carbide. It promotes WC and Co3O4 phase formation, reduces internal stress and increases hardness by approximately 6%. Craft2 also lowers the friction coefficient, shortens the running-in period and cuts wear rate by approximately 17% vs untreated samples. Fine spheri…

title: ICT Integration Challenges Among Secondary School English Teachers in Kavre, Nepal: A Qualitative Case Study
abstract: Background and Aim: Education policies of Nepal have prioritized the integration of ICTs through internet connectivity, funding computer labs, and providing digital learning materials and tools with the aim of providing equal access to quality education (Ministry of Education, Science and Technology [MOEST], 2016). The government of Nepal supported the establishment of ICT labs in community schools in Nepal by funding computing equipment. The relevance of ICT in education became particularly noticeable during the COVID-19 pandemic, which imposed a sudden shift to virtual learning environments globally. Government efforts such as the School Sector Reform Plan (SSRP) and the ICT in Education Master Plan reflect a strategic push toward digital integration in schools. Therefore, this study explores the challenges and barriers Secondary English teachers experienced in using ICT in Kavre district of Nepal. To achieve the objective, a qualitative case-study research design was employed. In-depth interviews, classroom observation, and document analysis were the major tools used to collect the information. Materials and Method: This study uses a qualitative case study design as suggested by Merriam (1998) to collect the experiences of three teachers teaching English at different secondary schools in Kavre district, Nepal, using purposive sampling. Data were collected using three approac…

title: Gas-Phase Pseudorotaxane Formation of Protonated Dibenzylamine with 21-Crown-7 and Vibrational Energy Redistribution Revealed by Cold Ion Spectroscopy
abstract: Abstract Pseudorotaxane formation is governed by a delicate balance among host–guest interactions, steric constraints, and solvent effects. Here, we investigate the complex of protonated dibenzylamine (dBAMH+) with 21-crown-7 (21C7), hereafter denoted as dBAMH+(21C7) in this study, using cryogenic UVPD spectroscopy, IR–UV DR spectroscopy, and quantum chemical calculations in the gas phase. The results of dBAMH+(21C7) were compared with those of the complexes with 15-crown-5 (15C5), 18-crown-6 (18C6), and 24-crown-8 (24C8). Although no stable dBAMH+(21C7) complex is detected by NMR spectroscopy in methanol, the complex is readily generated and isolated in the gas phase. The UVPD spectrum of dBAMH+(21C7) exhibits a congested vibronic structure resembling that of the threaded dBAMH+(24C8) pseudorotaxane rather than the simple spectrum of the nonthreaded dBAMH+(18C6) complex. Quantum chemical calculations show that a threaded form is more stable by more than 40 kJ mol–1 than a nonthreaded one for dBAMH+(21C7) in the gas phase. These results suggest that the dBAMH+(21C7) complex can adopt a threaded pseudorotaxane form. The unusually low photodissociation efficiency of dBAMH+(21C7) is also consistent with the smaller calculated oscillator strength and a substantial barrier along the dethreading pathway, providing further support for the formation of a pseudorotaxane. The IR–UV DR sp…

Strategic Opportunities and Key Challenges for China's Marine Energy Resource Development under the Framework of the 15th Five‑Year Plan
abstract: The 15th Five‑Year Plan period represents a critical window for China's transition from a maritime nation to a maritime power. This paper, guided by the outline of the 15th Five‑Year Plan and related policy documents, employs a combination of policy text analysis and industrial empirical analysis to systematically explore pathways and strategies for the efficient development and utilization of marine energy resources. The study finds that the 15th Five‑Year Plan provides a clear top‑level design for marine energy development, with three major strategic opportunities emerging: the "100‑million‑kilowatt" target for deep‑water offshore wind drives leapfrog industrial growth, with China's exploitable deep‑water wind resources exceeding 1.2 billion kilowatts and key technologies such as floating wind turbines having achieved major breakthroughs; deep‑water oil and gas have become the core replacement area for reserve and production increases, with the South China Sea containing 35 billion tons of oil and gas resources, and China having systematically mastered the full suite of exploration and development technologies in the deep‑water domain; the large‑scale utilization of marine energy opens a new track, aiming for an installed capacity of 400,000 kilowatts by 2030, with overall levels entering the world's first tier. Research Progress on Multimodal Physiological Sensing and System Integration of Flexible Bioelectronic Devices
abstract: Flexible bioelectronic devices provide mechanically compliant interfaces for acquiring, processing, and modulating physiological information across skin, organ, and neural systems. Their development has moved from single-parameter wearable sensors toward integrated platforms that combine electrophysiological, mechanical, thermal, and biochemical measurements with wireless communication, soft power modules, and algorithm-assisted interpretation. This review summarizes recent progress in the material basis, interface construction, multimodal sensing mechanisms, and system-level integration of flexible bioelectronics. Emphasis is placed on conductive hydrogels, elastomeric composites, liquid metals, laser-induced graphene, organic electrochemical transistors, porous soft structures, and adhesive interfaces that support low-impedance coupling, strain tolerance, and long-term operation. The review further discusses device designs for electrocardiography, electromyography, electroencephalography, pressure, strain, temperature, sweat metabolites, electrolytes, and inflammatory biomarkers, followed by integration strategies for crosstalk control, energy supply, wireless data transfer, intelligent analysis, and closed-loop feedback. It is demonstrated by current evidence that clinically oriented flexible bioelectronics require coordinated optimization of biointerface mechanics, signal f…

title: Culture-Commerce-Tourism Integration in Xiamen Shapowei: Economic Outcomes and Governance Logic
abstract: China's urban renewal has entered a stage of upgrading the existing assets. The integration of culture, commerce and tourism has become the mainstream approach for revitalizing old neighborhoods. However, the experience of leading benchmark projects is difficult to adapt to the limited resource endowments of small and medium-sized characteristic neighborhoods. The transformation of production-oriented waterfront fishing ports faces particularly prominent contradictions. This article takes the Shapowei Fishing Port District in Xiamen as a case and uses the longitudinal time-series comparison method to analyze the economic effects and governance logic of the integration of culture, commerce and tourism. The research shows that the gradual renovation of Shapowei achieved significant revitalization results, with the rent level increasing by more than doubled, the business structure being comprehensively upgraded, and the passenger flow scale continuously growing. The rent premium follows a three-layer transmission path of "space scene empowerment - cultural traffic transformation - business iteration value increase", essentially being the process of gradually realizing the potential rent of the space through the replacement of business types; the local fishing business types being squeezed out is the result of market spontaneous evolution, not an inevitable trend. Improving energy efficiency of the ore preparation process based on analyzing energy consumption of semi-autogenous grinding mills
abstract: In conditions when easily accessible ore reserves are depleting and the energy tariffs are rising, improving the energy efficiency of mining and processing plants is becoming a critical task. Ore preparation processes, particularly operation of semiautogenous grinding mills, which are major electricity consumers, hold the greatest optimization potential. The aim of this work is to analyze the actual energy consumption of a semi-autogenous grinding mill at the Kochkar gold ore deposit to develop practical recommendations for reducing specific energy costs. The study employs a comprehensive approach combining the Bond method for calculating the ore work index, direct measurements of electrical parameters (current, voltage, power) using AR5 and PKK-57 analyzers, and processing of statistical data using Python and MathCAD. The key results show that the average work index is 1.01 kWh/t; however, a weak correlation between the throughput and active power was identified. It was found that short-term interruptions in the ore feed fail to produce proportional energy savings. The practical significance of this work lies in justifying the need of transition to adaptive control systems and digital twins, which could reduce specific energy consumption by 10–15% and enhance the stability of the technological process.

title: Feasibility of measuring lumbar, postural, and biomechanical outcomes before and after a Rolfing® Structural Integration 10-series delivered by trainees: a single-arm pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background Rolfing® Structural Integration (RSI) is a manual and movement-education approach, traditionally delivered as a 10-session series, that aims to support postural organization, movement efficiency, and body awareness. Although the evidence base has expanded, prospective studies using standardized objective outcomes remain scarce. Before an adequately powered controlled trial can be justified, researchers should establish the feasibility of delivering the 10-series in an educational training setting and collecting objective postural, sensory, physiological, and biomechanical outcomes. Methods This single-arm, non-randomized pilot and feasibility study used pre–post measurements around a Rolfing® Structural Integration 10-series delivered in an educational training setting in Munich, Germany. Rolfers-in-training delivered the intervention under senior supervision. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, eligibility, retention, intervention completion, post-treatment measurement completion, data availability, and adverse-event data capture. Exploratory postural outcomes included individual DIERS formetric 4D rasterstereography parameters and an unvalidated exploratory z-normalized postural imbalance index. Secondary/exploratory outcomes included DIERS parameters, pressure pain threshold, perceived pain assessed using a visual analog scale, subject expectation,…

title: Evidence-gated integration of microbiome, metabolome, and host transcriptome data reveals a gap between reproducible signals and cross-layer mechanistic evidence in hepatocellular and colorectal cancer
abstract: Introduction Microbiome multi-omics studies frequently identify microbial, metabolic, and host transcriptional associations, but their reproducibility and support for connected biological mechanisms remain uncertain. We evaluated these relationships in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) using an eight-dimensional, non-compensatory evidence-gating framework. Methods Nine public HCC datasets spanning microbiome, metabolome, and host transcriptome profiles were analyzed alongside CRC microbial and metabolomic data and separate host transcriptomic datasets. Analyses included cross-cohort replication, participant-matched taxon–metabolite associations, host transcriptional responses, sensitivity testing, and independent evidence scoring. Complete mechanistic eligibility required support across all eight evidence dimensions. Results In HCC, 13 genera showed concordant directions and nominal significance across conventional leave-one-cohort-out analyses, but none met the adjusted external validation criterion. Six longitudinal plasma feature-window signals and 12 differential liver metabolites were identified without cross-specimen concordance under false discovery rate (FDR) correction. abstract: El artículo se ocupa de la pertinencia de diseñar materiales de apoyo y acompañamiento del trabajo realizado en el centro de escritura, desde un enfoque basado en movimientos retórico-discursivos y el modelo procedimental. Se analiza cómo los procesos de inferencia y las operaciones interdependientes del acto de escribir permiten entender mejor el manejo y desarrollo de habilidades de escritura. El artículo propone el diseño de un ejercicio de escritura, en el que bajo un discurso pedagógico se encauza una serie de aprendizajes esperados de habilidades de escritura correspondientes a la organización de ideas en el género del ensayo.

title: The Effect of Audit Quality, Tenure Audit, And Auditor Reputation On Fraudulent Financial Reporting with Institutional Ownership As A Moderation Variable in Industrial Companies Listed on the IDX For The 2021-2025 Period
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of audit quality, audit tenure, and auditor reputation on fraudulent financial reporting, with institutional ownership as a moderating variable in industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021–2025. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from audited financial statements and annual reports. The population consists of all industrial sector companies listed on the IDX, and purposive sampling yielded 49 companies or 245 firm-year observations. Fraudulent financial reporting is measured using the Beneish M-Score, audit quality is proxied by the natural logarithm of audit fees, audit tenure is measured by the length of the auditor-client engagement, auditor reputation is measured by a Big Four dummy variable, and institutional ownership is measured by the percentage of shares held by institutional investors. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA), with model selection through the Chow Test and Hausman Test. The results show that audit quality has a significant negative effect on fraudulent financial reporting (β = -0.284, p < 0.001); audit tenure has a significant positive effect (β = 0.157, p < 0.01); auditor reputation has a significant negative effect (β = -0.312, p < 0.001); and institutional ownership significantly streng…
