The Effect of Financial Distress on Audit Delay Through Audit Complexity as an Intervening Variable with The Audit Committee as A Moderation Variable in Industrial Companies Listed on The IDX For The 2021-2025 Period
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of financial distress on audit delay through audit complexity as an intervening variable, with audit committee as a moderating variable in industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the period 2021–2025. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from audited financial statements and annual reports. The population consists of all industrial sector companies listed on the IDX, and purposive sampling yielded 49 companies or 245 firm-year observations. Audit delay is measured as the number of days between the fiscal year-end and the date of the independent auditor's report, financial distress is measured using the modified Altman Z-Score, audit complexity is measured by the number of consolidated subsidiaries, and audit committee is measured by an audit committee effectiveness index. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The results show that financial distress has a significant positive effect on audit delay (β = 0.276, p < 0.001) and on audit complexity (β = 0.324, p < 0.001); audit complexity has a significant positive effect on audit delay (β = 0.298, p < 0.001) and partially mediates the effect of financial distress on audit delay (VAF = 26.0%); and audit committee significantly weakens the effect of audit complexity o…

title: Geomechanical reserves for optimizing open-pit slope design during the final mine development stage
abstract: This study explores the potential for additional geomechanical optimization of the slope design for deep openpit mines during the final operational stage. Feasibility of applying a reduced safety factor of 1.2 for slope sections with the Koashva deposit as a case study. The research provides a detailed analysis of the risks associated with rock mass fracturing, presence of carbonate rock, oxidation processes, and groundwater inflow. An assessment is conducted regarding the inward shift of the top edge of the slope and the consequent reduction in the overburden volume through implementation of a dedicated final development phase. Slope stability calculations were performed using the limit equilibrium method with circular slip surfaces for critical profiles of the hanging wall, where the initial safety factor equals 1.31. Results indicate that shifting the top edge into the ore body by 28.4 to 31.5 meters aligns the slope coordinates at the minus 188 meter level with the design configuration while significantly increasing recoverable reserves at the lower levels. For the adjusted contour during the final development stage, the calculated safety factor ranges from 1.24 to 1.26, fully complying with the regulatory requirements. An integrated approach that combines refined geomechanical modeling, optimized blasting operations, and a hierarchical monitoring system, slope optimization…

title: Blockchain-based labour credential management system for construction labourers
abstract: Purpose The construction industry relies heavily on a diverse workforce whose credentials include identity information, certifications, trade qualifications, employment histories, training records and medical documentation. Effective management of these credentials is essential to ensure workforce reliability, compliance and safety. Managing large volumes of labour credential data requires the storage efficiency and operational capabilities of relational database systems. Accordingly, this study aims to propose a hybrid labour credential management system that integrates blockchain and relational database technologies to support secure credential storage, tamper-evident verification and interoperability across multiple construction organisations. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a design science research methodology to design, develop and evaluate the proposed system. The architecture combines relational database storage with SHA-256 hashing, Merkle-tree aggregation and blockchain anchoring mechanisms to establish a secure credential verification environment. A prototype was developed and evaluated through internal and external validation involving ten construction industry professionals. Findings The findings demonstrated that the proposed system enables secure, efficient and tamper-evident credential verification while improving transparency, accessibility and t…

title: Design and statistical validation of low-cost electrogoniometers for elbow orthosis applications
abstract: Abstract This study presents the design, implementation, and statistical validation of four low-cost electrogoniometers for elbow joint angle measurement in orthotic applications. The proposed systems are four sensing configurations based on three hardware sensing modalities: infrared (IR) sensing with two calibration strategies, rotary potentiometry, and slide potentiometer, all integrated into a custom mechanical structure that enables indirect measurement while reducing mechanical stress on sensing components. Experimental validation was performed using a controlled elbow motion simulator and five healthy volunteers for preliminary assessment of device placement and wearable feasibility, with measurements compared against a reference digital goniometer. Performance metrics included mean absolute error (MAE), repeatability, linearity ( R 2 ), and statistical agreement. A one-way ANOVA revealed significant differences among sensing modalities ( p < 0.05), and Tukey’s post hoc analysis confirmed that the IR-based system exhibited significantly higher errors than calibrated IR-based and both potentiometer-based systems. Bland–Altman analysis demonstrated strong agreement for calibrated IR-based and potentiometer-based designs, with minimal bias and narrow limits of agreement. The calibrated IR achieved the highest accuracy (MAE ≈2.78°), while the slide potentiometer provided a f…

title: The Role of Personality Traits, Customer Journey Design, Omnichannel Trust, and Omnichannel Customer Experience in Shaping Value Co-Creation Behavior
abstract: Addressing empirical fragmentation in omnichannel literature, this study models how individual psychological attributes and structural service flows drive collaborative customer behaviors within emerging e-commerce markets. It evaluates the effects of Personality Traits and Customer Journey Design on Value Co-Creation Behavior, mediated by Omnichannel Trust and Omnichannel Customer Experience, alongside the moderating influences of Digital Proficiency and Channel Preference. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS via SmartPLS 4) was executed on survey responses gathered from 300 active Indonesian omnichannel shoppers through purposive sampling. Findings demonstrate that seamless journey designs and adaptive personality traits significantly elevate both customer trust and experiential quality, which directly propel value co-creation participation. Conversely, neither digital proficiency nor channel preferences exhibit significant moderating effects. The proposed model demonstrates moderate explanatory power, capturing variance across key outcomes with $R^2$ values of 0.533 for Customer Experience, 0.501 for Trust, and 0.359 for Value Co-Creation Behavior. Theoretically, this research extends Service-Dominant Logic and Trust Theory by establishing a dual-mediation mechanism that bridges micro-level individual traits and macro-level service architectures. The study's primary novelt…

title: Translocal identity work in virtual international assignments: digital diplomacy, psychological safety and cross-cultural trust
abstract: Purpose Despite the growing reliance on virtual international assignments in multinational corporations, how professionals negotiate professional legitimacy, belonging and cross-cultural trust within formal international assignment roles without physical relocation remains insufficiently understood. Grounded in Identity Work Theory, this study examines these efforts as translocal identity work in the absence of the spatial and cultural immersion that characterizes traditional expatriation. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative multiple case study was conducted across three multinational corporations in three sectors (technology, consulting, manufacturing). Thirty semi-structured interviews were carried out with virtual assignees, defined as employees formally assigned to manage cross-border responsibilities from their home base without planned relocation. The interviews were analyzed using a team-based thematic approach, with visual network elicitation used to prompt discussion of assignment-related relationships. Findings Three interrelated themes illuminate translocal identity work: (1) translocal professionalism, capturing the global professional identity and belonging virtual assignees sought to sustain while remaining locally based; (2) digital diplomacy, involving deliberate relational labor to build and sustain cross-cultural trust through digital channels and (3) pe…

title: Ensuring efficient operation of a mine dewatering plant when pumping highly abrasive and aggressive brines
abstract: The current stage of industrial development of many ore deposits is characterized by deteriorating hydrogeological and mining conditions. This makes the search for and development of engineering solutions to ensure uninterrupted operation of dewatering plants at low operating costs one of the most actual areas of applied research. Thus, justification and provision of rational operating modes for mine dewatering plants used for pumping water flows with particularly harsh physical and chemical properties, based on mutual impact of their technical and economic aspects of operation, constitutes a relevant scientific and practical problem, which solution will ensure sustainable development of the domestic mining industry in the medium term. The object of the study was multistage sectional pumps used for pumping highly abrasive and aggressive brines during the impact of the adjustable parameters of the mine dewatering plant on its reliability and cost-effectiveness of its operation. The results of the performed comprehensive assessment were used to justify the rational operating modes for mine dewatering plants utilized for pumping highly abrasive and aggressive brines. The paper describes in detail the developed engineering solutions aimed at ensuring efficient operation of the mine dewatering plants used for pumping water inflows with particularly harsh physical and chemical proper…

title: SPIRITUALITY, POWER, AND CORRUPTION: UNDERSTANDING THE PARADOXOF HIGHLY RELIGIOUS AFRICAN SOCIETIES
abstract: Religion has historically functioned as a central moral regulator in African societies, shaping ethical conduct, communal cohesion, and leadership accountability. Yet, paradoxically, many African nations, particularly Nigeria, exhibit persistent corruption, weak governance structures, and eroded social trust despite high levels of religiosity. This study critically examines the complex interplay between spirituality, moral authority, and corruption in African contexts, with a focus on Nigeria, seeking to understand why profound religious commitment does not automatically translate into ethical governance. This study employs a qualitative, desk-based methodology, the study analyses secondary data from scholarly publications, empirical reports, and institutional assessments. The study also adopts an interdisciplinary lens that incorporates sociology of religion, political science, and ethics.Conceptually, the research draws on Weber‟s theory of authority, the moral economy framework, and the instrumentalisation of religion, highlighting how religious institutions may simultaneously serve as moral guides and instruments of political legitimization. The study finds that while Christianity, Islam, and African Traditional Religion (ATR) retain ethical framework, their moral authority is frequently compromised through political patronage, prosperity-oriented doctrines, and erosion of …

title: Spatiotemporal differentiation and driving mechanism of vegetation phenology in a high-latitude region of China
abstract: Photosynthetic phenology describes the seasonal timing of vegetation photosynthetic activity. Using solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) data from 2001 to 2023, we extracted the start of the growing season (SOS), end of the growing season (EOS), and length of the growing season (LOS) in Hulunbuir, China, and compared forestland, grassland, and cropland. The results showed that SOS and EOS mainly occurred at 120–144 and 244–256 days of year (DOY), respectively, while LOS was mainly 100–130 d. Forestland SOS was earlier than that of grassland and cropland. Under the original thresholds, forestland LOS was slightly longer than grassland LOS, although their ranking was sensitive to threshold choice. Across the region, SOS advanced by 0.07 d yr -1 , EOS was delayed by 0.04 d yr -1 , and LOS lengthened by 0.10 d yr -1 . Earlier SOS occurred in central and northern Hulunbuir, whereas later SOS and shorter LOS characterized the southwestern forest–grassland transition zone. EOS advanced in the central Greater Khingan Mountains but was delayed to the east and west; LOS lengthened in the eastern and southeastern grassland but shortened in the mountains. Forestland SOS and LOS showed less interannual variation than those of grassland and cropland, and most valid pixels had Hurst estimates below 0.5. Land use type had the highest single-factor explanatory power for spatial SOS vari…

Beta-diversity partitioning reveals high floristic complementarity among tropical dry forest remnants in the Cauca River Geographic Valley, Colombia
abstract: Background and aims – Tropical dry forests are among the most threatened ecosystems on Earth, and in the Cauca River Geographic Valley of Colombia only about 500 ha remain. Where two sites share few species, either each holds a different set of taxa (turnover) or the poorer is a reduced version of the richer (nestedness), and these two components call for opposite conservation responses. We asked which one governs this flora, whether the answer depends on the method, and which fragment attributes predict each component. Material and methods – We analysed the presence and absence of 915 vascular plant taxa across 35 fragments. Compositional difference was separated into replacement and richness-difference contributions under two frameworks. Each component was related to the fragment’s position, elevation and area by constrained ordination, and tested for an increase with the geographic distance. Fragments were also ranked by the taxa they add to a growing selection. Key results – Compositional difference was very high (multi-site Jaccard = 0.977). Replacement dominated under both frameworks, though its estimated share differed (98% and 60%). Constrained ordination showed position and elevation to structure replacement, whereas area was unrelated to it and predicted only the richness-difference component. Dissimilarity increased with distance (Mantel r = 0.238, p < 0.001), but…

title: The Stabilization-Free Virtual Element Discretization for Anisotropic Diffusion Problems on Polygonal Meshes
abstract: This paper introduces a stabilization-free virtual element method designed for solving heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion equations on general polygonal meshes. The new method eliminates the need for stabilization and projection operator constraints by employing the extreme learning machines to locally approximate virtual element basis functions. In numerical experiments, the proposed method produces results identical to within roundoff error to those of the standard \(Q_1\) and \(P_1\) FEM on rectangular and triangular meshes, respectively. Numerical results demonstrate that the new method maintains optimal convergence rates for the \(L^2\) and \(H^1\) error on general polygonal meshes, even when the diffusion tensor is anisotropic, heterogeneous, or discontinuous.

Who stands with the virtual influencer? Trust in nonprofit versus corporate partnerships in social advocacy
abstract: Purpose This research investigates whether collaborations between virtual influencers (VIs) and organizations can reduce consumers' perceptions of opportunism and cynicism in social advocacy. It further examines the mediating role of trust and whether vulnerability disclosure moderates these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Two preregistered experiments (N = 640) examined responses to social advocacy campaigns. Study 1 compared three conditions: a VI advocating alone, a VI collaborating with a company, and a VI collaborating with a nonprofit organization (NPO). Study 2 used a 2 × 2 design crossing collaboration type (VI-company vs. VI-NPO) with vulnerability disclosure (budget constraints disclosed vs. not disclosed) to test whether disclosure moderated the indirect effects through trust. Findings In Study 1, VI-NPO collaboration generated higher trust and lower opportunism and cynicism than VI-only advocacy, whereas the corresponding VI-company comparisons were not significant. Study 2 found the same nonprofit advantage over company collaboration. Trust mediated these differences in negative perceptions. Vulnerability disclosure reduced opportunism and cynicism but did not significantly increase trust or moderate the indirect effects through trust. Originality/value This research advances understanding of how organizational partnerships shape consumer responses to VI…

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Risk Early Warning for the NEV Power Battery Supply Chain—Framework Development and Case Analysis Based on Public Information
abstract: The rapid growth of new energy vehicles has made power battery supply chains strategically important but increasingly exposed to mineral-price volatility, supplier disruption, quality failures, demand changes, logistics delays, and policy uncertainty. This study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven early-warning framework through literature review, indicator design, public-case analysis, and scenario reasoning. The framework links five layers: data, indicators, models, warning levels, and management decisions. It organizes signals across upstream supply, internal operations, downstream demand, the external environment, and circular supply. Public disclosures from Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL) illustrate how material exposure, supplier performance, customer demand, and recycling capacity can enter the framework. Four warning levels connect model outputs with differentiated procurement, inventory, production, logistics, and supplier responses. The study does not claim unverified prediction accuracy because firm-level time-series data are unavailable. It instead specifies the data and governance needed for empirical validation. The findings show that AI adds value when heterogeneous signals are converted into interpretable risk assessments and timely, accountable actions.

title: Spatial patterns of citrate exudation along the rice root apex in low-phosphorus soil
abstract: Root-released citrate can promote phosphorus (P) mobilisation in soils, but its spatial distribution along intact roots remains poorly characterised. This brief research report presents the millimetre-scale mapping of citrate exuded by soil-grown Nerica-4 rice ( Oryza sativa × Oryza glaberrima ) roots using a zirconium-hydroxide (ZrOH) hydrogel sampling method. Plants were grown in rhizoboxes containing a soil with low P content amended with 50 or 250 mg P kg -1 . ZrOH hydrogels were deployed to the apical 3 cm of selected roots for 24 h. After removal, the gels were cut into 0.4×1 cm sections, citrate was eluted with 0.5 mol L -1 NaOH, and quantified by high-performance-ion-chromatography single-quadrupole mass-spectrometric detection. The method resolved clear longitudinal variation in citrate exudation. In all four examined roots, the most apical section showed both the highest citrate quantity per unit root length and the highest citrate concentration in the hydrogel. Total citrate recovered from gel segments ranged from 3.90 to 8.75 ng in soils supplied with high P and from 18.67 to 59.28 ng in soils supplied with low P. Although the limited replication (n = 2 per treatment) precluded inferential statistical analysis, the consistent apical maxima indicate that citrate exudation is concentrated in young root tissues, where it may support local P mobilisation ahead of the gr…

title: The double-edged sword of virtual influencer anthropomorphism: a paradoxical framework of social presence and identity threat
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how the perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers shape consumers’ attitude toward virtual influencers through the competing psychological pathways of social presence and identity threat. Design/methodology/approach Through a cross-sectional survey, a sample of 448 Instagram users in Egypt was collected and analyzed using CB-SEM through AMOS v.23. Findings Both perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers have a positive influence on both social presence and identity threat. Importantly, both social presence and identity threat concurrently mediate the relationships between both dimensions of anthropomorphism and attitudes toward virtual influencers. Therefore, both dimensions of anthropomorphism influence consumers’ attitudes toward virtual influencers through the positive mediating role of social presence and the negative mediating role of identity threat. Research limitations/implications The study expands anthropomorphism research to the virtual influencer context by showing that anthropomorphism is not unequivocally superior. Therefore, grounding in social presence and social identity theory, we suggest that anthropomorphism is a double-edged sword in shaping attitudes toward virtual influencers. Moringa seeds for water purification in rural areas
abstract: The availability of clean drinking water continues to be a major problem in most rural and resource-constrained areas because of the growing water pollution by microbial, physical and chemical contaminants. Traditional water treatment systems prove to be very costly, power-intensive and inappropriate when used in decentralised systems. This review examines the possibility of using Moringa oleifera Lam. seeds as a natural, low-cost and environmentally friendly alternative for purifying water, especially in rural areas. Biochemical composition, agronomic flexibility and botanical traits of the seeds of M. oleifera are investigated in terms of their capacity to treat water. The availability of water-soluble cationic proteins facilitates successful coagulation and flocculation of suspended particles and microorganisms through neutralisation of negatively charged suspended particles and microorganisms, leading to high turbidity reduction and reduction of microbial load. M. oleifera seeds have been reported to have up to 90–99 % turbidity removal efficiency, over 90 % removal of total coliforms and Escherichia coli in highly contaminated waters and moderate adsorption efficiency for selected heavy metals like lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd) and copper (Cu), showing that M. oleifera is a sustainable natural coagulant for decentralized water treatment systems. Other processes, such as antimicr…

title: Mechanization in agroforestry systems: a systematic review of technologies for improving operational capacity among family farmers
abstract: Agroforestry systems can support sustainable agriculture by integrating production, biodiversity conservation and ecosystem service provision, but their expansion is often constrained by labor-intensive field operations and lack of mechanization, especially in family farming contexts. This systematic review examined whether the scientific literature provides sufficient evidence of mechanization strategies capable of improving operational capacity and contributing to the scalability of agroforestry systems. The review followed the PRISMA 2020 framework. Searches in Scopus and Web of Science, complemented by Google Scholar, identified 629 records; after duplicate removal, title and abstract screening, and full-text assessment, 20 peer-reviewed studies were included. Data extraction covered agroforestry spatial context, field operation, technology type, operational performance, labor and ergonomic aspects, costs, environmental effects, family farming relevance, limitations and research gaps. A complementary criterion-based suitability assessment evaluated 34 machines, operational chains, prototypes and support technologies according to agroforestry specificity, operational capacity and scalability potential, smallholder suitability, technology readiness, adaptability to complex agroforestry systems, labor and ergonomic contribution, and environmental or agronomic compatibility. title: Architectural hedging capacity: preserving strategic optionality in AI provider relationships
abstract: Purpose Firms increasingly depend on a small number of external providers for artificial intelligence (AI) models, yet that dependence is not only imposed by supplier concentration; it can also be reproduced by a firm’s own technology-integration decisions. This paper aims to examine how provider-specific integration progressively erodes a firm’s ability to switch providers, and what company leadership can do about it. Design/methodology/approach This paper is conceptual. Using resource dependence theory as its base, it draws on transaction cost economics, modularity and real options reasoning, organisational routines theory, and the attention-based view to develop a mechanism and an organisational capability, formalised in four core propositions, a typology matrix and a remedy audit. Findings The paper develops integration drift, a reinforcing process in which locally rational integration decisions cumulatively raise the cost of switching providers. It also introduces architectural hedging capacity (AHC), an organisational capability enacted through three recurring routines: governance-enforced modularity, rehearsed recalibration and sustained managerial attention. And lastly, the argument also identifies a boundary condition in resource dependence theory: where dependence is continuously reproduced through organisational integration, maintaining autonomy requires continuously…

title: Dredging of thick productive placer deposits that exceed the dredger excavation capacity
abstract: In conditions of a decreasing share of the placer gold in the total volume of gold production in the Russian Federation, the importance of placers remains high in the eastern regions, including the Irkutsk Region. At the same time, there is a deterioration in the mining and geological conditions of the placer deposits, i.e. the share of hard-to-recover reserves and the number of sections that are not maintained in terms of their capacity and width is increasing, while construction of new large-capacity dredges in Russia is virtually nonexistent. Bearing in mind the fact that development of reserves with variable parameters along the placer and areas with high productive sediment layer thickness will be carried out using the existing dredges, the authors have justified the scope of application for two technological options for preparing such deposits for dredging using Type 250D dredges. The first option provides for transloading of the upper part of the producing layer into a trench along the dredge cut using an ASH 10.70 dragline excavator. The second option is based on excavator-automobile transportation of the same volumes of sand to the thin or barren placer sites using an EKG-5A excavator, BelAZ 7540 dump trucks and a Shantui SD-16 bulldozer. Tabular-analytical modeling was performed for comparative analysis, i.e. more than 200 technological schemes were designed with the …

title: Psychometric evaluation and cross-cultural adaptation of the capacity for compassion scale for European Portuguese healthcare professionals (CCS-vPT)
abstract: Introduction Healthcare delivery settings subject healthcare professionals to high physical and emotional demands, requiring a robust capacity for compassion. This study aimed to cross-culturally adapt the Capacity for Compassion Scale into European Portuguese (CCS-vPT) and evaluate its psychometric properties among healthcare professionals. Methods In Phase I, translation, back-translation, expert panel review (S-CVI = 0.86), and pilot testing were conducted. In Phase II, a sample of 269 healthcare professionals ( n = 252 complete cases) completed the CCS-vPT along with the Self-Compassion Scale (SCS) and the Professional Quality of Life Scale (ProQOL). Psychometric evaluation included Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA, principal axis factoring with oblimin rotation), internal consistency, and criterion validity analyses. Results EFA yielded a three-factor structure-compassion toward others, self-compassion, and presence/self-regulation in the face of suffering-explaining 47.8% of the total variance. This structure differs from the four-factor structure described for the original scale. Internal consistency was high (α = 0.88 overall; subscales 0.78–0.87). Test-retest reliability demonstrated good temporal stability ( p = 0.70). Criterion validity was supported by significant positive correlations with the SCS, whereas weak or non-significant associations were observed with the…

abstract: Мета роботи. У статті всупереч напрацьованій традиції розведення діалектики і феноменології виявлено не просто моменти їх сходження, а показана єдина змістовно-смислова спрямованість цих способів мислення. Методологія. Засобами досягнення поставленої мети постає сама діалектика у її класичному варіанті, позбавлена ідеологічної упередженості минулих часів та неопозитивістських перекручень. Наукова новизна. У статті обґрунтовується думка, що внутрішня складність діалектичного способу мислення принципово суперечить домінуючій культурі інтелектуального виробництва, яка все більше формується управлінською логікою та академічною комерціалізацією. Виникає парадоксальне на перший погляд бачення феноменології як діалектики – рух в самому собі через інше самому собі. Але такі формулювання дратують здоровий глузд, який прагне чіткої зрозумілої йому інструментальної формули. Такий перехід у своє інше обумовлює безперервність, неможливість зупинки – проте ця безперервність схоплюється через свої перериви: бачення очима відокремленого одного обертається переходом у інше – зв’язок усього з усім. Антропологічною засадою діалектики постає невпинне трансцендування у інше, яке утримує існуюче одне в існуванні, і цим діалектика напряму узгоджена з діалогічними концепціями розуміння людського Я, що у своєму становленні відкрите іншому. CONTRATAÇÕES PÚBLICAS, LOCAÇÃO VEICULAR E CAPACIDADE OPERACIONAL DA SEGURANÇA PÚBLICA NO AMAZONAS
abstract: Este artigo analisa de que modo os contratos públicos de locação veicular impactam a capacidade operacional da segurança pública no Estado do Amazonas. Parte-se do problema de compreender como o planejamento da contratação, a gestão contratual, a fiscalização administrativa e a execução financeira se relacionam com a continuidade dos serviços de apoio operacional veicular utilizados por instituições de segurança pública. O objetivo geral consiste em examinar a relação entre contratações públicas, governança administrativa e capacidade operacional, considerando as especificidades territoriais, logísticas e institucionais da realidade amazonense. Metodologicamente, a pesquisa adota abordagem qualitativa, natureza aplicada, objetivos exploratórios e descritivos, com utilização de pesquisa bibliográfica, pesquisa documental e estudo de caso instrumental. O corpus documental compreende normas jurídicas, contratos administrativos, registros públicos, informações extraídas do Portal da Transparência do Estado do Amazonas, sistema PROJUDI e documentos correlatos à execução de contratos de locação veicular. Os resultados indicam que falhas de planejamento, desarticulação entre setores administrativos, fragilidades na fiscalização e atrasos no pagamento podem repercutir diretamente sobre a disponibilidade de viaturas, a mobilidade institucional, a presença territorial do Estado e a conti…

title: Smart Policing as Institutional Transformation: Technology Adoption, Organisational Capacity, and Social Implications in Namibia
abstract: Smart policing is increasingly associated with the digital transformation of law-enforcement organisations, yet the presence of digital technologies does not by itself constitute institutional transformation. This study examines how smart policing is experienced as an organisational and social transformation process in Windhoek, Namibia, with particular attention to institutional capacity, technology adoption, organisational adaptation, and community experience. The study employed a qualitative design involving 19 participants: 10 police officials, three executive leaders from technology providers, two policy analysts, two City of Windhoek officials, and two community members. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and a focus group discussion and analysed using thematic analysis. The findings show that technology adoption is uneven across organisational units and depends on infrastructure, maintenance, staff capability, managerial support, and the ability of institutions to integrate digital systems into existing work practices. Participants described improvements in information access, case management, coordination, and responsiveness, but also identified fragmented implementation, insufficient training, uncertainty concerning responsibility, and limited public understanding of technology-mediated policing. title: Research into the motivational mechanism in activities of Russian mining companies in the critical metals segment as a factor in improving the quality of production efficiency
abstract: This paper presents a research into employee motivation in the mining industry of the Russian Federation. The mining industry is the foundation of economic stability for resource-rich countries and is critical to global supply chains. Despite having its own resource base, Russian industry has long remained dependent on imports of certain types of rare metals and rare-earth products. Given the sanctions, this dependence becomes a vulnerability; therefore, development of mining and processing of critical metals is a prerequisite for sustainability of technological processes. The industry’s development is impossible without skilled workforce. The analysis conducted allowed the authors to identify two main groups of challenges that contribute to the low efficiency of workforce provision: the first is related to recruitment and retention, while the second one concerns training and development. Both groups are interconnected in terms of candidates’ unrealistic expectations and subsequent professional deformation of their personalities. The authors propose using a comprehensive evaluation index to assess the impact of employee motivation on the production efficiency indicators. It is calculated as the weighted sum of 10 key components. The proposed index makes it possible to determine the level of motivation and make timely management decisions. title: Spatial Attention Mechanism for Improved Multi-Focus Satellite Image Fusion: SARA-Net Model
abstract: Multi-focus image fusion is crucial in various fields, particularly in satellite images, because it creates intricate images with augmented clarity. However, maintaining the original structure is challenging, leading to a reduction in performance. Therefore, this research proposes a Spatial Attention ResNet-50 Network (SARA-Net) model for fusing multiple satellite images. The proposed model utilizes an integration of ResNet-50 and Spatial Attention to effectively extract spatially significant features from actual images. Initially, satellite images from the publicly available SpaceNet datasets are preprocessed by normalization and grayscale conversion to provide consistency. ResNet-50 handles multi-scale feature extraction by residual learning, which addresses vanishing gradient issues, whereas spatial attention assigns adaptive weights to improve relevant spatial information within the feature map. The fusion layer combines these attention features to generate high-resolution and detail-preserving images. On the ten held-out test images, the proposed SARA-Net achieves a PSNR of 48.972 dB, an SSIM of 0.9953, and an entropy value of 8.4319, which is better than the existing methods.

title: Mechanism of Cd Immobilization by Iron-modified Biochar Based on Fe–BDOM–Cd Synergistic Effect
Study on the Mechanism and Molecular Design of Targeted Drug Release for a Tetravalent Oxaliplatin Prodrug Modified with Reactive Oxygen Species-Responsive Phenylboronic Ester
abstract: Oxaliplatin is the core drug for the first-line chemotherapy of colorectal cancer. It inhibits tumor cell proliferation by forming platinum-DNA adducts, but lacks tumor-targeting selectivity. Long-term use is easy to induce multidrug resistance, which limits its clinical application. The level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the tumor microenvironment is significantly higher than that of normal tissue, and this oxidative stress difference provides an ideal endogenous trigger condition for the construction of intelligent response prodrugs. With its axially modifiable site, a tetravalent platinum prodrug can introduce phenylborate ROS-sensitive joints, giving the prodrug microenvironment recognition ability. Based on the molecular design theory of tetravalent platinum prodrugs, this paper systematically sorts out the structural characteristics and response mechanism of phenylborate joints, compares the stability differences of prodrugs in normal low-ROS and tumor high-ROS environments, and deeply explains the oxidative fracture of the phenylborate bond and the targeted activation of active divalent oxaliplatin in situ reduction and release. Process, clarifying the drug-free advantages of "tumor activation and normal tissue passivation" of the system. On this basis, the law of the influence of structural factors such as connecting arm length, hydrophobic modified groups, and o…

title: Emotional Premium and Cost Escalation in Fan-Sign Events: A Mechanism Study of Affective Valuation and Scarcity-Driven Pricing
abstract: K-pop fan-sign events monetise parasocial attachment by converting low-priced albums into access tokens for scarce, personalised interaction. Through the analysis of ENHYPEN's fan-sign event in Shanghai – "THE SIN: BLISS", the cost escalation process is explored. A combination of research about parasocial interaction, FOMO, fan identity, platformization, the official rules of the event and the structure of the case. The analysis results show that limited capacity, emotional attachment, platform visibility and uncertainty are the factors that move the consumers' attention from "value of the material" of the albums to "value of access". This change invalidates the price anchoring, supports the unofficial price and can stimulate re-consumption using social comparison. In the interim, fan-sign events can provide emotional gratification, a sense of community, album need and service innovation. To maintain these advantages and to reduce such damage, the study suggests that selection probabilities should be made more transparent, the verification process should be made more transparent, and that waiting lists should be officially maintained, limits should be put on campaign-level spending, and fan engagement should not be based on the number of purchases. These can assist entertainment businesses or platforms to maintain their people's confidence and help prevent over-investment and o…

title: Single-Actuator Driven Symmetric Five-Bar Mechanism for Producing Reciprocal Rectilinear High-Deflection Motion for Pumping Bag-Valve-Mask (BVM)
Adverse Reaction Mechanism and Optimization Strategy of Therapeutic Vaccines for Glioblastoma
abstract: This paper focuses on glioblastoma therapeutic cancer vaccines as the research subject, introducing the mechanisms of action and side effects of therapeutic vaccines. Regarding local, systemic, nervous, and immune-related adverse reactions occurring in vaccine clinical applications, the article analyzes the core causes and solutions for adverse reactions from four aspects: improper antigen selection, imbalance in immune activation levels, the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment of the glioblastoma, and the overlap of side effects from multimodal combination therapies. At the same time, the paper looks ahead to the development direction of this field, pointing out that personalized vaccine development, combined application of vaccines with immune checkpoint inhibitors, and conducting larger-scale clinical trials are future research priorities. Therapeutic vaccines are an important means of precision treatment for glioblastoma, but they still face limitations such as adverse reactions. Balancing anti-tumor efficacy with therapeutic safety is the core key to future vaccine optimization and clinical translation

title: Digital Marketing and Inclusive Finance: A Mechanism Analysis from the Perspectives of Cost Optimization, Efficiency Enhancement, and Resource Allocation
abstract: Inclusive finance has long been limited by information asymmetry, insufficient physical branch coverage, and the "80/20 rule" mindset, which has left long-tail customer segments underserved. The spread of digital technology offers a possible way to ease these problems. Drawing on long-tail theory, market efficiency theory, and capital cost theory, this study employs a theory-driven literature review to examine how digital marketing supports inclusive finance, focusing on its pathways, main mechanisms, and practical limits. The review indicates that digital marketing changes traditional financial service models in three main ways: it reduces information asymmetry, extends service reach, and improves resource allocation. In practice, these effects come mainly from lower costs (reducing information costs, outreach costs, and customer acquisition costs) and higher efficiency (improving information matching, operational efficiency, and customer lifecycle management). Besides, the high initial customer acquisition cost (CAC), the structural mismatch between the cost and return when providing services to low-income groups (long-tail customers) on a large scale through low-profit products, as well as the weak business sustainability, still pose significant limitations to this model. This study has constructed a comprehensive theoretical framework to understand how digital marketing sup…

title: Resilience in the quiet months: an anticipatory reconstruction capacity framework and its diagnostic application to cyclone Ditwah, Sri Lanka
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to specify and apply a framework linking capacities built before a hazard to the outcomes that follow it, running from the immediate impact and response to the quality of eventual reconstruction. Using Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka, set against two South Asian cases, it argues that durable resilience accumulates in the quiet months between disasters. Design/methodology/approach This conceptual paper synthesises pre-disaster recovery planning, disaster risk reduction mainstreaming and build back better into one construct, anticipatory reconstruction capacity, expressed as testable propositions. It is applied to cyclone Ditwah using secondary data and probed through a structured comparison with Odisha and coastal Bangladesh. Findings The framework links three measurable capacities, namely, risk literacy, institutional integration and anticipatory investment, to a chain that runs from disaster impact through response to reconstruction. The present evidence bears on the first link: for Ditwah, impacts tracked weaknesses in these capacities rather than the hazard’s rarity and in the comparison, mortality from similar storms fell sharply where capacity had been built deliberately, though life-safety gains outpaced asset protection. Evidence on reconstruction quality itself awaits the maturing of recovery and is framed as a proposition for future testing. Researc…
venue: International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment

title: Research on the Impact of Digital Inclusive Finance on Corporate Financing Cost: Theoretical Mechanism and Empirical Test
abstract: Based on the data of A-share non-financial listed companies from 2011 to 2023, this paper matches the Peking University prefecture-level city digital inclusive finance index with corporate financial data, and empirically examines the impact of digital inclusive finance on corporate financing cost and its mechanism of action. Financing cost is measured by the financial expense ratio, and the industry and year fixed effects model is used for estimation. The study finds that the increase of the regional digital inclusive finance development level significantly reduces corporate financing cost; the mechanism analysis shows that digital inclusive finance plays its role by improving the external information environment of enterprises and raising analyst following and research report coverage. The heterogeneity analysis shows that this effect is more obvious in non-state-owned enterprises, the eastern region and larger-scale enterprises. The study provides an empirical basis for improving digital financial infrastructure, optimizing corporate credit information governance and differentiated credit pricing.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Legal Implications of Heir's Incompetence and Violation of Legitime Portie on the Will Reduction Mechanism
abstract: Testamentary deeds made by testators under curatorship raise questions about legal capacity and the protection of heirs' absolute share (legitime portie) under the Indonesian Civil Code. This study analyzes the validity of a will made by a testator under curatorship, comparing the requirements of a valid agreement with will formalities, and evaluates inkorting as a remedy for wills that infringe the legitime portie of Class I heirs. The research employs a normative juridical method with statute and case approaches, using the Civil Code and court decisions as primary legal materials and literature as secondary materials. The findings indicate that curatorship does not automatically render a will null and void; it remains valid if the formalities are fulfilled and no defect of consent, such as duress, fraud, or mistake, is proven. Infringement of the legitime portie does not nullify the entire deed but is resolved through proportional reduction until the absolute share of Class I heirs is met. The study concludes that disputes must distinguish defects in the validity of the deed from violations of the legitime portie, thereby ensuring legal certainty and protecting the rights of heirs.

title: From participation to data: collaborative mapping in the context of natural hazards and risks
Pore Structure and Sodium Storage Performance of Sodium-Ion Battery Anodes
abstract: Pore structure affects ion transport and interfacial reactions in sodium-ion battery anodes and provides space to accommodate volume changes. This paper focuses on hard carbon, alloy anode and conversion composite materials, discusses the role of pore size, connectivity, pore opening and internal voids in the sodium storage process, and analyzes the advantages and limitations of different pore structures. The article also compares the synthesis strategies such as template method, activation method, carbonization control, dealloying and composite precursor derivatization, and explains how these methods shape the pore structure. Studies have shown that the sodium storage process and failure mechanism of different anode materials are very different, and the functional requirements of the pore structure are also different. The formation of pores is often accompanied by changes in phase composition. The contribution of pore structure cannot be evaluated only by capacity. The evaluation should also consider the sodium storage mechanism and failure process of the material under comparable electrode preparation and test conditions.

title: English immersive game participation and attention, emotional health, and cognitive function in children: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Screen exposure is an important issue for children’s health. The existing research pays more attention to the duration of use, but not to the content type and immersion experience. English immersion game integrates language learning and game mechanism, which belongs to educational digital behavior. This study analyzes the daily English game duration, immersion and English integration of children aged 6–14, and their relationships with attention, working memory, executive function and emotional behavior. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 215 children. Based on the parents’ questionnaire, the data of English game participation were obtained: daily duration, 1–5 immersion self-evaluation, and English integration. The outcome includes all kinds of attention, working memory, executive function, emotion and ADHD symptoms. Multivariate linear regression controls total screen time, sleep, physical activity, age, gender and family SES. CPT, Flanker and Corsi were the main outcomes, and after Bonferroni correction, the four executive function and behavior indicators were set as exploratory outcomes, which were not corrected. Results English game time is positively correlated with selective attention ( β = 0.218, p = 0.001). It is significantly different from the primary analysis of working memory, and its effect size fell below the minimum-detectable-ef…

title: Framing the harvest: advertising message framing, perceived benefits and consumer participation in adoption agriculture
abstract: Purpose This study examines how advertising message framing influences consumer participation in adoption agriculture, an emerging agri-food service model. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on message framing theory and the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework, we developed a mediation model with regulatory focus and context-specific trust as two proposed moderators. A one-factor between-subjects experiment was conducted with Chinese consumers after pretesting stimuli. Hypotheses were tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) and bootstrapping, with artificial neural network (ANN) and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analyses for robustness. Findings Gain-framed ads outperform loss-framed ads on short-term, long-term and recommendation intentions, with small-to-moderate effect sizes. Functional and emotional-social benefits jointly mediate this relationship. In addition, a post-hoc exploratory analysis suggests a positive association between functional and emotional-social benefit appraisals. The proposed interactions of regulatory focus and context-specific trust are not significant. However, context-specific trust has a strong positive main effect on perceived benefits, suggesting a general positive association with benefit appraisals rather than a framing-specific moderating effect. Research limitations/implications This study has several limitations. It …

title: Machine learning prediction of energy band gaps in curcumin derivatives
abstract: Machine learning (ML) regression models using SMILES-encoded molecular fingerprints were developed to predict the band gaps of 19 synthesized curcumin derivatives. The goal was to develop a ML-based framework capable of estimating the band-gap values prior to synthesis, thereby guiding chemists in their experimental effort. Training data for the model were obtained from the Harvard Clean Energy Project (HOPV-15), restricted to 52,000 non-fullerene acceptor (NFA) organic molecules with density functional theory (DFT)-calculated band gaps. Multiple fingerprinting schemes, including Morgan fingerprints, MACCS keys, atom-pairs, and FCFP, were used to train a pool of regression models. These models were then applied to the 19 curcumin derivatives for band-gap prediction and compared to DFT simulation calculations. The accuracy of the predictions was enhanced by using the Most Common Substructure (MCS) approach, narrowing it to molecules sharing key curcumin motifs. This refinement reduced the average predictive error by 30% compared with using the full HOPV-15 dataset, highlighting the benefit of targeted feature selection. Finally, the model was applied to virtually generate and evaluate 1,225 unsynthesized curcumin derivatives by permuting side groups on the BF2-curcuminoid backbone, identifying ten candidates with predicted band gaps above 3.2 eV, which were selected as a proof-o…
venue: Journal of Metals, Materials and Minerals

title: Optimization of Local Revenue Through Collaborative Governance of the Tourism Sector in Bandung Regency
abstract: Tourism growth presents opportunities to increase local government revenue; however, its fiscal contribution depends on effective linkages among tourism activities, local enterprises, and revenue administration systems. This study examined how collaborative governance could support the optimization of tourism-related revenue in Bandung Regency, Indonesia. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, drawing on Ansell and Gash's collaborative governance framework to examine initial conditions, institutional design, facilitative leadership, and collaborative processes. The analysis was based on policy documents, regulatory frameworks, and administrative statistics related to tourism, taxation, and enterprise development. The findings revealed that tourism-related tax revenue increased from IDR 46.12 billion in 2021 to IDR 95.31 billion in 2024, while the number of microenterprises increased from 15,790 in 2021 to 72,731 in 2025. Existing regulations, interagency coordination forums, infrastructure development, tourism promotion, and capacity-building initiatives provided institutional foundations for collaboration. Nevertheless, challenges persisted, including limited accessibility, insufficient stakeholder capacity, inconsistent coordination, and inadequate integration between tourism activities and local revenue administration systems. The available evidence demonstrated go…

title: Consumer Perceptions and Behaviour in the Transition from Internal Combustion Engine Vehicles to Battery Electric Vehicles
abstract: In recent years, the world has been accelerating the development of electric vehicles, but the response of consumers is not consistent. This study focuses on how economic cognition, safety beliefs and technical knowledge affect consumers' willingness to shift from fuel vehicles to pure electric vehicles, and examines how these effects differ across income levels and household car scenarios. The study surveyed 296 car owners. The results showed that cost savings and driving experience were the main driving factors, while battery decay and endurance anxiety were the main obstacles. Regression analysis found that electric vehicle knowledge is the strongest predictor of purchase intention, economic factors and safety factors also have a significant positive effect. Different consumer groups have different preferences: people with higher incomes pay more attention to technology and performance, while buyers with limited budgets pay more attention to total cost of ownership. In addition, pure electric vehicles as a second commuter car are more acceptable than as the main household car. These results suggest that in order to accelerate the popularity of electric vehicles, not only price incentives, but also targeted consumer education and marketing for different usage scenarios are needed.
