title: Applications of Markov Chains in Financial Risk Modeling: A Critical Literature Review
abstract: Markov chains represent financial risk as movement between credit or market states. This review examines how that representation supports credit migration analysis, default estimation, market risk forecasting, and portfolio decisions. It compares foundational models with subsequent research on rating heterogeneity, switching volatility, and economic conditions. The literature supports Markov models as interpretable tools for connecting current information to future loss distributions, but their usefulness depends on the state definition and stability of transition probabilities. A three-state numerical illustration shows how persistent adverse conditions can amplify cumulative default risk through repeated migration. The review distinguishes physical probabilities used for forecasting from risk-neutral probabilities used for pricing, and explains why a transition matrix alone cannot determine portfolio tail risk. It concludes that Markov models are most credible when combined with economic conditioning, explicit dependence assumptions, parameter uncertainty, and evaluation on observations unavailable during estimation.

title: Nano-Drug Delivery Systems for Tumor Therapy: A Review of Design Strategies, Evaluation, and Mechanisms
abstract: Traditional cancer chemotherapy remains limited by serious systemic toxicity, poor tumor targeting, and multidrug resistance, resulting in unsatisfactory clinical therapeutic outcomes. Nano-drug delivery systems, featuring tunable physicochemical properties, EPR-mediated tumor accumulation and tumor microenvironment responsiveness, have emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations. However, existing studies focus on individual material optimization, lacking a systematic synthesis of the complete research paradigm. This paper adopts literature induction and comparative analysis to examine the complete research paradigm of tumor-targeted nano-delivery systems. It compares four mainstream nanocarrier platforms, including lipid-based, polymer-based, inorganic, and hybrid systems. It then evaluates their design strategies, physicochemical properties, in vitro cellular uptake and cytotoxicity assays, and in vivo therapeutic efficacy and biosafety verification. Furthermore, this paper clarifies the core mechanisms underlying targeted delivery, pH/redox-responsive drug release, multidrug resistance reversal and synergistic multi-modal therapy. The reviewed studies indicate that rationally designed nano-drug delivery systems can enhance drug accumulation in tumors, reduce off-target systemic toxicity, and improve therapeutic outcomes. The systematic synthesis offers val…

title: Design and Rationale of the Niigata Cardiovascular Disease Registry Using Linked Administrative and Clinical Data (NiCARDIA)
Research on the Diagnosis and Dynamic Intervention of Interaction Design Efficiency Bottlenecks Based on User Experience Metrics
abstract: A delayed review tells a design manager that work has stalled, but says little about why. The same difficulty arises with repeated requirement changes and clarification requests from developers after delivery. This paper uses user experience measurement to investigate such constraints during interaction design. Interview material, analyzed through grounded theory, yields four bottleneck categories: cognitive, process-related, collaborative, and tool-related. Observable indicators are assigned to these categories, and constraint theory informs the selection of responses. The resulting MLIE model repeats monitoring, identification, intervention, and evaluation as conditions change. Its application in an internet company's design team covered three intervention rounds. The procedure gives managers a way to examine evidence for a suspected constraint and then assess the response, reducing reliance on experience alone.

title: Faint companions to hot stars. Spectroscopic detection sensitivity and implications for survey design
abstract: Searches for black holes in binaries must distinguish genuinely dark companions from faint luminous stars. This is particularly challenging for massive hot stars. Their masses can exceed those of typical stellar black holes, while their spectra contain only a few broad lines. We developed a Fourier-domain method that converts isolated, broadened spectral lines into calibrated constraints on faint companions. In Fourier space, Doppler shifts are encoded in the phase, while the line profile defines a smooth amplitude envelope. A faint secondary introduces an oscillatory perturbation to the otherwise smooth log-amplitude. Expanding this perturbation to first order in the secondary-to-primary line-depth ratio, α, allows it to be profiled against the smooth baseline in a likelihood-ratio test with the single-star model. Because the model is analytic and nearly linear, its sensitivity can be evaluated transparently for individual spectra and at survey scale. It can be applied to single or multiple epochs without requiring full spectral disentangling. At small velocity separation v, the companion signal becomes degenerate with the smooth single-star profile. For the Fourier log-amplitude, the fractional uncertainty scales as Δα/α ∝ v^ -4 . If the primary velocity is known, the Fourier phase provides a more favorable detection channel whose sensitivity scales as v^-1. We demonstrated t…

title: AI-guided human-in-the-loop inverse design of high performance engineering structures
Speculating Future Food: Cancer Cells, Food Boundaries and Design Fiction
abstract: Food is closely connected to everyday habits, cultural identity and ideas of safety. Environmental contamination and emerging food technologies, however, have raised questions about how these ideas might change. Taking concerns surrounding nuclear contamination as its starting point, this paper considers a hypothetical future in which access to conventional food sources becomes severely restricted. Within this setting, cancer cells are introduced as an unusual visual reference for exploring the boundary between food and bodily tissue. The project involves eight food-like prototypes inspired by the morphological characteristics of cancerous tissue. Resin clay, pigments and transparent gel were used to reproduce selected textures and forms, while Japanese Omakase presentation conventions provided a recognisable dining context. The research follows a Research through Design approach, combining visual research, material experiments and iterative prototyping. Particular attention was given to the relationship between biological appearance and food presentation. The design process revealed difficulties in maintaining both qualities within the same object. Some prototypes appeared too similar to medical specimens, while others lost their biological associations when presented as refined dishes. Adjustments to surface treatment, scale and arrangement helped establish a visual balance. …

title: Legal Political Reform of the Establishment of A Land Bank as A Legal Instrument in Land Acquisition for Development
abstract: Land acquisition for development in Indonesia faces persistent challenges, including limited land availability, land speculation, overlapping institutional responsibilities, and disputes concerning community land rights. The establishment of the Land Bank Agency (Badan Bank Tanah) represents an institutional response to these challenges; however, its legal framework requires critical examination to ensure consistency between development objectives and the principles of agrarian justice. This study examined the legal policy underlying the establishment of the Land Bank Agency, its legal status, its role in land acquisition for development, and the normative reforms necessary to strengthen its contribution to public welfare. The study employed a normative juridical research method incorporating statutory, conceptual, case, and historical approaches. Primary, secondary, and tertiary legal materials were collected through library research and analyzed qualitatively using descriptive and prescriptive legal reasoning. The findings indicated a shift in land governance policy from reactive land acquisition toward proactive, planned, and sustainable land reserve management. The Land Bank Agency was identified as a special legal entity established by the central government to manage land in accordance with its statutory mandate and the state's right of control over land, rather than as a…

title: Research on the Development of Interactive Teaching Ability of Secondary and Higher Vocational English Teachers Based on Vocational Education Curriculum Reform and Foundational Literacy Orientation
abstract: Under the circumstances where vocational education curriculum reform is continuously deepening and the orientation towards foundational literacy is increasingly prominent, English teaching at both secondary vocational and higher vocational levels is shifting from knowledge imparting to the shaping of abilities and the integration of literacy. This poses higher requirements for teachers’ interactive teaching abilities. This study focuses on the connotation, current situation and development path of the interactive teaching abilities of English teachers at secondary and higher vocational levels, and conducts an empirical investigation of English teachers from multiple secondary and higher vocational colleges. The study finds that currently, teachers generally have a certain awareness of interaction, but there are still significant deficiencies in task-based interactive design, guiding multi-round dialogues in the classroom, and deep interaction enabled by information technology; their ability development is constrained by traditional teaching concepts, a single evaluation mechanism and the lack of systematic training. Based on this, the study proposes a development path for the interactive teaching abilities of English teachers at secondary and higher vocational levels from four aspects: target positioning, content construction, route design and support system, in order to system…
venue: World Journal of Education and Humanities

title: Coverage Without Capability: Understanding the Disparity Between Urban and Rural Low-Income Populations in Universal Healthcare Reform
abstract: Despite the coverage of Universal Healthcare (UHC) reforms being globally expanded and out-of-pocket costs substantively lowered, disparities between urban and rural populations persist, particularly for those with low income. This paper examines the mechanisms through which UHC reforms have failed to close this gap. Drawing on Amartya Sen's Capability Approach and Jennifer Ruger's Health Capability Paradigm, it evaluates equity as the substantive capability to achieve health outcomes, not formal entitlement. The 3A Framework and Marmot's Social Determinants of Health specify the conversion factors that determine whether coverage becomes actual capability to access medical resources and services. Cross-country evidence shows financial protection improves access to medical resources but not treatment outcomes. The binding constraint diverges by setting: social infrastructure in cities, physical infrastructure in rural areas. A comparative study between two contrasting cases of the hyper-dense, public transit-dependent, metropolitan Shenzhen and the mountainous, formerly impoverished rural Chishui County, Guizhou confirms that instead of financial coverage, spatial accessibility is the decisive conversion factor that produces proximity without access in Shenzhen and nominal equity without substantive medical abundance in Chishui.
venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media

title: When Does Cross-Market Transfer Help? Evidence from E-Commerce Markets
abstract: Multi-country platforms can share interaction data across their stores. Past studies report average gains, not what transfers. This study separates product popularity from co-interaction patterns, using XMarket ratings from 68 Amazon country–category stores, full-catalog ranking, and tuned closed-form recommenders. Duplicated variant reviews, which inflate accuracy, are merged. Foreign co-interaction patterns agree with local ones beyond a degree-preserving null. They lose less cross-country agreement than popularity in 95% of store pairs (difference scale) and 90% (chance-corrected scale), but only partly for one popularity-adjusted measure. In retrospective splits, pooling foreign data into stores with complete local data gives item-based models a small gain (mean +0.017 normalized discounted cumulative gain, NDCG@10, over a median of 0.105). Validation-tuned weighting does not improve it. Under a calendar cutoff, the estimate, +0.006 [−0.008, +0.014], is inconclusive (weakly positive at earlier cutoffs). With scarce local pattern data, foreign data close a median of 0.55–0.71 of the accuracy gap retrospectively. Under the calendar cutoff, they close 0.60 [0.22, 0.80] to 0.79 [0.34, 1.14] (less with more local data). With only user histories missing, they close almost none. Launched products gain only retrospectively. Exploratory tests link geographic distance to one populari…
venue: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research

title: Evolution of Major Shareholder Networks in China’s Shanghai A-Share Market: A Dynamic Network Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic evolution of major shareholder networks in Chinese listed companies from a complex network perspective. The shareholder–stock system is analyzed at the network level because ownership links are interdependent and may reveal collective structures that are not visible from firm-level statistics alone. Based on quarterly data on the top ten shareholders of Shanghai A-share companies covered by the historical dataset from 2011 to 2024, dynamic “shareholder–stock” bipartite networks are first constructed. Statistically validated projected shareholder networks are then derived using the Statistically Validated Network (SVN) method. Basic topological metrics, degree-distribution heterogeneity, community structures, and node-importance measures are analyzed to characterize the temporal evolution of network structure. Over the study period, expansion of the shareholder set was accompanied by declining density and average degree in the non-isolated subgraph, while its clustering coefficient increased, indicating increasing overall sparsity alongside persistent local interconnectedness. Relative to the surrounding periods, the 2020–2022 period exhibited a temporary structural reconfiguration, although the overall network scale remained relatively stable. This reconfiguration was characterized by a rebound in average degree, the expansion of large commun…

title: When Solar PV Energy Gets Worthless: Can Energy Storage Systems Save Citizen Participation PV Projects From Negative Electricity Prices?
abstract: The increasing frequency of negative electricity prices on the German day-ahead market poses a growing challenge to the economic viability of photovoltaic (PV) citizen participation models. With over 430 hours of negative prices recorded in 2024, PV-based participation schemes that rely on stable cash flows from electricity feed-in face significant revenue risks. This paper investigates whether the integration of co-located large-scale battery energy storage systems can stabilize financial returns within such models. We analyze a community-based variant of the generation-synchronous energy returns (EBeRE) participation concept, in which citizens virtually self-consume electricity from a shared 1.5 MW PV plant and surplus electricity is redistributed among participants through a formalized community sharing mechanism. A market-oriented battery storage system is modelled as a centrally dispatched, co-located green storage unit, optimized via day-ahead dispatch with perfect foresight, whose discharged energy is virtually allocated to participants ex post. Four representative household profiles, reflecting different consumption levels and degrees of sector coupling, are simulated for the year 2025. Results show that storage integration increases self-consumption rates by 3 to 36 percentage points depending on the user profile, with the largest gains observed for low-demand househol…

title: Impact of Dynamic Electricity Tariffs and Time-of-Use Grid Charges on Households with PV-BESS
abstract: This study uses simulation-based analysis to examine how a real-time pricing electricity tariff and time-of-use grid charges affect different residential households with photovoltaic generator and battery energy storage system. The study aligns with other research in terms of general trends. A novelty of this work is the completely reworked methodology regarding the level of detail in which the households are modeled. The findings confirm that economic benefits are achievable through price-based control, especially when combining real-time pricing electricity tariffs and time-of-use grid charges. With a standalone 5-kWh battery system and without a photovoltaic generator they save €153/year on electricity costs on average when just using real-time pricing. If the nominal charging power of the battery inverter is lifted from 2 kW to 3 kW the reference household saves €35/year, whilst the nominal discharge power of 1 kW is sufficient enough to reach the maximum savings for this usable battery capacity. Furthermore, if the time-of-use grid charges are incorporated as well the savings can be increased to €233/year on average. However, in case that an additional 10-kW photovoltaic generator is installed the savings are diminished to €64/year. Depending on the scenario, some households would even pay more than before. Photovoltaic systems reduce the potential savings of real-time pri…

title: Trade Unionism in Nigeria's Electricity Sector: Workers' Rights in Post-Privatization Distribution Companies
Assessment of the Relationship between Labour Force Ageing and the Labour Market in Lithuania in the Context of its Demographic Development
abstract: This study seeks to assess the relationship between population ageing in Lithuania and developments in the labour market. In analysing labour-resource dynamics and ageing-related demographic trends, the article prioritises an evaluation of the absolute and relative changes in the number of individuals of working age and older persons. To characterise the issue in greater depth, the publication also employs additional indicators associated with population (labour-force) ageing, including the demographic old-age coefficient and the median age. The link between population ageing and labour-market outcomes is further reflected through specific statistical indicators used in the analysis, such as the average age of employed persons and the average age of those exiting employment, derived from the Labour Force Survey data. A further priority of the study is to assess differences in labour-market integration opportunities for more vulnerable target groups in Lithuania, namely, for older people and for young people. By using correlation-regression analysis, the publication also examines the relationship between economic development (GDP) and labour-market conditions across the EU countries, while focusing on two demographically contrasting age groups: youth and older persons. Accordingly, the analysis does not rely solely on national statistics but, additionally, incorporates Eurostat …

title: Cross-Market Non-Destructive Quality Assessment of Arumanis Mangoes Using Genetic Algorithm–Optimized Ensemble Models and Low-Cost AS7265x UV–Vis–NIR Spectroscopy
abstract: Research background. Arumanis mango is a high-value tropical fruit whose market acceptance depends primarily on internal quality attributes. However, reliable quality grading remains difficult because Arumanis is a green-mature cultivar that shows minimal external colour changes during ripening. Moreover, most existing non-destructive sensing studies rely on controlled experimental conditions, high-cost instruments, or homogeneous sample sources, with limited evaluation of model robustness across heterogeneous market environments. Experimental approach. This research evaluates a low-cost, portable, and non-destructive quality assessment framework combining an AS7265x UV-Vis-NIR multispectral sensor with a genetic algorithm-optimised committee machine (GA-CM) to predict physicochemical parameters of Arumanis mangoes. A total of 200 samples were collected from both modern and traditional markets to capture variability in maturity levels and postharvest handling practices. Non-destructive spectral reflectance data were acquired at 18 wavelengths (410–940 nm), followed by destructive reference measurements of total soluble solids, total sugar, vitamin C, pH, and water content. Three base learners, e.g. linear regression (LR), support vector regression (SVR), and artificial neural network (ANN), were developed and integrated using two ensemble strategies: simple averaging and GA-bas…

title: Effect of Contractor Competency on the Quality of the Musanze Modern Market Renovation Project, Rwanda
abstract: Contractor competency is an important consideration in infrastructure quality. This study examined the associations of personnel’s technical skills, project management experience and compliance with construction standards with the quality of the Musanze Modern Market renovation project, implemented by Hugo Engineering Durability Company Ltd in Rwanda. Project quality encompassed structural integrity, timely completion and user satisfaction. Guided by the Resource-Based View, Contingency Theory and Total Quality Management, the study adopted a descriptive correlational design supplemented by interviews, observations and documentary review. A census targeted 135 stakeholders, of whom 127 returned completed questionnaires, yielding a 94.1% response rate. The four focal scales had reported Cronbach’s alpha coefficients ranging from .852 to .891. Quantitative analysis used descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression in SPSS, while interviews were analysed thematically. Reported bivariate associations with project quality were positive for technical skills (r = .814), project management experience (r = .779) and standards compliance (r = .742). However, inconsistencies between the correlation and regression tables prevented definitive interpretation of adjusted relationships, explained variance and hypothesis decisions. Respondents generally assessed structura…

title: Biodiversity as a Financial Determinant of Carbon Market Uncertainty: The Interplay of Oil Shocks, Green Finance, and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the determinants of carbon market uncertainty within a unified energy–finance–environment framework, with particular emphasis on the role of biodiversity, oil market shocks, green finance, and artificial intelligence (AI). Against the backdrop of recent global crises, including the COVID‐19 pandemic, the Russia–Ukraine conflict, and escalating geopolitical tensions in energy markets, oil price volatility has emerged as a key driver of instability in carbon pricing systems. The results reveal that biodiversity exerts a nonlinear, inverted‐U‐shaped effect on carbon market uncertainty, acting as a stabilizing force at both low, and high levels while generating transitional volatility at intermediate levels. Green bonds and AI exhibit state‐contingent effects, contributing to market stability under normal conditions but showing weaker, pro‐cyclical behavior during periods of stress. In contrast, oil price dynamics consistently amplify carbon market uncertainty, particularly under extreme conditions, confirming the dominant role of fossil fuel markets in shaping carbon risk. These findings highlight the need to consider the joint interaction of ecological factors, technological innovation, and energy market dynamics when assessing carbon market stability. The study contributes to the literature by introducing biodiversity as a financial determinant of ca…

title: Evaluation of Bacillus spp. for managing late leaf spot and promoting yield in peanut production
abstract: Late leaf spot (LLS), caused by Nothopassalora personata, is a major disease that can lead to severe defoliation and yield loss in peanut. Currently, LLS management relies on conventional fungicides; however, emergence of fungicide resistance and environmental concerns create a need for complementary sustainable management strategies. This study evaluated Bacillus-based treatments, in-furrow or broadcast sprays, for their effects on LLS management and peanut yield in four field trials across three years in South Carolina. Commercial products containing strains D747 and QST713, two locally-isolated B. amyloliquefaciens strains, and phorate were applied in-furrow and followed by standard chlorothalonil programs. Additional experiments evaluated varying in-furrow application rates of commercial Bacillus products and foliar applications of Bacillus-based products in alternation with chlorothalonil. Chlorothalonil alone reduced LLS incidence in three trials. Adding in-furrow treatments did not further reduce disease incidence compared to chlorothalonil alone but consistently reduced it vs. the untreated control in all four trials. In-furrow treatments of D747, QST713, and phorate performed similarly; they significantly reduced defoliation and increased pod yield by 11.5-17.3% vs. chlorothalonil alone, while chlorothalonil alone did not improve yield over the untreated control. There…

title: A Novel Variant in Transformation/Transcription Mediator-Associated Protein (TRRAP) at a Known Hot Spot Causing a Blended Phenotype: Implications for Further Research
Occurrence of Leaf Spot on Solidago canadensis caused by Colletotrichum aenigma in China
abstract: Solidago canadensis is a rhizomatous perennial plant native to North America that has invaded eastern China and continues to spread northward and westward (Uzelac et al. 2025). In June 2025, leaf spot on S. canadensis was obsered in Chibi (29.811199° N, 113.577812° E), Xianning City, Hubei Province, China. The disease incidence reached 10% across surveyed fields covering 100 square meters. Initially, small necrotic spots appeared, which rapidly expanded into irregular grayish-brown lesions with a reddish-brown outer ring. Collected leaf samples were used to isolate the pathogen by single-spore isolation method (Choi et al. 1999). The isolates grown on potato dextrose agar (PDA) plates at 25°C in the dark for 5 to 7 days of incubation with similar morphology, and two representative isolates, QM-1 and QM-2 were used for further study. The colony surface presents a circular, white, cottony morphology and undergoes a brownish-gary discoloration. Conidia were unicellular, oval, and hyaline, usually in size from 10.47 to 21.16 × 3.14 to 6.98 μm in size (n = 50). The morphological characteristics were consistent with published descriptions of the Colletotrichum sp. (Liu et al. 2022). For accurate classification, genomic DNA of two representative isolates was extracted from mycelia using a DNA extraction kit (TSINGKE Biotech Co., Ltd.). For molecular identification, the regions of acti…

title: Skin Microbiota of Field-Grown Processing Tomato Fruits in Relation to Alternaria Black Spot and Mycotoxin Contamination
abstract: Tomato is among the most widely cultivated vegetable crops worldwide. However, its high susceptibility to Alternaria is particularly concerning due to the ability of fungi of this genus to produce mycotoxins that pose potential health risks. Contamination of processed tomato products has been repeatedly reported in the literature, but little is known about the factors influencing contamination in field-grown processing tomatoes. In this study, we assessed the composition of the epidermal microbiota of processing tomato fruits in relation to Alternaria and mycotoxin contamination levels. Tomato crops exhibiting varying levels of contamination (based on symptom assessment, qPCR and LC-MS/MS analysis) were selected, and both healthy and diseased fruits were sampled. Our results revealed that processing tomatoes can be heavily contaminated with Alternaria mycotoxins at harvest. Visual symptoms were not reliable predictors of toxicological risk: the observed association between Stemphylium abundance and disease severity raises the hypothesis that Stemphylium may contribute to symptoms commonly attributed to Alternaria black spot. Conversely, fruits displaying atypical symptom profiles often contained high levels of Alternaria mycotoxins. Analysis of the tomato skin microbiota using 16S and ITS metabarcoding showed that fruit health status was associated with distinct microbial commu…

title: Estratégias de investimentos e eficiência do mercado de ações.
abstract: In the context of the national economy, part of the income generated is consumed to meet the priorities of individuals and legal entities, while the remainder is saved to cover future needs or risks. More specifically, the saved resources are mainly destined for investments and emergencies. Although not a widespread reality, a portion of the Brazilian population makes medium-term investments, to be used in an intermediate period. This article aims to present which strategies are most used in the country, and what the impact of investing in stocks is on the growth of the wealth of individuals.

title: A Janus Bilayer Portland Cement‐Based Moisture‐Electricity Generator via Hydrogen‐Bonding Network Regulation
abstract: ABSTRACT The ubiquitous interaction between ambient moisture and built environments presents a compelling opportunity for continuous energy harvesting through moisture‐electricity generation (MEG). However, current MEG materials fail to satisfy high‐power demands in buildings because hydrogen bonds, indispensable for the structural integrity of soft carbon‐chain networks, severely restrict water diffusion, and thus bottleneck MEG performance. Hydrated Portland cement, featuring a robust silicate backbone, allows aggressive modulation of the water hydrogen‐bonding network (HBN), emerging as an ideal platform for higher performance. Here, we developed a Portland cement‐based moisture‐electricity generator (CMEG) via a facile asymmetric acid etching strategy, extending MEG to cementitious material systems. The resulting CMEG presents a Janus bilayer architecture with a stark gradient in hygroscopicity across the layers to drive the unidirectional diffusion of water molecules. Mechanistically, the etching process induces the breakage of HBN, which unlocks ultrafast water diffusion throughout the top layer and thus accelerates selective ion transport toward the bottom layer. Remarkably, CMEG delivers an extremely high short‐circuit current density of 723 µA/cm 2 and output power density of 112.5 µW/cm 2 . Furthermore, CMEG demonstrates exceptional scalability, modular integration ca…

Customer satisfaction formation in private tutoring as a paid supplementary education service: A conceptual framework
abstract: As a common type of paid educational service, private tutoring is evaluated not only in terms of the learning support offered but also in terms of how the service is organised and delivered. In the current study, rather than the entire offerings of paid educational services, the focus is specifically on private tutoring. The reason is that, in addition to expecting improvement in academic achievement, the quality of private tutoring will also be influenced by pertinent fees, scheduling types, communication channels, reports on the latest educational progress, assurance from the service provider, and other types of experience. By referring to existing research on private tutoring, supported by relevant theoretical frameworks, including perceived value theory, service quality theory, customer satisfaction theory, and the application of a customer-based stakeholder viewpoint, a review-grounded conceptual framework is proposed in the current study to delineate how customer satisfaction with private tutoring is shaped. In the framework, there are two complementary domains, namely core educational service quality and Service-delivery credibility, with the former concentrating on the levels of learning support, instructional competence, and perceived educational payoff. Meanwhile, in the latter, the focus is on responsiveness, communication clarity, pricing transparency, and organisat…

title: Redes computacionales empresariales para la interconectividad y mejora en la calidad del servicio
abstract: Business computer networks are essential tools for ensuring interconnectivity and improving service quality within modern organizations. Technology companies such as Cisco Systems and TP-Link have developed economic models focused on providing connectivity solutions adapted to different business levels, from small offices to large corporations. Cisco Systems is recognized for its business model based on high-performance enterprise solutions, offering equipment such as switches, routers, firewalls, and network management platforms. Its strategy focuses on innovation, cybersecurity, cloud services, and specialized technical support. Cisco mainly serves medium and large companies that require robust, scalable, and secure infrastructure. In addition, the company integrates subscription and licensing models for advanced management and security services. On the other hand, TP-Link maintains a more affordable economic model aimed at small and medium-sized businesses as well as home users. The company stands out for providing low-cost and easy-to-implement networking devices, including wireless routers, managed switches, and business Wi-Fi systems. Its commercial strategy is based on cost-effectiveness, allowing organizations with limited budgets to improve connectivity without making large investments. Both companies significantly contribute to strengthening technological infrastructu…

title: Work link: A Web-Based Service Marketplace with Automated Booking Management
abstract: WorkLink is a web-based service marketplace that connects service seekers with independent service providers through one centralized application. Informal ways of finding local professionals make it hard to compare service category, experience, location, hourly rate, availability and customer feedback. The proposed system brings these activities into a single workflow: user authentication, provider profile management, service- and city-based discovery, availability display, scheduled booking requests, provider responses, notifications, completion and reviews. It is implemented with Node.js and Express (server and REST API), HTML, CSS and browser-side JavaScript (interface) and SQLite (persistent storage). JSON Web Tokens support authenticated sessions, passwords are protected with bcrypt hashing, and a node-cron task applies configured warning and automatic-rejection rules to unanswered pending bookings. Functional testing covered 16 scenarios across registration, authentication, provider management, filtering, booking transitions, scheduled rejection, notifications, completion, reviews, data retrieval and analytics, and all 16 passed. These are functional outcomes, not production-scale performance measurements. The work demonstrates a lightweight architecture for the basic local-service transaction lifecycle; production deployment would require payment integration, real-time c…

title: OFFICIAL PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL OF FIREFIGHTERS OF THE STATE FIRE SERVICE – BETWEEN THE SUPERIOR’S DISCRETION IN ASSESSMENT AND GUARANTEES OF PROTECTION FOR THE OFFICER
abstract: This article analyses the legal model of official performance appraisal for firefighters in the State Fire Service, with particular emphasis on the relationship between the scope of superiors’ discretion in assessment and the guarantees of legal protection afforded to the officer being appraised. The analysis covers the normative foundations, legal nature and functions of the official performance appraisal, the appraisal criteria and procedure, as well as the measures available for reviewing an issued appraisal. The body of administrative court case law concerning the classification of an official performance appraisal as an internal service act not subject to direct judicial-administrative review is also taken into account. The study indicates that the current model gives superiors a relatively broad scope of discretion in assessment, while firefighters' protection rests primarily on internal mechanisms. This leads to the conclusion that the existing arrangements do not fully balance the service's interests with the need to protect officers against arbitrary assessment. Consequently, de lege ferenda proposals focus, in particular, on clarifying appraisal criteria, strengthening the obligation to provide reasons for an appraisal, extending procedural guarantees, and considering limited judicial review in cases involving appraisals that produce part…

title: Analysis of Service Quality Using a Combination of The Servqual Method and Importance-Performance Analysis at Event Organizer
abstract: Service quality is essential for event organizing companies because participants expect comfortable facilities, accurate information, timely services, and responsive staff. This study evaluates service quality at an anonymized event organizing company and identifies practical priorities for improvement. A quantitative survey was conducted with 104 event participants selected through purposive sampling. Twenty service attributes were assessed across five SERVQUAL dimensions by comparing perceived performance with participant expectations. Importance–Performance Analysis (IPA) was then used to classify attributes into four quadrants, while a Fishbone diagram was applied to explore potential causes of priority service problems. The results showed an average SERVQUAL gap of −0.25, indicating that perceived service performance remained below expectations. Reliability recorded the largest negative gap (−0.32), followed by responsiveness (−0.29), empathy (−0.28), tangibles (−0.26), and assurance (−0.07). IPA identified seven priority attributes: venue comfort, supporting facilities, service clarity, information accuracy, ease of contact, understanding participant needs, and convenient service timing. Fishbone analysis suggested that staffing constraints, unclear task assignments, inconsistent communication procedures, inadequate facilities, and weak post-event evaluation contributed t…

title: Assessment of Strategic Management Practices Influencing Service Delivery in Kenya’s Level Five Public Hospitals
abstract: This study assessed the influence of strategic management practices on service delivery across 16 gazetted Level Five public hospitals in Kenya. Operating within the sub-national healthcare referral system, these institutions encounter persistent service delivery challenges despite adopting strategic management frameworks. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and Strategic Control theories alongside an integrated patient-centred healthcare delivery model, the research employed a quantitative cross-sectional descriptive survey design. Data were gathered from a target population of 160 heads of departments, utilising a sample size of 114 respondents determined via Yamane's formula. Structured questionnaires with Likert-scale items were used for data collection and subsequently analysed using SPSS version 27 through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression models. Descriptive findings showed that strategy formulation had a mean of 4.21 ( ), strategy implementation had a mean of 3.68 ( ), strategy evaluation recorded a mean of 3.75 ( ), and service delivery recorded a mean of 4.29 ( ). Pearson’s correlation analysis showed positive associations between service delivery and strategy formulation ( ), strategy implementation ( ), and strategy evaluation ( ). The regression coefficients indicated that strategy formulation, implementation, and evaluation …

title: 7-Ketolithocholic Acid Attenuates Oxidative Injury and Senescence-Associated Phenotypes in Feline Skeletal Muscle Stromal Cells Through SREBP-Associated Lipid Metabolic Regulation
abstract: Skeletal muscle-derived stromal cells represent a resident stromal population of skeletal muscle and contribute to tissue homeostasis and regeneration. However, the metabolic mechanisms linking oxidative stress and cellular senescence in skeletal muscle stromal cells remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluated the effects of palmitoylethanolamide, conjugated linoleic acid, 7-ketolithocholic acid (7KA), and phenylacetylglycine in an H2O2-induced oxidative injury model (2 mM, 2 h) established using feline skeletal muscle stromal cells (FSMSCs). Among the four compounds, 7KA exhibited the strongest protective activity, significantly improving cell viability from 76.48% in H2O2-treated cells to 90.71 ± 4.89% following 80 μM 7KA treatment, while reducing lactate dehydrogenase release from 146.00 ± 2.60% to 71.62 ± 6.78% (both p < 0.05). Furthermore, 7KA alleviated oxidative damage, inflammatory responses, and senescence-associated phenotypes, reducing MDA levels from 380.05 ± 21.10 to 147.49 ± 34.48 nmol/mg, decreasing TNF-α, MCP-1, IL-6, and IL-8 levels, and increasing NAD+ and ATP levels from 3.12 ± 0.18 to 5.15 ± 0.09 μmol/g and from 11.91 ± 0.12 to 15.12 ± 1.37 μmol/g, respectively (p < 0.05). 7KA also improved mitochondrial membrane potential and reduced senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that 7KA markedly modulated fatty acid meta…

title: Legal Aid and the Maintenance Regulation
abstract: This case note considers the CJEU decision in Winderwill. The case considers an application for modification of maintenance by a creditor in Germany, when the debtor also applied for modification in Sweden. The primary question in the preliminary ruling concerns when a document will be considered an “equivalent document” for the purposes of article 9(a) of the Maintenance Regulation. However, the case also demonstrates that applications made under the Maintenance Regulation can be complex and are not necessarily resolved easily. It provides evidence that legal aid applications made in the context of the Maintenance Regulation are not simple, and can cause delay, even where the creditor is a child utilising the Central Authority system.

title: Co‐Movements of High‐Order Moments and Risk Spillovers in the Time‐Frequency Domain Along the Supply Chains of the US Beef and Pork Industries
abstract: ABSTRACT The present analysis examines the multiscale co‐movements of high‐order moments, namely skewness and kurtosis, across the US beef and pork marketing channels. Monthly farm, wholesale, and retail prices, spanning January 1980 to February 2026, are employed. The results show that in the beef sector, co‐movements in the farm‐wholesale pair are strongly synchronized in medium horizons, with the wholesale leading the upstream transmission of risk to producers. Co‐movements in the beef wholesale‐retail pair are demand‐driven, with the retail level leading volatility dynamics. In the pork sector, the farm‐wholesale pair records significant negative co‐movements in asymmetry, with wholesale taking the leading role in recent years, indicating that crash risk is only weakly transmitted from packers to producers. The pork wholesale‐retail pair reported the weakest co‐movement across all moments and frequencies. To this end, we found that risk spillovers vary between scales and moments and are not uniformly spread across the two supply chains. Patterns depend significantly on both the industry (beef or pork) and the vertical level examined. Results suggest that wholesalers and retailers are likely to have a high degree of leverage over the cattle/hog producers.

title: Evaluating Spectral Preprocessing and Machine Learning for Hyperspectral Estimation of Leaf Photosynthetic Capacity in Subtropical Forests
abstract: Accurate estimation of the maximum carboxylation rate (Vcmax) and maximum electron transport rate (Jmax) is important for improving the representation of photosynthetic capacity in terrestrial carbon-cycle models. Leaf hyperspectral spectroscopy provides a promising approach for estimating these physiological traits, but the effects of spectral preprocessing and modeling strategy on prediction performance remain insufficiently evaluated, particularly across different forest types. In this study, leaf hyperspectral reflectance (400–2400 nm) and gas-exchange measurements were collected from subtropical evergreen needleleaf forest (ENF) and evergreen broadleaf forest (EBF) samples to systematically evaluate the estimation of Vcmax and Jmax using six spectral preprocessing methods and three machine learning algorithms. ENF and EBF showed broadly similar spectral signatures and comparable distributions of Vcmax and Jmax. Across the tested model configurations, derivative-based preprocessing methods generally improved prediction performance, while random forest (RF) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) generally outperformed partial least squares regression (PLSR). Using 99 leaf samples (36 ENF and 63 EBF samples) and internal leave-one-out cross-validation, the highest predictive performance was moderate, with R2 = 0.45 (RMSE = 9.89, MAE = 8.23) for Vcmax and R2 = 0.57 (RMSE = 15…

title: School social workers’ perspectives on parents’ knowledge, involvement, and capacity to prevent sexting among adolescents in South African schools
abstract: Abstract Sexting, including the consensual and non-consensual sharing of sexually explicit images, messages, or content through digital platforms, presents a growing challenge in South African schools, and parents are central to the prevention of adolescents’ digital risks. Although school responses have been the focus of research, limited attention has been given to school social workers’ perspectives on parents’ knowledge of sexting, involvement, and their capacity to support adolescents’ safe use of digital technologies. The aim of the study was to explore South African school social workers’ perceptions of parents’ knowledge, involvement, and capacity to prevent adolescent sexting. The study adopted a qualitative phenomenological research design. A total of thirty-six participants were identified through purposive and snowball sampling. Data were generated through face-to-face and online semi-structured interviews. Data were analysed using Tesch’s eight-step inductive content analysis. Participants reported gaps in parents’ digital literacy, limited supervision, and weak boundaries within the home environment, as well as uncertainty regarding how to discuss online sexual behaviour with adolescents. Participants reported that many parents felt overwhelmed by changing technologies and relied on schools to manage sexting-related issues. The study suggests that parent-targeted …

title: Building Capacity for Equity-Centered Knowledge Translation: Evaluation of Learner’s and Mentor’s Experiences in a Novel Open-Access Training Program
abstract: Knowledge Translation (KT) aims to connect knowledge with action in health and social settings where equity is always relevant. In this article, we share results of a mixed-methods evaluation of the Canadian Coalition for Global Health Research KT Summer Course, offered first as a pilot in 2020. This novel, open-access and equity-centered KT course brought learners and mentors around the world together in an applied learning environment. Evaluation results were overwhelmingly positive, with high levels of satisfaction and transformative impacts on learners’ practice and career trajectories. Situating the course among other exemplars of KT training, we share evaluation results and our responses to it. We highlight how the evaluation informs the evolution of a suite of capacity building initiatives that are creating pathways for practicing equity- and evidence-informed action.

title: In vitro propagation of Dianthus barbatus L. and cytokinin-mediated changes in its phenolic content and antioxidant capacity
abstract: Abstract Background Dianthus barbatus is a valuable ornamental and medicinal species with potential for the production of bioactive compounds, yet information on the integrated effects of plant growth regulators (PGRs) on its in vitro propagation and phytochemical responses remains limited. Thus, the effects of PGR treatments on in vitro seed germination, organogenesis, phytochemical profiles, and antioxidant responses of D. barbatus were evaluated. Results Surface-sterilized seeds for seedling establishment and seedling-derived nodal explants for shoot multiplication were cultured on Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium supplemented with 6-benzylaminopurine (BAP), thidiazuron (TDZ), or 6-(γ,γ-dimethylallylamino)purine riboside (2-iP) at 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 mg L − 1 . The maximum seed germination rate (66.7%) was achieved with 0.25 mg L − 1 BAP. During axillary shoot multiplication, 0.25 mg L − 1 TDZ induced the highest shoot production (11.1 ± 1.3 per explant) and total leaf number (38.3 ± 2.3), whereas PGR-free MS medium produced the longest shoots (3.8 ± 0.9 cm). Multiplied shoots were rooted on MS medium with indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), 4-chlorophenoxyacetic acid (4-CPA), or α-naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA) at 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 mg L − 1 . Rhizogenesis was most effective on PGR-free medium, yielding the highest root number​ (9.6 ± 0.9 per shoot), while 0.25 mg L − 1 IAA stimulated …

title: Numerical and experimental studies on the current capacity of VIPER high temperature superconducting cable
abstract: Abstract Growing demands for superconducting cables with high current density and excellent stability in nuclear fusion, high energy physics, and smart grids have rendered high temperature superconducting (HTS) cables based on REBCO coated conductors a critical technical route for next generation high field magnets. The Vacuum Impregnated Pressurized Roebel (VIPER) cable inherits the advantages of Twisted Stacked-Tape Cable (TSTC) and Cable-in-Conduit Conductor (CICC), constituting a novel HTS conductor architecture with high current carrying capacity and structural stability. To systematically investigate the influence of tape stacking number on the self-field current carrying performance of VIPER cables, three three dimensional electromagnetic models corresponding to 5 slot 8 layer, 5 slot 9 layer, and 5 slot 10 layer configurations were developed and simulated at temperature 77 K using Ansys Maxwel.The results demonstrate that the relative errors between simulated and experimental critical currents for all three configurations are within an acceptable range of 5%. As the number of stacked layers increases, the total current-carrying capacity rises from 3810.8 A (8 layers) to 4156.0 A (9 layers) and 4515.2 A (10 layers), while the inter-slot current distribution deviation decreases from 7.35% to 1.55%. Nevertheless, the self-field superposition effect intensifies, with a maxi…

title: Policy Mechanism Matters: State-Level Pharmacist Prescriptive Authority and Contraception Prescribing
abstract: Abstract Introduction State policies that authorize pharmacists to prescribe contraception could make contraceptive care more accessible in the US. Over half of states have implemented such a policy, either via: collaborative practice agreement (most restrictive), standing order, statewide protocol, or prescriptive authority (least restrictive). Methods We used national prescription claims to measure variation in pharmacist-prescribed contraception by state policy type and by pharmacy affiliation in the thirty-one states that had a relevant policy in place as of 2024. Results We identified a total of 3,447 pharmacists, or 3.3% of all retail pharmacists in the US, prescribing contraception. Pharmacists prescribing contraception were most commonly affiliated with Walmart (17.4%), CVS (15.7%), Rite Aid (10.1%), and Safeway (9.4%). States with prescriptive authority or statewide protocols had significantly higher rates of pharmacist-prescribed contraception (11.6% and 5.9% of retail pharmacists, respectively), compared with states with standing orders (1.0%) or collaborative practice agreements (2.3%). Conclusion This study found that the type of policy mechanism authorizing pharmacists to prescribe contraception plays a key role in determining uptake of this practice. State policies must be considered as part of a broader set of factors, including retail pharmacies’ policies, phar…

title: Microscopic diffusion mechanism of linezolid in carbon-based nanoporous materials: a molecular dynamics simulation study
abstract: Introduction Graphene aerogels are promising antibiotic delivery carriers owing to their ultralow density, hierarchical porous architecture, and high specific surface area. However, molecular transport within their nanoscale confined spaces remains poorly understood, limiting the rational design of carriers with controllable release performance. This study investigated linezolid diffusion within graphene aerogel-like confined structures. Methods All-atom molecular dynamics simulations using the OPLS-AA force field were performed with a solvent-free model containing more than 10,000 atoms. Randomly overlapping graphene sheets were used to represent the disordered porous framework. A controlled-variable approach was adopted to quantify the independent effects of temperature (240–380 K), carrier dosage (20–150 graphene sheets), and drug loading (1,000–5,832 molecules) on diffusion coefficients. Grid-based pore-size analysis was used to examine the relationship between local pore geometry and molecular transport. Results Increasing temperature enhanced diffusion nonlinearly over the investigated range. At fixed drug loading, increasing carrier dosage enlarged the mean local pore size from 3.97 to 7.32 Å and increased the diffusion coefficient overall, reaching 3.120 × 1 0 ‐ 12 m 2 / s . Increasing drug loading shifted the calculated pore-size distribution toward smaller local voids…

title: Design and experimental validation of a passive thermal-displacement compensation module for a compliant parallel mechanism
abstract: To address the degradation of motion accuracy in compliant parallel mechanisms caused by temperature variations, this study proposes a passive temperature-compensation module design method based on equivalent compliance matrix incorporating thermal effects. Thermally induced deformation is introduced into the compliance formulation in an equivalent manner, and design relationships are established among the thermal deformation characteristics, compensation directions, required compensation, and structural parameters of the compensation module. This extends thermal deformation modeling toward structure-level error suppression. A temperature-compensation module is designed and integrated into a 4-PPSP compliant parallel mechanism, and its 2R1T motion mode is theoretically and experimentally investigated. Under the controlled temperature differences considered, the proposed compensation reduces the thermally induced displacement error along the z -axis by 70.41% and the thermally induced angular errors about the x - and y -axes by approximately 65.6%, while the output displacement errors in all directions remain below 6%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method under the present experimental conditions and provide a new design approach for structure-level passive suppression of thermally induced errors in compliant parallel mechanisms.

title: Mechanism of dynamic rock fragmentation by electrohydraulic shock waves under multiphysics coupling
abstract: In response to the engineering demand for efficient fragmentation of deep hard rock, as well as the critical industrial challenges of low rock-breaking efficiency, high operational cost, and severe wear of drilling tools associated with traditional mechanical drilling, this paper focuses on electrohydraulic shock wave rock fragmentation (also known as electrohydraulic fragmentation) technology. Aiming at the limitation of existing studies that lack a dynamic evolution model integrating liquid electrical breakdown and rock-fragmentation process, a multiphysics numerical model coupling circuit field, current field, acoustic field, solid mechanics field, and dynamic damage field was developed. The model introduces an “electrical damage” variable to describe the evolution process of the liquid-medium breakdown, establishes a rock elastobrittle dynamic damage constitutive model considering strain-rate effects, and quantitatively characterizes rock mesoscopic heterogeneity through a Weibull distribution, enabling a complete reproduction of the nanosecond-scale dynamic process of electrohydraulic shock wave rock fragmentation. Based on the established multiphysics coupled model, this study clarifies the three-stage evolution law of plasma channels and the hysteretic propagation characteristics of induced shock waves, quantifies the regulatory effect of pulse parameters on liquid elect…

title: Theoretical Insights into Cosolvent Effects in PET Glycolysis: A Multiscale Transport-Activation Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Despite extensive advances in polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization, the molecular-level mechanisms by which solvents and cosolvents regulate PET swelling, transport, and bond cleavage remain insufficiently understood. Herein, an integrated molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) calculation was employed to systematically elucidate the roles of eight representative cosolvents─tetrahydrofuran (THF), 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (M-THF), 1,3-dioxolane (DOL), δ-valerolactone (DVL), cyclopentanone (CP), ethylene glycol (EG), anisole (AS), and benzyl alcohol (BnOH)─in PET solvation and degradation-related environments. Analyses of free-volume evolution, diffusion behavior, and electronic structure-derived descriptors capturing local polarity and orbital localization reveal pronounced solvent-dependent differences in chain relaxation, molecular mobility, and electronic activation pathways. Ether- and carbonyl-containing cosolvents primarily promote PET swelling and molecular transport by modulating local polarity and chain relaxation, whereas the protic cosolvent benzyl alcohol forms a dynamically reconfigurable, ethylene glycol-coupled hydrogen-bond network that enhances molecular mobility and stabilizes reactive oxyanion/transition-state structures. These distinct interaction modes give rise to computed differences in activation barriers, which e…

title: Experimental Investigation of Macroscopic–Mesoscopic Mechanical Responses and Combined Modification Mechanism of Polymer-Fiber Modified Coal Gangue-Based Shotcrete
abstract: Abstract To address the insufficient workability, pronounced brittleness, and limited crack resistance of coal gangue-based shotcrete, basalt fiber (BF) and styrene–butadiene rubber latex (SBR) were selected for combined modification. A Box–Behnken response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to design the experiments, with BF volume fraction (0.1–0.5%), BF length (6–18 mm), and SBR content (5–15%) selected as the influencing factors. Quadratic regression models were established for slump, rebound rate, 28 day uniaxial compressive strength (UCS), and 28 day splitting tensile strength (STS), and the optimal mixture proportion was obtained through multiobjective optimization. X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) were employed to elucidate the combined modification mechanism, including phase composition, microscopic morphology, chemical structure, and pore characteristics. The results demonstrated that all response surface models exhibited high fitting accuracy (with R2 > 0.98) and excellent predictive capability. BF volume fraction was identified as the most significant factor affecting the four investigated performance indicators, followed by BF length and SBR content. With increasing BF volume fraction and length,…

title: Ash Formation in Pulverized Biomass Combustion: How Evidence, Mechanism and Model Uncertainty Propagate to Deposit Risk
abstract: Pulverized biomass combustion offers a practical route to reduce fossil CO2 emissions while retaining existing coal-fired infrastructure, but its deployment is constrained by ash-related problems—slagging, fouling, high-temperature corrosion, SCR catalyst deactivation, and fine-particle emissions. These problems originate from the high mobility of alkali metals, chlorine, and sulfur in biomass fuels: unlike coal minerals, a considerable fraction of these elements is released into the gas phase and then undergoes homogeneous and heterogeneous reactions, nucleation, condensation, and sulfation. Ash behavior is consequently governed not by bulk ash content alone, but by the occurrence of forms of inorganic elements, their release pathways, the flue-gas cooling history, and the transformation of the resulting particles. This review integrates laboratory, pilot-scale, and industrial evidence to describe the formation of coarse fly ash and submicron particles (PM1), the coupling between the two particle populations through alkali-vapor uptake, and the effects of fuel properties, combustion atmosphere, cooling rate, and mineral additives. Thermodynamic, kinetic-reactor, aerosol-population, and CFD-coupled models are compared in terms of applicability and limitations. Prediction remains limited by fuel variability, uncertain kinetic parameters, and insufficient full-scale validation; p…

title: Mechanism of pressure on the etching precision of polymer nanostructured surfaces
abstract: Abstract Polymer nanostructures have been found extensive applications in fields such as integrated circuits and intelligent sensing. However, existing reactive ion etching (RIE) technologies still face challenges in achieving high precision and uniformity control. This paper systematically investigates the critical role of chamber pressure in O 2 /Ar RIE, revealing its profound influence on the morphology, etching rate, and uniformity of spherical-curved nanostructures. Experimental results demonstrate that chamber pressure is a critical parameter for modulating etching behavior: at 1–3 Pa, etching proceeds slowly but results in rough structures, making it suitable for constructing hierarchical micro/nanostructures; the 4–6 Pa range offers optimal etching uniformity, enabling high-precision morphological control; while pressures >7 Pa dramatically accelerate the etching rate, facilitating efficient material removal. Through macroscopic plasma fluid simulations, ion transport kinetics diagnostics, and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses, it is revealed that chamber pressure acts as a critical dial to modulate the competitive synergy between physical sputtering and chemical oxidation. The comprehensive diagnostics successfully unveil the underlying physics driving the morphological transition from rough anisotropic ‘flying-saucers’ to smooth isotropic nanospheres. This stu…

title: Risk Assessment for Urban eVTOL Operations and Air-Ground Cooperative Hazard Avoidance Mechanism
abstract: Abstract This study develops an eight-indicator framework for describing low-altitude operational risk and a candidate air-ground response architecture. The evidence is drawn from three distinct supplementary datasets: 1,000 source-labelled sortie records (772 retained after exposure and duration quality control; 740 operational and 32 simulated), a trajectory/alert slice aggregated to 123 occupied 500 m × 500 m by 5-min cells, and 6,079 occupied 5-min windows from 55 days of operational records. These datasets are analysed separately. In the 55-day series, the adjusted negative-binomial model estimated a rate ratio of 3.32 per one-level increase in mean sortie risk score (95% CI 3.13–3.52), while density had an independent rate ratio of 1.11 (95% CI 1.07–1.14). In the 700-cell trajectory pipeline, the score–alert association was not statistically distinguishable from unity (RR 1.0026 per point, 95% CI 0.9957–1.0095; p = 0.464). Near-perfect rolling-window AUCs were attributable to the close constructional dependence between sortie risk scores and event records and are not interpreted as independent predictive validation. Because the observations are low-altitude UAV operations and simulation records rather than commercial passenger eVTOL flights, the findings support a pilot assessment workflow, not eVTOL accident-risk estimates or validated operational thresholds.

title: Carbon Nitride-Modified Zr/SBA-15: A Highly Efficient Catalyst for Reductive Etherification of Furfural to Isopropyl Furfuryl Ether
abstract: Abstract The direct conversion of biomass-derived furfural (FUR) into isopropyl furfuryl ether (IPFE) via one-pot reductive etherification is a sustainable and economical route. However, this process remains challenging due to the need for bifunctional catalysts with balanced Lewis and Brønsted acid sites. In this work, a series of carbon nitride (CN)-modified Zr/SBA-15 catalysts (ZrxCNy/SBA-15) were synthesized by a simple impregnation method and evaluated for the reductive etherification of FUR using isopropanol as both the solvent and the hydrogen donor. The introduction of CN significantly enhanced the catalytic performance by increasing the dispersion of Zr species, enriching Lewis acid sites (LAS), and introducing Lewis base sites (LBS) from nitrogen functionalities. The optimized Zr4.4CN3.6/SBA-15 catalyst achieved a remarkable IPFE yield of 91.6% under mild conditions, substantially outperforming the CN-free counterpart (14.9% IPFE yield). By optimizing the reaction conditions, a 94.2% FUR conversion and a 92.7% selectivity to IPFE were achieved at 150 °C within only 20 min, corresponding to a productivity of 52.5 mmol·g–1·h–1, which was significantly superior to the results reported in the literature. title: Forecasting radial head arthroplasty in Germany through 2045
abstract: Abstract In this study, we aim to estimate the expected growth in radial head arthroplasties (RA) in Germany through 2045. To do this, autoregressive integrated moving-average (ARIMA), Error-Trend-Seasonality (ETS), and Poisson models were used to forecast trends in RA. Official data on demographics and procedures were used, provided by the Federal Statistical Office of Germany (Statistisches Bundesamt). The models project an increase in the number of radial head arthroplasties through 2045. Specifically, the incidence rate is expected to increase by around 80% to 2.56 per 100,000 inhabitants by then. The projected total number of RA in 2045 is 2,098. Based on our projections, this increase is mainly driven by a rising number of male and female patients aged 65 years and older, leading to a 2.1-fold increase in procedures performed for these patients in 2045 compared with 2023. In total, radial head arthroplasties are projected to be performed approximately three times more often in women than in men, corresponding to a projected total number of 1,574 radial head arthroplasties for women and 524 for men in 2045. Our results emphasize the need to improve implant development, surgical expertise, and training in this specific procedure.

Mid-field MRI with cochlear implants: a healthy volunteer study of magnet displacement, pressure perception, and temporal bone imaging
abstract: Abstract Purpose We hypothesised that 0.55T MRI would reduce magnet displacement risk and pressure perception compared to 1.5T MRI in healthy volunteers with bandaged cochlear implants (CIs) containing axial or rotating diametric magnets, while maintaining temporal bone image interpretability. Methods Ten healthy volunteers were bandaged with CIs (5 axial magnet; 5 rotating diametric magnet) and underwent consecutive 0.55T and 1.5T MRI sessions. Pressure perception was assessed using a visual analogue scale and magnet displacement was evaluated. Optimised 2D T2-weighted fast spin echo (2D T2-FSE) and constructive interference in steady state (CISS) temporal bone sequences were acquired at both field strengths in seven participants. Diagnostic confidence, artefactual degradation, and distances from CI-related artefact to anatomical structures were assessed. CI magnet translational and torque force were measured. Paired ordinal data were analysed using Wilcoxon signed-rank and Bland–Altman analysed agreement of distances. Results Axial CI magnets were displaced after 1.5T MRI in 4/5 participants but not 0.55T ( p = 0.04) with corresponding torque measured as 0.133 v 0.062 Nm. Rotating diametric magnets showed no displacement at either 1.5T or 0.55T with similar torque measurements at both field strengths (0.046 v 0.044 Nm). Pressure perception did not differ between MRI systems. …

title: Multi-Horizon AQI Forecasting Through the Heterogeneous Fusion of a Temporal Convolutional Network and a Graph-Conditioned Causal Transformer
abstract: Recent station observations provide a useful basis for air quality index (AQI) forecasting, whereas regional measurements may supply additional context at longer forecast leads. In this study, the forecasts of an independently trained temporal convolutional network (TCN) and a graph-conditioned causal transformer (Graph-CT) are combined. Both use the same input window of 24 h to predict all the hourly leads from 1 to 24 h, and their corresponding outputs are averaged. Air-quality records from 26 stations in the Chengdu–Chongqing economic circle are reconstructed on a common hourly grid, with causal input filling and evaluation restricted to observed targets. Learning rates and training durations are selected on 2021 data, followed by retrospective evaluation on the previously inspected 2022 benchmark. Across five runs, equal fusion achieves a pooled root mean square error (RMSE) of 18.036 ± 0.103 AQI, compared with 19.491 ± 0.063 for TCN, 18.284 ± 0.140 for Graph-CT, 19.413 ± 0.174 for iTransformer, and 19.043 ± 0.455 for Graph WaveNet under the common task. The paired interval includes zero, leaving the advantage over a two-member Graph-CT ensemble unresolved. Validation calibration slightly decreases the RMSE but increases the mean absolute error (MAE), and removing the transformer branch improves the evaluated configuration. Forecast averaging is therefore useful on this ben…

title: Housing Price Pressure and Employee Lawsuits: Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This study explores how rising housing prices affect employee–employer conflict through the lens of employee lawsuits. Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2013 to 2019, we find that the likelihood of employee lawsuits against a firm increases with housing prices in the city where the firm is located. To establish causality, we employ a staggered difference‐in‐differences approach based on the implementation of home purchase restriction policies designed to curb housing price growth, and we also use land supply as an instrument for housing prices. Mechanism and cross‐sectional analyses show that psychological pressure can be the key mechanism driving employee lawsuits. Additional analyses demonstrate that housing price pressure leads to substantiated employee lawsuits instead of vexatious lawsuits. Also, it does not significantly increase other types of litigation, indicating that the psychological pressure primarily affects internal labor relations rather than external stakeholder disputes. These findings indicate that external cost‐of‐living pressures can erode workplace relations and escalate labor conflict. Overall, our paper provides novel evidence on how macroeconomic housing market conditions shape employee–employer dynamics and labor litigation.

title: Forecasting the Cost of the Basic Family Food Basket in the Districts of Panama and San Miguelito: A Comparative Analysis of Statistical and Machine Learning Models
abstract: Forecasting food costs is an important tool for food security planning and management. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the performance of statistical and machine learning models for forecasting the monthly cost of the Basic Family Food Basket (BFFB) in Panama and San Miguelito. Monthly data from 2009 to 2024 were chronologically divided into training and test sets. A Naïve model was used as a benchmark, while ARIMA, Holt, Random Forest and XGBoost models were evaluated using MAE, RMSE and MAPE. The main evaluation used a fixed-origin multi-step forecasting scheme, complemented by a rolling-origin evaluation. Predictive accuracy was also assessed using the Diebold–Mariano test with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Random Forest yielded the lowest test-set errors (MAE = 13.82, RMSE = 17.23, MAPE = 3.92%), followed by XGBoost (MAE = 15.84, RMSE = 18.14, MAPE = 4.53%). The rolling-origin evaluation also showed favorable performance for both machine learning models, while the Diebold–Mariano test identified statistically significant differences in four of the ten pairwise comparisons based on the Holm p-values, all involving XGBoost. These results highlight the potential of machine learning models for BFFB cost forecasting and support their usefulness as tools for food security-related monitoring and planning.

title: Semantic complexity estimation and price-based multi-agent negotiation reduce tail latency and energy in edge-cloud generative inference
abstract: Abstract Serving large language models across mobile devices and cloud servers is hard because the cost of a generative query cannot be read off its input: a short prompt may trigger thousands of decoding steps. Schedulers therefore commit resources before knowing what a query will cost, and in a shared network many congest one server at once. In MAGS, each device runs a small probe that forecasts a query’s token count and generation entropy before decoding begins, then bids for cloud capacity against a congestion price broadcast by the server, selecting its per-token privacy parameter in the same bid under a metric differential privacy mechanism with explicit clipping. Two design choices follow from measurement. Splicing an 8B model’s lower layers into a 70B model’s upper layers destroys accuracy even with a trained adapter (24.7% versus 82.4% Pass@1 on GSM8K), so activation exchange stays within one model and the larger model is reached by prompt-level offload; and because migrating a key-value cache costs between 2.0 and 16.0 MB per decoder layer, the partition is fixed at prefill. Randomising the packet header cuts an eavesdropper’s identification of the source corpus from 71.1 to 24.7%. Across ten seeds MAGS lowers 99th-percentile latency by 17.1% and energy per token by 13.6% against a reactive PPO baseline given identical observations, and raises throughput by 20.7%; har…

title: An Ultra-Short-Term Probabilistic Load Forecasting Method Based on Joint Distribution Modeling
abstract: Ultra-short-term probabilistic load forecasting is of great significance for improving the safety and economy of the operation of new power systems. To address the problem that existing methods rarely focus on the dependence relationship between load forecast errors and the fluctuation characteristics of forecast output series, this paper proposes an ultra-short-term probabilistic load forecasting method based on joint distribution modeling. First, the Transformer model is used to perform high-precision point forecasting on historical load series, providing a reliable basis for subsequent uncertainty analysis. Second, based on an autoencoder, the forecast load series is reconstructed, and the reconstruction error is used as a deep fluctuation feature. The number of volatility patterns is determined through clustering-validity analysis, and the load scenarios are consequently divided into two representative fluctuation patterns, revealing the intrinsic relationship between the forecast-error distribution and load dynamic characteristics. Subsequently, for each pattern, a joint probability distribution model of load point forecast values and forecast errors is constructed separately; the Copula function is introduced to fit their dependence structure; the conditional error distribution is generated through inverse transformation; and finally, probabilistic prediction intervals ar…

title: An Interpretable and Privacy-Aware Machine Intelligence Framework for Accurate Disease Prediction using Electronic Health Data
abstract: The development of EHDs has completely changed healthcare operations through simplification of the process of using patient data to diagnose and provide appropriate treatment. Some success has already been seen within this field of research, although it is challenging to implement MI models in practical applications. The limitations of current work illustrate the necessity of having a unified MI approach which would guarantee the clinical appropriateness, transparency, privacy, and usability of this system. The goal of the research paper under consideration is to propose a three-stage process to design an MI framework for disease prediction that will be understandable and preserve personal data. The first step is to obtain EHD from many different places, some of which are organized and others of which are not. After that, the data are preprocessed, features are extracted, and finally, the data are anonymized. The next step is to train and evaluate different Machine Learning (ML) models, like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memories (LSTM), and others. An additional Explainable AI (XAI) layer is introduced into the analysis to help comprehend the findings. The next step of the research, which will happen in Phase 3 of the study, is cross-demographic validation and pilot test of the IPAMI Framework in the clinical environment. This research will bring improve…
