title: Risk Prediction for Heart Failure in Patients with Cancer: Current Models and Future Directions
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review: Cancer survivors have an elevated risk for developing heart failure due to prior chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and other overlapping co-morbid conditions. With the advancement in cancer treatment, there is an increasing number of survivors who are at an even higher risk of developing heart failure. There is a growing need for heart failure specific risk prediction models in this population to facilitate early diagnosis and timely management. This review aims to summarize most recent findings on heart failure risk prediction among patients with history of cancer. Recent findings: Current risk prediction models focus on heart failure risk at the time of cancer treatment and shortly thereafter. There is limited data on heart failure risk among long term survivors. Graphical Abstract Central Figure: Approach in determining heart failure risk before, during, and, after cancer treatment

title: District-level cotton yield prediction using temporal trends and climate covariates in Telangana, India (1998–2019)
abstract: District-level cotton yield combines long-term technological change with shorter-term variation associated with climate, management, pests and measurement error. We evaluated trend-assisted reconstruction of observed cotton lint yield for 6 Telangana districts from 1998–2019 (132 district-year observations). Daily India Meteorological Department (IMD) rainfall and temperature series were rebuilt into June–September rainfall totals and mean temperature. September-ending standardised precipitation index (SPI-3) was calibrated separately for each district from July–September rainfall using a zero-adjusted two-parameter gamma distribution over 1951–2019. Standardised precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI) was excluded because the previously supplied approximation did not follow a recognised SPEI procedure. Nine machine-learning models predicted deviations from district-specific yield trends; raw yield was reconstructed by adding the predicted deviation to the trend. Under retrospective conditional leave-one-district-out validation (LODO), Extra Trees achieved pooled raw-yield R² = 0.531, mean district raw-yield R² = 0.405 ± 0.139 and root mean square error (RMSE) = 0.891 quintals per hectare (q/ha). The trend-only baseline already achieved pooled raw-yield R² = 0.514 and RMSE = 0.906 q/ha, so Extra Trees improved squared-error performance by only 3.3 %. Residual-scale R² was…

title: The Use of Phase Change Materials in Ground Source Heat Pump Applications: Research Review and Future Opportunities
abstract: This paper provides a critical review of the existing technical literature on various methods for integrating phase change materials (PCMs) into ground source heat pump (GSHP) systems. It identifies the main barriers and challenges associated with the proposed methods, as well as proposes viable ways to overcome them. The methods for integrating PCMs into GSHPs are grouped into five categories: (1) PCM incorporated into GHE backfill or grout; (2) PCM used in thermal storage tanks coupled to GSHP systems; (3) PCM incorporated into heat-transfer fluid as microencapsulated or related PCM slurries; (4) PCM incorporated into energy geo-structures; and (5) PCM incorporated into building envelopes. The outcomes of this critical review highlight that utilising PCMs in backfill materials around ground heat exchangers (GHEs) enhances thermal performance, regulates soil temperature, and reduces the need for large ground space, though challenges such as low thermal conductivity and potential leakage remain. PCM storage tanks offer energy efficiency benefits, but their cost-effectiveness and long-term performance have yet to be addressed. The use of PCM fluids in GSHP applications is still limited, facing issues such as tube clogging and viscosity-related pressure drops. Integrating PCMs into energy geo-structures shows potential for improved heat transfer efficiency and reduced thermal str…

title: Persistent Acid Mine Drainage and Iron-Associated Arsenic Storage at the Pintor Mine, Portugal: Historical Evidence for Rehabilitation
abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) produces iron (Fe)-rich precipitates that retain arsenic (As), forming contaminant stores susceptible to disturbance during mine rehabilitation. We re-examined aqueous As partitioning and solid-phase geochemical evidence from a 1996–1998 investigation at the abandoned Pintor W–As mine, Portugal. During two 1996 sampling campaigns, adit drainage had pH 3.1–3.9 and operationally dissolved As concentrations of 1126–2208 µg L−1. These concentrations decreased by 99.5–99.8% over 1.8 km, but corresponding changes in As loads could not be determined without concurrent flow measurements. Streambed coatings contained 2.9–4.0 times more As than paired sediments, and an Fe-rich outlet crust had 3.85% aqua regia-extractable As. Dark-oxalate extraction accounted for 48–82% of recovered As across the analysed solids. The concentration gradient coincided with As enrichment in Fe-rich deposits, consistent with Fe-associated retention. Later investigations commissioned by Empresa de Desenvolvimento Mineiro, S.A. (EDM) confirmed that acidic, As-bearing drainage remained present in 2007 and 2022–2024. The historical evidence identifies priorities for pre-intervention characterisation of As-bearing deposits, monitoring particulate As export during excavation, evaluating dissolved and particulate As loads through the proposed treatment system, and assessing As accumulation …

title: A review of battery energy storage peak-shaving dispatch strategies: operational performance and battery degradation
abstract: The substantial proportion of renewables connected to the grid and the continuously widening peak-to-valley load difference is the reason for placing significant pressure on peak-shaving in power systems. Battery energy storage systems have become a key enabling technology for peak shaving and valley filling because of their fast response times and flexible deployment. Existing study has concentrated mainly on short-term peak-shaving performance and operational economics. Nevertheless, the interaction among cycle aging, calendar aging, dynamic changes in State of Health (SOH), and dispatch strategies has received insufficient attention. Furthermore, research on degradation models, evaluation metrics and parameter settings lacks consistency. This paper summarizes four mainstream control strategies for peak-shaving dispatch of battery energy storage systems—ranging from threshold control and time-of-use pricing to predictive optimization and intelligent dispatch—and summarizes the evolutionary logic and operational characteristics of each technology. Based on representative studies, this paper carries out a comparative analysis in terms of operational performance and battery degradation. The results show that existing methods have not yet established a consistent evaluation and optimization framework that balances peak-shaving performance, battery lifespan, and full-life-cycle ec…

title: Comparative Life Cycle Assessment of Spodumene Processing Routes for Battery Grade Lithium Hydroxide Production in Australia, China and Finland
abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for lithium-ion batteries has intensified the need for sustainable and resilient supply chains for battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM). This study presents a cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of three hard-rock spodumene-based LHM supply routes: the conventional Australian–Chinese route (BASE), integrated Australian production (I-AUS), and integrated European production in Finland (I-FIN). The functional unit is 1 kg of battery-grade LiOH·H₂O at the refinery gate. Fifteen environmental impact categories were assessed, with emphasis on acidification, eutrophication, global warming, land use, freshwater consumption, and cumulative energy demand. I-FIN exhibits the lowest impacts across all categories, with a Global Warming Potential (GWP) of 10.21 kg CO₂-eq/FU, 22% and 34% lower than I-AUS and BASE, respectively. Compared with BASE, I-FIN reduces Freshwater Consumption (FWC) and Cumulative Energy Demand (CED) by 38% and 37%, respectively. Conversion/refining is the main environmental hotspot, contributing approximately 40–45% across most categories. Monte Carlo analysis indicates low uncertainty. Sensitivity analysis identifies ore grade, beneficiation recovery, and thermal-energy supply as key parameters, with lower-carbon thermal energy reducing GWP by up to 16%. Overall, integrated regional production, efficient beneficiati…

Design, Validation, and Early In Vivo Testing of an Electric Bioreactor for Conditioning of Plant-Based Vascular Grafts
abstract: Small-diameter vascular grafts remain limited by thrombosis, incomplete endothelialization, and insufficient cellular organization. Plant-based vascular grafts are an emerging scaffold platform that uses decellularized plant microarchitecture and cellulose-rich matrices, but their translation requires controlled pre-implant conditioning strategies that organize seeded endothelium without compromising cell viability. Here, we developed and evaluated a model-informed electric-perfusion bioreactor for conditioning endothelialized plant-based vascular grafts. Multilayer grafts were fabricated from decellularized leatherleaf scaffolds, characterized by sequential gravimetric fractionation and qualitative gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, and conditioned in a custom parallel-plate electric-field chamber that supports electrical stimulation, luminal perfusion, or combined electric-perfusion conditioning. Analytical electric-field modeling was used to estimate local graft-region exposure and guide selection of biologically tolerated stimulation conditions. A 24 h live/dead screen identified 0 to 70 V/m as a biologically tolerated range using a study-defined 90% viability screening criterion; normalized viability fell below this threshold at 80 and 90 V/m, with a sharp decrease to 51% at 100 V/m. Within this range, electrical stimulation, flow conditioning, and combined electric-per…

title: Exploring the Design Space for Drivers’ In-Vehicle Experience in Automated Vehicles
abstract: As automated vehicles (AVs) accumulate functions and information layers, integrating and orchestrating drivers’ in-vehicle experiences remain insufficiently understood design challenges. This study examines sensory, cognitive, hedonic, and social aspects of in-vehicle experience and how experiential values, functions, and interactions are linked over time. We conducted a systematic literature review of 128 papers and studied 27 AV owners using UX Curve elicitation and semi-structured interviews. Based on interview coding and UX Curve ratings, we propose a conceptual framework organizing ten experiential value dimensions across four experience phases: anticipation, familiarization, functional dependence, and practice & meaning transformation. These dimensions include aesthetic pleasure, comfort, efficiency, safety & security, economic sustainability, novelty, flexibility & control, emotional management, relatedness, and identity. We further derive five experience design patterns and articulate an experience-driven design space through four generative charts for future human–vehicle interaction (HVI) design exploration.

title: Possibilities of Using Solar Photovoltaics and Electric Batteries in Agricultural Greenhouses in The Island of Crete, Greece
abstract: Mitigation of the global environmental challenge of climate change requires the elimination of carbon emissions. Agricultural greenhouses are energy intensive production systems based mainly on fossil fuels. However, several renewable energy technologies are reliable and cost-effective and they could be used in them for heat and power generation. The possibility of using a solar photovoltaic and a battery storage system meeting the electricity demand in a grid-connected greenhouse in Crete, Greece which already uses locally produced solid biomass to cover the heat demand has been investigated. It has been estimated that the use of a solar photovoltaic system with nominal power 31.29 kWp generating 48,500 kWh/year can meet the annual power demand in an existing greenhouse with covered surface 3,300 m2 in Crete. The cost of the solar photovoltaic system is estimated at 40,000 €. The capacity of Lithium-ion batteries for achieving one day power autonomy in the greenhouse has been estimated at 147.64 kWh while their cost is estimated at 63,333 €. The combined use of a solar photovoltaic system meeting the electricity demand and solid biomass meeting the heat demand results in a net-zero emissions greenhouse. Both renewable energy technologies are mature and economically attractive and they are currently used in Crete in many sectors. The current work indicates that decarbonization …

title: Deep Learning-Based Optimization of Bionic Cooling Ducts for Heavy-Duty Vehicle Electric Drive Systems
abstract: Liquid cooling has become a predominant method for electric motor thermal management due to its superior heat transfer coefficient. However, conventional cooling channel designs often struggle to achieve an optimal balance between thermal dissipation performance and pressure loss. Inspired by the streamlined morphological features of diving beetles, this paper proposes a novel bionic cooling channel design. By extracting the hydrodynamic profile of the diving beetle’s body, a series of bionic diving beetle-inspired spoiler tubes were designed and integrated into the cooling ducts to optimize flow patterns. A deep learning-based framework was established to correlate these bionic geometric parameters with the thermal–hydraulic performance of the motor. The results demonstrate that the developed ANN model achieves an average R2 of 0.95 across the three output parameters, indicating high predictive accuracy. Compared to traditional structures, the optimized biomimetic channel yielded a 16.09% reduction in pressure drop relative to the conventional reference channel at the same flow rate. Furthermore, under real-vehicle operating conditions, the maximum winding temperature of OBDBS was comparable to that of IBDBS, while the cooling-channel pressure drop was reduced by 7.34%. This study demonstrates that the integration of bionic morphological principles with the GA-ANN-NSGA-II mult…

abstract: LIBRAS (Língua Brasileira de Sinais) estrutura-se como a ponte essencial na efetivação da inclusão social, aliada ao desenvolvimento cognitivo do Surdo, além de fomentar um ambiente de comunicação interativa por aproximação e vivencias educativas em pares. title: Annular Finite‐Time Stochastic H∞ Control for Singular Switching Markov Jump Systems Subject to Wiener Process: A Dual Asynchronous Control Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates annular finite‐time stochastic control for singular switching Markov jump systems (SSMJSs) subject to the Wiener process by resorting to a dual asynchronous control scheme. In view of the impact of mode detection delay and incomplete information transmission, the double asynchronous controller consisting of switching signal asynchrony and stochastic jumping mode asynchrony is designed, which can more accurately characterize the mode mismatch between the operating subsystem and the controller. By combining the mode‐dependent stochastic double‐index Lyapunov function, the mode‐dependent average dwell‐time (MDADT) technique, and the hidden Markov model (HMM) approach, sufficient conditions are first proposed to ensure that the underlying systems carry out annular finite‐time admissibility (AFTA) with a prescribed performance level. Furthermore, appropriate auxiliary variable matrices are introduced to effectively decouple controller gains from Lyapunov matrices, and the asynchronous controllers are thereby successfully obtained by means of strict linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Finally, a simulation example of the oil catalytic cracking process (OCCP) is given to verify the correctness of the obtained results.

Effectiveness of Phonics-Based Gamification as A Low-Technology Teaching Strategy for Kindergarten Reading Development
abstract: This study determined the effectiveness of using phonics-based gamification as a low-technology-based teaching strategy to enhance reading instruction among kindergarten students at Marigondon Elementary School, Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu, during the School Year 2026–2027. It utilized a quasi-experimental research design, specifically the Non-Equivalent Control Group Pretest-Posttest Design, involving two intact Kindergarten classes with 25 learners each. The control group received traditional phonics instruction, while the experimental group participated in phonics-based gamification activities. A researcher-developed Phonemic Awareness Development Assessment Tool measured learners' skills across six phonemic awareness competencies before and after the intervention. Data were analyzed using frequency counts, percentages, means, standard deviations, and an independent-samples t-test at the 0.05 significance level. Pretest results showed that all learners in both groups were classified at the Beginning level across all six skills. Posttest results showed that the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group, leading to the rejection of the null hypothesis. Learners also responded positively to the gamification activities, expressing enjoyment, active participation, and motivation to learn. Based on these findings, the study developed a Phonemic Awareness Lesson Guid…

title: Precipitation data fusion method incorporating local structural enhancement strategy
abstract: Abstract Precipitation data fusion combines gauge observations with spatially continuous satellite products to improve precipitation estimation. However, representing local precipitation patterns remains challenging in regions with complex terrain and sparse gauge networks. This study proposes a local structural enhancement-based precipitation data fusion (LSE-PDF) framework. First, a local structural enhancement and virtual station generation (LSE-VS) module applies weights derived from a two-dimensional Pascal’s array to emphasize the central region of satellite precipitation patches. An adaptive spatial attention mechanism further adjusts the feature weights. A convolutional neural network coupled with long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) then integrates the enhanced spatial features with station time series to generate virtual enhanced stations. Second, collaborative Yang-ChiZhong interpolation combines virtual and observed stations with satellite precipitation data to produce continuous precipitation fields. The framework was evaluated in Shandong Province and a mountainous region of Southwest China. The three experimental scenarios contained 1,308, 109, and 32 observations, respectively. LSE-VS achieved root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 42.6696, 8.3630, and 9.7043 mm and mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 19.0572, 5.3566, and 8.6750 mm. These errors were lower than those of the…

title: Regional Distribution, Virulence Phenotype Identification and Resistant Cultivar Deployment Strategy of Soybean Cyst Nematode in China
abstract: Soybean cyst nematode (SCN, Heterodera glycines Ichinohe) is the most destructive soil-borne pathogen of soybean worldwide. This study elucidated the distribution, population density dynamics, virulence diversity, and economic impact of SCN across China, with systematic monitoring in Inner Mongolia and Anhui in 2025. Among 1,792 soil samples collected from 31 provinces (2015–2025), 58.71% tested positive across 22 provinces, and annual economic losses were estimated at >2.5 billion Chinese renminbi (ca US $375 million) at a conservative 5% yield loss rate. Virulence phenotyping identified five races (1, 2, 3, 4, 6) and six HG Types (HG 0, 2.5, 2.5.7, 1.2.5.7, 4.5, 1.2.3.5.7). Anhui exhibited the highest complexity with all six HG Types, while Inner Mongolia was dominated by HG 0, though the highly virulent HG 1.2.3.5.7 reached ~40% frequency in Hulunbuir. Genotyping of 60 commercial cultivars for rhg1 and Rhg4 copy numbers identified resistance categories, highlighting risks of sole reliance on PI88788-type resistance. A region-specific deployment strategy is recommended: high-copy rhg1-b cultivars for HG Type 0-dominated regions, and rhg1-a + Rhg4-a combination cultivars for regions with complex virulence profiles, thereby prolonging resistance durability. This study fills systematic monitoring gaps and provides a scientific basis for region-specific SCN management and resista…

title: Holistic Voltammetric Profiles as a Scalable Strategy for Metabolic Fingerprinting
abstract: Abstract Metabolic fingerprinting is a powerful approach for phenotypic characterization but typically relies on costly analytical platforms such as NMR spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. Here, we demonstrate that differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) data acquired directly from intact urine samples can be exploited as holistic metabolic fingerprints. Coupling voltammetric data with chemometric and machine-learning methodologies enabled the robust discrimination of individual metabolic phenotypes and gender, achieving cross-validated classification performances with AUC values up to 0.93. Importantly, DPV measurements exhibited reproducibility below 5%, confirming that the recorded fingerprints primarily reflect biological variations. Comparative analyses with 1H NMR metabolomics data further supported the biological relevance of the voltammetric fingerprints. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of holistic voltammetric profiles as a rapid, low-cost, and scalable approach for metabolic fingerprinting, providing a foundation for further investigation in metabolomics, phenotyping, and future point-of-care applications.

From Competitive Strategy to Perceived Performance: The Mediating Role of Technology Adoption in Microfinance Institutions
abstract: Background: Microfinance institutions (MFIs) in Northern Kenya operate in geographically dispersed and infrastructure-constrained markets in which competitive positioning and digital capability are increasingly intertwined. Aim:This study examined whether technology adoption statistically mediates the association between Porter’s generic competitive strategies and perceived MFI performance. Research Design: This study adopted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods research design to examine the influence of Porter’s generic strategies on the performance of conventional, Islamic, and hybrid microfinance institutions (MFIs) in Northern Kenya, and to determine the mediating role of technology adoption.Research Setting and Duration: The study was conducted in Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, and Isiolo counties in Northern Kenya. The target population comprised 500 managers and operational staff from participating conventional, Islamic, and hybrid MFIs. The study was conducted over a period extending from March 2025 to September 2026, with field data collection and analysis undertaken within a six-month period. Methodology: A cross-sectional correlational survey was used to estimate associations among Porter’s generic strategies, technology adoption, and perceived MFI performance. Findings: The findings provided clear statistical evidence of a significant indirect relationship between the…

title: The Children's Climate Vulnerability Index: An Integrated Approach to Assessing Climate Risk—Evidence From India
abstract: ABSTRACT Children are particularly vulnerable to climate‐related risks due to their biological sensitivity, their dependence on societal systems, and their limited ability to adapt to the stressors posed by the environment. This study assesses the climate risk and the resulting vulnerability of children at the state level in India with the Children's Climate Vulnerability Index (CCVI). Drawing on the IPCC vulnerability framework, the index combines measures of household‐reported and perceived climatic and environmental exposure, child‐specific sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. The CCVI is applied to four Indian states—Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand—that represent different climatic regimes and socioeconomic contexts. Results show substantial variation in children's climate vulnerability despite similar levels of exposure; sensitivity is the main driver of vulnerability in all states. Health, nutrition, and education‐related sensitivities consistently outweigh the impact of climatic hazards, while adaptive capacity has limited power to offset these pressures. By linking vulnerability patterns to child development outcomes, the study shows that children's climate risk is shaped more by developmental and institutional conditions than by hazard intensity alone. The findings underscore the need for child‐focused, multi‐sectoral adaptation strategies…

title: Transcript modification: A potential nutrient‐conserving strategy for polyploid plants
abstract: Abstract Premise Due to greater cell and nucleic acid nutrient requirements, polyploids have been hypothesized to be more constrained than related diploids in terms of cell synthesis and biomass accumulation when soil nutrients are limited. Methods Here, we grew autotetraploid and diploid Solidago gigantea plants in soils enriched or limited with nitrogen‐ and phosphorus‐(NP) and examined the expression patterns and nutrient composition of transcripts associated with different plant functions to assess whether transcriptome modification altered nutrient constraint patterns of polyploids. Results Relative to diploids and independently of soil nutrient treatment, autotetraploids upregulated transcripts associated with reproduction, growth, and development, but downregulated transcripts associated with photosynthesis. However, the differential expression of transcripts associated with environmentally responsive processes, including abiotic and biotic responses and tolerances, depended upon soil nutrient treatment. Specifically, compared to diploids, autotetraploids downregulated these transcripts when grown in NP‐limited soils but upregulated them when grown in NP‐enriched soils. We also found that relative nutrient usage in transcripts associated with environmental responses compared to core cellular processes was lower for autotetraploids than for diploids in NP‐limited but not …

title: Smart Power Monitoring System for Home Appliances.
abstract: The Smart power monitoring system for home appliances is designed to improve electrical energy management, safety, and reliability in residential buildings. The main objective of this project is to continuously monitor the electrical parameters such as voltage, current, power, and energy consumption of home appliances in real time. The system uses sensors, a microcontroller, and IoT technology to collect and analyse electrical data. It can automatically detect abnormal conditions such as overvoltage, undervoltage, overload, short circuits, and excessive power consumption. When a fault occurs, the system activates protective mechanisms to isolate the affected circuit and prevent damage to electrical appliances. The self-healing feature helps restore normal operation automatically when safe operating conditions are confirmed. The adaptive monitoring feature analyses energy usage patterns and helps optimize electricity consumption. Users can monitor the system through a mobile application and receive instant notifications about faults and energy usage. This project aims to reduce electricity wastage, improve household electrical safety, minimize manual intervention, and ensure reliable and efficient power management

title: Deep Temporal Learning Versus Electrical Integration for Regenerative-Braking Energy and Peak-Power Classes
abstract: Regenerative-braking energy is determined by battery-pack current, voltage, and event duration, yet temporal networks have been proposed to estimate it from compressed event sequences. We audited four archived architectures (1D CNN, LSTM, GRU, and TCN) on 8181 events from one publicly available electric-vehicle dataset and reanalyzed their validation design. Events were represented by 32 samples of current, voltage, state of charge, temperature, and elapsed time. The original three-repeat comparison changed the grouped holdout between repeats and used globally derived energy-class thresholds; one extreme event moved between development and test. A direct 32-point trapezoidal-integration baseline, calculated from the identical network input, achieved R2 = 0.999879, RMSE = 0.554 Wh, and MAE = 0.147 Wh over all events. On fixed, non-overlapping recording-group and strictly forward whole-group tests, its RMSEs were 0.302 and 0.414 Wh, respectively. We additionally evaluate paired four- versus five-channel neural models, group-level dependence, distribution shift, and energy-magnitude versus peak-power classifications. The results show that this full-event, post-event task is largely an electrical-integration problem; high energy-derived classification scores should not be interpreted as recognition of an independent braking state. These single-vehicle, offline results do not establ…

title: Telling the Retail Story: The Politics of American Capitalism
abstract: Abstract Kathleen Thelen's Attention Shoppers! American Retail Capitalism and the Origins of the Amazon Economy seeks to locate the Amazon retail firm in the core of the political economy of the United States. It asserts the importance of a particular pattern of the American experience—high consumption, low savings, considerable income and wealth inequality, low welfare-state levels, concentrated wealth—when compared with other advanced industrial democracies in Europe and East Asia. Thelen locates the major explanatory causes of this pattern in the specific policy conflicts in the United States as they are refracted through key features of U.S. institutions (namely, federalism and antimajoritarian features of U.S. political rules) and certain interpretations made by the U.S. Supreme Court concerning vertical and horizontal restraints of trade. She tells this story by tracing the way these policies have emerged to favor the specific features of the emerging retail industry. Sears was the exemplar of this already in the late nineteenth century; the company used the U.S. mail and catalogs to distribute goods and collect money. Subsequent conflicts continued to favor innovation in retail at the expense of preserving stability in production, in contrast to Europe. In the current period, Amazon exemplifies the process, with computer-based, home delivery by truck as well as postal se…

Linking ethics and CSR with business sustainability as a strategy for achieving the SDGs: A aystematic review from 2016 to 2025
abstract: In sustainability research, the understanding of the links between corporate social responsibility (CSR), business ethics, business sustainability, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is gaining in importance. However, the literature remains fragmented, with these themes being addressed in isolation rather than as interrelated facets of responsible business conduct. This study, therefore, attempts to analyze the role of ethics and CSR in business sustainability and in making the attainment of the SDGs possible. A systematic literature review (SLR) was performed following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) format, including publications published between 2016 and 2025. The review synthesizes significant methods, difficulties, and emerging patterns in the literature and suggests an integrated framework that explains the links among ethics, CSR, business sustainability, and SDG attainment. The report also sets a future research agenda based on these findings to deepen theoretical and empirical understanding of these interrelated areas.

Income Inequality, Credit-Financed Consumption, and Policy Uncertainty: A U.S. Analysis (1972–2025)
abstract: This study investigates whether rising income inequality fuels credit-financed household consumption in the United States, and how economic policy uncertainty affects credit, spending, and inequality. We estimate a vector autoregression with exogenous variables (VARX) in first differences using annual U.S. data for the 1972–2025 period, drawn from the U.S. Census Bureau and the Federal Reserve Economic Data. Inequality is measured by the Gini index and the 90th-/10th- and 50th-/10th-percentile income ratios. We find no evidence that rising inequality increases household credit growth. Instead, inequality affects spending directly, as a wider 90th-/10th-percentile gap raises expenditure growth. Policy uncertainty consistently reduces credit growth and widens the gap between middle and low incomes. Inequality is persistent: the 90th-/10th-percentile ratio partly corrects after a shock but retains about three-quarters of it and drifts upward, and its short-run changes are driven by consumption rather than credit. The study contributes aggregate time-series evidence that challenges the inequality–debt hypothesis, extends the credit-channel effect of policy uncertainty to household credit, and shows that its distributional cost falls on those at the bottom of the income distribution. The findings point to policy priorities in affordable credit access, income support, and macropruden…

title: Family language policy under developmental uncertainty: emotions and cross-border reorganization in a Chinese family in the Netherlands

abstract: Purpose of the work. The study is devoted to the theoretical and methodological substantiation and development of a conceptual model for the application of intelligent Big Data analysis & analytics – as a strategic tool for accelerating innovative business projects. The work is aimed at resolving the fundamental scientific contradiction between the need for forced commercialization of innovations and the avalanche-like growth of entropy, uncertainty and systemic environmental risks in the conditions of permanent macrosystemic transit of the global economy. title: Revisiting Momentum Through Dynamic Kernel Learning
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper revisits momentum through a dynamic kernel framework that links return continuation to the speed at which return‐relevant shocks propagate through prices. Using nearly 60 years of US equity data, we estimate nonnegative and geometric kernels that govern how past returns are weighted over time. The estimated decay parameter rises sharply after 2000, indicating faster dissipation of return persistence and a shorter effective horizon for continuation, coinciding with the documented weakening of traditional 12–1 momentum. In out‐of‐sample tests, the structured kernel models match or outperform common machine‐learning benchmarks while retaining economic interpretability, and these gains remain robust after controlling for volatility timing and trading frictions. The framework provides a parsimonious tool for tracking time variation in return propagation and for adapting momentum implementations to changing market conditions.

title: Caregiving Challenges Across the Treatment and Recovery Trajectory of Patients Undergoing Oesophageal Cancer Surgery: A Longitudinal Qualitative Study Guided by the Timing It Right Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Aims To explore caregiving challenges experienced by family caregivers of patients undergoing oesophageal cancer surgery across different stages of the treatment and recovery trajectory and how these challenges evolve over time. Design A longitudinal qualitative study guided by the timing it right framework. Methods Guided by the Timing It Right Framework, this descriptive qualitative study used semi‐structured interviews with 17 primary family caregivers of patients undergoing oesophageal cancer surgery. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Results Caregiving challenges varied across stages and evolved dynamically. Five stage‐specific patterns were identified: admission and treatment‐planning, emotional shock, disclosure challenges, and treatment decision‐making difficulties; preoperative, concerns about surgical tolerance, psychological burden, and surgical safety; postoperative, difficulties meeting care needs, limited caregiving knowledge and skills, and physical and psychosocial strain; hospital‐to‐home transition, difficulties obtaining care knowledge, nutritional management challenges, and difficulties responding to negative emotions and social withdrawal; and longer‐term adjustment, increasing time commitment, financial pressure, fear of recurrence, and anticipatory grief. Conclusion Caregiving challenges change throughout the disease trajectory. Nurses …

Effect of Non-Performing Loan Ratio and Loan-To-Deposit Ratio on The Stability of Quoted Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria
abstract: Financial stability of deposit money banks is vital for economic development, given their central role in financial intermediation and capital mobilization. Over the years, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced several prudential measures, including non-performing loan ratio and loan-to-deposit ratio, however, despite these measures, the banking sector continues to face challenges. This study examined the effect of non-performing loan ratio and loan-to-deposit ratio on the stability of quoted deposit money banks in Nigeria. An ex post facto research design and a longitudinal panel approach. Census sampling was used to select 13 quoted banking institutions with consistent financial reports for the period 2015–2024, resulting in 130 bank-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from the banks’ audited annual reports, Nigerian Exchange Group filings and relevant regulatory publications. Bank stability was measured using the Z-score. The data were analysed using panel regression analysis. The Hausman specification test supported the fixed-effects model. The findings revealed that Non-performing loan ratio had a negative and significant effect on stability while Loan-to-deposit ratio had a positive and significant effect on financial stability deposit money banks in Nigeria. The study concluded that sound asset quality and prudent deposit-funded lending are essenti…

title: Financial Deepening, Banking Infrastructure, and Regional Labor Absorption: Panel Evidence from Indian States
abstract: This study empirically examines how state-level financial deepening and banking infrastructure affect labor absorption across the 36 Indian States and Union Territories during the period of 2022–2025. The paper applies a Two-Way Fixed Effects panel econometric model with cluster-robust standard errors to assess the semi-elasticity of the Worker Population Ratio (WPR) with respect to aggregate commercial bank credit and operational branch footprints. The diagnostic tests indicate that unobserved heterogeneity among states accounts for 98.29% of the composite error variance, supporting the choice of fixed effects estimation over pooled models. Even though the static level models generate positive yet statistically insignificant semi-elasticities over the short four-year panel horizon due to low temporal variation, our first-differenced dynamic model shows that the annual growth of credit has a statistically significant positive within-state co-movement with regional labor absorption. The results suggest that while accumulated banking infrastructure and static credit stocks reflect a baseline structural capacity to alter total employment levels, the dynamic annual growth of credit provides immediate labor liquidity that supports short-run labor absorption. Strategies targeting state-specific credit provision mechanisms and financing for labor-intensive sectors are recommended to o…

Multi-response optimization of drilling performance in chemically treated kenaf/epoxy hybrid composites reinforced with Citrus Limetta peel fillers
abstract: Drilling-induced damage can compromise the hole quality and structural integrity of natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites. This study investigates the drilling performance of sodium bicarbonate-treated kenaf/epoxy hybrid composites containing 10 wt.% citrus limetta peel (CLP) filler. A full-factorial experimental design comprising 81 combinations was employed to evaluate the effects of feed rate (0.05–0.30 mm/rev), spindle speed (700–2800 rpm), drill diameter (4–8 mm), and drill point angle (90°–135°). Thrust force, surface roughness, and entry and exit delamination factors were considered as performance responses. Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) was used for multi-response optimization, while analysis of variance (ANOVA) quantified the contributions of the machining parameters and their two-factor interactions. The optimum combination was identified as 0.05 mm/rev feed rate, 1400 rpm spindle speed, 4 mm drill diameter, and 135° drill point angle. Under these conditions, the measured thrust force was 14.65 N, surface roughness was 1.2042 µm, and entry and exit delamination factors were 1.011 and 1.028, respectively. Drill diameter was the most influential main parameter, contributing 26.01% to the variation in Grey Relational Grade (GRG), followed by feed rate (21.68%), drill point angle (15.64%), and spindle speed (10.02%). Independent confirmation tests yielded a mean GR…

Integrated Scheduling of Wind Power and Pumped Hydroelectric Storage Based on an MILP Model
abstract: In this article, we develop a tractable mixed-integer linear programming framework for the annual scheduling of a hybrid offshore wind and pumped hydroelectric energy storage system. The proposed formulation uses McCormick envelopes to relax the non-convex hydraulic power relations while embedding generation dispatch within a direct current optimal power flow model. In particular, we incorporate a cumulative storage incentive into the objective function to capture the trade-off between net electricity-market revenue and intra-horizon water availability, examining its weighting multiplier through a systematic sensitivity analysis. We illustrate the performance of the proposed formulation applied to (i) a modified PJM five-bus benchmark and (ii) an IEEE 30-bus network hosting two hybrid installations, driven by historical wind profiles from Tamaulipas and locational marginal prices from the Mexican wholesale electricity market. Moreover, we assess the selected binary operating-mode sequences ex post by re-optimizing the continuous dispatch under the exact bilinear hydraulic equations. The numerical results demonstrate that coordinated dispatch enhances energy arbitrage and dynamic grid interaction. title: Dynamic Identification of Critical Nodes and Links in Virtual Power Plants for Sustainable Operation Using a Dual-Dynamic Cyber–Physical Criticality Index
abstract: Virtual power plants (VPPs) depend on tightly coupled electrical and communication infrastructures, so component criticality varies with operating conditions and functional roles. Existing methods often use static weights, underrepresent heterogeneous communication functions, and mix ranking construction with disturbance-based validation. This study proposes a role-aware identification method based on a dual-dynamic cyber-physical criticality index (D-D-CPCI). A two-layer VPP model represents hierarchical communication, primary and backup access paths, and communication-quality effects on distributed energy resource controllability. D-D-CPCI combines state-adaptive system weights with object-specific dynamic indicators and uses a causal trailing window for online updates without future disturbance information. A fixed distributed energy resource layout, selected under an equal-budget siting protocol, isolates identification performance from layout variability. The method is evaluated on an IEEE 39-bus VPP using 105 operating scenarios, comprising 70 calibration and 35 independent-test scenarios. Across 11 object groups and multiple Top-K budgets, D-D-CPCI achieves the or engineering-equivalent performance in 10 groups and exceeds the strongest benchmark of the same object group in eight groups. ST-MRC: A Service-Oriented Probabilistic Forecasting Method for Virtual Power Plant Aggregated Coupled Loads Based on Set Attention Encoding and Multi-Scale Residual Correction
abstract: Virtual power plants (VPPs) represent a novel energy service paradigm that aggregates distributed resources. With the rapid development of these services, individual resources within aggregations have been increasingly integrated as flexible loads for participation in electricity market trading and demand response. However, accurate forecasting of coupled loads remains challenging due to the stochastic nature of individual loads, coupling effects among multiple entities, and dynamic membership changes within aggregations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Set Transformer-based Multi-scale Residual Correction method ST-MRC for probabilistic load forecasting. The framework adopts a three-stage progressive architecture: individual forecasting, interaction encoding, and residual correction. Load forecasts are first generated for each entity, after which a Set Transformer encodes multi-entity interaction features via attention to capture nonlinear couplings such as coincident and complementary peak demands; subsequently, a multi-scale temporal convolutional network (TCN) with varying dilation rates extracts residual evolution patterns for adaptive error correction, and finally quantile regression produces both point forecasts and probabilistic prediction intervals to support deterministic decisions and uncertainty quantification. Deciding in the shadow of the state: when regulatory logic collides with market logic
abstract: Purpose Capital allocation models treat planning inputs as market-governed, even when they originate from political authority. Written for The Practice of Making Decisions section of Management Decision, this paper develops a three-phase response: classify each input, stress test it against a change of authority and design commitments that can move if the answer changes. Design/methodology/approach The process is built from the tasks the decision involves, not from theory. A constructed vignette of a wine producer entering Mendoza runs through the argument; three documented situations (utility privatization, wine internationalization, EU digital regulation) serve as retrospective illustrations. Findings Standard tools presume a judgment they do not perform: which institutional logic governs each input; tagging inputs by source, durability and evidence confidence comes first. In Mendoza the commitment changes form, not direction: purchase becomes staged entry sized to survive the incentive's loss. Research limitations/implications Retrospective illustrations show compatibility with documented responses, not conscious use or performance effects. Practical implications Each phase specifies questions, participants, outputs and revisit triggers; a decision matrix and a pre-commitment checklist support its use. title: How do green market orientation, green innovation and leadership styles interact for green new venture creation among family-owned enterprises?
abstract: Purpose Drawing on stakeholder theory and leader-member exchange theory, the study examines how a firm's tactical green market orientation – the implementation of eco-friendly marketing tactics – influences green innovation and, in turn, results in successful green new venture creation under different leadership styles. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from family-owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) involved in green initiatives in Oman using snowball sampling and analyzed to test the proposed model using partial least squares structural equation modeling in Smart PLS version 4.1.1.8. Findings The findings revealed that tactical green market orientation positively influences green innovation, and green innovation positively influences green new venture creation. Green innovation significantly mediates the relationship between tactical green market orientation and green new venture creation. Finally, the study found a positive but insignificant moderating impact of leadership styles on the associations of tactical green market orientation, green innovation and green new venture creation. Originality/value The results highlight the crucial interplay among tactical green market orientation, green innovation and hybrid leadership styles in promoting sustainable new venture creation in the unique context of family-owned MSMEs. title: Enhancing Community Resilience Through Disaster-Safe Market Preparedness in Kelud Volcanic Hazard Zone
abstract: This community service program aimed to enhance disaster preparedness among market traders and stakeholders in the Kelud volcanic hazard zone through education, skills training, and evacuation simulations. The activity employed a participatory action research (PAR) approach, involving Wage Market vendors, market managers, the Blitar City Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD), and the Blitar City Disaster Risk Reduction Forum (FPRB) as technical partners. The program included planning, action, observation, and reflection to develop a sustainable Disaster-Safe Market model. Initial outreach sessions provided basic disaster education, self-evacuation procedures, and first aid using counseling and audio-visual presentations. Knowledge gains were measured through pre- and post-tests, while practical skills in evacuation and first aid were trained via demonstrations and hands-on exercises using Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and evaluated with an SOP skills checklist. A miniature Wage Disaster Preparedness Market was used for table-top simulations to visualize market structure, evacuation routes, and assembly points. The final stage involved a full-scale evacuation simulation, resulting in the establishment of a Wage Market Disaster Preparedness Team. Among 30 participants, knowledge scores increased from 54.3 to 88.7, 82% achieved skilled competency in SOP-based procedure…

title: Do Big4 accounting firms affect foreign individuals’ investment decisions? Evidence from an emerging market
abstract: Purpose This paper focuses on an emerging market and investigates whether a firm’s audit engagement with a Big4 accounting firm is associated with foreign individuals’ investments. We hypothesize that Big4 accounting firms’ reputation may function as a heuristic trust signal for these investors. Design/methodology/approach We tested our hypothesis by utilizing 225 non-financial firms listed on Borsa Istanbul. The dataset covers 2005 to 2023 and contains 3,590 firm-year observations. Findings Our empirical evidence indicates that foreign individuals are more likely to invest in BIST-listed firms audited by a Big4 accounting firm (AF). Our results are consistent with prior studies showing that accounting firms’ reputation is associated with investors’ decisions. Our robustness analysis suggests that Big4 AFs’ reputation may lose importance when public governance declines. Research limitations/implications The primary limitation of this research is that investor-level data are not publicly available. We also did not incorporate audit-firm-level variables such as expertise and number of partners. Practical implications Our study has implications for managers, policymakers and accounting professionals. Managers seeking to signal trust to foreign individuals may consider the positive association between Big4 AF engagement and foreign investment. Social implications Policymakers shoul…

title: FX market connectedness during the Israel–Iran 12-day confrontation: evidence from minute-level data
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how volatility was transmitted across global and regional currencies during the June 2025 Israel–Iran confrontation. Design/methodology/approach Using minute-level FX data covering 12–24 June 2025, we apply a TVP-VAR connectedness framework with APARCH-based volatility modelling to track how shocks moved across currency pairs in real time. Findings EUR/USD and GBP/USD generate large outward spillovers, while USD/CNY records the strongest positive full-horizon NET position. Regionally exposed currencies are predominantly net receivers, although transmitter and receiver positions change across short intraday horizons. EGP/USD, ILS/USD and SAR/USD mainly absorb shocks from dominant global pairs, while SAR/USD shows more limited volatility, consistent with its pegged exchange-rate regime. Connectedness also increases sharply on 18 June despite the absence of a single discrete major event in the study's chronology. We interpret this as heightened market repricing during evolving geopolitical uncertainty, while recognising that the connectedness measure does not identify the specific information responsible. Several currency pairs also switch between transmitter and receiver roles within 2–5-min intervals. Originality/value The study provides new evidence on how geopolitical stress is transmitted through the FX network at minute-level frequency. Its main c…

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS AND ASSESSMENT OF THE CURRENT STATE OF MARKET SEGMENTS IN AZERBAIJAN'S FOOD INDUSTRY
abstract: This article presents a comparative analysis and assessment of the current state of market segments in Azerbaijan's food industry. The study examines the level of development of the main product market segments, consumer demand, the competitive environment, pricing policies, and marketing activities within the food industry. It also evaluates the competitiveness of domestic products against imported goods, the key factors influencing consumer behavior, and the current positions of market participants. The findings of the comparative analysis indicate significant differences among market segments in terms of development, innovation adoption, and competitiveness. Based on the research results, the article offers practical recommendations aimed at improving the efficiency of market segmentation, strengthening the competitiveness of food industry enterprises, and supporting the sustainable development of Azerbaijan's food sector.

title: Climate conditions, financial uncertainty and market resilience in African equity markets: an event-driven probabilistic deep learning approach
abstract: Purpose This paper examines stock-market volatility in Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria, South Africa and Tunisia under geopolitical and financial uncertainty and physical climate conditions. African evidence rarely integrates event-time shock analysis with full-distribution forecasting while distinguishing physical climate signals from climate-related financial risk. The study develops an event-driven probabilistic framework grounded in a Climate–Market Conditioning Framework (CMCF). Design/methodology/approach The study combines cumulative abnormal volatility (CAV) analysis with Mixture Density Network–Long Short-Term Memory (MDN-LSTM) volatility and return-density models. Daily market data from January 2015 to April 2025 are combined with Geopolitical Risk, Financial Stress Index and National Aeronautics and Space Administration Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources climate indicators. Forecasts use a strict chronological holdout and are compared with Generalised Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH)(1,1)-Normal, GARCH(1,1)-Student-t, Exponential GARCH (EGARCH), Glosten–Jagannathan–Runkle-GARCH (GJR-GARCH), Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting. Distributional performance is additionally benchmarked against probabilistic GARCH using the weighted interval score (WIS). Findings Shock responses are heterogeneous across markets. title: Governance modes and their applicability boundaries in compensated rural homestead withdrawal: a control-rights comparison of organization-led and market-coordinated governance
abstract: Inroduction Rural land restructuring must reconcile asset reuse with household security and accountable governance. Methods This conceptual-comparative study examines compensated homestead withdrawal in China using documentary analysis, a narrative literature synthesis, and four structured cases. Results The analysis separates compensation instruments from governance structures and distinguishes administrative coordination from member-authorized collective autonomy. It specifies control-rights closure across decisions, subsequent use, benefits, accountability, and risk bearing, alongside qualification-right buffering through credible household safeguards. Verified source evidence shows that stated willingness, withdrawal scale, and compensation preferences cannot substitute for durable land-use and welfare outcomes. Case contrasts identify conditional coordination and protection requirements without establishing causal effects or performance rankings. Discussion International comparison connects these propositions to dispersed-rights coordination, livelihood reconstruction, and post-transfer accountability while preserving institutional differences.

title: Improving Posyandu Cadres’ Skills to Support Primary Care Integration
abstract: Posyandu is currently undergoing health-system transformation through the integration of primary care services targeting all stages of the human life cycle, with Posyandu cadres playing a key role in service delivery. Cadre regeneration remains necessary; however, some newly recruited Posyandu cadres have not previously received information or training on Posyandu management. This community service activity was conducted as a training program for newly recruited Posyandu cadres to improve their skills. The participants were 42 newly recruited Posyandu cadres from Kepanjen Kidul Subdistrict, Kepanjen Kidul District, Blitar City. The training was conducted over two days, 22–23 July 2026, by healthcare professionals from Kepanjen Kidul Community Health Center and community service team members from Poltekkes Kemenkes Malang. The classroom-based training included Posyandu management, simulation of effective communication using the SAJI model, and simulation of Posyandu services using the five-step procedure. The results indicated that the cadres had good perceptions and knowledge of Posyandu management and were able to simulate the five-step Posyandu service procedure. The training improved cadres’ knowledge, self-confidence, effective communication skills, and ability to provide Posyandu services. Therefore, training for Posyandu cadres should be conducted regularly.

title: Inside the service work ecosystem: a lived account of young workers
abstract: Purpose Existing service work ecosystem research primarily examines how systems are structured and managed, offering limited insight into how they are experienced by workers. This study addresses that gap by providing the first empirical, worker-centered account of how the service work ecosystem is lived, interpreted and navigated from within. Design/methodology/approach Five Lego® Serious Play® (LSP) workshops were conducted with 80 participants aged 18–26, all with frontline service experience and originating from Global South contexts (Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos). Visual, narrative and observational data were analyzed using an abductive, iterative approach, examining participants' interpretations and recurring visual patterns alongside transcripts, with Psychology of Working Theory (PWT) as a sensitizing lens. Findings Findings reveal a systemic pattern of constraint rather than opportunity. Work is experienced not as a pathway to mobility, but as a site where all three PWT needs (survival, social connection, self-determination) are persistently compromised through macro-level forces, organizational practices and relational dynamics. Pursuing self-determination carries a moral cost, conceptualized here as the guilt of aspiration. Navigating these conditions is itself invisible, uncompensated labor that depletes the very resources on which service quality depends. O…

title: Family-Based Tuberculosis Prevention Through Self-Management Education (SME) for Community Health Workers in Rural East Indonesia
abstract: Pulmonary Tuberculosis (TB) remains a significant public health concern in Indonesia, especially in East Nusa Tenggara Province. This community service program aimed to strengthen the knowledge and skills of community health workers (cadres) in delivering family-based TB prevention through a Self-Management Education (SME) approach. A pre–post descriptive design was implemented involving 35 active Integrated Service Post (ISP) health cadres in Manusak Village, Kupang Regency. The intervention included cadres training, developing and distributing educational materials (modules, posters, and leaflets), conducting structured home visits, and implementing monitoring tools. Cadres’ knowledge and skills were measured using a structured 15-item questionnaire and a skills observational checklist before and after the intervention. The results showed an increase in average knowledge scores from 57% before the intervention to 94% after the intervention. Cadres’ skills also improved markedly, with the proportion of cadres categorized as having good skills increasing from 6% at baseline to 94% after the intervention. This program demonstrates that SME is a feasible and effective approach to empowering community health cadres to deliver family-based TB prevention in rural settings. Each family affected by TB received four home visits over an eight-week period. Post-intervention observations …

title: Development and Validation of a Multidimensional Gen-AI Competence Scale for Pre-Service Science Teachers
abstract: The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) into education is transforming the competencies required of future teachers and creating a need for a robust multidimensional measure of Gen-AI competency. This study developed and validated a six-dimensional framework comprising output evaluation, use appropriateness, prompting & operation, technical integration, model literacy, and responsible practice among pre-service science teachers. Data were obtained from 426 biology, chemistry, and physics education students at Universitas Jambi, Indonesia. The responses were randomly split into EFA (n = 256; 60%) and CFA (n = 170; 40%) subsamples. An initial 84-item pool was evaluated through ten experts’ judgment using CVR and CVI, resulting in 63 content-valid items. The data were suitable for factor analysis (KMO = 0.972; Bartlett’s χ² = 20430.533; df = 1,953; p < 0.001), and EFA retained 33 items across six dimensions, with factor loadings of 0.502–0.811 and Cronbach’s alpha of 0.765–0.909. CFA supported the six-dimensional structure with acceptable fit (RMSEA = 0.063, CFI = 0.913, TLI = 0.904, SRMR = 0.052). The dimensions demonstrated satisfactory reliability and convergent validity (α = 0.754–0.909; CR = 0.752–0.910; AVE = 0.505–0.611), while HTMT values of 0.586–0.874 supported discriminant validity. The resulting measure provides an empirically supported bas…

title: Human Resource Management Strategies for Improving Work Effectiveness and Service Quality: A Case Study
abstract: This study aims to analyze human resource management strategies in improving work effectiveness and service quality at Mubarak Tour & Travel. The study employed a qualitative approach using a case study method. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, direct observation, documentation, and literature review. Informants were selected purposively and included the director, employees, marketing staff, mutawwif, and pilgrims who had used the services of Mubarak Tour & Travel more than twice. Data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification using the interactive analysis model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings indicate that Mubarak Tour & Travel faces limitations in its human resource structure, resulting in overlapping responsibilities and increased workload dynamics, particularly during periods of high pilgrim numbers and departure schedules. These challenges are managed through the optimization of available human resources, flexible task allocation, coordination and collaboration among employees, and competency development through briefings, direct guidance, experience sharing, and work evaluation. These strategies contribute to improving productivity, timely task completion, and employees’ ability to adapt to changing workloads. title: Smart Pregnant Women Movement: Education on Danger Signs and High-Risk Pregnancy in Blabak Village, Kediri Regency
abstract: Limited knowledge of pregnancy danger signs and high-risk conditions may contribute to delays in recognizing complications and seeking appropriate healthcare. This community service program aimed to improve pregnant women’s knowledge of pregnancy danger signs and high-risk conditions through the “Smart Pregnant Women Movement.” The program was conducted on November 10, 2025, in Blabak Village, Kediri Regency, and involved 18 pregnant women in the first to third trimesters. The intervention consisted of interactive health education, discussions, and question-and-answer sessions supported by PowerPoint presentations and educational leaflets. Knowledge was assessed before and after the intervention using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Before the intervention, 6 participants (33%) had good knowledge and 12 (67%) had moderate knowledge. After the intervention, the proportion of participants with good knowledge increased to 16 (88%), while only 2 (12%) remained in the moderate category. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test indicated a statistically significant difference between pre- and post-intervention knowledge scores (Z = −3.742; p < 0.001). The Smart Pregnant Women Movement was associated with improved knowledge of pregnancy danger signs and high-risk conditions and may serve as a practical community-based strategy to strengthen maternal h…

title: AI-mediated teacher learning in Chinese lesson study: regulating cognitive demands in EFL pre-service teachers
abstract: Purpose This study, guided by the cognitive theory of multimedia learning (CTML), investigates how multimodal large language models (MLLMs) mediate the professional learning of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) pre-service teachers within Chinese lesson study (CLS). It aims to elucidate the cognitive and dialogic mechanisms through which AI-supported mediation shapes teacher learning processes and participation. Design/methodology/approach A three-month intervention integrating MLLMs into CLS was conducted with 50 EFL pre-service teachers at a Chinese normal university. Adopting an interpretive qualitative design, data were collected from longitudinal reflective journals, MLLM interaction logs, field notes and two rounds of semi-structured interviews with 5 purposively selected focal participants. Data analysis combined deductive coding based on CTML (intrinsic, extraneous and germane cognitive load) with inductive thematic analysis to capture emergent patterns of AI-mediated learning and interaction. Findings The findings reveal that MLLMs functioned as cognitive-dialogic mediators in three key ways: (1) reducing linguistic and organizational barriers, thereby lowering extraneous cognitive load; (2) redistributing cognitive resources to support meaning-making and pedagogical reasoning; and (3) enabling deeper engagement in collaborative knowledge construction and reflective …

title: Counseling on Household-Scale Pharmaceutical Waste Disposal at Talise Public Health Center
abstract: Improper disposal of pharmaceutical waste can harm the environment and public health. Public knowledge regarding appropriate household-level drug disposal remains limited. This community engagement aimed to improve the knowledge, attitudes, and behavior of residents regarding the handling of expired and damaged medicines. The activity was conducted at Bumi Roviga Sub-Public Health Center, a unit under Talise Public Health Center, Palu City. A total of 24 respondents, selected randomly among parents attending child health checks or antenatal care, participated in the program. The counseling was delivered face-to-face and supplemented with printed educational flyers. A pre-test was administered at the location, while the post-test was distributed via WhatsApp using Google Forms one week later. Shapiro-Wilk normality tests indicated non-normal data distribution. Paired t-tests showed significant improvements (p<0.05) in knowledge (p=0.000), attitude (p=0.000), and behavior (p=0.000) scores, indicating the effectiveness of the intervention. This activity demonstrates that brief counseling supported by print media can effectively enhance public understanding of safe drug disposal at the household level. As a recommendation, household-level pharmaceutical waste education should be integrated into routine health promotion activities at community health centers, with periodic follow-up…

abstract: This study examines the development of Uzbekistan’s public service delivery system using secondary administrative data for 2017–2024. Descriptive statistical, comparative, and dynamic analyses were applied. From 2018 to 2024, the number of services offered through Public Service Centers (PSCs) increased from 63 to 403, while services available via the Unified Portal of Interactive Public Services (UPIPS) rose from 83 to 717. By 22 October 2024, automated services had increased from 10 to 186 and BPM-based services from 24 to 494. The findings show broader service coverage and greater automation; the article compares these trends by delivery channel and automation type

title: Universal design for learning in general chemistry: a pre-post study of inclusive teaching competence in pre-service teacher education
abstract: Abstract Inclusive STEM education places distinct demands on prospective chemistry teachers, owing to the discipline’s high cognitive load, the need to organize practice-oriented activities safely, and the requirement to ensure fair assessment in the context of diverse learners’ educational needs. The present study examined changes in inclusive chemistry teaching competence during a semester-long intervention grounded in Universal Design for Learning (UDL). A single-group pretest-posttest intervention design was implemented in the General Chemistry course (6 credits; 180 academic hours) at Zhanibekov University. The sample comprised 106 first-year university students. Over a 15-week semester, the UDL approach was embedded into the course through a sequence of design-based assignments targeting multiple means of engagement, representation, and action and expression. The course instructor served as the intervention implementer (teacher effect). Data collection included pre- and post-measures using self-report scales (knowledge, self-efficacy, attitudes, and intention to implement UDL), a case-based knowledge test, and the evaluation of student-generated pedagogical artifacts at two time points (T1 and T2) using a study-specific eight-criterion UDL design rubric (0–3 per criterion; total score 0–24). Data were analyzed using paired pre-post comparisons, effect size estimation, and…

title: Esco2 restrains pathological endothelial-mesenchymal transition through hidden isoform regulation in a Roberts syndrome model
abstract: Roberts syndrome is caused by biallelic ESCO2 pathogenic variants, but the mechanisms linking ESCO2 loss to embryonic endothelial failure remain poorly defined. Endothelial cells must maintain identity and resist endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), yet conventional transcriptomics measures gene abundance rather than isoform composition. Here, using endothelial-specific Esco2 deletion in a mouse model relevant to Roberts syndrome, we show that Esco2 loss causes yolk sac vascular remodeling failure, pathological EndMT, diversion from hemogenic endothelial fate, hemogenic endothelial depletion, impaired hematopoietic output, and embryonic lethality. Short-read single-cell RNA-seq revealed broad endothelial reprogramming, whereas single-cell long-read isoform sequencing uncovered a hidden layer of isoform dysregulation that conventional gene-level analysis failed to resolve. Esco2-deficient endothelium exhibited transcriptome-wide isoform switching, disruption of a multi-tier splicing-factor network, and predicted broad loss or rewiring of protein-coding output. Chromatin occupancy profiling localized Esco2 to exonic regions near alternatively spliced loci, supporting a cotranscriptional route to spliceopathy. Whole-genome sequencing showed that local DNA variation was insufficient to explain these changes, supporting a predominantly posttranscriptional mechanism. These fin…

Enhanced output voltage regulation in a seven-level inverter with minimal active power switches for renewable energy applications
abstract: Smart inverters are a prevalent solution in renewable energy applications due to their capacity to provide output voltage with minimal harmonic distortion and ease of control and operation. This trend has driven the rapid growth of power converters in various renewable energy applications. This research aims to design a strategy and implementation technique for a single-phase seven-level (SPSL) inverter that can control output voltage accurately. This research is innovative because it constructs an SPSL inverter with six active power switches and a new control strategy. This inverter comprises two active power switches that operate as a three-level direct current (DC) voltage shaper and four active power switches for polarity inversion. This inverter is controlled using advanced sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) methods. The inverter SPSL was selected because it can produce smoother sine waves with a total harmonic distortion (THD) less than the IEEE standard. The SPSL inverter's power circuit is controlled by a microcontroller-based control system, which enables the inverter to dynamically adapt to changes in load and operating conditions. This study performed simulations and verified the design performance via hardware implementation. The results from the simulations and lab tests indicate that the inverter works well with a THD of 4.16%; the SPSL inverter created in t…

title: Digital leapfrogging or digital divide? Internet penetration and structural transformation in Africa
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate whether digitalization accelerates structural transformation in African economies or reinforces existing structural inequalities. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data on African countries and a rigorous fixed-effects framework, complemented by dynamic System GMM estimation, the analysis provides a direct test of the digital structural transformation hypothesis. Findings The results show a strong and robust positive effect of internet penetration on structural transformation, even after controlling for key macroeconomic and demographic factors. Sectoral evidence reveals a clear mechanism: increased internet access reduces the share of agriculture while significantly expanding the services sector, confirming that digitalization actively reallocates economic activity across sectors. Crucially, interaction results show that the impact of internet penetration is stronger in slower-growing, less advanced economies, providing compelling evidence in favor of the digital leapfrogging hypothesis rather than the digital divide. Originality/value These findings establish digital infrastructure as a central driver of modern structural change and suggest that expanding internet access can serve as a powerful policy tool for accelerating inclusive development in Africa.

title: Regulations, infrastructure and financial efficiency: evidence from 101 economies
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether regulatory quality or information infrastructure better predicts financial system efficiency and investigate the pathway through which regulation translates into operational outcomes across 101 economies. Design/methodology/approach The World Bank B-READY 2025 data set is used to separately measure regulatory framework quality and public-service infrastructure as predictors of operational efficiency. OLS with HC3-robust standard errors is estimated across eight institutional variables and four income groups, with formal mediation analysis and robustness checks including region fixed effects and principal component digital infrastructure. Findings Payment interoperability rules and credit registry accessibility are the institutional variables most robustly associated with efficiency. Information infrastructure transmits approximately 29% of the total regulatory effect, consistent with partial mediation. A steep income gradient persists after controlling for all institutional variables. Decomposing efficiency reveals distinct channels: credit registry accessibility is associated with credit efficiency; payment interoperability rules are associated with payment efficiency. title: Decoupling growth from degradation: a fractional frequency Fourier analysis of India's aviation sector and the environmental Kuznets Curve
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India's aviation sector from 1970 to 2021. Using the ecological footprint as an indicator and a novel fractional frequency Fourier approach, it tests the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. The results reveal a U-shaped relationship, contradicting the EKC, and highlight the negative environmental impact of increased air freight. However, financial development supports sustainability by enabling cleaner technologies. The study aims to inform policy by proposing strategies such as carbon pricing, renewable fuel adoption, and green logistics to decouple aviation growth from environmental harm. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a fractional frequency Fourier approach to examine the long-run relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India from 1970 to 2021. The ecological footprint is used as a comprehensive measure of environmental impact. This advanced econometric method captures structural breaks and nonlinearities more effectively than traditional models.
